emails.subject: The 10-Point: An 'Unsettled Vibe' Creeps Through Markets
emails.contentEn:
Big Tech Earnings and Fed Rate Decision Put Stock Rally to the Test
Plus, America's big cities are rapidly losing kids, and Trump puts off a major escalation of his military campaign against Iran

1. FROM MY DESK
Predictions of an AI-driven hiring wipeout have yet to materialize. Companies across tech, transportation and defense are hiring again, offering a bright spot as investors brace for a big week. This year's stock rally has already withstood inflation, war and eye-watering AI budgets, but investors may be reaching their limit. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq composite both fell last week for the second time in a row, weighed down by familiar threats. Pressures could mount in the days ahead as Microsoft and Meta Platforms report earnings on the same day the Fed delivers an unusually unpredictable interest-rate decision.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
• President Trump has put off a major escalation of his military campaign against Iran as officials weigh dwindling air defense stocks.
• A surprising portion of rent-stabilized apartments go to NYC's wealthiest renters.
• Darline Graham, the late Sen. Lindsey Graham's sister who in recent years had run South Carolina's Commission for the Blind, is getting a crash course in Hill politics.
• David Fox, who helped make Kirkland & Ellis a legal powerhouse, now sees artificial intelligence as the industry's future.
• The Gordie Howe International Bridge—a long-awaited project linking Detroit and Windsor, Ontario—will open to traffic today. We take you inside the decadelong saga to open the bridge.
• In a series of new rules and laws, China is reordering the wealth landscape, seeking to better control how money leaves the country.

3. LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
S&P 500 Futures 7,519.25 (+0.96%) | DJIA Futures 52,649.00 (+1.01%) | Nasdaq 100 Futures 28,729.50 (+1.58%)
As of 7/27/2026, 6:23:06 AM ET
• United Chief Executive Scott Kirby called Delta's CEO last year to discuss a potential merger but the talks didn't progress, according to people familiar with the matter.
• A federal probe into the financial empire of Dodgers owner Mark Walter began with an internal whistleblower and evolved into an examination of whether fraud occurred in private-credit deals.
• Legal challenges to the Paramount-Warner deal are delaying integration plans, limiting Warner's ability to operate independently and driving up costs for the companies.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
America's big cities are rapidly losing kids.
With the nation's fertility rate at record lows, the number of children under 18 is falling across the U.S. The decline is especially pronounced in large cities, according to a Journal analysis. The number of children under 18 living in big U.S. cities is down 6% in the past decade, compared with a 1% decline nationwide. Even cities that are gaining population are losing children. Families with children cite concerns about costs, safety and quality of life in their move away from cities. Also contributing to the drop is a growing number of childless residents opting to stay that way, report Rachel Louise Ensign and Paul Overberg.

5. Nvidia is in talks with OpenAI to guarantee $250 billion in financing for a data center.
Nvidia is in talks to provide a roughly $250 billion backstop for OpenAI as part of a massive data-center project, one of the most ambitious financial transactions yet in America's AI boom. The guarantees from Nvidia would help the ChatGPT maker lease a 10-gigawatt project that SoftBank's energy subsidiary is developing in southern Ohio, people familiar with the matter said. In total, the project could cost more than $500 billion, report Anissa Gardizy, Amrith Ramkumar and Corrie Driebusch. The power for the project is controlled by the U.S. government and funded separately by Japan under a recent trade deal.

6. SEE THE STORY
Here's how House Democrats turned against Israel aid.
What a difference two years makes. More than 100 House Democrats voted for an amendment this month that sought to cut off military financing for Israel. The vote, which failed, was seen as a key barometer of where the party stands amid growing concern about Israel's military actions in Gaza. In graphics, we break down how different groups of Democrats—leadership, progressives, millennials—shifted on Israel, and who led the way.

7. HAPPENING TODAY
• Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is scheduled to arrive in Washington, where he is due to meet with Trump.
• Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER
$9,325
That's how much Waymo's robotaxis have been fined in parking tickets in Austin, Texas, since the company came to town in 2024, according to documents the Journal obtained through an open-records request. Such parking mishaps are becoming a visible point of friction as Waymo and other robotaxi companies scale their services across the U.S.

9. AND FINALLY…
Singles are so burned out they're letting spreadsheets evaluate their dates.
Forget intuition. Young adults are rushing home to crunch the numbers before they decide if the date actually went well. These singles are part of a cohort of “love hackers” who believe data could hold the cure to their dating woes. They say dating apps that spit out an unlimited menu of potential partners make it too easy to miss obvious red flags. But some love gurus say there is an element of humanity that can get lost in the spreadsheet cells.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
• Opinion: The key to U.S. leadership and AI safety is 'alignment,' which improves capability while cordoning off dangerous knowledge.
• WSJ | Buy Side: Streamline your obligations and check to see if you could save money with a debt-consolidation loan.
emails.contentZh:
科技巨頭財報與聯準會利率決策考驗股市多頭
此外，美國大城市孩童數量正快速流失，川普暫緩對伊朗軍事行動的重大升級

1. 編輯手記
外界原本預期AI將引發大規模裁員潮，但這一幕至今尚未成真。科技、運輸與國防業者正重新展開招募，為投資人在關鍵一週前帶來一絲亮點。今年的股市漲勢已挺過通膨、戰爭與驚人的AI支出，但投資人的耐性可能正逼近極限。標普500與那斯達克綜合指數上週雙雙連續第二週下跌，受到熟悉的威脅拖累。隨著微軟與Meta同日公布財報、而聯準會又將做出異常難以預測的利率決策，未來幾天市場壓力恐將升溫。

2. 今日頭條
• 川普總統已暫緩對伊朗軍事行動的重大升級，因官員正評估防空存量日益吃緊的問題。
• 令人意外的是，相當一部分受租金管制的公寓竟落入紐約市最富有租客手中。
• 已故參議員林賽·格雷厄姆的姊姊達琳·格雷厄姆，近年曾主持南卡羅來納州盲人委員會，如今正緊急惡補國會政治運作。
• 曾協助建立凱易律師事務所法律地位的大衛·福克斯，如今視人工智慧為業界的未來。
• 連接底特律與安大略省溫莎、籌備已久的戈迪·豪國際大橋今日通車。我們帶你回顧這座橋歷經十年的興建曲折。
• 中國正透過一系列新規與法令重塑財富格局，試圖更嚴格掌控資金外流。

3. 市場即時動態
標普500期貨 7,519.25（+0.96%）｜ 道瓊期貨 52,649.00（+1.01%）｜ 那斯達克100期貨 28,729.50（+1.58%）
截至美東時間2026年7月27日上午6:23:06
• 據知情人士透露，聯合航空執行長史考特·柯比去年曾致電達美航空執行長討論潛在合併，但談判並未取得進展。
• 對道奇隊老闆馬克·沃爾特金融帝國的聯邦調查，起初源於內部吹哨者，如今已演變為對私募信貸交易是否涉及詐欺的深入審查。
• 派拉蒙與華納合併案面臨的法律挑戰正拖延整合計畫，限制華納獨立營運的能力，並推高雙方成本。

4. 獨家搶先看
美國大城市的孩童數量正快速流失。
隨著全國生育率創下歷史新低，18歲以下人口在美國各地持續減少，而根據《華爾街日報》分析，這種下滑在大城市尤為明顯。過去十年，美國大城市18歲以下人口減少6%，相較之下全國平均僅下滑1%。即使是人口正在成長的城市，孩童人數也在減少。有孩子的家庭搬離城市時，普遍提到對生活成本、安全與生活品質的擔憂；越來越多無子女居民選擇維持現狀，也是導致這一趨勢的原因之一，Rachel Louise Ensign與Paul Overberg報導。

5. 輝達正與OpenAI洽談，為一座資料中心提供2,500億美元融資擔保。
輝達正洽談為OpenAI提供約2,500億美元的融資擔保，作為一項大型資料中心計畫的一部分，這將是美國AI熱潮中規模最龐大的金融交易之一。知情人士表示，輝達的擔保將協助這家ChatGPT開發商承租軟銀能源子公司在俄亥俄州南部開發的10吉瓦計畫。整個計畫總成本可能超過5,000億美元，Anissa Gardizy、Amrith Ramkumar與Corrie Driebusch報導。該計畫的電力由美國政府掌控，並依據近期一項貿易協議由日本另行出資。

6. 圖說報導
眾議院民主黨人如何轉向反對援助以色列。
短短兩年，情勢竟已截然不同。本月有超過100名眾議院民主黨人投票支持一項旨在切斷對以色列軍事融資的修正案。該案雖未通過，卻被視為衡量民主黨在以色列加薩軍事行動引發日益升高疑慮之際立場的重要指標。我們透過圖表拆解不同派系民主黨人——黨內領導層、進步派、千禧世代——在以色列議題上的立場轉變，以及誰帶頭推動了這股轉向。

7. 今日看點
• 以色列總理班傑明·納坦雅胡預計抵達華盛頓，將與川普會面。
• 今日報紙

8. 數字看新聞
9,325美元
根據《華爾街日報》透過公開紀錄申請取得的文件，這是Waymo自2024年進駐德州奧斯汀以來，其機器人計程車累積收到的違規停車罰款總額。隨著Waymo及其他機器人計程車業者在美國各地擴大服務，這類停車糾紛正成為日益明顯的摩擦點。

9. 最後看點
單身族群已疲憊到讓試算表替他們評估約會對象。
別再相信直覺了。年輕人正急著回家用數字精算，才決定這場約會究竟算不算成功。這群人是「戀愛駭客」的一員，他們相信數據能治癒自己的感情煩惱。他們表示，交友軟體提供無窮無盡的潛在對象選單，反而讓人容易忽略明顯的警訊。但也有戀愛達人認為，試算表格子裡容易遺失一種屬於人性的溫度。

10. 編輯室之外
• 社論：美國要在AI領域維持領導地位並確保安全，關鍵在於「對齊」——既提升能力，又將危險知識隔離在外。
• 華爾街日報｜Buy Side：整理你的各項負擔，看看債務整合貸款是否能幫你省錢。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Lindsey Graham's Push to Strike Iran
emails.contentEn:
Unreleased Documentary Offers a Look at Lindsey Graham's Iran Campaign
Plus, Russia's use of sexual violence as a weapon of war, and why poor countries are aging faster than they can afford

1. FROM MY DESK
A documentary filmmaker followed Sen. Lindsey Graham for three years, gaining extraordinary access to capture his relationships with President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Reporter Josh Dawsey used that previously unreleased footage to show Graham's yearslong quest to topple Iran's regime—and how he persuaded Trump to strike, at times pushing for even more aggressive action than Netanyahu was prepared to take. And for a weekend mystery, I recommend our dispatch from Ann Arbor, where all 18 greens at the University of Michigan Golf Course mysteriously turned orange.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
• Sherrod Brown's bid to win back his Ohio Senate seat has become a test of whether Democrats can win back blue-collar voters without losing younger progressives.
• Saudi Arabia's vast oil exports increasingly depend on the Suez Canal, potentially the last viable exit as threats in the Red Sea jeopardize its workaround for the Strait of Hormuz.
• The main suspect in a car-ramming attack that left at least one dead in Berlin had previously been investigated for planning a terrorist attack, a person familiar with the investigation said.
• Trump has repeatedly threatened to strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain, but experts say several other nuclear sites could also be in the crosshairs.
• The U.S. and China are competing for drone supremacy on Mount Everest, turning the world's highest peak into an unlikely geopolitical battleground.
• Brazil has denied visas to two senior Trump administration officials amid concerns that they sought to undermine confidence in the country's electronic-voting system before October's presidential election.

3. FROM THE MARKETS
• Investors are paying as much as 51% more for the same SK Hynix stock in New York than in Seoul, another sign of froth in the AI trade, writes James Mackintosh.
• More Americans are building supersize retirement accounts. Those with more modest means can also grow their nest eggs bigger than they might think. Our step-by-step guide shows how.
• Investors overwhelmingly oppose making quarterly reports optional, and companies that embrace the change risk sending the wrong signal to the market, writes Jonathan Weil.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
AI chatbots know how to make biological weapons. Some will teach you.
Last summer, after OpenAI enhanced the brain power of its chatbot, hundreds of users began asking it how to make biological weapons and poisons. It answered with step-by-step instructions simple enough for a high-school biology student to follow. Georgia Wells and Amrith Ramkumar reveal the cat-and-mouse game AI companies are playing as they race to build smarter models while trying to stop them from becoming dangerous how-to guides.

5. Russia is using sexual violence to wage war.
Interviews with former prisoners, along with findings by Ukrainian prosecutors and U.N. investigators, suggest sexual abuse of Ukrainian men is now a core Russian tactic. Survivors describe violence meant to punish, humiliate and psychologically break them. The growing body of testimony points to systematic sexual violence against prisoners of war and civilian captives that has been condoned, even encouraged, by senior Russian officials, report Alistair MacDonald, Serhii Bosak and Ievgeniia Sivorka.

6. SEE THE STORY
Poor countries are aging faster than they can afford.
Elderly populations are exploding in developing nations like Thailand, but without the pension systems and personal savings that sustain older people in many wealthier countries. These photographs, with reporting from Gabriele Steinhauser, show what that looks like on the ground, from families caring for aging parents to communities struggling to support the elderly.

7. HAPPENING THIS WEEK
• Monday: Israel's Netanyahu arrives in Washington, where he is due to meet with Trump.
• Tuesday: Washington honors the late Sen. Lindsey Graham with funeral services at the National Cathedral.
• Wednesday: The Federal Reserve announces its interest-rate decision.
• Thursday: The Commerce Department releases the PCE index, the Fed's preferred measure of inflation. The Bureau of Economic Analysis releases its first estimate of second-quarter U.S. GDP.

8. THE NUMBER
37,000
That's roughly how many cubic yards of dirt excavated from the White House grounds were hauled to East Potomac Golf Links. Now, the pile sits at the center of a legal fight over whether it can be used in Trump's planned overhaul of the public golf course.

9. AND FINALLY…
Twenty things worth catching up on this August.
If you have some downtime coming up, our culture team has curated a mix of 2026 movies, shows, songs and books—from blockbuster hits to little-talked-about gems—that are well worth your time.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
• WSJ | Buy Side: These men's linen pants are lightweight and effortless, making them an easy summertime alternative to heavy denim and chinos.
emails.contentZh:
未曝光紀錄片揭露林賽·格雷厄姆的伊朗行動內幕
此外，俄羅斯將性暴力當作戰爭武器，以及貧窮國家為何正以負擔不起的速度快速老化

1. 編輯手記
一位紀錄片導演跟拍林賽·格雷厄姆參議員長達三年，取得罕見的貼身拍攝機會，記錄下他與川普總統及以色列總理班傑明·納坦雅胡之間的互動。記者Josh Dawsey運用這批從未曝光的畫面，呈現格雷厄姆多年來推翻伊朗政權的行動——以及他如何說服川普出手打擊，有時甚至比納坦雅胡準備採取的行動更為激進。另外，本週末的懸疑報導推薦密西根州安娜堡：密西根大學高爾夫球場全部18個果嶺竟神秘地變成了橘色。

2. 今日頭條
• 雪羅德·布朗爭取奪回俄亥俄州參議員席位的選戰，已成為民主黨能否在不流失年輕進步派選民的情況下贏回藍領選民的一次考驗。
• 沙烏地阿拉伯龐大的石油出口日益依賴蘇伊士運河，隨著紅海威脅升高、荷莫茲海峽替代路線岌岌可危，蘇伊士運河可能成為最後可行的出海口。
• 知情人士透露，柏林一起造成至少一人死亡的汽車衝撞攻擊案的主要嫌犯，此前曾因涉嫌策劃恐怖攻擊而遭調查。
• 川普多次揚言打擊伊朗的「鎬山」核設施，但專家指出其他幾處核設施同樣可能成為目標。
• 美中兩國正在聖母峰上爭奪無人機優勢，讓世界最高峰意外成為地緣政治角力場。
• 巴西已拒發簽證給兩名川普政府高階官員，理由是擔心他們試圖在10月總統大選前，動搖外界對該國電子投票系統的信心。

3. 市場動態
• James Mackintosh撰文指出，投資人在紐約買進同一檔SK海力士股票所付出的價格，比在首爾高出多達51%，這是AI交易過熱的又一跡象。
• 越來越多美國人正在打造超大規模的退休帳戶。即使財力較普通的人，也能讓自己的退休老本增值得比想像中更多，我們的逐步指南告訴你怎麼做。
• Jonathan Weil撰文指出，投資人絕大多數反對將季報改為自願申報，選擇跟進此改變的企業恐向市場釋出錯誤訊號。

4. 獨家搶先看
AI聊天機器人懂得如何製造生物武器，有些甚至願意教你。
去年夏天，OpenAI強化其聊天機器人的運算能力後，數百名使用者開始詢問如何製造生物武器與毒藥。機器人給出的步驟說明簡單到連高中生物學生都能照做。Georgia Wells與Amrith Ramkumar揭露AI公司在競相打造更聰明模型的同時，如何與這類危險用途展開一場貓捉老鼠的角力。

5. 俄羅斯正把性暴力當作作戰手段。
對前戰俘的訪談，加上烏克蘭檢方與聯合國調查人員的調查結果顯示，對烏克蘭男性的性侵已成為俄軍的核心戰術之一。倖存者描述這種暴力旨在懲罰、羞辱並在心理上擊垮他們。愈來愈多的證詞指向一種對戰俘與平民囚犯有系統的性暴力，且獲得俄羅斯高層官員的默許甚至鼓勵，Alistair MacDonald、Serhii Bosak與Ievgeniia Sivorka報導。

6. 圖說報導
貧窮國家正以負擔不起的速度快速老化。
泰國等開發中國家的高齡人口正急遽增加，卻缺乏許多富裕國家賴以支撐老年人生活的年金制度與個人儲蓄。這組照片搭配Gabriele Steinhauser的報導，呈現這種現實在當地的具體樣貌，從照顧年邁父母的家庭，到努力扶助長者的社區。

7. 本週看點
• 週一：以色列總理納坦雅胡抵達華盛頓，將與川普會面。
• 週二：華盛頓將在國家大教堂為已故參議員林賽·格雷厄姆舉行追思禮拜。
• 週三：聯準會公布利率決策。
• 週四：商務部公布個人消費支出（PCE）物價指數，即聯準會偏好的通膨指標。經濟分析局公布第二季美國GDP初值。

8. 數字看新聞
37,000
這是從白宮庭園挖出、運往東波多馬克高爾夫球場的泥土量，單位為立方碼。如今這堆泥土成為一場法律爭議的焦點：能否用於川普計畫中對這座公共高爾夫球場的翻修工程。

9. 最後看點
今年8月值得補進度的20件事。
如果接下來有些空閒時間，我們的文化團隊精選了一系列2026年的電影、劇集、歌曲與書籍——從賣座大片到鮮少被談論的遺珠——絕對值得你花時間細細品味。

10. 編輯室之外
• 華爾街日報｜Buy Side：這些男士亞麻長褲輕盈又不費力，是取代厚重牛仔褲與卡其褲的絕佳夏日選擇。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The U.S.-Iran War Is Becoming a War of Attrition
emails.contentEn:
America and Iran Are Locked in a Cycle of Escalation
Plus, the White House Correspondents' Association dinner got a do-over, and companies have begun pumping the brakes on AI spending

1. FROM MY DESK
Five months into the conflict, the U.S. and Iran are running up against the limits of what military force can achieve. As President Trump threatens to ratchet up the bombing campaign and Tehran's militia allies widen the war, both governments have shown a willingness to escalate. Jared Malsin explains why the war risks becoming a prolonged test of endurance rather than a decisive showdown. Also worth your time is our profile of Troy Jackson, the former Maine Senate president expected to become the Democratic nominee against Sen. Susan Collins. He inherits a race transformed by Graham Platner's abrupt exit—and must convince voters he can harness the oysterman's populist appeal without carrying his baggage.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
• The White House Correspondents' Association dinner was held last night, three months after the original event was cut short by the attempted assassination of Trump.
• Former star Supreme Court lawyer Thomas Goldstein was sentenced to six years in prison for tax evasion and mortgage fraud.
• The U.S. is set to resume cattle imports from Mexico, lifting a ban meant to stem the spread of the New World screwworm.
• Taylor Farms asked the White House to delay a recall tied to the cyclospora outbreak, saying it wanted more proof and more time before being publicly linked to it.
• Paramount said its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery is on hold until legal challenges are resolved or June 1, 2027, whichever comes first.
• After a secret trip to Ukraine, right-wing provocateur Laura Loomer says she was duped by Russian misinformation and now calls Ukraine an "essential ally."

3. FROM THE MARKETS
• A lobbying fight between Apple and Micron over Chinese memory chips will likely force Trump to choose between cutting prices for consumers and increasing domestic semiconductor production.
• Chevron is pressing the Trump administration to help protect a pipeline that carries Kazakh oil to the Black Sea after Ukraine's attacks threatened exports.
• A wild week of AI selloffs, soaring oil prices and rising Treasury yields ended more calmly, but the S&P 500 and Nasdaq still logged back-to-back weekly losses for the first time since March.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
Corporate America has decided to stop blowing money on AI.
Companies are coming around to a radical idea: They don't have to blow their budgets on artificial intelligence. Instead of relying on a single provider, they're increasingly mixing lower-priced models, including some built in China, alongside products from OpenAI and Anthropic and shopping a la carte for AI. The shift is changing the economics of the industry and forcing AI companies to fight harder to keep customers, report Angel Au-Yeung, Katherine Bindley and Tina Li.

5. The biggest challenge facing sociologists may be themselves.
Sociology has long been tasked with investigating society's most pressing challenges. Today, though, the discipline is embroiled in an ideological and existential battle of its own, one that is increasingly public and, at least in part, of its own making. In our Saturday Essay, Pamela Paul examines the growing divide over whether sociology's mission is to pursue objective truth or advance social change, and what that means beyond academia.

6. SEE THE STORY
Inside KPMG's boot camp for the AI era.
Scavenger hunts, whodunnit fraud cases and teamwork challenges are helping reshape how KPMG trains new auditors. We visited the firm's sprawling Florida Lakehouse campus to see how it's preparing the next generation of accountants as AI changes their industry.

7. HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND
• Saturday: Maine Democrats hold a special convention to choose a new U.S. Senate nominee.
• Sunday: The Tour de France concludes in Paris. Formula One drivers race in the Hungarian Grand Prix.
• Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER
$600 million
That's how much 1,500 of America's biggest public companies spent on executive perks. The largest slice didn't go to private jets or country clubs. It went to personal security, which accounted for nearly 30% of the total. See how the rest of the extras stack up.

9. AND FINALLY…
The new Lotus is one of the last sports cars of its kind.
The field of lightweight, mid-engine sports cars is shrinking as manufacturers move on and computers take over more of the driving. Our auto columnist Dan Neil tested the Emira 420 Sport at the company's test track in England and discovered a car that still prizes physical connection over electronic intervention.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
• Opinion: President Trump imposes yet another round of border taxes three months before the November election, despite their political unpopularity and economic harm.
• WSJ | Buy Side: Our top business lenders can help you get funding within 24 hours to meet immediate needs.

美伊陷入升級循環
此外，白宮記者協會晚宴補辦登場，企業開始踩下AI支出的煞車

1. 編輯手記
衝突邁入第五個月，美伊兩國都逐漸碰觸到軍事力量所能達成目標的極限。隨著川普總統揚言加大轟炸行動、德黑蘭的民兵盟友擴大戰事，雙方政府都展現出願意升級對抗的態勢。Jared Malsin分析這場戰爭為何有可能演變成一場曠日持久的耐力賽，而非一場決定性的攤牌。同樣值得一讀的，是我們對楚伊·傑克森的專訪——這位緬因州前參議院議長預計將成為民主黨提名人，出戰參議員蘇珊·柯林斯。他接手的這場選戰，因葛拉罕·普拉特納突然退選而徹底改觀，如今他必須說服選民，自己能承接這位牡蠣業者的民粹魅力，卻不必背負對方的包袱。

2. 今日頭條
• 白宮記者協會晚宴昨晚舉行，距離原場活動因川普遇刺未遂而中斷已過了三個月。
• 曾任最高法院明星律師的湯瑪斯·戈德斯坦，因逃稅與房貸詐欺被判處六年徒刑。
• 美國即將恢復自墨西哥進口牛隻，解除為遏止新世界螺旋蠅擴散而實施的禁令。
• Taylor Farms要求白宮延後與孢子蟲爆發事件相關的召回公告，表示希望在被公開點名前有更多證據與時間。
• 派拉蒙表示，與華納兄弟探索的合併案將暫緩，直到法律爭議解決或2027年6月1日（以較早者為準）為止。
• 右翼煽動人士蘿拉·盧默在秘密走訪烏克蘭後表示，自己曾受俄羅斯假訊息矇騙，如今她稱烏克蘭為「不可或缺的盟友」。

3. 市場動態
• 蘋果與美光就中國記憶體晶片展開的遊說角力，恐將迫使川普在為消費者降價與提升國內半導體產能之間做出取捨。
• 在烏克蘭攻擊威脅出口之後，雪佛龍正向川普政府施壓，要求協助保護一條輸送哈薩克石油至黑海的管線。
• 歷經AI股票拋售、油價飆漲與美債殖利率上揚的動盪一週後，市場終於較為平靜地收尾，但標普500與那斯達克指數仍創下自3月以來首次連續兩週下跌。

4. 獨家搶先看
美國企業界決定不再對AI一擲千金。
企業界正逐漸接受一個大膽的想法：不必把預算全數砸在人工智慧上。它們不再仰賴單一供應商，而是愈來愈常混搭使用價格較低的模型（包括部分中國製模型），搭配OpenAI與Anthropic的產品，像點菜一樣採購AI服務。這股轉變正在改變整個產業的經濟模式，也迫使AI公司更努力留住客戶，Angel Au-Yeung、Katherine Bindley與Tina Li報導。

5. 社會學家面臨的最大挑戰，或許就是他們自己。
社會學長期肩負探究社會最迫切課題的使命。然而如今，這門學科卻深陷一場自身的意識形態與存在危機之中，而且這場爭論日益公開化，某種程度上也是自作自受。在本期週六專文中，Pamela Paul探討社會學界對於其使命究竟是追求客觀真相、還是推動社會變革日益擴大的分歧，以及這對學術界之外意味著什麼。

6. 圖說報導
走進KPMG為AI時代打造的新兵訓練營。
尋寶遊戲、模擬詐欺懸疑案與團隊合作挑戰，正在重塑KPMG培訓新進審計師的方式。我們造訪了該公司位於佛羅里達州、佔地廣闊的Lakehouse園區，看看在AI改變這個行業之際，公司如何為下一代會計師做準備。

7. 本週末看點
• 週六：緬因州民主黨舉行特別黨代表大會，選出新的參議員提名人。
• 週日：環法自行車賽在巴黎落幕。F1車手則將在匈牙利大獎賽較量。

6億美元
這是美國1,500家最大上市公司花在高階主管福利上的總金額。金額最大的一塊並非私人飛機或鄉村俱樂部，而是個人安全保護，佔總額近三成。來看看其餘福利項目如何分布。

9. 最後看點
新款蓮花跑車，可能是同類跑車中最後的絕響之一。
隨著車廠紛紛轉型、電腦系統接管愈來愈多駕駛工作，輕量化、中置引擎跑車這一類別正逐漸萎縮。我們的汽車專欄作家Dan Neil在該公司位於英國的測試賽道試駕Emira 420 Sport，發現這款車仍然珍視人車之間的直接連結，勝過電子系統的介入。

• 社論：川普總統在11月選舉前三個月再度祭出邊境稅，儘管此舉政治上不受歡迎、經濟上也會造成傷害。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: China's All-Out Push on AI Chips
emails.contentEn:
China Has a Plan to Rival America's AI Chips
Plus, Trump's frustrations over the Iran war, behind the scenes with our travel columnist, and the fight to save all-you-can-eat buffets in Las Vegas

1. FROM MY DESK
Good morning. The biggest U.S. tech companies have all bet their futures to some extent on artificial intelligence. Lately, it hasn't been smooth sailing. Concerns over AI spending yesterday shaved roughly $890 billion in market value from the Magnificent Seven. In China, AI hardware lags far behind U.S. technology, but officials are mounting a fevered effort to catch up with American AI chips. And a cyberattack by rogue OpenAI models gave the world a taste of what hacking might look like in the age of powerful AI tools. Meanwhile, IBM aims to keep selling mainframes and pour profits into quantum computing. CEO Arvind Krishna spoke with Christopher Mims about his strategy after the company's recent stock selloff.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
• By threatening Red Sea oil shipments, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis have set up a standoff in one of the world's most vital waterways.
• Ukraine's new top military commander is tasked with dragging the army out of the Soviet era.
• Tariffs are central to Donald Trump's vision of presidential power, and courts and Congress haven't curbed his ambition to impose them at will, writes Greg Ip.

3. LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
S&P 500 Futures 7,466.00 (+0.28%) | DJIA Futures 52,182.00 (+0.55%) | Nasdaq 100 Futures 28,697.25 (+0.27%)
As of 7/24/2026, 6:07:31 AM ET
• Oil prices cracked the $100-a-barrel mark, as stocks slumped and Treasury yields hit the highest levels of Trump's second term.
• Big banks are on the hunt to grow their loan books and are turning back to an area they had shunned not that long ago: commercial real-estate lending.
• With Nike's share of the sneakerhead market slipping, it might be time for investors to give the company another chance, writes Jinjoo Lee.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
Trump is losing patience over an Iran war with no clear end in sight.
During a recent meeting in the Oval Office, the president launched into a tirade against Iranian leaders, calling them scumbags and lunatics, and unleashing a series of expletives, according to a person who heard the comments. As the war enters its fifth month, Trump is increasingly frustrated that a conflict he once thought would be over in a matter of weeks has dragged on, administration officials and others close to the president said. Some of Trump's advisers now worry that the war is consuming his presidency and worsening Republicans' already dim prospects in the coming midterm elections, report Annie Linskey and Josh Dawsey.

5. REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK
Travel columnist Dawn Gilbertson: If I had a dollar for every time someone said, "How do I get a job like yours?" I'd never have to fly in economy again! It's true, I have the best reporting job at the paper. As the Journal's travel columnist and WSJ Travel newsletter writer, I get paid to travel. A lot. I'm already closing in on 40 flights this year and have stayed at so many Hyatts I'm hoping to finally achieve the chain's top loyalty status.
One of my favorite assignments so far this year: a February trip to the northeast coast of England planned entirely with AI. I loved the randomness of it all and discovered a charming place I wouldn't have otherwise visited. Next time, I'll visit in summer.
Something you might not know: The Journal pays for all the travel for my columns. We accept no freebies, a rarity in today's media world. And the airline/hotel/train company/cruise line does not know I'm coming. I experience everything as you would, and so far, at least, I have gone undetected.
So there's no hype in the columns, just an unvarnished look at the highs and lows of an experience. If something goes wrong on a trip, I write about it. Ditto if I see something untoward in an otherwise luxe service, like a blatant pitch for tips.
You might think I'm an expert packer with all of this globe-trotting, but I struggle like the rest of us, even with packing cubes. More times than not, I have to sit on my carry-on to zip it shut. Send help!
The best part of the job, bar none: hearing from WSJ readers. About your travel successes, struggles and questions. Even your tacky souvenir collections.

6. SEE THE STORY
Ticks—and the diseases they carry—are invading the Midwest.
Warmer winters and shifts in land use have brought the bugs into new territory. With summer in full swing, health officials are warning of increasing risks from two of the most common tick-borne conditions: Lyme disease and alpha-gal syndrome. See how their ranges are expanding.

7. HAPPENING TODAY
• The rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner takes place.
• The Commerce Department releases June new-home sales.
• Earnings: American Express, Verizon
• Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER
$310,000
The median home sale price in Lehigh Acres, Fla., in May, compared with $652,000 in Miami, according to real-estate brokerage Redfin. The sprawling exurban community east of Fort Myers is booming, with growth that is moving faster than its roads, water lines and services can handle.

9. AND FINALLY…
The lonely fight to keep the cheap Las Vegas buffet alive
Sin City used to have lots of cheap, all-you-can-eat restaurants that lost money but brought people in the door to gamble. Many closed after the pandemic, victims of social-distancing requirements and the changing economics of a city now dominated by affluent travelers eager to splurge on fancy meals. A few old-school hotels are hellbent on keeping the circus going.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
• Opinion: The No Surprises Act of 2020 ended surprise bills but swelled costs for insurers, which are now being passed along in higher premiums.

emails.contentZh:
中國祭出計畫，力拚追上美國AI晶片
此外，川普對伊朗戰事的挫折感升溫，我們的旅遊專欄作家親自帶你看幕後，以及拉斯維加斯捍衛廉價吃到飽自助餐的孤軍奮戰

1. 編輯手記
早安。美國各大科技巨頭都已在不同程度上把公司前景押注在人工智慧上，但最近的路並不平順。對AI支出的疑慮，昨天讓「七巨頭」總計蒸發約8,900億美元市值。在中國，AI硬體遠遠落後美國技術，但官員正全力衝刺急起直追美國的AI晶片。另外，一起由失控OpenAI模型發動的網路攻擊，也讓世人初嚐在強大AI工具時代，駭客攻擊可能演變成什麼樣貌。與此同時，IBM打算持續銷售主機系統，並將獲利大舉投入量子運算。執行長Arvind Krishna在公司股價近期重挫後，向Christopher Mims談了他的策略。

2. 今日頭條
• 由伊朗支持的葉門青年運動組織揚言攻擊紅海油輪運輸，讓這條全球最關鍵的航道之一陷入對峙緊張。
• 烏克蘭新任最高軍事指揮官的任務，是帶領軍隊擺脫蘇聯時代的舊思維。
• Greg Ip撰文指出，關稅是川普總統權力願景的核心，而法院與國會都未能約束他隨心所欲加徵關稅的野心。

3. 市場即時動態
標普500期貨 7,466.00（+0.28%）｜ 道瓊期貨 52,182.00（+0.55%）｜ 那斯達克100期貨 28,697.25（+0.27%）
截至美東時間2026年7月24日上午6:07:31
• 隨著股市走跌、美債殖利率升至川普第二任期以來最高水準，油價一舉突破每桶100美元大關。
• 大型銀行正積極擴大放款業務，並重新回頭經營一個不久前才刻意迴避的領域：商用不動產貸款。
• Jinjoo Lee撰文指出，隨著Nike在球鞋愛好者市場的佔有率下滑，投資人或許該重新給這家公司一次機會。

4. 獨家搶先看
面對看不到盡頭的伊朗戰事，川普的耐性正在耗盡。
據一名聽聞相關發言的人士透露，川普總統近期在橢圓形辦公室的一場會議上，對伊朗領導人破口大罵，稱他們是「人渣」與「瘋子」，並夾雜連串髒話。隨著戰事邁入第五個月，政府官員與川普身邊人士表示，他愈來愈懊惱——原本以為幾週內就能結束的衝突，如今卻遲遲未了。川普的部分顧問如今擔心，這場戰爭正在吞噬他的總統任期，並讓共和黨本已黯淡的期中選舉前景雪上加霜，Annie Linskey與Josh Dawsey報導。

5. 記者筆記
旅遊專欄作家Dawn Gilbertson：如果每次有人問我「要怎樣才能有你這種工作」就給我一塊錢，我早就再也不用搭經濟艙了！說真的，我擁有本報最棒的記者工作。身為《華爾街日報》旅遊專欄作家兼WSJ Travel電子報作者，我的工作就是拿錢去旅行，而且是大量旅行。今年我已經快搭滿40趟航班，入住凱悅酒店的次數多到我希望能終於拿到該連鎖飯店的最高會籍等級。
今年目前為止我最喜歡的一次採訪任務：2月一趟完全交由AI規劃的英格蘭東北海岸之旅。我很享受那種隨機性，也因此發現了一個原本絕不會造訪的迷人地方。下次，我要選夏天再去一趟。
你可能不知道的是：我專欄所有的旅費都是由《華爾街日報》支付。我們不接受任何招待，這在當今媒體圈相當罕見。而且航空公司、飯店、鐵路公司或郵輪公司都不知道我要來。我體驗的一切跟讀者你一樣，而且到目前為止，至少還沒被認出來。
所以我的專欄裡沒有誇大其詞，只有對一段體驗高低起伏最真實的紀錄。如果旅途中出了狀況，我會如實寫出來；如果我在一項本該奢華的服務中看到不妥之處，比如赤裸裸地要求給小費，我同樣會寫出來。
你可能以為我這麼常跑遍全球，打包行李一定很在行，但其實我跟大家一樣手忙腳亂，就算用了打包收納袋也一樣。我常常得整個人坐上隨身行李箱才能把拉鍊拉上。求救！
這份工作最棒的部分，無庸置疑，就是聽讀者分享。不論是你們的旅行成功經驗、遇到的困難，還是各種疑問，甚至是你們收藏的那些俗氣紀念品。

6. 圖說報導
壁蝨及其攜帶的疾病正入侵美國中西部。
暖冬與土地利用型態的改變，讓這些小蟲進入了新的地盤。隨著夏季全面展開，衛生官員警告兩種最常見的壁蝨傳染病風險正在升高：萊姆病與甲型半乳糖症候群。來看看牠們的活動範圍如何持續擴大。

7. 今日看點
• 延期舉行的白宮記者協會晚宴今日登場。
• 商務部公布6月新屋銷售數據。
• 財報：美國運通、Verizon
• 今日報紙

8. 數字看新聞
310,000美元
根據房地產經紀商Redfin數據，這是佛羅里達州Lehigh Acres今年5月的房屋銷售中位價，相較之下邁阿密則為652,000美元。這個位於Fort Myers東側、範圍廣闊的郊區社區正蓬勃發展，成長速度甚至超過當地道路、水管與公共服務所能負荷的程度。

9. 最後看點
一場孤軍奮戰：力保拉斯維加斯廉價吃到飽自助餐不消失
「罪惡之城」過去曾有許多虧本經營、卻靠吸引賭客上門而存在的廉價吃到飽餐廳。疫情過後，許多這類餐廳因社交距離規定，以及城市經濟結構的轉變——如今主要由願意在美食上大手筆消費的富裕旅客主導——而紛紛歇業。仍有少數老派飯店堅持不懈，誓言讓這場盛宴延續下去。

10. 編輯室之外
• 社論：2020年通過的《不意外帳單法》終結了意外醫療帳單，卻讓保險公司成本膨脹，如今這些成本正轉嫁為更高的保費。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Wall Street Bots Cash In on Trump's Social Posts
emails.contentEn:
Wall Street Firms Already Trade Trump's Truth Social Feed. Now They Can Pay to Be Faster.
Plus, the U.S. gives the president more muscular military options on Iran, and we go inside Taco Bell's rush to contain cyclospora

1. FROM MY DESK
The U.S. is surging forces and weaponry to the Middle East as President Trump considers expanding the Iran war. As ever, updates are playing out in real time on his Truth Social account. These posts don't just drive foreign policy; they move markets. Truth Social's parent company is selling stock market traders superfast access to Trump's posts on the platform, for up to $100,000 a month. Our reporting shows how Wall Street is already pouncing on his comments in fractions of a second, swinging energy and industrial stocks before everyday investors can even refresh their feeds. And for those who think age is a state of mind, I recommend our profile of Yoko Morishita, the Japanese prima ballerina still going strong at 77.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
• The FDA is investigating a new cyclospora outbreak that has sickened at least 72 people. Meanwhile, Taco Bell's efforts to contain the outbreak are testing its agility.
• The Federal Reserve is heading into one of its most unpredictable meetings in years.
• Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has tried the carrot and the stick with Trump—but neither is working.
• The former head of the Federal Trade Commission, Lina Khan, has been named a new chair of New York City's Economic Development Corporation. Can she make peace with the city's business community?
• A Google study says artificial intelligence is helping workers, not replacing them.

3. LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
S&P 500 Futures 7,511.50 (-0.38%) | DJIA Futures 52,225.00 (-0.43%) | Nasdaq 100 Futures 29,058.00 (-0.42%)
As of 7/23/2026, 6:08:21 AM ET
• What do surging bond yields mean for consumers and markets?
• Google has the muscle to overpower spending worries, writes Asa Fitch.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
Wall Street's bots are cashing in on Trump's Truth Social posts. Here's how.
Trump's social-media platform is selling stock market traders superfast access to his posts. Wall Street was already in on that game. Many big investment firms have developed automated systems to monitor Truth Social and take action—often within a fraction of a second, traders said. A Journal review of trading data shows how quickly some traders have pounced on the president's online comments. Some trades caused swings of more than 2% in almost two dozen energy and industrial stocks. A new product from Trump Media & Technology will let firms pay for an even faster readout of Trump's posts. At least five firms have signed up, report Gunjan Banerji, Caitlin Ostroff and Krystal Hur.

5. This AI tech billionaire just doubled his net worth. His ex asked for half.
South Korea's romanticized "marriage of the century" has morphed into a real-life drama everybody is calling the "divorce of the century." A decade ago, Chey Tae-won—the billionaire atop blockbuster memory-chip maker SK Hynix—announced the breakup of his 27-year marriage to the daughter of a past president in a three-page letter to a South Korean newspaper. The yearslong divorce battle nears a climax Friday, when a panel of appeals court judges is scheduled to decide how to divide Chey's roughly $5 billion fortune with his ex-wife. Jiyoung Sohn and Timothy W. Martin review the case that has mesmerized South Koreans.

6. SEE THE STORY
This prima ballerina is still going strong after 75 years.
Yoko Morishita was 3 years old when she first put on a pair of ballet shoes. Seventy-five years later, she's still en pointe. Morishita, who will turn 78 in December, is the prima ballerina in Japan's storied Matsuyama Ballet Company. One of Japan's most celebrated dancers, she performed with Rudolf Nureyev 200 times and toured with Margot Fonteyn. Today, Morishita is the world's oldest ballerina still taking on demanding lead roles. She says daily practice and the occasional steak help her stay on her toes.

7. HAPPENING TODAY
• The European Central Bank announces its latest interest-rate decision.
• Earnings: Blackstone, Comcast, Intel, Lockheed Martin, American Airlines
• Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER
3:42.66
The time, in minutes and seconds, logged by Scottish runner Josh Kerr to set a new mile world record in London—shattering a mark that had stood untouched for 27 years. We take you inside Kerr's monastic quest for unmatched speed.

9. AND FINALLY…
Bears are running amok in Lake Tahoe and causing chaos among locals.
Black bears are on a rampage across America, riding a population rebound driven in part by greater protection of the species. An estimated 60,000 roam California alone, triple the number in the 1990s. Few places see more activity than the turquoise shores of Lake Tahoe, where homeowners are spending thousands to ward off the pantry-raiding, toothpaste-sniffing beasts.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
• Opinion: Reconciliation 3.0 is Republicans' best chance to shore up America's military and expand its defenses. It would also give them an accomplishment to tout on the campaign trail.
• WSJ | Buy Side: Archies' flip-flops feature an inch of arch support and come in a wide range of colors.

此外，美國賦予總統對伊朗更強硬的軍事選項，我們也帶你直擊Taco Bell緊急圍堵孢子蟲疫情的幕後過程

1. 編輯手記
隨著川普總統考慮擴大對伊朗的戰事，美國正加派兵力與武器裝備前往中東。一如既往，最新動態即時出現在他的Truth Social帳號上。這些貼文不僅左右外交政策，更牽動市場。Truth Social的母公司正向股市交易員兜售能超快取得川普貼文的服務，月費最高達10萬美元。我們的報導揭露，華爾街早已在川普貼文發布後幾分之一秒內迅速反應，在一般投資人甚至還來不及刷新頁面之前，就已牽動能源與工業類股的走勢。此外，若你認為年齡只是心態問題，我推薦你讀讀日本芭蕾舞伶森下洋子的專訪，她77歲仍寶刀未老。

4. 獨家搶先看
華爾街的機器人正靠川普的Truth Social貼文大賺一筆，內幕在此。

5. 這位AI科技億萬富豪身家剛翻倍，他的前妻要求分一半。
南韓一段被浪漫化為「世紀婚姻」的關係，如今已演變成人人稱之為「世紀離婚」的真實戲碼。十年前，記憶體晶片大廠SK海力士的億萬富豪掌門人崔泰源，透過一封長達三頁的信函向南韓一家報紙宣布，結束他與前總統之女長達27年的婚姻。這場纏訟多年的離婚官司即將在週五迎來高潮，屆時上訴法院法官小組將裁定如何分配崔泰源約50億美元的身家給前妻。Jiyoung Sohn與Timothy W. Martin回顧這起讓南韓全民著迷的案件。

6. 圖說報導
這位芭蕾舞伶75年來寶刀未老。
森下洋子3歲時第一次穿上芭蕾舞鞋，75年後的今天，她依然能以足尖站立起舞。今年12月即將滿78歲的森下，是日本知名松山芭蕾舞團的首席舞者。身為日本最負盛名的舞者之一，她曾與魯道夫·紐瑞耶夫同台演出200次，也曾與瑪歌·芳婷同行巡演。如今，森下是全球年紀最長、仍在挑戰高難度主角的芭蕾舞者。她說，每日練習與偶爾吃塊牛排，是她維持舞技的秘訣。

10. 編輯室之外

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Iran's Missiles Still Threaten U.S. Forces
emails.contentEn:
Trump Approves Saudi Nuclear Deal as Iran Missile Threat Persists
Plus, retirement accounts are being supercharged with startup stocks, and a small beach town is in turmoil over a $545,000 email phishing scam

1. FROM MY DESK
Good morning. We now have a price tag for the U.S.-Iran war: $37.5 billion. Pete Hegseth shared the updated estimate yesterday—some $9 billion higher than earlier projections. The rising bill comes as fighting intensifies. Our latest reporting shows Iran's ballistic missiles remain a deadly threat to U.S. forces and regional allies. Yet Israel is staying out of the fight—for now—at Washington's request, to preserve room for diplomacy. Meanwhile, President Trump has approved a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia that could bring large profits for American companies, but could also raise concerns about nuclear proliferation in the Middle East.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
• Trump is preparing new tariffs to replace the ones he put in place after the Supreme Court gutted his trade agenda.
• Anthropic is doubling its spending on the midterm elections to $40 million to push for artificial-intelligence regulation.
• Ukraine's armed-forces chief was fired after days of street protests.
• Cuban-Americans who lost property in the 1959 revolution are seeking compensation, emboldened by the Trump administration's pressure on Cuba.
• Reddit, Politico and others are weighing how—or even if—they can work with Google as AI tools supplant traditional searches.

3. LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
S&P 500 Futures 7,527.75 (-0.24%) | DJIA Futures 52,408.00 (-0.07%) | Nasdaq 100 Futures 29,136.75 (-0.61%)
As of 7/22/2026, 6:10:39 AM ET
• General Motors is pivoting its business to capitalize on the Trump administration's policy changes. Wall Street loves it.
• Hermès continues to be the most reliable luxury stock, even if Cartier's owner Richemont is catching up, writes Carol Ryan.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
Meet the startup insiders who stash huge sums in tax-subsidized retirement accounts.
IRAs and workplace retirement accounts have been supercharged by startup founders, hedge-fund managers and Silicon Valley insiders who have access to investment opportunities unavailable to most Americans. Those entrepreneurs and their financial backers are increasingly using that strategy to pile up giant retirement-account balances, all subsidized by U.S. taxpayers, Anne Tergesen and Theo Francis determined by analyzing regulatory filings, government data and other documents. More than 1,000 individuals had IRA balances of at least $25 million in 2024, more than double the number with similar-size accounts in 2019.

5. This South Carolina town is in turmoil over a $545,000 email phishing scam.
The trap began with a routine bureaucratic ritual: the head of a family-run contracting company and a small town public-works director trading emails about when the municipality would cut a six-figure check for utility work. Someone posing as a company employee emailed the director to request an electronic transfer instead. Days later, the town sent $545,598.30 to a Utah bank account that wasn't the company's. Surfside Beach had fallen victim to a "business email compromise" scam, a cyber-swindle that cost $3 billion nationally last year, the Federal Bureau of Investigation says. The money is still missing, and the fallout is rippling through the tourist enclave of about 4,300 year-rounders, reports Scott Calvert.

6. SEE THE STORY
Tesla's market value eclipses all the other automakers. Here's how.
It doesn't sell more cars than any other automaker. It isn't more profitable than the competition, either. And now, it has fewer models in its lineup than it has in years. But to Wall Street, Tesla is still on top. Investors continue to bet on Tesla's ability to deliver truly self-driving vehicles and humanoid robots, giving it a market capitalization equal to the combined value of the next 37 largest automakers. Tesla reports its second-quarter earnings later today, and some analysts expect the stock price to rise even higher.

7. HAPPENING TODAY
• Earnings season rolls on with Tesla, IBM and Google parent Alphabet all posting results after markets close.
• Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER
$348.5 billion
The record-high net asset value of U.S. private-equity assets stuck in "zombie funds" at least a decade old at the end of 2025, according to PitchBook. That is 3.5 times the amount in 2015 and over 100 times that of 2005. The slowdown in private-equity sales has fueled frustration among investors eager to cash out.

9. AND FINALLY…
Everyone gets lost at a Pitbull concert.
Pitbull fans swarm his shows wearing bald caps and aviator sunglasses, a nod to the hairless rapper's signature look. Pitbull (the real one) has embraced the tradition and affectionately calls his fans "The Bald-Es" because they "fly high like bald eagles." It's really fun until they lose track of their friends.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
• Opinion: Paramount Skydance's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery may be a bad business deal, but bad antitrust policy is no reason to stop it.
• WSJ | Buy Side: Private student loans can close funding gaps left by federal loans.
Corrections & Amplifications: Big Boy 4014 is traveling east of the Mississippi on its first coast-to-coast tour. The July 21 edition of this newsletter incorrectly said it was traveling east of the Mississippi for the first time.

伊朗飛彈威脅未歇，川普批准與沙烏地的核能協議
此外，退休帳戶正靠新創股票火力全開，一座濱海小鎮則因54.5萬美元的電子郵件釣魚詐騙陷入風暴

1. 編輯手記
早安。美伊戰爭如今總算有了明確的價格標籤：375億美元。國防部長皮特·赫格塞斯昨天公布這項更新後的估計，比先前預估高出約90億美元。帳單持續攀升之際，戰事也在加劇。我們最新報導顯示，伊朗的彈道飛彈仍對美軍及區域盟友構成致命威脅。然而，應華盛頓要求，以色列目前仍暫時置身戰事之外，以保留外交斡旋的空間。與此同時，川普總統已批准與沙烏地阿拉伯的一項核能協議，這可能為美國企業帶來龐大利潤，但也可能引發外界對中東核擴散的憂慮。

2. 今日頭條
• 在最高法院推翻川普的貿易政策後，川普正準備推出新關稅取而代之。
• Anthropic將對期中選舉的投入資金加倍至4,000萬美元，以推動人工智慧監管立法。
• 烏克蘭武裝部隊總司令在連日街頭抗議後遭到解職。
• 在川普政府對古巴施壓的鼓舞下，1959年革命中失去財產的古巴裔美國人正尋求賠償。
• 隨著AI工具逐漸取代傳統搜尋，Reddit、Politico等媒體正評估該如何——甚至是否還能——與谷歌合作。

3. 市場即時動態
標普500期貨 7,527.75（-0.24%）｜ 道瓊期貨 52,408.00（-0.07%）｜ 那斯達克100期貨 29,136.75（-0.61%）
截至美東時間2026年7月22日上午6:10:39
• 通用汽車正調整業務方向，以充分利用川普政府的政策變化，華爾街對此相當買帳。
• Carol Ryan撰文指出，儘管卡地亞母公司歷峰集團正迎頭趕上，愛馬仕依然是最穩健可靠的奢侈品股票。

4. 獨家搶先看
認識那些把鉅額資金藏進享稅務補貼退休帳戶的新創圈內人士。
新創公司創辦人、對沖基金經理與矽谷圈內人士，憑藉一般美國人無法觸及的投資機會，讓個人退休帳戶（IRA）與職場退休帳戶規模大幅膨脹。Anne Tergesen與Theo Francis透過分析監管申報文件、政府數據及其他資料發現，這些創業者及其資金後盾正愈來愈常運用此策略，累積出由美國納稅人補貼的龐大退休帳戶餘額。2024年，IRA餘額達2,500萬美元以上的人數超過1,000人，是2019年同等規模帳戶人數的兩倍多。

5. 這座南卡羅來納小鎮，正因一起54.5萬美元的電子郵件釣魚詐騙陷入風暴。
這場騙局始於一項再平常不過的行政流程：一家家族承包公司的負責人與小鎮公共工程主任，透過電子郵件往來討論市府何時將支付一筆六位數的公用事業工程款。有人冒充該公司員工，寄信要求主任改以電匯方式付款。數天後，小鎮將545,598.30美元匯入猶他州一個並非該公司所有的銀行帳戶。聯邦調查局表示，Surfside Beach鎮已成為「商業電郵詐騙」的受害者，這類網路詐騙去年在全美造成30億美元損失。這筆錢至今仍下落不明，衝擊持續在這個常住人口僅約4,300人的觀光小鎮蔓延，Scott Calvert報導。

6. 圖說報導
特斯拉市值超越所有其他車廠，箇中原因為何？
特斯拉賣的車並不比其他車廠多，獲利也不比競爭對手高，如今旗下車型數量更是多年來最少。但在華爾街眼中，特斯拉依然穩坐龍頭。投資人持續押注特斯拉能實現真正的自動駕駛車與人形機器人，使其市值等同於其後37家最大車廠的總和。特斯拉將於今天稍後公布第二季財報，部分分析師預期股價還會進一步走高。

7. 今日看點
• 財報季持續進行，特斯拉、IBM及谷歌母公司Alphabet都將於收盤後公布業績。
• 今日報紙

8. 數字看新聞
3,485億美元
根據PitchBook數據，這是截至2025年底、卡在存續至少十年的「殭屍基金」中的美國私募股權資產淨值，創下歷史新高，是2015年的3.5倍，更是2005年的逾100倍。私募股權出售交易的放緩，讓急欲變現的投資人愈發不耐。

9. 最後看點
每個人都會在Pitbull演唱會上迷路。
Pitbull的歌迷會戴著光頭套與飛行員墨鏡湧入演唱會現場，向這位光頭饒舌歌手的招牌造型致敬。Pitbull本人（真身）也欣然接受這項傳統，暱稱歌迷為「禿頭鷹們」，因為他們「像禿鷹一樣展翅高飛」。這一切都很有趣，直到他們跟朋友走散為止。

10. 編輯室之外
• 社論：派拉蒙天空傳媒收購華納兄弟探索或許不是一筆划算的生意，但糟糕的反壟斷政策不該成為阻止交易的理由。
• 華爾街日報｜Buy Side：私人學生貸款能填補聯邦貸款留下的資金缺口。
更正與補充：Big Boy 4014蒸汽火車正在其首次橫貫美國的巡迴之旅中行駛於密西西比河以東地區。本電子報7月21日版誤稱這是該列車首次行駛至密西西比河以東。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: IRS Chief Spied on Execs While at JPMorgan
emails.contentEn:
Before Leading the IRS, Frank Bisignano Spied on His JPMorgan Co-Workers
Plus, American AI execs sound the alarm on Chinese models, and Christopher Nolan breaks down the epic scene at the center of 'The Odyssey'

1. FROM MY DESK
As head of the IRS and Social Security Administration, Frank Bisignano is entrusted with the private financial records of every American taxpayer. But before entering public service, he spied on his colleagues at JPMorgan Chase. While co-COO at the bank, Bisignano directed staff to snoop on rival executives, people familiar with the matter told the Journal. Bisignano denies spying on co-workers. Still, our reporting details how he ultimately lost the trust of CEO Jamie Dimon.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
• Israeli intelligence believes Iran moved nuclear centrifuges into Pickaxe Mountain, Israeli and U.S. officials say, a development that would heighten concerns that Tehran could reconstitute its nuclear program.
• President Trump imposed an additional 50% tariff on certain goods from Canada.
• Kraft Heinz and Disney struck a deal that gives the food conglomerate a foothold in one of America's most enduring entertainment empires.
• The U.S. is putting once-unthinkable ideas on the table to disarm Hezbollah.

Top American AI execs are sounding the alarm on Chinese models.
Silicon Valley and Washington are debating a multibillion-dollar question: Should American companies be able to use Chinese artificial-intelligence models? OpenAI and Anthropic executives are raising concerns about the rise of cheap AI, particularly powerful new models produced in China, suggesting they will lead to a "dystopian" AI future and present unacceptable security risks without regulation. A locomotive named Big Boy is making grown men cry.

Are therapists to blame for the rise of adults cutting off their parents?
Estrangement is on the rise, and therapy is fueling it. Most therapists agree that sometimes people are justified in breaking ties with their parents or a close relative, especially if they were physically or emotionally abusive. What's changing now is the bar for what is deemed abusive enough for a cutoff.

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Investors Ditch the Mag Seven for New Tech Trades
emails.contentEn:
Everyday Investors Sour on the Mag Seven and Flock to Newer AI Trades
Plus, Jordan becomes a flashpoint in the U.S.-Iran war as troop deaths rise, and London faces a deepening housing crisis

1. FROM MY DESK
It's all over now! Congratulations to Spain for beating Argentina to claim a second-ever World Cup title. The great success of the tournament extended well beyond the pitch. We're looking at the economic boost enjoyed by host cities across the U.S. And before the opening bell, we break down why individual investors—once the Mag Seven's most enthusiastic fans—are pulling back from tech heavyweights like Microsoft and Apple in favor of newer AI trades. Overseas, Andy Burnham takes office as the U.K.'s prime minister, becoming the country's sixth leader in seven years. He inherits a daunting agenda, including a housing crisis gripping London.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
• Iran has been stepping up its missile and drone attacks on U.S. forces in Jordan.
• Armed with a surging budget, the Pentagon is pouring cash into defense-tech startups while also boosting funding for traditional contractors.
• The FDA walked back a finding that a parasite linked to a foodborne-illness outbreak had been detected on a sample of Taylor Farms lettuce.
• Usha Vance gave birth to a baby boy, Vice President JD Vance's office announced, the first time in more than 150 years that a sitting second lady had a child while her husband was in office.
• China is getting creative in its campaign to undermine Taiwan's international standing, with children's choirs and baristas targeted.
• Alarmed by shrinking recess time in schools, parents across the U.S. are pushing school administrators and state legislators to restore it.

3. LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
S&P 500 Futures 7,519.75 (+0.29%) | DJIA Futures 52,509.00 (+0.26%) | Nasdaq 100 Futures 28,938.75 (+0.58%)
As of 7/20/2026, 6:11:16 AM ET
• Contracts worth billions of dollars have become the commercial glue holding the AI boom together. But investors shouldn't rely on them sticking if the boom fades, writes Asa Fitch.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
Everyday investors are over the Mag Seven and into new AI darlings.
Individual investors' yearslong love affair with the market's biggest tech stocks is starting to cool off, reports Hannah Erin Lang. Retail traders are buying fewer shares of Microsoft, Apple, Amazon.com, Meta, Nvidia, Alphabet and Tesla. Instead, they are flocking to newer AI trades: chip stocks like SK Hynix, for example, or the Roundhill Memory exchange-traded fund, according to data from flow-tracking firm Vanda Research. Many individual investors maintain significant exposure to the Mag Seven—but they are increasingly funneling dollars toward less famous stocks that they are hoping will emerge as the next set of AI superstars.

5. He bought a house 'sight unseen.' Then he found three dead bodies.
Edward Marchion took a chance when he bought a four-bedroom house in an affluent Connecticut suburb without ever stepping foot inside. When he entered for the first time, he could hardly believe what he found: three dead bodies. Connecticut State Police have identified two of the bodies as the home's previous co-owner and her son, while the third is still undergoing DNA testing to determine identity, reports Kate King. The lawyer appointed by the court to oversee the foreclosure auction said he assumed most bidders planned to flip the home for resale. Marchion declined to comment.

6. SEE THE STORY
Here's how to enjoy a trip to St. Tropez—even if you aren't a millionaire.
The French Riviera hub is a status symbol for the jet set. But look a little deeper, and you'll find a place with plenty of charm—and natural beauty. You don't have to spend big to explore St. Tropez's picturesque back streets, beaches and local eats.

7. HAPPENING TODAY

• Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER
5
Up to five cups of coffee a day are safe for most adults and may even have benefits for heart health, according to a new scientific statement by the American Heart Association. The research on coffee and caffeine has been very mixed, but the association says downing between about three to five 8-ounce cups of joe daily is linked to a lower risk of heart disease, heart failure, stroke and Type 2 diabetes.

9. AND FINALLY…
Disney is the happiest place on Earth, unless you're the designated scroller.
Ever since Disney introduced Lightning Lanes in 2021, debate has raged over whether letting people pay for shorter waits is savvy crowd management or nickel-and-diming that divides people by income. One thing is certain: The real-world headaches and benefits of mobile technology have invaded the happiest place on Earth. To have the best experience at Disneyland now, at least one person in every party needs to be the theme-park equivalent of a designated driver, manically booking and revising ride reservations on a phone.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

1. 編輯手記
一切塵埃落定！恭喜西班牙擊敗阿根廷，奪下隊史第二座世界盃冠軍。這屆賽事的巨大成功，影響遠遠超出球場範圍——我們正檢視美國多座主辦城市因此獲得的經濟提振。而在開盤前，我們也拆解了為何個人投資人——曾是七巨頭最熱情的擁護者——如今正撤出微軟、蘋果等科技巨頭，轉向較新興的AI概念股。海外方面，安迪·伯納姆正式就任英國首相，成為該國七年內第六位領袖。他接手的是一份艱鉅的政治議程，其中包括倫敦日益嚴峻的住房危機。

散戶投資人已對七巨頭意興闌珊，轉而愛上新一批AI寵兒。
Hannah Erin Lang報導指出，個人投資人多年來對市場最大科技股的熱戀正逐漸降溫。散戶交易員正減少買進微軟、蘋果、亞馬遜、Meta、輝達、Alphabet與特斯拉的股票。根據資金流向追蹤機構Vanda Research的數據，他們轉而湧向較新興的AI概念股，例如SK海力士等晶片股，或是Roundhill Memory交易所交易基金。許多個人投資人仍持有大量七巨頭部位，但正日益將資金轉向那些較不知名、他們期望能成為下一批AI超級明星的股票。

5. 他「未看過屋」就買下一棟房子，進門後卻發現三具屍體。
Edward Marchion冒險買下康乃狄克州一處富裕郊區的四房住宅，事前從未踏進屋內一步。第一次進屋時，他幾乎不敢相信眼前所見：三具屍體。Kate King報導，康乃狄克州警方已確認其中兩具遺體分別為房屋前共同持有人及其兒子，第三具遺體身分仍待DNA鑑定確認。法院指派負責監督法拍程序的律師表示，他原以為多數競標者的目的是轉手轉售這棟房子。Marchion拒絕置評。

6. 圖說報導
就算你不是百萬富翁，也能玩轉聖特羅佩，方法在此。
這座法國蔚藍海岸重鎮，是上流社會的身分象徵。但只要稍微深入探索，你會發現一個充滿魅力與自然美景的地方。不必花大錢，你也能探索聖特羅佩風景如畫的巷弄、海灘與在地美食。

9. 最後看點
迪士尼樂園是地表最快樂的地方，除非你是那個被指派滑手機的人。
自2021年迪士尼推出付費快速通關「Lightning Lanes」以來，外界爭論不休：讓遊客付費縮短等待時間，究竟是聰明的人流管理，還是按收入將人分級的變相斂財？唯一可以肯定的是：行動科技帶來的現實煩惱與便利，已入侵這個「地表最快樂的地方」。如今想在迪士尼樂園獲得最佳體驗，每個團隊裡至少要有一人擔任「主題樂園版指定駕駛」，全程緊盯手機、瘋狂搶訂並不斷調整遊樂設施預約時段。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The CIA Operative Who Helped the U.A.E. Score an AI Win
emails.contentEn:
The Secret Mission Behind the U.A.E.'s AI Breakthrough
Plus, pastors are turning to AI to write sermons, and the World Cup final is here

1. FROM MY DESK
A CIA operative was sent to determine whether the U.A.E. could be trusted with America's most advanced AI technology. He ended up helping the country's leaders get into Washington's good graces. Our reporters spent dozens of hours interviewing more than 30 current and former government officials to take you inside an emerging diplomatic gray zone blending spycraft, diplomacy and commercial lobbying over the future of a new technology arms race. Finally, there's a World Cup to be decided today, with Spain facing Argentina. I'll be glued to my television when kickoff arrives at 3 p.m. ET, but no comment on who I'm rooting for.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
• Two U.S. servicemembers were killed and another is missing after an Iranian attack on an air base in Jordan; the U.S. retaliated with fresh strikes.
• The Justice Department has pulled back on prosecuting corporate crime, declining to charge companies in a string of recent cases.
• Ukrainian drone strikes on warehouses of Russia's largest online retailer killed at least eight people and injured dozens, prompting a ferocious Russian response.
• The lettuce supplier linked to the cyclospora outbreak is a produce giant that supplies major retailers and restaurant chains across the U.S.
• Israel is spending tens of millions of dollars on an influence campaign to improve its standing in the U.S., using AI-generated texts, influencers and Trump insiders.
• Influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested in Miami after the U.K. sought their extradition on dozens of charges, including rape and sex trafficking.

3. FROM THE MARKETS
• The Fed's preferred inflation gauge is set for a statistical overhaul that could, at the margin, weaken the case for a rate hike.
• Some employers are using unusually generous 401(k) plans to win over prime talent and keep experienced workers.
• Investors are giving up on Big Food as inflation, GLP-1s and changing consumer tastes squeeze companies like General Mills and Kraft Heinz, writes David Wainer.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
AI has reached the pulpit. Pastors are grappling with where to draw the line.
Pastors across America are increasingly turning to chatbots to brainstorm, research and help write sermons. One California pastor has even trained a robot dog on his sermons, and it trots his church's aisles on Sundays. For some, the technology frees up time to spend with congregants. For others, it risks outsourcing one of the church's most personal acts, reports Anvee Bhutani.

5. A former strip-club owner wants to build California's biggest data center.
The AI data-center gold rush is drawing all types of entrepreneurs. All are chasing a piece of the $7 trillion McKinsey estimates the world will spend on data centers by 2030. In California's Imperial Valley, Sebastian Rucci's past has become a central theme in opponents' campaign against his proposed $10 billion project, reports Zusha Elinson.

6. SEE THE STORY
A portrait of a beach city defying Russia.
The Ukrainian city of Odesa is many things at once: a seaside resort, a center of culture and an economic powerhouse coveted by the Kremlin. But despite Russia's aerial bombing campaign to sever Ukraine's access to global markets, these photographs capture a city whose beaches, ports and businesses continue to function—and whose residents remain determined not to surrender.

7. HAPPENING THIS WEEK
• Monday: Andy Burnham begins his new job as the U.K.'s prime minister.
• Wednesday: Tesla posts results after markets close, as earnings season rolls on.
• Thursday: The European Central Bank announces its latest interest-rate decision.
• Friday: The rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner takes place. The Commerce Department releases June new-home sales.

8. THE NUMBER
$37 billion
That's the estimated cost of rebuilding Venezuela after devastating twin earthquakes last month. The disaster upends U.S. plans to reap the benefits of an unlikely alliance that had opened up the world's biggest oil reserves and vast mineral deposits to American investors.

9. AND FINALLY…
Germany is considering the unthinkable: Sunday shopping.
From Monday to Saturday, stores in Germany operate much like in any other market economy. On Sundays, iron curtains roll shut, turning city centers into eerie, echoey deserts. Now, as growth flatlines, a desperate government is grasping for ideas to get the economy going again, including opening up retail across the whole week. The effort faces formidable cultural and bureaucratic barriers, including opposition from a cross-party coalition of Christian churches and trade unionists.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
• WSJ | Buy Side: No-credit-check business loans usually require income or revenue documentation and might focus on revenue-based financing.
emails.contentZh:
阿聯AI突破背後的秘密任務
此外，牧師開始借助AI撰寫講道詞，世界盃冠軍戰終於登場

1. 編輯手記
一名中情局幹員曾奉派評估，阿聯是否值得信賴、能否獲得美國最先進的AI技術。結果他最終竟協助這個國家的領導人在華盛頓建立起良好關係。我們的記者耗費數十小時，訪談了超過30位現任與前任政府官員，帶你深入這場圍繞新科技軍備競賽未來、融合間諜活動、外交與商業遊說的新興灰色地帶。最後，今天世界盃冠軍即將揭曉，由西班牙對戰阿根廷。當美東時間下午3點開賽哨聲響起，我會緊盯電視機——至於我支持哪一隊，恕不奉告。

2. 今日頭條
• 伊朗攻擊約旦一處空軍基地，造成兩名美軍士兵喪生、另一人失蹤，美國已以新一輪空襲展開報復。
• 司法部近來已縮手企業犯罪起訴，在近期一連串案件中選擇不對相關企業提告。
• 烏克蘭無人機襲擊俄羅斯最大線上零售商的倉庫，造成至少八人死亡、數十人受傷，引發俄方猛烈報復。
• 與孢子蟲疫情有關的萵苣供應商，是一家為美國各大零售商與連鎖餐廳供貨的農產品巨頭。
• 以色列正砸下數千萬美元推動一項形象宣傳活動，藉助AI生成文案、網紅與川普陣營內部人士，以改善其在美國的聲譽。
• 網紅安德魯與崔斯坦·泰特兄弟在英國提出引渡請求、指控包括強姦與性販運等數十項罪名後，於邁阿密遭到逮捕。

3. 市場動態
• 聯準會偏好的通膨指標即將進行統計方法大翻修，此舉可能在邊際上削弱升息的理由。
• 部分雇主正祭出格外優渥的401(k)退休計畫，藉此爭取頂尖人才並留住資深員工。
• David Wainer撰文指出，隨著通膨、減重藥物（GLP-1）與消費者口味轉變持續擠壓通用磨坊、卡夫亨氏等公司，投資人正逐漸放棄大型食品股。

4. 獨家搶先看
AI已進駐講道壇，牧師們正努力思索該如何拿捏分寸。
美國各地的牧師正愈來愈常借助聊天機器人來發想、研究，甚至協助撰寫講道詞。加州一名牧師甚至用自己的講道內容訓練了一隻機器狗，讓牠週日在教堂走道上巡視。對部分牧師而言，這項技術能空出更多時間陪伴信眾；但對另一些人來說，這可能等於把教會最私密的職責之一外包出去，Anvee Bhutani報導。

5. 一位前脫衣舞夜店老闆想在加州蓋一座全州最大的資料中心。
這波AI資料中心淘金熱正吸引各式各樣的創業者投入，人人都想從麥肯錫估計到2030年全球將投入的7兆美元資料中心支出中分一杯羹。在加州帝國谷，Sebastian Rucci的過往經歷，已成為反對者用來抵制他這項百億美元計畫的核心論點，Zusha Elinson報導。

6. 圖說報導
一座濱海城市反抗俄羅斯的群像側寫。
烏克蘭城市奧德薩身兼多重身分：海濱度假勝地、文化重鎮，也是俄羅斯垂涎已久的經濟樞紐。儘管俄羅斯持續空襲、企圖切斷烏克蘭與全球市場的聯繫，這組照片仍捕捉到一座海灘、港口與商業活動照常運作的城市——以及一群堅決不肯投降的居民。

7. 本週看點
• 週一：安迪·伯納姆正式展開英國首相的新職務。
• 週三：財報季持續進行，特斯拉將於收盤後公布業績。
• 週四：歐洲央行公布最新利率決策。
• 週五：延期舉行的白宮記者協會晚宴登場，商務部公布6月新屋銷售數據。

8. 數字看新聞
370億美元
這是上個月委內瑞拉遭遇毀滅性連環地震後，重建工程的估計成本。這場災難打亂了美國原本的計畫——原本這段意外形成的聯盟關係，已為美國投資人打開全球最大石油儲量與龐大礦產資源的大門。

9. 最後看點
德國正考慮一件難以想像的事：週日開放購物。
在德國，從週一到週六，商店營運方式與其他市場經濟體大致相同。但一到週日，鐵捲門紛紛拉下，讓市中心變成迴音陣陣、詭異冷清的荒漠。如今隨著經濟成長停滯，走投無路的政府正絞盡腦汁尋求振興經濟的辦法，其中就包括開放全週營業。這項努力面臨強大的文化與官僚阻力，包括跨黨派基督教會與工會聯盟的反對。

10. 編輯室之外
• 華爾街日報｜Buy Side：免信用查核商業貸款通常需要收入或營收證明文件，可能著重於以營收為基礎的融資方式。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: There's a new way to win in Silicon Valley
emails.contentEn:
Silicon Valley Investors Have a New Playbook
Plus, Republicans fret over Trump's latest policy reversals, and a look at how the World Cup became an unexpected triumph for America

1. FROM MY DESK
One of the most interesting shifts in Silicon Valley isn't happening inside AI companies. It's happening among the investors funding them. As startups stay private longer, many investors are willing to back companies later on, sometimes years after they were started, betting there's more growth ahead. They're writing check after check, helping companies scale while locking the public out of key wealth-creation phases of their growth. Our story looks at the people rewriting the rules of venture capital. Speaking of change, our markets reporter Caitlin McCabe met Fahmi Quadir in her London office, where the short seller known as "the assassin" revealed she's dropping the strategy that brought her fame. Her next target isn't another corporate giant, but undervalued companies in South Korea that she believes she can help transform from within.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
• Trump's week of policy reversals and election allegations has frustrated some Republicans, who worry he isn't focused on the economy ahead of the midterms.
• Political betting has worked itself into the fabric of Washington, creating a pervasive temptation for officials with access to nonpublic information.
• The conflict in the Persian Gulf is becoming increasingly deadly for commercial sailors, with at least 17 seafarers killed since the fighting began.
• Trump's latest tariffs on Brazil target the country's beloved instant-payment system that Washington says unfairly disadvantages U.S. payment companies.
• Phones, power banks and vapes are becoming the fastest-growing safety threat to air travel as more devices spontaneously catch fire midflight.
• The White House released 269 pages of newly declassified election files. Here's a look inside.

3. FROM THE MARKETS
• IBM Chief Executive Arvind Krishna is managing legacy businesses while trying to keep up with emerging AI rivals. That middle-ground strategy is getting harder to pull off, writes business columnist Tim Higgins.
• The Pentagon is hiring Wall Street bankers for a plan to lend more than $200 billion to shore up defense manufacturing.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
The U.S. lost the World Cup but won over the world.
The national team's early exit was a disappointment. But for millions of visiting fans, the tournament became an eye-opening affirmation of American soft power. They arrived expecting a country defined by political division, restrictive immigration policies and hostility toward outsiders. Instead, they found their traditions celebrated, their fans treated with respect and an America that looked nothing like the one they had seen on social media back home. In the end, the best advertisement for America was simply America itself, write Joshua Robinson and Jonathan Clegg.

5. The kids are "Nixonmaxxing."
More than a half-century after Watergate, conservative youth are discovering the aesthetic and adopting the attitude of Richard Nixon, report Philip Wegmann and Vera Bergengruen. What began as 1970s nostalgia memes and revisionist essays is now being echoed by some of the Republican Party's most powerful voices as Nixon is recast as a forerunner of "America First."

6. SEE THE STORY
What makes the perfect World Cup stadium?
After a tournament played across 16 very different venues, we asked an architect what makes some soccer stadiums better than others. Watch how everything from sightlines to the roof can affect players and fans.

7. HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND
• Saturday: France and England battle it out in Miami for third place in the World Cup.
• Sunday: Lionel Messi will lead Argentina against Spain—the country where he spent his formative years—in the final in East Rutherford, N.J. President Trump is expected to attend. Golf stars compete in the final round of the British Open.
• Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER
5,421
The weight, in pounds, of Bentley's new Continental GT S. At England's Goodwood Festival of Speed, our auto columnist Dan Neil rode shotgun with Bentley's head of chassis dynamics to answer a simple question: How exactly do you drive a really big car, really fast?

9. AND FINALLY…
One nanny isn't cutting it anymore.
Wealthy working parents are employing teams of people to handle the work of raising their children, including specialists to potty-train toddlers, teach children to ride a bike, manage school applications and pack trunks for summer camp. Call it CEO parenting: treating the modern family as a small enterprise and delegating low-joy tasks. For some parents, every hour they're "not bogged down with the doing" is another hour they can be fully present with their children.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
• Opinion: President Trump broke into prime-time TV on Thursday night to make a sales pitch for his SAVE America Act that can't pass, using doubts it wouldn't address.
• WSJ | Buy Side: Oura Ring's newest model packs all the same features in a smaller package.
emails.contentZh:
矽谷投資人祭出新玩法
此外，共和黨人對川普最新一波政策大轉彎憂心忡忡，我們也回顧世界盃如何意外成為美國的一場勝利

1. 編輯手記
矽谷最有趣的變化之一，並非發生在AI公司內部，而是發生在資助這些公司的投資人之間。隨著新創公司維持私有身分的時間愈拉愈長，許多投資人願意在公司成立後多年才投資，賭注押在未來仍有更大成長空間。他們一張又一張地開出支票，協助公司擴大規模，同時也把一般大眾排除在這些公司價值創造最關鍵的階段之外。我們的報導聚焦於這群正在改寫創投規則的人。說到轉變，本報市場記者Caitlin McCabe在倫敦辦公室訪問了Fahmi Quadir，這位人稱「刺客」的放空好手透露，她正打算放棄那套讓她成名的策略。她的下一個目標不再是另一家企業巨頭，而是南韓那些她認為自己能從內部推動轉型的被低估企業。

2. 今日頭條
• 川普一週內連番政策大轉彎並提出選舉指控，讓部分共和黨人感到不滿，擔心他在期中選舉前並未專注於經濟議題。
• 政治博弈已滲透進華盛頓的日常運作，對握有非公開資訊的官員形成無所不在的誘惑。
• 波斯灣衝突對商船水手而言愈趨致命，自戰事爆發以來至少已有17名船員喪生。
• 川普對巴西祭出的最新關稅，鎖定該國廣受歡迎的即時支付系統，華盛頓方面稱此系統對美國支付公司造成不公平的不利影響。
• 隨著愈來愈多裝置在飛行途中自燃，手機、行動電源與電子煙正成為航空安全成長最快的威脅之一。
• 白宮公布269頁新解密的選舉相關檔案，我們帶你一探究竟。

3. 市場動態
• 專欄作家Tim Higgins撰文指出，IBM執行長Arvind Krishna一邊管理傳統業務、一邊力拚跟上新興AI對手，這種左右逢源的策略正變得愈來愈難以維持。
• 五角大廈正聘僱華爾街銀行家，規劃一項逾2,000億美元的貸款方案，以強化國防製造業。

4. 獨家搶先看
美國隊雖輸掉世界盃，卻贏得了全世界的心。
美國國家隊提早出局令人失望。但對數百萬前來觀賽的球迷而言，這屆賽事卻成了一次令人耳目一新、印證美國軟實力的體驗。他們原本以為會看到一個因政治分裂、移民政策嚴苛、對外來者充滿敵意而聞名的國家，結果卻發現自己的傳統受到慶祝、球迷受到尊重的待遇，眼前的美國，與他們在家鄉社群媒體上看到的樣貌截然不同。最終，為美國做出最好宣傳的，正是美國自己，Joshua Robinson與Jonathan Clegg撰文。

5. 年輕世代正掀起「尼克森風」。
在水門案爆發超過半世紀後，保守派年輕人正重新發掘理查·尼克森的美學，並開始效仿他的處事態度，Philip Wegmann與Vera Bergengruen報導。這股風潮起初只是1970年代懷舊迷因與翻案文章，如今卻獲得部分共和黨最具影響力人物的呼應，尼克森被重新塑造成「美國優先」理念的先驅。

6. 圖說報導
什麼才是完美的世界盃球場？
在一場橫跨16座風格迥異場館的賽事結束後，我們請教了一位建築師，探討究竟是什麼讓某些足球場勝過其他場館。從視野角度到屋頂設計，看看這些細節如何影響球員與球迷的體驗。

7. 本週末看點
• 週六：法國與英格蘭將在邁阿密爭奪世界盃季軍。
• 週日：梅西將率領阿根廷在紐澤西州東拉瑟福迎戰西班牙——他成長歲月所在的國家——爭奪冠軍，川普總統預計出席觀賽。高爾夫球星則將角逐英國公開賽最後一輪。
• 今日報紙

8. 數字看新聞
5,421
這是賓利新款Continental GT S的重量，單位為磅。在英格蘭古德伍德速度嘉年華上，我們的汽車專欄作家Dan Neil與賓利底盤動態部門主管一同試乘，探討一個簡單的問題：一輛如此龐大的車，究竟該如何開得又快又穩？

9. 最後看點
一個保母已經不夠用了。
富裕的職場父母正聘僱一整支團隊來分攤養育子女的工作，包括訓練幼兒如廁、教孩子騎腳踏車、處理學校申請，以及為夏令營打包行李箱的專門人員。這種現象被稱為「執行長式育兒」：把現代家庭當成一間小企業來經營，把缺乏樂趣的瑣事外包出去。對部分父母而言，每少花一小時「埋首處理雜務」，就能多換來一小時全心陪伴孩子的時間。

10. 編輯室之外
• 社論：川普總統週四晚間打進黃金時段電視節目，為他那項注定無法過關的《拯救美國法案》大力促銷，利用外界的疑慮而非化解它們。
• 華爾街日報｜Buy Side：Oura戒指最新款把同樣的功能濃縮進更小巧的機身。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: How IBM's Bold Bet Backfired on Wall Street
emails.contentEn:
The Boardroom Debate That Led to IBM's Historic 25% Stock Plunge
Plus, well-off boomers are upsizing, not downsizing—and a shortcut to private-equity riches is minting young millionaires

1. FROM MY DESK
One of the biggest shocks to Wall Street this week was IBM's AI profit warning, which triggered a 25% plunge in its shares—the worst in the company's history. The news has sparked discussions about whether IBM should be broken apart or an activist investor will come hunting for the century-old company. We have the inside story on the board's gamble on transparency, how it backfired and what lies ahead for Big Blue. In case you missed it: President Trump delivered an extraordinary prime-time address last night focused on election security. Read our takeaways here.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
• Trump's tightening squeeze on Iran will heap more pain on its battered economy.
• Shredded iceberg lettuce supplied to Taco Bell restaurants has been linked to a parasitic outbreak that has infected thousands of people.
• The Treasury's top tax policy official was ousted after clashing with the White House over IRS audits.
• In the global hunt for rare earths, the U.S. is trampling allies.
• Well-off boomers are increasingly upsizing their homes as they get older, ripping up the traditional script for aging.

3. LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
S&P 500 Futures 7,511.50 (-0.87%) | DJIA Futures 52,440.00 (-0.66%) | Nasdaq 100 Futures 28,724.25 (-1.72%)
As of 7/17/2026, 6:11:50 AM ET
• Charts: Here's what is happening behind the market's swings.
• Meta plans to hire a top Amazon computing executive as the social media giant's data-center ambitions grow.
• The SEC has been flooded with complaints over its proposal to no longer require public companies to report quarterly results.
• Gas prices will stay higher for longer, even if oil prices fall, writes Jinjoo Lee.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
This shortcut to private-equity riches is minting young millionaires.
Instead of grinding from associate to managing director, a new wave of dealmakers are finding ways to buy HVAC and plumbing outfits, specialized manufacturers and other small and midsize businesses. Financing such deals is a far cry from traditional private equity. These would-be business owners scrape together financing on a deal-by-deal basis. They use loans from the U.S. Small Business Administration; seek funds raised from specialized investors; or cobble together money from friends, family offices, private-equity funds and SBA-licensed small-business investment companies. And that is just the start, reports Miriam Gottfried.

5. The sky was the limit for turning offices into apartments—until some columns buckled.
Developer Nathan Berman and his company, MetroLoft, have been at the leading edge of the conversion boom. But last week's construction disaster at Berman's most ambitious project to date—turning the former Pfizer headquarters in Midtown Manhattan into 1,600 apartments—is raising questions about what can go wrong in complex conversions. And with Manhattan's apartment vacancy rate below 2%, city officials have to decide whether to hit the brakes on the wave of projects now under way, report Nicholas G. Miller, Peter Grant and Kevin T. Dugan.

6. SEE THE STORY
Ozempic is dulling tastes. He has spices for that.
How Americans live—and eat—is being transformed by GLP-1 medications. Lior Lev Sercarz, a chef and spice master, has become acutely aware of the shift. Here, he offers his guide to eating in the GLP-1 era.

7. HAPPENING TODAY
• Christopher Nolan's blockbuster adaptation of "The Odyssey" lands in movie theaters.
• Economic data: The University of Michigan releases its preliminary July consumer-sentiment survey.
• Earnings: Fifth Third Bancorp, Regions Financial
• Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER
$38 billion
This summer's travel season is being powered by a historic pile of airline points, which airlines value at around $38 billion. That reservoir of credit card-powered miles helps feed demand, allowing airlines to report strong revenue despite volatile jet-fuel prices and broader economic jitters.

9. AND FINALLY…
After 3,000 years, people are getting around to reading The Odyssey—at least on Wikipedia.
Christopher Nolan is finally getting people to do their homework. Readers are digging into various editions of the ancient Greek epic before Nolan's movie adaptation hits theaters this weekend. TikTok is full of videos of readers holding up their copies of the translation by University of Pennsylvania classicist Emily Wilson, which Nolan has referenced as a source. The roughly 500-page book saw a significant increase in sales last year, according to publisher W.W. Norton.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
• Opinion: House Republicans on Wednesday unveiled a $95 billion budget framework to boost defense and further subsidize farmers. Is this really all the GOP can come up with?
• WSJ | Buy Side: These men's linen shirts look elevated, while helping you feel cool and casual.
emails.contentZh:
董事會的一場辯論，如何導致IBM股價歷史性重挫25%
此外，手頭寬裕的嬰兒潮世代選擇換大屋而非縮小住宅，一條私募股權致富捷徑正在造就年輕百萬富翁

1. 編輯手記
本週華爾街最大的震撼之一，來自IBM發出的AI獲利警訊，導致股價重挫25%，創下該公司史上最慘跌幅。這則消息也引發外界討論：IBM是否該拆分業務，或即將迎來覬覦這家百年企業的維權投資人。我們深入報導了董事會這場「透明度豪賭」的內幕、為何弄巧成拙，以及「藍色巨人」未來的走向。如果你錯過了：川普總統昨晚發表了一場聚焦選舉安全的罕見黃金時段演說，點此閱讀我們的重點整理。

2. 今日頭條
• 川普對伊朗持續加大施壓，將讓其本已疲弱的經濟雪上加霜。
• 供應給Taco Bell餐廳的碎冰山萵苣，被證實與一起已造成數千人感染的寄生蟲疫情有關。

4. 獨家搶先看
這條私募股權致富捷徑，正在打造一批年輕百萬富翁。
一批新世代交易撮合者，不再從初級分析師一路苦熬到董事總經理，而是找方法直接買下暖通空調、水電工程行，以及各種專業製造商與中小企業。這類交易的融資方式，與傳統私募股權大相逕庭：這些準企業主往往逐案拼湊資金，方式包括申請美國小型企業管理局貸款、向專業投資人募資，或是東拼西湊來自親友、家族辦公室、私募股權基金以及SBA認證小型企業投資公司的資金。而這還只是開端，Miriam Gottfried報導。

5. 把辦公大樓改建成公寓，原本前景一片大好——直到有些梁柱撐不住了。
開發商Nathan Berman與其公司MetroLoft，一直站在這波辦公大樓改建潮的最前線。但上週他至今最具野心的計畫——將曼哈頓中城前輝瑞總部改建成1,600戶公寓——發生施工事故，讓外界開始質疑複雜改建工程可能出現哪些問題。而隨著曼哈頓公寓空置率跌破2%，市府官員如今必須決定，是否要為這波正在進行中的改建熱潮踩下煞車，Nicholas G. Miller、Peter Grant與Kevin T. Dugan報導。

Ozempic正在讓人的味覺變遲鈍，他有辦法用香料解決。
GLP-1藥物正在改變美國人的生活方式與飲食習慣。廚師兼香料大師Lior Lev Sercarz對這股轉變感受特別深刻。在這篇報導中，他分享自己在「GLP-1時代」的飲食指南。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Quiet Cash Fueling Trump's Second Term
emails.contentEn:
To Catch Europe's Most Elusive Criminals, Police Look to U.S. DNA Tactics
Plus, the AI backlash has tech executives fearing for their lives, and Wall Street traders are having their best year ever

1. FROM MY DESK
This morning, I want to highlight a remarkable story from our Paris bureau: a close look at how police in France skirted European privacy laws to crack one of the country's most perplexing cold cases. Nearer to home, our investigations team looks at the mystery money powering President Trump's second term, a complex web of funds and $781,948,878 in donations—that we know of.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
• As U.S. strikes on Iran continue, military experts say opening the Strait of Hormuz would require more troops and months of effort.
• The Trump administration is considering placing a bond of $100,000 on some green-card seekers applying at U.S. consulates abroad.
• The Pentagon plans to screen troops for testosterone deficiency as Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth continues his revamp of the country's military.
• U.S. Ambassador to Canada Pete Hoekstra has become something of a household name north of the border by embracing Trump's blunt tone.
• England was five minutes from the World Cup final until Argentina made a stunning comeback.
• Artificial intelligence is helping companies dig deeper into workers' digital footprints before—and after—hiring.

3. LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
S&P 500 Futures 7,605.50 (-0.12%) | DJIA Futures 52,842.00 (-0.11%) | Nasdaq 100 Futures 29,564.25 (-0.43%)
As of 7/16/2026, 6:00:54 AM ET
• Investors can't stop piling more money into stock-market bets.
• Evicting Wall Street from the housing market will be messy, writes Carol Ryan.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
Here's a visual breakdown of the mystery money powering Trump's second term.
Presidents have always raised money from private donors—to run for office, throw inaugural balls and build presidential libraries. But Donald Trump has turned his second term into an unprecedented fundraising blitz, raising well over half a billion dollars from wealthy donors and stashing it in a sprawling network of nonprofits, cultural institutions and committees that he and his allies control. The Journal reviewed financial disclosures and interviewed donors to better understand how much money is flowing to Trump-linked groups. Marianne LeVine and Maggie Severns report.

5. The AI backlash has tech executives fearing for their lives.
In recent months, mounting opposition to AI has given rise to a surge of violent rhetoric, threats against people and property, and a serious attempt at harm. The phenomenon has executives at tech companies large and small reconsidering their personal security arrangements and how they talk about their products to a public that is increasingly wary of the technology and the societal changes it is ushering in. Police in San Francisco have responded to several threats against employees of Anthropic and OpenAI, according to records viewed by the Journal. Lindsay Ellis, Zusha Elinson and Tina Li report.

6. SEE THE STORY
A trip on a lobster boat is one of the best ways to see Maine's coast.
Cruise travelers to Maine often miss what makes the area special by staying far from its craggy shoreline. The state's coast is best experienced at sea level, aboard smaller boats run by locals rather than from behind the glass of a luxury liner. Lobstermen, along with captains of mail boats and historical vessels, offer a front-row seat to the people, places and traditions that lie beyond Maine's cruise-ship routes. Here are three excursions that will take you into coves, harbors and waterways the big ships can't reach.

7. HAPPENING TODAY
• Economic data: The Commerce Department releases June retail sales.
• Earnings: Netflix, UnitedHealth Group, General Electric, U.S. Bancorp, Abbott Laboratories, State Street
• Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER
7
Homes in Hinsdale, Ill., spent a median of seven days on the market in May. Demand for the historic Chicago suburb has steadily increased, pushing the median sales price to $1.74 million so far this year. The draw isn't just its stately properties—local agents note its highly rated public schools and walkable downtown are attracting buyers who are also considering the city's priciest suburbs, including Glencoe, Kenilworth and Winnetka.

9. AND FINALLY…
How much do you know about life expectancies? Take our quiz to find out.
Do you know which countries have the highest longevity? How about the U.S. state where people live the longest, on average? Test your know-how with this WSJ quiz.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
• Opinion: Democrats are blocking legislation that is vital for national defense and gathering intelligence on America's enemies.
• WSJ | Buy Side: Some of the best fiduciary financial advisers for retirees.
emails.contentZh:
為緝拿歐洲最難捉摸的罪犯，警方轉向美國式DNA偵查手法
此外，AI反彈浪潮讓科技高層人人自危，華爾街交易員正迎來史上最佳的一年

1. 編輯手記
今天早上，我想特別推薦一篇來自本報巴黎分社的精彩報導：深入剖析法國警方如何遊走於歐洲隱私法邊緣，破解該國最令人費解的懸案之一。回到國內，我們的調查團隊則深入追查為川普總統第二任期提供資金的神秘金流——一個由多個基金構成的複雜網絡，目前已知捐款金額高達781,948,878美元。

2. 今日頭條
• 隨著美國持續對伊朗發動空襲，軍事專家表示，若要重新開通荷莫茲海峽，將需要更多兵力並耗時數月。
• 川普政府正考慮對部分在美國海外領事館申請綠卡的人士，徵收10萬美元保證金。
• 隨著國防部長皮特·赫格塞斯持續推動軍隊改革，五角大廈計畫對官兵進行睪固酮缺乏症篩檢。
• 美國駐加拿大大使皮特·霍克斯特拉，因全盤採納川普直言不諱的作風，如今在加拿大已小有名氣。
• 英格蘭原本只差五分鐘就能挺進世界盃決賽，卻遭阿根廷戲劇性逆轉。
• 人工智慧正協助企業在招募前後，更深入挖掘員工的數位足跡。

3. 市場即時動態
標普500期貨 7,605.50（-0.12%）｜ 道瓊期貨 52,842.00（-0.11%）｜ 那斯達克100期貨 29,564.25（-0.43%）

• Carol Ryan撰文指出，把華爾街資金逐出住宅市場的過程恐將相當混亂。

4. 獨家搶先看
一張圖看懂為川普第二任期提供資金的神秘金流。
歷任總統向來都會向私人捐款者募款——用於競選、舉辦就職舞會、興建總統圖書館。但川普已將自己的第二任期，變成一場前所未見的募款狂潮，從富裕捐款者手中募得逾五億美元，並將這些資金藏進一個由他與盟友掌控、涵蓋非營利組織、文化機構與各類委員會的龐大網絡之中。本報審視財務揭露文件並訪談捐款者，試圖釐清究竟有多少資金流向與川普有關的團體，Marianne LeVine與Maggie Severns報導。

5. AI反彈浪潮讓科技高層人人自危。
近幾個月來，社會對AI日益升高的反對聲浪，引發了一波暴力言論、針對人身與財物的威脅，甚至出現真正意圖傷害他人的嚴重案例。這股現象促使大小科技公司的高層重新檢討自身的人身安全安排，也重新思考該如何向日益對這項技術及其帶來社會變革心生警惕的大眾說明自家產品。根據本報審視的紀錄，舊金山警方已多次針對Anthropic與OpenAI員工遭受的威脅出動處理，Lindsay Ellis、Zusha Elinson與Tina Li報導。

6. 圖說報導
搭乘龍蝦船，是欣賞緬因州海岸線最棒的方式之一。
搭郵輪造訪緬因州的旅客，往往因為船隻遠離崎嶇海岸線，而錯過了這片區域真正的魅力所在。緬因州海岸最好的體驗方式，是搭乘由當地人駕駛的小型船隻貼近海面遊覽，而不是隔著豪華郵輪的玻璃窗遠觀。龍蝦漁夫，以及郵船與歷史船隻的船長們，能帶你近距離接觸郵輪航線之外的人物、地點與傳統。以下三趟行程，將帶你深入大型郵輪無法抵達的海灣、港口與水道。

7. 今日看點
• 經濟數據：商務部公布6月零售銷售數據。
• 財報：Netflix、聯合健康集團、奇異公司、美國合眾銀行、亞培、道富銀行
• 今日報紙

8. 數字看新聞
7
今年5月，伊利諾州欣斯代爾的房屋掛牌待售天數中位數僅為七天。這座歷史悠久的芝加哥郊區需求持續攀升，將今年迄今的銷售中位價推高至174萬美元。吸引買家的不只是氣派的房產本身——當地房仲指出，該區評價極高的公立學校與適合步行的市中心，正吸引原本也在考慮Glencoe、Kenilworth與Winnetka等該市最昂貴郊區的買家。

9. 最後看點
你對平均壽命了解多少？來做做我們的測驗看看。
你知道哪些國家的人均壽命最長嗎？那美國又是哪一州的居民平均活得最久？來測試一下你的知識水準，做做這份華爾街日報測驗。

10. 編輯室之外
• 社論：民主黨正在阻擋對國防安全及蒐集美國敵對勢力情報至關重要的立法。
