emails.subject: The 10-Point: The U.S. and Iran Race Against the Clock
emails.contentEn:
The U.S. and Iran Face Dwindling Options to End the War
Plus, blockbuster stock sales threaten to overwhelm the bull market, and pressure builds over Israel's treatment of Palestinian prisoners

1. FROM MY DESK
Good morning. Thousands of you have written in with questions about where the war with Iran is headed. By far, the most common one is: What, exactly, is President Trump's exit strategy?

The short answer is that options are shrinking fast. Trump's plan is to wrest control of the Strait of Hormuz by resuming strikes and reimposing a naval blockade—one Tehran is gambling it can outlast. But with oil prices rising and the midterms looming, his clock is ticking faster than Iran's. This is no longer a search for a quick victory; it is a high-stakes test of endurance. There is more news below.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
• The U.A.E. has gained expanded access from the U.S. to coveted AI chips after aiding America by carrying out dozens of airstrikes against Iran and intercepting hundreds of missiles.
• The House passed legislation supported by Trump to make daylight-saving time permanent year-round. Speaking of the House: We went on the road with Mike Johnson and his 1,477 unread text messages.
• New York City officials are inspecting other buildings in the city after a Midtown Manhattan conversion project was at risk of partial collapse last week.
• Two million Americans are still locked out of an improving job market.
• China's growth slowed in the second quarter of the year to the weakest pace in more than three years, as surging exports buoyed by the AI boom failed to compensate for a struggling domestic economy.

3. LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
S&P 500 Futures 7,605.75 (+0.19%) | DJIA Futures 52,878.00 (+0.16%) | Nasdaq 100 Futures 29,939.75 (+0.50%)
As of 7/15/2026, 6:23:20 AM ET
• The rush for cash by some of the world's largest companies is putting the long bull market at risk.
• IBM lost $69 billion in market value in a single day as its shares plunged 25% in an AI-fueled selloff.
• Virtually everything worked in big banks' favor in the second quarter, but there is no shortage of things that could go wrong, writes Jonathan Weil.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
Pressure is building over Israel's treatment of Palestinian prisoners.
Reports from Israeli groups and interviews with former detainees detail alleged violence, medical neglect and starvation. The Journal interviewed a dozen Palestinians released from Israeli prisons since 2024. All said they experienced physical abuse. Government officials in Israel have said they intentionally made life harder for detainees after Oct. 7. The changes were designed to toughen punishments for terrorists and enhance deterrence against extremism, some officials have said. They say basic standards of care are met, and deny allegations of systematic abuses. Still, pressure is building on Israel to provide a more thorough accounting of its prisons, as more reports of alleged abuses come to light, report Feliz Solomon and Anat Peled.

5. England is on the cusp of World Cup history—because its best players left England.
England may not have won the World Cup for 60 years, but there can be no doubt that English soccer has become the most powerful force in the game. The Premier League stands alone as the richest, strongest and most popular league on the planet. It is no coincidence that more players at this World Cup were based in the Premier League than anywhere else. But the most unexpected part of the Three Lions' march to the semis is that it wasn't built on the might of the Premier League. Instead, England's run has been powered by players who have left English soccer far behind, report Jonathan Clegg and Joshua Robinson.

6. SEE THE STORY
We asked economists where inflation, growth and interest rates are heading in the months ahead.
The road ahead for the U.S. economy looks like a two-lane highway: stubbornly elevated inflation in one lane, strengthened growth and employment in the other. That is the consensus from 72 forecasters surveyed this month by the Journal. Economists highlighted an economy that is resilient yet uneven, fueled by AI investment, fiscal stimulus and last year's rate cuts. At the same time, they question how long those supports can last—and where the Fed goes next with interest rates.

7. HAPPENING TODAY
• World Cup: England vs. Argentina in Atlanta
• Earnings: BlackRock, Johnson & Johnson, Morgan Stanley, United Airlines
• Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER
1 million
That is how many beers a group of 1,000 (mostly) strangers are aiming to collectively drink together. What started as an offhand joke at a London pub has sparked a "herculean effort." Most members of the 1 Million Beers group chat on WhatsApp aren't heavy drinkers; many log an average of half a beer a day. But a dedicated four have hit 1,000 beers each in less than a year.

9. AND FINALLY…
We spent $1,300 to test a new VIP airport service. Was it worth it?
Well-heeled travelers are splurging to avoid hordes and hassles inside the airport. Our travel columnist Dawn Gilbertson tested the newest Miami outpost of PS, a private luxury terminal. Dawn says these private terminals, which sit in separate buildings away from main airports, are "basically business-class lounges on steroids." And no one cares if you're flying basic economy or first class as long as you pony up for a pricey membership ($1,250 to $4,850 plus hefty per-visit fees) or a day pass ($1,300 to $4,950).

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
• Opinion: Justices Elena Kagan and Amy Coney Barrett came to Congress with an urgent request: They need more protection from violent threats.
• WSJ | Buy Side: Here's what borrowers should know about federal student loan rates for the 2026-2027 academic year.
emails.contentZh:
美伊在時間壓力下尋求出路
此外,重磅股票拋售恐衝擊多頭市場,以色列對待巴勒斯坦囚犯的方式也持續引發壓力

1. 編輯的話
早安。許多讀者來信詢問與伊朗的戰爭將如何收場,其中最常見的問題是:川普總統的退場策略究竟是什麼?

簡短的答案是:選項正在迅速減少。川普的計畫是透過恢復空襲、重新實施海軍封鎖,奪回荷莫茲海峽的控制權——德黑蘭則賭上自己能撐得比美國更久。但隨著油價上漲、期中選舉逼近,川普的時鐘比伊朗走得更快。這已不再是速戰速決的追求,而是一場高風險的耐力賽。詳細報導請見下方。

2. 今日頭條
• 阿聯在協助美國對伊朗發動數十次空襲、攔截數百枚飛彈後,已從美國獲得更多珍貴AI晶片的取得管道。
• 眾議院通過川普支持的法案,將日光節約時間全年永久實施。談到眾議院:我們跟拍了眾議院議長麥克．強森,他手機裡累積了1,477則未讀簡訊。
• 紐約市官員在上週曼哈頓中城一處改建案面臨部分倒塌風險後,正在檢查市內其他建築物。
• 兩百萬美國人仍被排除在持續改善的就業市場之外。
• 中國第二季經濟成長放緩至三年多來最疲弱的速度,AI熱潮帶動的出口激增仍不足以彌補疲軟的內需經濟。

3. 市場即時動態
標普500指數期貨 7,605.75(+0.19%)| 道瓊工業指數期貨 52,878.00(+0.16%)| 那斯達克100期貨 29,939.75(+0.50%)
截至美東時間 2026年7月15日上午6:23:20
• 全球部分最大型企業爭相籌措現金,恐讓長期多頭市場陷入風險。
• IBM單日市值蒸發690億美元,股價在AI帶動的拋售中重挫25%。
• 大型銀行第二季幾乎所有因素都對其有利,但仍有不少潛在風險,Jonathan Weil撰文分析。

4. 獨家搶先看
以色列對待巴勒斯坦囚犯的方式引發愈來愈大壓力。
以色列團體的報告以及對前被拘留者的訪談,揭露了據稱存在的暴力、醫療疏忽與飢餓對待。《華爾街日報》訪問了十幾位自2024年以來獲釋的巴勒斯坦人,他們都表示曾遭受身體虐待。以色列政府官員表示,他們在10月7日事件後刻意讓被拘留者的生活更加艱難,這些改變旨在加重對恐怖分子的懲罰、強化對極端主義的嚇阻。官員們表示已達到基本照護標準,並否認存在系統性虐待的指控。儘管如此,隨著更多指控虐待的報告陸續曝光,以色列被要求就其監獄狀況提供更完整交代的壓力正在升高,Feliz Solomon與Anat Peled報導。

5. 英格蘭站上世界盃歷史的門檻——因為其最優秀的球員都已離開英格蘭。
英格蘭已經60年未能奪得世界盃冠軍,但英格蘭足球無疑已成為這項運動中最強大的力量。英超聯賽獨佔鰲頭,是全球最富有、最強大、最受歡迎的聯賽。本屆世界盃來自英超的球員數量高於其他任何聯賽,絕非巧合。但三獅軍團挺進四強最出人意料之處在於,這並非仰賴英超的實力所致。相反地,英格蘭的這波佳績,是由早已離開英格蘭足壇的球員所帶動,Jonathan Clegg與Joshua Robinson報導。

6. 延伸閱讀
我們詢問經濟學家,未來幾個月通膨、成長與利率將走向何方。
美國經濟前方的道路就像一條雙線道高速公路:一線是頑固偏高的通膨,另一線則是增強的成長與就業。這是《華爾街日報》本月調查的72位預測專家的共識。經濟學家指出,美國經濟展現韌性卻也參差不齊,受到AI投資、財政刺激與去年降息的推動。與此同時,他們也質疑這些支撐力道能持續多久——以及聯準會下一步的利率動向。

7. 今日焦點
• 世界盃:英格蘭對阿根廷,於亞特蘭大進行
• 財報:貝萊德、嬌生、摩根士丹利、聯合航空

8. 數字看新聞
100萬
這是一群約1,000名(大多是)互不相識的人,目標要一起喝下的啤酒杯數。這項行動起源於倫敦一間酒吧的隨口玩笑,如今已演變成一場「艱鉅任務」。這個名為「100萬杯啤酒」的WhatsApp群組成員大多不是重度飲酒者,許多人平均一天只喝半杯啤酒。但已有四位死忠成員在不到一年內各自喝下1,000杯。

9. 最後,還有這則……
我們花了1,300美元體驗機場VIP服務,值得嗎?
手頭闊綽的旅客正砸重金,只為避開機場內的人潮與麻煩。本報旅遊專欄作家Dawn Gilbertson體驗了私人豪華航廈品牌PS在邁阿密最新開幕的據點。Dawn表示,這些位於主要航廈之外獨立建築內的私人航廈,「基本上就是加強版的商務艙貴賓室」。而且無論你搭的是經濟艙還是頭等艙都無所謂,只要你願意支付高額會員費(1,250至4,850美元不等,外加高昂的單次造訪費)或單日通行證(1,300至4,950美元)。

10. 編輯室之外
• 社論:大法官凱根與艾米．柯尼．巴瑞特向國會提出緊急請求:她們需要更多保護,以防範暴力威脅。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: How China Holds Almost All the Cards Over Russia
emails.contentEn:
How Xi Went From Admiring Putin to Managing Him
Plus, data-center builders are racing to offload stakes worth billions, and the superrich are snapping up neighboring properties to create private compounds

1. FROM MY DESK
Inflation is back in focus this morning, with new CPI data and major bank earnings offering a dual look at how Americans are keeping up. Elsewhere, we are monitoring the escalating standoff between the U.S. and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz. We're also looking ahead to this week's World Cup semifinals, where England and Argentina prepare to renew one of sport's greatest—and most volatile—rivalries on the pitch. And I highly recommend our deep dive into the shifting power dynamic between China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
- Oil markets and Middle East producers appear to be aligning around a new reality: The Strait of Hormuz is no longer expected to return to a prewar norm.
- A wave of nationalist fervor in Iran is creating a difficult atmosphere for the country's diplomats, making it harder to agree to U.S. terms to permanently end the fighting.
- Darline Graham, the sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina, was selected to finish out her brother's term in the Senate.
- Gov. Kathy Hochul is banning large data-center construction for up to a year, making New York the latest state to confront the rollout of sites powering the AI boom.

3. LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
S&P 500 Futures 7,557.50 (-0.07%); DJIA Futures 52,640.00 (-0.24%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 29,597.00 (+0.41%) as of 7/14/2026, 6:07:50 AM ET.
- A dozen blue states, led by California, are seeking to block the Paramount-Warner merger, arguing the tie-up is anticompetitive, would harm theaters and would raise prices for TV bundles.
- Corporate bonds have the best yield in years—but higher long-term yields might not compensate for the higher risks, writes Telis Demos.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
Data-center builders are racing to offload stakes worth billions. Across the U.S., data-center developers and operators are working with bankers to sell majority equity stakes worth tens of billions of dollars in their companies this summer, according to people familiar with the efforts. Shortages of everything from electricians and plumbers to gas turbines and memory chips have driven up the cost of building new centers. Bankers are pitching private-equity firms on a hot asset class benefiting from unrelenting demand for computing power, reports Anissa Gardizy.

5. REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK
Chief China Correspondent Lingling Wei: I've covered China and Xi Jinping for 15 years, and in that time I've watched his relationship with Vladimir Putin evolve from an equal partnership into something far more complicated. But it was a photograph that sparked this story. When Putin visited Beijing in May, Chinese state media published images of him standing before a giant portrait of the two leaders. Viewed from the side, Xi appeared to loom over Putin in the picture. Chinese diplomats told me the staging wasn't meant to belittle Putin; viewed from the front, they said, the two figures take roughly equal share of the picture's frame. People who know Putin say he is acutely sensitive to exactly that kind of symbolism. Xi took care to tend to his counterpart's feelings.
Still, beneath the public warmth is a relationship increasingly shifting in China's favor—with Xi extracting concessions from Putin across areas ranging from energy to a new regional development bank.
What surprised me most in the reporting: how openly some foreign-policy experts now use words like "vassalage" to describe Russia's trajectory—language that would have seemed extreme just a few years ago. The biggest challenge was capturing the tensions beneath a partnership both sides insist has "no limits," especially when reporting on two of the world's most secretive governments. My colleague Thomas Grove and I spent weeks reporting this out.
The timing feels especially urgent. Putin has staked his legacy on projecting strength. And yet the man Xi once admired is now, in ways large and small, the one being managed.

6. SEE THE STORY
Shut out of the U.S., Cubans are building a 'new Miami' in southern Brazil. Curitiba, one of Brazil's most prosperous and orderly—some would say boring—cities, has become an unlikely outpost of the Cuban diaspora as tougher U.S. immigration policies coupled with the Trump administration's squeeze on the island's Communist government force many to build new lives farther south.

7. HAPPENING TODAY
- World Cup: France and Spain meet in a huge semifinal clash in Dallas.
- Economic data: The Labor Department releases the June consumer price-index.
- Earnings: Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup

8. THE NUMBER
$9.99 — This is the magic number that makers of everyday goods are obsessed with. Companies are redesigning packaging and slashing marketing budgets to keep product prices under this psychologically important threshold. Maintaining prices under $10 has long been a tried-and-true strategy used by U.S. retailers—and it is more important than ever with many Americans feeling stretched by inflation—but it is getting harder.

9. AND FINALLY…
The superrich aren't just buying mansions—they want the entire block. The ultimate billionaire flex is no longer buying a mansion, or even two. Deep-pocketed buyers are increasingly snapping up neighboring properties to create private compounds, with amenities from parking to padel. "Landmaxxing"—the quest to optimize one's land holdings by acquiring more acreage—drove the luxury market during the first part of the year, according to a new midyear report from Coldwell Banker.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
- Opinion: President Trump told the truth about Iran's lying regime. Now let him act on it—and stick to the strategy.
emails.contentZh:
習近平如何從仰慕普京到管束普京
另外，資料中心建設商正競相拋售價值數十億美元的股份，超級富豪則爭相收購鄰近房產以打造私人莊園

1. 編輯手記
今天早上，通膨話題再度成為焦點，最新的CPI數據與各大銀行財報從兩個角度呈現了美國民眾應對物價上漲的狀況。此外，我們也持續關注美國與伊朗在荷莫茲海峽問題上不斷升級的對峙。本週世界盃準決賽也令人期待，英格蘭與阿根廷即將在球場上重燃這項運動史上最偉大、也最動盪的對抗之一。此外，我強烈推薦我們對中國國家主席習近平與俄羅斯總統普京之間權力關係轉變的深度報導。

2. 今日頭條
- 石油市場和中東產油國似乎正逐漸接受一個新現實：荷莫茲海峽預計不會再恢復到戰前的常態。
- 伊朗國內民族主義情緒高漲，使該國外交官處境艱難，也讓伊朗更難同意美國提出的永久停火條件。
- 已故南卡羅來納州參議員林賽·格雷厄姆的姊姊達琳·格雷厄姆，獲選接任其弟弟未完成的參議員任期。
- 紐約州長霍楚爾將禁止大型資料中心建設長達一年，使紐約成為最新一個對抗AI熱潮所帶動資料中心擴張的州。

3. 市場直擊
截至美東時間2026年7月14日上午6:07:50，標普500期貨報7,557.50點（-0.07%）；道瓊期貨報52,640.00點（-0.24%）；那斯達克100期貨報29,597.00點（+0.41%）。
- 以加州為首的十幾個藍州正尋求阻止派拉蒙與華納的合併案，主張此併購具反競爭性，將損害電影院並提高電視套餐價格。
- 企業債券近年來擁有最佳殖利率——但更高的長期殖利率未必能彌補更高的風險，Telis Demos撰文分析。

4. 獨家搶先報導
資料中心建設商正競相拋售價值數十億美元的股份。據知情人士透露，今夏美國各地的資料中心開發商與營運商正與銀行家合作，出售旗下公司價值數百億美元的多數股權。從電工、水電工到燃氣渦輪機和記憶體晶片的全面短缺，推高了新建資料中心的成本。銀行家正向私募股權公司推銷這一受惠於運算能力需求不減的熱門資產類別，Anissa Gardizy報導。

5. 記者筆記
首席中國特派記者魏玲靈：我報導中國與習近平已有15年，這段期間我目睹他與普京的關係從平等夥伴演變為遠比表面複雜得多的關係。而促成這篇報導的契機，是一張照片。今年5月普京訪問北京時，中國官媒發布了他站在兩位領導人巨幅畫像前的照片。從側面看，畫面中習近平似乎在普京之上。中國外交官告訴我，這樣的畫面安排並非要貶低普京；他們說從正面看，兩人在畫面中所佔的比例大致相等。熟悉普京的人士說，他對這類象徵意義極為敏感，習近平因此格外留意照顧對方的感受。
然而，在公開的熱絡氛圍之下，這段關係正日益向中國一方傾斜——習近平已在從能源到新的區域開發銀行等多個領域，從普京身上取得讓步。
在採訪過程中最讓我驚訝的是，如今一些外交政策專家竟公開使用「附庸」這樣的字眼來形容俄羅斯的走向——這種措辭在幾年前還顯得極為激進。最大的挑戰在於，如何捕捉這段雙方都堅稱「沒有限度」的夥伴關係背後的緊張態勢，尤其是在報導這兩個世界上最神秘的政府時更是如此。我與同事湯瑪斯·格羅夫花了數週時間才完成這篇報導。
這個時間點格外緊迫。普京已將自己的歷史地位押注在展現實力之上。然而，這位曾讓習近平仰慕的人物，如今卻在大大小小的層面上，反過來成為被管束的一方。

6. 圖說報導
被美國拒之門外，古巴人正在巴西南部打造「新邁阿密」。庫里提巴是巴西最繁榮、最井然有序——甚至有人說有些沉悶——的城市之一，如今卻意外成為古巴僑民的聚集地，因為美國移民政策收緊，加上川普政府對古巴共產政府的施壓，迫使許多人南遷重新開始生活。

7. 今日看點
- 世界盃：法國對西班牙在達拉斯進行的重量級準決賽。
- 經濟數據：勞工部將公布6月消費者物價指數。
- 財報：美國銀行、摩根大通、富國銀行、高盛、花旗集團

8. 數字看新聞
9.99美元——這是日常用品製造商魂牽夢縈的神奇數字。企業正重新設計包裝並削減行銷預算，以將產品價格維持在這個心理門檻之下。將價格維持在10美元以下，長期以來一直是美國零售商屢試不爽的策略——在許多美國人感到通膨壓力沉重的當下，這一策略比以往任何時候都更加重要——但要做到這點也越來越困難。

9. 最後看點
超級富豪不只是買豪宅——他們要整個街區。億萬富豪最新的炫富方式已不再是買一棟豪宅，甚至兩棟都不夠。財力雄厚的買家正日益收購鄰近房產，打造私人莊園，配備從停車場到板式網球場等各種設施。「地產極大化」（Landmaxxing）——透過收購更多地產來優化土地持有的追求——根據高爾威地產（Coldwell Banker）最新年中報告，這股風潮在今年上半年主導了豪宅市場。

10. 新聞室之外
- 評論：川普總統道出了伊朗政權說謊的真相。現在該讓他採取行動——並堅持既定策略。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Scramble to Find Lindsey Graham's Successor
emails.contentEn:
What Lindsey Graham's Death Means for the Balance of Power on Capitol Hill
Plus, an onslaught of artificial-intelligence bonds tests investors' limits, and Apple's 'thermonuclear' response to the OpenAI threat

1. FROM MY DESK
Good morning. We start this week in Washington, where lawmakers are reeling from the sudden death of Sen. Lindsey Graham over the weekend. The loss comes at a perilous moment for Senate Republicans, compounding the challenges of pushing through President Trump's agenda and confirming key nominees just months before the midterm elections. As one Senate colleague noted, Graham's death "will impact everything."

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
- Goldman Sachs general counsel Kathryn Ruemmler, who has defended her ties to Jeffrey Epstein, is digging in at the investment bank and complicating the search for her successor.
- Apple CEO Tim Cook is going to battle against OpenAI, betting that litigation can delay a rival from upending the iPhone era.
- Sen. Mitch McConnell said his lengthy Senate absence has been because of his recovery from a fall and a bout of pneumonia, breaking a weekslong silence about his hospitalization.
- Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh faces his first big call: whether to undo last year's rate cuts.
- The U.S. and Iran traded new rounds of attacks as the two countries' standoff over the Strait of Hormuz deepens.

3. LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
S&P 500 Futures 7,600.25 (-0.26%); DJIA Futures 52,936.00 (+0.06%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 29,758.00 (-0.91%) as of 7/13/2026, 6:03:31 AM ET.
- The U.S. is tapping in to its national stocks of crude with abandon and the withdrawals are pushing an old system to its breaking point.
- How cheap or expensive the market looks depends on who is defining the "E" in the S&P 500's P/E ratio, writes Jonathan Weil.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
We take you inside Lindsey Graham's final mission: saving Ukraine. Graham, who had a personal rapport with Trump, spent his final days in the role of a U.S. power broker that had defined much of his career: meeting foreign leaders, pressing for hawkish U.S. foreign policy and planning to make the rounds on Sunday morning TV news shows. When the South Carolina Republican landed Saturday in Washington, colleagues said he was tired but elated after a whirlwind of meetings in Europe and Ukraine. He had spent his 71st birthday on the road, buoyed by a NATO summit in Turkey where Trump praised the alliance and embraced Ukraine. Hours later, Graham was pronounced dead, Robbie Gramer, Vera Bergengruen and Yoko Kubota report.

5. The quarter-trillion-dollar onslaught of AI bonds is testing investors' limits. Wall Street is sending a message to tech companies engaged in a historic borrowing spree to fund investments in artificial-intelligence infrastructure: for pity's sake, please slow down. Over the past several weeks, the investment-grade corporate bond market has struggled to absorb a combined $75 billion of bond issuance from Nvidia, SpaceX and Amazon.com. That marks a shift from earlier in the year, when investors were generally happy to hand money to so-called AI hyperscalers by any possible means, reports Sam Goldfarb.

6. SEE THE STORY
How much do you know about the sports business? Try our quiz. Forget about who has the best won-lost record, or who is likely to be the most valuable player. Forget about the best college team or that blown call by the referee. Let's talk about what really matters in sports: money.

7. HAPPENING TODAY
- The Senate returns for its first session since Sen. Lindsey Graham's death.

8. THE NUMBER
$22 million — That is the windfall one Pennsylvania family received for selling its struggling farmland to a data-center developer, joining a new class of multimillionaires cashing in on the AI data-center boom. The Kiliti family hopes that the incoming technology infrastructure will do more for the local economy than make landowners rich.

9. AND FINALLY…
On these islands, animals always come first. While other countries guarantee protections for animals, Ecuador is the only nation in the world to formally grant them distinct constitutional rights. The upshot: Galápagos animals walk around like they own the place, because they kind of do. Across the archipelago, marine iguanas routinely stretch out across boardwalks and walking paths, forcing tourists to either wait patiently or find another route. On Isabela Island, a local sea lion known as Panchito has become famous for commandeering the loungers at Cormorant Beach House.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
- Opinion: Lindsey Graham understood that U.S. national security depends on American global leadership.

林賽·格雷厄姆之死對國會權力平衡意味著什麼
另外，人工智慧債券的猛烈攻勢正在考驗投資人的極限，蘋果對OpenAI威脅祭出「核彈級」回應

1. 編輯手記
早安。本週我們從華盛頓開始，週末林賽·格雷厄姆參議員的驟逝令國會議員們震驚不已。這一損失發生在參議院共和黨人的危險時刻，使得在期中選舉前僅剩數月之際，推動川普總統議程和確認重要提名人選的挑戰更加複雜。正如一位參議院同僚所言，格雷厄姆的離世「將影響一切」。

2. 今日頭條
- 高盛總法律顧問凱瑟琳·魯姆勒曾為自己與傑弗里·愛潑斯坦的關係辯護，如今她在這家投資銀行內堅守立場，使繼任人選的尋覓變得更加複雜。
- 蘋果執行長提姆·庫克準備與OpenAI開戰，賭上訴訟策略以拖延這個競爭對手顛覆iPhone時代的腳步。
- 參議員米奇·麥康諾表示，他長期缺席參議院是因為從一次跌倒和肺炎中恢復，打破了他對自己住院一事持續數週的沉默。
- 聯準會主席凱文·沃許面臨上任以來的首個重大決策：是否要撤銷去年的降息。
- 隨著兩國在荷莫茲海峽的對峙加劇，美國與伊朗又展開新一輪攻擊。

3. 市場直擊
截至美東時間2026年7月13日上午6:03:31，標普500期貨報7,600.25點（-0.26%）；道瓊期貨報52,936.00點（+0.06%）；那斯達克100期貨報29,758.00點（-0.91%）。
- 美國正毫無節制地動用其國家原油儲備，而這些提領正將一套舊有體系推向崩潰邊緣。
- 市場看起來便宜或昂貴，取決於誰在定義標普500本益比中的「E」（獲利），Jonathan Weil撰文分析。

4. 獨家搶先報導
帶你深入了解林賽·格雷厄姆的最後使命：拯救烏克蘭。與川普私交甚篤的格雷厄姆，在生命最後幾天仍扮演著貫穿其大半職業生涯的美國權力掮客角色：會見外國領袖、力推鷹派美國外交政策，並計畫在週日上午的電視新聞節目中巡迴亮相。這位南卡羅來納州共和黨人週六抵達華盛頓時，同僚們說他雖疲憊但興高采烈，剛結束在歐洲和烏克蘭馬不停蹄的一連串會面。他在旅途中度過了71歲生日，土耳其的北約峰會上川普讚揚了聯盟並擁抱烏克蘭，令他倍感振奮。數小時後，格雷厄姆被宣告死亡，Robbie Gramer、Vera Bergengruen與Yoko Kubota報導。

5. 規模達兩千五百億美元的AI債券攻勢正在考驗投資人的極限。華爾街正向那些為人工智慧基礎設施投資而展開歷史性借貸狂潮的科技公司傳達一個訊息：拜託各位，放慢腳步吧。過去幾週，投資級公司債市場一直難以消化輝達、SpaceX和亞馬遜合計750億美元的債券發行量。這與今年稍早的情況形成鮮明對比，當時投資人普遍樂於以任何可能的方式將資金交給所謂的AI超大規模企業，Sam Goldfarb報導。

6. 圖說報導
你對體育商業了解多少？來做做我們的測驗。別管誰的勝負紀錄最好，或誰可能是最有價值球員。別管哪支大學球隊最強，或裁判的誤判。讓我們來談談體育界真正重要的事：金錢。

7. 今日看點
- 參議院自格雷厄姆參議員逝世以來首次復會。

8. 數字看新聞
2200萬美元——這是賓夕法尼亞州一個家庭將其經營困難的農地出售給資料中心開發商所獲得的意外之財，加入了因AI資料中心熱潮而致富的新一代多百萬富翁行列。基利提家族希望，即將進駐的科技基礎設施除了讓地主致富外，也能為當地經濟帶來更多助益。

9. 最後看點
在這些島嶼上，動物永遠優先。雖然其他國家也保障動物權益，但厄瓜多是全球唯一正式賦予動物明確憲法權利的國家。結果就是：加拉巴哥群島的動物大搖大擺地四處走動，彷彿這裡就是牠們的地盤——事實上也確實如此。在整個群島，海鬣蜥經常懶洋洋地躺在木棧道和步道上，迫使遊客要嘛耐心等待，要嘛另覓路線。在伊莎貝拉島，一隻名叫潘奇托的當地海獅因霸佔科莫蘭海灘小屋的躺椅而聲名大噪。

10. 新聞室之外
- 評論：林賽·格雷厄姆深知，美國的國家安全有賴於美國的全球領導地位。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The People Trying to Stop AI
emails.contentEn:
Inside the Hard-Line Movement Against AI
Plus, Wagner's remnants are building a drug empire in Africa, and economists say the Iran war could leave inflation higher for longer

1. FROM MY DESK
The AI boom is contending with a surge of backlash. As companies race to build more powerful models and sprawling data centers, resistance to the technology is hardening. One of our top stories follows the activists who believe artificial intelligence poses an existential threat and are upending their lives to try and stop its advance. Then, if Europe is on your summer itinerary, Chelsey Dulaney has smart advice on avoiding the biggest crowds and making the most of your trip.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
- Longtime Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham has died at 71. A close Trump ally, he pushed for tough action against Iran and support for Israel and Ukraine.
- Tehran believes it has emerged as a regional hegemon and is ready to escalate over the Strait of Hormuz, Yaroslav Trofimov writes. Fighting between the U.S. and Iran intensified overnight.
- In a nail-biting game, Argentina beat Switzerland to advance to another World Cup semifinal. There, it will face England, which defeated Norway last night.
- Black Democrats across the South are fighting for political survival after a Supreme Court ruling pushed many Alabama voters into Republican-leaning districts.
- The Iran war didn't hurt the U.S. nearly as much as economists feared, but it left inflation more persistent and the Fed with no room to cut interest rates.
- New York City's Department of Investigation has launched an inquiry into the Manhattan high-rise where two supporting columns buckled this week.

3. FROM THE MARKETS
- The standard ways to protect against economic shocks might no longer work in a world of wars, trade conflicts and extreme weather, writes James Mackintosh.
- Wall Street is waiting for evidence that AI can change the economics of making drugs.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
Wagner's remnants are building an opioid empire. The Russian state absorbed much of the mercenary group's operations after its founder Yevgeny Prigozhin was killed in a plane crash. But several hundred members remain in the Central African Republic, where they control the trade of tramadol—a painkiller known as the poor man's cocaine—beyond the reach of law enforcement or even Moscow itself. That's giving the group fresh impetus and enabling it to exploit the country's rich gold and timber resources, reports Nicholas Bariyo.

5. Michigan is at the center of a battle for the Democratic Party's future. Democrats remain deeply divided about how to start winning national elections again. Now, the state's U.S. Senate primary is becoming the first major electoral test of the party's direction since the implosion of Graham Platner's Senate campaign in Maine. If progressive Abdul El-Sayed wins, it would signal that the party is shifting left in the industrial heartland, not just in coastal and deeply blue enclaves, reports John McCormick.

6. SEE THE STORY
Venezuela's earthquake revealed a healthcare system already in crisis. Decades of mismanagement left the country's public-health system unable to cope with the disaster. Our visual reporting shows foreign doctors treating patients in modern field hospitals and volunteers turning everything from baseball fields to a McDonald's into lifelines for survivors.

7. HAPPENING THIS WEEK
- Tuesday: The Labor Department releases the June consumer price-index. France faces Spain in the World Cup semifinals.
- Wednesday: Lionel Messi's Argentina plays against England for a chance to advance to the World Cup Final.
- Thursday: The Commerce Department releases June retail sales.
- Friday: The University of Michigan releases its preliminary July consumer-sentiment survey. Christopher Nolan's blockbuster adaptation of "The Odyssey" lands in movie theaters.

8. THE NUMBER
17 — That's the age of Dave Lee, a New York teenager who has become his family's de facto financial adviser. After teaching himself about investing in middle school, he persuaded his mom to open her first brokerage account and now advises his parents on everything from investments to retirement planning.

9. AND FINALLY…
Nigel Farage wanted a political showdown. Now he's fighting a trash can. The right-wing U.K. populist stepped down from Parliament last week amid growing scrutiny over donations from wealthy supporters, and said he'd seek re-election—a chance, he told voters, to stick it to the establishment. It might have backfired: After all other major parties boycotted the vote, his most prominent competitor is a comedian who calls himself Count Binface.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
- WSJ | Buy Side: Functional footwear meets casual summer style with these top-rated flip flops.
emails.contentZh:
深入反AI強硬派運動內部
另外，「瓦格納」殘餘勢力正在非洲建立毒品帝國，經濟學家表示伊朗戰爭可能使通膨在更長時間內維持高位

1. 編輯手記
AI熱潮正面臨日益高漲的反彈聲浪。隨著企業競相打造更強大的模型和龐大的資料中心，社會對這項技術的抵制也日趨強硬。我們今天的頭條報導之一，追蹤了那些認為人工智慧構成存亡威脅、不惜顛覆自己人生也要試圖阻止其發展的行動者。此外，如果歐洲是你今年夏天的旅遊行程，Chelsey Dulaney提供了避開人潮、盡享旅程的實用建議。

2. 今日頭條
- 資深共和黨參議員林賽·格雷厄姆逝世，享年71歲。他是川普的親密盟友，力主對伊朗採取強硬行動，並支持以色列和烏克蘭。
- Yaroslav Trofimov撰文指出，德黑蘭認為自己已崛起為區域霸主，並準備在荷莫茲海峽問題上進一步升級。美國與伊朗的戰鬥一夜之間加劇。
- 在一場扣人心弦的比賽中，阿根廷擊敗瑞士晉級世界盃準決賽，將對陣昨晚擊敗挪威的英格蘭。
- 最高法院一項裁決將許多阿拉巴馬州選民劃入偏共和黨選區後，南方各地的黑人民主黨人正為政治生存而奮戰。
- 伊朗戰爭對美國造成的傷害遠不如經濟學家擔心的那麼嚴重，但卻使通膨變得更加頑固，讓聯準會沒有降息的空間。
- 紐約市調查局已對本週兩根支撐柱彎曲的曼哈頓高樓展開調查。

3. 市場動態
- James Mackintosh撰文指出，在一個戰爭、貿易衝突和極端天氣頻發的世界裡，傳統的經濟避險方式可能已不再奏效。
- 華爾街正等待證據，證明AI能改變藥品製造的經濟模式。

4. 獨家搶先報導
「瓦格納」殘餘勢力正在建立鴉片類藥物帝國。創辦人普里格津在空難中身亡後，俄羅斯政府接管了這個傭兵組織的大部分業務。但仍有數百名成員留在中非共和國，他們掌控著曲馬多——這種被稱為「窮人的古柯鹼」的止痛藥——的貿易，完全不受執法機構甚至莫斯科本身的約束。這為該組織注入了新的動力，使其得以開採該國豐富的黃金和木材資源，Nicholas Bariyo報導。

5. 密西根州正成為民主黨未來走向之爭的核心戰場。民主黨在如何重新贏得全國大選這個問題上依然存在深刻分歧。如今，該州的美國參議院初選正成為緬因州格雷厄姆·普拉特納參選崩潰後，該黨路線的首場重大選舉考驗。如果進步派人士阿卜杜勒·艾爾-薩耶德勝出，將意味著該黨不只在沿海和深藍飛地，也在工業腹地向左轉，John McCormick報導。

6. 圖說報導
委內瑞拉的地震揭露了一個早已陷入危機的醫療體系。數十年來的管理不善，使該國的公共衛生體系無力應對這場災難。我們的圖像報導顯示，外國醫生在現代化的野戰醫院中救治病患，志工們則將從棒球場到麥當勞的各種場所，改造成倖存者的生命線。

7. 本週看點
- 週二：勞工部公布6月消費者物價指數。法國在世界盃準決賽對陣西班牙。
- 週三：梅西率領的阿根廷對陣英格蘭，爭奪晉級世界盃決賽的機會。
- 週四：商務部公布6月零售銷售數據。
- 週五：密西根大學公布7月消費者信心初值調查。克里斯多福·諾蘭改編自《奧德賽》的鉅片在戲院上映。

8. 數字看新聞
17歲——這是紐約青少年戴夫·李的年齡，他已成為家中事實上的理財顧問。他在中學時自學投資知識，說服母親開設了人生第一個證券帳戶，如今從投資到退休規劃，樣樣都要向他請教。

9. 最後看點
奈傑爾·法拉奇原本想要一場政治對決，如今卻在跟一個垃圾桶較勁。這位英國右翼民粹主義者上週因富有支持者的捐款問題受到日益嚴格的審視而辭去國會議員職務，並表示將尋求連任——他告訴選民，這是給建制派一點顏色瞧瞧的機會。但此舉可能適得其反：由於所有其他主要政黨都抵制這場補選，他最有力的競爭對手竟是一位自稱「垃圾桶伯爵」的喜劇演員。

10. 新聞室之外
- WSJ | Buy Side：功能性鞋履與休閒夏日風格的完美結合，這些是評價最高的人字拖。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The White House Gambled on Intel. It's Working.
emails.contentEn:
Washington's Bet on Intel Is Starting to Pay Off
Plus, Texas goes after Wall Street's stock-exchange duopoly, and Apple alleges OpenAI stole trade secrets to develop competing devices

1. FROM MY DESK
Last summer, Tim Cook went to Washington hoping to avoid steep semiconductor tariffs. He left with an unexpected pitch from President Trump: Have Apple manufacture some of its chips at Intel. The White House has made fixing the chip maker its pet project, Robbie Whelan reports, and now the effort is beginning to pay off. And for a change of pace, our auto columnist Dan Neil answered your questions on everything from EVs to why Detroit is no longer the center of the car universe.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
- Apple sued OpenAI alleging the AI company stole trade secrets as part of its effort to develop competing devices. OpenAI said it has "no interest in other companies' trade secrets."
- The Trump administration is increasingly pessimistic about a nuclear deal with Iran, acknowledging the president's goal might not be achievable through peace talks.
- Investigators found evidence that Corey Lewandowski, a former top aide to Kristi Noem, may have been involved in improperly awarding DHS contracts.
- Potentially thousands across the U.S. have been sickened by a food-borne parasite, but officials still don't know the source. The illness can cause explosive diarrhea and vomiting.
- More than a year into Ken Martin's tenure as DNC chair, the Democratic Party is lagging Republicans in fundraising.
- Trump flew home from Turkey earlier this week on an older Air Force One plane after officials worried his new luxury jet lacked adequate defensive capabilities.

3. FROM THE MARKETS
- SK Hynix's historic U.S. debut helped investors regain their appetite for the AI trade. Its American depositary receipts soared 13% after a $26.5 billion share sale, while the major indexes edged higher to cap a volatile week.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
An IPO gold rush is under way. Texas wants in. Stock trading has never been bigger, and Texas dreams of a land grab from the duopoly of the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq. The Texas Stock Exchange began trading Friday, the culmination of years spent wooing companies, reshaping corporate laws and positioning the state as America's next financial hub. Now, its listing team is hustling to sign up big companies to make splashy switches from NYSE and Nasdaq to TXSE, reports Corrie Driebusch.

5. The war in Ukraine is shifting against Putin, but he isn't giving in. For four years, Russia has bet on outlasting Ukraine in a war of attrition. Now, Moscow is finding out that time isn't necessarily on its side as Kyiv's increasingly capable drones pound supply routes to the front and refineries deep inside Russia. Ukraine's stretched army hasn't buckled as Russia hoped and is even pushing back the invaders in places with small counterattacks. But the long struggle isn't over, and Ukraine still has major vulnerabilities, report Marcus Walker, Thomas Grove and Alexander Ward.

6. SEE THE STORY
This Charleston home looks centuries old. It was built in 1995. When Will and John Hardee bought what they called the "Grey Gardens" of the block, they saw potential beneath the neglect. They spent more than $3 million transforming the fixer-upper into a home with custom details, moody interiors and four fountains that embody the charm of historic Charleston.

7. HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND
- Saturday: The World Cup continues with Norway vs. England in Miami and Argentina vs. Switzerland in Kansas City.
- Sunday: Wimbledon concludes.

8. THE NUMBER
800,000 — That's how many job applications Bending Spoons received last year. The company behind AOL hired just 286 people—an acceptance rate of less than 0.04%, making it roughly 100 times as hard to land a job there than get into Harvard.

9. AND FINALLY…
Grandma's house is the hottest restaurant in town. Grandma-style cooking has been popular for about as long as we've had grandmas, but now it's having a moment. Restaurants around the world are embracing "grandmacore dining," with recipes passed down through generations and spaces designed to feel like grandma's house.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
- Opinion: President Trump's cleanout of the Election Assistance Commission is probably the first of many such firings after the Supreme Court's ruling in Trump v. Slaughter.
emails.contentZh:
白宮押注英特爾，如今開始見效
另外，德州向華爾街的證交所雙頭壟斷發起挑戰，蘋果指控OpenAI竊取商業機密以開發競爭產品

1. 編輯手記
去年夏天，提姆·庫克前往華盛頓，希望能避開嚴苛的半導體關稅。他離開時卻收到川普總統一個意想不到的提議：讓蘋果把部分晶片生產交給英特爾代工。Robbie Whelan報導，白宮已將拯救這家晶片製造商視為重點專案，如今這項努力開始收到成效。換個話題，我們的汽車專欄作家Dan Neil也回答了讀者的提問，內容從電動車到底特律為何不再是汽車產業中心，無所不包。

2. 今日頭條
- 蘋果起訴OpenAI，指控這家AI公司在開發競爭裝置的過程中竊取商業機密。OpenAI表示對「其他公司的商業機密毫無興趣」。
- 川普政府對與伊朗達成核協議日益悲觀，承認總統的目標或許無法透過和談實現。
- 調查人員發現證據，顯示克里斯蒂·諾姆的前高級助理科里·勒萬多夫斯基可能涉及不當授予國土安全部合約。
- 美國可能有數千人因食源性寄生蟲而生病，但官員仍未查明感染源。這種疾病會引發劇烈腹瀉和嘔吐。
- 民主黨全國委員會主席肯·馬丁上任逾一年，但民主黨在募款上仍落後共和黨。
- 由於官員擔心川普的新型豪華專機防禦能力不足，他本週稍早改搭較舊款的空軍一號從土耳其飛回國內。

3. 市場動態
- SK海力士在美國歷史性掛牌，幫助投資人重拾對AI概念股的胃口。在一筆265億美元的股票發行後，其美國存託憑證飆升13%，主要指數也小幅上漲，為波動的一週畫下句點。

4. 獨家搶先報導
IPO淘金熱正在展開，德州想分一杯羹。股票交易規模空前龐大，德州夢想從紐約證交所和那斯達克的雙頭壟斷中搶下一塊地盤。德州證券交易所週五開始交易，這是該州多年來拉攏企業、改革公司法規、力圖將自己打造成美國下一個金融中心的成果。如今，其上市團隊正積極遊說大型企業，讓它們高調地從紐約證交所和那斯達克轉往德州證交所，Corrie Driebusch報導。

5. 烏克蘭戰局正逐漸對普京不利，但他仍不肯讓步。四年來，俄羅斯一直押注能在消耗戰中撐得比烏克蘭久。如今，莫斯科發現時間未必站在自己這邊，因為基輔日益強大的無人機正猛烈打擊通往前線的補給路線以及俄羅斯境內深處的煉油廠。烏克蘭疲於應付的軍隊並未如俄羅斯所願崩潰，甚至在某些地方發動小規模反攻擊退侵略者。但這場持久戰尚未結束，烏克蘭仍存在重大弱點，Marcus Walker、Thomas Grove與Alexander Ward報導。

6. 圖說報導
這棟查爾斯頓的房子看起來有幾百年歷史，但其實建於1995年。當威爾和約翰·哈迪購入這棟被稱為街區「灰色花園」的房子時，他們在破敗中看見了潛力。他們斥資超過300萬美元，將這棟需大修的房子改造成擁有訂製細節、氛圍感十足的室內設計，以及四座噴泉、充分展現查爾斯頓歷史魅力的住宅。

7. 本週末看點
- 週六：世界盃賽事持續進行，挪威對英格蘭在邁阿密開打，阿根廷對瑞士在堪薩斯城開打。
- 週日：溫布頓網球賽落幕。

8. 數字看新聞
80萬——這是Bending Spoons去年收到的求職申請數量。這家AOL母公司去年僅錄取286人——錄取率不到0.04%，比進入哈佛大學還要難上約100倍。

9. 最後看點
奶奶的家，成了城裡最紅的餐廳。祖母風格的料理幾乎與「有奶奶」這件事一樣古老，但如今正大受歡迎。世界各地的餐廳紛紛擁抱「奶奶核」用餐風潮，端出代代相傳的食譜，並將空間設計得如同奶奶家一般溫馨。

10. 新聞室之外
- 評論：川普總統對選舉協助委員會的整肅，恐怕只是最高法院在「川普訴斯勞特案」裁決後一連串類似解僱行動的開端。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Making of Trump's Stock-Trading Frenzy
emails.contentEn:
The Wall Street Firm at the Center of Trump's Trading Spree
Plus, Netflix is rethinking some of its core strategies to compete with rivals, and the chaotic sweepstakes to replace Graham Platner has begun

1. FROM MY DESK
President Trump's financial disclosures revealed a stunning explosion in his stock trading. Our big story this morning examines the institution at the center of this trading spree: Charles Schwab. On the World Cup front, one of the tournament's biggest stars is a 6-foot-5 viking who has his own theme song: Norway striker Erling Haaland. Ahead of Norway's match against England tomorrow, we look at the secrets of Haaland's success, with clues from a Norwegian scientist and his youth soccer coach.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
- Israel shared new intelligence with the U.S. that it said indicated a fresh Iranian plan to kill Trump, people familiar with the matter said.
- A chaotic scramble is under way for Democrats to replace Graham Platner with a new nominee in the Maine Senate race, already drawing in more than half a dozen candidates.
- Ukraine's drones are now reaching Siberia and imperiling Russian energy assets.
- Volkswagen wants to halve its lineup of cars as part of its second major overhaul in under two years.
- U.S. biotechs are keeping more secrets to beat copycats in China.
- Colleges are juicing application numbers by letting students write fewer essays.

3. LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
S&P 500 Futures 7,581.75 (-0.09%); DJIA Futures 52,825.00 (+0.12%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 29,819.00 (-0.39%) as of 7/10/2026, 6:07:45 AM ET.
- OpenAI's No. 2 executive plans to step down from her full-time role following medical leave, a major leadership change ahead of the company's planned IPO.
- Specialized makers of turbines are a new pick-and-shovel play for investors, writes Jinjoo Lee.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
Netflix is exploring live TV and bundles as it struggles to keep viewers hooked. Netflix remains the industry leader among subscription-streaming services, but shares are down more than 40% over the past 12 months. Its share of TV viewership fell to 7.8% in April, according to Nielsen, the lowest level since May 2025. To bolster engagement, executives have recently discussed adding live channels that would continuously stream certain programs, or shows and films from a certain genre, according to people familiar with the matter. The company has also explored bundling other subscription-based streaming services, including NBCUniversal's Peacock, into its offering, report Jessica Toonkel and Ben Fritz.

5. Work on Trump's E. Jean Carroll defamation case divides Sullivan & Cromwell. When law firm Sullivan & Cromwell took on Trump as a client last year, its co-chairman Robert Giuffra drew a red line for partners who were wary of working for the polarizing president. Giuffra assured partners it would stay out of the president's appeal of sex-abuse and defamation cases. Sullivan & Cromwell reversed course after being asked by Trump's personal lawyer. The firm in recent weeks has come to Trump's aid in one of the Carroll cases, deepening its relationship with the president as well as a rift within its ranks over how far it should go to accommodate him, report C. Ryan Barber, Joe Palazzolo and Josh Dawsey.

6. SEE THE STORY
Our map traces 18 American inventions that created the modern world. From the bustling labs of the Northeast to the remote deserts of the Southwest, American ingenuity can be found everywhere. This map traces locations historically associated with the breakthroughs that have defined the nation's 250-year legacy.

7. HAPPENING TODAY
- World Cup: Spain vs. Belgium in Inglewood, Calif.
- Earnings: Delta Air Lines

8. THE NUMBER
$4.86 billion — There is a surprise winner from the Iran war: Africa's richest man. Surging demand for refined petroleum products has boosted Nigerian industrialist Aliko Dangote's wealth by some $4.86 billion this year, bringing his net worth to around $34.8 billion. Dangote went "through hell" building a $20 billion oil refinery. Now, the tycoon is reaping the benefits: The refinery reached full capacity in February—just in time to supply global markets with fuel that doesn't need to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

9. AND FINALLY…
People are lining up to see a plant that smells like a dumpster. Corpse flowers are showstoppers in the staid world of conservatories and botanic gardens. Their prehistoric look and yearslong waits for blooms make them intriguing. But the biggest draw might be the deathlike stench when they open—and people are willing to wait hours to catch a whiff.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
- Opinion: Trump is hailing Toyota's announcement that it will expand truck production in Texas. It is a deflection from the dismal reality that his border taxes are raising costs and have failed to usher in a manufacturing renaissance.
emails.contentZh:
川普炒股狂潮的幕後推手
另外，Netflix正重新思考核心策略以應對競爭對手，取代格雷厄姆·普拉特納的混亂爭奪戰已經展開

1. 編輯手記
川普總統的財務揭露文件顯示，他的股票交易量出現驚人暴增。我們今天的頭條報導聚焦於這波交易熱潮背後的核心機構：嘉信理財（Charles Schwab）。至於世界盃方面，本屆賽事最耀眼的明星之一，是身高6呎5吋、擁有專屬主題曲的「維京戰神」——挪威前鋒厄林·哈蘭德。在挪威明日對戰英格蘭之前，我們探究哈蘭德成功的秘訣，並訪問了一位挪威科學家和他的青少年足球教練提供線索。

2. 今日頭條
- 據知情人士透露，以色列向美國分享了新情報，指稱伊朗有新的暗殺川普計畫。
- 民主黨正陷入一場混亂的爭奪戰，試圖在緬因州參議院選舉中找到新人選取代格雷厄姆·普拉特納，目前已吸引超過六名候選人加入。
- 烏克蘭的無人機如今已能打擊到西伯利亞，威脅俄羅斯的能源資產。
- 福斯汽車計畫將旗下車型陣容砍半，這是該公司不到兩年內第二次重大改組。
- 美國生技公司正加強保密，以防中國仿冒者搶先。
- 大學正透過減少學生所需撰寫的論文數量，來灌水申請人數。

3. 市場直擊
截至美東時間2026年7月10日上午6:07:45，標普500期貨報7,581.75點（-0.09%）；道瓊期貨報52,825.00點（+0.12%）；那斯達克100期貨報29,819.00點（-0.39%）。
- OpenAI第二號高層計畫在病假結束後不再回任全職職位，這是該公司籌備上市之際的重大領導層變動。
- 專業渦輪機製造商正成為投資人眼中新的「賣鏟人」投資標的，Jinjoo Lee撰文分析。

4. 獨家搶先報導
Netflix為留住觀眾苦苦掙扎，正探索直播電視與訂閱組合方案。Netflix仍是訂閱串流服務業的龍頭，但過去12個月股價已下跌逾40%。據尼爾森數據，其電視收視份額在4月降至7.8%，創2025年5月以來新低。據知情人士透露，為提升用戶黏著度，高層近期已討論加入持續播放特定節目或特定類型影劇的直播頻道。公司也在探索將其他訂閱制串流服務（包括NBC環球的Peacock）打包進其方案中，Jessica Toonkel與Ben Fritz報導。

5. 川普與E·珍·卡羅爾誹謗案的相關工作，讓蘇利文與克倫威爾律師事務所內部產生分歧。當蘇利文與克倫威爾去年接下川普這位客戶時，共同主席羅伯特·久夫拉曾向那些不願為這位爭議總統效力的合夥人劃下一條紅線：保證事務所不會插手總統在性侵及誹謗案件上的上訴。但在川普私人律師的要求下，事務所改變了立場。該所近幾週已在其中一起卡羅爾案件中出手協助川普，這既加深了與總統的關係，也在內部就應該在多大程度上迎合他這一問題上引發分歧，C. Ryan Barber、Joe Palazzolo與Josh Dawsey報導。

6. 圖說報導
我們的地圖描繪了18項創造現代世界的美國發明。從東北部繁忙的實驗室到西南部偏遠的沙漠，美國人的創造力無處不在。這張地圖標示出與定義美國250年歷史的種種突破相關的地點。

7. 今日看點
- 世界盃：西班牙對比利時，在加州英格塢舉行。
- 財報：達美航空

8. 數字看新聞
48.6億美元——伊朗戰爭中出現了一位意外的贏家：非洲首富。精煉石油產品需求激增，使奈及利亞實業家阿里科·丹格特今年身家增加約48.6億美元，淨資產達到約348億美元。丹格特為建造耗資200億美元的煉油廠「歷經地獄般的考驗」。如今這位大亨開始收穫成果：這座煉油廠2月達到滿載產能——恰好趕上向全球市場供應無需經過荷莫茲海峽運輸的燃料。

9. 最後看點
人們正排隊觀賞一株聞起來像垃圾桶的植物。屍花在溫室園藝與植物園這個沉靜的世界裡向來是吸睛焦點。它們史前般的外觀，加上數年才開一次花的等待，讓人著迷。但最大的吸引力或許是花朵綻放時那股如死屍般的惡臭——人們願意排隊數小時只為聞上一聞。

10. 新聞室之外
- 評論：川普大肆宣揚豐田將擴大在德州卡車產能的消息，此舉是在轉移焦點，掩蓋他的邊境稅正推高成本、卻未能帶來製造業復興這一慘淡現實。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Inside Graham Platner's Rise and Fall
emails.contentEn:
The Red Flag That Foreshadowed Graham Platner's Fall
Plus, Costco's 'secret weapons' are becoming millionaires, and Wall Street's peace trade collides with renewed Iran fighting

1. FROM MY DESK
Graham Platner is out of the race for Senate in Maine, ending a run that had drawn broad grassroots support but was plagued by controversy. The red flag that led to his implosion was hiding in plain sight. Turning to the Iran war: We look at how President Trump's peace plan fell apart—and how the explosive end of the ceasefire is threatening to reopen ruptures in the oil market. For a lighter read this morning, I highly recommend our profile of Tony Barzar, a Costco cashier-turned-millionaire—and one of the retailer's secret weapons.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES
- After a partial collapse risk at the former Pfizer headquarters in New York, investors and lenders say they are reconsidering future commitments to complex real-estate conversions.
- Jewish Democrats considering 2028 presidential bids are confronting their party's hostility toward Israel.
- As the race for artificial-intelligence supremacy heats up, Beijing is considering tightening its grip on its homegrown technology that American companies love.
- The Trump administration's pressure campaign against Cuba is zeroing in on the island's most valuable export: the doctors and nurses it deploys abroad.

3. LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
S&P 500 Futures 7,541.25 (+0.17%); DJIA Futures 52,619.00 (-0.01%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 29,643.75 (+0.59%) as of 7/9/2026, 6:04:58 AM ET.
- The merger of Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery is set to emerge with nearly $80 billion in debt—a burden that could weigh on decisions including streaming investments and sports rights.
- The taboo against owning cigarette stocks hasn't gone away, but new gray areas are emerging, writes Carol Ryan.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
Counterfeit air-bag parts are killing U.S. drivers. The government can't stop it. After at least 10 deaths, regulators are racing to stop dangerous counterfeit air-bag parts from ending up in used cars. But unlike a traditional recall, investigators don't know where many of the parts came from or where they ended up. Ryan Felton traces the gray-market supply chain, from online marketplaces to repair shops, that has made the parts nearly impossible to track.

5. REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK
Joe Parkinson and Drew Hinshaw: Our series on Europe's rupture with America came to us first in a whisper, and then in a crescendo, as we realized that behind closed doors officials on both sides of the Atlantic were full of emotion and reproach when they spoke about the state of the world's most powerful military alliance. The White House felt let down that Europe didn't do more to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. European governments, after the Greenland crisis, had come to see the U.S. not just as an unpredictable ally but as a potential threat. The questions for us became: What was Europe going to do about it? And what were America's best friends really saying, in their most candid moments?
It took months of reporting as we traveled across Europe and managed to speak with heads of government, their ministers and top aides to reconstruct important meetings, and even review classified assessments that European intelligence agencies have given leaders struggling to navigate the new Washington. What we learned was just how influential Mark Carney was in shaping how Europeans saw the U.S. and the road forward. Canada's prime minister has been regularly texting, calling and even jogging with European presidents, prime ministers and chancellors, many of whom he knew from his days as Bank of England governor. He and his European partners face a long road as they try to make their governments less reliant on a superpower that has, historically, been their protector.

6. SEE THE STORY
Gen Z and Millennial collectors are turning vintage IKEA into investment pieces. The Swedish retailer built its brand on bringing affordable furniture design to the masses. Paradoxically, its vintage stock is now out of reach for many buyers. For years, collectors have sought out items from IKEA's early decades—especially rare products made before its 1985 debut in the U.S. Today, a growing cohort of millennials and Gen Zers is fueling a market expansion driven by nostalgia, appreciation for good design and recognition of future value. The average IKEA item listed on the online marketplace Chairish now carries a price tag of nearly $1,000.

7. HAPPENING TODAY
- World Cup: France vs. Morocco in Boston
- Economic data: U.S. jobless claims, existing-home sales
- Earnings: PepsiCo

8. THE NUMBER
22.2% — That's the increase in the median price of a single-family home in San Francisco from May 2025 to May 2026. A land grab is under way in the area, where AI wealth is already driving up prices. Buyers are racing to snap up properties ahead of highly anticipated potential public offerings from giants like OpenAI and Anthropic.

9. AND FINALLY…
Buc-ee's is on a rampage. No mascot is safe. The beloved rest-stop chain is expanding at a steady clip around the U.S. That pace is matched only by its race to knock out rival mascots—including an alligator, a duck and chickens. Its federal trademark lawsuit against Mickey the Moose, an institution across northern Ohio, has left some Buckeyes sour on Buc-ee's, which opened its first store in the state this spring.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
- Opinion: The Trump administration's suggestion that the Smithsonian Institution's National Museum of American History offer a less biased approach to American history isn't an attempt to whitewash the country's complexity or its difficult chapters.
emails.contentZh:
預示格雷厄姆·普拉特納垮台的警訊
另外，好市多的「秘密武器」正成為百萬富翁，華爾街的「和平交易」與伊朗戰事重燃相互碰撞

1. 編輯手記
格雷厄姆·普拉特納退出緬因州參議院選舉，結束了這場獲得廣泛基層支持、卻爭議纏身的競選之路。導致他崩盤的警訊其實早已顯而易見。轉向伊朗戰爭：我們探討川普總統的和平計畫如何瓦解——以及停火協議的爆炸性終結，如何有可能重新撕裂石油市場的裂痕。今天早上想讀點輕鬆的內容，我強烈推薦我們對托尼·巴薩爾的專訪，他是從好市多收銀員變身百萬富翁的傳奇人物，也是這家零售商的「秘密武器」之一。

2. 今日頭條
- 紐約前輝瑞總部大樓出現部分倒塌風險後，投資人與放款機構表示，他們正重新考慮未來對複雜房地產改建案的承諾。
- 考慮參選2028年總統的猶太裔民主黨人，正面臨黨內對以色列的敵意。
- 隨著人工智慧霸權之爭升溫，北京正考慮加強對美國企業喜愛的本土技術的管控。
- 川普政府對古巴的施壓行動，正瞄準該島最有價值的出口項目：其派遣海外的醫生和護士。

3. 市場直擊
截至美東時間2026年7月9日上午6:04:58，標普500期貨報7,541.25點（+0.17%）；道瓊期貨報52,619.00點（-0.01%）；那斯達克100期貨報29,643.75點（+0.59%）。
- 派拉蒙天空之舞與華納兄弟探索的合併案完成後，將背負近800億美元的債務——這一負擔可能會影響包括串流投資和體育版權在內的多項決策。
- 對持有菸草股的忌諱並未消失，但新的灰色地帶正在浮現，Carol Ryan撰文分析。

4. 獨家搶先報導
偽造安全氣囊零件正在奪走美國駕駛人的性命，政府卻無力阻止。在至少10人死亡後，監管機構正競相阻止危險的偽造安全氣囊零件流入二手車市場。但與傳統召回不同的是，調查人員不知道許多零件的來源，也不知道它們最終流向何處。Ryan Felton追蹤了從網路市場到維修廠這條幾乎無法追蹤的灰色市場供應鏈。

5. 記者筆記
Joe Parkinson與Drew Hinshaw：我們關於歐洲與美國關係破裂的系列報導，起初只是竊竊私語，後來逐漸擴大成一片喧囂，我們意識到，當大西洋兩岸的官員在閉門會議中談論這個世界上最強大軍事聯盟的現狀時，話語中充滿了情緒和責難。白宮認為歐洲在重新開放荷莫茲海峽問題上沒有盡到應盡的努力，感到失望。歐洲各國政府在格陵蘭危機之後，已開始將美國視為不僅是難以預測的盟友，更是潛在的威脅。我們面臨的問題變成了：歐洲打算怎麼應對？美國最親密的盟友在最坦誠的時刻，究竟在說些什麼？
我們花了數月時間走訪歐洲各國，設法與各國政府首腦、部長及高級幕僚交談，重建重要會議的內容，甚至審閱了歐洲情報機構提供給各國領袖、協助他們應對新華盛頓局勢的機密評估報告。我們了解到的是，馬克·卡尼在塑造歐洲人如何看待美國及未來道路方面，發揮了多大的影響力。這位加拿大總理定期與歐洲各國總統、總理和總理們通簡訊、通電話，甚至一起慢跑——他與許多人是在擔任英格蘭銀行行長期間結識的。他和他的歐洲夥伴們，在試圖讓各自政府減少對這個歷來一直是他們保護者的超級大國的依賴上，還有很長的路要走。

6. 圖說報導
Z世代與千禧世代收藏家正把復古IKEA家具變成投資珍品。這家瑞典零售商靠著把平價家具設計帶給大眾而打響品牌。諷刺的是，如今其復古庫存卻讓許多買家望而卻步。多年來，收藏家一直在搜尋IKEA早期幾十年的產品——尤其是1985年進軍美國市場前生產的稀有商品。如今，越來越多千禧世代和Z世代因懷舊情懷、對優良設計的欣賞，以及對未來增值潛力的認可，正推動這個市場擴張。目前在網路市集Chairish上架的IKEA商品平均售價已接近1,000美元。

7. 今日看點
- 世界盃：法國對摩洛哥，在波士頓舉行
- 經濟數據：美國失業救濟申請人數、成屋銷售
- 財報：百事公司

8. 數字看新聞
22.2%——這是舊金山獨棟住宅中位數價格從2025年5月到2026年5月的漲幅。這個地區正上演一場土地爭奪戰，AI財富已經在推高房價。買家正競相搶購房產，以期在OpenAI和Anthropic等巨頭備受期待的潛在上市之前卡位。

9. 最後看點
Buc-ee's正大肆擴張，沒有一個吉祥物是安全的。這家深受喜愛的休息站連鎖店正以穩定的速度在美國各地擴張，其擴張速度只有它擊敗對手吉祥物——包括一隻鱷魚、一隻鴨子和幾隻雞——的速度能與之匹敵。該公司對俄亥俄州北部地標吉祥物「麋鹿米奇」提起的聯邦商標訴訟，讓一些俄亥俄州人對今年春天才在該州開設首家分店的Buc-ee's心生不滿。

10. 新聞室之外
- 評論：川普政府建議史密森尼學會國家美國歷史博物館，對美國歷史採取較不偏頗的敘事方式，這並非試圖粉飾這個國家的複雜性或其艱難篇章。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Democrats Scramble to Stave Off Disaster
emails.contentEn:
Good morning. As the NATO summit convenes for its second day in Turkey, a key leader to watch is Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who steered Europe away from President Trump. In New York, mere blocks from our newsroom, contractors are racing to stabilize a high-rise that was at risk of collapsing. We take you inside the conversion project at the heart of the crisis. The U.S. is out of the World Cup, but the tournament drama continues: Argentina's Lionel Messi set a new record for missed penalty kicks—yet the defending champions still managed a last-minute comeback to advance.

TODAY'S HEADLINES
1. Trump said he believes the ceasefire with Iran is over after another round of Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Apple is ramping up its investment in U.S.-made chips, with plans to spend more than $30 billion with Broadcom in the next five years. USDA officials called grocers including Walmart, Kroger and Albertsons about lowering beef prices ahead of the July 4 holiday weekend. Florida cities are already cutting spending ahead of a pivotal property-tax vote in November. A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer fatally shot a Mexican immigrant who was trying to evade arrest in Texas. War in Ukraine: A look inside Kyiv's heavily bombed Lukyanivka district reveals a resilient neighborhood determined to carry on with daily life despite the Kremlin's missile barrages.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
2. DJIA Futures 52,523.00 (-674.00, -1.27%); S&P 500 Futures 7,478.25 (-73.00, -0.97%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 28,992.50 (-399.00, -1.36%) as of 7/8/2026, 6:02:42 AM ET.
Anthropic's political risks are real, but OpenAI's loom even larger, writes Asa Fitch.

READ IT HERE FIRST
3. Smucker's $5 billion bet on the Twinkie flopped. Here's why. In 2024, Mark Smucker, chief executive of food giant J.M. Smucker, took the stage at an industry conference and bit into a golden, crème-filled Twinkie. "Tastes like growth," he said. His company had just acquired Hostess, the maker of Twinkies, in a $5 billion deal and it seemed like a coup. The Covid-19 pandemic had supercharged America's snacking habit: Some 70% of consumers were eating at least two a day, Smucker says. Buying the owner of Ding Dongs and Donettes gave the jam-and-jelly maker entry into a $65 billion market for snacks. But three years later, the deal isn't tasting quite so sweet, reports Jesse Newman.

4. This Canadian steered Europe away from the U.S. Facing threats from Trump, Mark Carney has emerged as the unexpected central figure in a high-stakes project to reshape the Western alliance. The Journal spoke to heads of government, their ministers and top aides to reconstruct the closed-door meetings where the partnership began to splinter. This is the second in a two-part series from Drew Hinshaw, Joe Parkinson and Daniel Michaels revealing the contents of deliberations among America's allies forced to debate how they might salvage their alliance—or prepare for its unraveling.

5. The Platner succession crisis lays bare Democrats' deep divisions ahead of the midterms. Democrats are scrambling to stave off disaster in the pivotal Maine Senate race as the fallout from damaging new allegations against Graham Platner threatens to intensify simmering rifts within the party. The progressive and establishment factions of the party are already clashing over a potential replacement for Platner in Maine after prominent politicians on both sides called on the oyster farmer to drop out following allegations Monday that Platner sexually assaulted a woman he was romantically involved with. Platner has denied the allegations. The jockeying comes amid an increasingly fraught nationwide battle for the party's identity ahead of November's midterm elections, report Sabrina Rodriguez, Tarini Parti and Eliza Collins.

SEE THE STORY
6. Fans refuse to let the Land Rover die. Ever since Jaguar Land Rover ceased production of the classic Land Rover Defender, fans have been snapping up discontinued models and breathing new life into them. Now, the value of old Land Rovers is rocketing as a new generation of enthusiasts falls in love with this simple off-roader, and they can sell for up to $170,000 in the U.S.

HAPPENING TODAY
7. Economic data: The Federal Reserve is scheduled to release minutes from its June meeting, which could shed light on whether officials still foresee a rate hike this year. Earnings: Costco, Levi Strauss

THE NUMBER
8. 28% — That's the hefty premium increase Centene is seeking for its 2027 Obamacare plans in Washington state—after already boosting rates by 35% this year. It is part of a broader trend as some of the country's largest Affordable Care Act insurers push for double-digit hikes for the second year in a row. Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Illinois is following a similar path, requesting a 15% increase for 2027—on top of a 28% increase this year.

AND FINALLY...
9. Lionel Messi is the greatest player ever. Why is he so bad at penalty kicks? For more than 20 years, Messi has been able to do anything he wants on a soccer pitch, bending the game to his will and conjuring otherworldly moves out of thin air. But there's one skill that seems to leave this 5-foot-7 maestro looking up at everyone else. It just happens to be one of the easiest shots in soccer. We look inside the data to explain why Argentina's captain struggles from 12 yards out.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
10. Opinion: By rescinding endorsements and pushing out Graham Platner, big-name Democrats now try to salvage their chances of unseating Sen. Susan Collins. But they can't say they weren't warned.
emails.contentZh:
民主黨拼命補救以避免災難
早安。隨著北約峰會在土耳其進入第二天議程，值得關注的關鍵人物是加拿大總理馬克·卡尼，他引導歐洲逐漸疏遠川普總統。在紐約，距離我們新聞編輯室僅幾條街之遙，承包商正競相穩固一棟有倒塌風險的高樓。我們帶你深入了解這場危機核心的改建工程。美國隊已無緣世界盃，但賽事的戲劇性仍在延續：阿根廷的梅西刷新了罰球失誤的紀錄——但這支衛冕冠軍隊仍在最後一刻完成逆轉晉級。

今日頭條
1. 川普表示，在伊朗再次對荷莫茲海峽船隻發動攻擊後，他認為與伊朗的停火協議已經破裂。蘋果正加大對美國製晶片的投資，計畫未來五年內向博通投入超過300億美元。美國農業部官員致電沃爾瑪、克羅格和奧爾巴森等雜貨商，商討在7月4日假期週末前降低牛肉價格。佛羅里達州各城市已開始在11月一場關鍵的財產稅表決前削減開支。一名美國移民及海關執法局官員在德州開槍打死一名試圖躲避逮捕的墨西哥移民。烏克蘭戰事：深入基輔遭到猛烈轟炸的盧基揚尼夫卡區，這個社區儘管遭受克里姆林宮的飛彈連番襲擊，仍展現出堅韌不拔、堅持日常生活的一面。

市場直擊

獨家搶先報導
3. 史姆克花50億美元押注Twinkie（奶油夾心蛋糕）卻踢到鐵板，箇中原因為何？2024年，食品巨頭J.M.史姆克的執行長馬克·史姆克在一場產業大會上登台，咬了一口金黃色、夾著奶油餡的Twinkie，說道：「嚐起來就是成長的味道。」他的公司當時剛以50億美元收購了Twinkie製造商Hostess，看似一樁妙招。新冠疫情大幅推升了美國人的零食消費習慣：史姆克表示，約有70%的消費者每天至少吃兩個。收購Ding Dongs和Donettes的母公司，讓這家果醬果凍製造商得以打入一個規模650億美元的零食市場。但三年後，這樁交易嚐起來卻不再那麼甜蜜，Jesse Newman報導。

4. 這位加拿大人引導歐洲逐漸疏遠美國。面對川普的威脅，馬克·卡尼已意外成為重塑西方聯盟這項高風險計畫的核心人物。本報訪問了多國政府首腦、部長及高級幕僚，重建了這場夥伴關係開始出現裂痕的閉門會議內容。這是Drew Hinshaw、Joe Parkinson與Daniel Michaels兩部曲系列報導的第二篇，揭露美國盟友被迫討論如何挽救聯盟——或為其瓦解做準備——的內部審議內容。

5. 普拉特納的接班危機，暴露出民主黨在期中選舉前的深刻分歧。隨著針對格雷厄姆·普拉特納的最新指控餘波持續發酵，威脅加劇黨內暗流洶湧的裂痕，民主黨正拼命補救緬因州這場關鍵的參議院選戰，避免釀成災難。在週一有指控稱普拉特納性侵一名與他有戀愛關係的女性、雙方陣營重量級政治人物都呼籲這位牡蠣養殖業者退選後，民主黨進步派與建制派已就緬因州潛在的替代人選展開角力。普拉特納否認了這些指控。這場角力發生在11月期中選舉前，全國範圍內爭奪該黨定位的戰役日益緊張之際，Sabrina Rodriguez、Tarini Parti與Eliza Collins報導。

圖說報導
6. 車迷們不肯讓路虎就此消亡。自從捷豹路虎停產經典的路虎衛士車型以來，車迷們便一直搶購停產車款並為它們注入新生命。如今，隨著新一代愛好者迷上這款樸實的越野車，二手路虎的價值正快速飆升，在美國售價最高可達17萬美元。

最後看點
9. 梅西是史上最偉大的球員，為什麼罰球卻踢得這麼差？20多年來，梅西在足球場上幾乎無所不能，隨心所欲地掌控比賽節奏，憑空變出令人歎為觀止的動作。但有一項技能，卻讓這位身高僅5呎7吋的球場大師顯得技不如人——偏偏還是足球場上最容易的射門方式之一。我們深入數據，解析這位阿根廷隊長為何在12碼罰球點屢屢受挫。

新聞室之外
10. 評論：透過撤回背書並逼退格雷厄姆·普拉特納，知名民主黨人如今試圖挽救擊敗參議員蘇珊·柯林斯的機會。但他們不能說自己沒有被提醒過。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Silicon Valley's New Turf War
emails.contentEn:
The biggest stories we're tracking this morning all have a common theme: war. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired missiles at two commercial ships near the Strait of Hormuz—an escalation that threatens to complicate negotiations to end the war. The Journal's Yaroslav Trofimov examines how drone warfare, AI-guided weapons and other battlefield innovations are reshaping modern combat in Ukraine and beyond. And in Silicon Valley, a different kind of war is brewing: AI giants like OpenAI and Anthropic are fighting to secure new business customers—and handing out tons of free computing power to woo startup founders.

TODAY'S HEADLINES
1. Belgium knocked the U.S. out of the World Cup after a political firestorm that saw American striker Folarin Balogun return to the pitch. Europe is racing to plug security holes after the U.S.'s NATO pullback. At the same time, Canada is rushing to build up its military as its relationship with the U.S. frays. Maine Senate Democratic nominee Graham Platner said his campaign would reflect on the "best path forward" after a woman he was romantically involved with publicly alleged that he sexually assaulted her, an allegation he denied. Some of the largest banks in the country have been exploring an acquisition that could allow them to get around limits on fees they earn on debit-card transactions. In Clearwater, Fla., locals are clashing with Scientologists over the future of the seaside city's downtown.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
2. DJIA Futures 53,495.00 (+123.00, +0.23%); S&P 500 Futures 7,581.50 (-10.00, -0.13%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 29,646.75 (-294.25, -0.98%) as of 7/7/2026, 5:55:53 AM ET.
Big tech reining in its artificial-intelligence spending may be a tantalizing prospect for some, but it would also be a costly one, writes Dan Gallagher.

READ IT HERE FIRST
3. AI giants are handing out tons of free computing power to grab a share in startups. Startup founders are enjoying a wave of computing credits and fielding competing offers from AI-model makers racing to land new enterprise customers. Cursor, the AI-coding company bought by Elon Musk's SpaceX, offered a 75% discount through July 5. The pitched battle for business users comes as AI companies seek lasting streams of revenue. Offers from organizations such as OpenAI and Anthropic are so rich that some early-stage startup founders say they won't need to raise money as soon as they expected, and others have been able to play AI companies off one another, report Kate Clark, Berber Jin and Angel Au-Yeung.

4. There's a new way of war, but is it evolution or revolution? The way wars are fought is changing fast, as new technologies upend military doctrines on everything from procurement to executing operations. But just how radical will this transformation be in years to come? And are the hundreds of billions of dollars being invested by the U.S., its allies and rivals in new tanks, planes and warships going to become the equivalent of buying horses and arrows on the eve of machine guns and howitzers? Yaroslav Trofimov examines how militaries worldwide are grappling with breakneck technological change and the lessons from Ukraine and the Persian Gulf.

5. The Iran war has oil-rich Alaska freaked out about $9 gas. Remote towns and villages in the state aren't connected to the road system, so they pay hefty premiums to procure gasoline, heating oil and diesel for cranking out electricity. Many communities had no choice this year but to place their fuel orders in the spring, just as the Iran war sent prices soaring. That means that even if the U.S. and Iran reach a peace deal and the strait reopens permanently, rural Alaskans will be stuck with exorbitant energy prices long after they have come down for the rest of the country. The state's plight is a paradox given its vast fossil-fuel resources—and its place at the heart of President Trump's energy agenda, reports Benoît Morenne.

SEE THE STORY
6. These workers told us how they do their jobs in 116-degree heat. India regularly experiences the type of blazing weather the U.S. has faced in recent weeks. The Journal spoke to workers in and around New Delhi—where the peak temperature this summer hit 115.7 degrees Fahrenheit—to hear how they cope with ever more ferocious summers.

HAPPENING TODAY
7. The NATO Summit begins in Ankara, Turkey. SpaceX is set to join the Nasdaq 100 index before the opening bell. World Cup: Argentina vs. Egypt in Atlanta; Switzerland vs. Colombia in Vancouver.

THE NUMBER
8. 40% — Airlines are finally getting some relief at the jet-fuel pump: Fuel prices are down 40% from their peak in April. But analysts say fares aren't likely to follow. Travelers are continuing to pay the higher prices—and carriers aren't rushing to bring back the flights and routes that were trimmed during oil's surge.

AND FINALLY...
9. People keep sneaking into an empty IBM campus. This town has had enough. In Somers, N.Y., the long-vacant former IBM campus has become a magnet for "urban explorers" who prowl abandoned buildings. The global "urbex" phenomenon isn't new, but it's been turbocharged by artsy videos on Instagram and TikTok that spur others to create their own posts, luring still more curiosity seekers. The monthslong influx has rattled the Westchester County town of 21,500 that calls itself the "Cradle of the American Circus."

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
10. Opinion: OpenAI now wants more regulation and taxation and even partial government ownership. Is this the devil's political testing of CEO Sam Altman?

矽谷的新地盤之戰
今天早上我們追蹤的重大新聞都有一個共同主題：戰爭。伊朗伊斯蘭革命衛隊向荷莫茲海峽附近的兩艘商船發射飛彈——這一升級行動可能使結束戰爭的談判更加複雜。本報Yaroslav Trofimov探討無人機戰爭、AI導引武器等戰場創新如何重塑烏克蘭及其他地區的現代戰鬥形態。而在矽谷，另一種戰爭正醞釀中：OpenAI和Anthropic等AI巨頭正激烈爭奪新的企業客戶——並發放大量免費運算資源，藉此拉攏新創公司創辦人。
