迷因股炒家有了新的最愛速食連鎖店：在大批散戶交易者湧入這家業績低迷的餐飲業者後，Wendy's股價本週飆漲。Dan Gallagher撰文指出，記憶體晶片熱潮的長期威脅在於創新。

獨家搶先報導
3. 伊朗重創了一座美軍海軍基地，並促使美國重新盤算戰略，以下是事件經過。當伊朗的飛彈和無人機瞄準美國在中東海軍行動的神經中樞時，部分攻擊確實命中目標。位於巴林的美國海軍基地在2月下旬到6月間屢遭鎖定攻擊。根據本報對衛星影像、社群媒體影片以及現役及退役軍人訪談的分析，成功突破防禦的攻擊造成了大範圍損害——這項損害五角大廈從未公開承認。這座基地連同至少另外20處美軍據點遭到攻擊的影響，正促使五角大廈重新評估其在該地區的整體軍事部署，Anika Arora Seth、Shelby Holliday、Denise Blostein與Milàn Czerny報導。

4. 我們的世界盃球迷歡樂指數矩陣，揭曉誰玩得開心、誰過得悲慘。有些球迷在世界盃度過人生最歡樂的時光，另一些則正倒數著回家的日子。為了量化這種歡樂與悲慘的程度，我們為賽事中的每個支持者群體設計了一套排名。我們的指數將球隊在場上的表現與16個主辦城市球迷的享受程度進行對比繪製。Jonathan Clegg與Joshua Robinson考量了從預期進球數到當地天氣狀況，乃至身穿蘇格蘭格紋短裙、汗流浹背的球迷盛大遊行等各種因素。

5. 華爾街意識到，光靠金錢無法對抗馬姆達尼。去年佐蘭·馬姆達尼當選紐約市長時，華爾街許多人選擇保持沉默，靜觀這位民主社會主義者將如何治理城市。如今，在他的門生和盟友本週橫掃初選之後，這座城市的部分商業菁英正準備採取行動——至少他們計畫這麼做。在捐款人與政治策略師之間的通話中，事後檢討的結論相當直白：光靠金錢，無法拯救那些基層動員薄弱、訊息模糊不清的候選人。但下一步該怎麼走，目前仍不明朗，Kevin T. Dugan報導。

圖說報導
6. 來做我們的測驗，看看你的生活方式透露出你屬於哪個經濟階層。美國人認為，階層不僅由收入決定，也取決於態度和生活方式的選擇。這是本報近期一項調查的結論，該調查詢問了2,000人認為自己屬於哪個經濟階層。

今日看點
7. 世界盃：烏拉圭對西班牙，在瓜達拉哈拉舉行；埃及對伊朗，在西雅圖舉行；挪威對法國，在麻州福克斯堡舉行，另有其他賽事。經濟數據：密西根大學公布6月消費者信心終值。電影《女超人》上映。

數字看新聞
89.9萬美元——在南達科他州西部的黑山地區，歷史悠久的Lead地區57754郵遞區號，5月中位數掛牌價達到89.9萬美元，根據Realtor.com的客製分析，成為該州房價最高的市場。這個人口約3,000人的社區，與南達科他州以平原著稱的刻板印象大相逕庭，感覺更像是一座西部滑雪村，而非中西部農業小鎮。

最後看點
9. 美國人想為當初懷疑歐洲熱浪而道歉。歐洲的熱浪正變得越來越頻繁——也越來越致命，本週的熱浪是兩個月內的第二波。英國氣溫接近華氏100度，巴黎等城市甚至超過這個數字。這波熱浪讓來自美國一些最炎熱、最潮濕州份的僑民和遊客感到徹底困惑：一輩子在酷熱天氣中生活，怎麼會沒有為此做好準備？

新聞室之外
10. 評論：自由派一如預期地譴責保守派最高法院大法官為川普的大規模驅逐出境政策開了綠燈。但法官的職責是按照法律文字進行解釋，而非強加自己的政策偏好。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: A Third Wave of Inflation, Driven by AI
emails.contentEn:
A wave of progressive victories in New York by candidates backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani didn't just expose deep ideological fractures within the Democratic Party—it escalated a high-stakes battle for its direction. Mamdani burnished his role as a kingmaker, though the sweep further strains relations between Jewish voters and the Democratic Party. Globally, the cultural fascination with socialism can no longer be dismissed as mere vibes. The Journal's Greg Ip explores how the stigma surrounding state ownership is fading—and why, from Indonesia to Belgium, nationalization is back in vogue.

TODAY'S HEADLINES
1. Two powerful earthquakes hit Venezuela, causing buildings to collapse in Caracas, rattling other cities and leaving dozens dead. President Trump canceled a signing ceremony for a bipartisan housing bill, berated GOP lawmakers and criticized European allies during a whirlwind day. CoinEx, a crypto exchange founded by a Chinese engineer, has become a major hub for illicit Iranian cash. Meet the Ukrainian soldiers who refuse to quit after years on the front line. Jeffrey Epstein's longtime executive assistant Lesley Groff was interviewed by the House Oversight Committee about her association with the sex offender. Here's what she told Congress.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS
2. DJIA Futures 52,334.00 (+55.00, +0.11%); S&P 500 Futures 7,481.50 (+53.25, +0.72%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 30,148.50 (+634.25, +2.15%) as of 6/25/2026, 5:58:51 AM ET.
Micron's blockbuster earnings quiets the artificial intelligence doubters. Domino's still holds potential value for investors even though the American appetite for pizza is waning, writes David Wainer.

READ IT HERE FIRST
3. Forget work. Passive income is the new American dream. If the mythos of the American dream is to work hard and get ahead, it's being eclipsed for some by the dream of not having to work at all. It's not that the fantasy is new. But it is gaining fuel from a growing feeling that traditional work is broken. On social media, passive-income obsessives test out eccentric schemes and compare notes. Some seekers make real money and win back time. But many ideas thrown around online are duds or, worse, scams. And lately, AI is putting the quest on steroids: People are pumping chatbots for moneymaking hacks and using content generators to rapidly churn out videos, books and other media they hope to monetize online, reports Joe Pinsker.

4. A lurid lawsuit, a salami scandal and a trash-can thief are vexing JPMorgan's PR department. They're being called the all-star team of infamous JPMorgan Chase employees. A woman who dumped out and walked off with a special-edition Knicks trash can in broad daylight. An investment banker whose lawsuit alleged sexual harassment by a former colleague in excruciating detail. A startup founder who expensed "cellulite butter" to the bank during her trial for defrauding the bank. Their stories all went viral because of details that seemed, at times, surreal. Candace Choi and Ben Glickman offer a guide to the (former) employees who've recently landed in the spotlight.

5. The data-center boom is sparking a third wave of inflation. Inflation has a new catalyst: America's massive AI build-out is beginning to push up prices on everything from smartphones to electricity. The question now is how widely that build-out might ripple through the economy, and how long it could keep inflation elevated. The answers will have big consequences, reports Justin Lahart.

SEE THE STORY
6. A Malibu mansion seen in 'The O.C.' and 'Austin Powers' is asking $90 million. A roughly 17,700-square-foot blufftop mansion in Malibu, Calif.,—which served as a set in movies and television shows such as "Austin Powers" and "The O.C."—is coming on the market for $90 million. Known as Venezia Pacifica, the nine-bedroom residence is on a cul-de-sac in Point Dume, with roughly 176 feet of bluff frontage overlooking the Pacific near one of the best surf breaks in Southern California.

HAPPENING TODAY
7. World Cup: U.S. vs. Turkey in Los Angeles; Japan vs. Sweden in Dallas; Ecuador vs. Germany in East Rutherford, N.J., among other matches. Economic data: The Fed's preferred inflation measure, the personal consumption expenditures price index, is released. Earnings: BlackBerry, Darden Restaurants

THE NUMBER
8. $15 billion — It took years to discover that an Hermès fortune was missing, and subsequent legal proceedings have yet to untangle who is to blame. Hermès heir Nicolas Puech filed a lawsuit last year valuing his alleged losses at more than $15 billion, naming his former wealth manager, luxury group LVMH and its chief executive, Bernard Arnault, among the defendants. Meanwhile, prosecutors in Paris are probing the matter and recently placed three lawyers under formal investigation. All three have denied wrongdoing. Now, LVMH is fighting back.

AND FINALLY...
9. Meet the Harvard data nerd defending America's goal at the World Cup: Matt Freese, who holds an Ivy League economics degree, came out of practically nowhere to secure the job as the U.S. national team's starting goalkeeper. The 27-year-old's analytical approach and love of numbers have been integral to his rise. Ever since he was a kid, he has looked out onto a soccer pitch and understood it as math.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
10. Opinion: Tuesday's primary sweep in New York by the Democratic Socialists of America was a rout for the far left over the left.
emails.contentZh:
由AI驅動的第三波通膨
市長佐蘭·馬姆達尼支持的候選人在紐約掀起一波進步派勝選浪潮，這不僅暴露了民主黨內部深刻的意識形態裂痕，也升級了一場攸關該黨未來走向的高風險之爭。馬姆達尼進一步鞏固了自己作為造王者的角色，儘管這場全面勝利也讓猶太裔選民與民主黨之間的關係更加緊張。放眼全球，各界對社會主義的文化迷戀已不能再被視為單純的氛圍現象。本報Greg Ip探討圍繞國有化的污名如何逐漸消退——以及為何從印尼到比利時，國有化正重新蔚為風潮。

今日頭條
1. 兩次強震襲擊委內瑞拉，造成加拉加斯多棟建築倒塌，並波及其他城市，導致數十人死亡。川普總統在忙亂的一天中，取消了一項兩黨住房法案的簽署儀式，斥責共和黨議員，並批評歐洲盟友。由一名中國工程師創辦的加密貨幣交易所CoinEx，已成為伊朗非法資金流動的主要樞紐。認識那些在前線多年後仍拒絕放棄的烏克蘭士兵。傑弗里·愛潑斯坦的長期行政助理萊斯利·格羅夫接受眾議院監督委員會就其與這名性犯罪者的關係進行訪談，以下是她向國會透露的內容。

市場直擊
2. 截至美東時間2026年6月25日上午5:58:51，道瓊期貨報52,334.00點（+55.00，+0.11%）；標普500期貨報7,481.50點（+53.25，+0.72%）；那斯達克100期貨報30,148.50點（+634.25，+2.15%）。
美光亮眼的財報讓人工智慧懷疑論者噤聲。David Wainer撰文指出，儘管美國人對披薩的熱情正在消退，達美樂對投資人而言仍具潛在價值。

獨家搶先報導
3. 別工作了，被動收入才是新美國夢。如果說美國夢的傳統敘事是努力工作、力爭上游，那麼對某些人而言，這個夢想正逐漸被「完全不用工作」的夢想所掩蓋。這種幻想本身並不新鮮，但隨著人們日益覺得傳統工作模式已然崩壞，這股風潮正持續獲得助力。在社群媒體上，被動收入的狂熱追求者不斷嘗試各種稀奇古怪的方案，並互相交流心得。有些追尋者確實賺到了真金白銀，也贏回了時間。但網路上流傳的許多點子不是行不通，就是根本是騙局。而近來AI更是為這股追逐熱潮火上加油：人們不斷向聊天機器人索取賺錢秘訣，並利用內容生成工具快速產出影片、書籍等各種媒體內容，希望藉此在網路上變現，Joe Pinsker報導。

4. 一樁香豔訴訟案、一起臘腸醜聞，加上一名垃圾桶竊賊，正讓摩根大通的公關部門頭痛不已。他們被戲稱為摩根大通惡名昭彰員工的「全明星隊」：一名女子在光天化日之下倒空並偷走一個尼克隊特別版垃圾桶；一名投資銀行家提起訴訟，鉅細靡遺地指控遭前同事性騷擾；一名新創公司創辦人在因詐騙該銀行而受審期間，竟向銀行報銷「消脂霜」費用。這些故事之所以在網路上瘋傳，正是因為其中的細節有時顯得超現實。Candace Choi與Ben Glickman為讀者整理了這些近期成為焦點的（前）員工指南。

5. 資料中心熱潮正引爆第三波通膨。通膨出現了新的催化劑：美國大規模的AI基礎設施擴建，正開始推高從智慧型手機到電力等各類商品的價格。如今的問題是，這波擴建究竟會在多大範圍內波及整體經濟，又會讓通膨維持高位多久。這些答案將帶來重大影響，Justin Lahart報導。

圖說報導
6. 曾出現在《The O.C.》和《王牌大賤諜》中的一棟馬里布豪宅，開價9千萬美元。這棟位於加州馬里布崖頂、面積約1萬7,700平方英尺的豪宅——曾在《王牌大賤諜》和《The O.C.》等電影電視劇中作為拍攝場景——即將以9千萬美元的價格上市求售。這棟名為Venezia Pacifica的九臥室豪宅，坐落在Point Dume一條死巷內，擁有約176英呎的崖岸線，俯瞰太平洋，緊鄰南加州最佳衝浪點之一。

今日看點
7. 世界盃：美國對土耳其，在洛杉磯舉行；日本對瑞典，在達拉斯舉行；厄瓜多對德國，在紐澤西州東拉瑟福德舉行，另有其他賽事。經濟數據：聯準會偏好的通膨指標——個人消費支出物價指數公布。財報：黑莓、Darden餐廳集團

數字看新聞
150億美元——花了數年時間才發現愛馬仕家族的一筆財富不翼而飛，後續的法律訴訟至今仍未釐清責任歸屬。愛馬仕繼承人尼可拉斯·普厄什去年提起訴訟，指稱其損失估計超過150億美元，被告名單包括他的前財富管理顧問、精品集團LVMH及其執行長貝爾納·阿爾諾。與此同時，巴黎檢方正對此事展開調查，近期已將三名律師列為正式調查對象，三人均否認有不當行為。如今，LVMH正展開反擊。

最後看點
9. 認識這位在世界盃守護美國球門的哈佛數據宅：擁有常春藤盟校經濟學學位的馬特·弗里斯，幾乎是從默默無聞中脫穎而出，拿下美國國家隊主力門將的位置。這位27歲球員的分析思維和對數字的熱愛，是他崛起的關鍵所在。從小時候起，他望向足球場時，看到的就是數學。

新聞室之外
10. 評論：週二美國民主社會主義者在紐約橫掃初選，這是遠左派對左派的一場潰敗。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Inside the Ellison-Trump Alliance
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Larry Ellison didn’t join the gaggle of CEOs traveling with President Trump on his state visit to China, nor was he at a White House dinner Trump hosted for tech titans. The Oracle billionaire didn’t need to be.

Instead, Ellison has cultivated a more private, symbiotic friendship with Trump—fueled by tens of millions in political donations—that has parlayed his family into a dominant position in the American tech and media landscape. Our latest reporting pulls back the curtain on the Ellison-Trump alliance—and looks at how both men, and Ellison’s son David, have benefited.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

U.S.-Iranian trash talk is disrupting peace negotiations . Israeli troops stationed in Lebanon are increasingly caught between U.S. limits on Israel’s military operations and domestic pressure to fight on against Iran-backed Hezbollah. Insurance companies are more exposed to the embattled private-credit industry than their financial disclosures reflect, according to a report. Progressive allies of Zohran Mamdani swept through New York’s primaries, handing defeats to mainstream Democrats in deep-blue congressional districts. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is expected to formally wind down its hantavirus response today. In a special podcast series, we look at how to solve the housing crisis . Everyone has an idea.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

Source: Factset, Market data as of 6/24/2026, 5:48:18 AM ET

📈 Follow our live financial coverage all day.

The stratospheric rally has left tech stocks vulnerable to sharp reversals. In the artificial-intelligence race , Amazon has an incumbent advantage, while Google stands out for some innovative approaches, writes Jinjoo Lee.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

China is luring the world to the yuan—and hobbling Western sanctions.

The White House has entered talks with Iran over a new nuclear deal, relying on a traditional strength: the promise of sanctions relief and access to some of roughly $100 billion in frozen assets. Yet, that leverage is waning . Tehran has blunted the U.S. sanctions campaign in recent years by successfully using China’s financial architecture—built on the yuan—that operates beyond Washington’s reach. Both Iran and Russia have used the currency to carry out oil sales and other trade, evading controls on dollar transactions, report Rory Jones, Austin Ramzy and Costas Paris.

4

Europeans are terrified of spending money, and it’s hurting the economy.

Europeans have doubled down on frugality in recent years—another economic headache for the continent. Consumers’ reluctance to spend is a key reason why Europe has lagged behind the U.S., where robust spending especially among higher-earners has driven growth. European companies that make some of the most coveted products in the world—luxury handbags, watches, clothes—now depend heavily on American and Asian consumers for growth. People around the world are feeling the sticker-shock of higher prices, but recent inflation has taken a larger psychological toll on Europeans, reports Chelsey Dulaney.

5

Our travel columnist tried the TSA’s new way to dodge airport security lines.

The Transportation Security Administration is testing a new, remote terminal with screening to alleviate the passenger crush at airports. At the pilot site in Framingham, Mass.—about 30 minutes outside Boston Logan—travelers can check bags, clear security and hop on a bus directly to the airport, where they’re dropped off at a secure gate. Travel columnist Dawn Gilbertson tested the setup on a Saturday during the start of summer vacation season. Airport dads, families and infrequent fliers will delight in the breathing room and lack of snaking lines. But for this frequent flier, the extra step ultimately felt like a waste of time.

6

Will anyone buy this cheap EV truck with hand-crank windows and no radio?

A new automotive startup is betting that Americans are so fed up with high car prices they will consider buying a two-seat, all-electric pickup truck with hand-crank windows and no radio. Slate Auto, a Michigan-based carmaker backed by Amazon.com founder Jeff Bezos, is racing to begin production later this year of its first model: an overtly spartan, compact truck that will start in the mid-$20,000 range. Trucks like these have been missing from U.S. roads for over a decade.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

World Cup: Switzerland vs. Canada in Vancouver; Scotland vs. Brazil in Miami; Czechia vs. Mexico in Mexico City, among other matches Economic data: May new-home sales Earnings: Micron Technology THE NUMBER

8

 14.4%

The number of ultrawealthy individuals jumped by 14.4% last year to 556,850 people worldwide by the end of 2025, according to wealth-intelligence firm Altrata. Marking the fastest pace of growth since 2017, the spike in individuals worth over $30 million was fueled, in part, by lower inflation, resilient corporate earnings and booming enthusiasm for AI investment.

AND FINALLY...

9

The World Cup’s other hydration break is a high-speed beer run.

At a World Cup loaded with tension and geopolitical intrigue, nothing has been more polarizing than the disruptions known as “hydration breaks.” These three-minute pauses, which occur midway through each half, have been derided around the globe as commercial land grabs that cater to sponsors, break up momentum and violate the spirit of soccer. There is, however, one thirsty group that can’t get enough of them—and it isn’t the guys running around in the heat for 90 minutes.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: The teachers union order to Democrats is clear : Opt into the federal school-choice program, and risk losing our election endorsement and campaign money.

✏️ 賴瑞・艾利森（Larry Ellison）並未加入陪同川普總統出訪中國的一眾企業執行長之列，也沒有出席川普為科技巨頭舉辦的白宮晚宴。這位甲骨文（Oracle）億萬富豪其實無須露面。

相反地，艾利森與川普培養出一種更私密、互利共生的友誼——靠著數千萬美元的政治獻金推動——讓他的家族在美國科技與媒體版圖中占據主導地位。我們最新的報導揭開了艾利森與川普聯盟的內幕，並探討兩人，以及艾利森之子大衛，如何從中獲益。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
美伊之間的口水戰正在擾亂和平談判。駐黎巴嫩的以色列部隊日益陷入兩難：一方面受美國對以色列軍事行動的限制，另一方面又面臨國內持續打擊伊朗支持的真主黨的壓力。據一份報告指出，保險公司對陷入困境的私募信貸產業的風險敞口，比其財務揭露所顯示的還要大。左傾的佐赫蘭・馬姆達尼（Zohran Mamdani）盟友在紐約初選中橫掃全場，讓主流民主黨人在深藍選區慘遭挫敗。美國疾病管制與預防中心（CDC）預計今日正式終止其漢他病毒應對行動。在一個特別播客系列中，我們探討如何解決住房危機——人人都有自己的看法。

市場直擊

2
道瓊期貨 51999.00　跌83.00　跌0.16%；標普500期貨 7444.75　漲7.25　漲0.10%；那斯達克100期貨 29789.25　漲123.25　漲0.42%
資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年6月24日美東時間上午5:48

科技股的驚人漲勢已讓其容易出現大幅回調。在人工智慧競賽中，亞馬遜擁有既有優勢，而Google則以一些創新做法脫穎而出，Jinjoo Lee撰文分析。

獨家搶先看

3
中國正吸引全世界轉向人民幣——並削弱西方的制裁效力。

白宮已就新的核協議與伊朗展開談判，倚仗的是傳統籌碼：解除制裁的承諾，以及讓伊朗取得約1000億美元被凍結資產中部分款項的機會。然而，這項籌碼正在減弱。近年來，德黑蘭成功利用以人民幣為基礎、超出華盛頓管轄範圍的中國金融架構，削弱了美國的制裁行動。伊朗和俄羅斯都利用人民幣進行石油銷售及其他貿易，藉此規避對美元交易的管制，Rory Jones、Austin Ramzy與Costas Paris報導。

4
歐洲人不敢花錢，這正在傷害經濟。

近年來，歐洲人愈發精打細算——這是歐洲大陸的另一個經濟隱憂。消費者不願花錢，是歐洲經濟落後於美國的關鍵原因之一；在美國，尤其是高收入族群的強勁消費支出推動了經濟成長。生產全球最搶手商品——奢華手袋、手錶、服飾——的歐洲企業，如今嚴重依賴美國和亞洲消費者來維持成長。全球民眾都感受到物價上漲的衝擊，但近期的通膨對歐洲人造成的心理衝擊尤其嚴重，Chelsey Dulaney報導。

5
本報旅遊專欄作家試用了TSA避開機場安檢排隊的新方法。

美國運輸安全管理局（TSA）正在測試一種新型遠端航廈安檢方式，以紓解機場的乘客擁擠問題。在麻州法明罕（Framingham）的試點站——距離波士頓洛根機場約30分鐘車程——旅客可以在此辦理行李托運、通過安檢，然後直接搭巴士前往機場，抵達後被送至安全管制區內的登機門。旅遊專欄作家道恩・吉伯森（Dawn Gilbertson）在暑假旺季開始的某個週六親自體驗了這套流程。對於帶著孩子的家庭與不常搭機的旅客而言，這種空間感和免排長龍的體驗令人欣喜；但對這位常客而言，多出來的這道程序終究感覺像是浪費時間。

6
會有人買這款配備手搖車窗、沒有收音機的廉價電動皮卡嗎？

一家新創車廠賭的是：美國人已經對居高不下的車價感到厭煩，願意考慮購買一款配備手搖車窗、沒有收音機的雙座純電皮卡。Slate Auto是一家總部位於密西根、由亞馬遜創辦人傑夫・貝佐斯（Jeff Bezos）投資的車廠，正加緊腳步準備在今年稍後開始量產其首款車型：一款刻意走極簡風格的小型皮卡，起售價落在2萬多美元區間。這類車型已經在美國道路上絕跡超過十年。

今日焦點

7
世界盃：瑞士對加拿大（溫哥華）；蘇格蘭對巴西（邁阿密）；捷克對墨西哥（墨西哥城），以及其他多場賽事。經濟數據：5月新屋銷售。財報：美光科技（Micron Technology）。

數字看世界

8
14.4%
根據財富情報公司Altrata的數據，去年全球超級富豪人數躍增14.4%，達到55萬6850人，是2017年以來成長最快的一年。這波成長部分得益於通膨降溫、企業獲利穩健，以及市場對AI投資的熱情高漲。

最後一則

9
世界盃另一種「補水暫停」，其實是一場高速啤酒狂奔。

在這屆充滿緊張氣氛與地緣政治角力的世界盃賽事中，最具爭議的莫過於被稱為「補水暫停」的比賽中斷。這種在每個半場中段出現、長達三分鐘的暫停，被全球球迷批評為迎合贊助商、破壞比賽節奏、違背足球精神的商業手段。然而，有一群人對此樂此不疲——而他們並不是在酷熱中奔跑90分鐘的球員。

新聞室之外

10
社論：民主黨面臨教師工會下的最後通牒再清楚不過：加入聯邦擇校方案，就要承擔失去選舉背書與競選資金的風險。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The ‘Perp Futures’ Shaking Up Wall Street
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Brits used to laugh at the Italians for their rapid turnover of government leaders. Now, they are facing similar turmoil as they lose their fifth prime minister in seven years. Following Keir Starmer’s sudden resignation, the once-unthinkable looks likely: an unpopular populist taking power. We look at the forces that broke the U.K.’s longstanding two-party system.

In other news: The $100-million-plus CEO is back with a bang. Just a year after nine-figure compensation packages seemed to be fading, our annual CEO pay ranking shows a resurgence in executive wealth—though the names at the very top of our list might surprise you.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Some of President Trump’s key goals for the Iran war have been dropped—or shifted. To understand what has changed, we reviewed his statements before, during and after the war. A generational clash is pitting Democrats against Democrats in primaries across the U.S. Latin America has become more Trump-aligned than ever. Here’s how. U.S. auto-safety regulators have opened an investigation into a fatal wreck involving a Tesla that crashed into a home, killing one person. Federal investigators concluded that the 2021 collapse of the Champlain Towers South condominium in Surfside, Fla., began roughly three weeks before the building fell.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 51866.00 -253.00 0.49 S&P 500 Futures 7444.00 -97.25 1.29 Nasdaq 100 Futures 29883.25 -770.25 2.51

Source: Factset, Market data as of 6/23/2026, 6:03:46 AM ET

📈 Follow our live financial coverage all day.

The CFTC’s approval of so-called perp futures has triggered a selloff in U.S. exchanges’ shares—and at least one high-profile lawsuit. Former Fed chairman Alan Greenspan left a lasting legacy for stock market investors: the Greenspan Put . But there’s a question mark over whether the put still exists—and whether it is a good thing, writes James Mackintosh.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

These forces broke the U.K.’s two-party system.

Starmer’s likely successor, ex-Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham, will be the sixth new face at 10 Downing Street in seven years. It’s a remarkable turn of events for a country that has long prided itself on political stability. Between 1945 and 2016, Britain had just 13 prime ministers and power flipped between Labour and the Conservatives. Now, prime ministers change on average every 14 months. Britain’s merry-go-round of leaders has turned the country into a political laughingstock—the new Italy of Europe—and spooked investors, pushing up government borrowing costs and curbing foreign investment. It has also hampered the government’s ability to deliver key long-term changes in policy, undermining voter trust, report Max Colchester and David Luhnow.

4

Sam Altman’s wealth has surged by billions after OpenAI partnerships with personal investments.

Much of the OpenAI CEO’s wealth is tied up in a vast network of tech companies that include everything from nuclear fusion to a startup trying to create a new city on the Mediterranean. A growing number of them have entered into business partnerships with OpenAI, creating a web of investments that are receiving scrutiny ahead of the company’s planned IPO. Altman doesn’t own any direct equity in OpenAI, creating an unusual situation where his financial motives aren’t fully aligned with the company he runs. Berber Jin and Nate Rattner identified dozens of his investments and analyzed the impact of some deals on his wealth.

6

What does it take to bring a Ukrainian home from Russian captivity?

More than four years into Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, thousands of prisoners of war have been exchanged by both sides. It’s one of the few areas of cooperation between Russia and Ukraine. After almost two years in a Russian prison, Ukrainian soldier Oleksandr “Sasha” Kenev was exchanged in a prisoner swap. The Journal follows Kenev’s journey and takes a look at what life is like for those who are still waiting for their loved ones to be exchanged.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

Midterms: Maryland, New York and Utah hold primary elections. Sports: The World Cup continues with matches including England vs. Ghana. The NBA draft begins. Earnings: FedEx, Carnival THE NUMBER

8

 $821 million

That’s how much Shankh Mitra was paid in 2025 from Welltower, a real-estate investment trust focused on senior housing and healthcare. That lands him one of the biggest executive-pay packages for a public-company CEO over the past decade, data from MyLogIQ show. More U.S. chief executives last year crossed a once-rare pay threshold than in any year since 2021—and nearly a dozen topped $200 million. Explore how CEOs compare on pay, performance and more with our interactive table .

AND FINALLY...

9

This writer went to a silent retreat for five days. She says it nearly broke her brain.

No phone, no laptop, no smartwatch, no ring, no pings. No TV, no reading, no journaling, no music. And no talking whatsoever—not even eye contact—as you sit, eat and stroll mindfully alongside 90 or so strangers. For five long days. Writer at large Pamela Paul recounts her stay at a silent Buddhist meditation retreat in the Berkshires. Her experience reveals just how disorienting it can be when a modern mind is suddenly cut off from constant digital input.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Alan Greenspan, the longtime Fed chairman who died Monday at age 100, always knew that neither he nor anyone else in Washington conducted the U.S. economy .
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 英國人過去總嘲笑義大利政府領導人更換頻繁。如今，他們自己也面臨類似的動盪，七年內即將失去第五位首相。繼施凱爾（Keir Starmer）突然辭職後，一度難以想像的局面似乎即將成真：一位不受歡迎的民粹主義者可能上台執政。我們探討了究竟是哪些力量瓦解了英國長期以來的兩黨體制。

其他新聞：年薪破億美元的執行長強勢回歸。就在九位數薪酬待遇看似逐漸式微僅一年後，我們的年度執行長薪酬排行榜顯示企業高層財富再度攀升——不過榜單最頂端的名字可能會讓你意外。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
川普總統在伊朗戰爭中的部分關鍵目標已遭放棄或調整。為了解其中變化，我們檢視了他在戰爭前、戰爭中及戰爭後的各項聲明。一場世代對立正讓民主黨人在全美初選中彼此廝殺。拉丁美洲如今比以往任何時候都更加親近川普——原因為何，我們一探究竟。美國汽車安全監管機構已針對一起特斯拉撞毀民宅、造成一人死亡的致命車禍展開調查。聯邦調查人員認定，2021年佛州瑟夫賽德（Surfside）尚普蘭大廈南棟（Champlain Towers South）倒塌事故，其實在大樓坍塌前約三週就已開始醞釀。

市場直擊

2
道瓊期貨 51866.00　跌253.00　跌0.49%；標普500期貨 7444.00　跌97.25　跌1.29%；那斯達克100期貨 29883.25　跌770.25　跌2.51%
資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年6月23日美東時間上午6:03

美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）核准所謂「永續期貨」（perp futures），已引發美國交易所類股拋售潮——並至少招來一起備受矚目的訴訟。前聯準會主席葛林斯潘（Alan Greenspan）為股市投資人留下一項深遠遺產：「葛林斯潘賣權」（Greenspan Put）。但如今這項賣權是否依然存在、是否仍是件好事，仍是個問號，James Mackintosh撰文分析。

獨家搶先看

3
正是這些力量瓦解了英國的兩黨體制。

施凱爾可能的接班人、前曼徹斯特市長安迪・伯納姆（Andy Burnham），將成為七年內第六位入主唐寧街10號的新面孔。對於一向以政治穩定自豪的英國而言，這是相當驚人的轉折。從1945年到2016年，英國僅歷經13位首相，且政權在工黨與保守黨之間輪替。如今，首相平均每14個月就換人。英國領導人的走馬燈已讓這個國家淪為政治笑柄——被戲稱為「歐洲的新義大利」——並嚇壞了投資人，推高政府舉債成本、抑制外國投資。這也削弱了政府推動長期關鍵政策變革的能力，進一步侵蝕選民信任，Max Colchester與David Luhnow報導。

4
Sam Altman的財富因OpenAI的合作夥伴關係與個人投資而暴增數十億美元。

這位OpenAI執行長的財富，很大一部分綁定在一個龐大的科技公司網絡中，範圍從核融合到一家企圖在地中海打造新城市的新創公司都有。這些公司當中，愈來愈多已與OpenAI建立商業合作關係，形成一張投資網絡，在該公司籌劃首次公開發行（IPO）之際受到密切審視。Altman本人並未直接持有OpenAI股權，這造成一種不尋常的局面：他的財務動機與他所經營的公司利益並非完全一致。Berber Jin與Nate Rattner整理出他的數十筆投資，並分析部分交易對其財富的影響。

一位烏克蘭人要從俄羅斯的關押中歸來，需要付出什麼代價？

俄羅斯全面入侵烏克蘭已超過四年，雙方已交換了數千名戰俘，這是俄烏之間少數仍存在合作的領域之一。烏克蘭士兵奧列克桑德・「薩沙」・凱涅夫（Oleksandr “Sasha” Kenev）在俄羅斯監獄關押近兩年後，於一次戰俘交換中獲釋。本報追蹤了凱涅夫的歸鄉之路，並探討那些仍在等待親人歸來者的生活現況。

今日焦點

7
期中選舉：馬里蘭州、紐約州與猶他州舉行初選。體育賽事：世界盃持續進行，包括英格蘭對迦納。NBA選秀大會開始。財報：聯邦快遞（FedEx）、嘉年華郵輪（Carnival）。

數字看世界

8
8.21億美元
這是尚克・米特拉（Shankh Mitra）2025年從專注於銀髮住宅與醫療照護的不動產投資信託公司Welltower領到的薪酬。這使他躋身過去十年間上市公司執行長最高薪酬待遇之列。MyLogIQ的數據顯示，去年跨過這道曾經罕見薪酬門檻的美國企業執行長人數，創下2021年以來新高——其中近十幾位薪酬超過2億美元。透過我們的互動表格，探索各執行長在薪酬、績效等方面的比較。

最後一則

9
這位作家參加了為期五天的靜默靜修，她說這幾乎讓她的大腦崩潰。

沒有手機、沒有筆電、沒有智慧手錶、沒有戒指裝置、沒有任何通知提示。沒有電視、沒有閱讀、沒有寫日記、沒有音樂。而且完全不能說話——甚至不能有眼神接觸——與大約90名陌生人一起靜坐、用餐、漫步，為期漫長的五天。特約作家帕梅拉・保羅（Pamela Paul）記述了她在伯克夏（Berkshires）一處佛教靜默禪修營的親身經歷。她的體驗揭示了，當現代人的心智突然被切斷持續不斷的數位資訊輸入時，會有多麼令人迷失方向。

新聞室之外

10
社論：週一以百歲高齡辭世、長期擔任聯準會主席的葛林斯潘，始終明白一件事：無論是他自己，還是華盛頓的任何人，都從未真正主導過美國經濟。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: What’s Threatening the Highflying Stock Market
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Good morning. We’re following the latest from the U.S.-Iran peace talks in Switzerland, where efforts to end fighting between Hezbollah and Israel in Lebanon and ease tensions over the Strait of Hormuz have been in focus.

Turning to the markets, there’s been unusual optimism as of late. But while U.S. stocks have the wind at their back, lurching drops in some recent sessions betray investors’ underlying jitters. We look at some of the biggest risks for this highflying stock market.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

U.K. Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced he would step down following a rebellion in his party, clearing the way for the country’s sixth leader in seven years. As war with the U.S. eases, Iran has stepped up hangings of dissidents. Far-right populist Abelardo de la Espriella was elected president of Colombia, setting the country on a collision course with cocaine networks and gangs. “CBS Evening News” anchor Tony Dokoupil is in the spotlight amid criticism of his network and its editor in chief, Bari Weiss. Can he weather the war? Progressive up-and-comer Dan Moraff rushed the vetting of Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner. He says he’s trying to blow up the way Democrats run campaigns.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 51985.00 -23.00 0.04 S&P 500 Futures 7556.25 -14.50 0.19 Nasdaq 100 Futures 30708.50 -11.25 0.04

Source: Factset, Market data as of 6/22/2026, 5:59:14 AM ET

📈 Follow our live financial coverage all day.

Picking an index just to avoid big initial public offerings isn’t likely to boost returns , writes Telis Demos.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Microsoft’s Nadella warns we can’t let artificial-intelligence giants eat the economy.

Satya Nadella helped usher in the AI boom. Now he has a tough message for the companies leading it. The chief executive of Microsoft is joining a growing effort to take on AI giants OpenAI and Anthropic. In an interview with the Journal, he outlined his vision for the next wave of the AI boom: one involving cheaper models, more user control and political messaging that wins the public’s trust. He also offered a blistering critique of how the race for AI supremacy has taken shape, report Bradley Olson and Tina Li.

4

Tide already dominates detergent. Why is P&G pushing a new version?

Every time Procter & Gamble pushes out a new product, it is making a calculated gamble, and the stakes are highest with its crown jewel—Tide detergent. So P&G wasn’t going to release the next iteration— a detergent “tile” called Tide evo —until it had made it the best it could. That took more than a decade. Executives at rival companies have expressed bewilderment at the resulting product—a flexible 3-inch white square made of detergent fibers that feels like a pad of fabric. They are confused by the shape and surprised by the price. But they are watching closely to see how consumers react, reports Natasha Khan.

5

Parents are turning to Wegovy for elementary school kids.

By prescribing GLP-1 medications early, doctors say they aim to prevent lifelong obesity and complications such as Type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure, which are showing up in younger children. These drugs aren’t yet approved for obesity in patients this young, and it isn’t certain that young children can safely use them without compromising a critical period of growth for their bones and brain. But doctors prescribing the drugs off-label say the risks of obesity complications for some patients are too serious not to try a treatment that can be so effective. These medicines are being tested in children as young as 6 , reports Andrea Petersen.

6

These global chokepoints carry much of the world’s trade:

MAP: ASHLEY CAI/WSJ

The war between the U.S. and Iran has exposed a painful vulnerability in the global economy: Disruptions at key chokepoints, like the Strait of Hormuz, can wreak havoc on international trade. In maps and charts, we break down how vital routes like the Strait of Malacca and the Panama Canal are vulnerable to the next geopolitical crisis.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

World Cup: Argentina vs. Austria in Dallas; Norway vs. Senegal in East Rutherford, N.J.; France vs. Iraq in Philadelphia; Jordan vs. Algeria in Santa Clara, Calif. THE NUMBER

8

 30%

That’s the surge in passengers Flix North America, which operates the Flixbus and Greyhound lines, saw on routes overlapping with Spirit within a week of the airline’s demise in early May. The bump spans roughly 130 routes previously served by the carrier. Air-travel turmoil, costlier airfares and rising gas prices this year have more Americans hopping the bus to travel.

AND FINALLY...

9

Redemption has come for the Bed Bath & Beyond believers.

Bed Bath & Beyond’s once-ubiquitous blue-and-white coupons are worth something again, providing the ultimate vindication for the die-hards who held onto the coupons long after that made any sense. The homegoods retailer stopped accepting them in 2023 when it filed for bankruptcy and closed its stores. It relaunched online later that year under new owner Overstock.com, which changed its name to Bed Bath & Beyond. Now, the chain is reopening bricks-and-mortar stores. And the paper coupon is back , with a twist: It’s also accepting old coupons.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: The Democratic Socialists of America are taking over big cities and bidding for gains in Congress.
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 早安。我們持續追蹤在瑞士進行的美伊和平談判最新進展，焦點集中在結束黎巴嫩真主黨與以色列間的戰事，以及緩解荷莫茲海峽（Strait of Hormuz）的緊張局勢。

轉向市場方面，近來出現異常的樂觀情緒。儘管美股一路順風，但近期部分交易日出現的劇烈重挫，暴露出投資人內心的不安。我們檢視了這波高漲股市所面臨的一些最大風險。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
英國首相施凱爾（Keir Starmer）宣布將辭職，此前他在黨內遭遇叛變，為該國七年內第六位領導人鋪路。隨著與美國的戰事趨緩，伊朗加大了對異議人士的絞刑處決。極右翼民粹主義者阿貝拉多・德拉埃斯普列拉（Abelardo de la Espriella）當選哥倫比亞總統，讓該國與可卡因販運網絡及幫派迎頭相撞。「CBS晚間新聞」主播東尼・多科皮爾（Tony Dokoupil）因其所屬電視網及總編輯芭莉・魏斯（Bari Weiss）遭受批評而備受矚目——他能撐過這場風暴嗎？民主黨進步派新星丹・莫拉夫（Dan Moraff）倉促完成了對緬因州參議員候選人格雷厄姆・普拉特納（Graham Platner）的審查。他表示，自己是想打破民主黨經營競選活動的舊有模式。

市場直擊

2
道瓊期貨 51985.00　跌23.00　跌0.04%；標普500期貨 7556.25　跌14.50　跌0.19%；那斯達克100期貨 30708.50　跌11.25　跌0.04%
資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年6月22日美東時間上午5:59

Telis Demos撰文指出，僅為了規避大型首次公開發行（IPO）而選擇某個指數，並不太可能提高報酬率。

獨家搶先看

3
微軟納德拉警告：不能讓人工智慧巨頭吞噬整個經濟。

薩蒂亞・納德拉（Satya Nadella）曾協助開啟這波AI熱潮，如今他要向引領這股風潮的企業傳達一項嚴厲訊息。這位微軟執行長正加入一股日益壯大的力量，準備對抗AI巨頭OpenAI與Anthropic。他在接受本報專訪時，勾勒出他對下一波AI熱潮的願景：更便宜的模型、更多使用者控制權，以及能贏得公眾信任的政治論述。他也對這場AI霸權爭奪戰目前的發展方式，提出了猛烈批評，Bradley Olson與Tina Li報導。

4
汰漬（Tide）早已稱霸洗衣精市場，寶僑（P&G）為何還要推出新版本？

寶僑每次推出新產品，都是一場精心計算的賭注，而風險最高的莫過於其王牌產品——汰漬洗衣精。因此，在確保推出的下一代產品做到盡善盡美之前，寶僑遲遲不願發表這款名為Tide evo的洗衣「錠片」。這一等，就是十多年。競爭對手的高層對這項最終產品的推出感到困惑不解——這是一款以洗衣纖維製成、質感如布墊般的3英寸柔軟白色方塊。他們對其形狀感到費解，也對其定價感到意外，但都在密切觀察消費者的反應，Natasha Khan報導。

5
家長開始讓小學生使用減重藥物Wegovy。

醫生表示，及早開立GLP-1類藥物處方的目的，是為了預防終身肥胖及第二型糖尿病、高血壓等併發症——這些病症如今正出現在愈來愈年幼的孩童身上。這類藥物目前尚未獲准用於這個年齡層的肥胖治療，也無法確定幼童能否在不影響骨骼與大腦關鍵發育期的情況下安全使用。但開立此類藥物（屬適應症外用途）的醫生表示，對某些病患而言，肥胖併發症的風險太過嚴重，不能不嘗試這種可能非常有效的療法。這些藥物目前正在年僅6歲的兒童身上進行測試，Andrea Petersen報導。

6
這些全球「咽喉點」承載著世界大部分的貿易：

地圖：ASHLEY CAI／WSJ

美伊戰爭暴露出全球經濟一項令人痛心的脆弱之處：荷莫茲海峽等關鍵咽喉要道一旦受阻，可能對國際貿易造成嚴重破壞。我們透過地圖與圖表，分析麻六甲海峽、巴拿馬運河等重要航道，在下一場地緣政治危機中有多麼脆弱。

今日焦點

7
世界盃：阿根廷對奧地利（達拉斯）；挪威對塞內加爾（紐澤西州東拉瑟福）；法國對伊拉克（費城）；約旦對阿爾及利亞（加州聖塔克拉拉）。

數字看世界

8
30%
這是經營Flixbus與灰狗巴士（Greyhound）路線的Flix North America，在精神航空（Spirit）5月初倒閉後一週內，於重疊航線上見到的乘客增幅。這波成長涵蓋約130條原本由精神航空經營的路線。今年航空旅行的動盪、機票漲價與油價上升，讓更多美國人改搭巴士出行。

最後一則

9
Bed Bath & Beyond的死忠信徒終於等到了救贖。

Bed Bath & Beyond那款曾經隨處可見的藍白色折價券，如今再度變得有價值，這對那些早已明知已無用處、卻仍捨不得丟掉折價券的死忠顧客而言，堪稱終極平反。這家家居用品零售商於2023年申請破產、關閉所有門市時，已停止接受這些折價券。同年稍後，公司在新東家Overstock.com旗下重新於線上開張，該公司隨後也更名為Bed Bath & Beyond。如今，這家連鎖店正重新開設實體門市，紙本折價券也回歸了，只是多了個新玩法：連舊折價券也照樣接受。

新聞室之外

10
社論：美國民主社會主義者（DSA）正在接管各大城市，並企圖在國會斬獲更多席次。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: U.S. Enemies Master the Art of Evading Sanctions
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Iran’s announcement it had closed the Strait of Hormuz yesterday, as clashes between Israel and Hezbollah flared again in Lebanon, undid for now the main achievement of the memorandum of understanding signed last week. Those developments are threatening U.S. plans to focus on Iran’s nuclear program during the fresh round of peace talks taking place in Switzerland.

Control over the strait is one of many cards analysts say Tehran holds in the negotiations that may allow it to resist Washington’s demands. And while Iran is eager for relief from U.S. sanctions, its government has still been able to generate billions of dollars in revenue, mainly by selling oil to China. More broadly, U.S. economic pressure in recent years has largely failed to curb rogue regimes such as Iran, Russia and North Korea, as they continue to find ways to sidestep sanctions.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

From smartphones to gaming consoles to PCs, buyers of consumer electronics are getting hit by rising prices driven by the skyrocketing cost of memory and storage chips . With more than $20 billion on the line, Coca-Cola and the IRS head to a federal appeals court this week in a tax fight over foreign profits . Some schools in the U.S. still have a few days left before summer vacation. That isn’t stopping retailers from kicking off back-to-school sales . Many readers see Belle Burden’s best-selling divorce memoir “Strangers” as a tidy narrative of a woman wronged, but that isn’t the whole story , writes Holly Peterson.

FROM THE MARKETS

2

When companies as a group turn into stock sellers, it’s a reasonable sign that shares are very overpriced , writes James Mackintosh. 🎧 CAE Consulting principal Kevin Koharki joins WSJ’s Take On the Week podcast to explain why investors need greater clarity on how big tech companies are accounting for AI data-center expenditures.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

They looked like they were getting rich on Polymarket—but none of it was real.

In January, a college student posted a video that showed him winning $100,000 on a wager that President Trump would publicly say the word “McDonald’s” that month. But the bet wasn’t real. The student is one of dozens of mostly college-age creators Polymarket paid to film themselves making fake trades and sometimes scoring fake wins, according to an analysis of more than 1,100 videos by the Journal, along with instructional materials and interviews with creators who have worked with the company. Polymarket said in a statement that it was “committed to maintaining accurate, fair, and transparent markets.” The company said it plans to conduct a comprehensive audit of active promotional content.

4

Jay Clayton is a pawn in a chess game between the president and Congress.

The loyal Trump ally has for the past 14 months led the U.S. attorney’s office for the Southern District of New York, where he pulled off the delicate feat of remaining in the president’s good graces while still exercising some level of independence. Last week, the president delayed his nomination to be director of national intelligence in an effort to force Congress to act on election legislation that currently lacks enough support to pass. Trump said he was stopping Clayton’s nomination until his current post as a top prosecutor was filled. That could leave Clayton in limbo indefinitely, report Corinne Ramey, Sadie Gurman and James Fanelli.

5

🎥 Baiju Bhatt left Robinhood as a billionaire. His next bet is his boldest yet.

PHOTO ILLUSTRATION: NIKKI WALKER

After years leading the brokerage, Bhatt stepped down as co-CEO in 2020. Four years later, he launched Cowboy Space, which is building solar-powered data centers in space. The company was recently valued at $2 billion and has grown to around 50 employees. Bhatt says he started the venture to fulfill a childhood dream. Watch the latest episode of The WSJ Money Interview, hosted by Gunjan Banerji.

6

This futuristic Japanese warship is on the market and winning fans.

The Mogami-class frigate is a sleek and stealthy warship that can hunt submarines , deploy underwater drones and operate with a lean crew. It’s the kind of high-tech weaponry that Japan wants to sell overseas as it looks to revitalize its defense industry, strengthen regional deterrence against China and help meet global demand for arms.

HAPPENING THIS WEEK

7

Tuesday: Maryland, New York and Utah hold primary elections. The NBA draft begins. Wednesday: New-home sales data. Trump is scheduled to meet with NATO chief Mark Rutte in Washington. Thursday: The Fed’s preferred inflation measure, the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, is released. The U.S. plays Turkey at the World Cup. Friday: The final June consumer-sentiment reading from the University of Michigan is due. Former Apollo Global Management CEO Leon Black is set to testify before the House Oversight Committee regarding his ties with Jeffrey Epstein . “Supergirl” opens in theaters (more arts & culture happenings here ).

THE NUMBER

8

 $28,596

The amount a home buyer could expect to fork out per year on basic homeownership expenses—mortgage payments, property taxes, insurance, maintenance and repairs—in 2025, according to data from Intercontinental Exchange and home-services marketplace Angi. That’s up from $20,618 in 2019. See how owning a home is getting more expensive in every way.

AND FINALLY...

9

Baseball has been invaded by an army of screaming, shirtless fans.

It started on a whim at a St. Louis Cardinals game in May. Now, sections packed with hundreds of rowdy, chanting, bare-chested fans have been appearing at ballparks from St. Petersburg to Seattle, injecting a jolt of life into America’s famously hidebound pastime. The movement has come to be called “Tarps Off,” and it has transformed otherwise unremarkable games into the best parties of the summer .

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 伊朗昨日宣布關閉荷莫茲海峽，加上黎巴嫩以色列與真主黨之間的衝突再度升溫，暫時抵銷了上週簽署的諒解備忘錄所取得的主要成果。這些發展正威脅著美國希望在瑞士新一輪和談中，將焦點集中在伊朗核計畫上的計畫。

分析人士指出，掌控海峽是德黑蘭在談判中握有的眾多籌碼之一，這可能讓伊朗得以抵抗華盛頓的要求。儘管伊朗急欲擺脫美國制裁，但其政府仍能透過主要向中國出售石油，創造數十億美元的收入。更廣泛來看，近年來美國的經濟施壓，在遏制伊朗、俄羅斯、北韓等流氓政權方面大多未能奏效，這些國家持續設法規避制裁。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
從智慧型手機、遊戲主機到個人電腦，消費電子產品的買家正因記憶體與儲存晶片成本飆升，而承受漲價衝擊。可口可樂與美國國稅局本週將為一場涉及境外利潤、金額逾200億美元的稅務糾紛，對簿於聯邦上訴法院。美國部分學校距離放暑假還有幾天，但這並未阻止零售商提前展開返校促銷。許多讀者將貝兒・伯登（Belle Burden）暢銷離婚回憶錄《陌生人》（Strangers）視為一則「無辜女性受害」的簡單故事，但事情並非全貌，Holly Peterson撰文分析。

市場動態

2
James Mackintosh撰文指出，當企業整體從買家變成賣家時，這是股價被嚴重高估的合理徵兆。🎧 CAE Consulting負責人Kevin Koharki在WSJ「Take On the Week」播客中，解釋為何投資人需要更清楚了解各大科技公司如何為AI資料中心支出做帳。

獨家搶先看

3
他們看起來像是靠Polymarket致富——但一切都是假的。

今年1月，一名大學生上傳影片，聲稱自己靠賭川普總統當月會公開說出「麥當勞」一詞而贏得10萬美元。但這筆賭注根本是假的。根據本報對逾1100支影片的分析，以及相關教學資料和曾與該公司合作的創作者訪談，這名學生只是Polymarket付費請來拍攝「假交易」、有時甚至「假獲勝」的數十名創作者之一，這些創作者多為大學生年紀。Polymarket在聲明中表示，公司「致力於維持準確、公平、透明的市場」，並表示計劃對現行推廣內容進行全面審查。

4
傑伊・克萊頓（Jay Clayton）是總統與國會之間棋局裡的一枚棋子。

這位川普的忠實盟友過去14個月來一直領導紐約南區聯邦檢察官辦公室，在此期間，他成功做到一件微妙的事：既維持總統的信任，又保有一定程度的獨立性。上週，總統延後了他出任國家情報總監的提名，意圖藉此逼迫國會就目前支持度不足、難以過關的選舉立法採取行動。川普表示，他將暫緩克萊頓的提名，直到他目前擔任的檢察官要職有人接替為止，這可能讓克萊頓無限期陷入懸而未決的處境，Corinne Ramey、Sadie Gurman與James Fanelli報導。

5
🎥 白居・巴特（Baiju Bhatt）以億萬富豪身分離開Robinhood，他的下一步棋更加大膽。

在領導這家券商多年後，巴特於2020年卸下共同執行長職務。四年後，他創立了Cowboy Space，該公司正在太空建造太陽能供電的資料中心。這家公司近期估值達20億美元，員工人數已成長至約50人。巴特表示，他創立這項事業是為了實現童年夢想。觀看由Gunjan Banerji主持的《WSJ Money Interview》最新一集。

6
這艘充滿未來感的日本軍艦正在市場上求售，備受青睞。

最上級巡防艦是一款外型俐落、具隱形能力的軍艦，能夠獵殺潛艦、部署水下無人載具，並以精簡的船員編制運作。這正是日本希望對外銷售的高科技武器，以振興其國防產業、強化對中國的區域威懾力，並協助滿足全球對武器的需求。

本週焦點

7
週二：馬里蘭州、紐約州、猶他州舉行初選。NBA選秀大會開始。週三：新屋銷售數據公布。川普預計在華盛頓與北約秘書長呂特（Mark Rutte）會面。週四：聯準會偏好的通膨指標——個人消費支出（PCE）物價指數公布。美國隊將在世界盃出戰土耳其。週五：密西根大學6月消費者信心指數終值公布。前阿波羅全球管理公司（Apollo Global Management）執行長里昂・布拉克（Leon Black）將就其與傑佛瑞・艾普斯坦（Jeffrey Epstein）的關係，在眾議院監督委員會作證。電影《超女》（Supergirl）上映。

數字看世界

8
28,596美元
根據洲際交易所（ICE）與居家服務平台Angi的數據，2025年購屋者每年在基本購屋開銷上——包括房貸還款、房產稅、保險、維護與修繕——預計要花費這個數字，較2019年的20,618美元大幅上升。看看擁有一棟房子在各個層面上是如何變得愈來愈昂貴。

最後一則

9
一支尖叫、光著上身的球迷大軍入侵了棒球場。

這一切始於5月一場聖路易紅雀隊（St. Louis Cardinals）比賽上的一時興起。如今，從聖彼德斯堡到西雅圖的各球場，都出現了擠滿數百名喧鬧、高喊口號、赤裸上身球迷的看台區塊，為這項素以保守著稱的美國國粹注入了一股活力。這股風潮如今被稱為「Tarps Off」，讓原本平淡無奇的比賽，變成了夏季最棒的派對。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: America’s Wealthiest Lose Faith in the Economy
emails.contentEn:
✏️ A U.S.-Iran agreement reached this week to stop the fighting has hit its first snag, with planned peace talks in Switzerland abruptly postponed. What’s next? The deal waives sanctions and reopens the Strait of Hormuz, but a lot can happen in the next few weeks once tough nuclear talks begin.

For now, the U.S. is working with Qatar on a plan to give Iran access to billions of dollars in frozen funds for humanitarian spending. The agreement also allows Tehran to sell its crude on the open market for the first time since 2018. Here’s a look at how quickly it can ramp up its oil output.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Fighting between Israel and Hezbollah flared again , just hours after a renewed ceasefire and as the U.S. and Iran were working to get their next round of peace talks back on track. California Gov. Gavin Newsom, under federal investigation, is leaning into his fight with President Trump—and turning the probe into a fundraising opportunity. With a comfortable 2-0 victory over Australia, Team USA guaranteed its place in the knockout stage of the World Cup. China’s navy is tightening the noose on Taiwan. Here’s how .

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

Artificial-intelligence leader Anthropic is on a weird collision course this fall between IPO hopes and ballot-box fears, writes Tim Higgins. Gibson Capital’s decision to pull $80 million out of private credit began with a realization that the asset class simply isn’t as great an investment as it once was.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Secretive Wall Street powerhouse Jane Street is seizing the AI spotlight.

Mystery has long shrouded the fast-growing trading giant. Now, as the firm pushes to become a major AI investor , it’s edging into the public eye. Its profits now top those of Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, helped in part by gains from investments in Anthropic and other private companies. Jane Street wants to get the word out about its AI investments and deals for computing power, eager to let AI companies know that it’s looking to make new investments and wants to be a partner for their businesses. The shift is catching some by surprise, reports Gregory Zuckerman.

4

For one California family, returning home after the fires became a 16-month saga.

The Figueroa family have regained their home, but not their neighborhood. Missi and Frank Figueroa and their three children moved into their newly built Altadena house last month. It sits on the same plot where the Eaton Fire destroyed their home of 10 years in January 2025. The firestorm damaged or destroyed around 6,000 local properties and killed 19 people. The Figueroas lost everything. But thanks to a mix of hard work, persistence and good fortune, the Figueroas are among a small batch thus far of displaced residents who are back. During the day, their neighborhood hums with laborers and vendors. But at night, it becomes a ghost town, reports Paul Kiernan.

5

America’s economic anxiety is rising up the income ladder.

A new WSJ poll finds that even those who consider themselves among the wealthiest classes in America carry high levels of concern about their current finances, the years ahead and the prospects for their children. More than 40% of Americans who call themselves upper class or upper-middle class say they haven’t saved enough money to retire comfortably. Only about 40% say their financial security is where they thought it would be at this point in their lives. Nearly three in five say they are strained by high gasoline prices. And those in the wealthiest classes have lost faith that an economy that has benefited them can lift future generations, reports Aaron Zitner.

6

Do you have to be rich to enjoy Nantucket? We found out.

Nantucket has become known for its beachfront real estate and fancy marinas. But a quieter, more laid-back version of the Massachusetts island exists if you know where to look. It’s one of quaint cobblestone streets, sunsets that have to be seen to be believed and secluded beaches where you can spend hours without seeing another soul. Our guide shows you how to enjoy the island without buying a six-figure membership to a golf club.

HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

7

Saturday: The World Cup continues with matches including Germany versus Ivory Coast. Sunday: The annual summer solstice in the Northern Hemisphere marks the first day of summer in that half of the world. At the World Cup, Spain faces Saudi Arabia, among other games. THE NUMBER

8

 >2 million

The number of students eligible to retake India’s nationwide undergraduate medical-school entrance exam on Sunday, after authorities voided the original test following allegations that some questions had been leaked in advance. This time, security is extraordinarily tight .

AND FINALLY...

9

This beloved movie was nearly destroyed by a single line of code.

The real story behind the “Toy Story” franchise is even better than the movies: Before anyone ever saw it, “Toy Story 2” was nearly destroyed by a single line of code. It only survived after a computer with the last known copy of the movie was rushed to Pixar in the back of a Volvo—saved by an unlikely cast of characters that included a six-month-old baby.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Behold the Democratic civil war that has erupted in California over a wealth-tax referendum. Trying to broker the peace is none other than Gov. Gavin Newsom.

✏️ 本週達成的美伊停火協議出現了第一個障礙：原訂在瑞士舉行的和談突然被推遲。接下來會如何發展？該協議解除制裁並重新開放荷莫茲海峽，但在艱難的核談判展開後，未來幾週仍可能發生許多變數。

目前，美國正與卡達合作，研擬讓伊朗動用數十億美元凍結資金以用於人道支出的方案。該協議也允許德黑蘭自2018年以來首次在公開市場出售原油。我們也探討了伊朗能多快提升其石油產量。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
就在停火協議重啟數小時後，以色列與真主黨之間的戰事再度爆發，此時美伊雙方正努力讓下一輪和談重回正軌。正遭聯邦調查的加州州長紐森（Gavin Newsom）正全力迎戰與川普總統之間的對立——並將這場調查轉化為募款契機。美國隊以2比0輕鬆擊敗澳洲，確保晉級世界盃淘汰賽。中國海軍正逐步收緊對台灣的封鎖，我們解析其手法。

市場直擊

2
Tim Higgins撰文指出，人工智慧領導廠商Anthropic今秋正陷入一場詭異的兩難：既盼望IPO，又擔憂選舉結果。Gibson Capital決定從私募信貸撤出8000萬美元，起因於該公司意識到這類資產已不再是曾經那麼出色的投資標的。

獨家搶先看

3
向來低調的華爾街勢力Jane Street正搶占AI鎂光燈焦點。

這家快速崛起的交易巨頭長期以來籠罩著神秘色彩。如今，隨著該公司力求成為主要的AI投資者，它也逐漸走向公眾視野。受惠於對Anthropic等私人公司的投資獲利，該公司獲利已超越高盛與摩根士丹利。Jane Street希望對外宣傳其AI投資與算力交易，急欲讓AI公司知道，該公司正在尋求新投資，並希望成為這些企業的合作夥伴。這項轉變讓不少人感到意外，Gregory Zuckerman報導。

4
對一個加州家庭而言，火災後返家之路，是一段長達16個月的漫長旅程。

菲格羅亞（Figueroa）一家重新擁有了自己的房子，卻找不回原本的社區。米西與法蘭克・菲格羅亞夫婦，以及他們的三個孩子，上個月搬進了在阿爾塔迪納（Altadena）新蓋好的房子——就位在他們住了10年的舊居所原址上，這棟舊居已於2025年1月毀於伊頓大火（Eaton Fire）。這場大火損毀或摧毀了當地約6000處房產，奪走19條人命。菲格羅亞一家失去了一切，但憑藉著辛勤努力、堅持不懈與一點運氣，他們成為目前少數已重返家園的流離失所居民之一。白天，他們的社區裡滿是工人與攤販的忙碌身影；但一到夜晚，這裡就變成一座空城，Paul Kiernan報導。

5
美國人的經濟焦慮正沿著所得階梯向上蔓延。

《華爾街日報》最新民調發現，即便是自認屬於美國最富裕階層的人，也對當前財務狀況、未來幾年及子女前景，抱持高度憂慮。超過四成自認屬於上層階級或中上階層的美國人表示，他們尚未存夠足以舒適退休的資金。僅約四成的人表示，自己目前的財務安全感符合原本人生規劃的預期。近五分之三的人表示，高油價讓他們感到吃緊。而最富裕階層的人，也已對「這個曾讓他們受益的經濟能提升下一代生活」這件事，失去了信心，Aaron Zitner報導。

6
一定要有錢才能享受南塔克特島（Nantucket）嗎？我們找到了答案。

南塔克特島以其海濱豪宅和高檔遊艇碼頭聞名。但如果你知道去哪裡找，這座麻州小島也存在著一個更寧靜、更悠閒的版本：鵝卵石小巷、美得令人難以置信的日落，以及可以獨自待上數小時、不見他人蹤影的隱密海灘。我們的指南教你如何不必花大錢加入高爾夫球俱樂部，也能盡情享受這座島嶼。

本週末焦點

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Apple’s Tim Cook Warns Price Hikes Are Unavoidable
emails.contentEn:
✏️ The global memory-chip shortage is coming for the iPhone. In an exclusive interview with the Journal, Apple CEO Tim Cook said that soaring component costs have made price increases “unavoidable.” While Apple is still working through which devices will be hit, we are likely to find out this September when its new products arrive. We look at what this means for consumers—and why the base price of the next iPhone could jump by $200 or more.

Also: The 10-Point won’t publish tomorrow for Juneteenth. Five years after June 19 became a federal holiday, states and cities still differ wildly on whether it is a paid day off. Check out our map to see how your region handles it. We’ll be back on Saturday.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

另外：《10-Point》明日因六月節（Juneteenth）不發行。6月19日成為聯邦假日已滿五年，但各州與城市在是否列為有薪假上，做法仍大相逕庭。查看我們的地圖，了解你所在地區的處理方式。我們週六見。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Hacker Sent to Soothe Washington’s AI Fears
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Trump administration officials have spent recent days fretting over the power of Anthropic’s next-generation AI software to potentially wreak havoc on global cybersecurity. Now, Anthropic is banking on a hacker —one who recently rang the alarm about the dangers of artificial intelligence—to help soothe the government’s nerves. Nicholas Carlini is part of a team dispatched to the nation’s capital to convince the White House that, even though there is no guaranteed safety in AI, it is better to release the software than to keep it under wraps. The episode reflects the chaos and uncertainty that rapidly advancing AI has brought to the cybersecurity world—and ramps up a monthslong spat between the government and Anthropic.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

Iran is returning to nuclear talks no longer afraid of America—but it still needs sanctions relief to stave off economic calamity. Mike Collins won Georgia’s GOP primary runoff over former college football coach Derek Dooley, setting up a showdown with Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff in November. Elon Musk is unleashing SpaceX’s new war chest to solve his AI problem.

The trillionaire has admitted SpaceX lags behind rivals like OpenAI, Anthropic and even Google and Chinese open-source models in the race to build out AI. He now has an $86 billion war chest to help change that. And the first target is getting enterprise customers who Musk hopes are willing to pay large sums for access to SpaceX’s tools and computing power. Buying AI-coding agent Cursor and renting out data-center capacity will give the company a launchpad to land more enterprise customers, report Becky Peterson and Angel Au-Yeung.

Xi’s enforcers are hunting down officials who consult mystics and borrow too much.

Chinese leader Xi Jinping has escalated his fight against corruption into a ruthless campaign to enforce political loyalty. Communist Party enforcers punished nearly a million people in 2025, the highest number on record. The Journal reviewed disciplinary statements on more than 940 officials punished under Xi, published by the party’s top internal watchdog from 2013 to this May. The data shows how Xi’s purges have evolved in their focus, from economic crimes and moral lapses—such as bribery, embezzlement and adultery—to include wide-ranging political offenses. Xi’s goal: keeping officials on their toes at all times, report Chun Han Wong and Andrew Barnett. The Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, the party’s top internal watchdog, didn’t respond to queries.

A scandal involving cigars and a canceled lacrosse season is rocking a Massachusetts town.

The boys gathered on an Ipswich, Mass., beach to celebrate their high-school graduation, some with medals draped over their gowns. Jutting from each mouth: cigars that may or may not have been real. The photos taken on June 7 mirrored those snapped all around the country lately. But in this coastal enclave dubbed America’s Best-Preserved Puritan Town, those snapshots have lit a burning debate . What’s beyond dispute: Six of the grads were on Ipswich High School’s lacrosse team, and administrators suspended all six from a playoff game two days later for violating state athletic association rules against tobacco use. The team ultimately voted to forfeit the contest—and just like that, their championship run went up in smoke. Now, Ipswich is in a fierce debate over whether the penalty matched the foul, reports Scott Calvert.

Estimates of how much Iranian assets abroad are worth vary, with Tehran saying it’s at least $100 billion. Other experts put it much lower. Tehran’s priority is to unblock an initial $24 billion in phases.
