That’s how much per night the SpringHill Suites East Rutherford—one of the hotels closest to the MetLife Stadium—is asking for the World Cup final weekend, with a two-night minimum. The stadium is hosting eight tournament matches, including the final on July 19. While hotels and Airbnbs across the U.S. might not be experiencing the hoped for World Cup windfall, hotels near the stadium aren’t despondent given their prime location. The Hampton Inn by Hilton next door wants $4,200 during the final weekend.

AND FINALLY...

9

‘Toy Story’ has won over every generation.

Hollywood’s longest-running animated film series—which has grossed more than $3 billion in theaters worldwide—belongs to an audience that spans generations. Part of the franchise’s enduring appeal lies in the deep emotional hooks embedded in the story of Woody, Buzz Lightyear and a closet full of other living toys. In “Toy Story 5,” the threat facing the toys isn’t a yard sale (“Toy Story 2”) or a donation box (“Toy Story 3”) but the digital devices seizing children’s attention . We look back at the films that brought the toys to this moment.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Which is a greater threat—China or Anthropic? The Trump administration can’t seem to decide judging from its order to restrict access to Anthropic’s frontier artificial-intelligence models.
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 川普政府官員近日一直憂心忡忡，擔心Anthropic下一代AI軟體的強大能力可能對全球網路安全造成嚴重破壞。如今，Anthropic正倚仗一位駭客——這位人士最近才剛對AI的危險性發出警訊——來幫忙安撫政府的緊張情緒。尼可拉斯・卡里尼（Nicholas Carlini）是被派往首都的團隊成員之一，任務是說服白宮：儘管AI無法保證絕對安全，但與其將軟體雪藏，不如將其釋出。這起事件反映出快速發展的AI，為網路安全領域帶來的混亂與不確定性——也讓政府與Anthropic之間長達數月的爭執進一步升溫。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
伊朗重返核談判桌，已不再畏懼美國——但仍需要解除制裁，才能避免經濟陷入災難。聯準會主席凱文・沃許本週將以尷尬的處境，迎來他任內的第一次會議。佛羅里達州的選區重劃，讓民主黨人陷入內鬥——而且情況愈演愈亂。眾議員麥克・柯林斯（Mike Collins）在喬治亞州共和黨初選決選中，擊敗前大學美式足球教練德瑞克・杜利（Derek Dooley），將於11月與民主黨參議員瓊・歐薩夫（Jon Ossoff）對決。一起原定於週日、在白宮草坪舉行UFC籠鬥賽的攻擊陰謀，因一位憂心忡忡的母親報警而被揭發。

市場直擊

2
道瓊期貨 52459.00　跌11.00　跌0.02%；標普500期貨 7596.75　漲9.50　漲0.13%；那斯達克100期貨 30491.50　漲177.75　漲0.59%
資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年6月17日美東時間上午5:54

急需現金的AI公司，正蜂擁湧入債券市場一個冷僻的角落。David Wainer撰文指出，隨著成本趨勢降溫、川普政府政策放鬆，保險業已出現反彈。

獨家搶先看

3
伊隆・馬斯克動用SpaceX的新戰備資金，來解決自己的AI困境。

這位身家上兆美元的富豪已承認，在打造AI的競賽中，SpaceX落後於OpenAI、Anthropic，甚至Google和中國的開源模型。如今他手握860億美元的戰備資金，準備扭轉局面。首要目標是爭取企業客戶，馬斯克希望這些客戶願意支付高額費用，以取得SpaceX的工具與運算能力。收購AI程式編寫代理公司Cursor，並出租資料中心產能，將為該公司提供爭取更多企業客戶的跳板，Becky Peterson與Angel Au-Yeung報導。

4
習近平的執法者正追查那些請教神秘術士、借貸過度的官員。

中國領導人習近平已將其反腐鬥爭，升級為一場強制政治忠誠的無情運動。中共紀律執法人員在2025年懲處了近百萬人，創下歷史新高。本報審閱了黨內最高內部監察機構自2013年至今年5月間公布的940多名遭習近平懲處官員的紀律處分聲明。數據顯示，習近平整肅行動的重點已逐漸演變，從經濟犯罪與道德敗壞——例如賄賂、侵吞公款與通姦——擴大到涵蓋範圍廣泛的政治罪行。習近平的目標：讓官員時時刻刻保持警惕，Chun Han Wong與Andrew Barnett報導。作為黨內最高內部監察機構的中央紀律檢查委員會未回應詢問。

5
一樁涉及雪茄與被取消長曲棍球賽季的醜聞，正震動麻州一個小鎮。

男孩們聚集在麻州伊普斯威奇（Ipswich）的一處海灘，慶祝高中畢業，有些人的畢業袍上還掛著獎牌。每個人嘴裡都叼著雪茄——真假難辨。這些攝於6月7日的照片，與近期全美各地拍下的畢業照如出一轍。但在這個素有「美國保存最完好的清教徒小鎮」之稱的沿海社區，這些照片卻點燃了一場激烈爭論。無可爭議的是：六名畢業生是伊普斯威奇高中長曲棍球隊的隊員，校方兩天後以違反州體育協會禁菸規定為由，將這六人禁賽一場季後賽。球隊最終投票決定棄賽——他們的冠軍之路，就這樣化為烏有。如今，伊普斯威奇正就這項處分是否與過失相稱，展開激烈辯論，Scott Calvert報導。

6
以下是伊朗數十億美元凍結資產的存放地點：

地圖：EMMA BROWN／WSJ

伊朗與川普政府展開談判，目光鎖定一項巨大獎賞：數百億美元被凍結在海外的資產，這些資金有助於重振其陷入危機的經濟。外界對伊朗海外資產價值的估算不一，德黑蘭聲稱至少有1000億美元，但其他專家的估計則低得多。德黑蘭的首要目標，是分階段解凍最初的240億美元。

今日焦點

7
聯準會將公布利率決議，市場焦點集中在沃許可能釋出的任何政策指引上。經濟數據：零售銷售與成屋待完成銷售。世界盃：迦納對巴拿馬（多倫多）；英格蘭對克羅埃西亞（達拉斯）；葡萄牙對剛果民主共和國（休士頓）；烏茲別克對哥倫比亞（墨西哥城）。

數字看世界

8
4500美元
這是SpringHill Suites East Rutherford——最靠近大都會人壽體育場（MetLife Stadium）的飯店之一——針對世界盃決賽週末開出的每晚房價，且須至少入住兩晚。該體育場將主辦八場賽事，包括7月19日的總決賽。儘管美國各地的飯店與Airbnb房源，可能並未如預期般迎來世界盃帶來的意外收穫，但體育場附近的飯店憑藉絕佳地理位置，並未因此感到氣餒。隔壁的希爾頓歡朋酒店（Hampton Inn by Hilton），決賽週末的房價開到4200美元。

最後一則

9
《玩具總動員》征服了每一個世代。

好萊塢史上最長壽的動畫系列電影——全球累計票房已超過30億美元——擁有跨世代的觀眾群。這個系列歷久不衰的魅力之一，在於胡迪、巴斯光年，以及一整櫃有生命的玩具們的故事中，蘊藏著深刻的情感牽引。在《玩具總動員5》中，玩具們面臨的威脅，不再是庭院拍賣（《玩具總動員2》）或捐贈箱（《玩具總動員3》），而是搶走孩子們注意力的數位裝置。我們回顧了這些將玩具們帶到今天這一步的電影。

新聞室之外

10
社論：中國與Anthropic，究竟哪個才是更大的威脅？從川普政府下令限制外界使用Anthropic最尖端AI模型的舉動來看，政府自己似乎也拿不定主意。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Inside the Race to Land an Iran Deal
emails.contentEn:
✏️ With the full text of the Iran peace deal still under wraps, world leaders and corporate boardrooms are racing to parse exactly what President Trump agreed to over the weekend. This morning, our reporters in Washington, D.C., take you behind the scenes of how the agreement came together during Trump’s 80th birthday celebration—including last-minute frustrations with Israel that nearly blew up the talks. We’re tracking the immediate fallout, from plunging oil prices to the frantic diplomatic scramble to keep this fragile truce on track before Friday’s formal signing in Geneva.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

General Motors is in talks with Lockheed Martin about making parts for the defense contractor’s weapons. The Justice Department’s senior leadership closed an investigation of Paramount’s bid for Warner Bros. Discovery before career staffers who were concerned about the acquisition had an opportunity to object. The U.S. Coast Guard has found that tankers ferrying sanctioned oil from Iran and Russia are using digital tools that risk the safety of the ships, their crews and the environment. Eight crew members are believed dead after a U.S. Air Force B-52 bomber they were on crashed shortly after takeoff at Edwards Air Force Base in California. This year’s World Cup was pitched as a showcase of North America’s collective ambition . Instead, the event has highlighted the current tensions between the U.S., Mexico and Canada.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 52139.00 10.00 0.02 S&P 500 Futures 7620.00 -6.50 0.09 Nasdaq 100 Futures 30876.50 12.25 0.04

Source: Factset, Market data as of 6/16/2026, 5:59:56 AM ET

📈 Follow our live financial coverage all day.

Stocks will have even more room to fly if the Strait of Hormuz reopens. Smartphone exposure haunts Qualcomm stock despite it diversifying into cars and data centers, write Asa Fitch and Dan Gallagher.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

The race to land an Iran deal loomed large behind Trump’s UFC birthday.

As fighters warmed up inside the White House and guests began to stream toward the canopy set up for cage fights on the lawn, Trump sat in the residence and added his digital signature to a document meant to wind down the war with Iran. The president had spent his birthday toggling between congratulatory calls and urgent conversations with senior aides and foreign leaders as he raced to lock in the fragile preliminary peace deal. The agreement Trump ultimately signed emerged after a frantic weekend in which he veered from the brink of a new military escalation to celebrating a breakthrough with what he called “the most rational” group of Iranian leaders, report Vera Bergengruen, Josh Dawsey, Robbie Gramer and Alexander Ward.

4

Trump’s personal lawyer was said to be part of a billionaire’s criminal defense.

Lawyers for Indian billionaire Gautam Adani pressed the Justice Department last year to drop a 2024 fraud case against the founder and chairman of energy and logistics giant Adani Group. They got nowhere. By the spring of 2025, senior DOJ officials had given the green light to proceed. Then, according to seven people familiar with the matter and records reviewed by the Journal, a powerful new player was said to have joined the Adani team: Boris Epshteyn, Trump’s personal attorney , report Joe Palazzolo, Rebecca Ballhaus, C. Ryan Barber, Josh Dawsey and Dave Michaels. Epshteyn denies any relationship with Adani.

5

Hotel owners are rebelling against Marriott’s loyalty program.

Dozens of America’s biggest hotel owners are pressuring Marriott International to share more of the wealth from its lucrative partnerships tied to the Marriott Bonvoy loyalty program. Marriott has said that fee revenue from its co-branded credit cards is expected to jump 35% this year to nearly $1 billion. Owners say that they previously believed the program was only breaking even and that the hotel giant is ripping them off. Marriott says it takes owners’ concerns seriously, reports Kate King.

6

It’s known as the Meat Wall—and it could be the hack to World Cup glory.

Any team hoping to lift the World Cup has spent years preparing for hurdles that range from penalty shootouts to the prospect of national humiliation. But the most daunting opponent this summer will be an obstacle never before witnessed at this tournament: a colossal slab of human flesh known as the Meat Wall. Formed by lining up the biggest, brawniest players inside the six-yard box, it is deployed with the express aim of obstructing the opposing goalkeeper. This hulking new tactic has turned the beautiful game into a wrestling match.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

WSJ live Q&A: What questions do you have about the direction of the Federal Reserve under its new chairman, Kevin Warsh? Join a live written chat with chief economics reporter Nick Timiraos from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. ET. World Cup: France vs. Senegal in New Jersey; Iraq vs. Norway in Massachusetts; Argentina vs. Algeria in Kansas City; Austria vs. Jordan in California. Midterms: Georgia holds runoff elections, including in the race for a Republican Senate nominee; voters will choose between a Trump-backed candidate and one backed by Gov. Brian Kemp. Alabama also holds runoffs, and Oklahoma and Washington, D.C., hold primary elections. THE NUMBER

8

 $829

The estimated starting lease price for Rivian’s new R2 electric SUV , which could exceed $1,000. The California-based automaker has high hopes that the new R2 will help take it from a scrappy EV startup to a mainstream, volume-selling automaker. But customers are already balking at the price, noting that current R2 leasing costs are close to Rivian’s higher-end models.

AND FINALLY...

9

Vultures are stinking up this North Carolina town. Locals want justice.

These days, you have to watch where you step in parts of Hillsborough, N.C. Those white splashes on the sidewalk aren’t fresh paint. They’re vulture poop . Lots of it. Large groups of black vultures have taken up residence in town, covering the quaint historic district in feathers and foul-smelling excrement. Officials are suing one couple for contributing to the mess.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Trump is touting his latest ceasefire deal with Iran as peace in our time, but the world is more likely to see it as a strategic retreat short of achieving his war aims .

Correction: Sunday’s newsletter incorrectly said Virginia would hold a primary on Tuesday.
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 伊朗和平協議全文仍未公開，各國領袖與企業董事會正競相解讀，川普總統上週末究竟同意了哪些條款。今早，我們駐華盛頓特區的記者帶你深入了解，這項協議如何在川普80歲生日慶祝活動期間敲定——包括與以色列之間一度差點讓談判破局的最後關頭摩擦。我們也持續追蹤事件的即時後續影響，從油價暴跌到各方為在週五日內瓦正式簽署前，設法讓這脆弱停火維持下去而展開的外交狂奔。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
通用汽車正與洛克希德馬丁（Lockheed Martin）洽談，為這家國防承包商的武器製造零組件。司法部高層在對此次收購案感到擔憂的資深職員有機會提出異議之前，就結束了對派拉蒙收購華納兄弟探索頻道案的調查。美國海岸防衛隊發現，運送伊朗與俄羅斯受制裁石油的油輪，正使用可能危及船隻、船員與環境安全的數位工具。美國空軍一架B-52轟炸機在加州愛德華茲空軍基地起飛後不久墜毀，機上8名機組人員恐已罹難。今年的世界盃原本被包裝成展現北美團結雄心的舞台，如今卻反而凸顯出美國、墨西哥與加拿大之間的緊張關係。

市場直擊

2
道瓊期貨 52139.00　漲10.00　漲0.02%；標普500期貨 7620.00　跌6.50　跌0.09%；那斯達克100期貨 30876.50　漲12.25　漲0.04%
資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年6月16日美東時間上午5:59

若荷莫茲海峽重新開放，股市將有更大的上漲空間。Asa Fitch與Dan Gallagher撰文指出，儘管高通已朝汽車與資料中心多元布局，智慧型手機曝險仍持續困擾其股價。

獨家搶先看

3
爭取達成伊朗協議的競速，正是川普UFC生日派對背後的重頭戲。

當拳手在白宮內熱身、賓客開始湧向草坪上為籠鬥賽搭建的天篷時，川普正坐在官邸內，為一份旨在結束對伊朗戰爭的文件加上他的電子簽名。這位總統的生日，是在祝賀電話與同高階幕僚、外國領袖的緊急通話之間來回切換中度過，只為搶在時限內敲定這份脆弱的初步和平協議。川普最終簽署的這份協議，是在一個瘋狂的週末後出爐——他先是徘徊在新一輪軍事升級的邊緣，隨後又與他口中「最理性」的一批伊朗領導人一同慶祝這項突破，Vera Bergengruen、Josh Dawsey、Robbie Gramer與Alexander Ward報導。

4
據稱，川普的私人律師曾參與一位億萬富豪的刑事辯護。

印度億萬富豪高塔姆・阿達尼（Gautam Adani）的律師去年曾向司法部施壓，要求撤銷2024年對這位能源與物流巨頭阿達尼集團創辦人兼董事長的詐欺案，但沒有得逞。到了2025年春天，司法部高層已放行讓案件繼續推進。隨後，據七位知情人士及本報審閱的紀錄顯示，一位強而有力的新角色據稱加入了阿達尼團隊：川普的私人律師鮑里斯・埃普斯坦（Boris Epshteyn），Joe Palazzolo、Rebecca Ballhaus、C. Ryan Barber、Josh Dawsey與Dave Michaels報導。埃普斯坦否認與阿達尼有任何關係。

5
飯店業主正群起反抗萬豪的忠誠會員計畫。

數十位美國最大飯店業主，正向萬豪國際（Marriott International）施壓，要求該公司從其獲利豐厚、與萬豪Bonvoy忠誠計畫掛鉤的合作關係中分出更多利益。萬豪表示，來自聯名信用卡的手續費收入，預計今年將激增35%，逼近10億美元。業主們表示，他們原本以為這項計畫只是打平，如今卻認為這家飯店巨頭其實在坑他們一筆。萬豪表示，公司重視業主的疑慮，Kate King報導。

6
它被稱為「肉牆」——這可能是奪得世界盃榮耀的祕訣。

任何一支渴望捧起世界盃的球隊，都花了數年時間備戰各種難關，從十二碼點球大戰到全國蒙羞的可能性都包括在內。但今年夏天，最令人畏懼的對手，將是這項賽事史上前所未見的一道障礙：一堵由人體組成、被稱為「肉牆」的龐然大物。這堵牆由最魁梧、最強壯的球員在小禁區內一字排開組成，目的明確：阻擋對方守門員的視線。這種笨重的新戰術，已讓這項美麗的運動變成了一場摔角比賽。

今日焦點

7
《華爾街日報》線上問答：對於新任主席凱文・沃許領導下的聯準會走向，你有什麼問題？加入首席經濟記者尼克・提米拉歐斯（Nick Timiraos）主持的即時文字聊天，時間為美東時間上午10時至11時。世界盃：法國對塞內加爾（紐澤西）；伊拉克對挪威（麻州）；阿根廷對阿爾及利亞（堪薩斯城）；奧地利對約旦（加州）。期中選舉：喬治亞州舉行決選，包括共和黨參議員候選人之爭——選民將在川普支持的候選人與州長布萊恩・坎普（Brian Kemp）支持的候選人之間做出選擇。阿拉巴馬州也舉行決選，奧克拉荷馬州與華盛頓特區則舉行初選。

數字看世界

8
829美元
這是Rivian新款電動休旅車R2的預估起租價，實際可能超過1000美元。這家總部位於加州的車廠，對新款R2寄予厚望，希望能藉此讓公司從一家苦苦掙扎的電動車新創企業，轉型為主流的大規模量產車廠。但消費者已對這個價位有所遲疑，指出目前R2的租賃成本，已逼近Rivian高階車款的水準。

最後一則

9
禿鷲正讓北卡羅來納州一座小鎮臭氣沖天，居民要求討回公道。

如今，走在北卡羅來納州希爾斯伯勒（Hillsborough）部分街區時，你得看清楚腳下踩的是什麼。人行道上那些白色斑漬，可不是新油漆，而是黑禿鷲的糞便——而且數量驚人。大批黑禿鷲已在鎮上安家落戶，讓這個古色古香的歷史街區，佈滿羽毛與惡臭排泄物。官員正對一對夫婦提告，指控他們助長了這場髒亂。

新聞室之外

10
社論：川普將他與伊朗達成的最新停火協議，吹捧為「我們這個時代的和平」，但世人恐怕更可能將其視為一場未能達成戰爭目標的戰略性撤退。

更正：週日版電子報誤稱維吉尼亞州將於週二舉行初選。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The U.S. and Iran Say They Have a Deal
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Fresh from announcing a peace deal with Iran and celebrating his 80th birthday, President Trump is flying to Europe for a summit with fellow leaders in the Group of Seven . The high-level discussions are certain to center on the interim agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, lift the U.S. blockade and pause the war, as well as the tabled topics of technology, trade and global economic imbalances. And although the world leaders are expected to shower Trump with praise over the deal, there will also be questions on how such a complicated pact could hold together.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Iran and the U.S. agreed on an interim peace deal although the text of the accord is unlikely to be released publicly until an expected signing ceremony on Friday in Switzerland. The president hosted a UFC cage fight at the White House, a spectacle that merged corporate interests on one of America’s most famous plots of public land with exclusive access for select VIPs. For decades, the Federal Reserve believed talking openly made its policy work better, but Kevin Warsh believes the opposite —the new chairman’s first meeting is on Wednesday. Anthropic is racing to resolve its latest conflict with the Trump administration , meeting with officials and dispatching top technical staff to Washington in pursuit of a deal to end export restrictions on its most powerful artificial intelligence models. The entrepreneur Charlie Javice has been seeking a presidential pardon for her criminal conviction for defrauding JPMorgan Chase when she sold her company to the bank. The U.K. plans to ban children under the age of 16 from major social-media platforms, increasing pressure on big tech companies to shield younger users from harmful online content.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 52023.00 418.00 0.81 S&P 500 Futures 7521.50 86.50 1.16 Nasdaq 100 Futures 30534.75 580.00 1.94

Source: Factset, Market data as of 6/15/2026, 6:02:20 AM ET

📈 Follow our live financial coverage all day.

While the frenzy over AI is sending technology-company valuations through the roof in the U.S. and Asian markets, there are still some relative bargains in China . The luxury handbag’s heyday could be ending , writes Carol Ryan.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Oil executives are sounding the alarm over dwindling stockpiles.

Chevron CEO Mike Wirth has repeatedly warned on TV of an impending supply crunch . Neil Chapman, the No. 2 at Exxon Mobil, has said the U.S. is approaching “unheard-of inventory levels.” So far, financial markets have shrugged off the warnings and the Trump administration doesn’t foresee a jump in energy prices. But the executives’ message is essentially the same: The world is guzzling so much oil that some U.S. storage hubs now risk falling below their minimum operating levels, report Collin Eaton, Benoît Morenne and Michael R. Gordon. At that point, prices will have to surge to stop the run on supplies, they said.

4

Here’s how the Pentagon plans to fix its pricey missile problem.

The U.S. military is using nonstandard contracts and tasking defense companies to design new weapons from scratch to cut years of production time and hundreds of millions of dollars off their cost, reports Drew FitzGerald. Even before the Iran war cut into U.S. armament supplies, lawmakers and military brass worried that the U.S. can’t rearm itself fast enough to deter threats and respond to conflicts. The cheap precision munitions take aim at the U.S. military’s longer-running problem: the contract competitions, design debates and budget battles that have mired Pentagon weapons programs with yearslong delays and cost overruns.

5

Work from home is here to stay—even if some CEOs don’t love it.

The past couple of years have seen a wave of big companies announcing plans to require employees to spend more time in the office . But across the broader economy, the evidence suggests that the return to the office has stalled out, reports Justin Lahart. The disconnect between the high-profile return-to-office mandates and the broader data could in part be because, big as they are, those companies account for just a portion of the 163-million-strong U.S. workforce.

6

AI deepfakes are getting weirder and harder to spot in the midterms.

Political campaigns are employing AI in a range of campaign ads to elevate candidates and attack opponents, fueling concerns that the wave of fake content will undermine the midterm elections. The AI-altered image above shows a muscular version of Mike Rogers that was circulated recently to bolster the GOP Senate candidate from Michigan.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

The Group of Seven summit begins. World Cup: Spain vs. Cape Verde in Atlanta; Belgium vs. Egypt in Seattle; Saudi Arabia vs. Uruguay in Miami; Iran vs. New Zealand in California. Economic Data: Industrial production and the Empire State manufacturing survey. Earnings: Canopy Growth, Dave and Buster’s THE NUMBER

8

 $7.1 billion

The amount of venture funding in 2025 for U.S. space-technology firms excluding SpaceX, up from $2.5 billion a year earlier, according to data provider PitchBook. Last year’s haul was the strongest since companies raised almost $4 billion in 2021.

AND FINALLY...

9

This Congo soccer superfan says he can stop goals.

Michel Kuka Mboladinga is the Democratic Republic of Congo’s national team’s most famous fan, known for his practice of holding a statue-like pose throughout entire games —a tribute to his country’s founding prime minister, Patrice Lumumba. Known for his snappy suits and steely gaze, Mboladinga stays frozen to give his side the strength to block shots and to win battles on the pitch.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Who is “ The Smallest Man Who Ever Lived ”? Politics has produced a lot of contenders for the title.
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 剛宣布與伊朗達成和平協議、並慶祝完80歲生日，川普總統即將飛往歐洲，與七大工業國（G7）其他領袖召開峰會。這場高層會談的焦點，勢必集中在重新開放荷莫茲海峽、解除美國封鎖並暫停戰爭的臨時協議上，此外，科技、貿易與全球經濟失衡等議題也已排上議程。儘管各國領袖預料將對這項協議大力讚揚川普，但外界也將質疑，這樣一份複雜的協議究竟能否維持下去。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
伊朗與美國就臨時和平協議達成共識，不過協議全文預計要等到週五在瑞士舉行的簽署儀式後才會公開。總統在白宮主辦了一場UFC籠鬥賽，這場盛事將企業利益，與美國最著名公共用地之一，以及僅限特選貴賓進入的獨家待遇，結合在一起。數十年來，聯準會一直認為公開透明的溝通有助於政策發揮效果，但凱文・沃許卻持相反看法——這位新任主席的首次會議將於週三舉行。Anthropic正加緊努力，解決與川普政府之間的最新衝突，與官員會面並派遣頂尖技術人員前往華盛頓，力求達成協議，以終止對其最強大AI模型的出口限制。企業家查莉・賈維斯（Charlie Javice）因在將公司出售給摩根大通時詐騙該行而遭定罪，她一直在爭取總統特赦。英國計劃禁止16歲以下兒童使用主要社群媒體平台，這將加大對大型科技公司的壓力，要求其保護年輕使用者免受有害網路內容侵害。

市場直擊

2
道瓊期貨 52023.00　漲418.00　漲0.81%；標普500期貨 7521.50　漲86.50　漲1.16%；那斯達克100期貨 30534.75　漲580.00　漲1.94%
資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年6月15日美東時間上午6:02

儘管AI熱潮正推動美國與亞洲市場科技公司估值飆升，中國市場仍存在一些相對划算的標的。Carol Ryan撰文指出，奢華手袋的全盛時期可能即將結束。

獨家搶先看

3
石油業高層正對庫存日益減少發出警訊。

雪佛龍執行長麥克・沃斯（Mike Wirth）已多次在電視上警告，供應緊縮即將來臨。埃克森美孚（Exxon Mobil）第二號人物尼爾・查普曼（Neil Chapman）表示，美國正逼近「前所未見的庫存水準」。目前為止，金融市場對這些警告不以為意，川普政府也不預期能源價格會飆升。但這些高層傳達的訊息本質上是一致的：全球石油消耗量之大，已讓美國部分儲油樞紐面臨跌破最低運作水準的風險，Collin Eaton、Benoît Morenne與Michael R. Gordon報導。他們表示，一旦到了那個地步，價格勢必得飆升，才能遏止供應被搶購一空的局面。

4
以下是五角大廈打算如何解決其昂貴飛彈難題的方法。

美國軍方正採用非標準合約，並委託國防公司從零開始設計新武器，藉此縮短數年的生產時間，並節省數億美元成本，Drew FitzGerald報導。早在伊朗戰爭衝擊美國軍火供應之前，國會議員與軍方高層就已擔憂，美國無法以足夠快的速度重新武裝自己，來嚇阻威脅並應對衝突。這批廉價精準彈藥，正是針對美軍長期存在的老問題而來：合約競標、設計爭議與預算角力，多年來一直讓五角大廈的武器計畫深陷延遲與成本超支的泥淖。

5
在家工作模式將持續下去——即便部分執行長並不樂見。

過去這兩年來，一波大型企業陸續宣布計畫，要求員工增加進辦公室的時間。但從整體經濟來看，證據顯示，重返辦公室的趨勢已經停滯，Justin Lahart報導。這種高調的重返辦公室政策與更廣泛數據之間的落差，部分原因可能在於：儘管這些企業規模龐大，但在美國1.63億人的勞動力中，它們也僅占其中一部分。

6
AI深偽影片正變得愈來愈詭異、也愈來愈難以識破，並滲入期中選舉。

政治競選團隊正在各類競選廣告中運用AI技術，藉此拉抬候選人聲勢或攻擊對手，這也加深了外界的憂慮：這波假造內容浪潮恐將破壞期中選舉的公正性。上方那張經AI變造的圖片，顯示了一個肌肉發達版本的麥克・羅傑斯（Mike Rogers），該圖近期被用來為這位密西根州共和黨參議員候選人造勢。

今日焦點

7
七大工業國峰會開幕。世界盃：西班牙對維德角（亞特蘭大）；比利時對埃及（西雅圖）；沙烏地阿拉伯對烏拉圭（邁阿密）；伊朗對紐西蘭（加州）。經濟數據：工業生產指數與紐約州製造業調查。財報：Canopy Growth、Dave and Buster's。

數字看世界

8
71億美元
根據數據供應商PitchBook統計，2025年美國太空科技公司（不含SpaceX）獲得的創投資金總額，較前一年的25億美元大幅成長。這是自2021年企業募資近40億美元以來，表現最強勁的一年。

最後一則

9
這位剛果超級球迷聲稱自己能阻止對手進球。

米歇爾・庫卡・姆博拉丁加（Michel Kuka Mboladinga）是剛果民主共和國國家隊最有名的球迷，以在整場比賽中維持雕像般靜止不動的姿勢聞名——這是為了向該國建國總理帕特里斯・盧蒙巴（Patrice Lumumba）致敬。以俐落西裝與堅定眼神著稱的姆博拉丁加，靠著保持不動，為自己支持的球隊注入力量，幫助他們擋下射門、在場上贏得勝利。

新聞室之外

10
社論：「史上最渺小之人」究竟是誰？政壇上，角逐這個「頭銜」的候選人可不少。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Rich Californians Get Creative
emails.contentEn:
✏️ In the face of California’s proposed billionaire tax, the state’s ultrawealthy are getting creative…with help from a multitude of advisers. The Journal’s Juliet Chung reports on inventive tax-planning strategies , which include buying dream vacation homes, boosting charitable giving and even buying expensive assets like art or yachts and keeping them outside of California.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Even as the U.S. and Iran appear close to a deal, the new head of Tehran’s feared paramilitary force, Ahmad Vahidi, has emerged as a key power broker who is pushing a hard line at the negotiating table. The Knicks’ 53-year wait for a championship is over —and it took one final miracle. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is betting on his popularity and influence to push Democratic socialist allies into office. The Trump administration’s decision to halt all foreign use of Anthropic’s most-capable AI models was prompted by conversations between Amazon CEO Andy Jassy and U.S. officials including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. A relentless measles outbreak in Utah that has been spreading for nearly a year is putting the U.S. on a path to losing its longstanding measles-elimination status .

FROM THE MARKETS

2

SpaceX’s retail-powered market debut is helping to steady markets that have been shaken by the war in the Middle East, the runaway chip rally and higher interest rates. The logic behind the SpaceX index trade was faulty, writes James Mackintosh. Here’s a guide to the biggest winners from the SpaceX IPO.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

AI is supercharging deepfake nudes—and unleashing a new form of bullying among kids.

Artificial intelligence has made it trivially easy for anyone with a phone to digitally undress people and post explicit deepfakes online, which has introduced a new type of bullying and harassment among young people. These AI “nudify” tools are evolving and multiplying , report Georgia Wells and Rachel Wolfe. Laws cracking down on them have lagged behind cases and aren’t always enforced. Schools don’t know how to handle them. Parents are left trying to help their children regain a sense of safety as they try to scrub the images from the internet.

4

Why the bisexual man is Hollywood’s breakout star.

These days there’s no keeping Hollywood’s gay icons and hetero heartthrobs apart, writes Pamela Paul. Appreciated by both men and women, the new male lead is either boldly or just barely bisexual—and he’s suddenly everywhere, from “Heated Rivalry” to “The Night Manager.” So why all the bi now? It’s possible that bisexuality’s allure offers straight women some kind of fantasy corrective to the manosphere. Then again, on-screen bisexuals may just reflect demographic reality : Bisexuality is now the fastest-growing sexual orientation, with the number of American adults identifying as bisexual tripling since the ’90s.

5

A housing crisis is coming for Juneau’s most historic homes.

The Alaska city’s oldest neighborhood is Telephone Hill, which has homes dating back to when a 19th-century gold rush put the area on the map. Now, many local leaders want to see them bulldozed to make way for new, denser housing—which has ignited an outcry on the edge of an unbroken wilderness, reports Jim Carlton. The fight playing out in Alaska’s capital mirrors those across America, where demand for housing is running up against limited supply. But Juneau (population 31,600) faces a distinct bottleneck: It is bound on one side by the ocean and on the other by towering mountains with glaciers and impenetrable forests.

6

Europe’s arms race is creating boomtowns—so why are locals so unhappy?

DANIEL KISS/WSJ.

Europe’s defense boom promised to revive struggling towns across the continent, but it is instead sparking division and resentment in places like the English shipbuilding hub of Barrow-in-Furness and Bergerac in France's wine country. These tensions are creating headwinds for politicians trying to convince voters they must invest even more in defense to counter Russia and China, often at the expense of social spending.

HAPPENING THIS WEEK

7

World Cup: Matches continue all week, including England vs. Croatia on Wednesday and U.S. vs. Australia on Friday. Monday: The G7 Summit begins. Industrial production and the Empire State manufacturing survey. Tuesday: Primaries in Oklahoma and Virginia. New housing starts data. Wednesday: The Federal Reserve announces its interest-rate decision, where the focus is on any guidance from new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. Retail sales and pending home sales data. Friday: Juneteenth; stock and bond markets will be closed. Toy Story 5 opens in theaters.

THE NUMBER

8

 55

The age at which the so-called rule of 55 lets people who leave their employers pull money from a 401(k) or 403(b) retirement plan penalty-free. In contrast, with an individual retirement account, they would typically forfeit 10% of the money they pull out before age 59½. The Journal’s Anne Tergesen writes about a tax break few people know about, and even fewer use.

AND FINALLY...

9

This writer takes 24-hour “micro-retreats”—and thinks you should, too.

Science suggests you don’t need a long vacation to recharge. A 24-hour break that interrupts your routine —and puts you into a flow state—can be hugely restorative. Science writer Elizabeth Svoboda discusses the benefits of checking into a room a little after noon, then returning around the same time the next day.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 面對加州提議課徵的億萬富豪稅，該州的超級富豪們正在眾多顧問的協助下，發揮創意應對。本報記者Juliet Chung報導了各種別出心裁的節稅策略，包括購買夢想中的度假別墅、增加慈善捐款，甚至購買藝術品或遊艇等昂貴資產，並將其留在加州境外。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
儘管美伊看似即將達成協議，德黑蘭令人聞風喪膽的準軍事部隊新任領導人艾哈邁德・瓦希迪（Ahmad Vahidi），已崛起成為在談判桌上力主強硬路線的關鍵權力掮客。紐約尼克隊苦等53年的總冠軍終於到手——而且是靠著最後一刻的奇蹟才實現。紐約市長佐赫蘭・馬姆達尼（Zohran Mamdani）正押注自身人氣與影響力，推動民主社會主義盟友當選公職。川普政府決定禁止外國使用Anthropic最強大AI模型的決策，起因於亞馬遜執行長安迪・賈西（Andy Jassy）與包括財政部長史考特・貝森特（Scott Bessent）在內的美國官員之間的對話。猶他州一場已持續近一年、難以遏止的麻疹疫情爆發，正讓美國走向失去長期保持的「麻疹消除」地位。

市場動態

2
SpaceX由散戶投資人撐起的市場首秀，正有助於穩定受中東戰事、晶片股狂飆與利率上升衝擊而動盪的市場。James Mackintosh撰文指出，SpaceX指數交易背後的邏輯其實站不住腳。以下是SpaceX IPO最大贏家指南。

獨家搶先看

3
AI正在讓深偽裸照氾濫成災——並在孩童之間掀起一種新型霸凌。

人工智慧已讓任何拿著手機的人，都能輕而易舉地將他人數位「脫衣」，並在網路上發布露骨的深偽影像，這也為年輕人帶來一種新型態的霸凌與騷擾。Georgia Wells與Rachel Wolfe報導，這類AI「去衣」工具正不斷演進、數量激增。相關取締法規遠遠落後於實際案例，且執法也並不徹底。學校不知該如何應對。家長們只能努力幫助孩子在試圖從網路上清除這些影像的同時，重新找回安全感。

4
為何雙性戀男性成為好萊塢的新晉紅人。

Pamela Paul撰文指出，如今好萊塢的同志偶像與異性戀萬人迷之間的界線，早已不再分明。這種新型男主角同時受到男性與女性青睞，無論大膽出櫃還是若隱若現，都屬雙性戀——而且突然間無所不在，從《炙熱對決》（Heated Rivalry）到《夜班經理》（The Night Manager）都能見到蹤影。為何雙性戀如今如此當紅？有一種可能是，雙性戀的魅力為異性戀女性提供了某種對抗「男性圈」（manosphere）文化的幻想式修正。不過，螢幕上的雙性戀角色，或許也只是反映了人口結構的現實：如今雙性戀已是成長最快的性傾向，美國成年人自認雙性戀的比例，自1990年代以來已成長三倍。

5
一場住房危機，正籠罩著朱諾（Juneau）最具歷史意義的老宅。

這座阿拉斯加城市最古老的社區名為「電話山」（Telephone Hill），區內房屋最早可追溯至19世紀淘金熱讓此地聲名大噪的年代。如今，許多地方領袖希望將這些老屋夷平，為更密集的新住宅騰出空間——此舉在這片緊鄰未經開發荒野的地區，引發了強烈抗議，Jim Carlton報導。這場在阿拉斯加州首府上演的爭執，與全美各地住房需求超過有限供給所引發的衝突如出一轍。但朱諾（人口3萬1600人）面臨獨特的瓶頸：一側緊鄰海洋，另一側則是有冰河與密不透風森林的高聳山脈。

6
歐洲的軍備競賽正在打造出一批「爆發式繁榮」的城鎮——但為何當地居民卻如此不滿？

歐洲的國防榮景原本承諾能振興大陸各地陷入困境的城鎮，卻反而在英格蘭造船重鎮巴羅因弗內斯（Barrow-in-Furness）與法國葡萄酒之鄉貝爾傑拉克（Bergerac）等地，激起分裂與怨懟。這些緊張情勢，正為那些試圖說服選民「必須進一步加碼國防投資、以抗衡俄羅斯與中國」的政治人物，帶來逆風——而這往往是以犧牲社會支出為代價。

本週焦點

7
世界盃：本週賽事持續進行，包括週三的英格蘭對克羅埃西亞，以及週五的美國對澳洲。週一：G7峰會開幕。工業生產指數與紐約州製造業調查公布。週二：奧克拉荷馬州與維吉尼亞州舉行初選。新屋開工數據公布。週三：聯準會公布利率決議，市場焦點集中在新任主席凱文・沃許可能釋出的任何政策指引上。零售銷售與成屋待完成銷售數據公布。週五：六月節，股市與債市休市。《玩具總動員5》上映。

數字看世界

8
55
這是所謂「55歲規則」（rule of 55）允許離職員工在不受罰的情況下，從401(k)或403(b)退休帳戶提領資金的年齡門檻。相較之下，若使用個人退休帳戶（IRA），在59歲半之前提領資金，通常得放棄10%的金額作為罰款。本報記者Anne Tergesen撰文介紹了這項鮮少人知曉、更少人懂得運用的稅務優惠。

最後一則

9
這位作家熱衷「24小時微靜修」——她認為你也該試試。

科學研究顯示，你並不需要長假才能充電。一段打斷日常作息、能讓你進入心流狀態的24小時休息時光，就能帶來極大的恢復效果。科普作家伊莉莎白・斯沃博達（Elizabeth Svoboda）談到了中午過後入住房間、隔天差不多同一時間退房的做法，能帶來哪些益處。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Life in a Ukrainian City as Russia Closes In
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians face a daily question: Is now the time to drop everything and flee? As the Russian army continues to grind forward slowly, churning up everything in its path, residents living along the 800-mile front confront an agonizing choice. Over the course of a year, The Wall Street Journal followed citizens of Druzhkivka as they wrestled with leaving their homes while the fabric of their lives was slowly, painfully torn apart.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

The U.S. and Iran have turned from renewed war to the cusp of peace after a U.S. helicopter crash spurred an escalation that then led both sides to back down and negotiate. As President Trump nears his 80th birthday, his team has made a strategic decision to make him omnipresent , drawing a contrast with his predecessor—and showing Americans more of the good and bad of an aging president. Everything about the SpaceX IPO befitted Elon Musk’s original goal: striving for superlatives to reignite public support for space travel, writes Tim Higgins. The Kennedy Center said it began work to remove Trump’s name from the building, even as it blew past a court-ordered deadline. The U.S. defeated Paraguay 4-1 in its World Cup opener, a history-making victory that Jason Gay says should deliver a momentary respite for Team USA. Sarah Longwell, a former GOP operative is now running a news site for anyone who feels, in her words, “politically homeless.”

FROM THE MARKETS

2

SpaceX soared 19% , ending its first day of trading with a market value of $2.1 trillion, pulling off the largest initial public offering ever, and one of the smoothest. America has a credit card problem , just not the one you think, writes Telis Demos. 📊 Charts: Here’s why oil prices haven’t gone through the roof —yet.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

McDonald’s is no longer happy planning every meal around Coke.

Since a handshake deal in 1955 sealed a union between the two brands, they’ve together become icons of American capitalism—and America itself. But now the relationship is having problems. It’s not that they aren’t committed to one another, but that McDonald’s is no longer content with just Coke , report Heather Haddon and Laura Cooper. The burger chain is on the hunt for new business: Growth in U.S. burger sales has slowed, and Starbucks and Dunkin’ are showing that drinks generate billions of dollars on their own. McDonald’s this spring introduced its own custom sodas and refreshers, and it is gearing up to launch a line of energy drinks anchored by Red Bull—a first for the Golden Arches.

4

Inside the grand plan to end the hellscape that is Penn Station.

Many of the fans who visit New York City this month for the World Cup will squeeze through the decaying bowels of Pennsylvania Station, which is both the nation’s busiest transit hub and—literally—a scuzzy pit. Yet this past week, a venture known as Penn Transformation Partners unveiled a model for a new Penn Station selected by the Trump administration to be made real. It is, according to Andy Byford, the transit whiz who will oversee the project for Amtrak, not just another fanciful design exercise—but the best chance yet to right an act of civic vandalism since the original was destroyed in the 1960s, reports Joshua Chaffin.

5

Josh Shapiro is no-drama. Is that what Democrats want in 2028?

Known for a type-A, centrist streak and a mantra of “GSD,” or “Get S— Done,” the Pennsylvania governor has established himself as a popular moderate in a divided purple state. His unique profile has set him apart from the rest of the expected Democratic field, reports Sabrina Rodriguez. Some Democratic voters say they want a more combative stance against Trump. California Gov. Gavin Newsom—another Democrat with potential 2028 presidential ambitions—has established a national brand as a foil to Trump. But Shapiro is wagering that voters across the political spectrum are fatigued by political theater, and that his path to the White House runs through his home state.

6

Knicks mania is causing culinary mayhem.

UTOPIA BAGELS

From electric-blue Jalen Brunson rigatoni to a Knicks-themed Dunkin doughnut, the Journal’s food columnist took a bite out of the blue-and-orange culinary chaos that’s ensued as Knicks fever sweeps New York City.

HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

7

Saturday: The World Cup continues with matches including Brazil vs. Morocco. Sunday: Flag Day. President Trump turns 80. The White House is hosting a UFC Freedom 250 fight on the South Lawn. At the World Cup, Germany faces first-time qualifier Curaçao. THE NUMBER

8

 $35,000

How much 20-year-old Hunter Guo lost after Polymarket released a note to provide “additional context” for a bet that he had already made. Guo had stumbled on the controversial practice in prediction markets of issuing “clarifications” to betting contracts that are already being traded.

AND FINALLY...

9

Why WSJ’s autos reporter plans to drive his 2005 Pontiac Vibe into the ground.

With Americans hanging on to their old cars longer than ever, Ryan Felton wrote about why he'll never part with his unusual—but much beloved—General Motors-Toyota hatchback.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: In our political age of envy, the press and Democrats are preoccupied by Elon Musk’s otherworldly wealth . But deserving more attention is how he has enriched the country by building a remarkable company.
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 數十萬烏克蘭人每天都要面對一個問題：現在是不是該放下一切、逃離家園的時刻？隨著俄羅斯軍隊持續緩慢推進、所到之處無不遭到蹂躪，居住在這條長達800英里前線沿線的居民，正面臨一場痛苦的抉擇。《華爾街日報》花了一年時間，追蹤德魯日基夫卡（Druzhkivka）市民在苦苦掙扎是否離開家園的同時，眼看自己的生活結構被緩慢而痛苦地撕裂。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
一架美軍直升機墜毀事件引發局勢升級後，美伊雙方一度重燃戰火，如今卻又轉向和平邊緣，雙方均已退讓並展開談判。隨著川普總統即將迎來80歲生日，其團隊已做出策略性決定，要讓他無所不在——藉此與前任總統形成對比，並讓美國人更多看到這位年邁總統的優點與缺點。Tim Higgins撰文指出，SpaceX的IPO處處體現了伊隆・馬斯克最初的目標：力求創下各項紀錄，重新點燃公眾對太空旅行的支持。甘迺迪中心表示，已開始著手將川普的名字從建築物上移除，儘管此舉已大幅超過法院裁定的期限。美國隊在世界盃開幕戰以4比1擊敗巴拉圭，Jason Gay認為，這場創造歷史的勝利，應能讓美國隊獲得片刻喘息。前共和黨幕僚莎拉・朗威爾（Sarah Longwell）如今經營一個新聞網站，服務對象是她口中那些「政治上無家可歸」的人。

市場動態

2
SpaceX股價暴漲19%，以2.1兆美元的市值結束首個交易日，締造史上規模最大、也最平順的首次公開發行之一。Telis Demos撰文指出，美國確實有信用卡問題——只是並非你想的那種。📊 圖表解析：這就是為何油價至今尚未一飛沖天的原因。

獨家搶先看

3
麥當勞不再滿足於每一餐都圍繞可口可樂打轉。

自1955年一紙握手協議締結兩大品牌之間的聯盟以來，兩者已共同成為美國資本主義——乃至美國本身——的象徵。但如今，這段關係出現了裂痕。並非雙方不再彼此忠誠，而是麥當勞已不再滿足於只有可口可樂，Heather Haddon與Laura Cooper報導。這家漢堡連鎖店正在尋找新業務：美國漢堡銷售成長已放緩，而星巴克與Dunkin'則證明了飲品本身就能創造數十億美元營收。麥當勞今年春天推出了自家客製化汽水與清涼飲品，並準備推出以紅牛為主打的能量飲料系列——這是金拱門史上頭一遭。

4
深入了解終結賓州車站「人間煉獄」慘況的宏大計畫。

本月許多為了世界盃前來紐約市的球迷，都得擠過賓夕法尼亞車站腐朽不堪的內部——這裡既是全美最繁忙的交通樞紐，也確確實實是個骯髒的深坑。但就在上週，一個名為Penn Transformation Partners的企業聯盟，公布了一份獲川普政府選定、即將付諸實現的新賓州車站模型。負責為美鐵（Amtrak）監督此計畫的交通專家安迪・拜福德（Andy Byford）表示，這不僅僅是又一次天馬行空的設計練習，而是自1960年代原始建築遭拆除以來，糾正這樁「城市破壞行為」的最佳機會，Joshua Chaffin報導。

5
喬許・夏皮洛（Josh Shapiro）作風低調不張揚。這是民主黨在2028年想要的特質嗎？

這位賓州州長以強勢中間派作風及「GSD」（把事情搞定）口號聞名，已在這個政治立場分裂的搖擺州，樹立起頗受歡迎的溫和派形象。Sabrina Rodriguez報導，他獨特的定位，讓他有別於其他預料將角逐民主黨提名的人選。部分民主黨選民表示，他們希望看到對川普採取更強硬對抗姿態的候選人。加州州長紐森——另一位有意角逐2028年總統大位的民主黨人——已建立起與川普針鋒相對的全國知名度。但夏皮洛押注的是：橫跨政治光譜的選民已對政治作秀感到厭倦，而他通往白宮的道路，將從自己的家鄉州開始。

6
尼克隊熱潮正引發一場美食界的騷動。

從電光藍的「布朗森通心粉」到尼克隊主題的Dunkin甜甜圈，本報美食專欄作家品嚐了尼克狂熱席捲紐約市之際所掀起的這場藍橙雙色美食大亂鬥。

本週末焦點

7
週六：世界盃持續進行，包括巴西對摩洛哥。週日：國旗日。川普總統迎來80歲生日，白宮將在南草坪主辦UFC「Freedom 250」格鬥賽。世界盃賽事中，德國將迎戰首次晉級的庫拉索。

數字看世界

8
35,000美元
這是20歲的洪特・郭（Hunter Guo）在Polymarket針對他已下注的一筆賭局發布「補充說明」後所蒙受的損失金額。郭無意中發現了預測市場中一項備受爭議的做法：針對已在交易中的投注合約發布「澄清說明」。

最後一則

9
為何本報汽車記者打算把他那輛2005年龐帝克Vibe一路開到報廢為止。

隨著美國人把舊車開得比以往更久，Ryan Felton撰文分享了他為何永遠不會捨棄這輛雖然奇特、卻深受他喜愛的通用汽車—豐田合作掀背車。

新聞室之外

10
社論：在我們這個充滿嫉妒情緒的政治年代，媒體與民主黨人一心關注伊隆・馬斯克那超凡脫俗的財富。但真正值得更多關注的，是他如何藉由打造一家了不起的公司，讓這個國家變得更加富裕。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: What to Know as SpaceX Makes Its Trading Debut
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Elon Musk’s SpaceX is set to make its stock-market debut today in the largest IPO ever—and perhaps the most closely watched. Reporter Corrie Driebusch has been following the company for years. Below, she shares a few behind-the-scenes details of her reporting ahead of this momentous event. Elsewhere, Corrie explains everything you need to know about SpaceX’s trading debut, and speaks to The Journal podcast about whether it’s worth the hype .

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

President Trump insisted a deal on peace talks with Iran would be completed in coming days, pulling back from his threats just hours earlier to launch more military strikes. Google sued a group of scammers that it says used its Gemini AI model to create fake websites that look like the real thing. Trump and his allies have discussed pushing lawmakers to pass a resolution aimed at voiding his first-term impeachments . Tulsi Gabbard, the departing director of national intelligence, revoked two Biden-era intelligence reports that said involvement by foreign adversaries in the mysterious illness known as Havana Syndrome was unlikely. With campaigns that blend manliness with populist outrage, “dudebro” candidates hope influencer-style swagger will win over voters , writes Pamela Paul. Texas ranchers are on the front lines of the campaign to stop the advance of the deadly New World screwworm —and head off potentially massive financial losses.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 51701.00 454.00 0.89 S&P 500 Futures 7444.50 48.50 0.66 Nasdaq 100 Futures 29910.25 158.50 0.53

Source: Factset, Market data as of 6/12/2026, 5:52:13 AM ET

📈 Follow our live financial coverage all day.

Trade deficits and surpluses will be on the agenda at next week’s G-7 summit in France as the global economy is threatened again by imbalances , Greg Ip writes. It’s tempting to bet wearable companies like Oura and Whoop have cracked the code on turning self-optimization into a durable, fast-growing business. The history of consumer-health hardware suggests otherwise, David Wainer writes.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Anthropic and OpenAI are getting ready for a costly price war ahead of their IPOs.

Big companies and startups, chafing at rapidly escalating artificial intelligence costs, are increasingly turning to tools that tap in to cheaper AI models, including some from China. One company said it’s saving millions of dollars using open-source alternatives, report Bradley Olson and Tina Li. That’s raising pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic to lower their prices , a prospect that could hurt their ability to grow into profitable enterprises.

4

Switzerland has a radical proposal on immigration: Cap the population.

Disgruntled by rising living costs and disillusioned by unfulfilled economic and social promises, the Swiss are at the vanguard of industrialized countries questioning the benefits of immigration, even the high-skilled workers many vie to attract. On Sunday, they will vote in a referendum to put a hard ceiling on the country’s population . The proposal from the right-wing Swiss People’s Party aims to limit the number of permanent residents, which include both foreign nationals and Swiss citizens, to below 10 million until 2050, from a current 9.1 million. The vote is expected to be close, Tom Fairless reports.

6

What Elon Musk bought and sold during his quest to “own no house”

The SpaceX CEO could choose to live in an elaborate palace, a modern house custom-designed by a famous architect or even his own luxury skyscraper. Instead, Musk has made his base in several traditional, stucco houses near each other in a nondescript, upscale suburban area about a 15-minute drive from downtown Austin. Get a closer look at the homes connected to him .

HAPPENING TODAY

7

World Cup: The tournament kicked off yesterday with Mexico’s 2-0 victory over South Africa and South Korea's 2-1 win against the Czech Republic. Today, Canada faces Bosnia-Herzegovina at 3 p.m. ET in Toronto, and the U.S. plays its first match against Paraguay at 9 p.m. ET in Los Angeles. Economic data: The University of Michigan is set to update its Index of Consumer Sentiment. In May, the index fell to the lowest level recorded since the survey began in 1952. The premiere of “Disclosure Day,” Steven Spielberg’s sci-fi thriller starring Emily Blunt, who is having a blockbuster year . THE NUMBER

8

 >$50,000

The bonuses some teachers in a Louisiana school district will receive this year thanks to increased tax revenue linked to a Meta data-center construction project. That’s larger than some of their salaries. Local officials said the windfall, funded by a portion of the parish’s sales tax, reflects an influx of economic activity that is helping to revitalize a slumping region.

AND FINALLY...

9

They had their weddings all planned out. Then came “Knicks in 5.”

New York could clinch its first NBA Championship title since 1973 with a win against the San Antonio Spurs tomorrow night. For some fans, that basketball fever dream is creating a wedding nightmare. Couples are weighing just how to incorporate Game 5 into their own special days—or looking for ways to dissuade guests from pulling the game up on their phones during key moments.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: The midterm elections are about 150 days away. Will Republicans exploit the coming weeks to pass accomplishments they can sell to voters ?
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 伊隆・馬斯克旗下的SpaceX，今日將以史上規模最大——或許也是最受矚目——的首次公開發行（IPO），正式在股市掛牌上市。記者Corrie Driebusch已追蹤這家公司多年。以下，她分享了在這場重大事件前，她採訪報導過程中的一些幕後花絮。此外，Corrie還解析了關於SpaceX上市首日你需要知道的一切，並在《The Journal》播客中，探討這是否真的值得這番炒作。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
川普總統堅稱，與伊朗的和平談判協議將在未來幾天內完成，此前他才在數小時前威脅要發動更多軍事打擊。Google控告一群詐騙者，指控他們利用該公司的Gemini AI模型，打造出看似真實的假網站。川普及其盟友已討論推動國會議員通過一項決議，意圖使他第一任期內遭到的彈劾無效化。即將卸任的國家情報總監圖爾西・加巴德（Tulsi Gabbard），撤銷了兩份拜登時期的情報報告，這兩份報告曾指出，外國敵對勢力涉入名為「哈瓦那症候群」的神祕疾病的可能性不高。Pamela Paul撰文指出，靠著融合陽剛氣質與民粹式憤怒的競選手法，「兄弟型」（dudebro）候選人希望以網紅般的自信姿態贏得選民青睞。德州牧場主人正站在防堵致命「新世界螺旋蠅」擴散行動的第一線——並試圖搶先阻止可能造成的巨額財務損失。

市場直擊

2
道瓊期貨 51701.00　漲454.00　漲0.89%；標普500期貨 7444.50　漲48.50　漲0.66%；那斯達克100期貨 29910.25　漲158.50　漲0.53%
資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年6月12日美東時間上午5:52

Greg Ip撰文指出，隨著全球經濟再度受到失衡問題威脅，貿易逆差與順差問題將成為下週在法國舉行的G7峰會議程焦點。人們很容易相信，像Oura和Whoop這樣的穿戴裝置公司，已經找到將「自我優化」轉變為持久、快速成長事業的訣竅。但David Wainer撰文指出，消費者健康硬體產業的歷史卻顯示情況恐非如此。

獨家搶先看

3
Anthropic與OpenAI正在為即將到來的IPO，備戰一場代價高昂的價格戰。

面對迅速攀升的人工智慧成本，大型企業與新創公司紛紛不堪重負，愈來愈多轉向使用成本較低的AI模型，其中部分來自中國。Bradley Olson與Tina Li報導，有一家公司表示，靠著使用開源替代方案，省下了數百萬美元。這正對OpenAI與Anthropic形成壓力，迫使兩者降價——而這可能損及它們發展成獲利企業的能力。

4
瑞士提出一項激進的移民提案：為人口設定上限。

對生活成本上漲感到不滿、對未兌現的經濟與社會承諾感到幻滅，瑞士人如今站在已開發國家質疑移民益處（即便是各國競相爭取的高技能人才）的最前線。週日，瑞士將就一項為該國人口設定硬性上限的公投進行投票。這項由右翼瑞士人民黨提出的提案，旨在將包括外國國民與瑞士公民在內的永久居民人數，從目前的910萬，限制在2050年前不超過1000萬。Tom Fairless報導，這場投票預料將十分接近。

伊隆・馬斯克在追求「不擁有任何房子」過程中，買賣了哪些東西

這位SpaceX執行長大可選擇住進富麗堂皇的宮殿、由知名建築師量身設計的現代豪宅，甚至自己的豪華摩天大樓。但馬斯克卻選擇在距離奧斯汀市中心約15分鐘車程、一處毫不起眼的高檔郊區，落腳於幾棟彼此相鄰的傳統灰泥房屋。近距離看看與他有關的這些住宅。

今日焦點

7
世界盃：賽事昨日開幕，墨西哥以2比0擊敗南非，南韓則以2比1擊敗捷克。今日，加拿大將於美東時間下午3時在多倫多迎戰波士尼亞與赫塞哥維納，美國隊則將於美東時間晚上9時在洛杉磯迎來對巴拉圭的首戰。經濟數據：密西根大學將更新其消費者信心指數。今年5月，該指數跌至該調查自1952年開始以來的最低紀錄。電影《Disclosure Day》首映，這部史蒂芬・史匹柏執導的科幻驚悚片，由今年星運正旺的艾蜜莉・布朗（Emily Blunt）主演。

數字看世界

8
逾5萬美元
這是路易斯安那州某學區部分教師今年將領到的獎金，得益於與Meta資料中心建設案相關的稅收增加，這筆金額甚至超過部分教師的薪水。地方官員表示，這筆由該教區部分銷售稅資助的意外之財，反映出湧入的經濟活動，正協助振興這個原本陷入低迷的地區。

最後一則

9
他們原本已經規劃好婚禮，結果來了一句「尼克五戰奪冠」。

紐約隊明晚若擊敗聖安東尼奧馬刺隊，將奪得自1973年以來首座NBA總冠軍。對部分球迷而言，這場籃球美夢，卻正演變成一場婚禮惡夢。新人們正在權衡，該如何將第五戰安排進自己的大喜之日——或是想方設法勸阻賓客，別在關鍵時刻掏出手機看比賽。

新聞室之外

10
社論：距離期中選舉大約還有150天。共和黨會利用接下來這幾週，通過一些能向選民推銷的政績嗎？

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Inside the Biggest World Cup Ever
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Today marks the start of the biggest World Cup ever, featuring an expanded field of 48 teams playing in three countries. Our sports editor, Joshua Robinson, is in Mexico City for the opening matches, and our team will be on the ground reporting from Kansas City, Los Angeles and across the U.S. as the tournament unfolds. If you need a team to root for—or a backup for Team USA— check out our interactive guide .

Another must-read for your morning: The old adage “doing good while doing well” drove microfinancing, a movement using tiny loans intended to end poverty. But as Gabriele Steinhauser reports, hundreds of billions of dollars later, it hasn’t made a dent .

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

The U.S. launched a fresh wave of attacks on Iran, hitting dozens of targets including air defenses and radar sites near the Strait of Hormuz. OpenAI is considering drastically lowering its prices as it seeks to win customers from rival Anthropic. Months after a spasm of cartel violence paralyzed Guadalajara, Mexico is mounting a multimillion-dollar security dragnet to show that the World Cup is safe. China is propping up the world economy by importing a lot less oil . For over three years, Jared Kushner has striven to build a set of luxury hotels and resorts in Albania. It isn’t going well .

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 50753.00 406.00 0.81 S&P 500 Futures 7336.25 57.75 0.79 Nasdaq 100 Futures 29168.75 337.50 1.17

Source: Factset, Market data as of 6/11/2026, 5:56:06 AM ET

📈 Follow our live financial coverage all day.

Charging users for subscriptions is Meta’s latest bid to build a business outside advertising . Its chances don’t look great, writes Asa Fitch.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

You have no idea what a trillion dollars is—and we have proof.

IMAGE: EMIL LENDOF/WSJ; ISTOCK

Not long ago, the word trillionaire only appeared in the Journal as hyperbole. It was an obviously exaggerated way of describing an inconceivable fortune—like calling someone a bazillionaire. But now that SpaceX is going public, it might just be something we call Elon Musk. And as it turns out, $1 trillion is such a large number and so far beyond the human imagination that we can’t wrap our minds around it . In this interactive, visual-led piece, Ben Cohen offers ways to help you comprehend the incomprehensible scale of this enormous sum.

4

Hundreds of billions in loans didn’t make a dent in global poverty.

Giving tiny loans to shoestring entrepreneurs was meant to be capitalism’s cure for global poverty. Microfinance, loans issued in communities not served by traditional banks, would help poor people in developing countries start businesses and work their way toward prosperity. Microfinance lenders have advanced hundreds of billions of dollars to poor people in countries from Albania to Zimbabwe. Prominent voices including Hillary Clinton and Natalie Portman told inspiring tales of women entrepreneurs lifting the fortunes of their communities. Along with easing poverty, microfinance aimed to expand access to education and end gender inequality. Few of those aspirations have come to pass , reports Gabriele Steinhauser.

5

It took decades of struggle to forge America into a soccer nation.

Soccer in America has never been treated like any other sport. In a country that can’t even agree on what to call the game, it has been alternately loved like an underground band, ridiculed as a poisonous foreign import, and, for most of its history, ignored. But if the U.S. is in a position to co-host the largest ever World Cup, it’s because of a bubbling undercurrent that has sustained the game in America for over a century. Today, it boasts one of the best-attended domestic leagues in the world, a men’s national team that is regularly ranked in the top 15, and a vibrant soccer culture. How it got there is not a linear story , report Joshua Robinson and Jonathan Clegg.

6

Here’s what the SpaceX IPO means for this Texas border town.

PHOTO ILLUSTRATION: WSJ

Micah Maidenburg visits Brownsville, Texas, the city next to Starbase—which Elon Musk created to house SpaceX employees—ahead of the company’s massive IPO. The offering is expected to create a slew of new millionaires in the area. He spoke to business owners, politicians and residents to find out how they are preparing.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

The 2026 FIFA World Cup kicks off, with Mexico versus South Africa and South Korea versus the Czech Republic. The European Central Bank is expected to raise interest rates for the first time in three years. Earnings: Adobe THE NUMBER

8

 35%

Shares of Cracker Barrel shot up as much as this after Chief Executive Julie Felss Masino unveiled a more profitable outlook and said diners were returning. Loyal customers have come back as the restaurant chain refocused on dishing up deals, nostalgia and its most die-hard fans’ favorite foods. But Cracker Barrel isn’t out of the woods yet.

AND FINALLY...

9

Rent is so high, New Yorkers are living with nuns.

Welcome to the NYC rental market, where the median asking rent hit $3,616 in the first quarter this year, 20% above pre-pandemic levels, according to Realtor.com. To manage on a starting salary, some young professionals are turning to convents . Convent boarding houses are affordable and clean—some charge around $800 a month—but there are rules: curfews, chores and sometimes nuns who vet boyfriends.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: After weeks of insisting a deal with Iran is around the corner, Trump may be admitting the reality. Is he ready at last for a new approach?
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 今天是史上規模最大世界盃的開幕日，賽事擴大為48支球隊、在三個國家舉行。我們的體育編輯Joshua Robinson已抵達墨西哥城採訪開幕賽事，我們的團隊也將在賽事展開期間，於堪薩斯城、洛杉磯及全美各地實地報導。如果你需要一支支持的球隊——或美國隊之外的備案——可以參考我們的互動指南。

今早另一則必讀新聞：「行善亦能獲利」這句老話，曾推動小額信貸這項旨在終結貧窮的運動。但Gabriele Steinhauser報導指出，數千億美元投入後，貧窮問題卻幾乎未見改善。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
美國對伊朗發動新一波攻擊，打擊數十處目標，包括荷莫茲海峽附近的防空與雷達設施。OpenAI正考慮大幅降價，以求從對手Anthropic手中搶走客戶。在一波幫派暴力癱瘓瓜達拉哈拉數月後，墨西哥正部署一項耗資數百萬美元的維安行動，以證明世界盃安全無虞。中國正透過大幅減少石油進口，來支撐世界經濟。三年多來，賈瑞德・庫許納（Jared Kushner）一直努力在阿爾巴尼亞打造一系列豪華飯店與度假村，但進展並不順利。

市場直擊

2
道瓊期貨 50753.00　漲406.00　漲0.81%；標普500期貨 7336.25　漲57.75　漲0.79%；那斯達克100期貨 29168.75　漲337.50　漲1.17%
資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年6月11日美東時間上午5:56

Asa Fitch撰文指出，向用戶收取訂閱費，是Meta試圖打造廣告業務以外收入來源的最新嘗試，但成功機率看起來並不樂觀。

獨家搶先看

3
你根本不知道一兆美元有多龐大——我們有證據。

不久前，「兆萬富翁」（trillionaire）這個詞在本報出現時，還只是一種誇張修辭手法，用來形容一種難以想像的財富——就像稱某人為「億億萬富翁」一樣，明顯帶有誇大成分。但如今，隨著SpaceX即將上市，這個詞或許很快就會用來形容伊隆・馬斯克本人。事實證明，1兆美元這個數字實在太過龐大，遠遠超出人類想像所能觸及的範圍，讓人根本無法真正理解。在這篇以視覺呈現為主的互動報導中，Ben Cohen提供了幾種方法，幫助你理解這筆龐大到難以想像的金額。

4
數千億美元的貸款，並未讓全球貧窮問題有絲毫改善。

向白手起家的創業者提供小額貸款，原本被視為資本主義解決全球貧窮的良方。小額信貸——向未獲傳統銀行服務的社區提供貸款——原本旨在幫助開發中國家的窮人創業，逐步邁向富裕。小額信貸機構已向從阿爾巴尼亞到辛巴威等國的窮人，發放了數千億美元貸款。包括希拉蕊・柯林頓與娜塔莉・波曼在內的知名人士，都曾講述女性創業者提升社區命運的勵志故事。除了緩解貧窮外，小額信貸也曾旨在擴大教育普及、終結性別不平等。但Gabriele Steinhauser報導，這些願景幾乎都未能實現。

5
美國要打造成一個足球國家，經歷了數十年的奮鬥。

美國足球從未受到與其他運動同等的待遇。在這個連該怎麼稱呼這項運動都無法達成共識的國家裡，足球時而被當作地下樂團般小眾追捧，時而被嘲笑為毒害人心的外來舶來品，而在其大部分歷史中，則根本乏人問津。但如果說美國如今有資格聯合主辦史上規模最大的世界盃，那是因為一股暗流已在美國持續醞釀了一個多世紀，支撐著這項運動的發展。如今，美國擁有全球觀眾人數最多的國內聯賽之一、一支經常排名世界前15的男子國家隊，以及蓬勃發展的足球文化。Joshua Robinson與Jonathan Clegg報導，這一切並非一路直線發展而來。

6
SpaceX的IPO，對這座德州邊境小鎮意味著什麼。

Micah Maidenburg造訪了德州布朗斯維爾（Brownsville）——這座城市緊鄰伊隆・馬斯克為安置SpaceX員工而打造的「星際基地」（Starbase）——探訪這家公司即將進行的大規模IPO前夕的當地情況。這次上市預計將在當地造就一批新的百萬富翁。他採訪了企業主、政治人物與居民，了解他們正如何為此做準備。

今日焦點

7
2026年FIFA世界盃開幕，賽事包括墨西哥對南非、南韓對捷克。歐洲央行預計將三年來首次升息。財報：Adobe。

數字看世界

8
35%
在執行長茱莉・費爾斯・馬西諾（Julie Felss Masino）公布更亮眼的獲利前景、並表示顧客正逐漸回流後，Cracker Barrel股價一度飆漲這個幅度。隨著這家餐飲連鎖店重新聚焦於推出優惠、懷舊氛圍及死忠粉絲最愛的餐點，忠實顧客已逐漸回籠。但Cracker Barrel尚未完全脫離困境。

最後一則

9
房租高到讓紐約人開始跟修女同住。

歡迎來到紐約市租屋市場：根據Realtor.com數據，今年第一季的租金中位數已達3616美元，較疫情前水準高出20%。為了在起薪範圍內生活，部分年輕上班族開始轉向修道院求助。修道院提供的宿舍價格實惠、環境整潔——部分月租僅約800美元——但也有規矩要遵守：門禁、家務分擔，有時修女還會替房客審查男朋友。

新聞室之外

10
社論：在數週堅稱與伊朗的協議即將達成後，川普或許正逐漸承認現實。他終於準備好改弦更張了嗎？

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Loyalists Who Could Make Musk a Trillionaire
emails.contentEn:
✏️ On Friday, SpaceX is expected to debut in the biggest IPO of all time, a deal predicted to make Elon Musk the world’s first trillionaire. The stock offering also will be a landmark moment for everyday investors in Wall Street’s retail revolution. Individual investors now wield expanding, market-moving power—and Musk knows just how to tap it. At Tesla, they make up about a third of the shareholder base. Now, Musk is expected to set aside an unusually large portion of SpaceX shares sold in the offering for individual investors. The Journal’s Hannah Erin Lang and Corrie Driebusch look at how Musk is leaning on this army of loyalists .

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

The U.S. launched military strikes against Iran in retaliation for the downing of a U.S. Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz. Trump regulators are proposing an expansive new set of rules on how they will govern the booming prediction markets . Democrats in Maine set aside the controversies surrounding political newcomer Graham Platner and selected him as their nominee to challenge GOP Sen. Susan Collins. Former Fox News host Steve Hilton advanced to the general election to succeed California Gov. Gavin Newsom in November. Rep. Nancy Mace was knocked out of the race for South Carolina governor. An effort in San Francisco to raise taxes on companies with highly paid executives has failed .

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 50544.00 -365.00 0.72 S&P 500 Futures 7332.25 -60.50 0.82 Nasdaq 100 Futures 28755.50 -361.50 1.24

Source: Factset, Market data as of 6/10/2026, 5:53:52 AM ET

📈 Follow our live financial coverage all day.

Where are investors riding out the turbulence in chip stocks? Transportation stocks, options bets and profitable companies are among the popular alternatives . Now is a good time to buy into America’s mega utility merger, writes Jinjoo Lee.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

The world’s great powers are learning they have limits.

After taking office last year, President Trump unapologetically pushed a might-makes-right vision to remake the international order around a U.S. sphere of influence, a worldview not that dissimilar from Russia’s or China’s. The future seemed shaped by an oft-repeated line from ancient Greek historian Thucydides: “The strong do what they will, and the weak suffer as they must.” Yet now it seems that the weak aren’t as weak as many had believed. The strong can’t really do what they want either. As technology levels the field between stronger and weaker nations, old-fashioned wars of conquest may no longer be possible, reports Yaroslav Trofimov.

4

At these airport lounges, videogames are more important than drinks.

Emma and Jordan Walbridge are a husband-and-wife team on a mission to amp up airport downtime.The Walbridges, with backgrounds in hotels and medical-device sales, respectively, opened their first airport videogaming lounge at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport in 2018. Called Gameway, there are now 11 of them at airports across the country and two more are due to open this year. Portal in Minneapolis is the latest iteration of the concept with a few more bells and whistles. WSJ’s travel columnist Dawn Gilbertson visited lounges in Chicago and Minneapolis last week to see what the fuss is about.

5

We asked economists about the future of work and AI.

Will artificial intelligence improve workers’ lives, or hand them the equivalent of a pink slip? It’s one of the most pressing questions facing the U.S. today. For answers, we turned to 16 economists—including an economics Nobel winner, academics deeply engaged on questions about AI and former top government advisers—about what they think AI will mean for the economy, workers and workplaces. Read highlights from their conversations with the Journal’s Te-Ping Chen and Justin Lahart.

6

FIFA is staking its $3.8 billion World Cup on an unprecedented grass experiment.

Soccer’s global governing body is spending millions to ensure every World Cup pitch plays the same. See how scientists are engineering grass that delivers a consistent game across 16 venues—even in stadiums where it’s never grown before.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

WSJ live Q&A: What questions do you have about the California primaries? Join a live written chat with WSJ reporter Laura Nelson from 3 p.m. - 4 p.m. ET. World Cup: The single-biggest soccer tournament in history starts tomorrrow. Join a live written chat with the Journal’s sports editor, Joshua Robinson, and executive news editor Jonathan Clegg from 1 p.m. - 2 p.m. ET. Economic data: U.S. inflation data for May. Earnings: Oracle THE NUMBER

8

 $70 billion

The House passed a Republican-led $70 billion immigration-enforcement bill , ending a monthslong stalemate over the slice of federal spending. The measure will fund Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol over Democrats’ objections for the remainder of Trump’s second term.

AND FINALLY...

9

Why is the Supreme Court debating which Founding Fathers were drunks?

Do drug users have a constitutional right to own a gun? The answer may depend on what the Supreme Court thinks about the drinking habits of the Founding Fathers. Faced with a docket of tough cases on modern-day problems, justices are increasingly looking to the past for answers. This time machine is driven by originalism —the legal philosophy that says the meaning of the Constitution’s words shouldn’t evolve over time. Though fashionable for decades, the court’s conservative supermajority has embraced the theory with new fervor.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: There’s no evidence so far that fraud has affected the results of the L.A. mayoral race, but the state’s loose voting rules and dilatory counting fuel distrust in elections .

✏️ 週五，SpaceX預計將以史上規模最大的IPO正式掛牌上市，這筆交易預料將讓伊隆・馬斯克成為全球首位兆萬富翁。這次股票發行，對於華爾街散戶投資革命中的一般投資人而言，也將是個具指標意義的時刻。個人投資者如今擁有日益擴大、足以撼動市場的影響力——而馬斯克深諳如何善用這股力量。在特斯拉，散戶約占股東結構的三分之一。如今，馬斯克預計將把這次發行中一個異常龐大的比例，保留給個人投資者認購。本報記者Hannah Erin Lang與Corrie Driebusch探討了馬斯克如何倚仗這支忠實信徒大軍。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
美國對伊朗發動軍事打擊，以報復荷莫茲海峽附近一架美軍阿帕契直升機遭擊落。川普政府監管機構正提議一套全新的廣泛規則，用以規範蓬勃發展的預測市場。緬因州民主黨人不顧政壇新人格雷厄姆・普拉特納（Graham Platner）身陷的爭議，選定他作為挑戰共和黨參議員蘇珊・柯林斯（Susan Collins）的黨內提名人選。前福斯新聞主持人史蒂夫・希爾頓（Steve Hilton），晉級11月加州州長大選（接替紐森）的正式選舉。眾議員南希・梅斯（Nancy Mace）則在南卡羅來納州州長選戰中出局。舊金山一項針對高薪執行長企業加稅的提案未能通過。

市場直擊

2
道瓊期貨 50544.00　跌365.00　跌0.72%；標普500期貨 7332.25　跌60.50　跌0.82%；那斯達克100期貨 28755.50　跌361.50　跌1.24%
資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年6月10日美東時間上午5:53

投資人正躲到哪裡去避開晶片股的動盪？交通運輸類股、選擇權操作與獲利穩健的企業，都是熱門的替代選擇。Jinjoo Lee撰文指出，現在正是布局美國那樁大型公用事業合併案的好時機。

獨家搶先看

3
世界各大強權正在體認到，自己也有極限。

自去年上任以來，川普總統毫不掩飾地推動一種「強權即公理」的願景，力圖以美國勢力範圍為核心重塑國際秩序——這種世界觀與俄羅斯或中國的做法並無太大差異。未來似乎正如古希臘史學家修昔底德那句常被引用的名言所預示：「強者為所欲為，弱者逆來順受。」然而，如今看來，弱者並不像許多人以為的那麼弱。強者其實也無法真正為所欲為。Yaroslav Trofimov報導，隨著科技拉近強國與弱國之間的實力差距，老派的征服型戰爭恐怕已不再可行。

4
在這些機場貴賓室裡，電玩比飲料更受重視。

艾瑪與喬丹・沃布里奇（Emma and Jordan Walbridge）這對夫妻檔，正致力於為旅客的機場候機時光增添樂趣。這對背景分別來自飯店業與醫療器材銷售業的夫婦，於2018年在達拉斯沃斯堡國際機場開設了他們第一間機場電玩休息室。這個名為Gameway的品牌，如今已在全美各地機場開設11間分店，今年還將再開兩間。位於明尼阿波利斯的Portal，是這個概念最新的升級版本，多了幾項花俏功能。本報旅遊專欄作家道恩・吉伯森上週走訪了芝加哥與明尼阿波利斯的休息室，一探箇中魅力。

5
我們詢問了經濟學家對工作與AI未來的看法。

人工智慧究竟會改善勞工的生活，還是等同於發給他們一張解僱通知書？這是當今美國面臨的最迫切問題之一。為尋求解答，我們訪問了16位經濟學家——包括一位經濟學諾貝爾獎得主、深入研究AI議題的學者，以及前政府高階顧問——了解他們認為AI將對經濟、勞工與職場帶來什麼影響。閱讀他們與本報記者Te-Ping Chen及Justin Lahart對談的精華內容。

6
FIFA正將其38億美元的世界盃，押注在一場前所未見的草皮實驗上。

這個足球界的全球管理機構，正斥資數百萬美元，確保每一座世界盃球場的草皮品質一致。看看科學家如何培育出能在16座場館——甚至包括從未種過這種草皮的球場——維持一致比賽水準的草種。

今日焦點

7
《華爾街日報》線上問答：對於加州初選，你有什麼問題？加入本報記者Laura Nelson主持的即時文字聊天，時間為美東時間下午3時至4時。世界盃：史上規模最大的足球賽事將於明日開幕。加入本報體育編輯Joshua Robinson與執行新聞編輯Jonathan Clegg主持的即時文字聊天，時間為美東時間下午1時至2時。經濟數據：5月美國通膨數據公布。財報：甲骨文（Oracle）。

數字看世界

8
700億美元
眾議院通過了一項由共和黨主導、金額達700億美元的移民執法法案，結束了這筆聯邦支出經數月僵持不下的局面。該法案將在民主黨反對聲中，為移民及海關執法局與邊境巡邏隊提供資金，資助範圍涵蓋川普第二任期剩餘時間。

最後一則

9
最高法院為何在爭論哪些開國元勳是酒鬼？

吸毒者是否擁有受憲法保障的持槍權利？答案或許取決於最高法院如何看待開國元勳的飲酒習慣。面對一系列涉及現代難題的棘手案件，大法官們正愈來愈頻繁地從歷史中尋求答案。驅動這台時光機的，是「原意主義」（originalism）——這種法律哲學主張，憲法文字的含義不應隨時間演變。這套理論雖已流行數十年，但如今最高法院的保守派絕對多數，正以前所未有的熱情擁抱它。

新聞室之外

10
社論：目前尚無證據顯示，舞弊影響了洛杉磯市長選舉的結果，但加州寬鬆的投票規則與拖沓的計票程序，正助長了民眾對選舉的不信任感。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Wall Street’s Rush to Fund the AI Bonanza
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Iran’s ballistic-missile salvos against Israel show an appetite for risk that didn’t exist before the war. Driven by emboldened regional ambitions, Tehran's leaders are gambling that direct strikes—coupled with President Trump's desire to keep a potential peace deal on track—will pressure Israel’s Benjamin Netanyahu to scale back his military offensive against the Iranian-allied Hezbollah militia in Lebanon. While both sides have since halted their attacks, Israel remains focused on Hezbollah. That leaves the country teetering on the brink of a new civil war as an already strained ceasefire pushes the country toward a dangerous sectarian confrontation.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Trump was met with a chorus of boos at Madison Square Garden in New York City, as he attended the NBA Finals . The Knicks lost to the San Antonio Spurs, ending a 13-game winning streak. Republican Spencer Pratt failed to advance in the Los Angeles mayoral primary . Trump and his associates are escalating allegations of election fraud in California, a playbook they have used previously to sow doubt about election results. The Pentagon updated its list of Chinese businesses the U.S. has identified as aiding Beijing’s military.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

OpenAI filed to stage an initial public offering , potentially as soon as this fall, that will test investor appetite for artificial-intelligence companies. University endowments are about to strike it big on the SpaceX IPO. Countries will build larger emergency crude-oil reserves to reduce their vulnerability to future energy shocks, writes Carol Ryan.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Lebanon is teetering on the edge of a new civil war.

The country’s government is barely able to manage the basic requirements of statehood. It can provide electricity for only a few hours a day and people avoid its flattened currency in favor of dollars. Its military is only the second-most-powerful force in the country after Hezbollah—or the third counting Israel, which has been expanding its monthslong occupation. But Lebanon is now being pressed by the U.S., Israel and many of its own people toward a confrontation with Hezbollah that risks tilting the country into a new civil war , report Omar Abdel-Baqui and Wael Taleb.

4

Wall Street is rushing to fund the AI bonanza in every conceivable way.

Funding rounds and IPOs raising 11-figure sums. Blockbuster bond sales spanning three continents. The casual announcement of an $85 billion equity raise. Such is life on Wall Street at the dawn of the AI build-out. Tech companies are hungry for cash to invest in data centers, and investors are forking it over through all possible means, in all parts of the globe, reports Sam Goldfarb. It’s a flurry of fundraising that has mostly supported markets by powering technological advances, even as it has tested their ability to absorb it all.

5

Wyoming’s data-center boom meets the ‘man camp.’

Twenty years ago, Stan and Tammy Higgins moved into a home on Wyoming’s windswept shortgrass prairie. From their back window, they saw grazing cattle, roaming antelope and coyotes. That pastoral scene is gone: Heavy trucks, earth movers and hundreds of construction workers have run nearly around the clock for about two years building a Meta data center. To the east, Microsoft recently announced plans to triple the acreage of its complex. To the south, work is getting started on Project Jade, which could be one of the biggest data centers in the U.S. Now comes the “man camp.” In America’s least populous state, companies must import armies of workers—and find somewhere to put them, reports Joe Barrett.

6

A new front is opening in the fight to break China’s rare-earth dominance.

Western companies are pouring money into Brazil’s rare-earth industry , hoping the South American nation can help loosen China’s grip on the minerals used in electric vehicles, wind turbines and advanced weapons. Brazil has resisted pressure to join a U.S.-led minerals bloc, insisting it will accept investment from any country willing to help develop the industry.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

Elections: Maine’s Democratic primary election for U.S. Senate. Other primaries to watch include North Dakota, Nevada and South Carolina. Earnings: J.M. Smucker, Cracker Barrel Old Country Store THE NUMBER

8

 1 million

The number of square feet of Manhattan office space leased by AI companies in the first quarter. Thanks to AI, the Manhattan office market is on pace this year for its best leasing performance since 2000 . While AI is still a relatively small contributor to the borough’s overall office market, some of the industry titans are already starting to reshape neighborhoods like SoHo and Hudson Square.

AND FINALLY...

9

A dog walker and a dentist are locked in a bitter feud over who owns the beach.

A recent trial in Shorewood, Wis., had all the trappings of a minor legal dispute. A disgruntled neighbor. A defendant representing himself who called his own father as a character witness. A $313 fine. But if academic and devoted dog walker Paul Florsheim gets his way, the case will go all the way to the Wisconsin Supreme Court . At stake is what right people in Wisconsin have to take a shoreline stroll.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: The Iranian regime has made a Lebanon ceasefire a prerequisite for a nuclear deal, but it also controls Hezbollah, which is refusing to cease fire. That’s what brought about the weekend military exchange.
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 伊朗對以色列發射彈道飛彈，展現出戰前不曾出現的冒險意願。受到日益膨脹的地區野心驅使，德黑蘭領導層正在賭一件事：直接發動攻擊——加上川普總統希望維持潛在和平協議不脫軌的意願——將能迫使以色列的班傑明・納坦雅胡收斂其對伊朗盟友真主黨民兵在黎巴嫩的軍事攻勢。儘管雙方此後已停止攻擊，以色列仍將焦點放在真主黨身上。這讓黎巴嫩瀕臨一場新內戰的邊緣，一份原本就已緊繃的停火協議，正將這個國家推向危險的教派對抗。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
川普出席NBA總決賽時，在紐約麥迪遜廣場花園遭到滿場噓聲。尼克隊敗給聖安東尼奧馬刺隊，終結了13連勝紀錄。共和黨籍的史賓賽・普拉特（Spencer Pratt）未能晉級洛杉磯市長初選。川普及其黨羽正加碼指控加州選舉舞弊——這是他們過去用來對選舉結果散播疑慮的慣用手法。五角大廈更新了其認定協助北京軍方的中國企業名單。

市場直擊

2
道瓊期貨 50981.00　漲125.00　漲0.25%；標普500期貨 7448.75　漲32.75　漲0.44%；那斯達克100期貨 29683.25　漲228.50　漲0.78%
資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年6月9日美東時間上午5:39

OpenAI已提交首次公開發行申請，最快可能於今秋掛牌，這將考驗投資人對AI企業的胃口。大學校產基金即將靠SpaceX的IPO大賺一筆。Carol Ryan撰文指出，各國將建立更大規模的緊急原油儲備，以降低未來能源衝擊帶來的脆弱性。

獨家搶先看

3
黎巴嫩正瀕臨一場新內戰的邊緣。

這個國家的政府幾乎無法履行國家最基本的職能：每天供電僅數小時，民眾也因本國貨幣大貶而寧可使用美元。其軍隊只是國內第二強大的武裝力量，僅次於真主黨——若把持續擴大佔領行動已達數月的以色列算進去，甚至只能排第三。但如今，美國、以色列及黎巴嫩自身的許多民眾，正共同向黎巴嫩施壓，逼其與真主黨對抗，這可能讓國家滑向一場新內戰，Omar Abdel-Baqui與Wael Taleb報導。

4
華爾街正透過各種可能的方式，搶著資助這波AI盛宴。

融資輪次與IPO動輒募得11位數金額。橫跨三大洲的重磅債券發行。輕描淡寫宣布的850億美元股權募資案。這就是AI建設熱潮初期華爾街的日常寫照。科技公司渴求現金以投資資料中心，而投資人正透過各種可能的管道、在全球各地慷慨掏錢，Sam Goldfarb報導。這波募資狂潮，大致上藉由推動技術進步支撐了市場，但也同時考驗著市場消化這一切的能力。

5
懷俄明州的資料中心熱潮，遇上了「男性工人營」。

20年前，史丹與譚美・希金斯（Stan and Tammy Higgins）搬進懷俄明州一處風吹草動的短草草原上的住家。從他們家後窗望出去，能看到吃草的牛群、遊蕩的羚羊與郊狼。如今，那片田園景象已不復存在：重型卡車、挖土機與數百名建築工人，近兩年來幾乎日夜不停地趕工，興建一座Meta資料中心。往東邊看，微軟最近宣布計畫將其園區面積擴大兩倍。往南邊看，代號「Jade計畫」的工程已經動工，可能成為美國規模最大的資料中心之一。如今，「男性工人營」也隨之而來。在這個美國人口最少的州，企業必須引入大批工人——還得想辦法安置他們，Joe Barrett報導。

6
打破中國稀土主導地位的鬥爭，正開闢出一條新戰線。

西方企業正大舉投資巴西的稀土產業，希望這個南美國家能協助削弱中國對電動車、風力渦輪機與先進武器所需礦物的掌控力。巴西已頂住壓力，拒絕加入美國主導的礦產聯盟，堅持只要有國家願意協助開發這項產業，都願意接受其投資。

今日焦點

7
選舉：緬因州舉行美國參議員民主黨初選。其他值得關注的初選包括北達科他州、內華達州與南卡羅來納州。財報：J.M. Smucker、Cracker Barrel Old Country Store。

數字看世界

8
100萬
這是今年第一季AI公司在曼哈頓承租的辦公空間平方英尺數。得益於AI，曼哈頓辦公室市場今年有望創下自2000年以來最佳租賃表現。儘管AI目前對該區整體辦公室市場的貢獻仍相對有限，但部分產業巨頭已開始重塑蘇活區與哈德遜廣場等社區的樣貌。

最後一則

9
一位遛狗人士與一位牙醫，正為誰擁有這片海灘而展開激烈纏鬥。

威斯康辛州肖伍德（Shorewood）近期一場審判，具備一起小型法律糾紛的所有要素：一位心懷不滿的鄰居、一位自行辯護、還找來自己父親作為品格證人的被告，以及一筆313美元的罰款。但如果這位學者兼熱心遛狗人士保羅・佛羅斯海姆（Paul Florsheim）如願以償，這起案件將一路打到威斯康辛州最高法院。爭議的核心在於：威斯康辛州民眾究竟有什麼權利，可以沿著海岸線散步。

新聞室之外

10
社論：伊朗政權已將黎巴嫩停火列為達成核協議的先決條件，但它同時也掌控著拒絕停火的真主黨——這正是週末軍事交火的由來。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Why North Korea’s Economy Is Flourishing
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Good morning. We are straight into a busy news week: Iran and Israel have exchanged fire . And China’s Xi Jinping is in North Korea for a two-day summit, as he attempts to reassert Beijing’s authority over its nuclear-armed neighbor. The Journal’s Dasl Yoon and Timothy W. Martin examine why North Korea is the world’s most surprising growth story .

Meanwhile, soccer teams from across the globe are arriving in North America for the World Cup. Ahead of kickoff, we look at how FIFA engineered this tournament into a global phenomenon —and why Canada and Mexico are already winning , by one measure.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

President Trump said Israel and Iran must immediately stop shooting , after exchanges of fire renewed fear of escalation and tested his fragile Middle East ceasefire. SpaceX’s years of courting the national-security establishment are paying off , helping the 24-year-old company land new contracts totaling billions of dollars. A top Senate Democrat is introducing a bill to restrict how the Pentagon uses artificial intelligence. New York Rep. Dan Goldman is struggling to hold on to his seat in a hotly contested primary where Israel has dominated the conversation. A powerful 7.8-magnitude earthquake struck off the southern coast of the Philippines, prompting a tsunami threat across the region. PepsiCo is using autonomous trucks to distribute beverages and chips to multiple grocery stores in Texas, Arizona and Arkansas.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 50877.00 -59.00 0.12 S&P 500 Futures 7425.25 24.75 0.33 Nasdaq 100 Futures 29226.00 199.50 0.69

Source: Factset, Market data as of 6/8/2026, 5:59:32 AM ET
