Wall Street is warning that more market turmoil could lie ahead , after Friday’s selloff left investors few places to hide. Buyers who get an IPO’s offer price historically have seen the biggest returns , and SpaceX isn’t likely to be different, writes Telis Demos.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

The world’s most surprising economic success story is…North Korea.

The country’s economy is flourishing in ways not seen in years, aided by arms sales and troop deployments to Russia, supplies and financing from China, and the ability to flout international sanctions to import more energy, components and materials. The Kim regime slammed North Korea’s borders shut during the Covid-19 pandemic. It has since reopened to only a select few outsiders, including Russian and Western travelers and diplomats. Those visitors describe a North Korea unrecognizable from the past , especially its capital, Pyongyang, where the elite live, report Dasl Yoon and Timothy W. Martin.

4

This hidden figure has close ties to Bill Gates and Jeffrey Epstein.

Dr. Melanie Walker is one of the many technicolor characters who populated Epstein’s universe. The Seattle doctor was a confidante to Epstein and Bill Gates. Compared with other Epstein associates, Walker, now 54 and a professor at UW Medicine, has largely remained off the public radar . Yet she may have been most consequential as one of the people who helped Epstein ingratiate himself in Gates’s world after his 2008 conviction for soliciting a minor for prostitution, report Khadeeja Safdar and Joshua Chaffin. Walker’s lawyer says she was in a “coercive relationship” with Epstein.

6

Barcelona’s Sagrada Família nears completion—and inflames a tourism backlash.

One of the world’s most famous construction sites, the Basilica of the Sagrada Família, is finally nearing completion after 144 years of work. Not everyone is celebrating. As the city prepares for a visit by Pope Leo XIV to inaugurate the church’s tallest tower, a glaring gap has opened up between the religious vision that inspired the building and the worldwide tourist magnet it has become.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

The New York Knicks return to Madison Square Garden to host the San Antonio Spurs for Game 3 of the NBA Finals. Apple holds its annual developer conference. Earnings: Campbell’s THE NUMBER

8

 48%

Vancouver and Guadalajara boast the top occupancy rates ahead of the soccer World Cup at nearly 50%, according to CoStar. In the U.S., only one city, San Francisco, is outpacing Canada and Mexico’s hotel bookings. Some U.S. hotel owners say they are getting decent rates, but the foreign host cities hold a number of advantages, including often more rabid soccer fans and overall affordability.

AND FINALLY...

9

Nvidia takes the top spot in the 2026 list of Best Companies for the Future.

Nvidia is No. 1 in the Journal’s inaugural ranking of Best Companies for the Future, topping a list heavy on tech stalwarts as AI reshapes business. The chip maker is joined in the top five by Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta Platforms and Cisco Systems, a group largely propelled by strong scores for innovation, financial strength and AI readiness. Most rankings of companies look backward, measuring them based on past performance. Our new ranking looks forward .

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Across the progressive state of California last week, voters rejected state and local tax increases .
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 早安。本週一開始就是繁忙的新聞週：伊朗與以色列已互相開火。而中國國家主席習近平正在北韓進行為期兩天的高峰會，試圖重新確立北京對這個擁核鄰國的權威。本報記者Dasl Yoon與Timothy W. Martin探討了為何北韓成為全球最令人意外的經濟成長故事。

與此同時，來自全球各地的足球隊伍正陸續抵達北美，準備參加世界盃。在開幕前夕，我們探討了FIFA如何將這項賽事打造成一場全球現象——以及以某項指標來看，為何加拿大與墨西哥已率先勝出。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
在雙方互相開火重新引發局勢升級疑慮、並考驗其脆弱的中東停火協議後，川普總統表示，以色列與伊朗必須立即停止交火。SpaceX多年來對國安體系的積極經營終於開花結果，這家成立24年的公司，正藉此拿下總值數十億美元的新合約。一位參議院民主黨大老正提出一項法案，限制五角大廈使用人工智慧的方式。紐約州眾議員丹・戈德曼（Dan Goldman），在一場以以色列議題為主導、競爭激烈的初選中，正苦苦爭取保住自己的席位。菲律賓南部外海發生規模7.8強震，引發區域海嘯威脅。百事可樂正利用自駕卡車，向德州、亞利桑那州與阿肯色州多家雜貨店配送飲料與洋芋片。

市場直擊

2
道瓊期貨 50877.00　跌59.00　跌0.12%；標普500期貨 7425.25　漲24.75　漲0.33%；那斯達克100期貨 29226.00　漲199.50　漲0.69%
資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年6月8日美東時間上午5:59

在週五的拋售潮讓投資人幾乎無處可躲後，華爾街正警告未來恐有更多市場動盪。Telis Demos撰文指出，以IPO發行價買進的投資人，歷來都能獲得最大報酬，而SpaceX預料也不會例外。

獨家搶先看

3
全球最令人意外的經濟成功故事是……北韓。

這個國家的經濟正以多年未見的方式蓬勃發展，得益於對俄羅斯的武器銷售與部隊派遣、來自中國的物資與資金支持，以及規避國際制裁、進口更多能源、零組件與物資的能力。金氏政權在新冠疫情期間，曾全面關閉北韓邊境。此後，該國僅對少數外國人重新開放，包括俄羅斯及西方旅客與外交官。這些訪客描述了一個與過去截然不同、幾乎難以辨認的北韓——尤其是精英階層居住的首都平壤，Dasl Yoon與Timothy W. Martin報導。

4
這位低調人物，與比爾・蓋茲及傑佛瑞・艾普斯坦關係密切。

梅蘭妮・沃克（Melanie Walker）博士，是艾普斯坦人際網絡中眾多形形色色人物之一。這位西雅圖醫師，同時是艾普斯坦與比爾・蓋茲的知己。相較於其他與艾普斯坦有關聯的人物，如今54歲、任教於華盛頓大學醫學院的沃克，大多未曾進入公眾視野。然而，她可能是協助艾普斯坦在2008年因誘拐未成年人賣淫遭定罪後，重新打入蓋茲人際圈中最關鍵的人物之一，Khadeeja Safdar與Joshua Chaffin報導。沃克的律師表示，她與艾普斯坦之間存在一種「脅迫關係」。

巴塞隆納聖家堂即將完工——卻也點燃了一場旅遊業反彈聲浪。

聖家堂是全球最著名的建築工地之一，經過144年的施工，終於即將完工。但並非人人都為此歡欣鼓舞。隨著這座城市準備迎接教宗良十四世（Pope Leo XIV）到訪、為教堂最高塔樓進行祝聖，這棟建築當初的宗教願景，與如今已成為全球旅遊磁鐵的現實之間，出現了明顯落差。

今日焦點

7
紐約尼克隊回到麥迪遜廣場花園，主場迎戰聖安東尼奧馬刺隊，進行NBA總決賽第三戰。蘋果舉行年度開發者大會。財報：金寶湯（Campbell's）。

數字看世界

8
48%
根據CoStar數據，在世界盃開賽前，溫哥華與瓜達拉哈拉的飯店入住率高居榜首，接近50%。在美國，僅有舊金山一座城市的訂房表現超越加拿大與墨西哥。部分美國飯店業主表示，他們拿到的房價還算不錯，但這些外國主辦城市擁有多項優勢，包括往往更為狂熱的足球迷，以及整體較為親民的物價。

最後一則

9
輝達（Nvidia）榮登2026年「最具未來潛力企業」榜首。

在本報首度推出的「最具未來潛力企業」排行榜中，輝達拿下第一名，在這份因AI重塑商業版圖而由科技巨頭盤據的榜單中脫穎而出。與這家晶片製造商並列前五名的，還有Alphabet、微軟、Meta Platforms與思科系統（Cisco Systems），這個群體主要受惠於在創新能力、財務實力與AI準備度方面的優異表現。多數企業排行榜著眼於過去，依過往表現評分；而我們這份全新排行榜，著眼的則是未來。

新聞室之外

10
社論：上週，在進步派主導的加州，選民否決了州與地方層級的加稅提案。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Having Kids in America After 40
emails.contentEn:
✏️ What’s it like having kids in America after 40? More people are becoming older parents...and confronting new and often surprising financial realities. While many describe having more patience, flexibility and financial stability than they would have had earlier, they’re also running into difficult questions about their careers, savings and health. The Journal’s Dalvin Brown spoke to four families about the experience —and finances—of later-in-life parenthood.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz showed how a single country can weaponize an economic pinch point to seismic effect, exposing a global flaw that will take years to fix. More employers are requiring weigh-ins and health coaching before covering GLP-1s for weight loss or dropping coverage altogether. As Rahm Emanuel positions himself for a potential 2028 presidential bid, the 66-year-old showcased his vitality over the weekend by biking across New Hampshire. A new political movement is giving voice to young Indians frustrated by unemployment, low wages and what they see as a political system that has ignored their concerns.

FROM THE MARKETS

2

When President Trump jawbones the market, bet against him at your peril , writes Greg Ip.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

This cattle empire turned out to be a giant Ponzi scheme.

Rancher Brian McClain appeared to have a successful 80,000-head operation in Kentucky, powered by a $50 million loan from an agricultural bank and $120 million from investors. Yet when the lender got around counting his cattle, it enumerated only 8,916 animals: McClain had burned through more than $170 million, placating the bank’s occasional concerns and appeasing investors by paying out “shares of the profits” that often stayed on paper. Now, amid suits and countersuits among the lender bank, investors, a bankruptcy trustee and McClain’s family, details of the alleged Ponzi scheme are emerging , report Margot Patrick and Patrick Thomas.

4

These new college football millionaires are spending $80,000 on their high school proms.

ALISHA JUCEVIC FOR WSJ; BRIAN KAISER FOR WSJ; ZACHARY STINSON; JASMYN RENEÉ

Elite football programs now expect recruits to graduate from high school in December of their senior year so they can be on campus in January to learn playbooks and train with teammates. That means that while high school classmates are finishing up their last semester, these athletes are collecting Name, Image and Likeness checks. With the money, young superstars are remaking the high school rite of passage into a cultural phenomenon all their own, part victory lap and part personal branding opportunity.

5

Foreign businesses are fleeing Cuba as its economy collapses.

Spanish hotel giants Iberostar and Meliá have said they’re giving up management of at least a dozen Cuban hotels each and Mastercard and Visa are suspending transactions by non-U.S. foreign visitors, according to Cuba’s central bank. There’s also uncertainty over the future of Sherritt International, a Canadian mining company that’s one of Cuba’s key foreign investors. The exodus is delivering another blow to the island’s collapsing economy as the Trump administration ratchets up pressure, report Ryan Dubé, Amanda Coletta and Deborah Acosta.

☀️

6

Our guide shows the far-flung base camps that World Cup teams are calling home.

AUDREY VALBUENA

Of all the logistical challenges involved in staging the tournament, the toughest was figuring out where to put the 48 teams. Now, as the entire soccer world descends on the U.S., Canada and Mexico, teams are turning high school fields into practice pitches, checking into college dorms and luxury hotels and enduring the summer heat. Here’s where teams are setting up shop .

HAPPENING THIS WEEK

7

Monday: China's Xi Jinping is scheduled to visit North Korea for the first time in seven years as Beijing seeks to strengthen ties with its ally. Apple holds its annual developer conference . Tuesday: Maine’s Democratic primary election for U.S. Senate, which Graham Platner, the scandal-plagued oyster farmer , is expected to win. Wednesday: U.S. inflation data for May. Bill Gates is set to testify before the House Oversight Committee on his ties to Jeffrey Epstein, which have begun to erode his carefully crafted image . Thursday: The 2026 FIFA World Cup kicks off. Friday: SpaceX is expected to start trading on the Nasdaq, in an unconventional IPO that could be the largest of all time . The premiere of Disclosure Day, Steven Spielberg’s sci-fi thriller starring Emily Blunt, who is having a blockbuster year .

THE NUMBER

8

 >200

How many people David Grutman says he chats with a day. The hospitality entrepreneur behind LIV nightclub spoke with the Journal’s Gunjan Banerji about building relationships, structuring deals and why he still worries about money in the latest episode of The WSJ Money Interview.

AND FINALLY...

9

The U.S. needs mechanics and electricians, so big business is spending to create some.

Philanthropies and big employers, such as Ford, are ramping up programs to persuade more Americans to don tool belts . New efforts announced just this year already total around $400 million. The latest campaign is a $90 million Bloomberg Philanthropies effort launching this coming week focused on helping more high-school students land jobs in the trades.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 40歲後在美國生兒育女，是什麼樣的體驗？愈來愈多人成為高齡父母……並面臨新的、往往令人意外的財務現實。許多人表示，比起年輕時，如今他們擁有更多耐心、彈性與財務穩定度，但也遇到關於職涯、儲蓄與健康的棘手問題。本報記者Dalvin Brown採訪了四個家庭，了解他們晚年育兒的經驗——以及財務狀況。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
伊朗關閉荷莫茲海峽一事顯示，單一國家如何能將一個經濟咽喉點武器化、造成震盪般的衝擊，也暴露出一項需要數年才能修補的全球性缺陷。愈來愈多雇主要求員工先接受體重測量與健康指導，才提供GLP-1類減重藥物的給付，甚至乾脆取消相關給付。隨著拉姆・伊曼紐（Rahm Emanuel）為可能角逐2028年總統大位布局，這位66歲的政治人物上週末藉由騎單車橫越新罕布夏州，展現自己的活力。一場新興政治運動，正為那些對失業、低薪，以及他們認為長期忽視其訴求的政治體制感到不滿的印度年輕人發聲。

市場動態

2
Greg Ip撰文指出，當川普總統對市場口頭施壓時，與他對賭風險極高。

獨家搶先看

3
這個養牛帝國，原來是一場龐大的龐氏騙局。

牧場主人布萊恩・麥克萊恩（Brian McClain）表面上在肯塔基州經營著一個擁有8萬頭牛、看似成功的養牛場，資金來自一家農業銀行提供的5000萬美元貸款，以及投資人出資的1.2億美元。然而，當放款銀行終於前去清點牛隻數量時，卻只數到8916頭：麥克萊恩已燒掉超過1.7億美元，靠著支付往往只存在於紙面上的「利潤分成」，來安撫銀行偶爾浮現的疑慮及投資人。如今，隨著放款銀行、投資人、破產受託人與麥克萊恩家族之間互相提告、對簿公堂，這起據稱屬於龐氏騙局的案件細節正逐漸浮現，Margot Patrick與Patrick Thomas報導。

4
這些新晉大學美式足球百萬富翁，在自己的高中畢業舞會上豪擲8萬美元。

精英美式足球校隊如今期望招募的球員，能在高三那年12月就從高中畢業，以便在1月就進入大學校園學習戰術手冊、與隊友一同訓練。這意味著，當高中同班同學還在完成最後一個學期時，這些運動員早已開始領取姓名、肖像與形象權（NIL）的支票。靠著這筆錢，這些年輕的超級新星，正將高中畢業舞會這項傳統成年禮，改造成專屬於他們自己的文化現象——一半是慶功巡禮，一半是個人品牌經營機會。

5
隨著經濟崩潰，外國企業正逃離古巴。

西班牙飯店巨頭Iberostar與Meliá均表示，將放棄各自在古巴管理的至少十幾家飯店，萬事達卡與Visa則暫停了非美國籍外國旅客的交易服務，古巴央行證實了這項消息。加拿大礦業公司Sherritt International——古巴主要的外國投資者之一——未來走向也充滿不確定性。隨著川普政府持續加大施壓力道，這波撤資潮正對這座已陷入崩潰的島國經濟，帶來又一記打擊，Ryan Dubé、Amanda Coletta與Deborah Acosta報導。

6
我們的指南帶你了解世界盃各隊落腳的遙遠大本營。

在籌辦這項賽事所涉及的所有後勤挑戰中，最棘手的莫過於安置這48支球隊。如今，隨著整個足球世界湧向美國、加拿大與墨西哥，各隊紛紛把高中球場改造成練習場地、入住大學宿舍與豪華飯店，並忍受夏季酷暑。以下是各隊落腳之處。

本週焦點

7
週一：中國國家主席習近平預計時隔七年再度訪問北韓，北京希望藉此強化與這個盟友的關係。蘋果舉行年度開發者大會。週二：緬因州舉行美國參議員民主黨初選，深陷醜聞的牡蠣養殖業者格雷厄姆・普拉特納預計將勝出。週三：5月美國通膨數據公布。比爾・蓋茲將就其與傑佛瑞・艾普斯坦的關係，在眾議院監督委員會作證——這段關係已開始侵蝕他精心塑造的形象。週四：2026年FIFA世界盃開幕。週五：SpaceX預計將在那斯達克掛牌交易，這是一場可能創下史上最大規模紀錄、形式也不同尋常的IPO。電影《Disclosure Day》首映，這部史蒂芬・史匹柏執導的科幻驚悚片，由今年星運正旺的艾蜜莉・布朗主演。

數字看世界

8
逾200
這是大衛・格魯特曼（David Grutman）表示自己每天會聊天交談的人數。這位LIV夜店背後的餐旅業企業家，在最新一集《WSJ Money Interview》中，與本報記者Gunjan Banerji談到了如何建立人脈、規劃交易架構，以及為何他至今仍會為錢感到擔憂。

最後一則

9
美國需要更多技工與電工，因此大型企業正砸錢培養人才。

包括福特在內的慈善機構與大型雇主，正加大力度推動計畫，說服更多美國人投身技術行業。今年才剛宣布的新一輪計畫，總金額已達約4億美元。最新一項行動，是彭博慈善基金會（Bloomberg Philanthropies）將於下週啟動、金額達9000萬美元的計畫，重點在協助更多高中生從事技術類工作。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Graham Platner’s Messy Rise
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Who is Graham Platner? To many, the presumed Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Maine is an oyster farmer with an authentic working-class voice. To others, he’s a dilettante who benefitted from family money. Either way, one thing is clear: The 41-year-old veteran is one of this year’s biggest political gambles . The Journal’s Aaron Zitner reports on how Platner’s dark years have become a liability for Democrats in their quest to win back the Senate. This is part of our profile series on the figures reshaping their parties ahead of the 2026 midterms: read the rest here .

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra advanced to the general election for California governor , according to the Associated Press. The other leading candidate, former Fox News host Steve Hilton, is pitching a MAGA makeover of California, though he hasn’t clinched his spot yet. A sticking point in the talks to end the Iran war is Tehran’s demand for early access to cash , which leaves President Trump in a politically hazardous situation. Russian President Vladimir Putin's allies continue to travel on Western-made private jets , despite sanctions aimed at punishing Moscow’s elite over Ukraine. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum is refusing to extradite the governor of Sinaloa, accusing Washington of meddling in the country’s internal affairs . In an excerpt from his new book , Vice President JD Vance reflects on how the death of Charlie Kirk influenced his family to embrace a new life.

FROM THE MARKETS

2

The selloff in technology and AI stocks was a grim reminder of the market’s dependence on a thinning group of top performers. The labor-market rebound means Kevin Warsh’s job as Federal Reserve chairman just got a lot more complicated , writes Nick Timiraos.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Americans are keeping their cars longer than ever—and it’s remaking the auto industry.

Some drivers are squeezing more miles out of their vehicles and eschewing new rides because of sticker shock, high interest rates and economic jitters. Thanks to advancements, today’s cars last longer than vehicles of generations past. The average vehicle on U.S. roads is about 13 years old, a historic high and a 20% jump from a decade ago. The reality is fundamentally reshaping the economics of buying, selling and fixing vehicles in America, reports Sharon Terlep. Automakers, long laser-focused on the new-car market, are now pouring resources into propping up used-car sales, aftermarket parts and maintenance work.

4

Wait, why are restaurants now charging $40 for chicken?

Diners are happy to pay upscale prices for other meat dishes, says Dawn Eldridge, owner of the Brooklyn restaurant The Sparrow. But fancy chicken angers people in a different way. The beloved yardbird has become a proxy for the affordability crisis due to a mix of slim restaurant margins, inflation, a national protein obsession and consumer expectations, reports Alina Dizik. Chicken dish prices grew 22% over the past four years in fine dining restaurants, according to Datassential—and the median cost of a chicken entree is more than fish and shellfish, despite chicken being a lower-cost ingredient.

5

Two Texas billionaires and a U.S. senator are battling over “America’s resort.”

For nearly two decades West Virginia Sen. Jim Justice has owned the Greenbrier, the historic resort in the heart of Appalachia and the centerpiece of his business empire. Founded in 1778, the luxury outpost has hosted U.S. presidents, royalty and the rich and famous. But Robert and Blake Rowling say they can run it better. The father and son, billionaire hoteliers from Dallas, are waging a takeover of the resort —and many locals are rooting for the Texans, reports Kris Maher. The Greenbrier is now caught between dueling lawsuits and barbs traded by a wealthy U.S. senator and the deep-pocketed owners of more than 50 luxury hotels.

6

Stop asking the Journal’s auto columnist for advice—and just buy the Genesis GV80.

GENESIS MOTOR

With the spacious GV80, Hyundai Motor Group furthers its ambition to rule the premium SUV market. Dan Neil writes that he’s—mostly—smitten by the classy car , which has a conventional gas powertrain.

HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

7

Sunday: The Tony Awards cap what WSJ’s critic called a sorry season for musicals, but a strong one for plays . The French Open tennis tournament ends. The Formula One Monaco Grand Prix. THE NUMBER

 $2,300

The approximate cost of EcoFlow’s “balcony solar” system . Residents of Utah and Maryland can now use this type of system to combat skyrocketing utility bills, and seven more states have recently passed laws to make it possible. In states with the highest energy costs—such as California and Hawaii—plug-in solar systems could pay for themselves in three years or less, says Moncef Krarti of the University of Colorado, Boulder.

AND FINALLY...

9

Your next great meal may be at a gas station.

Fueled by changing consumer appetites, convenience store fare has gone from questionable to mouthwatering. From mahi-mahi tacos to breakfast pizza, here’s what to order on your next road trip .

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Many of America’s worst policy experiments have been bipartisan mind melds. A new example comes this week from Bernie Sanders, who wants the feds to take ownership stakes in AI companies .

✏️ 格雷厄姆・普拉特納究竟是誰？在許多人眼中，這位被視為緬因州聯邦參議員民主黨提名人選的人物，是一位擁有真實勞工階層聲音的牡蠣養殖業者；但在另一些人眼中，他不過是個靠家族財富坐享其成的業餘玩家。無論如何，有一點很清楚：這位41歲的退伍軍人，是今年最大的政治豪賭之一。本報記者Aaron Zitner報導了普拉特納那段不堪回首的過去，如何成為民主黨力圖奪回參議院多數的一大負擔。這是我們針對2026年期中選舉前重塑各黨政治版圖人物所做人物側寫系列報導的一部分，點此閱讀其餘報導。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
據美聯社報導，前衛生與公共服務部長哈維爾・貝塞拉（Xavier Becerra）已晉級加州州長大選。另一位主要候選人、前福斯新聞主持人史蒂夫・希爾頓，正主打將加州改造成「讓美國再次偉大」（MAGA）風格的訴求，不過他尚未確定入圍資格。結束伊朗戰爭談判中的一個癥結點，在於德黑蘭要求提前取得現金，這讓川普總統陷入一個政治上頗為棘手的處境。儘管西方已對莫斯科精英實施制裁、以懲罰其在烏克蘭問題上的作為，俄羅斯總統普丁的盟友仍持續搭乘西方製造的私人飛機出行。墨西哥總統克勞迪婭・薛恩鮑姆（Claudia Sheinbaum）拒絕引渡錫那羅亞州州長，指控華盛頓干涉該國內政。副總統萬斯在其新書節錄內容中，談到查理・柯克（Charlie Kirk）之死如何促使他的家庭擁抱一種新的生活方式。

市場動態

2
科技股與AI類股的拋售潮，令人痛苦地提醒市場對一小群表現最佳個股的高度依賴。Nick Timiraos撰文指出，勞動市場的反彈，讓凱文・沃許出任聯準會主席的任務，一下子變得複雜許多。

獨家搶先看

3
美國人把車開得比以往更久——這正在重塑整個汽車產業。

由於價格令人咋舌、利率居高不下加上經濟前景不明，部分車主正設法讓愛車多撐一段里程，並避免換購新車。得益於技術進步，如今的汽車比過去世代的車輛更耐用。美國道路上車輛的平均車齡約為13年，創下歷史新高，較十年前大增20%。Sharon Terlep報導，這項現實正從根本上重塑美國購車、賣車與修車的經濟模式。長期以來緊盯新車市場的車廠，如今正投入資源，力挺二手車銷售、售後零件與維修業務。

4
等等，為什麼餐廳現在賣一份雞肉要收40美元？

布魯克林餐廳The Sparrow老闆道恩・埃爾德里奇（Dawn Eldridge）表示，顧客很樂意為其他肉類料理支付高檔價位。但高檔雞肉卻以另一種方式激怒了顧客。Alina Dizik報導，這道深受喜愛的家禽料理，因餐廳利潤微薄、通膨、全民對蛋白質的執著，以及消費者期待等多重因素交織，已成為「可負擔性危機」的縮影。根據Datassential數據，過去四年來，高檔餐廳的雞肉料理價格上漲了22%——儘管雞肉本是成本較低的食材，一份雞肉主菜的中位數價格卻已高於魚類與貝類海鮮。

5
兩位德州億萬富豪與一位聯邦參議員，正為「美國度假勝地」的所有權而爭鬥。

近20年來，西維吉尼亞州參議員吉姆・賈斯提斯（Jim Justice）一直擁有格林布萊爾（Greenbrier）——這座位於阿帕拉契心臟地帶的歷史悠久度假村，也是他商業帝國的核心資產。這處創立於1778年的豪華度假勝地，曾接待過美國總統、王室成員與各界名流富豪。但來自達拉斯的億萬富豪飯店經營者羅伯特與布萊克・羅林（Robert and Blake Rowling）父子表示，他們能經營得更好。這對父子正發動一場收購格林布萊爾的行動——而許多當地居民都在為這對德州人加油打氣，Kris Maher報導。格林布萊爾如今陷入一連串訴訟纏鬥，以及這位富有的聯邦參議員與坐擁50多家豪華飯店的財力雄厚業主之間的唇槍舌戰。

6
別再問本報汽車專欄作家的建議了——直接買Genesis GV80就對了。

隨著空間寬敞的GV80問世，現代汽車集團正進一步實現稱霸豪華休旅車市場的野心。Dan Neil撰文表示，他對這款配備傳統燃油動力系統的優雅車款——大致上——十分心動。

本週末焦點

7
週日：東尼獎頒獎典禮壓軸登場，本報劇評稱今年是音樂劇的慘淡一季，卻是舞台劇的豐收年。法網公開賽落幕。F1摩納哥大獎賽舉行。

數字看世界

8
2300美元
這是EcoFlow「陽台太陽能」系統的大約售價。猶他州與馬里蘭州居民如今可使用這類系統來對抗飆升的電費，另有七個州近期通過法律，讓這類系統得以合法安裝。科羅拉多大學波德分校的Moncef Krarti表示，在電費最高的州——例如加州與夏威夷——插電式太陽能系統最快三年內即可回本。

最後一則

9
你下一頓美味大餐，或許就在加油站。

隨著消費者口味改變，便利商店的食物已從讓人存疑，搖身變成令人垂涎。從鬼頭刀塔可餅到早餐披薩，這裡整理了你下次公路旅行該點些什麼。

新聞室之外

10
社論：美國史上不少最糟糕的政策實驗，都是跨黨派攜手促成的結果。本週又添一例：伯尼・桑德斯（Bernie Sanders）希望聯邦政府能在AI公司中持有股權。

更正：卡瑪拉・哈里斯是前副總統。週五版《10-Point》誤將她描述為前總統。

✏️ The era of anything goes in private-credit underwriting is coming to an end. Under pressure from investors, lenders are hiking costs and curbing sweeteners. Some are even tightening underwriting criteria to entire industries because of the threat that AI poses.

Elsewhere in today’s newsletter: We look at the lucrative underground economy surrounding the New York Knicks’ historic playoff run and the gloves-off brawl that could come with a Gavin Newsom-Kamala Harris presidential contest. Plus, the Journal’s Emily Glazer takes us inside her yearslong investigation into Bill Gates’s cracking public image.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

The Food and Drug Administration has launched a safety study of the abortion pill. Americans on GLP-1s are overwhelming retailers with their nonstop returns.

Small stocks are trouncing market giants—and that’s not a good sign , writes James Mackintosh. Rocket Lab gives investors another way besides SpaceX to play the space race , writes Asa Fitch.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

‘Like two cats circling’: Kamala Harris and Gavin Newsom weigh a 2028 showdown.

The former president and California’s governor have much in common—fellow Bay Area Democrats who insist they’re friends but don’t always act like it. Newsom, 58, and Harris, 61, have shared mentors, staffers, donors, friends and consultants for more than two decades, going neck and neck in the parochial world of Bay Area politics. They have exchanged endorsements and snubs, each wary of the other, according to people close to them. The conspicuously liberal politicians live in exclusive locales at two ends of the Golden State and appear on a collision course for the keys to the big white mansion at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue, report Tarini Parti and Eliza Collins.

4

Meet the SpaceX employees who are about to become overnight millionaires.

Once Elon Musk’s rocket-and-satellite company makes its stock-market debut, thousands of current and former employees will be able to more easily cash in on their equity stakes, which they have watched soar in value in the run-up to what is set to be the biggest initial public offering of all time. The beneficiaries include not just engineers and other white-collar workers, but the legions of technicians who build the rockets, as well as baristas and other salaried employees who work at SpaceX campuses in California, Texas and Florida, report Becky Peterson and Corrie Driebusch.

6

An unsung Brazilian city offers slow life and magic encounters.

When photographer Tyler Mitchell first visited Havana over a decade ago, he was captivated by Afro-Cuban culture—the centuries-old buildings and spiritual practices rooted in West African traditions. The pull of documenting another city washed in pastels and marked by deep grooves of history led him to Salvador, the capital of the Brazilian state of Bahia, in March. His photos capture a place as vibrant as its facades .

HAPPENING TODAY

7

WSJ live Q&A: What questions do you have about the $75 billion SpaceX IPO? Submit them here , and our reporters may answer starting today at 2 p.m. ET. Economic data: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the May jobs report. New York sports showdowns: The Knicks face the San Antonio Spurs tonight for Game 2 of the NBA Finals, while the Yankees host their longtime rivals, the Boston Red Sox, at home. THE NUMBER

8

 1

Ryanair CEO Michael O’Leary says the low-cost carrier is diverting an average of nearly one flight a day because of drunken behavior on board, up from one a week a decade ago. In the U.K., having a pint—or three—before a morning flight is a tradition as sacred as Sunday roast. O’Leary thinks it’s time to sober up —and is calling for U.K. airports to stop selling alcohol in the mornings, or at least cut patrons off after two rounds.

AND FINALLY...

9

Wall Street mania is pushing Knicks tickets to $176,000.

If sports and money have converged in recent years, a championship run by the favorite team of Wall Street, Big Law, real-estate bigwigs and celebrities might mark the singularity. The downside is that no one really understands what a seat should be worth . That’s giving Knicks season-ticket holders an option between living New York glory or cashing in big. For everyone else, as one Manhattan executive put it, scrambling to see the team’s first trip to the finals since the Clinton administration “is like the f—ing ‘Hunger Games.’”

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

✏️ 私募信貸市場「什麼都行」的年代即將終結。在投資人施壓下，放款機構正調高成本、削減優惠條件。部分機構甚至因AI帶來的威脅，而收緊對整個產業的放款標準。

今日電子報其他內容：我們探討了圍繞紐約尼克隊歷史性季後賽之旅所形成的一門有利可圖的地下經濟，以及一場可能發生的紐森對哈里斯2028年總統之爭，將會如何撕破臉大戰一場。此外，本報記者Emily Glazer也帶我們一探她耗時多年、深入調查比爾・蓋茲公眾形象逐漸崩解的內幕報導。

艾瑪・塔克（Emma Tucker）
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1
共和黨參議員通過了一項700億美元的移民執法法案，但並未如願撤銷川普總統的「反武器化」基金。美國食品藥物管理局已對墮胎藥展開一項安全性研究。Anthropic呼籲頂尖AI實驗室考慮放慢開發步調，並警告AI模型即將具備無需人類介入即可自我改進的能力。Siri是市面上最笨的聊天機器人之一，蘋果希望藉由一次大改版，帶動其AI領域的重返榮耀之路。即時衛星情資，讓烏克蘭的無人機攻擊比以往更加致命。使用GLP-1類藥物的美國人，正以源源不絕的退貨潮讓零售商應接不暇。

市場直擊

2
道瓊期貨 51722.00　漲51.00　漲0.10%；標普500期貨 7566.75　跌34.25　跌0.45%；那斯達克100期貨 30195.50　跌292.75　跌0.96%

James Mackintosh撰文指出，小型股正大幅跑贏市場巨頭——這可不是個好兆頭。Asa Fitch撰文指出，Rocket Lab為投資人提供了SpaceX之外，另一種參與太空競賽的途徑。

獨家搶先看

3
「像兩隻互相繞圈的貓」：卡瑪拉・哈里斯與紐森正在盤算一場2028年對決。

這位前副總統與這位加州州長有許多共通點——兩人都是灣區出身的民主黨人，都堅稱彼此是朋友，行為舉止卻不總是如此。58歲的紐森與61歲的哈里斯，二十多年來共享導師、幕僚、金主、朋友與顧問，在灣區這個地方派系色彩濃厚的政治圈中不分軒輊。據親近兩人的人士透露，他們彼此互相背書，也曾互相冷落，各自對對方都有所提防。這兩位立場鮮明的自由派政治人物，分別居住在加州兩端的頂級社區，如今看似正朝著角逐賓夕法尼亞大道1600號那棟白色大宅鑰匙的方向，迎頭相撞，Tarini Parti與Eliza Collins報導。

4
認識一下這些即將一夜致富的SpaceX員工。

一旦伊隆・馬斯克旗下的火箭與衛星公司完成股市首秀，數千名現任與前任員工，將更容易將手中的股權變現——這些股權的價值，在這場預料將是史上規模最大的首次公開發行前夕，已一路飆升。受益者不僅包括工程師等白領員工，還包括負責建造火箭的大批技術人員，以及在SpaceX位於加州、德州與佛州園區工作的咖啡師等領薪員工，Becky Peterson與Corrie Driebusch報導。

5
一座鮮為人知的巴西城市，提供慢活步調與奇妙邂逅。

十多年前，攝影師泰勒・米契爾（Tyler Mitchell）首次造訪哈瓦那時，就被非裔古巴文化深深吸引——那些歷經數百年的建築，以及植根於西非傳統的靈性習俗。這股記錄另一座色彩粉嫩、歷史刻痕深厚城市的衝動，促使他在今年3月前往巴西巴伊亞州首府薩爾瓦多。他的照片捕捉到這座城市外觀般活力四射的一面。

今日焦點

7
《華爾街日報》線上問答：對於這場750億美元的SpaceX IPO，你有什麼問題？在此提交你的問題，我們的記者將從今日美東時間下午2時起解答部分提問。經濟數據：美國勞工統計局公布5月就業報告。紐約體育大戰：尼克隊今晚將迎戰聖安東尼奧馬刺隊，進行NBA總決賽第二戰；洋基隊則將主場迎戰宿敵波士頓紅襪隊。

數字看世界

8
1
瑞安航空執行長邁可・奧利里（Michael O'Leary）表示，這家廉價航空公司如今平均每天約有一班航班，因機上乘客酒醉滋事而必須改降，而十年前這種情況一週才發生一次。在英國，早班飛機起飛前先來一品脫——或三品脫——啤酒，是如同週日烤肉一般神聖不可侵犯的傳統。奧利里認為，該是清醒一下的時候了——他呼籲英國各機場停止在上午時段賣酒，或至少在客人喝完兩輪後就不再供應。

最後一則

9
華爾街的狂熱，正把尼克隊門票價格推高到17.6萬美元。

如果說近年來體育與金錢已日益交融，那麼這支深受華爾街、頂級律師事務所、地產大亨與名流青睞的球隊闖入總冠軍賽，或許正標誌著這股趨勢的奇異點。壞消息是，沒有人真正清楚一個座位究竟該值多少錢。這讓尼克隊的球季套票持有者，面臨一個抉擇：親身見證紐約的榮耀時刻，還是趁機大賺一筆。對其他人而言，正如一位曼哈頓高階主管所言，為了搶著見證這支球隊自柯林頓政府時代以來首度打進總冠軍賽，簡直「就像他媽的《飢餓遊戲》」。

新聞室之外

10
社論：川普或許討厭自己成為「法律戰」（lawfare）的攻擊目標，但他確實深諳如何將這套手法，用來對付任何冒犯他的人。這正是約翰・波頓（John Bolton）的故事寫照——他如今同意認罪協商，說穿了只因犯下了寫一本批評他的書這樁「罪行」。

The statue wars that swept away monuments six years ago are back. This time, the battle is to restore them . Traditionalists are suing and lobbying local governments to resurrect memorials to Confederate generals, Founding Fathers and European explorers. Russia’s elite is souring on the war. Putin doesn’t seem to care.

Russia’s inability to break through the stalemate in Ukraine is becoming so evident that significant voices in the Russian establishment have publicly started to call for an end to the conflict . The big question is whether President Vladimir Putin will acknowledge this reality and abandon his aspiration to extinguish Ukrainian independence. ✏️ President Trump isn’t shy about diving into the weeds, shaping mergers and weighing in on psychedelic drugs from the West Wing. His involvement in regulatory decisions—calls that were once made by independent agencies—is dramatically shifting the balance of power across Washington, D.C. It’s also reordering how influence campaigns are waged. Our reporters take you inside Trump’s takeover of the American regulatory machine.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Voting ended in California’s primary elections but final results for the messy gubernatorial and the Los Angeles mayor’s race could take a while. In Iowa’s Republican primary for governor, Zach Lahn defeated Rep. Randy Feenstra—a rare rebuke for Trump. Veteran “60 Minutes” correspondent Scott Pelley was fired by CBS News , a day after taking aim at Editor in Chief Bari Weiss’s leadership during a staff meeting. The U.S. and Iran exchanged heavy fire in some of the most intense fighting in months, testing the fragile ceasefire. The death of a student who was handcuffed as he lay dying from multiple stab wounds has sparked a debate in Britain over whether efforts to stamp out racism in policing have swung too far. Eating a diet high in ultraprocessed foods is associated with an increased risk of dementia , according to new research.

3

Trump is taking over the American regulatory machine.

A few weeks after returning to the White House last year, the president signed an executive order requiring independent agencies for the first time to submit major regulations to the White House budget office. Trump has fired the Democratic commissioners at multiple agencies, including the Federal Trade Commission. Former agency officials across administrations say it is highly unusual for presidents to be so intimately involved in the details of regulatory reviews. But these days, companies are directly approaching the president instead of pleading their cases with staff or senior officials at the agencies, report Josh Dawsey, Dana Mattioli, Rebecca Ballhaus and Jessica Toonkel.

4

America’s data center build-out is falling way behind schedule.

Tech companies are earmarking unprecedented sums of money to finance the build-out of massive data centers, such as a planned $80 billion equity raise by Google parent Alphabet. But even as the piles of capital secured have grown larger, the ability to deploy it in the artificial intelligence race has become less certain . Issues such as supply-chain backlogs, permitting fights and power-supply availability have caused data center construction to fall behind targeted timelines, with the gap growing wider in recent months. Google, however, has taken a novel approach to getting around some of the major bottlenecks, reports Katherine Blunt.

5

See how the Middle East’s ceasefires remain plagued by violence.

The conflicts that have battered the Middle East over the past three years—in Gaza, Lebanon and now Iran—are all, on paper, in ceasefire. In practice, fighting persists on every front. Strikes, skirmishes and military operations keep the region on edge. The fighting is less intense than before, but persistent enough to leave all three arenas in an uneasy limbo between war and peace, report Andrew Dowell, Emma Brown and Daniel Kiss. Here’s where things stand.

Elon Musk has made about $3.6 million an hour over 31 years. Here are other ways to measure his wealth.

The initial public offering for SpaceX could make the tech founder the world’s first trillionaire. Just how wealthy is he? His fortune now stands at roughly $970 billion, mostly in stock, according to a WSJ analysis. Accumulating that amount over his career averages out to $992 a second. We put together a visual guide to Musk’s virtually incomprehensible wealth—and look at some things he could do with his current fortune.

✏️ Walk into our newsroom, and you’ll see shelves of print editions dating back to our founding in 1889. I was flipping through an issue from 1977 the other morning—a special edition dedicated entirely to explaining our reporting process to readers. Trust in our reporting and authority is the currency we seek to earn with all we produce. To that end, we are launching a new section in the 10-Point called “Reporter’s Notebook.” Each week, our journalists will take you behind the scenes of the day’s biggest stories. In this first edition, reporter Christopher Weaver explains how he and his colleagues investigated abusive billing practices by autism-therapy businesses .

Now, on to today’s headlines:

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

The U.S. is pressing neutral Oman to pick a side and cut ties with Iran. The Trump administration signaled a retreat on its nearly $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund. Berkshire Hathaway’s $6.8 billion deal to acquire a major home builder reflects its conviction that the housing market will recover from its yearslong slump. READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Jill Biden talks about her memoir and a marriage where difficult things weren’t discussed.

In an interview with WSJ’s Kara Voght, the former first lady talks about her husband’s health, losing the East Wing and Nancy Pelosi. “View From the East Wing,” out today, is the first accounting of the Biden administration from the person closest to the president himself. It tells us things we never knew, such as the fact that Jill supported the notion that Joe Biden, now 83, should take a cognitive test, because she thought he could pass it. There are also details we’d only heard from one side: Jill confirms, for example, that Vice President Kamala Harris urged Biden to endorse her immediately after he dropped out, just as Harris describes in her own telling of the 2024 race.

4

The NRA is going through a messy breakup as its charitable arm splits and rebrands.

A breakup is under way at the National Rifle Association, the nation’s oldest gun-rights group. The NRA Foundation, the organization’s charitable arm, is declaring independence from the more famous political wing and rebranding itself as The 1791 Foundation. The fracture comes after the NRA sued the NRA Foundation in January, alleging that a “disgruntled faction of former NRA directors” had seized control of the charity, positioned it as a direct competitor and misused some $160 million in funds. Gun-rights advocates are watching the spat with dismay , reports Zusha Elinson. The NRA didn’t respond to requests for comment.

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK

5

I started investigating autism-therapy providers alongside my colleagues Tom McGinty and Anna Wilde Mathews late last year. To do this, we turned to a trove of Medicaid data that we had access to under a unique research agreement with the federal government. I was surprised to see that Indiana held nine of the top 10 most expensive providers per patient for Medicaid in 2023, and initially suspected a data-entry error. But interviews with state officials confirmed the anomalies—and that we had uncovered a much larger story.

Less than two weeks after WSJ published its investigation of Piece by Piece Autism Centers, the nation’s costliest autism-therapy provider, Indiana barred it from billing the state’s Medicaid program. Piece by Piece Autism Centers shut down in May. Our reporting continues: Check out our latest investigation on autism-therapy providers billing private health plans here . — Reporter Christopher Weaver

Critics maintain that college-entrance tests limit opportunity for Black, Hispanic and poor students. The pandemic accelerated a growing trend of schools making the exams optional or getting rid of them altogether. More recently, schools have been re-tightening test mandates. MIT reinstated the SAT requirement in 2022, and Yale University followed suit last week.

America’s most dysfunctional zoo is trying to put its checkered past behind it.

There is a Nile crocodile loose somewhere in central Louisiana. It’s in good company. A private zoo here has also misplaced a Marabou stork, a lynx, two Indian crested porcupines, a family of capybaras, a mob of kangaroos, a flock of flightless Rheas, a herd of water buffalo and an entire safari exhibit of bison, zebras and antelope. Now even the founder wants to escape. Last week, Gabriel Ligon donated the zoo’s roughly 125 remaining animals to a group of employees who are turning the facility into a nonprofit.

走進我們的新聞編輯室,你會看到一排排陳列的印刷版報紙,最早可追溯至1889年創刊時期。前幾天早上,我隨手翻閱了一份1977年的報紙——那是一期完全用來向讀者解釋我們報導流程的特別版。信任,是我們透過每一則報導努力賺取的貨幣。基於此,我們在「10-Point」電子報中推出一個新單元,名為「記者筆記」。每週,我們的記者將帶你深入了解當日最重大新聞背後的幕後故事。在這第一期中,記者Christopher Weaver說明他與同事如何調查自閉症療育機構涉嫌浮濫收費的行徑。

接下來,是今日頭條:

艾瑪．塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

美國正向立場中立的阿曼施壓,要求其選邊站並與伊朗斷絕關係。川普政府釋出訊號,可能在近18億美元的「反武器化」基金上讓步。波克夏海瑟威以68億美元收購一家大型建商,反映其對房市將從長年低迷中復甦的信心。哥倫比亞總統大選中,一位極右派的政壇新人已躍居領先——原因為何,本文詳述。俄羅斯已向其位於敘利亞的空軍基地運送新一批補給,顯示莫斯科打算在阿薩德政權垮台後,仍保留這處重要的軍事據點。

吉兒．拜登談她的回憶錄,以及一段有些難言之隱從未被討論的婚姻。
在接受本報記者Kara Voght專訪時,這位前第一夫人談到丈夫的健康狀況、失去東廂辦公室,以及與南希．裴洛西的關係。今日出版的《東廂視角》一書,是拜登政府時期首度由與總統本人關係最親近之人所寫下的第一手記述。書中透露許多我們過去不知道的事,例如吉兒其實支持83歲的喬．拜登接受認知能力測試,因為她認為他能夠通過。書中也提到一些我們過去只聽過單方說法的細節:例如吉兒證實,副總統賀錦麗在拜登退選後隨即敦促他立刻背書支持她——這與賀錦麗自己對2024年大選的說法一致。

全國步槍協會正經歷一場混亂的分家,其慈善部門獨立分割並改名。
全美歷史最悠久的槍枝權利團體「全國步槍協會」(NRA)正在經歷一場分裂。該組織的慈善部門「NRA基金會」正宣布脫離較知名的政治部門獨立,並改名為「1791基金會」。這場分裂始於今年一月NRA對NRA基金會提告,指控「一群心懷不滿的NRA前董事」奪取了該慈善機構的控制權,將其定位為直接競爭對手,並挪用約1.6億美元資金。槍枝權利倡議人士正憂心忡忡地關注這場糾紛,Zusha Elinson報導。NRA對置評請求未作回應。

記者筆記

我從去年年底開始,與同事Tom McGinty及Anna Wilde Mathews一起調查自閉症療育機構。為此,我們透過與聯邦政府的一項特殊研究協議,取得了大量Medicaid(醫療補助)數據。令我驚訝的是,印第安納州在2023年每名病患收費最高的十大Medicaid業者中就佔了九席,我一開始還懷疑是資料輸入錯誤。但與州官員的訪談證實了這些異常數據——我們也因此發現了一個更大的故事。

在《華爾街日報》發表對「Piece by Piece自閉症中心」(全美收費最高的自閉症療育機構)的調查報導後不到兩週,印第安納州就禁止該機構向該州Medicaid請款。Piece by Piece自閉症中心已於五月結束營業。我們的追蹤報導仍在持續:歡迎點閱我們針對自閉症療育機構向私人醫療保險浮濫收費的最新調查報導。——記者Christopher Weaver

Oura執行長談論人們過度執著的健康數據。
圖片:ALEX HOTZ
Oura的用戶長期以來一直要求推出更小尺寸的戒指,該公司最新款產品正是對此的回應。本報與Oura執行長Tom Hale對談,談及公司最新的改款設計、健康追蹤的未來趨勢,以及健康焦慮日益普遍的現象。點此觀看我們的訪談。

今日焦點

選舉:加州州長初選。另外還可關注愛荷華州、紐澤西州、蒙大拿州、新墨西哥州與南達科他州的初選。財報:Palo Alto Networks、Dollar General  📰 今日報紙

數字看新聞

1,100人以上
這是加州大學系統中,聯署要求校董事會恢復大學入學考試的數學與科學教授人數,他們表示準備不足的學生正在拉低學術標準、耗費教學資源。批評者則堅持,入學考試會限制黑人、西裔與貧困學生的機會。疫情加速了學校將考試列為選擇性、甚至完全取消考試的趨勢。但近來,學校開始重新收緊考試要求。麻省理工學院已於2022年恢復SAT要求,耶魯大學上週也跟進。

最後,還有這則……

美國最「失序」的動物園,正努力擺脫過去的混亂歷史。
路易斯安那州中部某處,目前仍有一隻尼羅鱷在外遊蕩,而牠並不孤單。這座私人動物園同時還遺失了一隻非洲禿鸛、一隻猞猁、兩隻印度冠豪豬、一整窩水豚、一群袋鼠、一群不會飛的美洲鴕、一群水牛,以及整個包含野牛、斑馬與羚羊的野生動物展區的動物。如今就連創辦人本人也想「脫身」。上週,Gabriel Ligon將動物園剩餘約125隻動物捐贈給一群員工,他們正計畫將這處設施轉型為非營利機構。

編輯室之外

社論:埃克森美孚股東投票支持管理層將公司註冊地從紐澤西州遷至德州的決定。企業是否已將「離開懲罰企業的州、遷往不這麼做的州」視為一種公司治理的責任?

✏️ The S&P 500 has had one of its best two-month runs ever. That often means more good times ahead. A massive frenzy over memory chips is sending shares of tech companies soaring. While skeptics are troubled by the sheer scale of the moves, Wall Street—and history—suggests this rally has room to run.

Away from the trading floors, the Journal’s Juliet Chung takes you inside an exclusive retreat where heirs collectively worth $7 billion learn the secrets to staying rich. As wealth at the top explodes, more families are grappling with how to make sure that money doesn’t screw up their kids—and the kids don’t screw up the money .

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

The U.S. and Iran exchanged fresh blows , with the U.S. striking what it said were air-defense radar and drone sites and Kuwait coming under attack after Iran said it was retaliating. President Trump’s insistence that several Gulf States must sign on to the Abraham Accords is a complicating factor in negotiations to end the war . A White House memo on Trump’s latest physical exam lacks details of the results of tests to assess his cardiovascular health, doctors who read the report say . Federal safety officials and lawmakers are at odds over a major safety fix that could cost $50,000 per airplane. Nvidia unveiled the first personal laptops designed for running AI “agents.” In Colombia, a far-right lawyer who promises an iron-fisted crackdown on drug thugs took the most votes in Sunday’s first round of the presidential election.

Berkshire Hathaway agreed to buy home builder Taylor Morrison for $6.8 billion in cash. The deal is one of Greg Abel’s first big moves as CEO. There are some clear advantages for OpenAI or Anthropic in being the first to go public , writes Asa Fitch.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

At this exclusive retreat, wealthy kids learn how not to blow an inheritance.

On a drizzly morning, a dozen of the wealthiest kids in the world convene in an Austin Airbnb to consider a question: “Why do you think it is your parents want you to work?” Certainly, none of the college students and 20-somethings in this room need to. They’re here for a retreat run by R360, a peer-membership group for families worth at least $100 million. Such retreats are part of the wealth industry’s answer to making sure the kids are all right. What was once a cottage industry of such training has metamorphosed, with nearly every multifamily office, bank and peer-membership group offering its own version, reports Juliet Chung.

4

Taiwan’s opposition leader comes to the U.S. with a message straight out of Beijing.

Cheng Li-wun, the chairwoman of the Kuomintang, is set to begin a two-week U.S. tour that is billed as a peace mission but also carries the weight of U.S.-China geopolitics. It is happening as Beijing is urging Washington to rethink its support for Taiwan, a self-ruled democratic island that doesn’t recognize Beijing’s claim to govern it. Her message for an American audience is that Taiwan operates under a constitution that already supports the principle that the island and the mainland are part of a single China, report Lingling Wei, Yoko Kubota and Joyu Wang.

 EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: How did the California governor’s race become a hot mess for Democrats?

Scandals, missteps and a lack of Democratic unity have complicated the state’s gubernatorial election , explain Laura J. Nelson and Eliza Collins.

A: It has been a long, strange trip—and a bit of a headache for Democrats—leading up to Tuesday’s gubernatorial primary to choose a successor to California Gov. Gavin Newsom.

A front-runner dropped out after allegations of sexual misconduct and assault, another went viral after an on-camera incident, a billionaire candidate assailed the wealth of other billionaires, and Democrats, for a fleeting moment, were grateful for Trump—and that was all in the past few months.

California’s political leaders didn’t coalesce around one of the half-dozen prominent Democrats in the race, resulting in a messy primary that briefly prompted worries that the party could be shut out of the November runoff—an outcome that could pave the way for a Republican.

That concern has passed. There are dozens of candidates on the ballot, but recent polls show the contest has tightened into a three-person race. The two candidates who get the most votes will advance to the November election.

The top contenders are former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra, a Democrat; billionaire investor and philanthropist Tom Steyer, a Democrat; and former Fox News host Steve Hilton, a Republican.

The latest polling found that among likely voters, Becerra had 25%, Hilton had 21% and Steyer 19%. (The margin of error was 2 percentage points.)

SEE THE STORY

6

Here are the adversaries Trump has threatened and prosecuted.

IMAGE: DREW AN-PHAM/WSJ

An emboldened Justice Department with acting Attorney General Todd Blanche at the helm is ramping up efforts to investigate and prosecute Trump’s perceived enemies. More than four dozen people have found themselves in the president’s crosshairs since he returned to office for a second term. Here’s a visual guide to those individuals.

The WSJ Global Food Forum kicks off in Chicago. Earnings: Hewlett Packard Enterprise 📰 Today's paper

8

 25%

Roughly a quarter of American professionals hit a wall in their careers before their so-called peak earning years, going at least five years without a real boost in pay or position. That’s the central finding of a new study tracking the careers of 1.3 million midcareer professionals since 2000. It suggests that even in an economy with high employment, many workers run into an invisible barrier to upward mobility just when their careers are supposed to gain momentum.

AND FINALLY...

9

Britain’s elite are in a race to save their favorite relish.

When the makers of a salty condiment called Gentleman’s Relish said poor sales couldn’t justify producing it any longer, much of the British establishment mobilized to see if there was a way to save its favorite umami-rich anchovy paste . At least three approaches have been made to buy the brand, which is as ubiquitous to upper-class larders as French’s mustard is to New York hot-dog stands.

標普500指數迎來史上最佳兩個月漲勢之一,這種走勢往往預示著更多好日子還在後頭。記憶體晶片掀起的瘋狂熱潮,正推動科技股股價飆升。儘管懷疑論者對這波漲勢的規模之大感到不安,但華爾街——以及歷史經驗——都顯示這波行情還有續航空間。

離開交易大廳,本報記者Juliet Chung帶你走進一場專屬聚會,參與者是身家合計高達70億美元的富二代繼承人,學習如何守住財富的秘訣。隨著頂層財富持續膨脹,愈來愈多家族正努力確保財富不會毀了孩子——孩子也不會毀了財富。

艾瑪．塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

美國與伊朗再度交火,美方表示其打擊目標為防空雷達與無人機基地,科威特則在伊朗宣稱展開報復後遭到攻擊。川普總統堅持要求數個波斯灣國家必須加入《亞伯拉罕協議》,這成為結束戰爭談判中的複雜因素。閱讀過川普最新體檢報告的醫師表示,白宮發布的備忘錄缺乏評估其心血管健康檢測結果的細節。聯邦安全官員與國會議員就一項可能讓每架飛機成本增加5萬美元的重大安全改裝方案意見不一。輝達發表了首款專為運行AI「代理人」而設計的個人筆電。在哥倫比亞,一位承諾對毒梟採取鐵腕鎮壓的極右派律師,在週日總統大選首輪投票中拿下最多票數。

在這場專屬聚會上,富二代們學習如何不揮霍掉自己的遺產。
一個細雨紛飛的早晨,一群全球最富有的孩子齊聚奧斯汀一間Airbnb民宿,思考一個問題:「你們認為父母為什麼希望你們工作?」這個房間裡的大學生與二十多歲年輕人,其實根本沒有工作的必要。他們正在參加由R360主辦的聚會——這是一個專為身家至少一億美元家族設立的同儕會員組織。這類聚會,是財富管理產業對「確保下一代過得好」這個問題所提出的解方之一。曾經只是小眾的相關訓練產業,如今已徹底蛻變,幾乎每一家多家族辦公室、銀行與同儕會員組織都推出了自己的版本,Juliet Chung報導。

台灣在野黨領袖赴美,傳遞的訊息卻與北京如出一轍。

專家觀點

問:加州州長選舉是如何演變成民主黨的一團亂局?
醜聞、失誤與民主黨內部缺乏團結,讓這場州長選舉變得複雜,Laura J. Nelson與Eliza Collins解釋原因。

答:這是一段漫長且離奇的旅程——對民主黨人來說也相當頭痛——最終走到週二這場州長初選,選出加州州長蓋文．紐森的繼任人選。

一位領先者在遭指控性行為不當與性侵後退選,另一位候選人因鏡頭前失態而爆紅,一位億萬富豪候選人抨擊其他億萬富豪的財富,而民主黨人一度短暫地慶幸有川普可以攻擊——這一切都發生在過去短短幾個月內。

加州的政治領袖並未團結支持這場選戰中半打知名民主黨候選人中的任何一位,導致初選陷入混亂,一度引發外界擔憂該黨可能無緣進入11月的決選——這樣的結果恐為共和黨鋪路。

這項擔憂如今已經消退。選票上仍有數十位候選人,但近期民調顯示,選戰已收斂為三人之爭。得票最高的兩位候選人將晉級11月大選。

目前的領先者分別是:民主黨籍的前衛生與公共服務部長哈維爾．貝塞拉;民主黨籍的億萬富豪投資人暨慈善家湯姆．史泰爾;以及共和黨籍的福斯新聞前主持人史蒂夫．希爾頓。

最新民調顯示,在可能投票的選民中,貝塞拉支持率為25%,希爾頓21%,史泰爾19%(誤差範圍為2個百分點)。

延伸閱讀

以下是川普威脅並起訴過的對手名單。
圖片:DREW AN-PHAM/WSJ
在代理司法部長陶德．布蘭奇的領軍下,一個更加大膽的司法部正加緊調查與起訴川普眼中的敵人。自他二度就任總統以來,已有超過四十多人成為總統鎖定的目標。以下是這些人物的視覺化指南。

今日焦點

《華爾街日報》全球食品論壇在芝加哥開幕。財報:Hewlett Packard Enterprise  📰 今日報紙

數字看新聞

25%
大約四分之一的美國專業人士,在所謂的職涯收入巔峰期到來之前,就已在職涯上遭遇瓶頸——至少五年薪資或職位都未曾實質提升。這是一項追蹤130萬名職涯中期專業人士(自2000年起)的新研究的核心發現。這顯示即便在高就業率的經濟環境下,許多勞工仍會在職涯本應加速上升之際,撞上一道看不見的向上流動障礙。

最後,還有這則……

英國上流社會正競相搶救他們最愛的一款調味醬。
當這款名為「紳士風味醬」(Gentleman's Relish)的鹹味調味品製造商表示,銷售量已不足以支撐繼續生產時,英國上流建制派紛紛動員起來,設法拯救這款他們最愛、鮮味濃厚的鯷魚醬。目前至少已有三方提出收購這個品牌的意向,它在上流家庭儲藏室裡的普及程度,不亞於法式芥末醬之於紐約熱狗攤。

編輯室之外

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Cracks in Bill Gates’s Image
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Bill Gates spent years crafting his image. Now it’s cracking. The billionaire’s staff carefully cultivates his reputation—down to keeping a custom-size mannequin to test his outfits. That kind of attention to detail has helped burnish the philanthropist’s profile as one of the world’s most admired men. But Gates’s image has been shattered as details of his association with the late Jeffrey Epstein have spilled into public view. The Journal’s Emily Glazer reports on how the fallout from these revelations is now eroding efforts to protect Gates’s reputation .

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Even if the White House resolves its standoff with Senate Republicans over the president’s $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund, a new “wounded bear caucus” shows that President Trump now faces an expanded group of intraparty foes with little to lose. A fight over a marine terminal on Miami’s Fisher Island, often dubbed the wealthiest ZIP Code in America, has erupted among some of the city’s most powerful economic players. Days after Graham Platner announced his Maine Senate bid, his wife informed the campaign about sexually explicit texts with several women she had previously discovered on the Democrat’s phone. A handful of African nations are rejecting American health aid , outraged by the Trump administration’s demands for access to private health records and even minerals in exchange for lifesaving medicine. Jeff Bezos and Elon Musk each had difficulties this past week in their renewed space rivalry, underscoring the challenges to their sci-fi dreams , writes Tim Higgins.

FROM THE MARKETS

2

Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is urging the central bank to pay more attention to alternative inflation measures like the trimmed mean, turning what had been a technical debate among economists into a live question for policy. Golf is getting cooler and younger , and the stock market has noticed, writes Jinjoo Lee.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Nearly half of home-insurance claims result in zero payout.

Home insurers pitch policies as a peace-of-mind financial safety net, but in a disaster, customers can find the apparent guarantee of compensation evaporates . The five biggest home insurers as a group didn’t pay out on more than 44% of claims resolved last year, up from 36% a decade earlier, a WSJ analysis found. Several factors are driving nonpayment rates higher, report Jean Eaglesham and Jaclyn Jeffrey-Wilensky. Prime among them: Insurers are responding to years of losses by getting tougher on claims. Representatives of the five insurers said they investigate all claims and ensure amounts owed under the policies are paid promptly, fairly and fully.

4

These family farmers are making more from clicks than crops.

AARON AGOSTO FOR WSJ

The Welkers—Nick, his brother Scott, and their father, Bob—are part of a growing class of “aginfluencers” monetizing farm life . Followers of the Montana family tune in for a taste of farming in Big Sky Country: sweeping drone shots of golden grain fields and brothers wrestling with monster tractor tires. In a bad crop year, 40-year-old Nick said he can earn $5,000 from farming—and six figures posting about it. That money has helped the family business weather weak crop prices and persistent drought that has punished farms across America, reports Amira McKee.

 EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: With the AI landscape shifting so quickly, how are investors hunting for the next winners?

Columnist James Mackintosh wrote about how investors are deciding where to put their money, and when to do it .

A: Where will the money be made next in AI? Should investors just buy anything with a hint of AI, or try to find the parts of the AI supply chain, the “stack,” where bottlenecks capture more of the value?

Searching out the bottlenecks looks tempting because the returns so far for anyone who got it right have been extraordinary.

First up, after the launch of ChatGPT in 2022, was Nvidia. Its GPUs turned out to be the best way to train the large language models, and soaring demand meant Nvidia could keep jacking up the price of new chips. Its shares are up 15-fold since November 2022.

This year, new bottlenecks emerged even as Nvidia slowed, facing competition from chips developed by Amazon, Alphabet and Cerebras, which recently went public.

Some investors are instead spreading their bets; their basic argument is that AI is changing so fast that it’s hard to anticipate the bottlenecks.

Others are trying to decide whether AI models will be a winner-takes-most market or a highly competitive commodity, how long chip bottlenecks will endure, the possibility of pricing power for data centers and the rewards for the usually dull business of supplying power.

And another alternative is to try to own everything. As more AI stocks tap public markets to satisfy their vast capital needs, a widely diversified AI portfolio becomes possible.

SEE THE STORY

6

More Americans are aging alone. Amy Kant told us what it’s like.

TONY LUONG FOR WSJ

The 65-year-old is single with no children, and is finding that big questions—such as who should make financial decisions on her behalf if she falls ill—are often intensified when aging alone. How to handle eldercare? Estate planning? Where will she live in her later years? She spoke to the Journal about navigating these questions without the built-in safety net of a family.

HAPPENING THIS WEEK

7

Monday: The WSJ Global Food Forum kicks off in Chicago. Tuesday: California’s gubernatorial primary. Former first lady Jill Biden is set to publish a memoir. Wednesday: The NBA finals begin, with the New York Knicks tipping off against the San Antonio Spurs. Friday: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the May jobs report.

THE NUMBER

8

 $36,000

The price of a bottle of Domaine de la Romanée-Conti wine that was stolen from L’Auberge Provençale Inn and Restaurant in Virginia’s Shenandoah Valley. The ultra-wealthy drool over expensive wines from the domaine, and Romanée-Conti’s high demand and hefty price have also motivated thieves and counterfeiters, helping to foster a black market for rare spirits.

AND FINALLY...

9

Nobody can agree how to keep the sharks out of South Africa’s new Club Med.

The resort’s expansion into South Africa has run into a problem—and this one’s got teeth. The waters off the Indian Ocean coast where throngs of swimmers will soon congregate are home to the world’s three most-dangerous shark species . The local government has proposed an old tactic to keep guests from becoming chum: Putting a shark net adjacent to the beach. But scientists aren’t fans of the plan.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

WSJ | Buy Side: Auto-refinance rates start below 5% for borrowers with excellent credit, but others might also find competitive rates.
emails.contentZh:
比爾．蓋茲花了多年精心打造自己的形象,如今這個形象正逐漸出現裂痕。這位億萬富豪的團隊向來細心經營他的聲譽——甚至還備有一具依他身形訂製的人形模特兒,用來試穿服裝。正是這種對細節的講究,讓這位慈善家得以躋身全球最受敬重人士之列。但隨著他與已故傑佛瑞．艾普斯坦之間的關聯細節逐漸浮上檯面,蓋茲的形象已然破碎。本報記者Emily Glazer報導,這些爆料的後續效應正如何侵蝕外界為保護蓋茲聲譽所做的努力。

艾瑪．塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

即便白宮與參議院共和黨人就總統近18億美元的「反武器化」基金僵局達成解決,一個新的「受傷的熊派系」顯示,川普總統如今面臨的黨內反對勢力已然擴大,且這些人幾乎沒有什麼好損失的。邁阿密Fisher Island(常被稱為全美最富有的郵遞區號)一處海運碼頭的爭端,已在該市部分最具經濟實力的人物之間爆發。就在葛拉罕．普拉特納宣布角逐緬因州參議員席位後不久,他的妻子向競選團隊通報了她先前在這位民主黨人手機上發現、與多名女性往來的露骨簡訊內容。少數幾個非洲國家正拒絕美國的醫療援助,原因是對川普政府要求以私人健康紀錄、甚至礦產作為換取救命藥物條件感到憤怒。傑夫．貝佐斯與伊隆．馬斯克在這場重啟的太空競賽中,上週各自遭遇挫折,凸顯他們科幻夢想所面臨的挑戰,Tim Higgins撰文分析。

市場動態

聯準會主席凱文．沃許正敦促央行更加關注諸如「調整平均值」等替代性通膨指標,將原本僅止於經濟學家之間的技術性辯論,轉變為攸關政策走向的現實議題。高爾夫球運動正變得愈來愈酷、愈來愈年輕化,股市也已注意到這股趨勢,Jinjoo Lee撰文分析。

獨家搶先看

近半數的房屋保險理賠最終結果為零給付。
房屋保險公司將保單宣傳為安心的財務安全網,但在災難發生時,顧客往往發現看似有保障的理賠承諾其實形同虛設。《華爾街日報》分析發現,五大房屋保險公司整體而言,去年結案的理賠案中,超過44%未獲得任何給付,高於十年前的36%。Jean Eaglesham與Jaclyn Jeffrey-Wilensky報導,多項因素正推升拒賠比例。其中最主要的原因是:保險公司正因多年虧損而對理賠採取更嚴格的審查態度。這五家保險公司的代表則表示,他們會調查所有理賠案件,並確保保單應付金額迅速、公平且全額給付。

這些家庭農場靠點閱率賺得比種田還多。
維克家族——尼克、他的哥哥史考特,以及父親鮑伯——是日益壯大的「農業網紅」群體之一,他們將農場生活變現。這個蒙大拿家族的追蹤者,只為欣賞大天空之州的農耕風光:空拍下的金色麥田,以及兄弟倆與巨型曳引機輪胎搏鬥的畫面。尼克說,即便在收成不佳的年份,他也能從務農賺進5,000美元——而發文分享則可賺進六位數。這筆收入幫助這個家族企業撐過疲弱的作物價格,以及重創全美農場的持續乾旱,Amira McKee報導。

專家觀點

問:在AI局勢瞬息萬變之際,投資人如何尋找下一批贏家?
專欄作家James Mackintosh撰文探討投資人如何決定資金投向,以及該在何時進場。

答:AI領域下一波財富將在何處產生?投資人是否應該只要沾上一點AI概念就買進,還是該試著找出AI供應鏈——也就是所謂「堆疊」——中,瓶頸環節能攫取更多價值的部分?

尋找瓶頸環節看似誘人,因為迄今為止,凡是押對寶的人,報酬都相當驚人。

2022年ChatGPT問世後,率先受惠的是輝達。其GPU晶片被證明是訓練大型語言模型的最佳方式,需求暴增也讓輝達得以不斷調高新款晶片的價格。自2022年11月以來,其股價已上漲15倍。

今年,即便輝達的成長步調放緩,新的瓶頸也隨之浮現,面臨來自Amazon、Alphabet與最近剛掛牌上市的Cerebras所開發晶片的競爭。

部分投資人則選擇分散押注,他們的基本論點是:AI變化速度太快,難以預先判斷瓶頸會出現在哪裡。

另一些人則在思考,AI模型市場未來將是贏家通吃,還是高度競爭的大宗商品市場;晶片瓶頸將持續多久;資料中心是否具備定價權的可能性;以及那項通常枯燥乏味的供電業務所能帶來的回報。

還有另一種選擇是乾脆什麼都持有。隨著愈來愈多AI相關企業為滿足龐大資金需求而登上公開市場,打造一個高度分散的AI投資組合也變得可行。

延伸閱讀

愈來愈多美國人正獨自老去。艾米．坎特告訴我們那是什麼感覺。
圖片:TONY LUONG FOR WSJ
這位65歲的單身女性沒有子女,她發現一旦獨自老去,諸如「萬一生病誰該替她做財務決策」這類重大問題往往會被放大。該如何安排老年照護?遺產規劃怎麼辦?晚年要住在哪裡?她向本報談及,在缺乏家庭這道內建安全網的情況下,如何面對這些問題。

本週焦點

週一:《華爾街日報》全球食品論壇在芝加哥開幕。週二:加州州長初選。前第一夫人吉兒．拜登的回憶錄即將出版。週三:NBA總決賽開打,紐約尼克隊迎戰聖安東尼奧馬刺隊。週五:美國勞工統計局公布五月就業報告。

數字看新聞

36,000美元
這是一瓶從維吉尼亞州仙那度河谷「普羅旺斯客棧」餐廳遭竊的羅曼尼康帝酒莊葡萄酒的價格。超級富豪對這座酒莊出產的昂貴美酒趨之若鶩,羅曼尼康帝的高需求與高昂價格,也助長了竊賊與偽造者的犯意,催生出稀有烈酒的黑市交易。

最後,還有這則……

沒有人能就如何把鯊魚擋在南非新開幕的地中海俱樂部(Club Med)度假村之外達成共識。
這座度假村在南非的擴張計畫,遇上了一個「真的會咬人」的問題。印度洋沿岸海域即將湧入大批戲水遊客,而這片海域正是全球三種最危險鯊魚物種的棲息地。當地政府提議採用一種老方法,防止遊客成為「魚餌」:在海灘旁設置防鯊網。但科學家們並不看好這項計畫。

編輯室之外

華爾街日報｜Buy Side:信用優良的借款人可享有低於5%的汽車貸款再融資利率,其他借款人也可能找到具競爭力的方案。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: AI Cracks a Famous Math Problem
emails.contentEn:
✏️ A math problem stumped humans for 80 years—and AI just cracked it. Until recently, the most advanced AI models couldn’t do basic math. So mathematicians were astonished when OpenAI announced that one of its models found a new solution to a longstanding puzzle known as the Erdős problem. The Journal’s Ben Cohen explains what AI found , how we missed it—and why it matters.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

President Trump’s top aides have discussed whether he should kill the administration’s nearly $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund in exchange for getting immigration enforcement funding passed next month. New York City Mayor Zohran still hasn’t hired a chief executive to run the little-known but powerful Economic Development Corporation, which is worrying executives in real estate and finance. Ships are sailing “dark” to sneak out of the Strait of Hormuz , sometimes in collaboration with the U.S. military, creating a tiny relief valve for the global economy. Michele Spagnuolo, the Google engineer accused of using company data to bet on Polymarket, had a long list of enviable accomplishments .

FROM THE MARKETS

2

Stocks closed at records yesterday , with the Dow industrials rising 0.7% and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both up 0.2%, after comments from Trump gave investors more hope about a possible peace deal with Iran. Albert Manifold, BP’s ousted chairman, clashed with a fellow director earlier this year over the handling of sensitive talks about a potential deal, a sign of simmering boardroom tensions.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Greg Brockman—the billionaire coding genius making the tough decisions at OpenAI.

After a career spent in the shadow of better-known co-founders, the 38-year-old has stepped into the spotlight this year , report Keach Hagey and Laura J. Nelson. His new role overseeing product has made him the face of OpenAI’s new strategy on the eve of its IPO. The world learned from recent testimony that his stake is worth close to $30 billion, making him one of the 100 richest people in the world on paper, and vastly richer than the reported wealth of Altman, who holds no direct OpenAI equity. Brockman and his wife, Anna, have also taken on new political prominence, giving $50 million to super PACs aligned with Trump and the AI industry.

4

Robotaxis are spreading across the U.S.—and so is the backlash.

This was supposed to be the year that robotaxis hit Main Street, as companies like Alphabet’s Waymo, Tesla and Amazon’s Zoox launch AI-powered autonomous rides in dozens of cities. But as hundreds of robot cars collide with humans , both literally and figuratively, tensions are rising, reports Sean McLain. Criticism is mounting from drivers, law enforcement and local governments from California to New York—and as the companies attempt to scale, robotaxis face more scrutiny than ever before.

 EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: The U.N. is going broke. Why?

Reporter James T. Areddy wrote about the budget troubles facing the global intergovernmental organization.

A: The United Nations is in a liquidity crisis as the U.S. and China withhold payments to the institution in a jostle for control.

Washington has failed to pay billions of dollars owed to the international body and exited dozens of its programs and agencies, including the World Health Organization, to combat what Trump describes as wasteful spending and bad policymaking. The U.S. is more than $4 billion in arrears to the U.N.

China has compounded the U.N.’s problems by slow-walking its own payments, even as Beijing declares itself the organization’s leading defender and, in a jab at the U.S., the “de facto No. 1 financial contributor.” Beijing still owes the U.N. $455 million even after injecting almost $850 million this week into the organization during a visit by Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi.

The U.N. relies on U.S. and Chinese money for 42% of its basic funding.

Secretary-General António Guterres has warned that the U.N. is in a “race to bankruptcy” and cited a “very real prospect of the financial collapse of our organization.” On the current trajectory, the U.N. says it will be out of cash by mid-August—just when the process of picking a successor to Guterres shifts into high gear.

SEE THE STORY

6

This safari can take you to see one of Europe’s rarest wild cats.

LYNXPERIENCE

The Iberian lynx was on the verge of extinction in 2002, with just 94 cats left in their natural habitat. Now, thanks to a two-decade conservation initiative across southern Spain and parts of Portugal, there are an estimated 2,700 in the wild. As the number of cats has grown, so has a burgeoning safari trade. For around $350 a day, Jamie Lafferty booked a trip with one of the ecotourism companies that have popped up in recent years— here’s what he saw .

HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

7

Saturday: The Champions League final, which pits Stan Kroenke’s Arsenal against Paris Saint-Germain. Sunday: Colombia holds the first round of its presidential election. 📰 Today's paper 

THE NUMBER

8

 $11 billion

How much projected revenue FIFA is targeting in this year’s soccer World Cup, a record. Boosted by an expanded field of 48 teams this year, FIFA is leveraging the potent cocktail of an American World Cup to pack its war chest with money it plans to redistribute to its 211 member nations around the world. For fans, that means publicly listed World Cup tickets start in the hundreds of dollars—and soar into the thousands.

AND FINALLY...

9

This Chevy EV is funky…and fast.

一道困擾人類80年的數學難題,如今被AI破解了。直到最近,最先進的AI模型還連基本數學都做不好。因此,當OpenAI宣布其中一款模型針對一道名為「艾狄胥問題」的長年謎題找到新解法時,數學家們大感震驚。本報記者Ben Cohen說明AI發現了什麼、我們過去為何錯過了它——以及這項突破為何重要。

艾瑪．塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

川普總統的高層幕僚已討論是否該撤銷政府近18億美元的「反武器化」基金,以此換取下個月移民執法經費法案的通過。紐約市長佐赫蘭至今仍未任命一位執行長,來主管那個雖不起眼卻擁有實權的「經濟發展公司」,這讓房地產與金融業高層深感憂心。船隻正「熄燈」偷偷駛離荷莫茲海峽,有時甚至與美軍相互配合,為全球經濟創造出一個微小的緩解閥。Google工程師Michele Spagnuolo被控利用公司數據在Polymarket上下注,他過去擁有一長串令人稱羨的成就。

市場動態

昨日股市收在歷史高點,道瓊工業指數上漲0.7%,標普500與那斯達克指數均上漲0.2%,原因是川普的談話讓投資人對與伊朗達成和平協議的可能性更具信心。BP遭撤換的董事長Albert Manifold今年稍早曾與另一名董事就一項潛在交易的敏感談判處理方式發生衝突,顯示董事會內部的緊張關係正在醞釀。

獨家搶先看

葛雷格．布洛克曼——這位億萬富豪程式天才,正在OpenAI做出艱難決策。
在長年活在更知名的共同創辦人陰影下之後,這位38歲的技術長今年終於躍上鎂光燈焦點,Keach Hagey與Laura J. Nelson報導。他新接掌的產品督導職務,讓他成為OpenAI在首次公開發行前夕新戰略的代言人。外界從最近的證詞中得知,他的持股價值接近300億美元,使他躋身全球百大富豪之列(以帳面計算),遠遠超過據報未持有OpenAI直接股權的奧特曼的財富。布洛克曼與妻子安娜,近來也在政治圈嶄露頭角,已捐贈5,000萬美元給與川普及AI產業立場一致的超級政治行動委員會。

機器人計程車正在全美各地擴張——反彈聲浪也隨之而來。
本應是機器人計程車正式攻進美國各大街道的一年,像Alphabet旗下的Waymo、特斯拉與亞馬遜旗下的Zoox等公司,都在數十座城市推出由AI驅動的自駕載客服務。但隨著數以百計的機器人車輛與人類發生「碰撞」——無論是實質上還是比喻意義上——緊張情勢正在升溫,Sean McLain報導。從加州到紐約,來自駕駛人、執法單位與地方政府的批評聲浪持續增加——隨著這些公司試圖擴大規模,機器人計程車正面臨前所未有的嚴格審視。

專家觀點

問:聯合國正瀕臨破產,原因為何?
本報記者James T. Areddy撰文探討這個全球政府間組織面臨的預算困境。

答:由於美國與中國在爭奪主導權的角力中扣留應繳款項,聯合國正陷入流動性危機。

華府未能支付積欠這個國際組織的數十億美元款項,並退出了包括世界衛生組織在內的數十個計畫與機構,理由是川普所稱的浪費支出與不當政策。美國積欠聯合國的款項已超過40億美元。

中國則因拖延自身的繳款進度,進一步加劇聯合國的財務困境——即便北京自詡為該組織的主要捍衛者,並藉此暗諷美國,自稱是「事實上的頭號財政貢獻國」。即使中國外長王毅本週訪問期間,北京已向聯合國注入近8.5億美元資金,但仍積欠聯合國4.55億美元。

聯合國基本經費有42%仰賴美中兩國的資金。

秘書長古特雷斯已警告,聯合國正處於「破產競賽」之中,並提及該組織「財務崩潰的風險確實存在」。按照目前的趨勢,聯合國表示最快到8月中旬即會斷炊——恰好正值遴選古特雷斯繼任人選的程序進入白熱化階段。

延伸閱讀

這趟野生動物之旅,能帶你一睹歐洲最稀有的野生貓科動物之一。
圖片:LYNXPERIENCE
伊比利亞猞猁在2002年一度瀕臨滅絕,野外僅剩94隻。如今,經過西班牙南部與葡萄牙部分地區長達二十年的保育行動,野外數量估計已回升至2,700隻。隨著猞猁數量增加,新興的野生動物觀光生態也隨之興起。Jamie Lafferty以每天約350美元的價格,參加了近年來興起的一家生態旅遊公司行程——以下是他看到的景象。

本週末焦點

週六:歐冠聯賽總決賽,史丹．克隆克旗下的兵工廠將對決巴黎聖日耳曼。週日:哥倫比亞舉行總統大選首輪投票。📰 今日報紙

這是國際足聯(FIFA)在今年世界盃鎖定的預期營收目標,創下歷史新高。受惠於今年擴軍至48支球隊的規模,國際足聯正利用美國主辦世界盃這帖強效組合,大舉充實其戰爭基金,計畫將這筆資金重新分配給全球211個會員國。對球迷而言,這意味著公開發售的世界盃門票起價數百美元起跳——甚至可能飆升至數千美元。

Blazer EV SS是這家車廠全電動跨界休旅車的性能版本,速度飛快——但外型有點古怪,本報記者Dan Neil撰文評測。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: America’s Bulging Credit-Card Bill
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Americans are falling behind on their $1.25 trillion credit-card bill. The one-two punch of inflation and high interest rates is pushing people across the U.S. to their financial limits , reports Dan Frosch. Middle-class households, in particular, are struggling to pay down balances as more families “shift to a pattern of survival debt,” said Bruce McClary, spokesman for the National Foundation for Credit Counseling.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

The U.S. and Iran are within reach of an agreement to wind down the war, said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, but President Trump has yet to sign off on it. Hezbollah’s one-way drones have turned into Israel’s top concern on its northern flank, overtaking more-traditional threats such as antitank missiles. A rocket being tested by Jeff Bezos’ space company Blue Origin exploded on its Florida launchpad , but there were no injuries. Corporate America is starting to ration AI as the bill for its massive computing needs comes due. Stan Kroenke, the owner of Arsenal, the Los Angeles Rams and other pro sports teams, explained in a rare interview why his teams can’t stop winning.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Take a look inside Vladimir Putin’s $26 billion quest for longevity.

As with some Silicon Valley billionaires, Russia’s president has long been fascinated with antiaging research. Now, Putin’s quest to stave off decline is a state priority relying on methods as wide-ranging as organ printing, harvesting mini-pigs and exposure to ultralow temperatures, reports Bojan Pancevski. Last month, Russia’s government announced that scientists are developing a gene-therapy treatment aimed at slowing cellular aging as part of “New Health Preservation Technologies,” Putin’s $26 billion longevity initiative. But unlike similar research funded by tech executives including Bezos, Sam Altman or Peter Thiel, the work promoted by Putin’s circle has produced little peer-reviewed research in major international journals.

4

Real-estate agents are quitting the slow housing market.

The slowest market in decades is stretching into its fourth year, and even real-estate agents who made it this far are reaching a breaking point , reports Nicole Friedman. Most agents are independent contractors and get paid when a deal closes. With fewer sales to go around and homes taking longer to sell, more agents are ditching the industry or finding second jobs. Exacerbating the situation, a legal settlement in 2024 that changed how real-estate agents get paid has encouraged some buyers to forgo hiring an agent—and the rise of AI has also made it easier for buyers and sellers who want to navigate the process on their own.

 EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: How can you avoid the small blunders that can sink large tax deductions?

The rules for charitable tax breaks depend on getting details right. Reporter Laura Saunders wrote about what you should know .

A: Two recent Tax Court decisions involving first cousins who donated 13.3 acres of land to Highland City, Utah, in 2018, are a case in point.

The judge ruled that Stephen Martin and Clint Martin, who were close growing up and later did business together, can’t deduct $665,000 for the land donation. A limited liability company owned by the cousins acquired the land for $22,000 at a delinquent-tax auction in 2014.

The decisions didn’t turn on the donation’s valuation. Instead, the cousins lost their deduction because they lacked a proper “contemporaneous written acknowledgment,” or CWA. That’s tax jargon for a statement from the town saying the Martins didn’t receive goods or services in exchange for their donation.

Michael Hamersley, the attorney for Stephen Martin, said his client thinks there are material flaws in the decision and plans to petition for a rehearing. Clint Martin says he plans to join this petition.

Whatever the outcome, these cases raise a question: Do they add to Americans’ perception that the IRS unfairly pursues well-meaning taxpayers who commit foot-faults of highly complex laws?

SEE THE STORY

CAMILLE BRESSANGE/WSJ

For years the alpine lake—which straddles the California-Nevada border—has been both a summer playground and winter ski destination for the wealthy. Lately, however, the Tahoe divide has intensified as the impact of California’s proposed wealth tax plays out on its shores. As wealthy Californians flee the state, deep-pocketed buyers are taking refuge in Nevada , which is starting to rival Florida as a tax haven for the elite.

美國人正逐漸無力償還高達1.25兆美元的信用卡帳單。通膨與高利率的雙重打擊,正將全美民眾逼向財務極限,Dan Frosch報導。全美信用諮詢基金會發言人Bruce McClary表示,中產階級家庭尤其難以償還餘額,愈來愈多家庭正「轉向一種求生式負債模式」。

艾瑪．塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

財政部長史考特．貝森特表示,美國與伊朗已接近達成結束戰爭的協議,但川普總統尚未簽署批准。真主黨的單向攻擊無人機,已成為以色列北部邊境最主要的憂慮,超越了反坦克飛彈等傳統威脅。傑夫．貝佐斯旗下太空公司藍色起源正在測試的一枚火箭,在佛羅里達發射台上爆炸,但無人受傷。隨著龐大運算需求的帳單即將到期,美國企業界已開始配給AI資源使用。阿仙納、洛杉磯公羊隊等多支職業球隊的老闆史丹．克隆克,在一次罕見的專訪中解釋了他旗下球隊為何屢戰屢勝。

市場即時動態
道瓊期貨 50858.00(+115.00,0.23%)| 標普500期貨 7592.00(+10.25,0.14%)| 那斯達克100期貨 30344.25(+37.25,0.12%)
資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年5月29日美東時間上午5:57:07
📈 全天追蹤我們的即時財經報導。

勞動所得占經濟產出的比重剛創下歷史新低,企業利潤占比卻逼近歷史新高,這也有助於解釋消費者為何情緒如此低迷,Greg Ip撰文分析。記憶體晶片如今身價已超越石油,但正如石油一樣,晶片也被普遍視為容易出現劇烈價格波動的大宗商品,Dan Gallagher撰文分析。

獨家搶先看

一窺弗拉基米爾．普丁260億美元的長壽追求計畫。
如同部分矽谷億萬富豪一樣,俄羅斯總統長期以來對抗衰老研究深感著迷。如今,普丁延緩衰老的追求已成為國家級優先要務,採用的方法五花八門,從器官列印、養殖迷你豬到暴露於極低溫環境,無所不包,Bojan Pancevski報導。上個月,俄羅斯政府宣布,科學家正在開發一種基因治療,旨在延緩細胞老化,作為「新型健康保存技術」計畫的一部分——這正是普丁260億美元的長壽計畫。但與貝佐斯、山姆．奧特曼或彼得．蒂爾等科技高層資助的類似研究不同,普丁圈子所推動的這項研究,幾乎未在國際主要期刊上發表過任何同儕審查的成果。

房地產經紀人正逃離低迷不振的房市。
這場數十年來最冷清的房市已進入第四個年頭,即便是撐到現在的房地產經紀人,也已逼近臨界點,Nicole Friedman報導。多數經紀人屬於獨立承包性質,唯有成交才能領到報酬。隨著成交量減少、房屋銷售時間拉長,愈來愈多經紀人選擇離開這個行業或另謀兼職。雪上加霜的是,2024年一項改變房地產經紀人收費方式的法律和解案,也促使部分買家乾脆不再聘請經紀人——AI的興起,也讓想自行處理買賣流程的買賣雙方變得更加容易。

專家觀點

問:如何避免因小疏失而毀掉一大筆稅務減免?
慈善捐贈稅務優惠的規定,取決於是否把細節做對。本報記者Laura Saunders撰文說明你該知道的事。

答:近期兩起稅務法庭裁決便是一例,涉及一對表兄弟,他們在2018年將13.3英畝土地捐贈給猶他州高地市。

法官裁定,自幼交情深厚、後來又一起做生意的史蒂芬．馬丁與克林特．馬丁,無法就這筆土地捐贈申報66.5萬美元的稅務減免。這對表兄弟共同持有的一家有限責任公司,曾在2014年一場欠稅拍賣會上以2.2萬美元購入這塊土地。

這起裁決的關鍵並非捐贈的估值問題,而是這對表兄弟因缺乏一份適當的「同期書面確認函」(簡稱CWA)而喪失減免資格——這是稅務術語,指的是由當地政府出具的聲明,證明馬丁兄弟並未因捐贈而換取任何商品或服務。

代表史蒂芬．馬丁的律師Michael Hamersley表示,其當事人認為這項裁決存在實質瑕疵,計畫申請重審。克林特．馬丁則表示,他也打算加入這項申請。

無論結果如何,這些案例都引發一個問題:它們是否加深了美國人對國稅局的觀感——認為國稅局會不公平地追究那些出於善意、卻在極其複雜的稅法上犯了小失誤的納稅人?

延伸閱讀

加州那些對稅賦感到厭倦的億萬富豪,正湧向太浩湖的內華達州沿岸尋求庇護。
圖片:CAMILLE BRESSANGE/WSJ
多年來,這座橫跨加州與內華達州邊界的高山湖泊,一直是富豪們的夏季度假天堂與冬季滑雪勝地。然而近來,隨著加州擬議中的財富稅政策逐漸落實,太浩湖兩岸的分化也愈演愈烈。隨著富裕的加州人逃離該州,財力雄厚的買家紛紛湧入內華達州尋求庇護——這裡正逐漸與佛羅里達州並駕齊驅,成為菁英階層的避稅天堂。

今日焦點

保羅．麥卡尼發行新專輯《The Boys of Dungeon Lane》,靈感來自他在利物浦的童年。財報:Genesco與Buckle  📰 今日報紙

數字看新聞

425萬美元
這是摩根大通被裁定須支付前員工Brent Ryan Bodner的金額,源於一起不當解僱訴訟案,起因是一份642.5美元、以公司卡支付的熟食拼盤,以及一場搞砸的2024年超級盃派對。這家銀行辯稱,Bodner動用公司卡支付一場在家舉辦的派對違反公司政策,且將這筆費用申報不實,並計畫對這項裁決提出上訴。

最後,還有這則……

今年夏天最難搶到的工作:牧場沙拉醬的歐洲親善大使。
在Hidden Valley Ranch刊登廣告,徵求歐洲地區夏季「牧場大使」職缺後,該公司收到超過6,000份申請——是一般職缺申請量的70倍。有志成為牧場大使的應徵者,附上各種花式輔助資料,包括把自己的臉P圖到牧場醬瓶身上的照片。裝滿剪貼簿與提案簡報的箱子,開始湧入招聘經理的辦公室。

編輯室之外

✏️ In a nautical no-man’s-land, an aging “shadow fleet” is successfully moving billions of dollars in sanctioned Iranian crude to China. Off the coast of Malaysia, our reporters watched firsthand as the Catalina 7, a U.S.-sanctioned vessel, carried out an elaborate deception. Through a thick hose, it transferred oil with a ship whose name was hidden by black paint. Such offshore trysts typically obscure a cargo’s origin before its journey to China.

While this illicit trade provides Tehran with a vital lifeline, a U.S. naval blockade and war-battered economy are magnifying pressure on the regime to secure a deal with Washington.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

U.S. forces conducted new military strikes against Iran after Tehran launched drones at commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Estonia, a tiny country on NATO’s eastern border with Russia, is preparing for a wider war . The Justice Department has opened a probe into writer E. Jean Carroll, who accused President Trump of sexually assaulting her 30 years ago. The Trump administration is in talks to fund U.S. drone companies. Meet Gen. Christopher LaNeve, a hardline four-star general tipped to be the next Army chief. Wealthy retirees are buying “ med-à-terres ” to be near their New York doctors.

3

One million new-car buyers are gone and they aren’t coming back soon.

The U.S. auto industry faces sobering new math : Some one million prospective buyers have defected from the new-car market since the start of the decade—and they aren’t expected back soon. Until recently, auto executives, analysts and economists believed that U.S. new-car sales were on a steady climb back to volumes last seen before the pandemic. That’s no longer the case. High gas prices, rising interest rates and stubborn inflation are keeping buyers at home and cars on the lots, reports Sharon Terlep.

4

China is exporting its factories across the world and spooking the competition.

“Made in China” is becoming “made by China”—all over the world. Faced with higher Western tariffs and weak demand at home, many Chinese factories are moving abroad, making everything from appliances to automobiles everywhere from North and South America to Eastern Europe. More Chinese companies could be coming to the U.S. after Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping reached a deal to establish a new bilateral “board of investment.” Yet many countries’ leaders worry the businesses are bringing China’s brutal rat-race competition with them, potentially crushing local incumbents and curbing salaries, report Hannah Miao and Stephen Wilmot.

 EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: LinkedIn projects today’s college grads will hold twice as many jobs as previous generations. How can they prepare for a career defined by non-stop disruption?

The young people crossing commencement stages this month are launching careers that will change in ways they can’t imagine. Columnist Callum Borchers offers some tips for navigating this new career odyssey :

A: Hone foundational skills and get really good at articulating how you can use them in a range of roles.

Some of these skills—communication, critical thinking—are oft-repeated to the point of triteness. One that’s less-talked-about, but important, is reflection.

Artificial intelligence is bound to create jobs we haven’t thought of. This year’s grads, and many of the rest of us, will apply for those newly created jobs someday. We’ll have to explain how the abilities we developed in past roles are transferable. Reflective people will be better at this and have an edge.

There are ways to practice reflection. One is to create a personal “one-sheet”—not a traditional résumé but a summary of your best qualities that aren’t tethered to a specific job or field. This is a tip from business consultant Jim Jaffe, who is still working at age 90 and has pivoted many times.

Another exercise is to fill out the “soft skills” and “technical skills” sections of your LinkedIn profile. A lot of us leave these fields blank, but LinkedIn says recruiters increasingly filter candidates by the skills listed in their bios. This is because titles are becoming less relevant as the nature of work changes.

SEE THE STORY

6

The beach house is getting a dark, moody makeover.

PHOTO: MADELINE TOLLE FOR WSJ

Social media is awash with rich, dark interiors, emboldening homeowners to try edgy, moody designs. Until recently, though, most of these darker palettes were found in primary homes, while beach houses remained the province of white drywall, breezy blues and sandy neutrals. That is starting to change , however, with waterfront homes using colors like deep-ocean navy, the slate gray of stormy seas, or the dark brown of old ship planks.

New Jersey has become an unlikely bright spot for the struggling industry for one simple reason: It has the most effective tax incentive program of any state.

A nasty contest to become commodore has torn this yacht club apart.

It was only after she was told she wouldn’t be commodore of the Sausalito Yacht Club that Marisa McArthur realized how badly she wanted it . From her post as rear commodore, it should have been a clear shot to the top. But when McArthur came before the nominating committee for her final promotion, the 50-year-old was told advancement was a no go. What followed was a contentious election campaign, McArthur’s expulsion, her husband’s and mother’s suspension and now a lawsuit.

在一片海上無主之地,一支老舊的「影子船隊」正成功將數十億美元的受制裁伊朗原油運往中國。本報記者在馬來西亞外海親眼目睹,美國制裁船隻Catalina 7號進行了一場精心策劃的欺瞞行動:透過一條粗管,它與一艘船名被黑漆遮蓋的船隻進行了石油轉運。這類海上「幽會」通常是為了在貨物運往中國之前掩蓋其真實來源。

儘管這種非法貿易為德黑蘭提供了重要的維生管道,但美國的海軍封鎖與戰爭重創的經濟,正加大該政權與華府達成協議的壓力。

艾瑪．塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

在德黑蘭向荷莫茲海峽的商船發射無人機後,美軍對伊朗展開新一輪軍事打擊。愛沙尼亞這個位於北約與俄羅斯邊境上的小國,正為更大規模的戰爭做準備。司法部已對作家E．珍．卡羅爾展開調查,她曾指控川普總統30年前對她性侵。川普政府正就資助美國無人機公司展開談判。認識一下克里斯多福．拉尼夫將軍,這位強硬派的四星上將被視為下一任陸軍參謀長的熱門人選。富裕的退休人士正購買「近醫宅」,以便就近前往紐約看診。

一百萬名新車買家已經消失,而且短期內不會回頭。
美國汽車產業正面臨一項令人清醒的新算式:自這個十年開始以來,已有約一百萬名潛在買家退出新車市場,且預計短期內不會回頭。直到最近,汽車業高層、分析師與經濟學家都還相信,美國新車銷量正穩步回升,終將重返疫情前的水準。如今情況已不再如此。高油價、上升的利率與頑固的通膨,正讓買家按兵不動、車輛滯留展示間,Sharon Terlep報導。

中國正將工廠輸出至全世界,並讓競爭對手為之膽寒。
「中國製造」正在全球各地演變成「中國經營」。面對西方更高的關稅與國內疲弱的需求,許多中國工廠正遷往海外,從南北美洲到東歐,製造從家電到汽車的各種產品。在川普與中國領導人習近平達成建立新的雙邊「投資委員會」協議後,可能有更多中國企業將進駐美國。然而,許多國家的領導人擔心,這些企業會將中國那種殘酷的削價競爭一併帶來,可能壓垮當地既有企業並壓低薪資水準,Hannah Miao與Stephen Wilmot共同報導。

專家觀點

問:LinkedIn預測,如今的大學畢業生一生將換的工作次數,將是上一代人的兩倍。他們該如何為這種充滿不斷變動的職涯做準備?
本月從畢業典禮舞台上走下來的年輕人,即將展開的職涯將以他們難以想像的方式不斷變化。專欄作家Callum Borchers就如何應對這場全新的職涯冒險提供了一些建議:

答:磨練基礎技能,並且要非常擅長闡述如何將這些技能運用在各種不同角色上。

其中一些技能——溝通、批判性思考——早已被反覆提及到近乎陳腔濫調的地步。而較少被談及、卻同樣重要的一項,是「反思能力」。

人工智慧勢必會創造出我們尚未設想過的工作。今年的畢業生,以及我們許多人,終有一天都會去應徵那些新創造出來的職位。屆時我們必須解釋,過去角色中培養的能力如何能夠轉移應用。善於反思的人在這方面會更有優勢。

練習反思的方法有很多。其中一種是製作一份個人「一頁式簡介」——不是傳統履歷,而是一份不侷限於特定工作或領域、總結你最佳特質的摘要。這是90歲仍在工作、且職涯多次轉型的企業顧問Jim Jaffe提供的建議。

另一項練習是填寫LinkedIn個人檔案中的「軟實力」與「技術能力」欄位。我們許多人都會把這些欄位留白,但LinkedIn表示,愈來愈多招募人員會依據個人簡介中列出的技能來篩選候選人,因為隨著工作性質的改變,職稱本身正變得愈來愈不具參考價值。

延伸閱讀

海濱別墅正迎來一波深沉、氛圍感十足的大改造。
圖片:MADELINE TOLLE FOR WSJ
社群媒體上充斥著濃郁深色調的室內設計,鼓舞了屋主們嘗試前衛、氛圍濃厚的風格。然而直到最近,這類較深沉的色調大多只出現在自用住宅中,海濱別墅則仍以白色石膏牆、輕盈的藍色調與沙灘中性色為主。如今這種情況正開始改變,愈來愈多濱水住宅開始採用深海軍藍、暴風海洋般的石板灰,或是老船板般的深棕色。

今日焦點

經濟數據:四月美國個人所得與支出數據。財報:好市多、Gap、戴爾科技、加拿大皇家銀行  📰 今日報紙

這是去年在紐澤西州拍攝、預算至少1,000萬美元的電影與電視劇數量,為該州帶來近10億美元的資金挹注——大約是2024年的兩倍。紐澤西州已成為這個陷入困境產業意想不到的一線曙光,原因很簡單:它擁有全美最有效的稅務獎勵計畫。

最後,還有這則……

一場惡質的船會會長之爭,撕裂了這家遊艇俱樂部。
Marisa McArthur是在被告知自己無法成為索薩利托遊艇俱樂部會長之後,才真正意識到自己有多渴望這個職位。從副會長的位置來看,晉升會長本該是理所當然的一步。但當McArthur在提名委員會面前爭取最後的升遷時,這位50歲的女性卻被告知晉升無望。隨之而來的是一場充滿爭議的競選活動、McArthur遭到除名、她的丈夫與母親遭到停權,如今更演變成一樁訴訟案。

✏️ President Trump has cemented his grip on the GOP. But at what cost? In Texas, Ken Paxton clinched the Republican Senate nomination, ousting longtime Sen. John Cornyn after a last-minute Trump endorsement helped to lift the firebrand. Yet Paxton’s win could hand Democrats a rare opening to flip the state.

Meanwhile, in South Dakota, a luxury survivalist community is tearing itself apart . The threat hasn’t come from Armageddon, but from friction that resembles a suburban homeowners’ association battle. Guns have been drawn and there have been offers to settle things with fists.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

The lawyer for the former JPMorgan Chase investment banker who has alleged in a lawsuit that a female colleague sexually assaulted him has exited the case shortly before a court hearing. Cuba’s tourism industry is completely unraveling as fuel shortages and economic turmoil scare away foreign visitors. The U.S. is racing to set up a quarantine facility in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola. Nursing isn’t known for glamour. But traveling nurses, an increasingly popular segment of the profession, are giving the field a surprising allure .
