Anthropic近期開始讓其強大AI模型Mythos的使用者,與可能面臨類似漏洞的其他人分享網路安全威脅資訊。谷歌與黑石集團計畫成立一家AI雲端公司,這是這家科技公司迄今為止向外部客戶銷售其專用晶片的最大嘗試。川普總統表示,應波灣領導人的要求,他將暫緩原訂對伊朗發動的美國攻擊行動。聖地牙哥一座清真寺發生槍擊案,造成三人死亡,當局表示正以仇恨犯罪案件進行調查。代表長島鐵路工人的工會在罷工三天後,與大都會運輸署達成協議。

市場即時看

道瓊工業指數期貨 49623.00(-0.29%);標普500期貨 7387.50(-0.52%);那斯達克100期貨 28860.00(-0.81%),截至美東時間2026年5月19日上午5:57:26。

看看全球政府債務狂潮如何在市場中掀起漣漪。一家鮮為人知的避險基金有望在SpaceX上賺進超過100億美元。這些圖表顯示川普的帳戶一直忙著交易大型科技股。

獨家搶先看

Zyn尼古丁袋在川普陣營中掀起熱潮——連小羅伯特·甘迺迪也不例外。
在川普與菸草業高層最近一次的午餐會上,話題轉向了市場上最熱門商品之一的尼古丁袋。總統打電話給他的衛生部長小羅伯特·甘迺迪,詢問他使用哪種尼古丁袋。據知情人士透露,川普對這項產品產生興趣,並告訴官員他希望看到更多尼古丁袋獲得核准。這種產品在川普政府內部擁有廣大愛好者。就在那次午餐後不久,食品藥物管理局公布了一項新政策,允許更多尼古丁袋上市銷售,即便它們尚未獲得該機構的科學核准,麗茲·艾斯利·懷特、喬許·道西與C·萊恩·巴柏報導。

中國正將基督徒關進監獄,但這位牧師拒絕屈服。
金明日牧師在政府多年的恐嚇下,讓他在北京的教會持續運作——甚至持續成長。如今身陷囹圄,他毫不妥協的信仰依然激勵著信徒。中國領導人習近平已成功運用數位監控與嚴厲刑罰,讓敢於發聲的維權人士、律師與商界領袖噤聲。但他仍無法完全掌控在中國人數達數千萬之眾的基督徒,布萊恩·斯佩傑爾報導。

專家觀點

問:為什麼俄羅斯的戰事進展不順?
馬可斯·沃克與阿娜絲塔西亞·馬蓮科剖析烏克蘭與俄羅斯這場曠日持久衝突的最新進展,以及基輔如何拖慢莫斯科的攻勢。

答:近幾個月來,烏克蘭軍隊已在戰術與技術上取得優勢,幾乎讓規模遠大於己的俄羅斯軍隊陷入停滯。
這個夏天將是一場考驗,看烏克蘭能否將這項微弱的優勢轉化為戰略轉捩點。
快速進步的烏克蘭無人機能力,正打擊入侵者在戰線後方的後勤補給,並猛烈打擊俄羅斯境內更深處的石油基礎設施與軍事目標。
在俄羅斯國內,隨著煉油廠遭到燃燒攻擊、當局又因擔憂異議聲浪而加強網路管制,人們對這場已不再遙遠的戰爭的不滿情緒正持續升高。
許多分析師警告,現在斷言這場自二戰以來歐洲規模最大的戰爭已到達轉捩點,恐怕言之過早。俄羅斯的戰事進展不順——但還不足以逼得普丁總統改變立場。而他至今仍未顯露出放棄征服烏克蘭野心的跡象。
總部設於維也納的軍事分析師、Gady Consulting負責人法蘭茲-史蒂芬·嘉迪表示:「烏克蘭目前的處境無疑比許多人預期的要強。」但他指出,戰爭涉及不斷的適應循環,問題在於俄羅斯能否找到應對烏克蘭進步的辦法。「在戰爭的這個階段,我們實際上只能有把握地展望未來幾週。」

凱西·李·吉福德想以一億美元出售她在康乃狄克州的濱水豪宅。
這位前晨間節目主持人搬到納許維爾後表示,她已準備出售自己與已故丈夫、美式足球名將法蘭克·吉福德共同擁有的格林威治房產。若能以開價成交,這將是康乃狄克州史上售出的最昂貴房產之一。吉福德的房子是一棟建於1930年代左右的地中海風格豪宅,面積超過1.5萬平方英尺,擁有八間臥室,還有泳池、泳池屋、網球場、私人海灘與碼頭。

今日焦點

普丁在川普訪問後幾天內抵達北京。這將是習近平醞釀多年、具分水嶺意義的重要時刻。肯塔基、阿拉巴馬、喬治亞、愛達荷、奧勒岡與賓夕法尼亞州舉行初選。財報:家得寶。

數字看世界

超過1萬美元——部分家庭為取得神經心理學家診斷證明所花費的金額,以此支持申請ACT、SAT等大學入學考試加時的請求。考試時間已成為高中生家長之間一場激烈的角力戰場。多年來,被診斷有身心障礙或醫療問題的學生一直獲准延長作答時間。但申請加時者的人數大幅激增,且集中在富裕地區。許多家長因此憤而抗議這種不公平現象。

最後一則……

「新郎怪獸」來了,手持意見清單與試算表。
這個曾為籠中鴿子到天花板花飾等各種需求創造市場的婚禮產業,終於將目光轉向了男性,提醒準新娘們四個重要的字:這也是他的大日子。這一季,預期會出現「新郎光鮮打扮」(熱毛巾與傳統剃刀刮鬍)、精心編排的新郎步入禮堂儀式、客製化新郎蛋糕、新郎情緒板、新郎專屬禮賓服務,說不定還會有新郎像埃及豔后一樣被人抬著走的場面。

新聞編輯室之外

評論:代理顧問機構Glass Lewis與機構股東服務公司(ISS)故態復萌,重拾對企業施壓的老套手法。本月,這對雙頭壟斷機構加入了紐約市審計長馬克·萊文的行動,試圖阻止艾克森美孚遷往德州。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Apple’s Secret Weapon
emails.contentEn:
Your guide to the WSJ's exclusive reporting and analysis.

The secret weapon behind Apple's popular MacBook Neo isn't a breakthrough piece of tech—it's imperfect chips. We unpack Apple's longstanding strategy for protecting its bottom line, and how it helps the tech giant achieve efficiencies that smaller rivals are struggling to match.

On a separate note: As someone who flies a great deal for work, I know firsthand that a seatmate can make or break your journey. Our team put together a helpful quiz to see if your own flight etiquette is up to par.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

Kevin Warsh wants lower rates. The data might make that impossible for the next Federal Reserve chair to achieve. TSA is experimenting with off-site screening to relieve airport congestion. Kyiv is entering a hopeful spring after surviving the war's darkest winter. Senators are introducing bipartisan legislation that would ban digital gambling ads targeting minors. Meet the mysterious crypto judges who settle Polymarket disputes. President Trump is discussing plans to install a helipad at the White House to prevent powerful new Marine One helicopters from damaging the South Lawn.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

DJIA Futures 49309.00 (-0.62%); S&P 500 Futures 7411.00 (-0.29%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 29200.75 (-0.11%) as of 5/18/2026, 5:59:55 AM ET.

The world can't get enough U.S. energy, keeping prices high for Americans. Pure-play AI investments are inherently risky, but some bets are riskier than others. And one of them—AI cloud player Nebius—has some intriguing upsides, writes Asa Fitch.

READ IT HERE FIRST

Apple is making hit products and high profits from imperfect chips.
Apple has managed to develop a booming business selling cheaper devices when most gadget makers are being hammered by rising costs. One of its secrets: using chips with slight defects. The strategy is apparent in the technical minutiae of the newly released MacBook Neo. Defective cores can be disabled, leaving a chip that still functions perfectly well to power different, often cheaper devices—in this case an entry-level laptop instead of a top-of-the-line iPhone. It's the latest example of Apple deploying a decades-old chip industry strategy to squeeze profits from lesser-performing processors by selling them like eggs, gas, diamonds or hotel rooms, segmented by good, better and best, report Rolfe Winkler and Yang Jie.

Here's how Nicki Minaj became Trump's ‘No.1 fan.'
The rap superstar has embraced a new status atop MAGA's A-list. What appears on the surface to be an unlikely relationship between the president and a star who once opposed some of his policies is in fact an outgrowth of a calculated effort to lure cultural heavyweights away from the Democratic Party, report Erich Schwartzel, Josh Dawsey and Maggie Severns. Minaj found a conduit to MAGA through one of the president's strongest young allies, a 29-year-old former campaign staffer named Alex Bruesewitz who scouts stars and influencers who back Trump. The 43-year-old is joining the cause at the height of her fame. Minaj's support, says Bruesewitz, equals “a big cultural victory for Republicans.”

EXPERT TAKE

Q: Is the weight-loss drug revolution causing a frailty epidemic?
As millions flock to GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic, Mounjaro and Zepbound, doctors warn the drugs can cause rapid and significant muscle loss. Natasha Dangoor reports:

A: GLP-1 drugs have been a success for public health and the pharmaceutical companies that make them. Taking them has improved health and happiness for millions of people. But for at least some of the 13 million Americans who use the drugs, losing muscle along with fat is an unexpected downside that isn't broadly discussed or immediately apparent.
The drugs can cause rapid and significant loss of lean muscle mass, up to 10%, comparable to a decade or more of aging, according to an analysis published by the American Diabetes Association.
The loss of lean tissue is similar to weight loss from dieting, but the magnitude over a short period can lead to frailty, instability and lack of coordination, doctors and researchers say. Another concern is that losing muscle could slow down patients' metabolism, leading to weight regain.
Drugmakers say weight-loss drugs should be taken only on the advice of a physician and as part of a long-term plan that includes diet and exercise.

We cataloged the secret memos, frantic texts and juicy confessions from the OpenAI-Musk trial.
For three weeks, the characters in the epic human saga about the past, present and future of OpenAI gathered in a federal courthouse, took the stand and swore to tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. Now a jury has to figure out what to make of it. We sifted through all the evidence and testimony to find out how a bunch of people who set out to build the world's most powerful technology for the benefit of humanity ended up fighting in a courtroom about money.

HAPPENING TODAY

Earnings: Baidu.

THE NUMBER

69% — The explosion in master's degree programs between 2005 and 2021, according to a report published by the Postsecondary Education and Economics Research Center. While grad school has long been the Plan B of young professionals, new data show that getting a master's degree isn't the guarantee it used to be. Master's degree holders under 35 are at the 77th percentile of unemployment, where the 50th percentile is normal, according to the Burning Glass Institute. Even associate-degree holders have had a higher employment level for the past year.

AND FINALLY...

Do you know how to behave on a flight? Take our quiz.
The Transportation Department started a campaign last fall to encourage better behavior on airplanes. So we're asking the hard questions. What kind of flier are you?

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

Opinion: Old, failed ideas have a way of appealing to young, naive people.
emails.contentZh:
為您導覽《華爾街日報》的獨家報導與分析。

蘋果熱門的MacBook Neo背後的秘密武器,並非什麼突破性的新技術——而是「不完美的晶片」。我們深入剖析蘋果長期以來用來保護獲利的策略,以及這如何幫助這家科技巨頭實現規模較小的對手難以企及的效率。

另外一則:身為經常因工作而搭機飛行的人,我親身體會到鄰座乘客可能成就、也可能毀掉一趟旅程。我們的團隊製作了一份實用測驗,看看您自己的飛行禮儀是否合格。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

凱文·沃許希望降息。但數據可能讓下一任聯準會主席難以如願。運輸安全管理局正試行場外安檢,以紓解機場壅塞。基輔在挺過這場戰爭最黑暗的冬天後,正迎來一個充滿希望的春天。參議員們正提出兩黨支持的立法,禁止針對未成年人投放數位賭博廣告。認識那些為Polymarket糾紛做出裁決的神秘加密貨幣裁判。川普總統正討論在白宮設置直升機停機坪的計畫,以防止強大的新款海軍陸戰隊一號直升機損壞南草坪。

市場即時看

道瓊工業指數期貨 49309.00(-0.62%);標普500期貨 7411.00(-0.29%);那斯達克100期貨 29200.75(-0.11%),截至美東時間2026年5月18日上午5:59:55。

全球對美國能源的需求似乎永無止境,讓美國人持續承受高價之苦。純AI題材投資本質上就有風險,但有些押注比其他更具風險。其中之一——AI雲端業者Nebius——則有一些頗具吸引力的潛在上檔空間,阿薩·菲奇寫道。

獨家搶先看

蘋果靠著不完美的晶片,打造出暢銷產品與豐厚利潤。
在大多數電子產品製造商因成本上漲而備受打擊之際,蘋果卻成功打造出一項銷售平價設備的蓬勃業務。其秘訣之一:使用帶有些微瑕疵的晶片。這項策略在新推出的MacBook Neo技術細節中表露無遺。有瑕疵的核心可以被停用,留下依然運作良好的晶片,用來驅動不同、通常也更便宜的裝置——在這個案例中,是一款入門款筆電,而非頂級iPhone。這是蘋果運用晶片業數十年來慣用策略的最新案例——透過像雞蛋、汽油、鑽石或飯店房型那樣分成「優、良、佳」等級,從表現較差的處理器身上榨取利潤,羅爾夫·溫克勒與楊傑報導。

妮姬·米娜杰如何成為川普的「頭號粉絲」。
這位饒舌天后已在MAGA陣營的名人榜上晉升到全新地位。表面上看來,這位總統與一位曾反對他部分政策的明星之間看似不太可能的關係,實際上是一項精心策劃、意在從民主黨手中拉攏文化重量級人物行動的成果,艾瑞克·施瓦策爾、喬許·道西與瑪姬·塞文斯報導。米娜杰是透過總統最有力的年輕盟友之一——29歲、曾任競選幕僚的亞歷克斯·布魯塞維茨——找到通往MAGA的門路,此人負責物色支持川普的明星與網紅。這位43歲的巨星正在她聲勢最高峰之際加入這項陣營。布魯塞維茨表示,米娜杰的支持等同於「共和黨的一大文化勝利」。

專家觀點

問:減重藥物革命正引發一場「衰弱症」流行病嗎?
隨著數百萬人蜂擁使用Ozempic、Mounjaro與Zepbound等GLP-1藥物,醫師警告這類藥物可能導致快速且顯著的肌肉流失。娜塔莎·丹古爾報導:

答:GLP-1藥物對公共衛生以及生產這些藥物的製藥公司而言都是一大成功。服用這些藥物已改善了數百萬人的健康與幸福感。但對於使用這些藥物的1300萬美國人中,至少有一部分人來說,肌肉隨脂肪一同流失,是一個未被廣泛討論、也不會立即顯現的意外副作用。
根據美國糖尿病協會發表的一項分析,這類藥物可能導致精瘦肌肉量快速且顯著地流失,幅度最高可達10%,相當於十年甚至更長時間的自然老化程度。
醫師與研究人員表示,精瘦組織的流失與節食減重類似,但在短時間內達到如此大的幅度,可能導致衰弱、不穩定與協調能力不足。另一項疑慮是,肌肉流失可能減緩患者的新陳代謝,導致體重反彈。
藥廠表示,減重藥物應僅在醫師指示下服用,並作為包含飲食與運動的長期計畫的一部分。

我們整理了OpenAI-馬斯克官司中的秘密備忘錄、慌亂簡訊與勁爆自白。
三週以來,這場關於OpenAI過去、現在與未來的史詩級人性大戲中的各方人物齊聚聯邦法院,登上證人席宣誓將說出真相、完整的真相、絕無虛假。如今陪審團必須釐清該如何看待這一切。我們梳理了所有證據與證詞,試圖弄清楚:這群原本立志打造造福人類的全球最強大科技的人,最終為何淪落到在法庭上為錢對簿公堂。

今日焦點

財報:百度。

數字看世界

69%——根據高等教育與經濟研究中心發布的報告,這是2005年至2021年間碩士學位課程數量的爆炸性成長幅度。儘管讀研究所長期以來一直是年輕專業人士的B計畫,但新數據顯示,取得碩士學位已不再像過去那樣是一種保障。根據Burning Glass研究院的數據,35歲以下碩士學位持有者的失業率落在第77百分位,而正常水準應為第50百分位。就連副學士學位持有者,過去一年的就業水準都高於他們。

最後一則……

您知道搭機該如何舉止得宜嗎?來做我們的測驗。
美國運輸部去年秋天啟動一項活動,鼓勵乘客在飛機上表現得更得體。因此我們要問一些尖銳的問題:您是哪一種類型的乘客?

新聞編輯室之外

評論:陳舊、失敗的思想總有辦法吸引年輕、天真的人們。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Suspicious Betting in Washington
emails.contentEn:
Your guide to the WSJ's exclusive reporting and analysis.

Insider traders have long looked to Wall Street for information. Now they're also turning to Washington. The rise of prediction markets has created a new temptation in the nation's capital, where the Trump administration's fast-moving agenda is giving those privy to government information a chance to cash in on the volatility. Regulators are playing catch-up.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

Suspicious betting in Washington is on the rise, and regulators are seeking information from Kalshi and Polymarket over wagers tied to political events and military operations. Sen. Bill Cassidy's run for re-election was cut short as voters heeded President Trump's call to oust the Louisiana Republican, with the incumbent expected to finish third in the GOP primary. Iran's seizure of a support vessel owned by a Chinese security firm near the Strait of Hormuz appeared to signal unwillingness to permit armed protection near its shore even for ships sailing on behalf of its strongest global backer. Israel killed Hamas's military leader in Gaza, eliminating a long-sought target linked to the Oct. 7 attacks despite a continuing cease-fire. The collapse of Spirit Airlines has set off a dash by rivals like Breeze and Allegiant, who are moving into its former routes. Amazon has quickly gone from an AI also-ran to a real contender, thanks to $200 billion in spending, custom chips and savvy deals, writes Tim Higgins.

FROM THE MARKETS

Coal is making a comeback as countries return to the polluting but reliable source of power after the Iran war effectively shut the Strait of Hormuz. Investing in AI involves a strong belief that it's different this time, and memory-chip makers are a particularly extreme example, writes James Mackintosh.

READ IT HERE FIRST

The world is awash in bourbon. That's a problem for big distillers.
On Jim Beam's campus near Louisville, Ky., warehouses are packed with barrels of liquor that may not have buyers, reports Laura Cooper. Since January, the brand's 65-foot-tall still has been on a break—a pause slated to last until at least 2027. Kentucky distilleries of all sizes have laid off staff or shut down. Even barrel suppliers are hurting. Most industry players didn't see the slump coming: Distillers added capacity during the pandemic as people stocked their bar carts. But now, as drinkers pinch pennies and become sober-curious, Jim Beam is trialing zero-alcohol drinks—the first time an alcohol-free product has carried its brand since Prohibition.

The World Cup's biggest grudge match: FIFA vs. the state of New Jersey.
Soccer's global governing body will stage eight World Cup matches—including the final—at the Garden State's MetLife Stadium. But just as the extravaganza is set to kick off, many New Jerseyans are viewing their hosting duties less as an honor and more as a costly burden they could do without, reports Joshua Chaffin. The clash between FIFA and New Jersey features the familiar rage of this populist era—namely, a public beaten down by rising costs snarling at global elites. It's fodder for the debate about the economic merits of hosting big sporting events.

EXPERT TAKE

Q: Tax-loss harvesting is the hottest thing on Wall Street. How does it work?
The stock-market surge has helped popularize a new strategy to secure gains without all the taxes. Reporter Miriam Gottfried broke it down.

A: With the stock market near record highs, it isn't enough to be winning anymore. Wealthy investors are now obsessed with losing, too. The hottest investment on Wall Street promises a magical-sounding mix of both: index-beating performance that also comes with losses to offset capital-gains taxes.
Millions of investors are sitting on big gains in concentrated stockholdings, be they shares of Magnificent Seven tech giants, plain-vanilla index funds or employee shares of hot tech companies.
The traditional move would be to turn to direct indexing, a form of tax-loss harvesting that has been an investing mainstay since the early 2000s. There is now $1.1 trillion invested in that strategy, according to research firm Cerulli Associates.
But for many investors who have ridden this ebullient stock market, direct indexing is no longer generating the losses it once did. So financial advisers are trying to turn up more losses for their clients by employing strategies that use leverage. Over $150 billion has flowed into this newer breed of tax-loss harvesting, known as long-short tax-aware, or tax-aware alpha, according to Brent Sullivan, who writes about the industry on his Substack, Tax Alpha Insider.
The strategy comes with some risks for investors.

Thomas Massie's fight against Trump is lonely and expensive.
The seven-term Republican Kentucky congressman—who has gained a following by bucking the president—will find out Tuesday whether his career can withstand Trump's opposition. The outcome will also signal whether Republicans are willing to adopt a form of MAGA politics that embraces leaders who break with Trump.

HAPPENING THIS WEEK

Tuesday: Primaries in Kentucky, Alabama, Georgia, Idaho, Oregon and Pennsylvania. SpaceX has scheduled a highly anticipated test flight of SpaceX's Starship rocket. Wednesday: The Fed will release the minutes from its April meeting, which could give clues on the outlook for interest rates. Nvidia reports earnings. Thursday: Stephen Colbert's final “Late Show.” Friday: “Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu” arrives in movie theaters, starring Pedro Pascal, Jeremy Allen White and Sigourney Weaver.

THE NUMBER

$45 billion — About how much more Americans have cumulatively spent on gasoline and diesel during the war with Iran than they did during the same period a year ago, according to an analysis of OPIS pricing data and federal demand figures. The surging costs are eating an outsize share of low- and middle-income consumers' paychecks, darkening their outlook relative to the well-off.

AND FINALLY...

This veterinarian's career took off when she started doing acupuncture for pets.
After discovering the treatment a decade ago, Dr. Kristen Miller eventually left Western medicine behind to launch a mobile practice sticking needles in dogs and cats. She charges up to $500 for house calls and now has a wait list. Depending on your point of view, she's either at the forefront of a promising medical specialty or a practitioner of a pseudoscience being propped up by humans who will do anything for their pets.
emails.contentZh:
為您導覽《華爾街日報》的獨家報導與分析。

內線交易者長期以來一直向華爾街尋求資訊。如今他們也把目光轉向了華府。預測市場的興起在美國首都催生了一種新誘惑——川普政府快速變動的施政議程,讓那些得知政府內幕消息的人有機會從波動中獲利。監管機構正在急起直追。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

華府的可疑下注活動正在增加,監管機構正向Kalshi與Polymarket索取與政治事件及軍事行動相關賭注的資訊。參議員比爾·卡西迪的連任之路提前告終,選民響應川普總統將這位路易斯安那州共和黨人拉下馬的號召,這位現任者預計將在共和黨初選中排名第三。伊朗在荷姆茲海峽附近扣押一艘中國安全公司所屬的支援船隻,似乎顯示即便是代表其最強大全球靠山航行的船隻,伊朗也不願讓武裝護衛靠近其海岸。以色列在加薩擊斃哈瑪斯軍事領袖,消滅了一個與10月7日攻擊事件有關、長期追捕的目標,儘管停火協議仍在持續。西南航空Spirit Airlines的倒閉引發了Breeze與Allegiant等競爭對手爭相搶進其原有航線。得益於2000億美元的支出、客製化晶片與精明的交易,亞馬遜已迅速從AI領域的邊緣角色躍升為真正的競爭者,提姆·希金斯寫道。

市場動態

隨著伊朗戰爭實質上封鎖了荷姆茲海峽,各國紛紛重回燃煤這種污染但可靠的能源,煤炭正捲土重來。投資AI需要堅信「這次真的不一樣」,記憶體晶片製造商正是這種信念特別極端的例子,詹姆斯·麥金塔許寫道。

獨家搶先看

全球波本威士忌氾濫成災。這對大型蒸餾廠來說是個問題。
在肯塔基州路易維爾附近的金賓廠區,倉庫裡堆滿了可能找不到買家的酒桶,蘿拉·庫柏報導。自一月以來,這個品牌高達65英尺的蒸餾器一直處於停工狀態——這次停工預計至少持續到2027年。肯塔基州各種規模的酒廠都已裁員或歇業。就連酒桶供應商也受到波及。大多數業界人士都沒料到這波低迷:蒸餾廠在疫情期間曾增加產能,因為當時人們紛紛囤積家用酒櫃。但如今,隨著飲酒者精打細算、開始嘗試少喝酒,金賓正在試銷零酒精飲品——這是自禁酒令以來,該品牌首次推出無酒精產品。

世界盃最大的恩怨對決:國際足聯vs.紐澤西州。
國際足球總會將在花園之州的大都會人壽體育場舉辦八場世界盃賽事——包括決賽。但就在這場盛會即將開踢之際,許多紐澤西人卻不太把主辦資格視為榮耀,反而更視之為一項可有可無、代價高昂的負擔,約書亞·查芬報導。國際足聯與紐澤西州之間的衝突,呈現出這個民粹主義時代熟悉的怒火——即被生活成本上漲壓得喘不過氣的民眾,對全球菁英怒目相向。這也為關於主辦大型體育賽事經濟效益的辯論提供了新的素材。

專家觀點

問:「稅損收割」是華爾街最熱門的話題。它是怎麼運作的?
股市飆漲讓一種既能鎖定獲利、又不必繳一堆稅的新策略廣受歡迎。記者米里安·戈弗里德為您解析。

答:在股市逼近歷史新高之際,光是「贏」已經不夠了。富裕投資人如今也對「輸」深深著迷。華爾街最熱門的投資標的,承諾了聽起來像魔法般的雙重效果:跑贏指數的績效,同時又帶來能抵銷資本利得稅的虧損。
數百萬投資人手握集中持股的龐大未實現獲利,無論是七大科技巨頭的股票、普通的指數型基金,還是熱門科技公司的員工股票皆然。
傳統做法是採用「直接指數化」,這是一種自2000年代初期以來就是投資主流的稅損收割形式。根據研究機構Cerulli Associates的數據,目前已有1.1兆美元資金投入這項策略。
但對許多搭上這波狂熱股市順風車的投資人來說,直接指數化已不再像過去那樣能製造出虧損。因此,理財顧問正嘗試透過運用槓桿的策略,為客戶製造出更多虧損。根據在其Substack專欄「Tax Alpha Insider」撰寫相關產業文章的布蘭特·蘇利文表示,已有超過1500億美元資金流入這種被稱為「多空稅務意識」或「稅務阿爾法」的新型稅損收割策略。
這項策略對投資人而言存在一定風險。

湯瑪斯·馬西對抗川普的戰鬥,孤獨且代價高昂。
這位七度連任的肯塔基州共和黨眾議員——因敢於違逆總統而贏得一批支持者——週二將會知曉,他的政治生涯能否禁得起川普的反對。這個結果也將顯示,共和黨人是否願意接納一種容許領導者與川普唱反調的MAGA政治型態。

本週焦點

星期二:肯塔基、阿拉巴馬、喬治亞、愛達荷、奧勒岡與賓夕法尼亞州舉行初選。SpaceX已排定備受矚目的星艦火箭試飛。星期三:聯準會將公布4月會議紀要,可能透露利率前景的線索。輝達公布財報。星期四:史蒂芬·科拜爾最後一集《深夜秀》播出。星期五:《星際大戰:曼達洛人與古古》上映,由佩德羅·帕斯卡、傑瑞米·艾倫·懷特與雪歌妮·薇佛主演。

數字看世界

450億美元——根據對OPIS定價數據與聯邦需求數據的分析,這是美國人在與伊朗開戰期間,相較於去年同期在汽油與柴油上累計多支出的金額。飆升的成本正吞噬中低收入消費者薪資中不成比例的一大部分,使他們相對於富裕階層的經濟前景更加黯淡。

最後一則……

這位獸醫的職涯,在她開始為寵物施行針灸後起飛。
十年前發現這項療法後,克莉絲汀·米勒醫師最終告別了西醫,開設了一間為狗貓扎針的行動診所。她的到府看診收費最高達500美元,如今已累積了候診名單。端看您的觀點而定,她要不是一項前景看好的醫學專科的先驅,就是一種偽科學的執業者,靠著願意為寵物付出一切的人們撐腰。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Inside AI’s Biggest Breakup
emails.contentEn:
Your guide to the WSJ's exclusive reporting and analysis.

Things got messy in the courtroom showdown over AI's biggest breakup. The three-week trial was technically about Elon Musk's allegations that he was snookered into fronting OpenAI millions. But the proceedings also revealed the mythmaking behind the AI industry—and exposed the financial anxieties, short tempers and personal vendettas that have shaped it. Musk has pushed for Sam Altman's removal as CEO, among other things. The changes he's pursuing would greatly complicate OpenAI's path to a potential IPO.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

Ahead of the midterms, President Trump's allies are counting on an unprecedented $347 million from a Trump-aligned political committee to flip the economy on Democrats. The titanic trial between Musk and Altman's OpenAI has revealed many of the personal and financial fault lines beneath Silicon Valley's AI boom. Former Energy Secretary Rick Perry and Texas energy billionaire Toby Neugebauer are in a bitter showdown over Fermi, an energy company they co-founded whose shares have plunged about 80% from their public debut. U.S. and Nigerian forces killed Islamic State's alleged No. 2, a man linked to terrorist attacks against religious minorities and the kidnapping of schoolchildren. JPMorgan Chase already faced a scandal after an ex-employee filed a sexual assault lawsuit, but AI-generated “deepfakes” have made the problem worse.

FROM THE MARKETS

Bond yields climbed sharply on Friday, sapping investors' appetite for stocks amid fears that an extended Middle East impasse will worsen inflation. SpaceX is aiming to go public on June 12, setting the stage for what is expected to be the biggest IPO of all time. It sounds like the investment opportunity of a lifetime: getting in on one of the hottest names on Wall Street, before its stock even starts trading. Financial advisers say buyer beware. Business-development companies are more complex than they seem, making discounts less attractive, Telis Demos writes.

READ IT HERE FIRST

Secret U.A.E. and Saudi Arabian strikes on Iran shattered an uneasy coexistence.
Both Gulf states carried out multiple strikes against the regime after they were attacked in the early days of the war, showing the depth of their involvement in the conflict and how much the region's geopolitics have been transformed, report Jared Malsin, Summer Said and Shelby Holliday. Before the war, such strikes would have been unthinkable. The U.A.E. and Saudi Arabia are now trying to re-establish deterrence against an Iranian regime that's less willing to compromise and holds new leverage with the Strait of Hormuz. Both the Pentagon and the Saudi Embassy in Washington declined to comment.

The U.S. is zeroing in on Cuban revolutionary patriarch Raúl Castro.
Though the 94-year-old holds no formal government office and is rarely seen in public, the younger of the two brothers who led the Cuban revolution still has the final say on the country's most important matters. Now, the Trump administration intends to prosecute Castro, shifting its pressure campaign from broad sanctions toward accountability for a man who symbolizes the Communist regime. Federal prosecutors have been working to secure an indictment against Castro, and could announce a criminal case as soon as next week, report José de Córdoba, Sadie Gurman and Vera Bergengruen.

EXPERT TAKE

Q: The global oil map is being redrawn. Who are the winners and losers?
Disruptions from the war in Iran are rewriting the geopolitics of energy everywhere. Jason Bordoff, a professor at Columbia University and the founding director of the Center on Global Energy Policy, breaks down how the global fault lines are shifting.

A: The crisis in the Strait of Hormuz is forcing governments to redefine energy security for an age of geopolitical fragmentation—one in which resilience depends not only on how much oil the world produces, but also where it flows, who can get it and which countries are able to absorb the shock when it's interrupted.
But while the oil market is global and rising costs are felt everywhere, the consequences are not evenly distributed.
Asia has been hit first and hardest. Last year, the region relied on the Middle East for roughly 60% of its imported oil. The disruption has been particularly severe not just for crude but for refined products like diesel and jet fuel, which have doubled in price since January.
In wealthier countries, pricier oil generally shows up first as inflation and weaker growth. In lower-income importing countries, it manifests as shortages: Bangladesh has limited air conditioning to 77 degrees. Laos has shortened its school week and Sri Lanka made Wednesday a public holiday. In Pakistan, cricket teams are playing to empty stadiums.
So far, shale production has shielded the U.S. But the most consequential effects of the crisis may not be the immediate price spikes around the world but the strategic policy shifts they prompt.
Just as nations dramatically rethought energy policy after the oil crises of the 1970s, a disruption of this scale will force governments around the world to adapt.

See how China is gaining power in contested waters.
Chinese fishing vessels pushed within 150 miles of a U.S. naval base in Japan last month, the latest advance in a decadeslong campaign. Beijing officials often claim these fleets are normal fishing boats. A spokesman for the Chinese Embassy in Washington said that China's navy, coast guard and fishing boats operate “in strict accordance” with domestic and international law. Yet the strategy poses a growing challenge for the U.S. in the Pacific, as the Trump administration stretches military resources across the Middle East, Latin America and the world.

HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

Saturday: The final of the Eurovision Song Contest, which five countries have chosen to boycott over Israel's inclusion—here's how the competition became a soft-power play. Sunday: The final round of the PGA Championship.

THE NUMBER

19% — How much Cadillac's EV sales jumped in the first quarter of 2026—against a decline of 27% in the overall EV market, year-over. Sales of the Cadillac Optiq grew by 65% in the quarter. WSJ's Dan Neil tested out the midsize SUV—and found it agreeably nimble and responsive.

AND FINALLY...

Is the secret to men's longevity a great butt?
Walk into any high-end gym right now and it will be hard not to spot men training their glutes. Equinox says male bookings of its “Best Butt Ever” class have increased 17% since 2024. Men who train with the Whoop app have doubled their booty exercises over the past 24 months, according to the company. For the man who wants to live forever, the body's largest muscle group is increasingly understood to be the foundation of physical strength and well-being.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

Opinion: The Trump Administration said this week it will pause $1.3 billion in Medicaid payments to California over fraud concerns. Maybe some facts can help sort reality from demagoguery.
emails.contentZh:
為您導覽《華爾街日報》的獨家報導與分析。

AI界最大分手案的法庭攻防戰,場面變得相當混亂。這場為期三週的審判,表面上是關於伊隆·馬斯克指控自己被騙、出資數百萬美元資助OpenAI的訴訟。但這場審理過程也揭露了AI產業背後的造神運動——並暴露出形塑這個產業的財務焦慮、暴躁脾氣與私人恩怨。馬斯克曾力推撤換執行長山姆·奧特曼等要求。他所追求的變革,將大幅複雜化OpenAI通往潛在IPO的道路。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

在期中選舉前夕,川普總統的盟友正指望一個親川普政治委員會提供空前的3.47億美元資金,扭轉民眾對民主黨的經濟觀感。馬斯克與奧特曼領導的OpenAI之間這場驚天官司,揭露了矽谷AI熱潮底下許多個人與財務層面的裂痕。前能源部長瑞克·佩里與德州能源億萬富豪托比·紐格鮑爾,正為兩人共同創立、股價自上市以來已重挫約80%的能源公司Fermi爆發激烈爭執。美國與奈及利亞部隊擊斃了據稱是伊斯蘭國二號人物的男子,此人與針對宗教少數群體的恐怖攻擊及綁架學童事件有關。摩根大通此前已因一名前員工提起性侵訴訟而陷入醜聞,如今AI生成的「深偽」影像更讓問題雪上加霜。

市場動態

週五公債殖利率大幅攀升,削弱了投資人對股票的胃口,原因是擔憂中東僵局延續將惡化通膨。SpaceX目標於6月12日上市,為預計將創下史上最大規模的IPO鋪路。這聽起來像是千載難逢的投資機會:搶在股票尚未開始交易前,就參與這個華爾街最炙手可熱的標的之一。但理財顧問提醒買家務必謹慎。企業開發公司(BDC)遠比表面看起來複雜,這讓折價交易的吸引力大打折扣,泰利斯·德莫斯寫道。

獨家搶先看

阿聯與沙烏地阿拉伯對伊朗的秘密打擊,粉碎了雙方原本脆弱的共處關係。
這兩個波灣國家在戰爭初期遭到攻擊後,對政權發動了多次打擊,顯示它們涉入這場衝突之深,也顯示該地區地緣政治已發生多大的轉變,賈瑞德·馬爾辛、桑瑪·賽義德與雪碧·哈勒戴報導。在戰爭爆發前,這類打擊本是難以想像之事。阿聯與沙烏地阿拉伯如今正試圖重建對一個較不願妥協、且因掌控荷姆茲海峽而握有新籌碼的伊朗政權的嚇阻力。五角大廈與沙國駐華府大使館均拒絕置評。

美國正將矛頭瞄準古巴革命元老勞爾·卡斯楚。
儘管這位94歲老人並無正式政府職務,也鮮少公開露面,但這位領導古巴革命的兄弟中較年輕的一位,對該國最重要事務仍擁有最終決定權。如今,川普政府打算起訴卡斯楚,將其施壓行動從全面制裁轉向追究這位共產政權象徵人物的責任。聯邦檢察官一直在爭取對卡斯楚提起公訴,最快可能在下週宣布這起刑事案件,荷西·德科爾多瓦、賽蒂·葛曼與維拉·貝根格倫報導。

專家觀點

問:全球石油版圖正被重新繪製。誰是贏家,誰是輸家?
伊朗戰爭造成的動盪,正重寫全球各地的能源地緣政治。哥倫比亞大學教授、全球能源政策中心創始主任傑森·博多夫,為您剖析全球斷層線的變化。

答:荷姆茲海峽危機正迫使各國政府為地緣政治碎片化的時代重新定義能源安全——在這個時代,韌性不僅取決於全球產油量,還取決於石油流向何處、誰能取得,以及當供應中斷時,哪些國家能夠承受衝擊。
然而,儘管石油市場是全球性的、成本上漲也是各地都能感受到的,但後果的分佈並不均等。
亞洲首當其衝、受創最深。去年,該地區進口石油約六成仰賴中東供應。這場動盪對原油以及柴油、航空燃油等精煉產品的衝擊尤其嚴重,這些產品自一月以來價格已翻倍。
在較富裕的國家,油價上漲通常首先表現為通膨與經濟成長放緩。在收入較低的進口國,則表現為短缺:孟加拉已將空調限溫在攝氏25度。寮國縮短了上學週,斯里蘭卡則將週三訂為公眾假日。在巴基斯坦,板球隊只能在空蕩的體育場比賽。
目前為止,頁岩油生產讓美國得以倖免。但這場危機最重大的影響,或許不在於全球各地立即出現的油價飆升,而在於這些飆升所催生的戰略性政策轉變。
正如各國在1970年代石油危機後大幅重新思考能源政策,如此規模的動盪也將迫使全球各國政府做出調適。

看看中國如何在有爭議的海域擴大影響力。
上個月,中國漁船逼近至距離美軍駐日海軍基地150英里範圍內,這是一場持續數十年行動的最新進展。北京官員經常宣稱這些船隊只是普通漁船。中國駐華府大使館發言人表示,中國的海軍、海警與漁船均「嚴格依照」國內與國際法運作。然而,隨著川普政府將軍事資源分散至中東、拉丁美洲與全球各地,這項策略正對美國在太平洋地區構成日益嚴峻的挑戰。

本週末看點

星期六:歐洲歌唱大賽決賽,五個國家已選擇因以色列參賽而抵制——以下是這項賽事如何演變成一場軟實力較量。星期日:PGA錦標賽決賽輪。

數字看世界

19%——凱迪拉克電動車銷量在2026年第一季的成長幅度——相較之下,整體電動車市場年減27%。凱迪拉克Optiq車型該季銷量成長65%。《華爾街日報》的丹·尼爾試駕了這款中型休旅車,認為它靈活度與反應性都相當令人滿意。

最後一則……

男性長壽的秘訣是擁有一副好臀部嗎?
現在走進任何一間高檔健身房,幾乎不可能沒注意到男性正在鍛鍊臀肌。Equinox表示,自2024年以來,男性預約「史上最強臀部」課程的人數已增加17%。根據Whoop這家公司的數據,使用其App訓練的男性,過去24個月臀部訓練量已翻倍。對於想要長生不老的男性而言,人體最大的肌肉群正日益被視為體能與健康的基礎。

新聞編輯室之外

評論:川普政府本週表示,將因詐欺疑慮暫停支付加州13億美元的醫療補助款(Medicaid)。或許一些事實有助於釐清現實與煽動言論之間的差異。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Trump’s High-Stakes China Visit
emails.contentEn:
Your guide to the WSJ's exclusive reporting and analysis.

Good morning. While Washington slept, President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping shared a final cup of tea to wrap their high-stakes summit. So, where do the two superpower leaders stand? Both sides hailed a reset in relations—though each has a starkly different idea of what that means. For Trump, it is about opening China's market to American business and reciprocal trade. Xi, meanwhile, wants “strategic stability,” a predictable relationship in which Washington doesn't impede Beijing's economic and geopolitical rise. Under the surface, however, there remains an intense rivalry that holds the potential to disrupt the world stage.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

Trump and Xi's tightly choreographed summit masks big differences between the U.S. and China. CIA Director John Ratcliffe made a rare visit to Havana to meet with Cuban officials as the Communist regime struggles to contain widespread blackouts and mounting social unrest. Yale University's medical school discriminated against white and Asian applicants, a Justice Department investigation found. The world is burning through its oil safety net during the Iran war. Markwayne Mullin, the new boss at DHS, is trying to clean house after Kristi Noem. EVs are suddenly the hottest used-car option—and the most affordable in total cost of ownership, writes Christopher Mims.

Honda's never faced a crisis like this—and a comeback won't be easy. The blockbuster Cerebras IPO is a huge bet on Nvidia fatigue, writes Dan Gallagher.

READ IT HERE FIRST

Southern Poverty Law Center got rich opposing Trump. Now he's trying to crush it.
Trump in his first term proved a windfall for the Southern Poverty Law Center, the antiracism nonprofit famed for its courtroom wins against the Ku Klux Klan decades ago. In 2017, the same year Trump took office and a white-nationalist rally in Charlottesville, Va., turned violent, annual contributions and grants to SPLC surged from $50 million to more than $130 million and have remained above $100 million nearly every year since. The stepped-up contributions have swelled the group's net assets to $787 million, according to SPLC's most recent financial filing. Now, the Trump administration and the Charlottesville rally are at the center of an indictment that threatens SPLC's reputation and finances, report Cameron McWhirter, Mark Maremont and Sadie Gurman.

Miami is getting much wealthier. It's also getting smaller.
Miami is booming, with waves of affluent people drawn to the metro area in recent years. Yet there is a countercurrent: Its population is shrinking. The result is a glittering urban center that is richer, smaller and built to cater to upscale living. Gone are the gritty warehouse districts, the nocturnal desolation of downtown and the shabby chic of South Beach. It is now a sophisticated, cosmopolitan hub with gleaming Cartier boutiques, avant-garde art installations and luxury districts dotted with Michelin-star restaurants. The new economic order is squeezing out the middle, reports Arian Campo-Flores.

EXPERT TAKE

Q: Are you eligible for a Covid-era loophole tax refund? Here's what to know.
Taxpayers could get money back from the IRS if they paid interest or penalties during the pandemic, explains Laura Saunders.

A: Millions of Americans could be owed billions of dollars in tax refunds of Covid-era interest and penalties due to a federal court decision.
A few months ago, a judge ruled in a case involving an individual that taxpayers didn't owe certain interest and penalties between early 2020 and mid-2023, even if the IRS imposed them. In effect, the decision turned off the consequences of failing to meet many tax deadlines during the pandemic.
As a result, filers can request refunds of certain payments and seek abatements of penalties and interest assessed but not yet paid.
Note: The IRS is expected to appeal the federal court decision. If the agency wins, these favorable treatments may not apply.
The decision applies to tax underpayments such as estimated taxes; interest on deficiencies determined on audit; and possibly interest that accrued regardless of when the liability occurred. It also applies to penalties for failure to file or pay taxes by certain deadlines (like April 15), and penalties for late filings of international information forms.
To be eligible for refunds and other favorable treatment, however, filers need to send paperwork to the IRS by July 10.

These are the big moments and key people on Trump's second state visit to China.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping staged a grand welcome for President Trump in Beijing this week, the first U.S. presidential visit to China in nearly nine years. The summit projected an air of friendship between the world's two most powerful nations, even as tensions simmer over trade, technology and geopolitical influence.

HAPPENING TODAY

Jerome Powell's term as Fed chair comes to an end. Earnings: Mizuho Financial, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial.

THE NUMBER

>$1.5 billion — The estimated value of art New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art will inherit once it merges with the Neue Galerie, cosmetics billionaire Ronald Lauder's esteemed collection of German and Austrian art. The Met said it will assume ownership and operation of Lauder's 25-year-old museum in 2028.

AND FINALLY...

A pro gambler and a secret database turned a 150-1 long shot into a soccer miracle. Here's how.
Last summer, professional gambler Tony Bloom spent $13 million to buy a stake in a team called Heart of Midlothian, betting that he could turn Scottish soccer on its head. The play was more than just obscure. Backing anyone but either of the Glasgow giants, Celtic or Rangers, is riskier than consuming week-old haggis. Those two clubs have won every Scottish league title since 1986. Just one year since Bloom's arrival, however, Hearts could bring one of the longest streaks in sports to an end.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

Opinion: Chinese President Xi Jinping offers a Greek-veiled warning to President Trump on Taiwan. But Mr. Xi might fall into his own trap if he thinks the U.S. really is in decline enough to risk a war.

為您導覽《華爾街日報》的獨家報導與分析。

早安。趁著華府沉睡之際,川普總統與中國領導人習近平共飲了最後一杯茶,為這場高風險峰會畫下句點。那麼,這兩位超級大國領袖目前的立場為何?雙方都宣稱關係迎來「重置」——儘管彼此對此的定義卻大相逕庭。對川普而言,這意味著讓中國市場對美國企業開放,並實現對等貿易。而對習近平來說,他想要的是「戰略穩定」——一種讓華府不阻礙北京經濟與地緣政治崛起的可預測關係。然而在表面之下,依然存在著一種可能擾亂世界舞台的激烈競爭關係。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

川普與習近平這場精心編排的峰會,掩蓋了美中之間的巨大分歧。中情局局長約翰·拉特克利夫罕見造訪哈瓦那,與古巴官員會面,此時這個共產政權正努力控制大範圍停電與日益升高的社會動盪。司法部一項調查發現,耶魯大學醫學院曾歧視白人與亞裔申請者。在伊朗戰爭期間,全球正迅速耗盡其石油安全緩衝存量。國土安全部新任負責人馬克韋恩·穆林正試圖在克莉絲蒂·諾姆之後進行內部整頓。電動車突然成為最熱門的二手車選擇——而且以總持有成本而言也最為划算,克里斯多福·敏斯寫道。

市場即時看

道瓊工業指數期貨 49792.00(-0.72%);標普500期貨 7440.75(-1.13%);那斯達克100期貨 29201.75(-1.64%),截至美東時間2026年5月15日上午5:57:34。

本田從未面臨過這樣的危機——而要谷底翻身並不容易。備受矚目的Cerebras IPO,是對「輝達疲勞」的一次豪賭,丹·加拉格爾寫道。

獨家搶先看

南方貧困法律中心靠著反川普致富。如今川普正試圖將其擊垮。
川普的第一任期為南方貧困法律中心帶來了一筆意外之財,這個反種族主義非營利組織以數十年前在法庭上擊敗三K黨而聞名。2017年——川普就任總統、維吉尼亞州夏綠蒂鎮爆發白人民族主義集會演變為暴力事件的同一年——SPLC的年度捐款與補助金從5000萬美元暴增至超過1.3億美元,此後幾乎每年都維持在1億美元以上。根據SPLC最新的財務申報文件,不斷增加的捐款已讓該組織的淨資產膨脹至7.87億美元。如今,川普政府與夏綠蒂鎮集會事件成為一起起訴案的核心,這起案件可能威脅到SPLC的聲譽與財務狀況,卡麥隆·麥克惠特、馬克·馬雷蒙與賽蒂·葛曼報導。

邁阿密正變得更富裕,同時也正在縮小。
近年來,一波波富裕人士湧入邁阿密都會區,讓這座城市持續蓬勃發展。然而卻有一股逆流:當地人口正在萎縮。結果是一個更富裕、更小、且專為高端生活方式打造的閃亮都市中心。過去粗獷的倉儲區、市中心夜晚的荒涼景象,以及南灘那種頹廢時髦的氛圍已不復見。如今這裡是一個精緻的國際化樞紐,擁有閃耀的卡地亞精品店、前衛藝術裝置,以及散布著米其林星級餐廳的奢華街區。這種新的經濟秩序正在擠壓中產階級的生存空間,阿里安·坎波-弗洛雷斯報導。

專家觀點

問:您符合新冠疫情時期漏洞退稅資格嗎?以下是您該知道的事。
勞拉·桑德斯解釋,若納稅人在疫情期間繳納了利息或罰款,可能可以從國稅局拿回退款。

答:由於一項聯邦法院判決,數百萬美國人可能有權獲得數十億美元的新冠疫情時期利息與罰款退稅。
幾個月前,一名法官在一起涉及個人的案件中裁定,即便國稅局曾徵收,納稅人在2020年初至2023年年中之間也不欠特定的利息與罰款。實質上,這項判決撤銷了疫情期間未能達成許多報稅截止期限的後果。
因此,報稅人可以申請退還部分已繳款項,並就已核定但尚未繳納的罰款與利息申請減免。
請注意:預期國稅局將對這項聯邦法院判決提出上訴。若該機構勝訴,這些優惠待遇可能將不再適用。
這項判決適用於預估稅等稅款少繳情形;審計核定的欠稅利息;以及可能不論負債發生時間為何而累積的利息。同時也適用於未能在特定截止日期(如4月15日)前申報或繳稅的罰款,以及國際資訊申報表逾期申報的罰款。
然而,若要符合退款及其他優惠待遇資格,報稅人須在7月10日前將相關文件送交國稅局。

以下是川普第二次國事訪問中國的重要時刻與關鍵人物。
中國領導人習近平本週在北京為川普總統安排了一場盛大歡迎儀式,這是近九年來美國總統首次訪問中國。這場峰會呈現出全球兩大最強國之間的友好氛圍,儘管在貿易、科技與地緣政治影響力方面的緊張關係仍在暗中醞釀。

今日焦點

傑洛姆·鮑爾的聯準會主席任期告終。財報:瑞穗金融、三菱UFJ金融集團。

數字看世界

超過15億美元——紐約大都會藝術博物館與新畫廊合併後,將繼承的藝術品估計價值,新畫廊收藏著化妝品億萬富豪羅納德·勞德備受推崇的德國與奧地利藝術品。大都會表示將於2028年接管勞德這座已有25年歷史博物館的所有權與營運。

最後一則……

一位職業賭客與一個秘密資料庫,如何將150比1的冷門賠率變成足球奇蹟。以下是詳情。
去年夏天,職業賭客東尼·布魯姆斥資1300萬美元收購了一支名為「中洛錫安之心」球隊的股份,賭上自己能顛覆蘇格蘭足球版圖。這項操作不只是冷門而已。押注格拉斯哥兩強塞爾提克或流浪者以外的任何球隊,風險比吃放了一週的哈吉斯羊雜還高。這兩支球會自1986年以來囊括了每一屆蘇格蘭聯賽冠軍。然而,在布魯姆入主僅僅一年後,哈茨隊有可能終結體壇史上最長連霸紀錄之一。

新聞編輯室之外

評論:中國國家主席習近平以希臘式的隱晦言詞,就台灣問題向川普總統發出警告。但如果習近平認為美國真的已經衰弱到願意冒險一戰的地步,他可能反而會落入自己設下的陷阱。

✏️ There’s a lot of debate on Wall Street still over whether or not we’re in an AI bubble, and what happens if—and when—that bubble bursts. One group that isn’t losing sleep over AI: the hedge-fund herd. Early bets on the stocks of chip makers and other AI hardware companies have just delivered stock-picking funds their best month in over two decades.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

The reign of ‘El Chapo’ is over but the bodies keep piling up.

As the U.S. targets corrupt Mexican officials who aided the imprisoned drug lord’s clan, a bloody civil war is raging for control of the Sinaloa cartel. It’s a war that the Chapitos, the heirs of Mexican drug boss Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán, appear to be losing, casting doubt on the future of a dynasty that once ruled vast swaths of the criminal underworld on its way to becoming the world’s top producer and smuggler of fentanyl. The fight among criminal pretenders to Guzmán’s throne has unfolded like a Shakespearean drama, sparked by betrayal, ambition, greed—and rivers of blood, report José de Córdoba and Santiago Pérez.
China’s best and brightest tech talent is going back to China.

For decades, making it in the U.S. was the ultimate sign of success for China’s top graduates. Now, many of them are coming home—and the reverse brain drain is fueling Beijing’s efforts to edge out the U.S. in AI, robotics and medical research. An unprecedented jostling for AI talent among the richest companies and global superpowers has skyrocketed tech researchers to NBA and Hollywood levels of wealth and spurred a cutthroat recruitment blitz across the industry, report Hannah Miao and Jon Emont.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: How is the U.S. government responding to hantavirus?

The Trump administration’s health officials are walking a tightrope on hantavirus: trying to avoid public panic and a repeat of what they view as pandemic-era missteps, while escalating the federal response to the threat, explain Sabrina Siddiqui and Jennifer Calfas.

A: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has increased the number of staff assigned to the effort from three late last week to around 100, according to internal CDC data viewed by the Journal.

The group working on hantavirus includes staffers from the agency’s National Center for Emerging and Zoonotic Infectious Diseases, according to CDC employees.

The increase in personnel reflects mounting urgency inside the administration to contain a rare hantavirus outbreak aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius before it spreads further.

But lingering skepticism among some top health officials about strict Covid-19 pandemic measures has made the administration cautious about imposing quarantines or other restrictions for a virus known to be less transmissible, but more deadly, than Covid, according to people familiar with the matter.

On Monday, 18 passengers returned to the U.S. and 15 of them were taken to a specialized quarantine facility at the University of Nebraska Medical Center in Omaha.

American officials have said the risk to the general public remains low.

What’s the secret to their 40-year marriage? Nine gut renovations.

PHOTO: KACEY GILPIN AND VORA QUINN FOR WSJ

Ann and Mark Farrow are a real-estate wild card : always at home, never settled. Over 40 years, the couple has bought, gutted and lived in nine properties around Tulsa, Okla., totaling roughly $14 million in transactions and leaving behind a trail of reimagined floor plans and high-end finishes. While nine overhauls would send most couples to mediation, the Farrows view logistical nightmares as a shared thrill.

 8%

Taking weight-loss drugs means eating less—and for many Americans, dining out less, too. A Cornell University study found that households with at least one GLP-1 user reduced their spending at fast-food chains, coffee shops and quick-service restaurants by 8% within six months of starting on the drugs. Research shows that those on GLP-1s are denting the restaurant business by cutting back on visits, eating less and skipping alcohol. The developments are roiling restaurants as they also deal with rising costs and try to hold on to any customer they can.

AND FINALLY...
No one cares about your GPA, and more career advice for new grads.

For all the talk about a tough job market and the threat AI poses to entry-level work, the unemployment rate for recent college grads is 5.6%. That’s higher than the national average but hardly apocalyptic. So you’re going to get hired sooner or later. For when that day comes, WSJ columnist Callum Borchers shares five things to know as you launch your career.

✏️ 華爾街目前仍在激烈爭論我們是否正處於人工智慧泡沫之中,以及萬一泡沫破裂會發生什麼事。有一群人完全不為AI憂心忡忡:對沖基金圈。早先押注晶片製造商及其他AI硬體公司股票的賭注,剛剛為選股型基金帶來二十多年來最佳的單月表現。

艾瑪・塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條
川普總統與中國領導人習近平的會晤原本被宣傳為兩個超級大國齊聚一堂,平息經濟與貿易爭端。但習近平就台灣問題發出的警告,直接引爆了新的緊張點。伊朗戰爭已加深選民對生活成本的焦慮,共和黨在如何因應這股不安上陷入分歧。前傳播主管丹妮絲・鮑威爾已被宣布贏得內布拉斯加州一場緊繃的民主黨初選,將角逐即將退休的共和黨眾議員唐・培根的席位。既然凱文・沃許已獲確認出任聯準會主席,我們回顧了過去八個動盪年頭如何將傑羅姆・鮑爾與央行逼到極限。一項新研究顯示,AI正讓「A」等成績變得唾手可得——這讓成績對想要評估應屆畢業生的雇主而言愈發沒有參考價值。軍用狙擊手正被無人機淘汰出局。

加密貨幣死忠派認為他們找到了下一個比特幣。華爾街正押注一家公司能檢測癌症復發的血液檢測技術,David Wainer撰文報導。

獨家搶先看
「矮子」的統治結束了,但屍體仍在不斷堆積。
隨著美國鎖定曾協助這位遭監禁毒梟集團的貪腐墨西哥官員,一場血腥內戰正在錫那羅亞販毒集團的控制權爭奪中爆發。這是一場「小矮子們」——墨西哥毒梟華金・「矮子」・古斯曼繼承人——似乎正在輸掉的戰爭,讓這個一度統治犯罪地下世界大片版圖、並成為全球頭號芬太尼生產與走私者的王朝,前途蒙上陰影。這場犯罪王位覬覦者之間的爭鬥,如莎士比亞戲劇般上演,背叛、野心、貪婪與鮮血交織其中,José de Córdoba與Santiago Pérez報導。

中國最優秀、最聰明的科技人才正在回流中國。
數十年來,在美國闖出一片天,是中國頂尖畢業生成功的終極象徵。如今,許多人選擇回國——這股「海歸」逆向人才流動,正助長北京在AI、機器人及醫學研究領域超越美國的努力。各大富豪企業與全球超級大國之間對AI人才的空前爭奪,已將科技研究人員的身價推升至媲美NBA球星與好萊塢明星的水準,並在業界掀起一場你死我活的招募大戰,Hannah Miao與Jon Emont報導。

專家問答
問:美國政府如何應對漢他病毒?
川普政府的衛生官員正在漢他病毒問題上走鋼索:一方面試圖避免公眾恐慌,及重蹈他們認為的疫情時期的失策;另一方面又在升級聯邦應對措施,Sabrina Siddiqui與Jennifer Calfas解釋。

答:根據《華爾街日報》取得的內部疾管中心資料,美國疾病管制與預防中心已將投入此事的人員數量,從上週稍早的3人增加到約100人。
負責處理漢他病毒的團隊,包括來自該機構「國家新興與人畜共通傳染病中心」的工作人員,據疾管中心員工透露。
人力的增加反映出政府內部日益升高的急迫感,要在疫情擴散前控制住「MV Hondius」號郵輪上罕見的漢他病毒疫情。
但部分高層衛生官員對嚴格的新冠疫情措施仍存有揮之不去的懷疑,這使得政府在對這種已知傳染力較低、但致死率高於新冠的病毒實施隔離檢疫或其他限制措施上,態度謹慎。
週一,18名乘客返回美國,其中15人被送往內布拉斯加大學醫學中心設立的專門隔離檢疫設施。
美國官員表示,對一般大眾的風險仍然偏低。

當看新聞
他們40年婚姻的祕訣是什麼?九次徹底翻修。
照片:KACEY GILPIN AND VORA QUINN FOR WSJ
安與馬克・法羅夫婦是房地產界的一張百搭牌:永遠住在家裡,卻從未真正安頓下來。40年來,這對夫妻在奧克拉荷馬州土爾沙市周邊買下、拆毀重建並居住過九處房產,交易總額約1400萬美元,留下一連串重新構思的平面圖與高級裝潢。九次翻修足以讓大多數夫妻走向調解,但法羅夫婦卻將這些後勤上的噩夢視為共同的樂趣。

今日焦點
美國將主導以色列與黎巴嫩之間的下一輪會談。伊隆・馬斯克控告OpenAI一案的結案陳詞即將展開。經濟數據:4月零售銷售及進出口物價指數將公布。財報:應用材料公司、Versant Media、Klarna、布魯克菲爾德、Newsmax。📰 今日報紙

數字看新聞
8%
服用減重藥物意味著吃得更少——對許多美國人而言,也意味著外食次數減少。康乃爾大學一項研究發現,家中至少有一人使用GLP-1藥物的家庭,在開始服藥後六個月內,在速食連鎖店、咖啡店與快餐店的支出減少了8%。研究顯示,GLP-1使用者正透過減少外出用餐、吃得更少及戒酒,對餐飲業造成衝擊。這些變化正衝擊餐飲業,業者同時還得應付成本上漲,並努力留住任何一位顧客。

最後,別錯過...
沒有人在乎你的GPA——給新鮮人的更多職涯建議。
儘管人們大談就業市場艱難、AI對初階工作構成威脅,應屆大學畢業生的失業率卻是5.6%。這個數字雖高於全國平均,卻遠稱不上末日景象。所以你遲早會找到工作。等到那天到來時,《華爾街日報》專欄作家Callum Borchers分享了展開職涯時該知道的五件事。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: What Trump’s Truth Social Storms Reveal
emails.contentEn:
✏️ A decade after he first took office, President Trump’s ability to dictate the national conversation online remains unmatched. His nighttime missives on Truth Social—sometimes 50-plus posts overnight—offer a rare window into what the world’s most powerful man is thinking about. We analyzed thousands of Trump’s posts and found that the president uses the social-media platform to spread conspiracy theories, attack his adversaries and amplify his frustrations about immigration, crime and more.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES
Jho Low, the alleged mastermind of one of the greatest financial frauds in history, is asking Trump for a pardon. The Trump administration has picked its next acting director of Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Walmart said it would cut or relocate about 1,000 corporate workers as it looks to combine more of its global-technology and product teams. The Iran war has spurred an expansion of overland shipping that avoids the Strait of Hormuz. A number of mall owners are banning anyone under 18 unaccompanied by an adult, following waves of teen disruptions at their properties. Germany’s “Little America” confronts the specter of U.S. troop withdrawal.

📈 Follow our live financial coverage all day.

Wall Street is getting more anxious about long-term inflation. A close look at a Blue Owl credit fund’s holdings raises questions about its valuations , writes Jonathan Weil.

READ IT HERE FIRST
These late-night Truth Social storms offer a window into the president’s mind.

Trump’s Truth Social account operates as a nearly around-the-clock, high-volume amplification system that blends his own voice with a network of partisan and fringe content. Since the start of his second term, Trump’s Truth Social account has ballooned to 12.6 million followers, up from about 8.6 million. Trump—with the help of staff—has posted at least 8,800 times, according to a Journal analysis. The after-hours posts often include some of the president’s sharpest and most divisive messaging, report Anthony DeBarros and Annie Linskey.
China’s ‘two billion feet’ are suddenly running from Nike.

Nearly a half-century ago, Nike co-founder Phil Knight traveled through China and laid out an ambitious vision—“One billion people, two billion feet”—that called for an aggressive push into the country. By 2010, China was among Nike’s most lucrative markets, offering a blueprint for U.S. companies seeking to cash in on China’s rise. Today, Nike’s China business is flailing —a cautionary tale of an American giant caught in the tar pit of China’s hypercompetitive and increasingly nationalistic consumer market, report Jon Emont and Inti Pacheco.

Be smarter about your finances.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: What do Trump and Xi want to achieve at their summit this week?

Trump is scheduled to arrive in Beijing for a two-day visit that will include meetings with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. The Journal’s Lingling Wei, Annie Linskey and Alexander Ward share what to expect :

A: The summit will be the first presidential visit to China since Trump traveled there nearly nine years ago. Trump and Xi’s meeting comes as the Iran war looms over both countries, Trump targets Beijing’s partners in Venezuela and Cuba and as the U.S.-China relationship aims to recover from tit-for-tat economic brinkmanship last year.

Both leaders seek tangible wins. Trump, who is traveling with a delegation including Elon Musk, wants China to help end the Iran war and make big purchases of U.S. products. Xi, faced with a deepening economic slump at home, wants a more predictable relationship with Washington, as he works to erode its political and military commitments to Taiwan.

Each side is trying to reduce dependence on the other without rupturing the relationship that makes both economies work.

Behind closed doors, Trump treats Xi with a deference he rarely extends to other leaders, according to people familiar with their meetings.

U.S. officials and analysts expect Trump and Xi to repeat their usual displays of bonhomie but make few political breakthroughs in bilateral ties.

A major uncertainty hanging over the meeting is Taiwan, the self-governing democratic island Xi hopes to bring under Beijing’s fold. He is expected to try to press Trump to reduce the U.S.’s military support for the island.

SEE THE STORY
Experts reveal the hidden strategies used to control a concert crowd of millions.

PHOTO: MAURO PIMENTEL/ AGENCE FRANCE-PRESSE/GETTY IMAGES

How do you control a crowd of roughly 2 million concertgoers? WSJ spoke with two crowd control experts who broke down the hidden engineering behind Copacabana’s free beach concerts.

HAPPENING TODAY
Economic data: Producer-price data for April, which will give an indication of pipeline inflationary pressures. Earnings: Alibaba, Cisco Systems, StubHub, USA Rare Earth, Nebius, Birkenstock 📰 Today's paper

THE NUMBER
Millions of borrowers are defaulting on their student loans, and they are nearly 40 years old on average. That’s almost 2½ years older than the profile of a student-loan defaulter before the pandemic, according to new research from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Borrowers 50 and older are now at higher risk of default than younger borrowers. Older borrowers have been falling behind since the federal government ended its pandemic-era payment pause.

AND FINALLY...
In this boxing ring, fighters trade crypto, not blows.

Welcome to lower Manhattan’s Church Street Boxing Gym, where steel usually sharpens steel. But on this night, the ring is occupied by traders buying and selling cryptocurrencies—bitcoin, ether, even Pengu, a penguin-themed memecoin. The prize: $10,000 in cash and an ornate Japanese katana. This is the frontier of esports-style live trading competitions, a high-octane subculture that feels like an underground rave. Here, trading is reimagined as a sport , complete with play-by-play commentators.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
Opinion: The Senate is poised this week to confirm Kevin Warsh as the new Chair of the Federal Reserve. His challenge will be navigating the economic reality he inherits of renewed inflation, an oil shock affecting consumer confidence, and a President who wants lower interest rates but higher tariffs.

✏️ 十年後重新掌權,川普總統主導網路輿論話題的能力依然無人能及。他在深夜於Truth Social發布的訊息——有時一晚超過50則貼文——提供了一扇罕見的窗口,讓外界一窺這位全球最有權勢的人物在想些什麼。我們分析了數千則川普的貼文,發現總統利用這個社群媒體平台散布陰謀論、攻擊對手,並宣洩他對移民、犯罪等議題的不滿。

艾瑪・塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條
被指控策劃史上最大金融詐騙案之一的幕後主使Jho Low,正向川普請求赦免。川普政府已選定下一任移民及海關執法局代理局長。沃爾瑪表示將裁撤或調動約1000名企業員工,以整合更多全球科技與產品團隊。伊朗戰爭已刺激避開荷莫茲海峽的陸路運輸擴大。多家購物中心業主開始禁止未滿18歲、無成人陪同的青少年入內,原因是這些場所接連發生青少年滋擾事件。德國的「小美國」正面對美軍可能撤離的隱憂。

道瓊期貨 49747.00 -122.00 -0.24% 標普500期貨 7442.00 +15.50 +0.21% 那斯達克100期貨 29387.00 +217.00 +0.74%

華爾街對長期通膨愈發感到不安。仔細檢視Blue Owl一檔信貸基金的持股後,對其估值產生了疑慮,Jonathan Weil撰文。

獨家搶先看
這些深夜的Truth Social風暴,揭露了總統的內心世界。
川普的Truth Social帳號運作起來像是一套近乎全天候、高流量的擴音系統,融合了他本人的聲音與一個由黨派及邊緣內容組成的網絡。自第二任期開始以來,川普的Truth Social帳號追蹤人數已膨脹到1260萬,高於此前的約860萬。根據《華爾街日報》分析,在幕僚的協助下,川普至少發布過8800則貼文。這些深夜貼文往往包含總統最尖銳、最具分裂性的言論,Anthony DeBarros與Annie Linskey報導。

中國的「20億隻腳」正突然逃離耐吉。
近半個世紀前,耐吉共同創辦人菲爾・奈特走訪中國,提出了雄心勃勃的願景——「十億人口,二十億隻腳」——呼籲大舉進軍這個國家。到了2010年,中國已成為耐吉最有利可圖的市場之一,為想在中國崛起中分一杯羹的美國企業提供了範本。如今,耐吉的中國業務正陷入掙扎——這是一個美國巨頭深陷中國市場高度競爭且日益民族主義化消費環境泥沼的警世故事,Jon Emont與Inti Pacheco報導。

聰明理財從此開始。

專家問答
問:川普與習近平本週峰會希望達成什麼目標?
川普預定抵達北京展開為期兩天的訪問,期間將與中國領導人習近平會晤。《華爾街日報》記者魏玲靈、Annie Linskey與Alexander Ward分享了各界的期待:
答:這將是川普九年來首次以總統身分訪華。川普與習近平的會晤,恰逢伊朗戰爭陰影籠罩兩國、川普鎖定北京在委內瑞拉和古巴的夥伴,以及美中關係正試圖從去年的針鋒相對經濟角力中復原之際。
雙方都在尋求實質性的勝利。川普此行帶著包括伊隆・馬斯克在內的代表團,希望中國協助結束伊朗戰爭,並大舉採購美國產品。習近平則面對國內經濟深陷低迷,希望與華府建立更可預測的關係,同時也在削弱美方對台灣的政治與軍事承諾。
雙方都試圖在不撕裂這段讓兩國經濟得以運轉的關係前提下,降低對彼此的依賴。
據熟悉會晤情況的人士透露,私下場合中,川普對待習近平的謙遜態度,是他極少對其他領導人展現的。
美國官員與分析人士預期,川普與習近平會一如既往地展現親善姿態,但在雙邊關係上不會有太多政治突破。
一項籠罩此次會晤的重大不確定因素是台灣——習近平希望將這個自治民主島嶼納入北京版圖。他預計將試圖向川普施壓,要求美國減少對該島的軍事支持。

當看新聞
專家揭露操控數百萬人演唱會人潮的隱藏策略。
照片:MAURO PIMENTEL/法新社/GETTY IMAGES
如何管控約200萬名演唱會觀眾組成的人潮?《華爾街日報》採訪了兩位人潮管控專家,他們拆解了科帕卡巴納海灘免費演唱會背後隱藏的工程學。

今日焦點
經濟數據:4月生產者物價數據,將顯示通膨的上游壓力跡象。財報:阿里巴巴、思科系統、StubHub、USA Rare Earth、Nebius、Birkenstock。📰 今日報紙

數字看新聞
數百萬借款人正拖欠學貸,他們的平均年齡接近40歲。根據紐約聯邦準備銀行的最新研究,這比疫情前學貸違約者的平均年齡高出約兩年半。50歲以上的借款人如今違約風險比年輕借款人更高。自聯邦政府結束疫情期間的還款暫緩措施以來,年長借款人的還款情況一直每況愈下。

最後,別錯過...
在這個拳擊場裡,選手交易的是加密貨幣,而非拳頭。
歡迎來到曼哈頓下城的Church Street拳擊館,平時這裡是鋼鐵磨鍊鋼鐵之地。但今晚,場內擂台上滿是買賣加密貨幣的交易員——比特幣、以太幣,甚至企鵝主題迷因幣Pengu。獎品是1萬美元現金及一把精美的日本武士刀。這是電競式現場交易競賽的新前沿,一種讓人感覺像地下狂歡派對的高辛烷值次文化。在這裡,交易被重新想像成一項運動,還有全程球評式的現場解說。

新聞編輯室之外

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Sweden’s Surprising Capitalist Makeover
emails.contentEn:
✏️ The world’s most surprising capitalist makeover is under way in Sweden. For decades, the Nordic country was shorthand for the brand of high-tax, high-spend government that managed people’s lives from cradle to grave through state-run hospitals, schools and care homes. No longer. With little fanfare, Sweden has embraced the market . The shake-up is lowering government spending and spurring innovation—while stirring fears about those left behind.

Our reporting might be an interesting read for U.K. Prime Minister Keir Starmer, whose response to last week’s local election drubbing has been a tack to the left as he finds himself fighting for his job .

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

Trump’s complaints about Iran war leaks have prompted aggressive DOJ investigations.

The president privately complained to acting Attorney General Todd Blanche about media leaks in the wake of the Iran war last month, according to administration officials familiar with the matter, prompting an aggressive push at the Justice Department to pursue those investigations. Blanche vowed to secure subpoenas specifically targeting the records of reporters who have worked on sensitive national security stories, one official said. The Journal has received subpoenas for records of reporters. Trump has focused his ire on articles that provided details on how he arrived at his decision to launch the war, and what his advisers had told him as he deliberated, officials said, report Sadie Gurman, Josh Dawsey and Aruna Viswanatha.
JPMorgan navigates the delicate art of paying off employees.

An employee comes forward with embarrassing workplace allegations fraught with legal risks. For bosses, the dilemma is thorny: Fight or pay? It’s a situation JPMorgan Chase found itself in weeks before a former banker filed a lawsuit filled with sensational accusations. It offered $1 million to settle his claims that a female colleague had sexually harassed and assaulted him and that co-workers had subjected him to discrimination, the Journal reported. The bank has said it investigated the claims and doesn’t believe they have merit. While such deals rarely come to light, paying employees to make potential scandals go away isn’t an uncommon practice. But the calculations over when and how much to negotiate have become more complicated , report Chip Cutter and Lauren Weber.

Washington Coverage Chief Damian Paletta brings you an expert guide to the politics, power and people in the nation’s capital. Sign up for our politics newsletter.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: Why are companies racing to put satellites into low-Earth orbit?

Reporter Micah Maidenberg explains how Amazon and a host of other companies are trying to catch up with SpaceX’s Starlink network:

A: Low-Earth orbit is often defined as between around 100 miles and 1,200 miles above ground. It’s home to well-known spacecraft such as the International Space Station and the Hubble Space Telescope.

For internet satellite operators, LEO has some real advantages: Satellites closer to Earth usually offer better performance to users on the ground than those stationed further out in space.

Thousands of these satellites are expected to be launched in the years ahead by SpaceX, Amazon.com, Blue Origin and Chinese satellite operators, among others. Internet satellites, wherever they’re located in space, are part of the lucrative market for high-speed internet connections.

Watch Micah’s explainer video on LEO satellites to learn more.

SEE THE STORY
Democrats are targeting new states to win the redistricting war.

SOURCE: COOK POLITICAL REPORT

Democratic leaders—acknowledging there might be little they can do to keep up with the GOP’s redistricting efforts for the 2026 election—are setting their sights on 2028 with plans to redraw maps in blue states like New York and Colorado. Party leaders are also looking to make gains in swing states, like Pennsylvania, if they can capture enough seats in state legislatures in November. The frantic push comes as two court rulings shatter the party’s optimism for beating Republicans in a gerrymandering battle that is upending the midterm landscape.

The Penn Station neighborhood, known for dirty streets and a claustrophobic train station, is improbably emerging as one of the hottest office markets in the city. The Michigan city’s residents say they are witnessing a defacement of the local landscape . Tree trimmers for DTE Energy have driven around the city in recent weeks cutting limbs that appear to be closing in on power lines as part of a long-term effort to reduce power outages. emails.subject: The 10-Point: Iran War Hangs Over Trump’s China Visit
emails.contentEn:
✏️ As the heads of the world’s two superpowers meet in Beijing later this week, President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping will have another nation looming over their summit: Iran. Trump is eager to move on from the Middle East war that is sapping his domestic power and straining the global economy. Both men head into the high-stakes summit seeking their own victories on Iran—Trump is prepared to push Xi to help broker an agreement that ends the conflict, while the Chinese are eager to ensure the current Iranian regime remains intact.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

READ IT HERE FIRST
China has dazzling technology and military muscle, but it is also an economic mess.

More than a decade into Xi’s rule, the country’s military has grown more formidable, its factories dominate global manufacturing and its technology pioneers are closing the gap with Silicon Valley. Yet big parts of its economy are a mess. A colossal property bust has destroyed trillions of dollars in wealth, consumer confidence has been gutted and the job market has grown bleak. The disconnect shows how Xi has made China’s security a priority over its economy , reports Brian Spegele.

Go inside the U.S.-China relationship.
A changing job market leans against men.

The American labor market is tilting away from men. Over the past year, nearly all net job growth has come from healthcare and social assistance, a sector with a dearth of men. Sectors with heavily male workforces have been losing jobs. The postpandemic period has seen an influx of women in their prime working years into employment. The share of men working has flatlined. This divergent path might widen in the years ahead, reports Justin Lahart.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: Is there a treatment for hantavirus?

Drug hunters have searched for years for a treatment for the disease. The latest outbreak, which has killed three people, adds increased urgency. Reporter Peter Loftus shares what we know about drugs and vaccines in development:

A: While hantavirus is generally contracted through exposure to infected rodents, the Andes strain in the current outbreak can be transmitted from person to person. Some promising projects that had been shelved due to a lack of consistent funding are seeking a new influx of money to pay for further testing and other research that could help create treatment options.

An international consortium of researchers from universities, biotech companies and a U.S. military research institute developed an antibody designed to attack hantavirus. In a study, the antibody protected hamsters from the Andes strain.

Antibodies were a critical tool in the fight against Covid-19. With the hantavirus antibody, the aim would be to give it to people exposed to the virus, to either ward off infection or limit the severity of any illness, said Kartik Chandran, professor of microbiology and immunology at Albert Einstein College of Medicine in New York and part of the team that developed it.

The antibody has only been tested in animals, and it wouldn’t be feasible to make a significant quantity to help with the current outbreak.

Chandran needs more money to move the research forward, but he said the consortium hasn’t been able to get the necessary funding because hantavirus outbreaks are rare and haven’t been a priority compared with other viruses.

Efforts to develop a hantavirus vaccine also continue.

SEE THE STORY
Private credit’s hot streak is over.

Private-credit firms delivered eye-popping returns to investors in recent years. That hot streak is over. The latest earnings results across the industry show returns that appear to be entering a more modest chapter, just as investors have grown worried about other aspects of private-credit funds that lend to riskier companies. Firms attribute the decline in returns to Fed rate cuts and rising defaults on their loans.

Apollo Global Management has been holding talks to sell MidCap Financial Investment, its publicly listed business-development company, a type of private-credit fund.

That’s a tough reality for thousands of wait-listed students across the country now, still holding out hope of getting into their dream schools after the May 1 commitment deadline passed.

AND FINALLY...
The world’s highest-flying repo men are collecting Spirit Airlines’ jets.

When Spirit Airlines shut down, it left dozens of bright yellow jets parked at airport gates around the U.S. Within hours, the repo men were coming for them . Nomadic Aviation Group started getting calls from leasing companies anxious to get their planes back as the company neared collapse. The next morning, with Spirit’s death now official, it had pilots fanning out to South Florida, Charlotte, Houston and Columbus, Ohio, to take the jets to airplane boneyards for storage. The somewhat grim task is surprisingly complex.

就業市場正朝著不利於男性的方向傾斜。
美國勞動市場正在偏離男性。過去一年,幾乎所有淨就業成長都來自醫療保健與社會援助業,而這是一個男性人數稀少的部門。以男性為主的部門則不斷失去工作機會。疫情後時期,大量處於工作黃金年齡的女性湧入就業市場。男性的就業比例則持平不前。這條分歧的道路在未來數年可能會進一步拉大,Justin Lahart報導。

問:漢他病毒有治療方法嗎?
藥物研發人員多年來一直在尋找這種疾病的治療方法。這次已造成三人死亡的最新疫情爆發,使得研發更為迫切。記者Peter Loftus分享目前正在研發中的藥物與疫苗現況:
答:雖然漢他病毒通常透過接觸受感染的囓齒動物傳染,但本次疫情中的安地斯病毒株可以人傳人。一些因缺乏穩定資金而被擱置的有前景計畫,正尋求新一輪資金挹注,以支付進一步測試及其他有助於開發治療方案的研究。
一個由多所大學、生物科技公司及一家美國軍方研究機構組成的國際研究聯盟,已研發出一種設計用來對抗漢他病毒的抗體。在一項研究中,該抗體成功保護倉鼠免受安地斯病毒株感染。
抗體曾是對抗新冠病毒的關鍵工具。針對漢他病毒抗體,目標是將其施用於曾接觸病毒的人,以防止感染或減輕任何病情的嚴重程度,紐約阿爾伯特・愛因斯坦醫學院微生物學及免疫學教授、該研發團隊成員之一的Kartik Chandran說。
該抗體目前只在動物身上測試過,而且要大量生產以應對當前疫情並不可行。
Chandran需要更多資金來推進研究,但他表示,由於漢他病毒疫情爆發罕見、且相較其他病毒並非優先事項,該研究聯盟一直無法獲得所需的資金。
研發漢他病毒疫苗的努力也仍在持續。

當看新聞
私募信貸的火熱行情已經結束。
私募信貸公司近年來為投資人帶來了令人瞠目結舌的回報。這股熱潮已經結束。整個產業最新財報顯示,回報似乎正進入一個較為平淡的階段,而此時投資人也已對放款給高風險企業的私募信貸基金的其他方面感到擔憂。各家公司將回報下滑歸咎於聯準會降息及貸款違約率上升。
阿波羅全球管理公司一直在洽談出售MidCap Financial Investment,這是其公開上市的商業發展公司(一種私募信貸基金)。

今日焦點
經濟數據:全美房地產經紀人協會將公布4月房屋銷售數據。財報:星座能源、福斯、Circle、Hims & Hers、西蒙地產。📰 今日報紙

數字看新聞
加州大學柏克萊分校去年從近6500人的候補名單中錄取的學生人數。在部分學校,候補名單的競爭甚至比該校整體錄取率更為嚴苛。對於目前全美數千名還在候補名單上、在5月1日的入學確認截止日過後仍抱著進入夢想學校希望的學生而言,這是一個殘酷的現實。

最後,別錯過...
全球最高飛的「回收員」正在收繳精神航空的飛機。
精神航空停飛後,留下數十架鮮黃色噴射機停在全美各地的機場閘口。短短數小時內,飛機回收員便已上門。Nomadic Aviation Group在該公司瀕臨倒閉之際,開始接到租賃公司焦急索要飛機的電話。隔天早上,隨著精神航空正式宣告死亡,該公司已派出飛行員分赴南佛羅里達、夏洛特、休士頓及俄亥俄州哥倫布市,將飛機送往飛機墳場存放。這項略顯淒涼的任務其實出乎意料地複雜。

新聞編輯室之外
評論:為什麼加州民主黨無法為州長及洛杉磯市長選舉端出更好的候選人陣容?

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Israel’s Secret War Base in Iraq
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Israel built and defended a secret Iran war base in Iraq. The base, set up for special forces and search-and-rescue teams, was almost discovered early in the conflict when a local shepherd reported unusual military activity in the area. Then, when the Iraqi military sent troops to investigate, Israel kept them at bay with airstrikes. Details of the base—and the risks Israel took to establish and protect it—help fill in the picture of how the country managed to fight an air campaign against an enemy around 1,000 miles away.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES
Israel set up a clandestine military outpost in the Iraqi desert to support its air campaign against Iran, people familiar with the matter including U.S. officials said. Israel’s military declined to comment. The absence of Iran’s supreme leader is complicating Tehran’s efforts to negotiate an end to the war. Mojtaba Khamenei hasn’t appeared publicly since U.S. and Iranian officials say he was injured in an airstrike more than two months ago. The cruise ship at the center of the hantavirus outbreak arrived in Spain’s Canary Islands. Passengers will be ferried to shore and put on flights home for quarantine . Wesley Edens, the co-founder of Fortress Investment Group and co-owner of the Milwaukee Bucks, was allegedly extorted by a sexual partner who threatened to share explicit videos of him if he didn’t pay her as much as $1.215 billion. Foshan, the factory town known as China’s furniture capital, is fighting to survive as American tariffs and overseas competition punish manufacturers. 🎧 Podcast: Will the AI race be enough to kick off a real nuclear-energy renaissance in the U.S.?

FROM THE MARKETS
Intel shares are now up 239% this year, and Sandisk is up 558%, as AI companies’ insatiable appetite for computing power continues to propel the great chip stock melt-up of 2026. The math behind juggling multiple important financial goals is simple: Here are five questions to help you make better financial decisions . Private credit probably isn’t a major threat , writes James Mackintosh, but the question is whether trouble in the sector could spill into the wider economy or—disaster—the wider financial system.

READ IT HERE FIRST
The world of high-school athlete transfers in Florida is wild.

Before Ah’Mari Stevens, a 17-year-old football player from South Florida, announced plans to attend Louisiana State University, he suited up for four different high schools—something that would be impossible in most of the U.S. due to interscholastic rules. Florida is different. School-choice laws mean athletes transfer easily, often without losing a moment of playing time. In the age of Name, Image and Likeness compensation, the result is a first-of-its-kind high-school transfer portal where teens jump from school to school, reports Harriet Ryan. While some praise the process, others see an out-of-control system in which children barely out of middle school have agents and social-media strategies, while education is an afterthought.
In a bid to flip the Senate, Democrats are pushing deep into Trump territory.

Former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown lost his seat in a 2024 MAGA wave that put Republicans back in control of the Senate. Now, the onetime three-term Ohio senator is seeking a comeback in a very different political environment , with an unpopular war and high prices denting President Trump’s poll numbers and alarming GOP strategists. Republicans are playing defense in Ohio and a growing number of other red states, where Democrats are counting on voter backlash to power them to victory this fall in their long-shot battle to retake the Senate, report Cameron McWhirter and Lindsay Wise.

Go inside what’s driving D.C.

Washington Coverage Chief Damian Paletta brings you an expert guide to the politics, power and people in the nation’s capital.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: We asked a church group to weigh in on Trump. What did they say?

Churchgoers at Annandale United Methodist Church in Virginia often drift into political debate . News associate Terell Wright paid them a visit.

A: On a recent Sunday, parishioners sat in a circle in a chapel next to the sanctuary to discuss Trump, the war in Iran and forgiveness. Here’s what several churchgoers had to say about their relationship with politics, war and faith under the current administration:

Jason Micheli, 48, the pastor, said he believes the Iranian government poses a threat to global security but vehemently opposes war. As a father of two sons who recently joined the military, he’s worried the war will result in negative consequences. Meily Grigg, 53, a special-education teacher, said Trump’s immigration policies have had an impact on some of her students, whose parents withdrew them from classes after fearing immigration services could separate them. She says she has prayed for the president throughout his second term despite her political disagreements. Jon Zimmermann, 62, a financial-services professional, said the president doesn’t deserve forgiveness for what he described as dividing the nation—because the president doesn’t seek it. Images of destruction in Iran and Gaza have made Zimmermann furious with Trump.

SEE THE STORY
After Allison Ellsworth’s Poppi exit made her a megamillionaire, she’s ready to talk money.

NIKKI WALKER

The 39-year-old and her husband became centimillionaires when they helped sell Poppi for $1.95 billion to PepsiCo last year. But not long ago, Ellsworth says she was so cash poor that she needed an interest-only loan for her Austin home and maxed out credit cards. Since the sale, she’s upgraded her house—while buying two more for her mom and aunt. Watch her full episode of The WSJ Money Interview here .

HAPPENING THIS WEEK
Monday: April existing home-sales figures. Tuesday: U.S. consumer-price data for April, which is expected to show that inflation has risen, driven largely by higher gasoline prices. Wednesday: Producer-price data for April, which will give an indication of pipeline inflationary pressures. Thursday: Trump is expected to visit China for a summit with leader Xi Jinping. Retail sales data for April. Closing arguments scheduled in Elon Musk’s lawsuit against OpenAI. Friday: Jerome Powell’s term as Fed chair ends. Jude Law plays Vladimir Putin in “The Wizard of the Kremlin,” a political satire film out in cinemas today. Check out what else is on in arts & culture this week .

THE NUMBER
How many new locations Barnes & Noble is on track to open this year. By year-end, the retailer expects to have 740 stores in the U.S., up from 627 in 2019. U.S. print book sales plateaued in 2025, according to Circana BookScan. But Barnes & Noble has found a way to adapt to the punishing bookselling environment—thanks, in part, to its unsentimental British CEO, James Daunt.

AND FINALLY...
Typing is being replaced by whispering—and it’s way more annoying.

One venture capitalist said visiting AI startups today is like showing up at a high-end call center—except everyone is chatting with AI . Mollie Amkraut Mueller, who runs her own AI business in Seattle, is hooked on Wispr Flow, a dictation app that users are pairing with coding tools like Claude Code and Codex to turn rambling, stream-of-consciousness prompts into coherent, usable text in seconds. Efficient, yes. Annoying, you bet.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
WSJ | Buy Side: Business-debt consolidation can improve your cash flow and repackage your obligations to potentially save you money.
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 以色列在伊拉克建立並守護了一座祕密的伊朗戰爭基地。這座為特種部隊及搜救隊設立的基地,在衝突初期差點被發現——當時一名當地牧羊人通報了不尋常的軍事活動。之後,當伊拉克軍方派兵前往調查時,以色列以空襲將他們擋在外圍。這座基地的細節——以及以色列為建立並保護它所承擔的風險——有助於拼湊出該國如何成功對一個遠在約1000英里外的敵人發動空中戰役的全貌。

艾瑪・塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條
據熟悉此事的人士(包括美國官員)透露,以色列在伊拉克沙漠中設立了一個祕密軍事前哨站,以支援其對伊朗的空中戰役。以色列軍方拒絕置評。伊朗最高領袖的缺席,正使德黑蘭爭取結束戰爭談判的努力更加複雜。美國及伊朗官員表示,穆傑塔巴・哈梅內伊自兩個多月前在一次空襲中受傷後,便未再公開露面。這艘漢他病毒疫情核心的郵輪已抵達西班牙的加那利群島。乘客將被送上岸並搭機返國進行隔離檢疫。Fortress Investment Group共同創辦人、密爾瓦基公鹿隊共同持有人Wesley Edens,據稱遭一名性伴侶勒索,對方威脅若他不支付最高12.15億美元,就要公開他的露骨影片。中國「家具之都」佛山這座工廠城鎮,正在美國關稅及海外競爭對製造商的重創下奮力求生。🎧 播客:AI競賽是否足以在美國引爆一場真正的核能復興?

市場即時看
英特爾股價今年迄今已上漲239%,晟碟(Sandisk)更上漲558%,原因是AI公司對運算能力的無盡渴求,持續推動2026年這波驚人的晶片股熔漲行情。同時兼顧多項重要財務目標背後的算法其實很簡單:這裡有五個問題,能幫助你做出更好的財務決策。私募信貸大概不會構成重大威脅,James Mackintosh撰文,但問題在於,該產業的動盪是否可能蔓延至更廣泛的經濟——或者,最糟的情況——蔓延至更廣泛的金融體系。

獨家搶先看
佛羅里達高中運動員轉學的世界瘋狂至極。
在17歲的南佛羅里達美式足球員Ah'Mari Stevens宣布將前往路易斯安那州立大學就讀之前,他已經在四所不同的高中出賽——這在美國多數地方是不可能發生的事,因為有校際規定限制。但佛羅里達不同。校方選擇制的法律讓運動員能輕易轉學,往往不會損失一分鐘的出賽時間。在姓名、肖像與形象權(NIL)報酬的時代,結果造就了一個史無前例的高中轉學平台,青少年在學校之間跳來跳去,Harriet Ryan報導。有人讚許這套流程,但也有人認為這是一個失控的體系——這些剛脫離國中沒多久的孩子,已經有經紀人和社群媒體策略,教育反倒成了次要之事。

為了在參議院翻盤,民主黨正深入川普的票倉。
前民主黨參議員Sherrod Brown在2024年的MAGA浪潮中失去席位,共和黨也因此重新掌控參議院。如今,這位曾三度連任的俄亥俄州參議員正試圖在一個截然不同的政治環境中東山再起——不受歡迎的戰爭與高物價正拖累川普總統的民調數字,並讓共和黨策士感到不安。共和黨正在俄亥俄州及愈來愈多其他紅州採取守勢,民主黨則寄望選民的反彈情緒,能助他們在今秋這場翻盤機會渺茫的參議院之戰中獲勝,Cameron McWhirter與Lindsay Wise報導。

深入了解華府脈動。
華府新聞主編Damian Paletta為您帶來首都政治、權力與人物的內幕導覽。

專家問答
問:我們請一個教會團體對川普發表看法。他們怎麼說?
維吉尼亞州安南代爾聯合衛理公會教堂的信眾,經常會不由自主地陷入政治辯論。新聞助理記者Terell Wright拜訪了他們。
答:某個週日,教友們坐在正殿旁一間小禮拜堂裡圍成一圈,討論川普、伊朗戰爭與寬恕的議題。以下是幾位教友對於他們在現任政府下與政治、戰爭及信仰之間關係的看法:
48歲的牧師Jason Micheli表示,他相信伊朗政府對全球安全構成威脅,但堅決反對戰爭。身為兩名剛加入軍隊的兒子的父親,他擔心這場戰爭會帶來負面後果。53歲的特殊教育老師Meily Grigg表示,川普的移民政策已影響到她的部分學生——這些孩子的家長因擔心移民局可能將家人拆散,而讓孩子休學。她說,儘管在政治上意見不合,她在川普整個第二任期內都持續為總統祈禱。62歲的金融服務業人士Jon Zimmermann表示,總統不值得被原諒,因為他所描述的分裂國家的行為,總統本人並不尋求寬恕。伊朗及加薩的破壞畫面,讓Zimmermann對川普感到憤怒。

當看新聞
Allison Ellsworth因出售Poppi致富成為千萬富翁後,她準備好談錢了。
NIKKI WALKER
這位39歲的創業家和丈夫,在去年將Poppi以19.5億美元賣給百事公司後,成了億萬富翁。但不久之前,Ellsworth說她窮到連奧斯汀的房子都需要靠只付利息的貸款,信用卡也刷爆了。出售公司後,她升級了自己的房子——同時也為母親和阿姨各買了一棟房子。在此觀看她完整一集的《華爾街日報財富人物專訪》。

本週焦點
週一:4月成屋銷售數據。週二:預計4月美國消費者物價數據將顯示通膨上升,主要受汽油價格上漲推動。週三:4月生產者物價數據,將顯示通膨的上游壓力跡象。週四:川普預計前往中國,與領導人習近平舉行峰會。4月零售銷售數據。伊隆・馬斯克控告OpenAI一案的結案陳詞排定進行。週五:傑羅姆・鮑爾的聯準會主席任期結束。裘德・洛在政治諷刺片《克里姆林宮的魔法師》中飾演弗拉基米爾・普丁,該片今日在戲院上映。查看本週藝文界還有哪些活動。

數字看新聞
邦諾書店(Barnes & Noble)今年預計新開設的門市數量。到年底,這家零售商在美國的門市預計將達740家,較2019年的627家增加。根據Circana BookScan的數據,美國印刷書籍銷售在2025年趨於平穩。但邦諾書店已找到方法在這個艱難的書籍銷售環境中適應——部分要歸功於其不帶感情用事的英籍執行長James Daunt。

最後,別錯過...
打字正被輕聲細語取代——而且更加惱人。
一位創投業者表示,如今拜訪AI新創公司,就像走進一間高檔的客服中心——只不過每個人都在和AI聊天。在西雅圖經營自家AI公司的Mollie Amkraut Mueller,已經迷上了聽寫應用程式Wispr Flow,使用者正將它與Claude Code、Codex等程式設計工具搭配使用,在幾秒鐘內把喃喃自語、意識流般的提示詞轉換成連貫、可用的文字。效率確實提升了,沒錯,但也真的很煩。

新聞編輯室之外
《華爾街日報》| Buy Side:企業債務整合能改善你的現金流,並重新規劃你的債務,或許能為你省下一筆錢。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Sailors Stuck in the Strait
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Thousands of low-wage sailors are trapped in the Persian Gulf. They hail from countries with little voice in the back-and-forth between Iran and the U.S., such as Syria, Indonesia or the Philippines. Yet they have become unwilling front-line witnesses in a 21st-century sea battle . The Journal spoke to more than a dozen of these seamen stuck near the Strait of Hormuz, who described deteriorating conditions tipping into a humanitarian crisis.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES
Washington’s attempts to shrug off exchanges of fire with Iran deepened Arab Gulf states’ concerns that any deal to end the war will expose them to future conflict with a vengeful Iran. Follow our live coverage here . President Trump and Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis have repaired their relationship and speak often as DeSantis weighs his next political move. Trump and his top aides are pressuring GOP leaders in South Carolina and other Southern states to pursue mid-decade redistricting plans after the Supreme Court weakened the Voting Rights Act. Chirayu Rana set off a public relations crisis at JPMorgan Chase after the claims he made in a sexual assault lawsuit went viral, stoked by AI fakes. Trump signed off on a plan to fire FDA Commissioner Marty Makary , following a tumultuous period for the regulator.

FROM THE MARKETS
A better-than-expected jobs report and a continuing chip-stock rally lifted stocks to new highs , with both the Nasdaq and S&P 500 closing at fresh records. Apple and Intel reached a preliminary agreement for the chipmaker to build some of the chips that power the iPhone company’s devices. It’s a labor market unlike any other : Unemployment has drifted up, layoffs are low, hiring is slow, and the economy needs far fewer new jobs than before.

READ IT HERE FIRST
Sailors in the Strait of Hormuz are low on supplies and stuck in a war zone.

The Persian Gulf has been transformed into a vast nautical prison for low-wage sea workers. Not classified as prisoners of war, these seafarers have been caught in the standoff between the U.S. and Tehran for more than two months, and are running low on basic provisions, report Milan Czerny, Joe Parkinson and Drew Hinshaw. The resulting juxtaposition offers a stark symbol of the economic fallout from the war: Sailors are stuck on ships loaded with fertilizer worth tens of millions, yet are rationing food. Over video calls, sailors showed WSJ burned skin and gaping wounds. Others played recordings from missiles hitting nearby vessels or medical emergencies unfolding at sea—or described the horror of watching a nearby ship consumed by flames.
The era of the tiger mom is over. Enter the beta mom.

Some nights after Sophie Jaffe is already in bed, her phone will ping with a new video from her 13-year-old son that shows him doing a back flip off a concrete wall or standing on someone’s shoulders. She usually won’t know precisely where in Los Angeles he is. That’s fine by her. After decades where the dominant expectation for high-achieving parents was to intensively helicopter, a new generation of moms is saying “enough.” They’re reclaiming date night, saying no to schlepping to 17 different after-school activities and making peace with dirty dishes in the sink. These acts of giving up—or giving in—are beginning to add up to something a feminist revolution, albeit a very low-key one, reports Rachel Wolfe.

Stay on top of your health.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: After the hantavirus outbreak, should you cancel your cruise?

The outbreak aboard the MV Hondius has revived memories of Covid-era cruise chaos. Reporter Caroline Tell wrote about why the current situation is very different .

A: Images of quarantined cruise passengers and officials in hazmat suits feel eerily reminiscent of the dozens of Covid-19 outbreaks that hit the cruise industry in early 2020.

Three passengers from the Oceanwide Expeditions-operated ship are now dead and several others are ill following an outbreak of the rare but severe rodent-borne disease, according to the World Health Organization. The comparison to Covid-19, however, may be largely psychological.

“Covid PTSD is real, and I understand why people are connecting this situation to what happened in 2020,” said Dr. Céline Gounder, a physician and clinical associate professor of medicine and infectious diseases at New York University’s Grossman School of Medicine. “Surface level, it feels like the same story all over again. But it’s not.”

That hasn’t stopped would-be travelers taking to online forums like Reddit to ask whether they should scrap their cruise plans in light of the outbreak.

SEE THE STORY
This secret diary has spilled into the Musk vs. OpenAI feud.

EMIL LENDOF/WSJ; GETTY IMAGES

The journal of OpenAI president Greg Brockman features heavily in the company’s legal battle with Elon Musk—and is the most human part of a trial between tech billionaires, writes Ben Cohen. Musk’s lawsuit against Brockman and Sam Altman has shaken loose a trove of evidence, offering a peek inside the minds of the people who have spent the past decade building AI. Here’s what he learned from reading their unvarnished emails, dishy texts—and one deeply personal journal.

HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND
Saturday & Sunday: The NBA playoffs continue through the weekend. 📰 Today's paper

THE NUMBER

The number of auto suppliers in the U.S. today that are owned by companies located in China , according to data compiled by AlixPartners. Even though Chinese cars aren’t on U.S. roads, American cars are full of parts made in China. Overall, Chinese companies have amassed ownership stakes in about 10,000 suppliers in America, according to the data, including stakes as small as 5%.

AND FINALLY...
The world has officially reached peak bagel.

At New York’s sixth BagelFest, fans lined up to try samples and schmears from local favorites and shops as far away as Denmark and Hawaii. This year’s Best Bagel winner was Starship Bagel, which is not based in New York—or even London or Montreal, cities with venerable bagel traditions of their own—but in Dallas, Texas. As bakers from Chicago to Berlin reimagine the bagel, here’s where to try the very best .
