emails.contentZh:
✏️ 數千名低薪船員被困在波斯灣。他們來自敘利亞、印尼或菲律賓等在伊朗與美國之間的博弈中幾乎沒有發言權的國家。然而,他們卻成了這場21世紀海上對峙中不情願的第一線見證者。《華爾街日報》採訪了十幾名困在荷莫茲海峽附近的這類海員,他們描述了正逐漸惡化、演變成人道危機的處境。

艾瑪・塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條
華府試圖對與伊朗的交火事件輕描淡寫,反而加深了阿拉伯灣國對於「任何結束戰爭的協議都可能讓他們暴露在與心懷報復的伊朗未來衝突風險中」的擔憂。在此追蹤我們的即時報導。川普總統與佛羅里達州長羅恩・迪桑蒂斯已修復關係,兩人在迪桑蒂斯權衡下一步政治動向之際經常交談。川普及其高級幕僚正向南卡羅來納州及其他南方州的共和黨領導人施壓,要求他們在最高法院削弱《投票權法》後推動年度中重劃選區的計畫。Chirayu Rana在他提出的性侵訴訟指控在AI假造內容的推波助瀾下瘋傳後,在摩根大通引發了一場公關危機。川普已批准解僱FDA局長Marty Makary的計畫,此前該監管機構經歷了一段動盪時期。

市場消息
一份優於預期的就業報告,加上晶片股持續上漲,將股市推升至新高,那斯達克指數與標普500指數雙雙創下歷史新高收盤紀錄。蘋果與英特爾就這家晶片製造商為iPhone製造商生產部分晶片達成初步協議。這是一個前所未有的勞動市場:失業率緩步上升,裁員數量低,招聘步調緩慢,而經濟所需的新增就業崗位遠少於以往。

獨家搶先看
荷莫茲海峽的船員補給短缺,受困戰區。
波斯灣已變成低薪海事工作者的巨大海上牢籠。這些不被歸類為戰俘的海員,已被困在美國與德黑蘭的對峙中超過兩個月,基本物資日益短缺,Milan Czerny、Joe Parkinson與Drew Hinshaw報導。這種處境形成了戰爭經濟後果的鮮明象徵:船員被困在載滿價值數千萬美元肥料的船隻上,卻要配給食物。透過視訊通話,船員向《華爾街日報》展示了灼傷的皮膚與裂開的傷口。其他人則播放了飛彈擊中附近船隻的錄音,或描述附近船隻突發醫療緊急事件的恐懼——或是目睹附近船隻被大火吞噬的驚悚經歷。

「虎媽」時代已經結束,「貝塔媽媽」時代來臨。
索菲・賈菲(Sophie Jaffe)有些夜晚已經上床睡覺,手機卻忽然響起提示音,收到她13歲兒子傳來的新影片,影片中他在混凝土牆上翻筋斗,或是站在別人的肩膀上。她通常不清楚他確切人在洛杉磯的哪個角落。她也不介意。在過去幾十年,對高成就父母的主流期待是密切「直升機」式管教,如今新一代母親正在說「夠了」。她們正重新奪回約會之夜、拒絕接送孩子跑17個不同的課後活動,並開始接受水槽裡堆著髒碗盤。這些放手——或者說妥協——的舉動,正逐漸累積成某種類似女性主義革命的東西,儘管是一種非常低調的版本,Rachel Wolfe報導。

掌握你的健康。

專家問答
問:漢他病毒疫情爆發後,該取消你的郵輪行程嗎?
「MV Hondius」號上的疫情爆發,喚起了人們對新冠時期郵輪混亂場面的記憶。記者Caroline Tell撰文說明目前情況為何大不相同。
答:隔離檢疫乘客及穿著防護裝的官員的畫面,令人不安地聯想到2020年初重創郵輪業的數十起新冠疫情爆發。
根據世界衛生組織的數據,這艘由Oceanwide Expeditions營運的郵輪上,已有三名乘客死亡,另有多人染病,起因是這種罕見但嚴重的囓齒動物傳播疾病爆發。然而,與新冠病毒的比較或許主要只是心理層面的。
「新冠創傷後壓力症候群是真實存在的,我理解為何人們會將這次的情況與2020年的經歷聯繫起來。」紐約大學格羅斯曼醫學院醫師暨臨床醫學及傳染病副教授Céline Gounder博士說。「表面上看起來,像是同樣的故事又重演一遍。但事實並非如此。」
這並未阻止有意出遊的旅客湧向Reddit等線上論壇,詢問是否應該取消郵輪計畫。

當看新聞
這本祕密日記已捲入馬斯克與OpenAI之爭。
EMIL LENDOF/WSJ; GETTY IMAGES
OpenAI總裁Greg Brockman的日記,在該公司與伊隆・馬斯克的法律大戰中大量被援引——也是這場科技億萬富豪之間審判中最具人情味的部分,Ben Cohen撰文。馬斯克對Brockman與山姆・奧特曼提起的訴訟,已挖掘出大量證據,提供了一窺過去十年打造AI的人們內心世界的機會。以下是他從閱讀他們未經修飾的電郵、閒聊簡訊——以及一本極度私人的日記中所學到的。

本週末焦點
週六及週日:NBA季後賽整個週末持續進行。📰 今日報紙

數字看新聞
根據AlixPartners匯編的資料,如今美國有超過60家汽車零件供應商屬於位於中國的公司所有。儘管中國汽車尚未行駛在美國道路上,美國汽車卻充斥著中國製造的零件。整體而言,根據該數據,中國企業已在美國約1萬家供應商中取得所有權,其中包括低至5%的小額持股。

最後,別錯過...
世界已正式迎來貝果的巔峰時刻。
在紐約第六屆「BagelFest」貝果節上,粉絲們大排長龍,只為品嚐當地熱門店家及遠自丹麥、夏威夷而來的貝果師傅所提供的樣品與抹醬。今年的「最佳貝果獎」得主是Starship Bagel——它並非位於紐約,甚至也不在倫敦或蒙特婁這些擁有悠久貝果傳統的城市,而是位於德州達拉斯。隨著從芝加哥到柏林的烘焙師傅們重新想像貝果,以下是品嚐頂級貝果的去處。

新聞編輯室之外
評論:法治精神在維吉尼亞州依然存在——該州最高法院週五駁回了選民在4月公投中通過的10比1民主黨傑利蠑螈選區劃分方案。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Chaos at the White House Over a New AI Model
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Artificial intelligence has gripped government and business leaders since ChatGPT’s debut. But a new generation of AI models—capable of wreaking havoc on small-town banks, hospitals and water plants via cyberattacks—is fueling fresh anxieties . These emerging threats have upended the Trump administration’s AI roadmap, potentially forcing a pivot toward the very thing the industry has lobbied against: increased federal oversight.

Also on the AI front: The Journal’s chief economics commentator, Greg Ip, looks at how AI has made it nearly impossible to gauge the economy’s true performance.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES
A federal trade court ruled President Trump didn’t have the authority to impose new global tariffs after a previous set of levies was struck down by the Supreme Court. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is coordinating with the World Health Organization to help global authorities contain a hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship. Saudi Arabia and Kuwait have lifted restrictions on the U.S. military’s use of their bases and airspace that blocked “Project Freedom” in the Strait of Hormuz. French prosecutors are summoning Elon Musk to Paris again—this time to face preliminary criminal charges in a sprawling investigation into his social-media platform, X.

Wall Street is taking over cryptoland , and being met with little resistance. Whirlpool has paid a dividend for 70 years. Now, it can’t afford one—and investors are questioning the company’s recovery plan. Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser has cleaned up some big problems. It’s time for the bank to show it can excel, writes Telis Demos.

READ IT HERE FIRST
Go inside ‘Project Freedom,’ Trump’s aborted bid to reopen the Persian Gulf.

Earlier this week, Iran launched a barrage of missiles and drones at commercial ships, at the U.S. Navy and at a U.S. ally, the United Arab Emirates. American helicopters sank Iranian fastboats, and Iranian drones hit a civilian ship. The intervening hours included the most serious escalation in the conflict since Trump declared a cease-fire in April. Then, almost as quickly as it started, Trump directed the U.S. operation to guide ships through the strait to be put on pause. The president halted operations on Tuesday, 36 hours after the project began. Ship traffic again grounded to a halt. The short-lived exercise , known as “Project Freedom,” exposed the limits of Trump’s ability to maneuver in the region, report Jared Malsin, Costas Paris, Shelby Holliday and Rebecca Feng.
Rupert Murdoch launches a high-stakes blitz against the NFL.

During a White House dinner, Murdoch warned Trump that if streamers gained rights to more games, it would kill broadcast networks, a person familiar with the evening’s events said. It was a bold play call , even for a media titan known for making them. Fox’s fear of losing games created a highly unusual situation where Murdoch was seeking to stir up trouble for a partner it pays billions.The lobbying comes as the Justice Department is investigating whether sports leagues, including the NFL, should continue to enjoy antitrust protections to collectively negotiate television rights on behalf of teams. Murdoch’s gambit underscores the stakes not only for Fox but also for other major media players, report Dana Mattioli, Josh Dawsey, Andrew Beaton and Joe Flint.

Make sense of AI’s impact on business.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: Why is Congress struggling to do the bare minimum?

The current session is marked by record-long government shutdowns, lawmakers sidelined on the Iran war and a wave of pending departures. Tim Hanrahan, Ken Thomas and Lindsay Wise explain why less is getting done :

A: There are several reasons. Recent years have seen a rise of intense partisanship, which deters dealmaking—as it can be politically risky to strike an agreement with the other party. Also, in recent years, Republicans have had very slim majorities in the House. That has empowered any small group of GOP lawmakers to create headaches for party leaders.

These challenges have derailed Congress repeatedly. Last year, a standoff with Democrats led to the longest full shutdown in U.S. history at 43 days. The more recent Department of Homeland Security funding lapse set the record for the longest partial shutdown.

While Republicans passed the “One Big, Beautiful Bill” last summer, they have been less successful elsewhere. Through late April, the current Congress has enacted just 90 laws, an anemic pace. The previous Congress passed 274, the fewest since the Civil War.

Congress has also stayed out of certain fights. Trump sidestepped lawmakers on tariffs and military actions, even though the Constitution gives them the power to levy taxes and declare war. Last week, the White House said it would simply reset the clock in the Iran war, avoiding a 60-day requirement to seek approval from Congress.

SEE THE STORY
Ted Turner used his media riches to become one of America’s biggest landowners.

PHOTO: TED THAI/THE LIFE PICTURE COLLECTION/SHUTTERSTOCK

The founder of CNN, who died Wednesday at age 87, owned roughly 2 million acres of land in at least six U.S. states, making him the fourth-largest landowner in the country, according to the Land Report magazine. Turner used the land for conservation and ecotourism. Take a closer look at Turner’s real-estate holdings over the years.

HAPPENING TODAY
Economic data: The April jobs report is due. Earnings: Wendy’s, Enbridge, Embraer 📰 Today's paper

THE NUMBER
 $2,500

The cheapest resale ticket for a first-round game between Portugal and Colombia in the coming World Cup, according to TicketData, which tracks activity across resale sites. Slated for June 27 in Miami—and likely featuring Cristiano Ronaldo in his final World Cup—the game now costs more than the Super Bowl. On FIFA’s ticket-resale site this week, prices for Portugal-Colombia ranged from $2,300 to a staggering $5.75 million. And those didn’t include FIFA’s 15% fee to buyers, or its 15% fee to sellers.

AND FINALLY...
Broadway has a problem: Audiences won’t stop laughing.

Many plays and musicals are supposed to draw chuckles, including dramas looking to inject a little levity into heavy dialogue, and some in theater have been pushing to welcome more audience engagement. But theatergoers today are howling like they’re at a comedy show. They’re even snickering at serious moments. For many theater lovers, it’s no laughing matter . Actors are taking to Instagram to rant about poorly timed giggles. One playwright rewrote lines because laughter drowned out key dialogue and backstage cues.

emails.contentZh:
✏️ 自ChatGPT問世以來,人工智慧一直牢牢抓住政府與企業領袖的目光。但新一代AI模型——有能力透過網路攻擊對小鎮銀行、醫院及水務廠造成嚴重破壞——正引發新一波焦慮。這些新興威脅已顛覆了川普政府的AI發展藍圖,可能迫使政策轉向該產業一直遊說反對的方向:加強聯邦監管。

另外在AI議題上:《華爾街日報》首席經濟評論員Greg Ip探討了AI如何讓衡量經濟真實表現變得幾乎不可能。

艾瑪・塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條
一家聯邦貿易法院裁定,在最高法院推翻此前一批關稅後,川普總統並無權力施加新的全球關稅。美國疾病管制與預防中心正與世界衛生組織協調,協助全球衛生當局遏止一艘郵輪上爆發的漢他病毒疫情。沙烏地阿拉伯與科威特已解除對美軍使用其基地與空域的限制,先前這些限制曾阻擋荷莫茲海峽的「自由計畫」行動。法國檢方再次傳喚伊隆・馬斯克前往巴黎——這次是為了一項針對其社群媒體平台X的大規模調查中的初步刑事指控出庭。

市場即時看
道瓊期貨 49869.00 +169.00 +0.34% 標普500期貨 7401.50 +38.50 +0.52% 那斯達克100期貨 28894.75 +212.50 +0.74%
資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年5月8日美東時間上午5:36:18。
📈 全天追蹤我們的即時財經報導,投資人正等待4月就業報告出爐。

華爾街正在接管加密貨幣世界,而且幾乎沒有遇到什麼抵抗。惠而浦(Whirlpool)已連續70年發放股利。如今,它卻付不起股利了——投資人也開始質疑該公司的復甦計畫。花旗集團執行長Jane Fraser已經解決了一些大問題。現在是時候讓這家銀行證明自己能夠更上一層樓了,Telis Demos撰文。

獨家搶先看
一窺「自由計畫」內幕——川普重新開放波斯灣的行動胎死腹中。
本週稍早,伊朗向商船、美國海軍及美國盟友阿拉伯聯合大公國發射了一連串飛彈與無人機。美軍直升機擊沉了伊朗的快艇,伊朗的無人機則擊中了一艘民用船隻。在這期間的數小時,是自川普4月宣布停火以來衝突最嚴重的一次升級。然後,幾乎和開始時一樣快,川普下令暫停美軍引導船隻通過海峽的行動。總統在週二喊停這項行動,距離該計畫啟動僅36小時。船運再度陷入停滯。這項名為「自由計畫」的短命行動,暴露了川普在該地區斡旋能力的局限,Jared Malsin、Costas Paris、Shelby Holliday與Rebecca Feng報導。

魯柏・梅鐸對NFL發動一場高風險攻勢。
據一位知情人士透露,在一場白宮晚宴上,梅鐸警告川普,如果串流平台獲得更多賽事轉播權,將扼殺無線電視台。即便對這位以敢於大膽出招聞名的媒體大亨而言,這也是一次大膽的策略。福斯擔心失去賽事轉播權,造成一種罕見的局面——梅鐸試圖為一個福斯每年支付數十億美元的合作夥伴製造麻煩。此番遊說之際,司法部正在調查包括NFL在內的體育聯盟,是否應繼續享有代表球隊集體協商電視轉播權的反壟斷豁免。梅鐸此舉不僅凸顯了福斯的利害關係,也凸顯了其他主要媒體業者所面臨的風險,Dana Mattioli、Josh Dawsey、Andrew Beaton與Joe Flint報導。

搞懂AI對商業的影響。

專家問答
問:為什麼國會連基本工作都難以完成?
本屆會期以創紀錄的長時間政府關門、國會議員在伊朗戰爭議題上被邊緣化,以及一波即將卸任潮著稱。Tim Hanrahan、Ken Thomas與Lindsay Wise解釋為何做成的事愈來愈少:
答:原因有幾個。近年來黨派對立日益加劇,這抑制了達成協議的意願——因為與另一黨達成共識在政治上可能有風險。此外,近年來共和黨在眾議院僅維持極微弱多數,這讓任何一小群共和黨議員都能給黨內領導層製造麻煩。
這些難題已一再讓國會陷入停擺。去年,與民主黨的對峙導致史上最長的完整政府關門,長達43天。而近期國土安全部的資金缺口,則創下史上最長部分政府關門的紀錄。
儘管共和黨去年夏天通過了「一項偉大又美好的法案」,但在其他方面卻鮮少成功。截至4月下旬,本屆國會僅通過90項法律,步調疲弱。上屆國會通過了274項,是南北戰爭以來最少的一屆。

✏️ There’s free-market capitalism and state capitalism. Now, there’s Trump capitalism. In recent months, the president has extended his hand into American business in unorthodox and, to some corporate leaders, alarming ways. Some executives are so wary of the president seeking a stake in their companies that they have prepared for Oval Office meetings by rehearsing what they would say to fend off his advances, lobbyists involved in the preparations said. Others welcome the president’s attention. Our reporters in Washington explore how the Trump administration became an activist investor —and Wall Street’s scramble to adapt.

We’re taking you inside the global effort to figure out where hantavirus will strike next.

The public-health hunt for passengers from the MV Hondius cruise ship and anyone they came into close contact with is critical to limit the spread of an obscure form of hantavirus, a rat-borne infection that killed three people on board. The WHO and other health authorities say the threat to public health is low. The rat-borne infection rarely spreads between humans. Yet the ship’s passengers are at risk, as well as perhaps people they came into close and extended contact with after leaving the ship. That’s why the Hondius’s operator, plus health authorities around the world and airlines, are mobilizing to trace the paths of the ship’s travelers, report Xavier Martinez, Jennifer Calfas and Jacob Passy.
The U.S. and China are pursuing guardrails to stop their AI rivalry from spiraling into a crisis.

Washington and Beijing are weighing the launch of official discussions about artificial intelligence, said people familiar with the matter, as their AI competition threatens to become the arms race of the digital era. What’s more, government leaders in both countries recognize that powerful AI models could trigger crises neither side is prepared to manage, reports Lingling Wei. The deliberation comes as the White House and the Chinese government are considering putting AI on the agenda for a summit next week in Beijing between President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

Go inside the U.S.-China relationship.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: What is a ‘compute tax’ and why is the idea gaining traction?

With conversations already bubbling up in response to public sentiment about AI and doom and gloom predictions abounding, Katherine Bindley explains one proposal that’s been floated to manage AI’s rapid expansion:

A: The unknown economic impacts of AI are prompting some to revisit an old idea with a fresh face: a tax on AI processing, aka “compute.”

Many people are concerned about massive job losses as a result of AI, the concentration of the market, its consumption of resources and the community impact of expanding data centers. Some see taxation as a way to offset the loss of labor taxes and to fund social services.

In one scenario, companies that operate data centers would be taxed. In another, corporations and other users would be taxed on their consumption of tokens, AI’s key unit of measurement.

Others propose more issue-focused solutions rather than a blanket tax. The debate is only expected to grow ahead of the next election season.

For AI safety issues, regulations might be better than taxes. And with labor, other policies could be adjusted, according to Erik Brynjolfsson, director of the Stanford Digital Economy Lab.

While a realignment of labor and capital taxes could help, he adds, the broader solution is for AI to augment work instead of replacing it, and for the labor market to become more dynamic with portable benefits and job retraining.

Over 20,000 sailors are trapped in the Strait of Hormuz. This is who they call.

PHOTO: REUTERS; DANIEL BATEMAN/WSJ

As the regional coordinator for the International Transport Workers’ Federation, Mohamed Arrachedi is one of the few people to whom sailors stranded since the closure of the Strait of Hormuz can turn for help. So far, Arrachedi and his team have received more than 2,000 requests for assistance. Conditions in the strait, he said, are getting worse. Watch our video to see how the union rep responds to daily calls for help from sailors facing bombs and dwindling supplies.

公共衛生單位正全力搜尋「MV Hondius」號郵輪的乘客,以及任何曾與他們密切接觸的人,這對遏止一種罕見鼠傳漢他病毒的傳播至關重要——這種病毒已在船上造成三人死亡。世界衛生組織及其他衛生當局表示,對公眾健康的威脅偏低。這種鼠傳感染病極少人傳人。然而,這艘郵輪的乘客,以及他們離船後或曾密切、長時間接觸的人,都存在風險。這正是為何Hondius號的營運方,加上全球各地的衛生當局及航空公司,都在動員追蹤這艘船乘客的行蹤,Xavier Martinez、Jennifer Calfas與Jacob Passy報導。

美中兩國正試圖為雙方的AI競賽設下護欄,以防止其失控演變成危機。
據熟悉此事的人士透露,華府與北京正權衡展開有關人工智慧的官方對話,因為兩國的AI競爭正有淪為數位時代軍備競賽的風險。此外,兩國政府領導人都認識到,強大的AI模型可能引發雙方都無力應對的危機,魏玲靈報導。這項磋商正值白宮與中國政府考慮將AI議題列入下週北京峰會議程之際,屆時川普總統將與中國領導人習近平會晤。

專家問答
問:什麼是「運算稅」,為何這個想法逐漸受到關注?
隨著針對AI的公眾情緒及末日預測早已引發討論,Katherine Bindley解釋了一項為管理AI快速擴張而提出的方案:
答:AI帶來的未知經濟衝擊,促使一些人重新審視一個老想法、給它換上新面貌:對AI處理能力(即「運算力」)徵稅。
許多人擔心AI導致大規模失業、市場集中,以及資源消耗和資料中心擴張對社區的影響。有些人將徵稅視為抵消勞動稅損失、資助社會服務的一種方式。
在一種情境中,經營資料中心的公司將被課稅。在另一種情境中,企業及其他使用者則將根據其消耗的代幣(AI的核心計量單位)被課稅。
其他人則提議採取更具針對性的解決方案,而非一律課稅。這場辯論預計將在下一個選舉季來臨前愈演愈烈。
史丹佛數位經濟實驗室主任Erik Brynjolfsson表示,在AI安全問題上,監管或許比課稅更有效。而在勞動議題上,其他政策則可以進行調整。
他補充說,雖然調整勞動與資本稅制或許有幫助,但更廣泛的解決方案,是讓AI增強工作而非取代工作,並讓勞動市場透過可攜式福利與職業再培訓變得更具彈性。

READ IT HERE FIRST
AI is forcing CEOs to make a stark choice: Lay off workers or make them do more.

Axon Enterprise President Josh Isner recently emailed the Taser maker’s more than 5,000 staffers and told them to essentially breathe: AI won’t trigger layoffs anytime soon, he assured them. Isner’s message underscores the extreme anxiety in American corporations over how many jobs could be lost to AI’s powers to speed up and supplant much of white-collar work. Among executives making such decisions, a split is emerging: Use AI to shrink the workforce or stretch it? Those diverging philosophies have been on display on earnings calls and in other recent announcements. Neither camp calls for more hiring anytime soon, report Chip Cutter and Lindsay Ellis.
A storied toolmaker closes its last hometown plant—and blames its tape measures.

Stanley Black & Decker will soon close its last factory in New Britain, Conn., ending its manufacturing work in a town the Stanley brothers turned into a hub of industry 183 years ago. The toolmaker says fewer buyers want the Connecticut plant’s single-sided tape measures, preferring double-sided ones made abroad instead. The idea that single-sided tape measures are becoming obsolete has provoked skepticism , starting with devotees of Stanley’s products. Some trade workers say the plant’s tape measures were the best money could buy. Current and former workers at the plant described the obsolescence rationale as camouflage for a cold-eyed decision to offshore manufacturing to a lower-cost country, reports John Keilman. Stanley said it explored all options to keep the plant open.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: Why are airlines cracking down on portable power banks?

The popular carry-on item is a leading cause of cabin fires , sparking more incidents than any other rechargeable device. Such risks have prompted airlines to add new precautions on top of banning charging them during flights, reports Amira McKee.

A: American Airlines last week prohibited passengers from recharging power banks using in-flight outlets, matching the policies of Delta Air Lines and Southwest Airlines. Some international carriers have taken even stronger steps.

The airplane fire threat is a side effect of the proliferation of cellphones, tablets and other electronic devices powered by rechargeable batteries. More travelers are toting portable chargers to keep their digital equipment powered throughout their journeys.

All lithium batteries can uncontrollably heat and catch fire through a chemical chain reaction known as thermal runaway. Power banks are especially vulnerable, because unlike cellphones or laptops, they are often made without built-in protection against fires.

Adding to the risk: Many of the power banks are cheaply made or even counterfeit, and passengers handle them with less care than their more expensive electronics, said Jeff Marootian, chief executive of safety firm UL Standards & Engagement.

In March, the International Civil Aviation Organization said the products should be within arm’s reach and never charged onboard. The FAA, which said it is considering the organization’s stricter guidance, currently bars the devices from checked luggage and restricts passengers to two portable chargers in carry-on bags.

But airlines’ rules vary, leaving passengers to navigate different restrictions on their portable chargers from one airline to the next.

SEE THE STORY
Our travel columnist tried out a $60 capsule hotel in Honolulu.

PHOTO: DAWN GILBERTSON/WSJ

WSJ’s travel columnist Dawn Gilbertson recently spent two nights at First Cabin International Hawaii, the first U.S. outpost of the popular Japanese capsule-hotel chain. The hotel, located a block from Waikiki Beach, opened a year ago with 103 pods. The tiny, no-frills cubes have room for a bed and not much else. But the price was more than right, Dawn writes. It cost $60 a night for a single-occupancy, premium-economy pod—a solid budget option in a destination where the average daily hotel-room rate topped $280 in 2025, according to CoStar.

 $200

That’s how much supercommuter Nicole Smith’s monthly fillups have increased compared with earlier this year. Smith drives 50 miles each way, three times a week, from Fredericksburg, Va., to the nation’s capital. As the ranks of America’s marathon commuters grow, many are being stung by rising fuel prices . Driving an average fuel-economy car 75 miles each way, every weekday, could cost roughly $500 a month to keep the tank filled just for commutes at today’s prices, if they prove sticky.

AND FINALLY...
The boy band heyday may be over—but the ‘man band’ era has just begun.

There’s money in man bands this summer. The Backstreet Boys are no longer boys—the oldest, Kevin Richardson, is 54, and the youngest, Nick Carter, is 46—but they’re commanding thousands of dollars from now-grown-up fans for tickets and travel. The group’s residency last summer at the Sphere in Las Vegas grossed more than $55 million on ticket sales, according to Billboard Boxscore. Other big acts from the ’90s and 2000s, like Boyz II Men and the Jonas Brothers, are also finding new demand on the reunion and nostalgia-obsessed touring circuit.

記憶體製造商是科技界目前最炙手可熱的類股,Dan Gallagher撰文。但它們是否賺得太多了?

獨家搶先看
AI迫使執行長們做出殘酷抉擇:裁員,或讓員工做更多事。
Axon Enterprise總裁Josh Isner最近向這家泰瑟槍製造商5000多名員工發送郵件,基本上要他們放寬心:AI短期內不會導致裁員,他向他們保證。Isner的訊息凸顯了美國企業界對於AI強大的加速及取代大量白領工作的能力,將導致多少工作崗位流失所懷有的極端焦慮。在做出此類決策的高管當中,一種分歧正在浮現:利用AI縮減人力,還是讓人力發揮更大效用?這兩種不同的哲學,已在近期的財報電話會議及其他公告中展現出來。無論哪一派,短期內都不打算擴大招聘,Chip Cutter與Lindsay Ellis報導。

一家歷史悠久的工具製造商關閉了它在家鄉的最後一座工廠——並將原因歸咎於它的捲尺。
史丹利百得即將關閉其在康乃狄克州新不列顛市的最後一座工廠,結束了該公司在這座由史丹利兄弟183年前打造成工業重鎮的城市中的製造業務。這家工具製造商表示,買家愈來愈少想要這座康乃狄克工廠生產的單面捲尺,轉而偏好從海外進口的雙面捲尺。單面捲尺正在過時的說法,已引發質疑——首當其衝的是史丹利產品的忠實愛好者。一些從事貿易工作的人士表示,這座工廠生產的捲尺是金錢能買到的最好產品。該工廠現任及前任員工形容,所謂「過時」的說法,只是為了掩飾一項將製造業外移到成本更低國家的冷酷決定,John Keilman報導。史丹利表示,公司已探索過所有讓工廠維持營運的方案。

專家問答
問:為什麼航空公司開始嚴格限制隨身電源?
記者Amira McKee報導,這種受歡迎的隨身物品是艙內火災的主要原因,引發的事故比任何其他充電式設備都多。這類風險已促使航空公司在禁止在飛行途中充電之外,新增了額外的預防措施。
答:美國航空上週已禁止乘客使用機上插座為行動電源充電,與達美航空及西南航空的政策一致。部分國際航空公司已採取更嚴格的措施。
飛機火災風險,是手機、平板及其他由可充電電池供電設備普及化所帶來的副作用。愈來愈多旅客攜帶行動電源,以確保旅途中電子設備電力充足。
所有鋰電池都可能透過一種名為「熱失控」的化學連鎖反應而失控過熱並起火。行動電源尤其脆弱,因為與手機或筆電不同,它們往往沒有內建的防火保護裝置。
安全公司UL Standards & Engagement執行長Jeff Marootian表示,增加風險的是:許多行動電源製造粗糙,甚至是仿冒品,而乘客對待它們的謹慎程度也不及對待較昂貴的電子設備。
今年3月,國際民航組織表示,這類產品應保持在伸手可及之處,且絕不應在機上充電。美國聯邦航空總署表示正考慮採納該組織更嚴格的指導方針,目前該局禁止此類設備放入托運行李,並限制乘客隨身攜帶最多兩顆行動電源。
但各航空公司的規定不一,讓乘客在不同航空公司之間必須應對不同的行動電源限制。

The great $110 trillion wealth transfer won’t happen any time soon.

Financial advisory firms like to talk about a looming event called “the great wealth transfer,” where the huge and very wealthy baby-boomer generation dies off and their children inherit their money. But the process may be more of a slow drip than a sudden windfall. People are living longer, and wealthy Americans in particular are spending large sums on longevity. When they do die, many will pass wealth first to their spouses. Boomers are still getting windfalls from their own elderly parents. Many Americans of modest means won’t inherit anything at all, report Rachel Louise Ensign and James Benedict.
Meet the secret team blowing up Ford's assembly line to make a $30,000 electric truck.

Ford’s secret project, kicked off in 2022, had an ambitious goal: to figure out how to make electric vehicles in the U.S. that could compete with the Chinese models clobbering competitors globally. The secret is now out as Ford races toward building its first model, a new truck it says will travel around 300 miles on a single charge and feature in-car technology to compete with Tesla and China. It’s aiming for a 2027 launch and a price tag of around $30,000. Getting there means tearing up a century of manufacturing practices in a notoriously hidebound industry. At stake for Ford is securing a future beyond the gas-guzzling pickups and SUVs that have long defined its bottom line, reports Sharon Terlep.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: What is hantavirus, the rodent-borne virus at the center of a cruise-ship outbreak?

Xavier Martinez explains what to know about the rare but potentially deadly disease .

A: Three people are dead and several others are ill after a suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean. Hantavirus is a family of viruses carried by rodents and spread to humans through contact with infected urine, droppings or saliva.

The most dangerous form in the Americas attacks the lungs, and about 38% of people who develop respiratory symptoms die. There is no vaccine and no cure; doctors can only manage symptoms and support breathing.

Hantavirus almost never spreads person to person, which makes this suspected outbreak especially unusual. The exception is a particular strain found primarily in Chile and Argentina—and the ship departed from Ushuaia, Argentina, last month.

“Seeing something on a cruise ship like a hantavirus infection is not something that's on anybody's bingo card,” said one immunologist. Authorities are still working to determine the source of exposure on board.

Home-security camera companies are embracing AI to give customers detailed descriptions of their surveillance, instead of generic motion alerts. The notifications are often spot on. 理財顧問公司喜歡談論一個即將到來的事件,稱為「巨大的財富轉移」——龐大且極為富裕的嬰兒潮世代逐漸凋零,其子女繼承他們的財富。但這個過程可能更像是細水長流,而非突如其來的巨額橫財。人們壽命變長,尤其是富裕的美國人,正花費鉅資延長壽命。等到他們真的過世時,許多人會先把財富傳給配偶。嬰兒潮世代本身,也仍在從他們年邁的父母身上獲得意外之財。許多財力普通的美國人,則根本繼承不到任何東西,Rachel Louise Ensign與James Benedict報導。

問:什麼是漢他病毒——這種郵輪疫情核心的鼠傳病毒?
Xavier Martinez說明關於這種罕見卻可能致命疾病的必知事項。
答:一艘郵輪在大西洋上疑似爆發漢他病毒疫情後,已造成三人死亡,另有多人染病。漢他病毒是一類由囓齒動物攜帶、透過接觸受感染的尿液、排泄物或唾液傳染給人類的病毒。
在美洲最危險的病毒株會攻擊肺部,出現呼吸道症狀者中約有38%會死亡。目前沒有疫苗也沒有解藥;醫生只能控制症狀並協助患者維持呼吸。
漢他病毒幾乎不會人傳人,這使得這起疑似疫情爆發格外不尋常。例外情況是主要出現在智利與阿根廷的一種特定病毒株——而這艘郵輪上個月正是從阿根廷的烏斯懷亞出發的。
「在郵輪上看到漢他病毒感染這種事,根本沒人料到過。」一位免疫學家說。當局仍在調查船上感染源。

Almost everyone loses—except a few sharks—on prediction markets. Here’s why.

For all types of bets, Polymarket and Kalshi make a simple pitch—users can monetize what they already know to make a quick buck—that has taken the world by storm . And yet, on Polymarket, 67% of profits go to just 0.1% of accounts, report Neil Mehta, Katherine Long and Caitlin Ostroff. On Kalshi, too, losers outnumber winners. The pros shell out for access to big-data streams from third-party providers to gain an edge. Casual traders “have no chance. Systematically,” a former professional poker player and statistician tells the Journal. Kalshi spokeswoman Elisabeth Diana said there are 2.9 unprofitable users for each profitable one based on data from the past month, and a figure subject to change as the exchange grows. A spokeswoman for Polymarket declined to comment.
A former WSJ columnist let AI look at her breasts—and she says she’s glad she did.

Joanna Stern wrote technology columns at the Journal for 12 years. “So you know I’ll do almost anything for a story,” she says. Joanna spent a year letting AI into as many parts of her life as she could. That experiment became her new book, “I Am Not a Robot: My Year Using AI for Almost Everything.” In this exclusive excerpt , she explains how new technology could improve the odds for women like herself who have an elevated risk of cancer.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: What can we learn from Berkshire CEO Greg Abel’s first annual shareholder meeting?

Abel was (mostly) all business in his debut as MC at the conglomerate’s meeting in Omaha, reports WSJ’s Krystal Hur.

A: Greg Abel succeeded Warren Buffett in January. Buffett was at the meeting, but this time sat in the first row with the other Berkshire directors. Abel paid several homages to Buffett throughout the Saturday meeting, acknowledging the former CEO’s role in shaping the company and its unusual business model.

But other parts of the meeting were less sentimental. The new CEO opened the meeting with a detailed breakdown of Berkshire’s businesses that ran around a half-hour longer than expected. The new take to the meeting was a departure from a more casual and folksy approach.

There were also key updates from the first quarter. Berkshire’s operating earnings rose 18% to $11.35 billion from $9.64 billion a year ago, and its cash pile swelled to a record $381.1 billion after accounting for a payable for purchasing some short-term government debt. Abel said Saturday that Berkshire has a shortlist of companies it is interested in either taking a stake in or acquiring entirely when the price is right.

These are the hiring hot spots where college grads are landing good jobs.

A string of cities across America’s Sunbelt are emerging as graduate-hiring hot spots in an otherwise challenging job market for young professionals, according to a new study by payroll processor ADP. Six of the list’s top 10—including Raleigh, N.C.; Tulsa, Okla.; and Charlotte, N.C.—are in the South. Other pockets of the country like Columbus, Ohio and California’s San Jose area also punch above their weight as early-career launchpads for their mix of hiring, pay and affordability. Nicknamed after the pop star who owns a waterfront mansion in Westerly, R.I., the tax is set to take effect in July. The measure exemplifies a trend playing out across the U.S. State and local governments are seizing on a juicy new target for plugging budget holes and easing housing shortages: second homeowners. The taxes are generating furious debate.

Americans will do anything to get Indian mangoes.

Welcome to Indian mango season in America, when a devoted and slightly unhinged community descends into a collective frenzy over the fruit. The faithful are leaving work, stalking WhatsApp groups and paying lobster prices for their fix. Importers field calls around the clock during this short but sweet season. Walk into any American grocery store and the mango on offer is almost certainly Mexican. At $10 a box, it’s affordable. But devotees swear Indian mangoes—typically priced at $50-$60 a box—are essentially a different fruit.

順帶一提亞馬遜:今天大都會慈善晚宴(Met Gala)回歸,這場耗資數百萬美元的盛會,由傑夫・貝佐斯及Lauren Sánchez Bezos私人出資贊助。大都會晚宴吸引的不僅僅是名人;一些商界重量級人物如今也成了紅毯上的常客。我們將全程關注並解析這場時尚界最盛大的夜晚之一。

在預測市場上,幾乎所有人都會輸——除了少數幾條大鯊魚。這是為什麼。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: When Shooting Suspects Turn to Chatbots
emails.contentEn:
✏️ A university student wanted to know how many classmates he’d need to kill to become notorious. ChatGPT had an answer. “Usually 3 or more dead, 5-6 total victims, pushes it onto national media,” the chatbot told Phoenix Ikner just minutes before prosecutors say he killed two people and injured six others at Florida State. The Journal’s Georgia Wells reports on the latest chilling case of a shooting suspect discussing violence with a chatbot —and the debate inside AI companies about the trade-offs between user privacy and potential violence.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES
The jet-fuel cost crisis that took down Spirit Airlines is turning into a disaster for the entire industry , especially budget airlines. Sean Curran rescued President Trump from an assassination attempt in Butler, Pa. About two years later, he has to answer for another . Departing Fed Chair Jerome Powell didn’t want to stay on the central bank’s board, but concluded he had no choice due to Trump’s legal challenges. The pressure on OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is mounting as the company prepares for an IPO, writes Tim Higgins. Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez Bezos have become front-row fixtures at fashion shows through business expansion and charitable giving.

FROM THE MARKETS
A war that seemed primed to pummel emerging economies reliant on Middle East imports hasn’t done the same to their stock markets, with AI and oil exports buoying shares from South Korea to Brazil . Stock indexes are contorting themselves to include SpaceX and OpenAI whether you like it or not, writes James Mackintosh.

READ IT HERE FIRST
ChatGPT is wrestling with its most chilling conversation: How do I plan an attack?

Florida State University student Phoenix Ikner uploaded an image of a handgun and asked OpenAI’s chatbot how to use it. Was there a safety to switch off? ChatGPT told him there wasn’t, according to a transcript reviewed by WSJ. Ikner logged off and, just minutes later, killed two people and injured six, prosecutors say. The case is one of at least two in just over a year in which mass shooting suspects have turned to AI chatbots as confidants to discuss violence. The carnage is sparking lawsuits, investigations and internal debate inside AI companies over when and how to intervene. Ikner has pleaded not guilty to charges of murder and attempted murder. OpenAI has said it trains its models to discourage users from committing real-world harm.
ActBlue has become integral to the Democratic Party. It's spending big—and mired in internal drama.

The fundraising platform is enmeshed in controversy fueled in part by the management style of CEO Regina Wallace-Jones, whose spending and legal decisions have raised concerns among Democrats and employees, report Tarini Parti, Josh Dawsey and Anthony DeBarros. Wallace-Jones, a former tech executive, has tried to run the group not like the political nonprofit that it is, but like a Silicon Valley firm that’s acquiring startups to stay relevant, according to people familiar with ActBlue’s operations. Now, the group faces investigations from the DOJ and Republicans in Congress that threaten a key cog of Democrats’ strategy to retake majorities in the House and Senate.

Follow the energy transition.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: What will the shutdown of Spirit Airlines mean for travelers?

The low-cost airline has been the butt of plenty of jokes. Columnist Dawn Gilbertson wrote about why she’s going to miss it —and why she thinks the haters will, too.

A: Whenever anyone asked me about flying Spirit Airlines, I gave what might be a surprising answer: It’s perfectly fine.

Not for everyone, to be sure. But a solid, affordable option for that Florida, Vegas or Caribbean vacation, as long as you knew what you were in for. Namely, those fees for everything including carry-on bags, soft drinks, coffee, cramped seats that didn’t recline and rocky reliability.

For many travelers on a budget, Spirit, like fellow discounter and one-time merger partner Frontier, was the difference between jetting off on vacation or staying closer to home.

Even if you never flew Spirit, you benefited from the airline’s presence. Competing airlines vigorously matched its fares, even if it was with one of those no-frills basic economy tickets. With Spirit gone, you can bet that dirt-cheap fares to Florida, for example, will be harder to come by.

SEE THE STORY
The U.S. wants to break China’s drone dominance. Here’s where it will struggle.

MERRILL SHERMAN

With drones revolutionizing the battlefield in Ukraine, Iran and beyond, the U.S. is striving to dominate this latest evolution in military technology. There’s just one problem: China got there first. In a series of graphics , we break down the parts that go into a typical FPV drone to show where the Pentagon might succeed—and where it’s likely to face challenges.

Monday: The Met Gala. The trial resumes in Elon Musk’s suit against OpenAI and its co-founders. Tuesday: Trade data for March. Primaries in Indiana. Wednesday: The ADP releases private payroll figures for April. Friday: The April jobs report is due. And a four-part adaptation of “Lord of the Flies” arrives on Netflix; check out what else is happening in arts & culture this week here .

The share of young men who said religion is very important to them in 2025, up sharply from 28% in 2023, and overtaking young women, according to a Gallup poll released in April. Gen Z is flocking to church for community, faith and dates thanks to meetup groups such as “Pizza to Pews” and “Holy Girl Walk.”

AND FINALLY...
An 62-year-old man is on a mission to whistle in the NFL.

Professional whistler Chris Ullman has performed for a U.S. president, on the “Tonight Show” and at a recent Baltimore Orioles game. He’s also been met with blank stares. Ullman, who had long careers in government and at investment giant Carlyle Group, sends “Happy Birthday” whistle-grams to former colleagues, including Fed Chair Jerome Powell and former Virginia Gov. Glenn Youngkin. Now, he’s on a mission to check what he sees as the final box of an award-winning career: whistling the national anthem at an NFL game.

✏️ 一名大學生想知道,要殺害多少同學才能變得惡名昭彰。ChatGPT給出了答案。「通常3人以上死亡,總計5到6名受害者,就會登上全國媒體版面,」這個聊天機器人告訴Phoenix Ikner——就在檢方指控他於佛羅里達州立大學殺害兩人、傷及六人的短短數分鐘之前。《華爾街日報》記者Georgia Wells報導了這起最新令人不寒而慄的案例——槍擊嫌犯與聊天機器人討論暴力行為——以及AI公司內部關於用戶隱私與潛在暴力風險之間權衡的辯論。

艾瑪・塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條
導致精神航空倒閉的航空燃油成本危機,正演變成整個航空業、尤其是廉價航空公司的災難。曾在賓州巴特勒救下川普總統一命、使其逃過刺殺的Sean Curran,如今約兩年後,得為另一起事件負責。即將卸任的聯準會主席傑羅姆・鮑爾原本不想繼續留任央行董事會,但因川普的法律挑戰,他認為自己別無選擇。OpenAI執行長山姆・奧特曼所承受的壓力正與日俱增,原因是該公司正為IPO做準備,Tim Higgins撰文。傑夫・貝佐斯與Lauren Sánchez Bezos透過業務擴張及慈善捐助,已成為時裝秀前排的常客。

市場消息
一場原本似乎將重創依賴中東進口的新興經濟體的戰爭,卻沒有對這些經濟體的股市造成同樣衝擊——AI及石油出口正撐起從南韓到巴西的股市,James Mackintosh撰文,股市指數正扭曲自身,不管你喜不喜歡,都得把SpaceX和OpenAI納入其中。

獨家搶先看
ChatGPT正應對它最令人不寒而慄的對話:我該如何策劃一場攻擊?
佛羅里達州立大學學生Phoenix Ikner上傳了一張手槍照片,詢問OpenAI的聊天機器人如何使用它。有沒有保險栓需要關掉?根據《華爾街日報》查閱的一份對話紀錄,ChatGPT告訴他沒有。Ikner登出後,短短幾分鐘內,檢方指控他殺害兩人、傷及六人。這起案例是過去一年多來,至少第二起大規模槍擊案嫌犯將AI聊天機器人當作討論暴力行為的知己。這起慘案正引發訴訟、調查,以及AI公司內部關於何時、如何介入的辯論。Ikner已對謀殺及殺人未遂指控表示不認罪。OpenAI表示,他們訓練其模型,以勸阻用戶對現實世界造成傷害。

ActBlue已成為民主黨不可或缺的一環。它正大手筆花錢——並深陷內部風暴。
這個籌款平台深陷爭議,部分原因來自執行長Regina Wallace-Jones的管理風格——她的支出及法律決策已引發民主黨人士及員工的擔憂,Tarini Parti、Josh Dawsey與Anthony DeBarros報導。據熟悉ActBlue營運情況的人士透露,這位前科技業高管Wallace-Jones,試圖不把該組織當作它本質上的政治非營利機構經營,而是像一家為了保持競爭力而收購新創公司的矽谷企業般運作。如今,該組織面臨司法部及國會共和黨人的調查,這些調查威脅到民主黨奪回眾參兩院多數席位策略中的一個關鍵環節。

追蹤能源轉型議題。

專家問答
問:精神航空的倒閉對旅客而言意味著什麼?
這家廉價航空一直是不少笑話的箭靶。專欄作家Dawn Gilbertson撰文說明她為何會懷念它——以及她認為那些嘲笑它的人其實也會懷念它。
答:每當有人問我對搭乘精神航空的看法,我的回答可能會令人意外:其實還算不錯。
當然不是對每個人都適用。但對於佛羅里達、拉斯維加斯或加勒比海度假來說,它是個可靠又實惠的選擇,前提是你清楚自己會面對什麼。也就是說,你得為隨身行李、軟性飲料、咖啡、狹窄且無法後仰的座椅,以及不太穩定的準點率支付各種額外費用。
對許多預算有限的旅客而言,精神航空與同為廉航、曾是合併夥伴的邊疆航空一樣,是能否成行度假或只能待在家附近的關鍵差別。
即使你從未搭過精神航空,你也因這家航空公司的存在而受惠。競爭對手為了與其票價抗衡,會積極跟進調降,即便只是那種陽春的基本經濟艙票種。如今精神航空消失了,可以肯定的是,例如飛往佛羅里達的超低票價將愈來愈難找到。

當看新聞
美國想打破中國在無人機領域的主導地位。以下是它將面臨困難之處。
MERRILL SHERMAN
隨著無人機在烏克蘭、伊朗及其他地方徹底改變戰場面貌,美國正努力主導這項軍事科技的最新演進。問題只有一個:中國早已捷足先登。透過一系列圖表,我們拆解了一台典型第一人稱視角(FPV)無人機的組成部件,呈現五角大廈可能成功、以及可能面臨挑戰的環節。

本週焦點
週一:大都會慈善晚宴。伊隆・馬斯克控告OpenAI及其共同創辦人的訴訟審理繼續進行。週二:3月貿易數據。印第安納州舉行初選。週三:ADP發布4月民間就業數據。週五:4月就業報告即將公布。此外,四集改編版《蒼蠅王》即將登陸Netflix;點此查看本週藝文界還有哪些動態。

數字看新聞
42%
根據4月公布的一項蓋洛普民調,2025年表示宗教對自己非常重要的年輕男性比例,較2023年的28%大幅攀升,並已超越年輕女性。Z世代正湧向教會,尋求群體歸屬、信仰,以及約會機會——這要歸功於「披薩到教堂」及「神聖女孩散步」等聚會團體。

最後,別錯過...
一位62歲的男子立志要在NFL吹口哨。
專業口哨表演者Chris Ullman曾為一位美國總統表演過,也曾登上《今夜秀》,以及最近一場巴爾的摩金鶯隊比賽。他也曾遭遇過一臉茫然的白眼。曾長年任職於政府及凱雷投資集團的Ullman,會向包括聯準會主席傑羅姆・鮑爾及前維吉尼亞州長Glenn Youngkin在內的前同事,傳送「生日快樂」口哨祝賀影片。如今,他立志要完成他心目中獲獎生涯的最後一塊拼圖:在NFL比賽中用口哨吹奏國歌。

emails.contentEn:
✏️ Spirit Airlines’ time ran out Thursday evening. In a 15-minute phone call, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Spirit CEO Dave Davis agreed that the budget carrier had exhausted alternatives. The brief conversation marked the end to a weekslong saga —and spelled the final chapter for a company that helped pioneer the ultradiscount model in the U.S.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES
President Trump ordered the withdrawal of 5,000 U.S. troops from Germany, escalating his clash with Berlin and NATO allies over their reluctance to support the war in Iran. The war, meanwhile, has offered China, Russia and North Korea a rare opportunity to learn about the capabilities and limitations of the U.S. military. Prospective candidates for the 2028 Democratic presidential primary race are already meeting major donors . The governor of Mexico’s northwestern Sinaloa state said he would temporarily step down after the U.S. charged him and other officials with drug trafficking. Michael Jackson’s biopic blinds us from the truth , writes Maureen Orth, who chronicled accusations of the singer’s serial pedophilia for Vanity Fair.

FROM THE MARKETS
Major stock indexes closed at fresh records after Iran handed Washington a new proposal for ending the war. Fed officials are no longer arguing about when to resume cutting, but are starting to talk about the conditions that would warrant a hike , writes Nick Timiraos. GameStop is preparing to make an offer for eBay , part of CEO Ryan Cohen’s plan to turn the retailer into a $100 billion-plus juggernaut. U.S. foreclosure filings hit a six-year high in the first quarter, and fast-rising homeownership costs are partly to blame.

READ IT HERE FIRST
This is how the Trump administration’s Spirit Airlines rescue unraveled.

Talks led by Lutnick couldn’t get bondholders and the government aligned, report Brian Schwartz, Alison Sider and Alexander Gladstone. Davis, the Spirit CEO, thanked Lutnick for his efforts leading the rescue talks. The commerce secretary referred the executive to the Transportation Department for help in winding down the Florida airline . The brief conversation marked the end to a weekslong saga featuring negotiations between members of Trump’s inner circle, executives leading major U.S. airlines, and investment firms wrapped up in Spirit’s bankruptcy.
OpenAI wants to go public. First, Sarah Friar needs to get it to grow up.

The chief financial officer, a veteran of Goldman Sachs, was brought in to give the AI startup the financial credibility needed to go public. Since then, Friar has spent months walking back CEO Sam Altman’s claims about spending—at times putting her at odds with her free-wheeling boss. She follows a line of women in Silicon Valley asked to tame the wilder impulses of companies—or their younger male founders. This time, she doesn’t have much room for error, report Berber Jin and Corrie Driebusch. If she moves too slowly, OpenAI could fall behind and hit the market behind Anthropic. Move too quickly, and she could stretch the business thin.

Every week, get a curated tour of our unique take on the sports world.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: Dr. Casey Means is a MAHA hero. Why did her surgeon general nomination fail?

Means was tapped for the job last year but Trump withdrew her nomination this week. Reporter Liz Essley White wrote about what went wrong for her.

A: Means was making a last-ditch attempt to win over Sen. Lisa Murkowski on a phone call Monday. But she found it difficult to get the senator to focus on her “Make America Healthy Again” message about the burden of chronic disease in America.

Instead, Murkowski asked whether she had fully vaccinated her infant son, Means said.

“I felt that it was extremely inappropriate,” she said. “I told her that sharing my family’s personal health information was absolutely out of the scope of this conversation.”

A Murkowski spokesman said the senator doesn’t disclose the contents of private conversations.

Three days later, as it became clear Means didn’t have enough support in the Senate for confirmation, Trump announced on Truth Social that he had a new surgeon general nominee and thanked Means for her service. It was the end of a year-long journey for the Stanford graduate who dropped out of her surgical residency to pursue holistic medicine.

Now, the failure of her nomination is prompting sharp barbs on social media as Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. blames Senate health committee chairman Sen. Bill Cassidy for delays that doomed Means. It has also put front and center some senators’ unease with the MAHA movement’s vaccine skepticism, and the White House’s attempt to manage the issue.

SEE THE STORY
How far does $1,000 get you on a trip to Venice? Take a look.

PHOTOS: SCARLETT CASCIELLO FOR WSJ

The Italian city is famous for its high prices and dense crowds. But our writer’s recent trip, which had a strict budget, proved that it’s possible to avoid both —especially if you're willing to visit during the fall shoulder season.

HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND
Saturday: Berkshire Hathaway’s annual shareholders meeting. The Kentucky Derby. Sunday: The Miami Grand Prix Formula One race, where team Mercedes hopes to extend its winning streak. OPEC meets for the first time since the U.A.E. quit the organization. The Milken Institute’s Global Conference begins. 📰 Today's paper

THE NUMBER
 $224,900

The base price for the 2026 Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series, a sub-brand that competes with Rolls-Royce and Bentley. But is the 577-horsepower luxury convertible in good taste? The Journal’s Dan Neil took the two-seater for a test drive to find out.

AND FINALLY...
BlackBerry stopped making phones—but it’s still running your life.

An astonishing number of people still rely on the company that once made phones with clicky keyboards —and they don’t realize it. Blackberry’s most lucrative product is not hardware, but the hidden software in 275 million cars on the road today. In fact, the company’s essential technology can be found in all sorts of unexpected places, writes Ben Cohen.

✏️ 精神航空的大限在週四晚間到來。在一通僅15分鐘的電話中,商務部長Howard Lutnick與精神航空執行長Dave Davis達成共識:這家廉價航空已經耗盡所有替代方案。這通簡短的通話,為一場歷時數週的救援風波畫下句點——也為這家曾在美國開創超廉價航空模式的公司,寫下最後一章。

艾瑪・塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條
川普總統下令從德國撤出5000名美軍,使他與柏林及北約盟國因對方不願支持伊朗戰爭而起的衝突進一步升級。與此同時,這場戰爭也為中國、俄羅斯及北韓提供了一個難得的機會,得以摸清美軍的能力與極限。有意角逐2028年民主黨總統初選的人選,已開始會見主要金主。墨西哥西北部錫那羅亞州州長表示,在美國以販毒罪起訴他和其他官員後,他將暫時卸任。曾為《浮華世界》記錄麥可・傑克森連環戀童指控的Maureen Orth撰文表示,麥可・傑克森的傳記電影蒙蔽了真相。

市場消息
在伊朗向華府提出結束戰爭的新提案後,主要股指收於歷史新高。聯準會官員已不再爭論何時恢復降息,而是開始討論可能需要升息的情境條件,Nick Timiraos撰文。GameStop正準備對eBay提出收購要約,這是執行長Ryan Cohen將這家零售商打造成市值逾1000億美元巨頭計畫的一環。美國第一季法拍申請案創六年新高,快速攀升的購屋成本是部分原因。

獨家搶先看
這就是川普政府拯救精神航空的計畫如何功虧一簣的過程。
由Lutnick主導的談判,始終無法讓債券持有人與政府達成一致,Brian Schwartz、Alison Sider與Alexander Gladstone報導。精神航空執行長Davis感謝Lutnick為主導這場救援談判所做的努力。這位商務部長將這位高管轉介給運輸部,協助處理這家佛羅里達航空公司的清盤事宜。這通簡短的通話,為一場歷時數週的風波畫下句點——期間涉及川普核心圈成員、美國各大航空公司高管,以及捲入精神航空破產案的投資公司之間的談判。

OpenAI想要上市。首先,Sarah Friar得先讓公司「長大」。
這位曾任職於高盛的財務長,是被延攬來為這家AI新創公司賦予上市所需的財務公信力。此後,Friar花了數月時間,收回執行長山姆・奧特曼對支出的種種說法——這有時讓她與這位我行我素的老闆意見相左。她延續了矽谷一連串被要求馴服公司(或年輕男性創辦人)野性衝動的女性行列。這一次,她幾乎沒有犯錯的空間,Berber Jin與Corrie Driebusch報導。如果她動作太慢,OpenAI可能落後,甚至在上市時間點上輸給Anthropic。動作太快,又可能讓公司的財務被拉得太緊繃。

每週為你帶來一趟精心策劃的體育世界獨特導覽。

專家問答
問:Casey Means醫生是MAHA運動的英雄人物。為何她的公共衛生局局長提名以失敗告終?
Means去年獲提名擔任此職,但川普本週撤回了她的提名。記者Liz Essley White撰文說明她出了什麼問題。
答:Means在週一一通電話中,做出最後一搏,試圖爭取參議員Lisa Murkowski的支持。但她發現很難讓這位參議員聚焦在她關於美國慢性病負擔的「讓美國再度健康」(MAHA)訊息上。
相反地,Murkowski詢問她是否已讓她的嬰兒兒子完整接種疫苗。
「我覺得這極其不恰當,」她說。「我告訴她,分享我家人的個人健康資訊,完全超出這次對話的範疇。」
Murkowski的一位發言人表示,這位參議員不會透露私下對話的內容。
三天後,隨著情勢愈發明顯——Means在參議院的支持不足以獲得確認——川普在Truth Social上宣布,他有了新的公共衛生局局長提名人選,並感謝Means的服務。這是這位史丹佛畢業生放棄外科住院醫師訓練、轉而投身整體醫學的一段長達一年旅程的終點。
如今,她提名案的失敗,正在社群媒體上引發尖銳批評——衛生與公眾服務部長小勞勃・甘迺迪指責參議院衛生委員會主席、參議員Bill Cassidy拖延程序,導致Means功敗垂成。此事也將部分參議員對MAHA運動疫苗懷疑論的不安,以及白宮試圖管控此議題的努力,推到了台前。

當看新聞
1000美元的預算,在威尼斯能玩到什麼程度?來看看。
照片:SCARLETT CASCIELLO FOR WSJ
這座義大利城市以物價高昂、人潮擁擠聞名。但我們作者最近一趟嚴格控制預算的旅程證明,只要願意選在秋季淡季出遊,兩者都是可以避開的。

本週末焦點
週六:波克夏海瑟威年度股東大會。肯塔基賽馬會。週日:邁阿密F1大獎賽,梅賽德斯車隊希望延續其連勝紀錄。自阿聯退出OPEC以來,該組織首度召開會議。米爾肯研究所全球大會開幕。📰 今日報紙

數字看新聞
224,900美元
2026年梅賽德斯-邁巴赫SL 680 Monogram Series的起售價,這是一個與勞斯萊斯、賓利競爭的子品牌。但這輛擁有577匹馬力的豪華敞篷車,品味究竟如何?《華爾街日報》記者Dan Neil試駕了這輛雙座跑車一探究竟。

最後,別錯過...
黑莓機不再生產手機——但它仍在支撐你的生活。
仍有數量驚人的人們,依賴著這家曾以喀噠作響鍵盤聞名的公司——而他們自己往往並未察覺。黑莓公司如今最賺錢的產品並非硬體,而是隱藏在全球現役2.75億輛汽車中的軟體。事實上,這家公司的核心技術,還出現在各種你意想不到的地方,Ben Cohen撰文。

新聞編輯室之外
評論:川普總統在伊朗問題上堅持到底,理應獲得肯定——尤其是在他身邊許多人都正逐漸失去信心之際。

✏️ When we first started reporting for our Cost of Divorce series , none of us were sure anyone would want to speak on the record about such a grueling experience. Yet, bit by bit, people did, often with unflinching candor. We heard from a twice-divorced divorce attorney, unwed exes navigating a messy legal landscape and more. In telling these stories, we wanted to help readers navigate the complex financial and emotional costs of divorce—a topic that remains somewhat taboo. For our final installment of the series, WSJ’s Veronica Dagher reflects on how the reporting gave her a new—and surprisingly optimistic—outlook on splitting up.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

EXPERT TAKE
Q: Do donor-advised funds have hidden risks for donors?

It’s not clear what legal rights charitable givers to donor-advised funds have, explains Laura Saunders.

A: Donor-advised funds, known as DAFs, have become popular with affluent and wealthy charitable givers. A major reason is to maximize tax breaks.

Donors can “bunch” gifts to a designated account at an umbrella charity sponsoring DAFs and get an upfront tax deduction. Then the DAF dollars can grow tax-free and be parceled out over time when the donor, who is an “adviser” to the account, recommends grants to favorite charities.

Now a federal lawsuit in Colorado is probing what “advisory” rights DAF donors have—if any. Philip Peterson, who is the adviser to a DAF set up by his father, complains that his DAF sponsor has refused to communicate with him since 2024 about a DAF with $21 million in 2023.

Under the law, DAF donors and advisers don’t have a legal right to demand grants, because they gave that up when they got the tax deduction. Donors were reminded of this when national DAF sponsors Fidelity Charitable and Vanguard Charitable recently paused grants to the Southern Poverty Law Center after the Department of Justice indicted it for financial crimes.

But must DAF sponsors communicate with advisers and consider grants? The Peterson case aims to find out.

Horse racing is betting on an influencer to bring in new fans.

PHOTO: MICHAEL SWENSEN FOR WSJ

At the Kentucky Derby this weekend, Griffin Johnson will be posting to his more than 12 million followers. He’s part of a push for younger crowds. An influencer will typically post sponsored content for a monetary fee; Johnson says he charges $20,000 to $25,000 for a standard post. In this case, the social-media star is willing to post in exchange for equity in racehorses instead, pocketing money if the horses win. Ask Johnson why he pivoted to be an unofficial ambassador for horse racing, and he’ll be frank: “To be honest, there’s a lot of billionaires.”

The war with Iran has given the small and fantastically wealthy federation of monarchies an opportunity to make a statement about its aspirations for regional power. Silicon Valley’s brightest parents broke their own school.

Tessellations, a pre-K to 8th-grade school in Cupertino, Calif., bore all the markings of the next big thing for young geniuses when wealthy Silicon Valley parents founded it six years ago. Instead, the institution—where tuition starts at $44,500, for preschool —has spiraled into bitter fights with neighbors, lawsuits from teachers and parents, and an internal war among tech executives who fought over the school’s future. The saga offers a rare window into high-end Silicon Valley schools for gifted children, where the stakes rival college. EXPERT TAKE
Q: What traits do the highest-earning women in America share?

Attributes long thought to be keys to professional success don’t always hold true for the top 1% of earners, explains columnist Callum Borchers.

A: Some are what you’d expect. They are uncommonly competitive, they negotiate salaries more often than most and many earned degrees from top-ranked universities. This is according to a study of women who make at least $775,000 a year. Federal data puts the top 1% of annual earnings in the U.S. around that level.

But there were more surprising findings: Top-earning women are less likely to describe themselves as tough or thick-skinned. They are also less likely to view themselves as unique or even unusual.

After speaking to some of them, I came to understand that a patch of thin skin and a dose of self-doubt can be motivational assets. They’re like elite athletes who use discouraging remarks to fuel their pursuits of even greater achievements.

Feeling preternaturally gifted can lead to complacency. But when you think you need to repeatedly demonstrate that you belong at the top, you don’t let up.

It’s also notable that many women in the 1% experienced financial instability as children, which seemed to light a fire.

Lululemon的新任執行長還沒上任,就已經被架在火上烤。
董事會一直承受著壓力。Lululemon那位漸行漸遠的創辦人已發起委託書爭奪戰,一位知名維權投資人也在一旁虎視眈眈。董事會正競相尋找新的執行長。當公司相中前耐吉高管Heidi O'Neill時,董事會原以為已經勝券在握。結果這項人事決定卻適得其反,慘遭反噬。宣布當天股價下跌13%,此後跌勢持續。分析師批評O'Neill在耐吉的任期表現,投資人也對她要到9月才會正式上任表示不滿,讓公司在這個脆弱的時刻失去正式領導人,Lauren Thomas與Suzanne Kapner報導。Lululemon表示,O'Neill獲得董事會的全力支持。

專家問答
問:「捐贈者建議基金」對捐贈人是否隱藏著風險?
Laura Saunders解釋,慈善捐贈人對「捐贈者建議基金」究竟擁有什麼樣的法律權利,目前並不明確。
答:捐贈者建議基金(DAF)在富裕及財力雄厚的慈善捐贈人之間頗受歡迎。一個主要原因是為了最大化稅務減免。
捐贈人可以將捐款「集中」到一個由總傘式慈善機構主辦的DAF指定帳戶,並獲得一筆即時稅務減免。之後,DAF資金可以免稅增值,並在捐贈人(帳戶的「顧問」)推薦撥款給心儀慈善機構時,分批撥出。
如今,科羅拉多州一宗聯邦訴訟正在探究DAF捐贈人究竟擁有(如果有的話)什麼樣的「顧問」權利。Philip Peterson是其父親設立的一個DAF的顧問,他抱怨該DAF主辦機構自2024年以來拒絕就一個2023年資產達2100萬美元的DAF與他溝通。
根據法律,DAF捐贈人及顧問並無要求撥款的法律權利,因為他們在獲得稅務減免時已放棄這項權利。全國性DAF主辦機構Fidelity Charitable及Vanguard Charitable近期在司法部以財務犯罪起訴「南方貧困法律中心」後,暫停對其撥款,這一舉動也提醒了捐贈人這一點。
但DAF主辦機構是否必須與顧問溝通,並考慮撥款申請?Peterson一案的目的正是要找出答案。

當看新聞
賽馬界正押注一位網紅,為這項運動帶來新粉絲。
照片:MICHAEL SWENSEN FOR WSJ
在本週末的肯塔基賽馬會上,Griffin Johnson將向他超過1200萬名粉絲發布貼文。他是吸引年輕族群這股潮流的一份子。網紅通常會收取一筆費用來發布贊助內容;Johnson表示他一則標準貼文收費2萬到2萬5000美元。但在這個案例中,這位社群媒體明星願意以賽馬股權來換取發文,若馬匹獲勝便能分得獎金。若問Johnson為何轉型成為賽馬界的非官方大使,他會坦率作答:「老實說,這裡有很多億萬富翁。」

芝加哥大學去年的錄取到入學轉換率大約是這個數字,較2011年的約40%大幅攀升。像芝大這樣的學校,正試圖最大化其「入學轉換率」——即獲錄取學生中最終入學的比例——以提升排名、財務狀況及外界觀感。大學招生這盤棋局,如今變得比以往更加複雜。學校正推動讓學生更早做出承諾,增加新的提前錄取階段,並更積極地運用候補名單。與此同時,由於學生申請的學校數量增加,大學也愈來愈難預測有多少申請者會真的入學。

最後,別錯過...
波克夏有個90年代風格的網站,巴菲特的粉絲們說千萬別亂動它。
Berkshirehathaway.com看起來設計幾乎自Netscape及AOL時代以來就沒更新過。這是有原因的:它確實沒更新過。華倫・巴菲特可能已於12月卸任,結束他長達六十年執掌這家企業集團執行長的生涯。但波克夏的網路形象,依然是這位自稱一生只發過一次電子郵件的人的忠實寫照。粉絲們喜愛這個網站毫無花俏的設計,並對其超快的載入速度讚嘆不已。

The U.S. wants to ban China’s high-tech cars, but they’re already in El Paso.

In Ciudad Juárez, Mexico, just 5 miles from the U.S. border, a commercial strip offers the buzzy Chinese car brands currently blocked from the American market. U.S. consumers, though, are warming to the Chinese car alternative . Federal regulations allow Mexican residents and those with dual citizenship to drive their cars into the U.S., even if their vehicles aren’t compliant with relevant standards—offering Americans along the border a firsthand look at the Chinese competition. Without a clear plan to deal with Chinese competitors, some U.S. automotive executives said in interviews, the arrival of affordable, high-tech Chinese cars could upend a U.S. industry that contributes $1.3 trillion to the economy each year, reports Ryan Felton.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: A study suggests married adults are less likely to get cancer than singles. Why?

Reporter Aylin Woodward breaks down the findings and the different factors that can raise cancer risk:

A: A study of more than 4 million cancer cases in the U.S. found that cancer rates were about 68% higher among men who have never married compared with those who have. For never-married women, the relationship was even more pronounced, with cancer rates roughly 83% higher, according to research published recently in the journal Cancer Research Communications.

Married people tend to have greater economic stability and better support systems, and they’re more likely to stick with treatment, according to Paulo Pinheiro, professor of cancer epidemiology at the University of Miami School of Medicine’s Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center and co-author of the findings.

Previous studies have found that married people who have cancer tend to get diagnosed earlier and have better survival rates.

Unmarried men had five times the rate of anal cancer; unmarried women experienced three times the rate of cervical cancer. Both are linked to the sexually transmitted infection HPV, or human papillomavirus, so the incidences may reflect differences in exposure and screening.

Married individuals tend to have healthier behaviors overall, including lower smoking and alcohol use, more stable sexual and reproductive relationships, all of which are risk factors for cancer, Pinheiro said. They are also more likely to engage in preventative care. It’s important to note, however, that the link doesn’t always hold true .

Britain has a tiny-window epidemic, and old ladies are to blame.

Unlike much of Europe, where neighbors might lean out from their windows to shout to one another Italian-style, a resident of a new-build apartment in England is lucky if they can squeeze a potted plant onto the sill of their tiny, prisonlike opening . Guidance from the British Standards Institution on window safety recommends that windows in any new building should accommodate 95% of the U.K. adult population—including small, elderly women—in terms of reach. ✏️ 早安。今天將迎來本季最忙碌的財報日之一,微軟、亞馬遜及其他科技巨頭將於盤後公布財報。在昨天OpenAI相關消息震撼該產業之後,投資人正尋求穩定。與此同時,聯準會將召開會議,這極可能是傑羅姆・鮑爾以主席身分主持的最後一次會議。市場預期他將維持利率不變,但所有目光都集中在他的卸任上。《華爾街日報》首席經濟記者Nick Timiraos將親自到場報導利率決議及鮑爾的最後一場記者會。

美國想封殺中國高科技汽車,但它們早已現身艾爾帕索。
在距離美國邊境僅5英里的墨西哥華瑞茲城,一條商業街上擺滿了目前仍被禁止進入美國市場、話題性十足的中國汽車品牌。然而美國消費者正逐漸對中國汽車這個替代選擇產生好感。聯邦法規允許墨西哥居民及具雙重國籍者將自己的車輛開進美國,即便這些車輛不符合相關規範——這讓邊境沿線的美國人得以第一手見識中國車的競爭力。一些美國汽車業高管在受訪時表示,若沒有明確的因應計畫來對抗中國競爭對手,平價、高科技中國汽車的到來,可能會顛覆這個每年為美國經濟貢獻1.3兆美元的產業,Ryan Felton報導。

天災正在重寫保險版圖。看看它如何影響你。
舊有的房屋保險規則正被顛覆。數十年來,飽受颶風之苦的沿海各州承受著最大的保費漲幅,而內陸各州則享有低廉的保費。如今,根據《華爾街日報》針對全美保費及天災所做的分析,冰雹、野火及風災正猛烈衝擊那些曾被認為能躲過最嚴重漲價的地區。房屋保費會因居住地點不同而出現巨大差異:跨越一條郡界,費用可能就翻倍不止,Carl Churchill、Jaclyn Jeffrey-Wilensky、Jean Eaglesham與Jason French報導。透過我們的互動地圖,看看你所在的郡表現如何。

專家問答
問:一項研究顯示,已婚成人罹癌風險低於單身者。為什麼?
記者Aylin Woodward拆解了這項研究結果,以及可能提高癌症風險的各種不同因素:
答:一項針對美國逾400萬癌症病例的研究發現,從未結婚的男性罹癌率比已婚男性高出約68%。對於從未結婚的女性而言,這種關聯更為明顯,罹癌率高出約83%,相關研究近期發表於《Cancer Research Communications》期刊。
邁阿密大學醫學院Sylvester綜合癌症中心癌症流行病學教授、該研究共同作者Paulo Pinheiro表示,已婚人士往往擁有更好的經濟穩定性及更完善的支持系統,也更可能堅持完成治療。
過去的研究也發現,已婚罹癌患者往往能更早獲得診斷,且存活率更高。
未婚男性罹患肛門癌的機率是已婚男性的五倍;未婚女性罹患子宮頸癌的機率則是已婚女性的三倍。這兩種癌症都與性傳染病人類乳突病毒(HPV)有關,因此這些發生率的差異,可能反映出暴露程度及篩檢率的不同。
Pinheiro表示,已婚人士整體上往往有更健康的生活習慣,包括較低的吸菸及飲酒率、更穩定的性行為與生育關係——這些都是癌症的風險因素。他們也更可能接受預防性照護。不過,值得注意的是,這種關聯並非總是成立。

✏️ OpenAI has long operated under the strategy that massive spending would yield massive growth. But as the company sprints toward a potential IPO by year’s end, that idea is facing its first serious stress test. Recent misses on revenue and user targets have sparked concern among some of its leaders about whether it can support its increased spending on data centers. OpenAI’s chief executive and chief financial officer said in a statement they are “totally aligned” on securing new computing resources. Even so, WSJ’s Berber Jin explains how the scrutiny is constraining CEO Sam Altman’s once-boundless ambitions.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

Claudia Sheinbaum is learning the price of appeasing Trump.

When word reached Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum last week that two CIA officials had died in a car wreck in northern Mexico while participating in a counternarcotics operation, she could have chosen to express outrage at an apparently egregious violation of Mexican sovereignty. Instead, she struck a muted response. The incident is the latest headache for Sheinbaum, whose concessions to the U.S. have fueled political tension with her leftist base. It also comes as both governments are starting to review the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, which is vital for Mexico’s export-led economy, report Santiago Pérez, José de Córdoba and Michael Amon.
The Fed’s rate cuts are on pause. But are they also off the table?

Federal Reserve officials are almost certain to hold their benchmark interest rate steady at their two-day meeting that concludes Wednesday. But Jerome Powell’s last meeting as chair marks a waypoint in a debate: How much longer can the committee defend its recent posture that its next move is more likely to be down than up? Officials are watching how the U.S. economy digests its fourth supply shock in five years. Each one could be treated as a one-off that doesn’t call for a policy response. The cumulative effect has officials on edge, reports Nick Timiraos.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: How is the Senate’s new housing bill affecting builders and the rental market?

The legislation passed by the Senate in March is already causing projects to pause and financing to dry up, explains reporter Rebecca Picciotto.

A: The bill is trying to make it easier to build more houses, but one of its provisions has stopped homebuilders in their tracks. It would force developers to sell, within seven years of completion, newly constructed homes that they built solely for the purpose of renting.

Investment in these so-called build-to-rent properties has quickly cratered. Developers say that investors won’t put money into new rentals that they can own for only a few years before having to sell them.

Already, at least $3.4 billion of investment for build-to-rent projects is frozen in place, according to an early survey of 14 build-to-rent firms. That translates to about 10,000 units of housing. And it’s just a sliver of the overall build-to-rent industry, which includes an estimated 1,700 firms.

The Senate bill isn’t yet law and some Congress members are pushing back. For now, the impact is a long pause of new construction of single-family rentals. But the longer the policy battle drags on, the more severe the damage to the build-to-rent industry.

SEE THE STORY
Meet the Indian Ocean islanders who were pummeled by history—and now by Trump.

PHOTO: MICHAEL M. PHILLIPS/WSJ

The people of the remote Chagos Archipelago have lived in limbo since being evicted in the 1960s and 1970s to create a buffer around the secret U.S.-U.K. military base on Diego Garcia. Then last year the exiles thought they had caught a break : Britain struck a deal that would see the U.K. cede the islands to Mauritius and lease back the base, perhaps allowing the exiles to go home. But Trump seems intent on killing the deal, leaving hundreds of Chagossians worried they have lost their last shot at a life on the islands.

3月由參議院通過的這項立法,已導致專案暫停、融資枯竭,記者Rebecca Picciotto解釋。
答:這項法案試圖讓建造更多房屋變得更容易,但其中一項條款卻讓建商動彈不得。它要求開發商必須在完工後七年內,出售那些純粹為出租目的而興建的新建住宅。
對這類所謂「建後出租」房產的投資已迅速枯竭。開發商表示,投資人不願把錢投入新出租物業,因為他們只能擁有這些物業幾年,之後就得出售。

emails.contentEn:
Ahead of the 250th anniversary of the United States, WSJ is exploring the triumphs, trials and innovations that have shaped America and the world in a special multimedia series, “USA250: The Story of the World’s Greatest Economy.” In this special edition of The 10-Point, we’re taking a look at the evolution of innovation in America. This newsletter brings you some of our favorite pieces so far. You can find all the coverage here .

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

 You ranked the most impactful U.S. inventions.

WSJ readers scored the country’s greatest breakthroughs, from the computer to the steamboat. Here are the results .

 Business historians say these are the greatest entrepreneurs in U.S. history.

ILLUSTRATION: ISRAEL G. VARGAS FOR WSJ

The top four names on the list—Henry Ford, John D. Rockefeller, Steve Jobs and Andrew Carnegie—aren’t remembered for optimizing stock prices, but for how they changed how people lived, worked, consumed and thought about tomorrow. Read the full rankings .

 Information technology unified the nation.

ILLUSTRATION: SHAWN MICHAEL JONES FOR WSJ

After America’s Revolution, slow communications made a lack of cohesion one of the biggest threats to the new nation. A series of technological revolutions—including the telegraph and the smartphone— made all the difference .

 The inventor dubbed “the Black Edison” beat Thomas Edison in court.

Granville T. Woods won a series of patent battles in the 1880s to protect his inventions, including a system to allow moving trains to communicate wirelessly.

As the U.S. grew, it helped turn sales pitches into an art—and an industry. Here’s a look at some of the biggest moments in America’s long and profitable relationship with sales pitches.

Q: What is Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s next move?

With Kevin Warsh’s confirmation back on track, the question is whether Powell will give up his seat on the Fed’s board next month. Chief economics correspondent Nick Timiraos has the latest on the Fed succession drama:

A: What’s left unresolved is whether Powell will give up his seat on the Fed’s board when his chairmanship ends or stay on as a governor, a position he can hold until January 2028.

Powell’s own test for the decision is that the criminal probe into him be “well and truly over, with transparency and finality.” Whether that threshold has been met is unclear.

If Powell leaves, Trump gets a second vacancy to fill beyond the seat being used to install Warsh. If Powell stays, Trump has no other scheduled vacancies on the Fed’s board before 2028.

Trump administration officials have said they hope and expect Powell to follow the tradition of his predecessors and leave.

People who know Powell say that he is more than eager to return to private life. But agreeing to leave soon could, at least implicitly, validate the pressure campaign Powell has spent the past year avoiding.

Staying would deny Trump another seat from which to challenge institutional norms; leaving would give Warsh room to lead the central bank and the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee.

Powell himself hasn’t signaled which way he is leaning, and the small circle of advisers and friends who might know are declining to discuss it. Some who admire the job Powell has done think the right move now is for him to leave if the probe is truly over.

SEE THE STORY
We’re tracking corporate layoffs in 2026.

With major employers including Nike, Morgan Stanley and Amazon recently announcing job cuts, anxiety is mounting over AI’s role in upending the workplace. Tech has been hardest-hit this year, with 40% more layoffs in the first quarter—and fresh announcements of another 10,000 positions lost in April, including at Meta and Snap. Here’s how this year’s job cuts are stacking up .

The AI splurge is costing big tech its workforce , write Dan Gallagher and Asa Fitch.

HAPPENING TODAY
Elon Musk’s lawsuit against OpenAI is set to begin this week in Oakland, Calif. King Charles and Queen Camilla arrive in the U.S. for a four-day state visit that will take them to Washington D.C., New York and Virginia. Earnings: Verizon, Domino’s, Bed Bath & Beyond 📰 Today's paper

THE NUMBER
 $50

How much Regal Cinemas recently charged for opening-night seats in the best theaters to see December’s “Dune: Part Three.” Eye-popping prices for the most in-demand movies on the best screens are becoming increasingly common as the cinema industry copies the audience-segmentation playbooks of airlines and hotels. Theaters are getting people who love movies and have discretionary income to pay substantially more. Some 17% of film tickets sold last year were for premium-format theaters with bigger screens and better sound, compared with 13% in 2021.

AND FINALLY...
This is how to not get poisoned at a world leaders summit.

Ahead of a May 14-15 summit between Trump and Xi Jinping in Beijing, hundreds of government officials on both sides are racing to make sure the two leaders say the right thing, go to the right place— and don’t get poisoned . It will be the first state visit by a U.S. president to China in nearly a decade, and it comes at a moment of deepening distrust between the two countries. The idea is that nothing goes wrong. The challenge is that so many things can.

✏️ 早安。我們仍在拼湊週六晚間發生在華盛頓希爾頓酒店槍擊案的完整經過。我們的記者及編輯——包括多位當時人在現場的同仁——掌握了暴露川普總統再度面臨槍手威脅的安全漏洞最新細節,並透過地圖、照片及影片重建了整起事件的經過。

另一則華府新聞:查爾斯三世國王今日抵達首都,公開紀念一個新生的美國共和國推翻其祖先統治250週年——同時也私下鞏固一段許多人擔憂正逐漸破裂的跨大西洋聯盟關係。

艾瑪・塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條
中國以國家安全為由,下令Meta撤銷對人工智慧新創公司Manus的25億美元收購案。伊隆・馬斯克在他對OpenAI提起的1800億美元官司中處於弱勢一方。加州的億萬富翁稅已取得足夠連署,可望進入公投提案。在加薩,一座城市舉行了20多年來首次地方選舉。這場基本上具象徵意義的投票,讓巴勒斯坦人得以表達求變的渴望。

市場即時看
道瓊期貨 49320.00 -72.00 -0.15% 標普500期貨 7189.25 -5.50 -0.08% 那斯達克100期貨 27454.75 +19.75 +0.07%
資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年4月27日美東時間上午6:00:15。
📈 全天追蹤我們的即時財經報導。

賴瑞・艾利森是全球最富有的人之一。他可能也是全球負債最多的人之一——甚至在他為華納兄弟探索案交易擔保逾400億美元之前就已如此。

獨家搶先看
這些簡單的安全漏洞,讓川普再度暴露在槍手威脅之下。
儘管有明顯的安全周界及嚴密安檢的警告,賓客們表示,他們只需出示晚宴門票或某場宴前酒會邀請函的複本,就能透過飯店周邊街道的多個檢查點進入。這些門票雖經工作人員審查,但並未經過掃描,也沒有身分核對,與會者說。賓客能在不經過安檢掃描的情況下,進入飯店大廳及較低樓層,只有在進入舉行晚宴的宴會廳前,才需通過金屬探測門。要進入這場晚宴,比進入許多大型體育賽事或演唱會場地都還容易,Sadie Gurman、C. Ryan Barber與Isabella Simonetti報導。

美國企業界正大舉吸金——而且不只是科技與金融業。
儘管面臨戰爭及消費者焦慮情緒,美國大型企業仍靠著健康的銷售成長,持續累積龐大利潤。標普500指數成分股公司中,剛過四分之一公布第一季財報,而華爾街對財報的預期顯示,美國大型企業的體質,遠比更廣泛的經濟隱憂所暗示的要健康得多。中東戰爭已讓經濟學家調降今年的成長預測。長期作為美國經濟引擎的消費者,則明顯感到情緒低落。高油價如同一種稅賦,一方面拖累家庭消費,一方面又推升通膨。然而,美國最大的上市公司,獲利與營收卻雙雙飆升,Theo Francis報導。

在Google上將《華爾街日報》設為優先來源,以獲取更多我們屢獲殊榮的新聞報導。

專家問答
問:聯準會主席傑羅姆・鮑爾的下一步是什麼?
隨著凱文・沃許的確認程序重回正軌,問題在於鮑爾是否會在下個月放棄他在聯準會董事會的席位。首席經濟記者Nick Timiraos帶來聯準會人事繼任大戲的最新進展:
答:目前尚未解決的問題是,鮑爾在主席任期結束後,是否會放棄他在聯準會董事會的席位,還是繼續留任理事——這個職位他可以一直擔任到2028年1月。
鮑爾本人為這項決定設下的檢驗標準,是針對他的刑事調查必須「真正、徹底地結束,並具透明度與確定性」。這項門檻是否已經達到,目前尚不清楚。
如果鮑爾離開,川普將獲得除了用來安插沃許的席位之外,另一個可填補的空缺。如果鮑爾留任,那麼在2028年之前,川普在聯準會董事會就沒有其他預定的空缺。
川普政府官員表示,他們希望且預期鮑爾會遵循其前任的慣例選擇離開。
熟悉鮑爾的人士表示,他已經迫不及待想回歸私人生活。但若同意盡快離開,某種程度上等於默認了鮑爾過去一年一直試圖迴避的施壓行動的正當性。
留任將剝奪川普另一個挑戰體制規範的席位;離開則會為沃許主導央行及利率決策機構聯邦公開市場委員會騰出空間。
鮑爾本人尚未表態傾向哪個選擇,而少數可能知情的顧問與朋友也不願討論此事。一些欣賞鮑爾工作表現的人認為,如果調查真的結束了,他現在正確的做法就是離開。

當看新聞
我們正在追蹤2026年的企業裁員潮。
隨著包括耐吉、摩根士丹利及亞馬遜在內的主要雇主近期紛紛宣布裁員,外界對AI在顛覆職場中所扮演角色的焦慮正持續升高。科技業是今年受創最重的產業,第一季裁員人數增加40%——4月又傳出包括Meta及Snap在內、再裁員1萬個職位的消息。以下是今年裁員潮的最新統計。
AI的豪賭正讓大型科技公司付出人力代價,Dan Gallagher與Asa Fitch撰文。

今日焦點
伊隆・馬斯克控告OpenAI一案本週將在加州奧克蘭開庭。查爾斯國王與卡蜜拉王后抵達美國,展開為期四天的國是訪問,將走訪華盛頓特區、紐約及維吉尼亞州。財報:威訊通訊、達美樂、Bed Bath & Beyond。📰 今日報紙

數字看新聞
50美元
Regal Cinemas近期為12月上映的《沙丘:第三部》最佳影廳首映夜座位所收取的票價。隨著電影院產業複製航空公司及飯店業的客群分眾策略,熱門電影在最佳影廳的驚人票價正變得愈來愈普遍。戲院鎖定的是那些熱愛電影、且有可支配所得願意多付一些錢的觀眾。去年售出的電影票中,約17%屬於配備更大螢幕及更優音效的高級影廳票種,高於2021年的13%。

最後,別錯過...
這是如何在世界領導人峰會上避免中毒的方法。
在5月14至15日川普與習近平於北京舉行峰會之前,雙方數百名政府官員正競相確保兩位領導人說對話、去對地方——並且不會中毒。這將是近十年來美國總統首次對中國進行國是訪問,而此時正值兩國之間互信日益低落之際。理念是確保一切萬無一失。挑戰在於,可能出錯的環節實在太多。

emails.contentEn:
✏️ A shooter was detained at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner, where President Trump was bundled from the stage. I was there with colleagues, as all hell broke loose in the ballroom of the Washington Hilton. The event brought together many of America’s top government officials in a single room, alongside business executives, celebrities and journalists. What we know so far .

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES
The 31-year-old suspect in the shooting is a Caltech grad who recently won a “teacher of the month” award. The event left some in the room, from cabinet secretaries to aides and reporters, grappling with the new reality that such violence has become a regular occurrence. Here’s the latest . Trump scrapped a trip by U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Pakistan for talks with Iran, leaving himself tough choices over how to push for concessions to strike a deal. Follow our live coverage . Gannon Ken Van Dyke—who allegedly made more than $400,000 in part by using classified information to bet on the ousting of Nicolás Maduro—was a U.S. Army soldier simultaneously chasing business success. He didn’t respond to requests for comment. America’s pandemic car bubble is trapping buyers in debt , with the average amount a borrower with negative equity carries on a vehicle up more than 40% since 2021.

FROM THE MARKETS
The AI frenzy is back and lifting the entire stock market to record highs, though signs of froth are everywhere, writes James Mackintosh. Moves in the loan market show that Wall Street is sorting software companies into winners and losers amid fears of AI disruption in the sector.

READ IT HERE FIRST
Bill Perkins told WSJ why he doesn’t think you should wait to spend your money.

The founder of Skylar Capital Management wagers in the notoriously boom-or-bust energy markets, while also working on two startups. But there’s nothing he seems quite as dedicated to as enjoying his life—and fortune . The Journal’s Gunjan Banerji sat down with the hedge-fund manager before one of the biggest energy shocks in years, and he explained why he’s hell-bent on “dying with zero.”

Stay tuned for the next episode of The WSJ Money Interview.
This small St. Louis suburb is leading America’s crusade against data centers.

In Festus, Mo., a backlash against the construction of data centers has reached a fever pitch, reports Will Parker. When the City Council last month approved a proposal by a St. Louis developer to build a data center to accommodate AI, residents erupted in protest. In the spring elections, a landslide vote removed four City Council incumbents who backed the project. With the midterms approaching, opposition to AI as well as the construction of data centers to support it is evolving into a campaign issue for all politicians. More than 90 local governments have enacted or are considering measures to limit data-center construction.

Go inside the U.S.-China relationship.

EXPERT TAKE
Q: What makes a truly great entrepreneur?

For three decades, Jonathan Bean and Blaine McCormick have asked business historians and thought leaders to rank the nation’s greatest entrepreneurs and businesspeople. As a part of WSJ’s yearlong series, “ USA250 : The Story of the World’s Greatest Economy,” the two researchers wrote about what their rankings say about both business and leadership .

A: While business visionaries are often the true agents of change, ranking them raises an inevitable question: What exactly does greatness in business mean? So, for our last survey in 2021, we asked our experts to rank “factors of greatness” that might explain the names in their rankings. (Note that since the list is five years old, some businesspeople at the forefront of innovation right now aren’t represented, like those in AI-related businesses.)

At the top of the experts’ list: “ability to imagine or envision the future” and “impact of product or service in reordering American life.” Contrast that with a factor they ranked much lower: “created wealth for shareholders.”

In other words, the entrepreneurs who loom largest in American history—Henry Ford, John D. Rockefeller, Steve Jobs, Andrew Carnegie, the top four names on our list—aren’t remembered for optimizing stock prices. They are appreciated for the way they changed how people lived, worked, consumed and thought about tomorrow. (Rounding out our list are luminaries from a range of eras and industries: Bill Gates, Thomas Edison, Sam Walton, Jeff Bezos, Walt Disney and J.P. Morgan.)

SEE THE STORY
Watch how the energy crisis is spreading across the world.

DANIEL KISS

In a war between oil exporters, petroleum importers are finding themselves at the front lines of a global energy crisis. Now, governments across the world are taking drastic steps to combat the crisis that range from cash handouts to fuel rationing. Here’s what the measures look like in practice .

HAPPENING THIS WEEK
Elon Musk’s lawsuit against Sam Altman and OpenAI is set to begin in Oakland, Calif. Tuesday: The Conference Board’s consumer confidence survey for April. Wednesday: The Federal Reserve announces a rate decision, where it is expected to leave the federal-funds target range unchanged at 3.50%-3.75%. Thursday: The advance estimate of first-quarter U.S. gross domestic product, which will give investors an indication of how America’s economy has fared during the war in the Middle East. The Labor Department reports weekly jobless claims.

THE NUMBER
 >40%

The share of America’s aviation mechanics who are over 60 and approaching retirement, according to a report from Oliver Wyman management consultants and the Aviation Technician Education Council. Though many aircraft technicians make six figures, airlines can’t find enough of them.

AND FINALLY...
San Francisco is going nuts over a giant sea lion named Chonkers.

The 2,000-pound Steller sea lion is about three times the size of the California sea lions that typically inhabit the San Francisco Bay. He swam up to a dock on Pier 39 a month ago and decided to stay—and online commenters can’t seem to get enough. “Chonkers the stellar sea lion is back at Pier 39 today!” reads one post. Another is entitled, “Pier 39’s Steller Sea Lion Belly Scratch Action!”

emails.contentZh:
✏️ 一名槍手在白宮記者協會晚宴上被制伏,當時川普總統被匆忙帶離舞台。我當時與同事們一起在場,親眼目睹華盛頓希爾頓酒店宴會廳裡秩序徹底失控的過程。這場活動齊聚了許多美國頂尖政府官員,還有企業高管、名人及記者共處一室。目前已知的情況如下。

艾瑪・塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條
這名31歲的槍擊嫌犯是加州理工學院畢業生,最近才剛獲頒「本月教師獎」。這起事件讓現場從內閣部長到幕僚及記者的許多人,不得不面對這種暴力已成家常便飯的殘酷現實。以下是最新進展。川普取消了美國特使Steve Witkoff及Jared Kushner原定前往巴基斯坦與伊朗會談的行程,讓他自己在如何推動達成協議上,面臨艱難抉擇。追蹤我們的即時報導。Gannon Ken Van Dyke——據稱靠著利用機密資訊押注尼可拉斯・馬杜洛遭罷黜而賺進逾40萬美元——曾是一名美國陸軍士兵,同時也在追求商業上的成功。他未回應置評請求。美國的疫情汽車泡沫正讓購車者深陷債務泥沼,負資產借款人在車輛上背負的平均貸款餘額,較2021年上升逾40%。

市場消息
AI熱潮捲土重來,將整個股市推升至歷史新高,儘管市場過熱的跡象隨處可見,James Mackintosh撰文。貸款市場的動向顯示,華爾街正在為軟體公司分出贏家與輸家,原因是外界擔憂該產業將面臨AI帶來的顛覆。

獨家搶先看
比爾・柏金斯告訴《華爾街日報》,他為何認為你不該等到以後才花錢。
這位Skylar Capital Management創辦人,在出了名大起大落的能源市場中下注,同時也經營著兩家新創公司。但比起這一切,他似乎最投入的,莫過於享受人生與財富。《華爾街日報》記者Gunjan Banerji,在近年來最嚴重的能源衝擊之一發生前,與這位對沖基金經理人坐下來對談,他解釋了自己為何一心想要「將財富花光,分毫不留」。

敬請鎖定下一集《華爾街日報財富人物專訪》。

這個聖路易斯郊區小鎮,正引領美國對抗資料中心的十字軍運動。
在密蘇里州費瑟斯鎮,一場反對興建資料中心的抵制行動已達到白熱化程度,Will Parker報導。上個月,當市議會核准一項由聖路易斯開發商提出、為容納AI而興建資料中心的提案時,居民們群情激憤。在春季選舉中,一場壓倒性的投票,罷免了四名支持該計畫的市議會現任議員。隨著期中選舉臨近,反對AI及支撐AI所需的資料中心建設,正演變成所有政治人物都必須面對的競選議題。全美已有超過90個地方政府,已通過或正在考慮限制資料中心建設的措施。

深入了解美中關係。

專家問答
問:什麼造就了真正偉大的企業家?
三十年來,Jonathan Bean與Blaine McCormick一直邀請商業史學家及思想領袖,為這個國家最偉大的企業家與商業人士排名。作為《華爾街日報》年度系列「USA250:全球最偉大經濟體的故事」的一部分,這兩位研究者撰文探討他們的排名對商業與領導力有何啟示。
答:儘管商業願景家往往才是真正推動變革的人,為他們排名卻難免引出一個無可迴避的問題:商業上的「偉大」究竟意味著什麼?因此,在我們2021年最後一次調查中,我們請專家們為可能解釋榜單人選的「偉大特質」進行排名。(請注意,由於這份榜單已有五年歷史,目前站在創新前沿的部分人士,例如AI相關企業人士,並未被納入其中。)
專家榜單之首,是「想像或展望未來的能力」以及「產品或服務重塑美國生活的影響力」。相較之下,排名遠低於此的是「為股東創造財富」這一項。
換句話說,美國歷史上這些最舉足輕重的企業家——亨利・福特、約翰・D・洛克斐勒、史蒂夫・賈伯斯、安德魯・卡內基,榜單前四名——之所以被人銘記,並非因為他們優化了股價。他們之所以受人推崇,是因為他們改變了人們生活、工作、消費及思考未來的方式。(榜單其餘的傑出人物,則來自各個時代與產業:比爾・蓋茲、湯瑪斯・愛迪生、山姆・沃爾頓、傑夫・貝佐斯、華特・迪士尼及J・P・摩根。)

當看新聞
觀看能源危機如何蔓延全球。
DANIEL KISS
在一場產油國之間的戰爭中,石油進口國正發現自己身處全球能源危機的最前線。如今,世界各國政府正採取從現金補貼到燃油配給等各種激烈手段,對抗這場危機。以下是這些措施在實務上的具體樣貌。

本週焦點
伊隆・馬斯克控告山姆・奧特曼及OpenAI的訴訟,將於加州奧克蘭開庭。週二:世界大型企業聯合會(Conference Board)公布4月消費者信心調查。週三:聯準會宣布利率決議,預計將聯邦基金利率目標區間維持在3.50%至3.75%不變。週四:第一季美國國內生產毛額初值,將讓投資人一窺中東戰爭期間美國經濟的表現。勞工部公布每週初領失業救濟金人數。

數字看新聞
超過40%
根據Oliver Wyman管理顧問公司及航空技術教育委員會的一份報告,美國航空維修技師中,已超過60歲、即將退休者的大致比例。儘管許多飛機技師薪資達六位數,航空公司卻招不到足夠的人手。

最後,別錯過...

這隻重達2000磅的北方海獅,體型約是一般棲息於舊金山灣的加州海獅的三倍大。牠一個月前游到39號碼頭的一處船塢,決定留下來——網友們的討論熱情似乎怎麼也不夠。「Chonkers這隻北方海獅今天又回到39號碼頭了!」一則貼文寫道。另一則貼文標題則是「39號碼頭北方海獅的肚皮抓癢秀!」。
