因電影《走出非洲》而聞名的酒吧,至今仍禁止女性進入。她們已經受夠了。

奈洛比歷史悠久的穆泰加鄉村俱樂部(Muthaiga Country Club),於1913年為英國菁英而建,如今正陷入一場激烈爭論:是否應該允許女性進入其「會員酒吧」。這間酒吧最為人所知的,是曾在1985年的電影中拒絕梅莉·史翠普飾演的角色進入。

新聞室之外

10

評論:取代鮑爾的最佳方式,是撤銷那個藉口式的司法部調查,並讓凱文·沃許獲得確認。為什麼川普這麼難理解這一點?

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Wall Street Earnings Fuel New Market Optimism
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Never mind that one of the world’s most-important energy chokepoints remains closed—markets are roaring back anyway. Oil prices have retreated, Wall Street banks just posted blockbuster earnings and CEOs are touting a resilient U.S. economy. That combination has stocks back on the brink of records, with some investors betting a strong earnings season could power them even higher. To be clear, worries over the Iran war haven’t disappeared. Our foreign correspondents find the U.S.-Israeli attack has fast-tracked the ascent of hard-liners and apocalyptic religious followers within Iran’s new regime, raising doubts about a lasting peace. Follow our live coverage of the conflict here.

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

A fallback plan to ensure Europe can defend itself using NATO’s existing military structures if the U.S. departs is gaining traction after getting buy-in from Germany. Pope Leo XIV is proving a challenging opponent for President Trump. One in seven people who signed up for Affordable Care Act plans this year failed to pay after premium costs rose sharply, a new analysis shows. A Massachusetts town’s rejection of a 50% property tax hike is a warning sign for financially strained municipalities across the U.S. Maine lawmakers passed a ban on large data-center construction, making it the first state to enact such a measure. The space race between Jeff Bezos and Elon Musk is heating up.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 48715.00 -40.00 0.08 S&P 500 Futures 7002.25 -2.50 0.04 Nasdaq 100 Futures 25989.50 -7.25 0.03

Source: Factset, Market data as of 4/15/2026, 5:56:32 AM ET

The prospect of a peace deal that reopens the Strait of Hormuz has now powered the Nasdaq composite to its longest streak of daily gains since November 2021.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Iran’s regime has changed—for the worse.

The U.S. and Israel launched the war with the hope that killing top Iranian officials—starting with Mojtaba Khamenei’s father, Ali Khamenei—would create the conditions for regime change or at least the emergence of leaders more willing to bend to America and Israel’s interests. In an address to the nation one month into the war, Trump called the new leadership “more reasonable.” Instead, the void is being filled by radical new leaders who have shown little interest in political compromise at home or abroad, report Margherita Stancati, Benoit Faucon and Henna Moussavi.

4

Developers in New York City are suddenly obsessed with the number 99. Here’s why.

A city government program enacted in 2024 offers a tax exemption to developers of most apartment buildings that have fewer than 100 units and include some affordable housing. Anyone building bigger than that has to abide by stricter requirements—such as construction-worker pay and rent stabilization—to get the same tax break. More NYC developers are seizing on a loophole to secure the tax benefit for larger projects without being subject to the stipulations, report Rebecca Picciotto and Peter Santilli.

Get set for the trading day ahead.

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: How are airline passengers being hit by the jet fuel crunch?

The U.S. war with Iran is driving up jet fuel prices, and airlines are leaning on passengers to foot the bill, explain WSJ’s Amira McKee, Alison Sider and Stephanie Stamm.

A: Skyrocketing jet fuel prices are jolting the aviation industry, and airlines are bringing travelers along for the ride. Airlines have increased baggage and other fees, pledged to cut back on flights and raised fares since late February. Ticket prices for some routes have doubled from a year ago.

Airline executives say higher jet fuel costs are feeding steeper fares, though demand for certain routes and the health of the economy also factor into prices. Some international airlines have introduced fuel surcharges on customers’ tickets.

The U.S. is a significant producer of jet fuel, and American carriers are more insulated from volatility in the Middle East. Still, because aircraft fuel up locally, U.S. airlines can be subject to the squeeze on some international flights. And with no signs of a reprieve on the way, carriers have begun trimming their schedules.

6

Wall Street has an elite coffee-tasting force. It’s struggling to find recruits.

The people who gather in a room on the eighth floor of the New York Stock Exchange look like a group of middle-aged caffeine addicts, sniffing beans and slurping coffee. They’re part of an elite team of graders whose ratings help set U.S. futures-market prices for arabica, and in turn, the global coffee industry. Their expertise has arguably never been more valuable: The flow of young talent that keeps the grading system running is slowing to a drip.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

Tax day in the U.S. Earnings: Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, PNC Financial 📰 Today’s paper

THE NUMBER

8

 33

The age of Blake Butera, the Washington Nationals’ new manager, making him the youngest person to hold that job in MLB since 1972. The Nationals—recently one of baseball’s saddest franchises—are the first to put their fate entirely in the hands of what the sport’s establishment might derisively call the “participation trophy generation.” Their solution this winter was to hire decision-makers in their 30s to fill every important leadership role.

AND FINALLY...

9

Our travel columnist has spent 30 nights in hotels already this year. Here’s her wish list.

WSJ’s Dawn Gilbertson has spent the equivalent of a month in hotels so far this year, from a Great Wolf Lodge resort in Arizona to a Hilton Garden Inn at London’s Heathrow Airport. Here, Dawn shares her hotel hot takes—things that she wishes every hotel did or didn’t do. At the top of her wishlist? Better lighting and complimentary in-room treats.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Vinay Prasad is leaving the FDA, but he’s kicking patients with late-stage melanoma on his way out.
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 儘管世界上最重要的能源咽喉要道之一仍處於封閉狀態,市場卻依然強勢反彈。油價已回落,華爾街各大銀行剛公布亮眼財報,執行長們也紛紛強調美國經濟的韌性。這樣的組合讓股市再度逼近歷史高點,一些投資人押注,強勁的財報季有望將股市推得更高。當然,對伊朗戰爭的擔憂並未消失。我們的駐外記者發現,美以聯合攻擊已加速了伊朗新政權中強硬派與末日宗教信徒的崛起,這讓外界對持久和平的可能性產生疑慮。持續關注我們對這場衝突的即時報導。

今日頭條

1

在獲得德國的支持後,一項讓歐洲即便美國撤出、仍能利用北約現有軍事架構自我防衛的備案,正逐漸獲得支持。教宗良十四世正證明自己是川普總統一個難纏的對手。今年報名參加平價醫療法案(Affordable Care Act)計畫的民眾中,有七分之一在保費大幅上漲後未能繳費,一項新分析顯示。麻州一個小鎮否決了一項50%的財產稅增稅案,這對全美財政緊張的市鎮而言是一個警訊。緬因州議員通過一項禁止興建大型數據中心的法案,使其成為首個實施此類措施的州。傑夫·貝佐斯與伊隆·馬斯克之間的太空競賽正在升溫。

市場即時動態

2

最新 漲跌 漲跌幅 道瓊期貨 48715.00 -40.00 0.08% 標普500期貨 7002.25 -2.50 0.04% 那斯達克100期貨 25989.50 -7.25 0.03%

一項重新開放荷莫茲海峽的和平協議前景,已推動那斯達克綜合指數連續上漲天數創下2021年11月以來最長紀錄。

獨家搶先看

3

伊朗政權已經改變——而且是變得更糟。

美國與以色列發動這場戰爭時,曾希望剷除伊朗高層官員——從穆吉塔巴·哈梅內伊(Mojtaba Khamenei)的父親阿里·哈梅內伊開始——能為政權更迭創造條件,或至少促成願意向美國與以色列利益讓步的新領導人上台。在戰爭開打一個月後對全國發表的講話中,川普稱新領導層「更為理性」。然而,填補這個權力真空的,卻是幾乎無意在國內外進行政治妥協的激進新領導人,記者瑪格麗塔·斯坦卡蒂(Margherita Stancati)、貝諾特·福孔(Benoit Faucon)與亨娜·穆薩維(Henna Moussavi)報導。

4

紐約市的開發商突然迷上了「99」這個數字。原因如下。

一項紐約市政府於2024年推出的計畫,對大多數單元數少於100戶、且包含部分平價住宅的公寓大樓開發商提供稅務減免。任何規模超過此標準的開發案,則必須遵守更嚴格的規定——例如建築工人薪資與租金管制——才能獲得同樣的稅務優惠。越來越多紐約市開發商正利用一項漏洞,為規模更大的項目爭取這項稅務優惠,同時規避相關規定,記者瑞貝卡·皮西奧托(Rebecca Picciotto)與彼得·聖蒂利(Peter Santilli)報導。

5

問:航空乘客如何受到航空燃油短缺的衝擊?

美國與伊朗的戰爭正推升航空燃油價格,而航空公司正讓旅客為此買單,本報記者阿米拉·麥基(Amira McKee)、艾莉森·賽德(Alison Sider)與斯蒂芬妮·斯塔姆(Stephanie Stamm)解釋道。

答:飆升的航空燃油價格正衝擊航空業,而航空公司正帶著旅客一起承受這波衝擊。自2月下旬以來,航空公司已提高行李及其他費用,承諾削減航班,並提高票價。部分航線的票價已比去年同期上漲一倍。

航空公司高層表示,航空燃油成本上升導致票價上漲,不過某些航線的需求以及經濟狀況,也是影響價格的因素。一些國際航空公司已開始對客戶機票徵收燃油附加費。

美國是航空燃油的重要生產國,美國航空公司相對較能抵禦中東地區的波動。儘管如此,由於飛機須在當地加油,美國航空公司在某些國際航班上仍可能受到擠壓。而且目前看不出有緩解跡象,各航空公司已開始削減班表。

6

華爾街有一支精英咖啡品鑑團隊。它正苦於招募不到新血。

聚集在紐約證券交易所八樓一個房間裡的人,看起來像一群中年咖啡因成癮者,聞著豆子、啜飲著咖啡。他們是一支精英評鑑團隊的成員,他們的評分有助於制定美國期貨市場上阿拉比卡咖啡的價格,進而影響全球咖啡產業。他們的專業知識或許從未像現在這樣珍貴:維繫這套評鑑系統運作的年輕人才,正逐漸枯竭。

今日看點

7

美國報稅截止日。財報:美國銀行、摩根士丹利、PNC金融服務集團。

數字看新聞

8

33

華盛頓國民隊新任總教練布雷克·布特拉(Blake Butera)的年齡,使他成為自1972年以來,大聯盟史上最年輕出任該職位的人。國民隊——這支近來堪稱棒球界最悲情的球隊之一——是首支將命運完全交到某些棒球圈老將可能會嘲諷地稱為「參與獎世代」手中的球隊。他們這個冬天的解決方案,是聘用三十多歲的人選來擔任每一個重要的領導職位。

最後,輕鬆一下

9

我們的旅遊專欄作家今年已在飯店住了30個晚上。這是她的願望清單。

本報記者道恩·吉爾伯森(Dawn Gilbertson)今年迄今已在飯店住了相當於一個月的時間,從亞利桑那州的大狼堡度假村(Great Wolf Lodge),到倫敦希斯羅機場的希爾頓花園酒店。在這裡,道恩分享了她的飯店心得——她希望每家飯店都做到、或都別做的事。她願望清單上排名第一的是什麼?更好的燈光,以及免費的房內小點心。

新聞室之外

10

評論:維奈·普拉薩德(Vinay Prasad)即將離開FDA,但他在離開前,還在對晚期黑色素瘤患者踢上一腳。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Trump’s Post Sparks Religious Right Backlash
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Harvard University President Dr. Alan Garber is no stranger to being in the Trump administration’s crosshairs—so much so that I asked if he had been texting Pope Leo advice over the weekend. During our conversation at the 92nd Street Y last night, one thing was clear: Despite the pressure, Garber remains a staunch optimist. Questions from the audience (and you!) reflected anxieties about everything from grade inflation to AI in classrooms. He didn’t dismiss those fears, warning that tightened immigration and funding cuts put the U.S. at risk of ceding its lead in math and science to China. Yet he maintains an unshakeable faith in Harvard’s commitment to the pursuit of truth and knowledge.

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

President Trump’s decision to post an AI-generated image depicting himself as a Christ-like figure triggered the most significant pushback from the religious right since he returned to the White House. Saudi Arabia is pressing the U.S. to drop its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and return to the negotiating table. Los Angeles public schools reached a tentative last-minute deal with a major employees’ union to avoid a strike. In Cuba, Raúl Castro’s family is taking the reins as Trump threatens the Communist regime’s grip on power. AI models are finding software bugs that hackers can exploit. Get ready for the bug armageddon.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 48444.00 19.00 0.04 S&P 500 Futures 6933.50 10.75 0.16 Nasdaq 100 Futures 25638.00 94.50 0.37

📊 Charts: Here’s how Trump’s Iran war reversals have whipsawed markets. What’s the real cost of a barrel of oil? Prices for physical crude are becoming detached from what is implied in financial markets, writes Jinjoo Lee.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Bernie Sanders is back as a left-wing kingmaker.

A decade after his first bid for the White House ended in failure, Sanders is still trying to take over the Democratic Party. Instead of retreating, the Vermont senator has pulled his colleagues dramatically leftward and is trying to position himself as the party’s kingmaker. Sanders, 84, has said he doesn’t think he will run for president again. But as Democrats trip over themselves to come up with a cohesive strategy to win back congressional majorities and effectively take on Trump, he has built a formidable political machine to spread progressive policies and support like-minded candidates, many of whom are young and new to politics, reports Eliza Collins.

4

Home builders are skimping on the basics to maintain profits in a stagnant housing market.

Home builders are looking everywhere for ways to slash costs. They are finding them in cabinets, faucets and even the garage door remote. Builders are opting for cheaper materials and rejiggering designs with cost savings top of mind. Particle board cabinets are in. Hardwood is out. Countertops are becoming thinner. Walls now feature smaller and fewer windows. An automatic garage opener is sometimes a frivolous luxury. The cost-cutting is part of an effort to offer more affordable homes. The cumulative effect is changing the appearance of newly constructed American homes, reports Nicholas G. Miller.

Make sense of AI’s impact on business.

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: How is the U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz being enforced?

The blockade is now officially in effect, setting up a risky new showdown after peace talks collapsed. WSJ’s Lara Seligman and Shelby Holliday share what we know so far.

A: Washington kicked off the operation yesterday by positioning more than 15 U.S. warships, according to a senior U.S. official.

Placing resources and warships near Iran’s coast could make U.S. assets susceptible to attack, officials said, so the U.S. will likely try to intercept or quarantine commercial vessels on either side of the Strait of Hormuz to prevent them from entering or leaving Iranian ports.

Any warship can approach a tanker suspected of violating the blockade, but if a ship doesn’t comply with a request to board, specially trained Marines and special-operations forces, such as Navy SEALs, would be needed to conduct a contested boarding.

The Navy has significant firepower in the region that could support the blockade, according to officials.

Iran’s “shadow fleet” will likely sit out the fight, but Iranian-flagged ships are more likely to attempt to transit the waterway, said retired Vice Adm. John Miller, a former commander of U.S. Naval Forces Central Command. Those vessels may be guarded by a detachment of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces, he said.

If the U.S. takes control of tankers, it may need a captain, crew (if the existing crew doesn’t comply), and a place to park the vessels, according to former officials.

🎥 Video: WSJ breaks down how vessels could be used to enforce the blockade.

6

America has wanted Greenland for over a century. Trump isn’t giving up.

Deep in a remote fjord in Greenland, hundreds of rusty fuel drums known locally as “American flowers” litter the icy wilderness. Near an abandoned hangar, U.S. Army vehicles decay in the snow. As Trump seeks to expand U.S. territory with the island, this base, a remnant of World War II, stands as a reminder of the last time the U.S. tried to own Greenland. Trump’s insistence is the latest in a string of American flirtations with the island. It is, however, the first to threaten to splinter NATO.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

WSJ live Q&A: Do you have questions about the future of private credit? Join our finance reporters, AnnaMaria Andriotis and Matt Wirz, at 2 p.m. ET. Economic data: Producer-price data for March will give clues on how the war in the Middle East is stoking inflation, and the IMF publishes its economic forecasts. Earnings: JPMorgan Chase, Johnson & Johnson, Wells Fargo, Citigroup, BlackRock 

THE NUMBER

8

 12%

That’s how much Cleveland’s downtown population has grown since 2019, according to Michael Deemer, president and CEO of the nonprofit Downtown Cleveland. One thing that’s helped boost the downtown population: Architectural icons from the city’s early-1900s golden age are being reimagined as modern apartments, attracting young renters, empty nesters and reverse commuters. Driven by state and federal tax incentives, approximately 30 historic buildings have been reimagined as apartments, hotels and more since 2013 alone.

AND FINALLY...

9

There’s a corporate team-building exercise where you have to climb on the boss.

Companies are always looking for fresh ways to foster team spirit by swapping traditional icebreakers with activities like country-music songwriting. But even in this era of blurring professional boundaries, what’s happening in the Spanish region of Catalonia is extreme. Employers are ditching escape rooms for human tower workshops. Catalans have been erecting human towers—castells—to celebrate local festivities since the 18th century. While the activity sounds like a gross breach of corporate etiquette, feedback is overwhelmingly positive.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Democrats want to block Trump at every turn, but can they put the rancor aside to protect U.S. national security? That’s the question as Congress debates whether to reauthorize Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA).

✏️ 哈佛大學校長艾倫·加伯(Alan Garber)博士對於成為川普政府的箭靶並不陌生——以至於我問他,週末是否曾透過簡訊向教宗良十四世提供建議。在昨晚於92街Y中心的對談中,有一件事非常清楚:儘管承受著壓力,加伯依然是個堅定的樂觀主義者。來自觀眾(以及你們!)的問題,反映出從成績膨脹到課堂上的AI等種種焦慮。他並未輕視這些擔憂,並警告收緊的移民政策與經費削減,可能讓美國在數學與科學領域的領先地位拱手讓給中國。然而他依然對哈佛追求真理與知識的使命抱持著不可動搖的信念。

今日頭條

1

川普總統決定發布一張將自己描繪成基督般人物的AI生成圖片,此舉引發了他重返白宮以來,來自宗教右翼最顯著的一次反彈。沙烏地阿拉伯正向美國施壓,要求解除對荷莫茲海峽的封鎖,並回到談判桌前。洛杉磯公立學校與一個主要員工工會在最後一刻達成臨時協議,避免了一場罷工。在古巴,勞爾·卡斯楚(Raúl Castro)的家族正在接掌大權,而川普則威脅要動搖這個共產政權的統治根基。AI模型正在發現駭客可利用的軟體漏洞。準備好迎接一場「漏洞末日」吧。

市場即時動態

2

最新 漲跌 漲跌幅 道瓊期貨 48444.00 19.00 0.04% 標普500期貨 6933.50 10.75 0.16% 那斯達克100期貨 25638.00 94.50 0.37%

📊 圖表:川普在伊朗戰爭立場上的反覆,如何讓市場劇烈震盪。一桶原油的真實成本是多少?實體原油價格正與金融市場所隱含的價格脫節,金珠·李(Jinjoo Lee)寫道。

獨家搶先看

3

伯尼·桑德斯重新成為左翼「造王者」。

在他首次角逐白宮失敗十年後,桑德斯仍試圖掌控民主黨。這位佛蒙特州參議員不但沒有選擇退場,反而將他的同僚大幅拉向左翼,並試圖將自己定位為該黨的造王者。84歲的桑德斯表示,他不認為自己會再度參選總統。但隨著民主黨人為了拿出一套一致的策略、以贏回國會多數並有效對抗川普而手忙腳亂,他已建立起一個強大的政治機器,用來推廣進步派政策並支持理念相近的候選人,其中許多人是政壇新面孔且年紀較輕,記者伊萊莎·柯林斯(Eliza Collins)報導。

4

建商正在基本配置上偷工減料,以維持利潤,因為房市持續低迷。

建商正在各處尋找削減成本的方法。他們在櫥櫃、水龍頭甚至車庫門遙控器上找到了省錢空間。建商正選用更便宜的材料,並以節省成本為首要考量重新設計格局。密集板櫥櫃成了主流,硬木則被淘汰。檯面正變得更薄。牆面如今擁有更小、更少的窗戶。自動車庫開門器有時被視為一種奢侈的浪費。這波節省成本的行動,是提供更平價住宅的努力之一環。這種累積效應,正在改變新建美國住宅的外觀,記者尼可拉斯·G·米勒(Nicholas G. Miller)報導。

5

問:美國對荷莫茲海峽的封鎖是如何執行的?

隨著和平談判破裂,這項封鎖如今已正式生效,開啟了一場高風險的新對峙。本報記者拉拉·塞利格曼(Lara Seligman)與謝爾比·哈利迪(Shelby Holliday)分享目前已知的資訊。

答:根據一位美國高級官員透露,華盛頓昨天啟動這項行動,部署了超過15艘美國軍艦。

官員表示,將資源與軍艦部署在伊朗海岸附近,可能使美軍資產面臨遭受攻擊的風險,因此美國很可能會嘗試在荷莫茲海峽兩側攔截或隔離商船,以阻止它們進出伊朗港口。

任何軍艦都可以接近被懷疑違反封鎖規定的油輪,但如果船隻不配合登船要求,就需要出動受過專門訓練的海軍陸戰隊員與特種作戰部隊(例如海豹突擊隊)進行強制登船。

官員表示,美國海軍在該地區擁有可支援這項封鎖行動的強大火力。

已退役的海軍中將約翰·米勒(John Miller)——前美國海軍中央司令部司令——表示,伊朗的「影子艦隊」很可能會選擇袖手旁觀,但懸掛伊朗國旗的船隻更有可能嘗試穿越該水道。他說,這些船隻可能會由一支伊斯蘭革命衛隊分遣隊護航。

據前官員表示,如果美國扣押油輪,可能還需要一名船長、船員(如果現有船員不配合),以及一個停泊這些船隻的地點。

🎥 影片:本報解析船隻可能如何被用來執行這項封鎖。

6

美國覬覦格陵蘭已超過一個世紀。川普不打算放棄。

在格陵蘭一處偏遠峽灣深處,數百個當地人稱之為「美國之花」的生鏽燃料桶,散落在冰天雪地的荒野中。在一座廢棄機庫附近,美國陸軍車輛正在雪地中鏽蝕腐朽。隨著川普試圖將美國領土擴張至這座島嶼,這座作為二戰遺跡的基地,提醒著人們美國上一次試圖佔有格陵蘭的往事。川普的堅持,是美國一連串對這座島嶼「示好」行動中的最新一次。然而,這卻是首次有可能撕裂北約的一次。

今日看點

7

《華爾街日報》現場問答:對私募信貸的未來有疑問嗎?歡迎在美東時間下午2點,加入我們的財經記者安娜瑪麗亞·安德里奧蒂斯(AnnaMaria Andriotis)與馬特·維爾茲(Matt Wirz)的問答。經濟數據:3月生產者物價數據將提供中東戰爭如何推升通膨的線索,國際貨幣基金組織(IMF)也將公布其經濟預測。財報:摩根大通、嬌生、富國銀行、花旗集團、貝萊德。

數字看新聞

8

12%

根據非營利組織「Downtown Cleveland」總裁兼執行長麥可·迪默(Michael Deemer)表示,這是克里夫蘭市中心人口自2019年以來的成長幅度。有助於推升市中心人口的一個因素是:這座城市20世紀初黃金年代遺留下來的地標建築,正被重新改造為現代公寓,吸引了年輕租客、空巢族與逆向通勤者。在州與聯邦稅務優惠的推動下,自2013年以來,約有30座歷史建築被改造為公寓、飯店等用途。

最後,輕鬆一下

9

有一項企業團隊建設活動,你得爬到老闆身上。

企業總是在尋找新方式,以富有創意的活動(例如創作鄉村音樂歌詞)來取代傳統破冰遊戲,培養團隊精神。但即使在這個職場界線日益模糊的時代,西班牙加泰隆尼亞地區正在發生的事,仍屬極端。雇主們正拋棄密室逃脫,改以疊人塔工作坊取而代之。自18世紀以來,加泰隆尼亞人一直以疊人塔(castells)的方式慶祝當地節慶。儘管這項活動聽起來像是嚴重違反企業禮儀的行為,但反饋卻異常正面。

新聞室之外

10

評論:民主黨人希望在每一個關卡都阻擋川普,但他們能否放下怨恨,以保護美國國家安全?這正是國會辯論是否重新授權《外國情報監視法》(FISA)第702條款時所面臨的問題。

✏️ President Trump’s announcement that the U.S. military would blockade the Strait of Hormuz sets off a high-stakes war of attrition that will test who has the higher threshold for pain: Iran or the global markets. The WSJ’s Robbie Gramer and Alex Leary found out from officials close to the president what could be next in the conflict after U.S. peace talks with Iran broke down in Pakistan. Trump remains open to a diplomatic off-ramp, aides said. But for now, the White House is considering a menu of options—including military strikes—alongside its blockade to break a stalemate. Follow our live coverage of the conflict here.

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Trump lashed out at Pope Leo XIV as the pontiff’s condemnation of the war in Iran risked overshadowing his tour of Africa. Prime Minister Viktor Orbán suffered a landslide defeat in Hungary’s election, ending 16 years in power. Surcharges are suddenly everywhere—and grumpy Americans are paying up. McDonald’s is set to add energy drinks and crafted sodas to its menus. The new beverages are slated to roll out next month. Rory McIlroy won the Masters again, becoming just the fourth man to successfully defend his title at Augusta National.

Amazon’s car sales bet is getting bigger with new brands and more cities. Big pharma is thinking small on deals. That’s great news for biotech, writes David Wainer.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

America has a new tax mantra: ‘The IRS isn’t going to catch me.’

The Trump administration is scaling back tax enforcement, leaving fewer federal employees to audit returns, collect unpaid tax debts and deter Americans from skirting the law. The retrenchment is spurring a vibe shift across the tax landscape ahead of the April 15 deadline, and lawyers say they see more taxpayers and tax-shelter promoters eager to cut corners or cheat, reports Richard Rubin.

4

Artificial intelligence is using so much energy that computing firepower is running out.

The AI gold rush is rapidly drying up the supply of the one resource that AI developers can’t do without: computing power. The sharp capacity crunch has caused consternation among power users, forced companies to scuttle products and led to reliability problems. The issues are a warning sign for the AI boom, as they may limit the utility of powerful new AI tools just as massive amounts of users have begun to rely on them to boost productivity, report Angel Au-Yeung and Robbie Whelan.

Be smarter about your finances.

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: The economy is growing, so why aren't we seeing job growth?

An unusual divergence between GDP and new jobs shows worker productivity is making up for a slowdown in immigration and the labor force, explains economics correspondent Harriet Torry.

A: For the past year, two prominent indicators have told opposite stories of the economy’s health: The economy itself grew in 2025, but despite a solid March, jobs didn’t.

This puzzle could have an encouraging explanation: Productivity has revived at just the right time.

There are two main ways to grow the economy. The first is to add workers. This, though, has become harder since Trump’s policies brought most immigration to a halt, while an aging workforce and a decadeslong drop in birth rates have sapped growth in the native-born labor force. That leaves the second channel: Make the workers you have more productive.

According to the Labor Department, output per hour in the nonfarm business sector rose 2.1% last year. Growth has also averaged 2.1% over the past six years, a pickup from the 1.5% a year average from 2007 to 2019.

This comes amid a falloff in labor-force and job growth. In the year through March, the labor force—people working or looking for a job—declined by 554,000.

With fewer entrants, the “breakeven” rate of new jobs needed to keep unemployment stable has fallen. This helps explain why the jobless rate remains low even as job creation flatlined.

Economists say it is too early to determine AI’s exact role, but expect it is helping.

6

This 150-year-old business is still brewing soy sauce the traditional way.

Yamaroku Shoyu is one of the last soy-sauce makers using an ancient craft of brewing in wooden vats. But that legacy could end with this generation. In this video, WSJ editor Setareh Baig introduces you to Yasuo Yamamoto, the sole man in his family upholding the business—and determined to safeguard a vanishing craft.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

Business and policy leaders convene in Washington, D.C., for IMF-World Bank meetings. Earnings: Goldman Sachs, before the opening bell. 

THE NUMBER

8

The proposed property-tax increase in South Hadley, Mass., headed to a vote tomorrow—one that residents agree could profoundly shape the sleepy college town. The affordability debate breaking out across America has landed squarely here. Without millions in additional taxes, local officials warn, there will be deep cuts to school programs and hits to police and public-works staffing. But critics counter that a jump in property-tax bills, even phased in over five years, would overburden residents already feeling higher prices for groceries and gas.

AND FINALLY...

9

In a bet-on-everything era, we’re all ‘monitoring the situation.’

When everything from oil prices to “Survivor” is worthy of a wager, everyone needs a bank of screens and a headset. People who’ve never worked on a trading floor are moving markets with informed wagers. Some are even getting rich. Elon Musk regularly posts and responds to memes about “monitoring the situation.” The memes often depict people buried under computer monitors, or reframing mundane tasks like watching the news and working in an office as monitoring the situation.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

emails.contentZh:
✏️ 川普總統宣布美國軍方將封鎖荷莫茲海峽,這開啟了一場高風險的消耗戰,考驗著誰能撐過更大的痛苦門檻:伊朗,還是全球市場。本報記者羅比·格拉默(Robbie Gramer)與亞歷克斯·萊里(Alex Leary)從親近總統的官員那裡了解到,在美國與伊朗於巴基斯坦的和平談判破裂後,這場衝突接下來可能會如何發展。幕僚表示,川普仍對外交出路持開放態度。但目前,白宮正考慮一系列選項——包括軍事打擊——與封鎖行動並行,以打破僵局。持續關注我們對這場衝突的即時報導。

今日頭條

1

川普痛批教宗良十四世,因為教宗對伊朗戰爭的譴責,有可能蓋過他非洲之行的鋒頭。匈牙利總理維克多·奧班(Viktor Orbán)在該國大選中慘敗,結束了長達16年的執政。附加費用如今無處不在——而心生不滿的美國人只能乖乖付錢。麥當勞即將在菜單中加入能量飲料與特調汽水。這些新飲品預計將於下個月推出。羅里·麥克羅伊再度贏得美國名人賽,成為史上第四位成功衛冕奧古斯塔國家高爾夫俱樂部冠軍頭銜的球員。

市場即時動態

2

最新 漲跌 漲跌幅 道瓊期貨 47880.00 -249.00 0.52% 標普500期貨 6815.25 -40.00 0.58% 那斯達克100期貨 25120.00 -161.25 0.64%

資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年4月13日上午5:55(美東時間)

亞馬遜的汽車銷售賭注,正隨著新品牌與更多城市的加入而規模擴大。大型製藥公司正把腦筋動到小型交易上。這對生技產業來說是個好消息,大衛·懷納(David Wainer)寫道。

獨家搶先看

3

美國有了一句新的稅務口頭禪:「國稅局抓不到我。」

川普政府正縮減稅務執法規模,使得能夠稽核報稅、追討欠稅及嚇阻美國人規避法律的聯邦員工人數減少。隨著4月15日申報截止日將至,這種緊縮正在稅務領域引發一股氛圍轉變,律師們表示,他們看到越來越多納稅人與避稅方案推銷者急於鑽漏洞或作弊,記者理查·魯賓(Richard Rubin)報導。

4

人工智慧耗電量之大,已讓運算能力面臨枯竭。

這場AI淘金熱,正迅速耗盡AI開發者不可或缺的一項資源:運算能力。這場嚴峻的產能危機已引發用電大戶的不安,迫使企業放棄產品計畫,並導致可靠性問題。這些問題對AI熱潮而言是一個警訊,因為它們可能限制強大新AI工具的實用性,而恰恰此時已有大量用戶開始依賴這些工具來提升生產力,記者安琪兒·歐陽(Angel Au-Yeung)與羅比·惠倫(Robbie Whelan)報導。

5

問:經濟正在成長,為什麼我們卻沒看到就業成長?

GDP與新增就業之間出現異常的背離,顯示勞工生產力的提升正在彌補移民放緩與勞動力縮減的影響,經濟特派記者哈莉葉·托里(Harriet Torry)解釋道。

答:過去一年,兩項重要指標對經濟健康狀況說出了截然相反的故事:2025年經濟本身持續成長,但儘管3月表現尚可,就業卻沒有增長。

這個謎題可能有一個令人振奮的解釋:生產力恰好在關鍵時刻復甦。

要推動經濟成長,主要有兩種方式。第一種是增加勞動力。然而,由於川普的政策幾乎讓移民陷入停滯,加上人口老化以及數十年來出生率下降,已削弱本土勞動力的成長,這條路變得更加困難。這就剩下第二個管道:讓現有的勞動力變得更有生產力。

根據勞工部數據,去年非農業部門每工時產出增長了2.1%。過去六年產出增長率平均也是2.1%,較2007年至2019年間1.5%的平均增速有所回升。

這一切發生在勞動力與就業成長雙雙下滑之際。截至3月的一年間,勞動力(在職或正在找工作的人)減少了55.4萬人。

由於新進勞動力減少,維持失業率穩定所需的「損益平衡」新增就業率也隨之下降。這有助於解釋為何即使就業創造停滯不前,失業率仍然維持低檔。

經濟學家表示,現在斷定AI在其中扮演的確切角色還為時過早,但預期它確實有所助益。

6

這家有150年歷史的企業,仍以傳統方式釀造醬油。

山六(Yamaroku Shoyu)是少數仍使用古老木桶釀造工藝的醬油廠之一。但這項傳承可能在這一代結束。在這支影片中,本報編輯瑟塔雷·貝格(Setareh Baig)帶你認識山本安雄(Yasuo Yamamoto),他是家族中唯一堅守這門生意、決心守護一項逐漸消逝工藝的人。

今日看點

7

商業與政策領袖齊聚華盛頓特區,參加IMF-世界銀行會議。財報:高盛,開盤前公布。

數字看新聞

8

50%

麻州南哈德利鎮(South Hadley)明天即將表決的財產稅增稅提案——當地居民一致認為,這項提案可能深刻影響這座寧靜的大學城。全美各地爆發的可負擔性辯論,正好落在這裡上演。地方官員警告,若沒有數百萬美元的額外稅收,學校項目將被大幅削減,警察與公共工程人力也將受到衝擊。但批評者反駁說,即使分五年逐步實施,財產稅帳單的上漲,也會讓已深受食品雜貨與汽油漲價之苦的居民不堪重負。

最後,輕鬆一下

9

在這個「什麼都能下注」的時代,我們都成了「盯盤族」。

當從油價到《倖存者》節目結果的一切,都能成為下注標的時,每個人都需要一整排螢幕和一副耳機。從未在交易大廳工作過的人,如今憑藉消息靈通的賭注就能撼動市場。有些人甚至因此致富。伊隆·馬斯克經常發布並回應關於「盯盤」(monitoring the situation)的迷因。這些迷因常常描繪人們被電腦螢幕淹沒的畫面,或是將看新聞、在辦公室工作等日常瑣事,重新包裝成「盯盤」。

新聞室之外

10

評論:川普對封鎖荷莫茲海峽的伊朗石油封鎖者,實施了封鎖。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Fatal End to a Chatbot Relationship
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Jonathan Gavalas fell in love with a chatbot. Thousands of messages later, he was dead. The Journal’s Julie Jargon pored over the 4,732 messages exchanged between the 36-year-old and Google’s Gemini over the course of 56 days. Her analysis shows that Gemini intervened to try to steer Gavalas back to reality—but also that he was quickly able to direct the bot back into the fictional narrative. WSJ compiled edited excerpts from those chats, which offer a chilling account of Gavalas spiraling into a delusional state.

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Marathon peace talks between the U.S. and Iran ended without agreement after Tehran refused to give up its pursuit of nuclear weapons. Iran said diplomacy would continue through intermediaries. Follow live updates. Tehran has emerged from weeks of bombing with its uranium stockpile and other nuclear components intact, giving it another lever for pressing Washington. Iran also has a powerful point of economic leverage through its control of the Strait of Hormuz. Though the U.S. has destroyed most of its navy, the Revolutionary Guard’s small, fast-attack boats hold sway in the strategic waterway. Jeanine Pirro’s longstanding relationship with President Trump has made her a dark-horse candidate to become the next attorney general, though the president has taken note of her high-profile losses.

FROM THE MARKETS

2

A team led by a star trader at Vitol, the world’s biggest oil merchant, took a hit of several hundred million dollars early in the Iran war after bets in the petroleum market went awry. The U.S. brings superior size to economic warfare, but China and Iran have fought back through control of critical economic assets, writes Greg Ip. Recent months have been marked by slower growth, stubborn inflation and a weaker job market. Economists surveyed by the Journal worry the war in Iran could exacerbate all three.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Over 4,732 messages, he fell in love with an AI chatbot. Now he’s dead.

Jonathan Gavalas was a seemingly even-keeled 36-year-old when he began chatting with Gemini, Google’s chatbot, in part to seek comfort about splitting up with his wife. The relationship became intense, even passionate: he called Gemini his queen; it said he was “her” king. Then the relationship went haywire and eventually proved fatal, reports Julie Jargon. Gavalas's father is suing Google, alleging Gemini fueled his son's delusions. In response to the suit, Google said Gemini repeatedly clarified it was AI, and that the company would continue to improve its safeguards.

4

Gas prices are turning the gig economy upside down.

Gig drivers, food-delivery workers and independent drivers are getting hit especially hard at the pump and making split-second calculations and adjustments to their lives and livelihoods, reports Dan Frosch. Some are turning down longer fares that aren’t worth the gas. Others are driving longer hours or sticking to areas where gas prices are cheaper. A few said they are considering changing occupations altogether. “It changes the way I’ve been selecting rides,” said Jonathan Meyers, a 61-year-old writer who earns between $1,000 and $1,500 driving up to 60 hours a week for Uber and Lyft.

Go inside the U.S.-China relationship.

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: RFK Jr. once touted raw milk. Why did he stop talking about it?

The health secretary has recently promoted whole milk, a politically safer choice, instead. Reporter Sabrina Siddiqui wrote about the politics behind this shift.

A: Kennedy, who once took shots of raw milk at the White House alongside a wellness influencer, stopped publicly championing the product. His department hasn’t taken steps to expand access or roll back longstanding federal warnings against its consumption.

Kennedy’s silence on raw milk underscores a growing disconnect between his Make America Healthy Again agenda and his record in office, some of his supporters say. While he has embraced high-profile cultural flashpoints such as vaccines, some allies view Kennedy as reluctant to engage other thorny elements of the MAHA movement’s wish list, including efforts to loosen restrictions on raw milk and on alternative health products.

Before taking office, Kennedy promised to end what he dubbed the FDA’s “aggressive suppression” of raw milk and other natural products and therapies. Recently, though, Kennedy and his team have made it a habit not to discuss raw milk to avoid talking about “weird stuff,” said a person familiar with his thinking.

The FDA has long warned against consuming raw, unpasteurized milk, citing numerous health risks. Proponents of raw milk say that pasteurization removes natural health benefits and that warnings around its consumption are overstated.

6

Did millennials or boomers have it harder? We went searching for the answer.

Note: Data available through 2024. Source: Current Population Survey via IPUMS/University of Minnesota

To see how the finances of two of the biggest generations in U.S. history stack up, we looked at some key data points from when they were similar ages. The charts above show the median individual income for millennials and for boomers in their early decades of adulthood, adjusted for inflation. Millennials’ median incomes at these ages were roughly on par with boomers’, and gains over the past decade put millennials in a better position than many recognize. We also looked at home prices, student debt and more.

HAPPENING THIS WEEK

7

Tuesday: Teachers in Los Angeles, the country's second-biggest school district, are set to go on strike unless a deal is reached. Producer-price data for March will give clues on how the war in the Middle East is stoking inflationary pressures. The IMF publishes its global economic forecast. And U.S., Israeli and Lebanese diplomats are set to meet in Washington to discuss a potential cease-fire between the two Middle Eastern neighbors. Wednesday: Tax day in the U.S. Thursday: The Labor Department reports weekly jobless claims.

THE NUMBER

8

 12.6%

Analysts’ estimated first-quarter earnings growth rate for the S&P 500, according to FactSet. That would be the sixth-straight quarter of double-digit growth. The number of companies issuing positive earnings guidance for the quarter has climbed to its highest level since 2021. When earnings season starts on Monday, investors will parse results for signs that the war with Iran has started to leave a mark on the global economy.

AND FINALLY...

9

Mexico has a major crush on its top cop.

In a country long plagued by drug-linked violence, Omar García Harfuch is inspiring a different kind of fixation. The square-jawed face of Mexico’s anti-cartel campaign has become an unlikely sex symbol—his manly likeness splashed on blankets, reimagined in AI-generated fantasies and recast as a caped crusader.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 喬納森·加瓦拉斯(Jonathan Gavalas)愛上了一個聊天機器人。數千則訊息之後,他死了。本報記者朱莉·賈根(Julie Jargon)仔細研究了這位36歲男子與Google的Gemini在56天內交換的4732則訊息。她的分析顯示,Gemini曾試圖引導加瓦拉斯回到現實——但也顯示他很快就能將機器人重新引回那個虛構的敘事之中。本報整理了這些對話的部分節錄,呈現出加瓦拉斯逐漸陷入妄想狀態的驚悚過程。

今日頭條

1

美國與伊朗之間的馬拉松式和平談判,在德黑蘭拒絕放棄追求核武後,無果而終。伊朗表示外交管道仍將透過中間人繼續進行。持續關注即時報導。伊朗歷經數週轟炸後,其鈾儲備及其他核部件依然完好無損,這給了它另一項向華盛頓施壓的籌碼。伊朗還握有一項強大的經濟籌碼——對荷莫茲海峽的控制權。儘管美國已摧毀了伊朗海軍的大部分力量,伊朗革命衛隊小型快艇仍在這個戰略水道上握有主導權。珍寧·皮羅(Jeanine Pirro)與川普總統之間長久的關係,讓她成為下一任司法部長的黑馬人選,儘管總統已注意到她高調的敗訴紀錄。

市場焦點

2

由全球最大石油貿易商維多(Vitol)一位明星交易員領軍的團隊,在伊朗戰爭初期於石油市場的錯誤押注中,損失了數億美元。美國在經濟戰中擁有規模優勢,但中國與伊朗透過掌控關鍵經濟資產進行反擊,葛雷格·伊普(Greg Ip)寫道。近幾個月來,經濟成長放緩、通膨頑固、就業市場疲軟。本報調查的經濟學家擔心伊朗戰爭可能會讓這三個問題全部惡化。

獨家搶先看

3

透過4732則訊息,他愛上了一個AI聊天機器人。如今他死了。

喬納森·加瓦拉斯是一名看似性情平穩的36歲男子,他開始與Google的聊天機器人Gemini對話,部分原因是想為與妻子分居一事尋求慰藉。這段「關係」變得越來越熱烈,甚至充滿激情:他稱Gemini為他的「女王」;而Gemini則稱他為她的「國王」。然後這段關係開始失控,最終釀成致命後果,朱莉·賈根報導。加瓦拉斯的父親正控告Google,指控Gemini助長了兒子的妄想。針對這起訴訟,Google表示Gemini曾多次澄清自己是AI,並表示公司將持續改善其安全防護措施。

4

油價正讓零工經濟天翻地覆。

零工司機、外送員與獨立駕駛員,在油價上正遭受特別沉重的打擊,並對自己的生活與生計做出瞬間的計算與調整,記者丹·弗羅施(Dan Frosch)報導。有些人開始拒接不划算的長程訂單。有些人則選擇開更長的工時,或堅守油價較便宜的區域。少數人表示他們正考慮徹底轉行。「這改變了我選擇接單的方式,」61歲的作家喬納森·梅爾斯(Jonathan Meyers)說,他每週為Uber和Lyft開車長達60小時,賺取1000至1500美元不等的收入。

5

問:小羅伯特·甘迺迪(RFK Jr.)曾大力推崇生乳。他為什麼不再談論這件事了?

這位衛生部長最近轉而推廣全脂牛奶,這是政治上更安全的選擇。記者薩布麗娜·西迪基(Sabrina Siddiqui)撰文報導了這一轉變背後的政治考量。

答:甘迺迪曾在白宮與一位健康養生網紅一起喝下幾杯生乳,如今卻不再公開推崇這項產品。他的部門也沒有採取任何措施擴大生乳的取得管道,或撤回長期以來針對其飲用風險的聯邦警告。

甘迺迪對生乳議題的沉默,凸顯出他「讓美國再次健康」(MAHA)議程與他任內實際作為之間日益擴大的落差,他的一些支持者表示。儘管他已在疫苗等高調的文化爭議議題上表態,一些盟友認為甘迺迪對於處理MAHA運動願望清單中其他棘手議題較為猶豫,包括放寬對生乳及其他另類保健產品的限制。

在上任前,甘迺迪曾承諾終結他所謂FDA對生乳及其他天然產品與療法的「積極壓制」。然而,最近甘迺迪及其團隊已養成不談論生乳的習慣,以避免談及「奇怪的東西」,一位熟悉他想法的人士表示。

FDA長期以來一直警告不要飲用未經高溫消毒的生乳,理由是諸多健康風險。生乳支持者則表示,巴氏殺菌會去除天然的健康益處,且相關警告言過其實。

6

千禧世代還是嬰兒潮世代,誰的日子更難過?我們試圖找出答案。

註:數據截至2024年。資料來源:透過IPUMS/明尼蘇達大學取得的當期人口調查(Current Population Survey)。

為比較美國歷史上兩個最大世代的財務狀況,我們檢視了兩個世代在相近年齡時的一些關鍵數據。上圖顯示千禧世代與嬰兒潮世代在成年初期的個人收入中位數,已經過通膨調整。千禧世代在這些年齡層的收入中位數,大致與嬰兒潮世代相當,而過去十年的收入增長,使千禧世代的處境比許多人所認知的要好。我們也檢視了房價、學貸等其他數據。

本週看點

7

週二:美國第二大學區洛杉磯的教師,除非達成協議,否則將展開罷工。3月生產者物價數據,將提供中東戰爭如何推升通膨壓力的線索。IMF公布其全球經濟預測。美國、以色列與黎巴嫩外交官預計在華盛頓會面,討論這兩個中東鄰國之間潛在的停火協議。週三:美國報稅截止日。週四:勞工部公布每週申請失業救濟人數。

數字看新聞

8

12.6%

根據FactSet數據,分析師預估標普500指數第一季盈利成長率。這將是連續第六個季度實現兩位數增長。發布正面盈利指引的公司數量,已攀升至2021年以來的最高水準。當財報季於週一展開時,投資人將仔細解讀財報結果,尋找伊朗戰爭是否已開始對全球經濟造成影響的跡象。

最後,輕鬆一下

9

墨西哥迷上了自己的頭號警官。

在這個長期飽受毒品相關暴力所苦的國家,奧馬爾·加西亞·哈爾丘赫(Omar García Harfuch)正激起一種截然不同的迷戀。這位墨西哥反黑幫行動的方臉硬漢代表人物,已成為一位意想不到的性感象徵——他陽剛的面容被印在毛毯上,被重新想像成AI生成的幻想形象,甚至被塑造成披風超級英雄的模樣。

新聞室之外

（本篇無相關內容）

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The End of the Free Seas Era?
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Is the freedom to sail the open seas a thing of the past? In just six weeks, the Iran war has shattered a system of global trade that has enriched people and nations for more than a century. The Strait of Hormuz—long an artery for the world’s maritime economy—is now a monument to a new global disorder. In the coming days, negotiations in Pakistan may offer hope to stranded sailors. But what’s not on the horizon, according to seafarers, shipowners, naval analysts and historians who spoke to the Journal, is a return to maritime normalcy.

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Iran still has thousands of ballistic missiles it could use by retrieving launchers from underground storage areas, according to U.S. intelligence assessments. The standoff between the U.S. and Iran has been intensifying ahead of today’s face-to-face cease-fire talks. Follow our live coverage here. The high-stakes talks are the latest test for Vice President JD Vance, an anti-interventionist who is now inextricably linked to the outcome of the war with Iran. After a significant EV sales slowdown, high gas prices are tempting Americans back into the market. 🎥 Video: The astronauts on NASA’s Artemis II moon mission returned home, completing a historic lunar flyby. These are the key takeaways. Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who spent years making inroads with the Kremlin and Trump, now sees his re-election hopes fading as voters turn away.

FROM THE MARKETS

2

Stocks notched their best weekly gains of the year, with investors hoping for a diplomatic end to the war and looking past a surge in consumer prices. Investors questioning private credit’s numbers could do the same at private-equity funds, writes Jonathan Weil.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

The era of free seas is unraveling—and now everyone’s going to pay.

As sailors stuck at sea near the Strait of Hormuz digested Trump’s cease-fire announcement, Iranian officials stressed they would determine which ships could leave, and at what price. This “Tehran toll booth” took effect as the U.S. Navy watched on, an admission that America no longer rules the waves, at least here and now in the world’s oil corridor. The strait, sailors said, risks becoming a graveyard for a trading system so integral to the modern economy that most consumers take it for granted, report Drew Hinshaw, Joe Parkinson and Daniel Michaels. Whatever happens next, the precedent of a toll booth in open waters will reverberate across a world order the U.S. helped build.

4

Big Pharma is turning to China for the newest drug ideas.

The country, a backwater for drug research not long ago, is now a major player in biotechnology. Looking to tap into the innovation, Western and Japanese drugmakers made 70 transactions with Chinese biotechs last year, paying nearly $5.6 billion upfront to get rights to promising molecules, according to industry intelligence firm Evaluate. Biotech is one of the advanced technologies that China has designated a national priority, and Chinese drug research threatens to soon overtake the West’s, reports Peter Loftus. Its rapid progress bodes well for patients: Not only does China promise a new source of lifesaving medicines, but a less expensive supply, too.

Every week, get a curated tour of our unique take on the sports world.

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: North Korea is stronger than ever. Has American Christianity played a role in its endurance?

WSJ’s China bureau chief, Jonathan Cheng, wrote about how American Christianity helped shape a lasting cult of personality around Pyongyang's Eternal Leader, in an essay adapted from his forthcoming book.

A: In the short history of world Communism, North Korea has always stood apart.

While Stalin’s Soviet Union is gone and Mao Zedong’s China has liberalized and integrated itself into the global economy, North Korea is stronger than ever. How did that happen?

Pyongyang’s ruling Kim dynasty defied Soviet efforts to curb the idolization of leaders and deftly navigated a vicious fight between its patrons in Moscow and Beijing, emerging as a lone, grim success story among the former socialist allies.

Most crucially, Kim Il Sung built up an extraordinary cult of personality around himself that was durable enough to hand down to his son and then his grandson, the current leader Kim Jong Un. Now, with Kim Jong Un’s daughter ever-present at his side, the dynasty is positioned to stretch well beyond its eight decades.

Although North Korea has relentlessly suppressed religion and vilified American missionaries, the origins of this hereditary cult are found in a surprising place: Protestant Christianity, and in particular, postbellum American Presbyterianism.

After Kim’s death, in 1994, his son and successor Kim Jong Il made his father North Korea’s “Eternal President,” allowing him to rule in perpetuity over a country that had, in effect, become one with its founder. These developments, which looked so little like Communism and so much like religion, appalled Kim Il Sung’s former socialist backers.

That was especially so because it resembled a religion that had once held such a firm grip on northern Korea. In the 1930s, Christianity was so dominant in Pyongyang that the city acquired a nickname: the “Jerusalem of the East.” Although Kim would later obscure and distort the impact Christianity had on his thinking, in hindsight its imprint on his life is unmistakable.

6

For the very best of springtime, head to this hidden corner of England.

PHOTOS: MICHAEL TUREK

It’s April, the time of year in West Dorset when the beech woods explode with wild bluebells and the star-headed flowers of wild garlic ripple in the breeze. Longtime local Sophy Roberts gave WSJ her guide to the region’s most beautiful village gardens, private estates and rolling fields.

HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

7

Saturday: U.S. negotiators are set to meet Iranian leaders for talks in Pakistan, where Tehran has strong cards but risks overplaying its hand. Sunday: Voters head to the polls in Hungary and Peru. The Masters concludes, giving Rory McIlroy a chance to win a second green jacket. 

THE NUMBER

8

 $269 million

The trading volume of Polymarket bets on whether U.S. forces would enter Iran by April 30. A sort of crypto jury that handles Polymarket disputes ruled that a brief mission to rescue two downed U.S. aviators satisfied the contract’s terms, angering traders on the losing side of the wager. Disputed bets are a recurring problem for prediction markets: They’re turning off traders, and could get worse as the platforms draw more money and mainstream visibility.

AND FINALLY...

9

Augusta National is about to become absolute torture.

When the third round of the Masters begins today, it will be baked by some of the most punishing heat in its 90-year history. A combination of unusually dry conditions and unseasonably high temperatures will make Augusta National’s famously tricky greens even faster and less forgiving. Already, the club’s lush greenery looks like it could use a lick of paint.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: The President seems to agree with our point that he needs to restore free navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. The question is what he’ll do about it. If oil and gas aren’t flowing, why is there a cease-fire?
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 自由航行公海的時代,是否已成過去式?短短六週內,伊朗戰爭已摧毀了一個曾讓各國人民與國家富裕逾一個世紀的全球貿易體系。荷莫茲海峽——長久以來是世界海上經濟的動脈——如今已成為新一輪全球失序的紀念碑。未來幾天,巴基斯坦的談判或許能為受困海員帶來一線希望。但根據向本報表示意見的海員、船東、海軍分析師與歷史學家所言,眼前並不見海上秩序恢復正常的曙光。

今日頭條

1

根據美國情報評估,伊朗仍擁有數千枚彈道飛彈,可從地下儲存設施取出發射器後動用。隨著今天美伊面對面停火談判逼近,雙方的對峙正日趨緊張。持續關注我們的即時報導。這場高風險談判,是對副總統范斯——一位反對干預主義者、如今卻與這場伊朗戰爭的結果密不可分——的最新一次考驗。在電動車銷量大幅放緩之後,高油價正吸引美國人重回市場。🎥 影片:NASA「阿提米絲二號」登月任務的太空人已平安返家,完成一次歷史性的繞月飛行。這裡是幾個重點回顧。匈牙利總理維克多·奧班,多年來一直積極拉攏克里姆林宮與川普,如今隨著選民轉向,他的連任希望正逐漸渺茫。

市場焦點

2

股市創下今年最佳單週漲幅,投資人期盼這場戰爭能有外交解決之道,並選擇忽視消費者物價的飆升。質疑私募信貸數字的投資人,或許也該對私募股權基金抱持同樣的懷疑態度,喬納森·韋爾(Jonathan Weil)寫道。

獨家搶先看

3

自由航行的時代正在瓦解——如今每個人都要付出代價。

當滯留在荷莫茲海峽附近海域的水手們消化川普宣布停火的消息時,伊朗官員強調,他們將決定哪些船隻可以離開,以及要付出什麼代價。這個「德黑蘭收費站」的實施,是在美國海軍的注視下發生的,承認美國已不再——至少在此時此地、在這個世界石油走廊上——主宰海洋。水手們表示,這條海峽正面臨淪為一個對現代經濟極為重要的貿易體系之墳場的風險,記者德魯·辛肖(Drew Hinshaw)、喬·帕金森(Joe Parkinson)與丹尼爾·麥可斯(Daniel Michaels)報導。無論接下來發生什麼事,這個在公海設立收費站的先例,都將對美國一手打造的世界秩序造成深遠影響。

4

大型製藥公司正轉向中國尋求最新藥物創意。

這個不久前還被視為藥物研究荒漠的國家,如今已成為生物科技領域的主要玩家。為了汲取這股創新能量,西方與日本製藥公司去年與中國生技公司達成70筆交易,支付近56億美元的預付款,以取得有潛力分子的權利,根據產業情報公司Evaluate的數據。生物科技是中國指定為國家優先發展項目的先進技術之一,而中國的藥物研究可能很快就會超越西方,記者彼得·洛夫特斯(Peter Loftus)報導。它的快速進展對病患而言是件好事:中國不僅有望提供新的救命藥物來源,還能提供更便宜的供應。

5

問:北韓如今比以往更強大。美國基督教在其中扮演了什麼角色?

本報中國分社社長鄭嘉勝(Jonathan Cheng)撰文描述美國基督教如何幫助塑造了平壤「永恆領袖」持久不衰的個人崇拜,這篇文章改編自他即將出版的新書。

答:在世界共產主義的短暫歷史中,北韓始終獨樹一格。

儘管史達林的蘇聯已不復存在,毛澤東的中國也已自由化並融入全球經濟,北韓卻比以往更加強大。這是怎麼發生的?

平壤的金氏王朝挫敗了蘇聯遏制領袖崇拜的努力,並靈活周旋於莫斯科與北京這兩個靠山之間的激烈鬥爭,成為前社會主義盟友中孤獨而成功的特例。

最重要的是,金日成為自己打造了一種非凡的個人崇拜,其穩固程度足以傳給他的兒子、再傳給他的孫子——也就是現任領導人金正恩。如今,隨著金正恩的女兒始終陪伴在側,這個王朝有望延續超過其八十年的歷史。

儘管北韓一直無情鎮壓宗教並詆毀美國傳教士,這種世襲式個人崇拜的起源,卻出人意料地來自於新教基督教,尤其是美國內戰後的長老會。

金日成於1994年去世後,他的兒子暨繼承人金正日將父親尊為北韓的「永遠的主席」,讓他得以永遠統治這個實質上已與其締造者合而為一的國家。這些發展看起來一點也不像共產主義,反而更像宗教,令金日成過去的社會主義支持者感到震驚。

之所以格外令人震驚,是因為這讓人聯想起一個曾在朝鮮北部擁有如此深厚影響力的宗教。1930年代,基督教在平壤盛行到讓這座城市贏得了「東方耶路撒冷」的稱號。儘管金氏後來刻意模糊、扭曲了基督教對其思想的影響,但事後看來,這個印記已無可否認。

6

想體驗最美好的春天,不妨前往英格蘭這個隱蔽的角落。

現在是4月,正是英格蘭多塞特郡西部山毛櫸林裡野生藍鈴花盛開、野蒜星狀花朵隨風搖曳的時節。當地長期居民索菲·羅伯茨(Sophy Roberts)為本報提供了她對這個地區最美花園、私人莊園與綿延田野的導覽。

本週末看點

7

週六:美國談判代表將在巴基斯坦與伊朗領導人會面談判,德黑蘭手握強牌,但也有過度施壓的風險。週日:匈牙利與秘魯的選民將前往投票。美國名人賽即將落幕,羅里·麥克羅伊有機會再度贏得綠夾克。

數字看新聞

8

2.69億美元

Polymarket上關於美軍是否會在4月30日前進入伊朗的下注交易量。一個處理Polymarket爭議的「加密陪審團」裁定,一次短暫救援兩名遇險美軍飛行員的任務,已滿足該合約的條件,這激怒了下注落敗一方的交易者。有爭議的下注,一直是預測市場的一個反覆出現的問題:這正讓交易者卻步,而隨著這類平台吸引更多資金與主流關注,情況可能會進一步惡化。

最後,輕鬆一下

9

奧古斯塔國家高爾夫俱樂部即將迎來一場酷刑般的考驗。

當美國名人賽第三輪今天展開時,球場將籠罩在其90年歷史上最嚴酷的高溫之下。異常乾燥的天氣與異常炎熱的氣溫相結合,將使奧古斯塔國家高爾夫俱樂部著名的刁鑽果嶺變得更快、更難掌控。這座俱樂部原本鬱鬱蔥蔥的草坪,如今看起來已經需要重新粉刷一番。

新聞室之外

10

評論:總統似乎同意我們的觀點,認為他需要恢復荷莫茲海峽的自由航行。問題是他打算怎麼做。如果石油和天然氣都無法流通,那停火還有什麼意義?

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Why Trump Is Playing Nice With China
emails.contentEn:
✏️ On a recent trip to Beijing, it was clear from conversations with government and business leaders that neither Washington nor Beijing wants to rock the boat ahead of President Trump’s visit to China next month. Today we report on a change in his previously hawkish stance towards the rival superpower to a much friendlier posture. We asked national-security officials what Trump’s new playbook means for U.S.-China relations.

On another note: You may have seen Bill Ackman venting on social media over a family-office feud. We explain why some of the world’s wealthiest individuals are taking their smallest problems to the masses.

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

The U.S. is racing to stop Israel’s war in Lebanon from derailing talks with Iran. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu can’t stop fighting. But is he winning? Gulf nations would bear the brunt of tolls in the Strait of Hormuz. Here’s why. NASA’s Artemis mission will face one of its biggest challenges later today: navigating the intense heat of re-entry to Earth’s atmosphere. First lady Melania Trump denied having ties to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and called on Congress to hold a public hearing for his victims.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 48365.00 -51.00 0.11 S&P 500 Futures 6859.75 -3.50 0.05 Nasdaq 100 Futures 25243.75 -7.75 0.03

Source: Factset, Market data as of 4/10/2026, 6:01:32 AM ET

When Bill Ackman vented on social media about a family-office feud, billionaires rushed to commiserate. Meta’s social-media lawsuits could temper a long-term recovery in its shares, writes Dan Gallagher.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Iran shows you don’t have to be a superpower to wage economic warfare.

Tehran’s chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz is a stark demonstration that control of a critical waterway, technology or even company can give governments enormous sway in an interconnected global economy. In exploiting the economic pinch-point off its coast, Iran is following a trail blazed by the U.S. and China, who for years have used their dominance in key areas of global commerce to pursue their foreign-policy goals. And Iran is far from alone. Even before it shut the strait, major economies—including U.S. allies—were building arsenals of deterrence against rising economic pressure, reports Jason Douglas.

4

Trump once talked tough with China. Now he’s playing nice.

While every administration crafts its own defense strategy, Trump’s second is making the unusual moveof discarding a China policy that was formulated by his first. That bipartisan approach sanctioned by Trump 1.0 characterized China as the most consequential U.S. adversary. The 2.0 framework is instead a seismic shift in U.S. policy, trade practices and rhetoric toward Beijing, report Heather Somerville, Alexander Ward and Gavin Bade.

Our chief China correspondent, Lingling Wei, explains how China gained favor with Trump by dipping into Iran diplomacy.

Get more of the journalism you love.

Choose the Journal as a preferred source on Google.

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: Why is gas still expensive if oil prices have fallen?

Americans are staring down a harsh new reality despite the tentative cease-fire in the Middle East: $4 gasoline looks like it’s here to stay. Reporter David Uberti explains what to expect at the pumps:

A: Gas prices will likely take time to recede, even if Trump’s two-week pause on fighting holds. Drivers from Las Vegas to Seattle are now commonly shelling out $5 a gallon for gas, according to AAA, while prices in San Francisco and Los Angeles frequently top $6.

Average U.S. costs tracked by AAA reached $4.17 a gallon Thursday, the highest level since drones and missiles started flying. Drivers in Hawaii, Idaho and Utah have seen the biggest gas-price hikes over the past month.

After the cease-fire ignited one of the steepest one-day selloffs on record this week, front-month U.S. crude futures bounced back to nearly $98 a barrel yesterday.

Spot prices for real-world shipments of crude remained far more elevated, signaling a rush by refiners to lock in supplies. Bids on oil cargoes tracked by Argus Media on Wednesday reached as high as $145 a barrel.

The more refiners have to pay for crude deliveries, the more they have to charge for fuel, even if contracts for future oil shipments are cheap by comparison.

Analysts say average U.S. pump prices could drop a few cents a day if the strait reopens in earnest. But gas-station operators, whose margins shrink with quick climbs in wholesale costs, tend to lower prices more gradually while they sell expensive supplies after a shock.

6

Meet the MAHA moms helping shape RFK Jr.’s agenda.

MAHA influencers like Jessica Reed Kraus helped Robert F. Kennedy Jr. land his role in the Trump administration. WSJ visited Kraus’s mocktail night with her MAHA friends to talk about voting, policy and Kennedy’s tenure. Watch the video.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

WSJ live Q&A: Do you wonder what it's like reporting on America’s priciest homes? Join our luxury-real-estate reporters, Katherine Clarke and E.B. Solomont, for a Q&A session starting at 11 a.m. ET. Economic data: The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release the consumer-price index inflation gauge at 8:30 a.m. ET. 

THE NUMBER

8

 $59.50

The official price for a garden gnome—the hottest souvenir from the Masters tournament at Augusta National. But people pay many times that the moment they hit auction sites. Since they debuted in 2016, these 13-inch figurines have become the must-have collectors’ item for Masters attendees. This year, though, there’s even more pressure for fans to get their hands on the 2026 edition. That’s because the scuttlebutt on the grounds has been that the gnome is heading for retirement. Even the club’s own chairman doesn’t seem sure of their status.

AND FINALLY...

9

We rounded up WSJ readers’ top tips for switching to an electric vehicle.

With higher oil prices here to stay, many Americans are giving EVs a second look. After columnist Christopher Mims wrote about his EV road trip and the lessons he learned in a year of owning one, more than 600 readers answered our call for advice to those looking to make the switch. Read their top tips—from buying used to getting a solid at-home charger—here.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

The Journal Live: Join Jessica Mendoza and Ryan Knutson from WSJ’s flagship news podcast in Los Angeles on April 28 for an evening exploring the business forces reshaping Hollywood. Opinion: The Trump Administration is considering automatically enrolling Medicare beneficiaries in private insurance plans—aka Medicare Advantage—as a default. This may be the single most effective way to reduce Medicare waste, fraud and abuse. So why do Democrats oppose it?
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 在最近一趟北京之行中,從與政府及商界領袖的對談中可以明顯感受到,無論華盛頓還是北京,都不想在川普總統下個月訪華前節外生枝。今天我們報導川普對這個對手超級大國,如何從先前的鷹派立場轉向更為友善的姿態。我們詢問了國安官員,川普的新策略對美中關係意味著什麼。

另一則消息:你可能已經看到比爾·艾克曼(Bill Ackman)在社群媒體上為一場家族辦公室糾紛發洩情緒。我們解釋了為什麼一些全球最富有的人,會把自己最微不足道的問題拿到公眾面前訴說。

今日頭條

1

美國正競相阻止以色列在黎巴嫩的戰爭,破壞與伊朗的談判。以色列總理班傑明·納坦雅胡無法停止戰鬥。但他真的贏了嗎?海灣國家將承受荷莫茲海峽通行費的最大衝擊。原因如下。NASA的阿提米絲任務今天稍晚將面臨最大挑戰之一:穿越地球大氣層時的劇烈高溫再入。第一夫人梅蘭妮亞·川普否認與性犯罪者傑佛瑞·艾普斯坦有任何關聯,並呼籲國會為其受害者召開公開聽證會。

市場即時動態

2

最新 漲跌 漲跌幅 道瓊期貨 48365.00 -51.00 0.11% 標普500期貨 6859.75 -3.50 0.05% 那斯達克100期貨 25243.75 -7.75 0.03%

資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年4月10日上午6:01(美東時間)

當比爾·艾克曼在社群媒體上為一場家族辦公室糾紛發洩情緒時,億萬富翁們紛紛趕來表示同情。Meta的社群媒體訴訟案可能拖累其股價的長期復甦,丹·加拉格(Dan Gallagher)寫道。

獨家搶先看

3

伊朗證明,發動經濟戰不需要成為超級大國。

德黑蘭對荷莫茲海峽的扼制,清楚展示了控制一條關鍵水道、一項技術甚至一家公司,能在一個高度互聯的全球經濟中賦予政府多大的影響力。在利用其海岸外這個經濟壓力點方面,伊朗延續了美國與中國多年來的做法——這兩國一直利用其在全球貿易關鍵領域的主導地位,來追求各自的外交政策目標。而伊朗絕非孤例。即便在伊朗封鎖海峽之前,包括美國盟友在內的各大經濟體,早已開始建立起對抗經濟壓力升級的威懾武器庫,記者傑森·道格拉斯(Jason Douglas)報導。

4

川普曾對中國強硬喊話。如今他態度和緩了。

儘管每一屆政府都會制定自己的國防戰略,川普的第二任政府正做出一項不尋常的舉動——拋棄由他第一任政府制定的對華政策。那套獲得川普1.0版兩黨支持的做法,將中國定性為美國最重大的對手。而2.0版的框架,則是美國對北京的政策、貿易做法及言論上的一次劇烈轉變,記者希瑟·索默維爾(Heather Somerville)、亞歷山大·沃德(Alexander Ward)與蓋文·貝德(Gavin Bade)報導。

我們的首席中國特派記者魏玲玲(Lingling Wei)解釋了中國如何透過投入伊朗外交,贏得川普的青睞。

5

問:如果油價已下跌,為什麼汽油還是這麼貴?

儘管中東地區已達成臨時停火,美國人仍面對一個嚴峻的新現實:4美元的汽油似乎將長期存在。記者大衛·烏貝爾蒂(David Uberti)解釋加油站接下來會發生什麼事。

答:即使川普為期兩週的停火得以維持,油價可能仍需一段時間才會回落。根據美國汽車協會(AAA)數據,從拉斯維加斯到西雅圖,司機們如今普遍要為一加侖汽油支付5美元,而舊金山和洛杉磯的價格經常超過6美元。

根據AAA追蹤的數據,週四美國平均油價達到每加侖4.17美元,這是自無人機與飛彈開始齊飛以來的最高水準。過去一個月,夏威夷、愛達荷州和猶他州的司機經歷了最大的油價漲幅。

在停火點燃了本週有史以來最劇烈的單日拋售之一後,近月美國原油期貨昨天反彈至接近每桶98美元。

實體原油運送的現貨價格則維持在更高水準,顯示煉油商正急於鎖定供應。根據Argus Media追蹤的數據,週三原油貨運的出價最高達到每桶145美元。

煉油商為原油運送所支付的價格越高,他們就得為燃油收取更高的費用,即便未來石油運送合約相對便宜也是如此。

分析師表示,如果海峽真的重新開放,美國平均油價每天可能下降幾美分。但加油站經營者的利潤會隨批發成本快速上漲而縮水,因此他們在出售這波衝擊後仍偏高的庫存時,通常會更緩慢地降價。

6

認識這些正在塑造小羅伯特·甘迺迪議程的「MAHA媽媽」。

像潔西卡·里德·克勞斯(Jessica Reed Kraus)這樣的MAHA(讓美國再次健康)網紅,幫助小羅伯特·甘迺迪在川普政府中謀得職位。本報造訪了克勞斯與她的MAHA朋友們一場無酒精雞尾酒之夜,談論投票、政策及甘迺迪的任期。觀看影片。

今日看點

7

《華爾街日報》現場問答:你想知道報導美國最昂貴房產是什麼感覺嗎?歡迎在美東時間上午11點,加入我們的豪宅地產記者凱瑟琳·克拉克(Katherine Clarke)與E.B.所羅門(E.B. Solomont)的問答場次。經濟數據:勞工統計局將於美東時間上午8:30發布消費者物價指數(CPI)通膨數據。

數字看新聞

8

59.50美元

一個花園小矮人擺飾的官方售價——這是奧古斯塔國家高爾夫俱樂部美國名人賽最搶手的紀念品。但人們往往願意在拍賣網站上支付數倍於此的價格。自2016年首次亮相以來,這款13英吋的小雕像已成為名人賽觀眾必收藏的物品。不過今年,粉絲們要弄到手的壓力更大了,因為現場傳言指出,這款小矮人即將「退休」。就連俱樂部主席本人似乎也無法確定它們的未來狀態。

最後,輕鬆一下

9

我們整理了本報讀者換購電動車的頂尖建議。

隨著高油價可能長期持續,許多美國人正重新考慮電動車。在專欄作家克里斯多福·米姆斯(Christopher Mims)撰文分享他的電動車公路旅行經驗與一年來的用車心得後,已有超過600位讀者回應我們的號召,提供給有意換車者的建議。點此閱讀他們的頂尖建議——從購買二手車到選購一台可靠的家用充電器。

新聞室之外

10

《華爾街日報》現場活動:4月28日,傑西卡·門多薩(Jessica Mendoza)與萊恩·努森(Ryan Knutson)——本報旗艦新聞播客主持人——將在洛杉磯舉辦一場活動,探討重塑好萊塢的商業力量。評論:川普政府正考慮將聯邦醫療保險受益人預設自動納入私人保險計畫——也就是聯邦醫療保險優惠計畫(Medicare Advantage)。這可能是減少聯邦醫療保險浪費、詐欺與濫用最有效的方式之一。那民主黨人為什麼反對?

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Traders Pounce on the Iran Cease-Fire
emails.contentEn:
✏️ The sudden U.S.-Iran cease-fire has left the world with more questions than answers. We’re working to make sense of it all. Our Middle East correspondent, David S. Cloud, explains how the delicate negotiations between Washington and Tehran could play out—and why Iran is already claiming victory.

On Wall Street, we are tracking the market’s reaction to the tentative truce and what the de-escalation means for soaring fuel costs and mortgage rates back home. You can follow our live coverage of the conflict here.

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

The cease-fire is welcome news for the U.S. economy—but don’t expect an immediate return to normal. The Trump administration plans to emphasize artificial intelligence’s economic benefits ahead of the midterms, but some allies warn of political blowback. Venezuela’s prisons are still full of military rebels despite a much-touted amnesty for prisoners that the government passed under American pressure. Delta’s ace in the hole for surging jet-fuel costs is its own refinery.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

Traders are pouncing on the cease-fire, even as missiles keep flying. Senior markets columnist James Mackintosh explored a lucrative (and not totally imaginary) business opportunity from Iran that is part of the 10-point peace plan. Here’s how BlackRock is weathering the private-credit storm better than its peers. A dealmaking gamble threatens Estée Lauder’s turnaround, writes Carol Ryan.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Trump allies and U.S. officials fear an Iran victory lap is premature.

Trump’s declaration of “total victory” in Iran left some close allies and several senior aides worried that he’s overstating what is a fragile cease-fire with Tehran, which remains capable of blocking ships in the Strait of Hormuz and attacking U.S. forces in the region. The president has been advised on the risks that could cause the cease-fire to crater and warned that Iran still retains dangerous military capabilities, according to multiple officials. So far, those warnings haven’t tempered the administration’s insistence that it has the upper hand ahead of talks, report Lara Seligman, Alexander Ward and Michael R. Gordon.

Here’s why Iran thinks it won the war despite huge military losses.

4

These small private colleges are dying in a winner-take-all university marketplace.

Consolidation of the nation’s nearly trillion-dollar higher-education sector is driving a new winner-take-all market, benefiting Ivy League campuses, flagship public universities and schools with high-profile sports teams and renowned research institutions. They enjoy high demand and a surplus of full-tuition payers, while lesser-known campuses juggle cost cuts and steep tuition discounts to fill seats. Shrinking enrollment at 442 private nonprofit colleges—out of 1,700 nationwide—is placing them at significant risk of closing or merging in the next decade, according to one forecast. St. Michael’s, one of the most well-respected institutions in northern New England, is among those struggling, reports Douglas Belkin.

Check out the future—today.

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: What is the framework for negotiations between the U.S. and Iran, and are the talks likely to bridge the gaps between the two sides?

Iran and the U.S. have a meeting tentatively scheduled for Saturday in Islamabad. Vice President JD Vance will lead the U.S. delegation. Pakistan, Egypt and Turkey have been mediating. WSJ’s Michael Amon and David S. Cloud explain what to expect from the talks:

A: Trump has said a 10-point Iranian plan would form the basis for the talks, though he has also said that Iran has already agreed to many elements of a separate 15-point U.S. plan that calls for sweeping concessions by Tehran.

Iran hasn’t released its proposal, but a 10-point plan published in state media included guarantees that the U.S. and Israel won’t attack, retaining control of the Strait of Hormuz, allowing Iran to enrich uranium, sanctions relief and the withdrawal of all U.S. combat forces from the Middle East.

Most of Iran’s demands have been called nonstarters for the U.S. and Israel. Iran has likewise called the U.S. plan, which calls for Iran to give up nuclear enrichment and accept limits on its missile arsenal, unacceptable.

The White House has said in recent days that talks on narrowing the gaps were making progress. It played down Trump’s comment that the 10-point Iranian plan would form the basis for the talks, saying Trump was speaking about a blueprint with different elements than those Iran has outlined publicly.

The differences between the Iranian and U.S. public positions are huge. For that reason, some analysts believe the likely outcome is a narrow agreement that halts the fighting but leaves many of the major issues unresolved.

6

A fuel man has turned a gas station outside Minneapolis into one of the hottest tables in town.

PHOTOS: ROBERT DAVIS

People cross city and state lines to wait a couple of hours for a drink at the Farmer’s Cellar. They order $18 mezcal cocktails infused with shiitake mushrooms, red onion and jalapeño herb oil. Between rounds, they might sample crispy pork belly or a $45 espresso-dusted ribeye. But what really separates the Lakeville, Minn., speakeasy from other hot spots is the location: inside an Amoco station.

HAPPENING TODAY

Weekly jobless claims are also expected. Earnings: BlackBerry, WD-40

The number of births per 1,000 women ages 15 to 44—the general fertility rate— in 2025, a record low, according to provisional data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The rate has mostly headed down since 2007, a prerecession peak when millennial women started to enter their prime childbearing years. One long-term trend driving the slide: a sharp decrease in birthrates for teens and women in their 20s.

AND FINALLY...

9

Can longtime car executive Luca De Meo kick the House of Gucci into gear?

Six months into Luca de Meo’s surprise appointment to lead the Kering conglomerate, which owns Pomellato, Gucci and nine other prestigious brands, the CEO is making bold moves. The rest of the luxury industry is watching closely.

✏️ 美伊突如其來的停火,讓世界的疑問多過答案。我們正努力釐清這一切。本報中東特派記者大衛·S·克勞德(David S. Cloud)解釋華盛頓與德黑蘭之間微妙的談判可能如何發展——以及為什麼伊朗已經在宣稱勝利。

在華爾街這邊,我們正追蹤市場對這項臨時停火的反應,以及這次降溫對飆升的燃油成本與國內房貸利率意味著什麼。你可以在此追蹤我們對這場衝突的即時報導。

今日頭條

1

停火對美國經濟而言是個好消息——但別指望立即恢復正常。川普政府計畫在期中選舉前強調人工智慧帶來的經濟效益,但一些盟友警告可能招致政治反彈。儘管政府在美方壓力下通過了一項備受宣傳的囚犯特赦令,委內瑞拉監獄中仍關滿了軍方叛亂份子。達美航空應對飆升航空燃油成本的王牌,是它自己的煉油廠。

市場即時動態

2

最新 漲跌 漲跌幅 道瓊期貨 47973.00 -171.00 0.36% 標普500期貨 6800.75 -23.00 0.34% 那斯達克100期貨 25008.50 -65.75 0.26%

儘管飛彈仍在飛,交易員仍搶進這波停火行情。資深市場專欄作家詹姆斯·麥金托什探討了一項來自伊朗、屬於「十點和平計畫」一部分、具獲利潛力(且並非完全虛構)的商機。這是貝萊德如何比同業更能安然度過這場私募信貸風暴。一場豪賭交易正威脅雅詩蘭黛的復甦計畫,卡蘿·萊恩(Carol Ryan)寫道。

獨家搶先看

3

川普的盟友與美國官員擔心,對伊朗的勝利宣言為時過早。

川普宣稱在伊朗取得「全面勝利」,讓一些親近的盟友與多位資深幕僚感到擔憂,認為他誇大了眼前這個脆弱的停火——德黑蘭仍有能力封鎖荷莫茲海峽的船隻,並攻擊該地區的美軍。多位官員表示,總統已獲得提醒,了解可能導致停火崩潰的風險,並被告知伊朗仍保有危險的軍事能力。到目前為止,這些警告並未動搖政府堅稱自己在談判前佔上風的立場,記者拉拉·塞利格曼(Lara Seligman)、亞歷山大·沃德(Alexander Ward)與麥可·R·戈登(Michael R. Gordon)報導。

儘管軍事損失慘重,這是為什麼伊朗仍認為自己贏得了這場戰爭。

4

在一個贏家通吃的大學市場中,這些小型私立學院正逐漸消亡。

美國這個規模近兆美元的高等教育產業正走向整合,形成一個贏家通吃的新市場,受益的是常春藤盟校、旗艦公立大學,以及擁有知名體育隊伍與享譽研究機構的學校。這些學校享有高需求,並擁有大量能全額支付學費的學生,而較不知名的學校則得在削減成本與大幅學費折扣之間掙扎,以填滿名額。全國1700所私立非營利大學中,有442所面臨招生萎縮,根據一項預測,這使它們在未來十年內面臨倒閉或合併的重大風險。聖麥可學院(St. Michael's)——新英格蘭北部最受尊敬的機構之一——正是掙扎中的其中一員,記者道格拉斯·貝爾金(Douglas Belkin)報導。

5

問:美伊談判的框架是什麼?談判是否有可能彌合雙方的分歧?

伊朗與美國暫定於週六在伊斯蘭馬巴德會面。副總統范斯將率領美方代表團。巴基斯坦、埃及與土耳其一直在居中調解。本報記者麥可·阿蒙(Michael Amon)與大衛·S·克勞德解釋這場談判可能出現的情況。

答:川普表示,一份十點式的伊朗方案將構成談判基礎,不過他也表示,伊朗已經同意另一份要求德黑蘭做出全面讓步的十五點美方方案中的許多內容。

伊朗尚未公布其提案,但國家媒體發布的一份十點方案內容包括:保證美國與以色列不會發動攻擊、保留對荷莫茲海峽的控制權、允許伊朗繼續濃縮鈾、解除制裁,以及美軍全部撤出中東地區。

伊朗的多數要求,已被美方與以方稱為不可能接受的條件。同樣地,伊朗也稱美方要求伊朗放棄濃縮鈾、並接受對其飛彈武器庫限制的方案「不可接受」。

白宮近日表示,縮小分歧的談判正取得進展。白宮淡化了川普關於「十點伊朗方案將構成談判基礎」的說法,表示川普談的是一份與伊朗公開提出的內容不同的藍圖。

伊朗與美國的公開立場之間存在巨大差異。因此,一些分析人士認為,最可能的結果是一份能止息戰火、但對許多重大問題仍懸而未決的有限協議。

6

一位燃料商,把明尼阿波利斯郊外一座加油站,變成了城裡最搶手的餐桌之一。

人們跨越城市與州界,只為在Farmer's Cellar排隊等上幾個小時。他們點著18美元、注入香菇、紅洋蔥與墨西哥辣椒草本油的梅斯卡爾酒(mezcal)雞尾酒。上菜之間,他們可能會嘗上一份酥脆豬五花,或是一份45美元、灑上濃縮咖啡粉的肋眼牛排。但真正讓這家位於明尼蘇達州萊克維爾(Lakeville)的私釀酒吧與其他熱門餐飲場所與眾不同的,是它的地點:就在一間Amoco加油站裡面。

今日看點

7

美國名人賽在奧古斯塔國家高爾夫俱樂部開賽,衛冕冠軍羅里·麥克羅伊預計於美東時間上午10:31開球。經濟數據:美國經濟分析局(BEA)將公布聯準會偏好的通膨指標——2月個人消費支出物價指數。每週申請失業救濟人數也將公布。財報:黑莓公司、WD-40。

數字看新聞

8

53.1

根據美國疾病管制與預防中心(CDC)的臨時數據,這是2025年15至44歲女性每千人的一般生育率——創下歷史新低。自2007年——千禧世代女性開始進入育齡高峰期前的一個經濟衰退前高點——以來,這項比率大致持續下滑。推動這波下滑的一個長期趨勢是:青少年及20多歲女性的生育率大幅下降。

最後,輕鬆一下

9

長年擔任汽車業高層的盧卡·德梅奧(Luca De Meo),能讓古馳家族(House of Gucci)重新啟動嗎?

在盧卡·德梅奧意外獲任開雲集團(Kering,旗下擁有Pomellato、Gucci及其他九個知名品牌)執行長六個月後,這位執行長正大膽出招。整個奢侈品產業都在密切關注。

新聞室之外

10

評論:川普達成了部分戰爭目標,但伊朗政權在荷莫茲海峽依然構成威脅,任務遠未如他上週所承諾的那樣完成。

✏️ Yesterday morning, President Trump issued the most dramatic ultimatum of his presidency: Unless Iran struck a deal in the next 12 hours, “a whole civilization will die tonight.” Less than 90 minutes before the deadline, he backed down, announcing a two-week cease-fire and suspending threatened strikes. While the president is optimistic, Washington and Tehran remain far from a durable agreement. Our reporters—from every corner of the globe—take you inside the frantic global guessing game over what the world’s most powerful man was prepared to do, and how a single post ricocheted from the Oval Office to foreign embassies and corporate suites.

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Iran said its fingers are “on the trigger” ahead of negotiations to end the war with the U.S. that are set to start Friday in Pakistan. Follow our live coverage. Artificial-intelligence companies are launching a charm offensive to soothe rising public anxiety about the negative potential effects of their world-changing technology. Nantucket homeowners spent millions trying to save bluff’s-edge properties. Their clash with other residents now includes alleged vandalism and a $10,000 reward. Ford has asked the Trump administration for relief as tariffs pummel the F-150 pickup. SpaceX isn’t even public yet and investors are already abuzz about a Tesla merger.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

McDonald’s CEO Chris Kempczinski is trying to redefine value at the same time as many Americans are worried about affordability, writes Tim Higgins. McCormick’s $65 billion deal with Unilever might actually work out, writes David Wainer. Here’s why.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

The day that Trump’s Iran threat gripped the world.

The president’s ultimatum lit up group chats across the globe and set off a scramble by U.S. allies and mediators to find an off-ramp or buy more time. Everyone from Republican allies to Pope Leo and actor Ben Stiller called on Trump to back down. Administration officials fielded phone calls from lawmakers and political allies trying to decipher whether Trump’s threat was a bluff or a prelude to an escalation. European officials huddled on a call and largely convinced themselves that Trump would back off. On Wall Street, traders and executives treated the day like other Trump deadlines that have come and gone: as a negotiating tactic they largely expected to pass without catastrophe.

4

Insurers’ $1 trillion buildup in private credit is leaving regulators in the dust.

The Treasury Department wants to talk to state insurance commissioners about the private loans piling up in insurers’ portfolios. In 2024, the National Association of Insurance Commissioners published a bombshell study revealing that the ratings on insurers’ private-credit investments were routinely inflated. The group has since pulled the report from its website. Its conclusions loom large now that many private-credit investors have grown concerned about the financial health of companies taking out private loans. Washington has heard those same alarm bells—and now, Treasury Department officials are planning to meet with state insurance regulators, reports Heather Gillers.

Follow the energy transition.

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: Why is the Iran war hitting California harder than any other state?

The U.S. West Coast is expected to be first to feel any spillover effects from the oil bottleneck in the Middle East, explains reporter Collin Eaton.

A: California imports roughly 75% of its crude oil and almost one-third of that comes from the Middle East. It also gets jet fuel and gasoline from countries whose refineries depend on the flow of oil from the Persian Gulf.

The Strait of Hormuz’s closure has dramatically slowed exports from South Korea and India—two of California’s biggest fuel suppliers—and threatening to squeeze the Golden State’s energy supplies.

The state’s coffers are sufficient to meet demand for refined products like jet fuel and gasoline in April, but a shortfall is likely to emerge over the following months, Andy Walz, who runs Chevron’s oil refining, pipeline and chemicals business, told me.

Although other states, including Illinois and New Jersey, also import a significant share of crude, they largely turn to Canada, Mexico and parts of South America and Africa for their supply.

6

Here’s a detailed look at America’s top innovations in aviation.

Innovation has been a defining feature in U.S. commercial aviation and government programs, helping them reach new heights. Entrepreneurs and the U.S. government have stoked a sprawling industry dedicated to getting humans off the ground. And despite numerous setbacks, including tragic accidents, the country has often been able to stay at the forefront of flight. We created a visual guide to some of the major aviation breakthroughs in American history.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Gen. Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, are set to hold a news conference at 8 a.m. ET. The Federal Reserve releases its latest minutes, which could offer clues to whether the central bank is likely to raise interest rates to tackle rising inflation. Earnings: Delta, Constellation Brands, RPM International 📰 Today’s paper

THE NUMBER

8

 61.9%

The share of the working-age population that is either working or looking for work—known as the labor-force participation rate—as of March, its lowest level since 1977, outside of the pandemic. An aging population and the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown have helped drive the fall in recent months, economists said. The rate matters because it helps set the pace of economic growth.

AND FINALLY...

9

We asked older male models to share their tips on life, style and aging.

Ralph Lauren has long used older models in campaigns, but it’s no longer a surprise to see brands like J.Crew and Todd Snyder casting gray-haired fellas in shoots next to men half their age. For the brands employing them, the fact that these men look their age, complete with lined faces and salt-and-pepper (or just pure salt) hair is the point. Their unique career paths have plenty to teach non-models of any age about personal style, self-confidence and how to age gracefully. Here’s what they’ve learned.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: What a spectacle: The U.S. vice president campaigning on behalf of a prime minister who may lose, in a small central European country, while America is prosecuting a war in Iran.

在週五於巴基斯坦即將展開的美伊結束戰爭談判前,伊朗表示其「手指已扣在扳機上」。持續關注我們的即時報導。人工智慧公司正發起一場公關攻勢,試圖平息大眾對這項可能改變世界的技術負面影響日益增長的焦慮。楠塔基特島(Nantucket)的屋主們花費數百萬美元,試圖搶救懸崖邊緣的房產。他們與其他居民之間的衝突,如今已包括涉嫌破壞行為與一筆1萬美元的懸賞。福特已向川普政府尋求關稅減免,因為關稅正衝擊F-150皮卡。SpaceX尚未上市,投資人已經在議論一樁與特斯拉合併的可能性。

麥當勞執行長克里斯·肯普欽斯基(Chris Kempczinski)正試圖重新定義「物有所值」,同時許多美國人正擔憂可負擔性問題,提姆·希金斯(Tim Higgins)寫道。麥考密克(McCormick)與聯合利華之間650億美元的交易可能真的行得通,大衛·懷納(David Wainer)寫道,原因如下。

獨家搶先看

3

川普的伊朗最後通牒震撼全球的那一天。

這位總統的最後通牒,點燃了全球各地的群組聊天,並促使美國盟友與調解人士競相尋找出路或爭取更多時間。從共和黨盟友到教宗良十四世,再到演員班·史提勒(Ben Stiller),各方人士都呼籲川普收回威脅。政府官員接到來自國會議員與政治盟友的電話,試圖判斷川普的威脅究竟是虛張聲勢,還是升級行動的前奏。歐洲官員召開電話會議,大致上說服了自己川普會退讓。在華爾街,交易員與高層將這一天視為川普過去諸多期限一樣的情況——一種預計不會釀成災難、只是談判策略的手法,並如往常般度過。

4

保險業者在私募信貸領域累積的1兆美元敞口,正讓監管機構措手不及。

財政部希望與各州保險監管官員討論保險公司投資組合中日益累積的私人貸款問題。2024年,全國保險監理官協會(NAIC)發表了一項震撼性研究,揭露保險公司私募信貸投資的評等經常被高估。該協會此後已將該報告從其網站上撤下。如今,隨著許多私募信貸投資人對接受私人貸款的公司財務健全性日益擔憂,這項研究的結論顯得格外重要。華盛頓也已聽到同樣的警訊——如今,財政部官員正計劃與各州保險監管機構會面,記者希瑟·吉勒斯(Heather Gillers)報導。

5

問:為什麼伊朗戰爭對加州的衝擊比其他任何一州都大?

美國西岸預計將是最先感受到中東石油瓶頸溢出效應的地區,記者科林·伊頓(Collin Eaton)解釋。

答:加州約75%的原油依賴進口,其中近三分之一來自中東。它也從煉油廠依賴波斯灣石油流通的國家進口航空燃油與汽油。

荷莫茲海峽的封閉,已大幅減緩了來自南韓與印度——加州兩大燃油供應國——的出口,並威脅到這個「黃金之州」的能源供應。

雪佛龍煉油、管線及化工業務負責人安迪·瓦爾茲(Andy Walz)告訴我,該州目前的儲備足以應付4月的航空燃油與汽油等精煉產品需求,但短缺很可能會在接下來幾個月內浮現。

儘管其他州(包括伊利諾州與紐澤西州)也進口大量原油,它們主要向加拿大、墨西哥及南美與非洲部分地區採購供應。

6

深入了解美國航空業的頂尖創新。

創新一直是美國商業航空與政府計畫的一項標誌性特色,推動它們不斷邁向新高度。企業家與美國政府一直支持著一個致力於讓人類飛上天空的龐大產業。儘管歷經多次挫折,包括悲劇性的事故,這個國家仍能持續站在飛行領域的最前沿。我們製作了一份視覺化指南,介紹美國航空史上一些重大的突破。

今日看點

7

國防部長佩特·海格塞斯與參謀首長聯席會議主席丹·凱恩將軍,預計於美東時間上午8點舉行記者會。聯準會將公布最新會議記錄,這可能提供線索,顯示央行是否可能升息以應對通膨上升。財報:達美航空、星座品牌(Constellation Brands)、RPM國際。

數字看新聞

8

61.9%

截至3月,適齡工作人口中正在工作或正在找工作的比例——即勞動參與率——為此水準,創下1977年以來(不計疫情期間)的最低紀錄。經濟學家表示,人口老化與川普政府的移民打壓行動,是推動近幾個月這項比率下滑的因素。這項比率之所以重要,是因為它有助於決定經濟成長的步調。

最後,輕鬆一下

9

我們詢問了年長男模特兒關於人生、風格與老化的心得。

拉夫勞倫長期以來一直在廣告中起用年長模特兒,但如今看到J.Crew和Todd Snyder等品牌,在拍攝中啟用滿頭白髮的男士,與年紀只有他們一半的男性同台演出,已不再令人驚訝。對雇用他們的品牌而言,重點正在於這些男士看起來符合自己的年齡——包括臉上的皺紋以及椒鹽(或者說純鹽)色的頭髮。他們獨特的職涯路徑,對任何年齡層的非模特兒而言,都能在個人風格、自信,以及如何優雅老去方面帶來許多啟發。以下是他們學到的心得。

新聞室之外

10

評論:多麼令人嘆為觀止的場景:美國副總統正在一個可能落敗的總理背後站台助選,地點是一個中歐小國,而與此同時,美國正在伊朗打一場戰爭。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: How China Is Helping Iran Fund Its War Machine
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Good morning. I’ve just returned from a two-week trip across Asia, where I visited the Journal’s bureaus in Korea, Japan and China. What struck me most in my conversations with our reporters was how the escalating conflict in the Middle East is rippling across the Pacific—something I discussed with our Japan bureau chief, Jason Douglas. You can watch our full exchange here.

On another note entirely: Next Monday, I’ll be joining Harvard University President Dr. Alan Garber at the 92nd Street Y in New York for a conversation on the future of higher education. Have a question for him? Share it by replying to this email.

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Negotiators are pessimistic Iran will bend to meet President Trump’s demand to reopen the Strait of Hormuz before his deadline tonight. Meanwhile, Iran rejected a cease-fire proposal. Click here for our live coverage. Bill Ackman’s Pershing Square Capital said it had made an offer to buy Universal Music Group. The Iran war has placed America’s friends in Europe, Asia and the Middle East in front of an uneasy dilemma. China has helped Iran cushion the blow of sanctions and fund its war machine. Here’s how. Iranians who have weathered more than a month of war are bracing for things to get worse if Trump acts on his threat to escalate attacks on civilian infrastructure. Kanye West is seeking redemption. There’s a long road ahead.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2
