Source: Factset, Market data as of 4/7/2026, 6:00:15 AM ET

American gas exporter Venture Global is set to benefit from the tightening global natural-gas market. Energy stocks are having a moment that could last, writes Jinjoo Lee.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

This prosecutor was floundering. Now he’s a go-to guy at Trump’s DOJ.

Under recently ousted attorney general Pam Bondi, the Justice Department transformed into an agency dedicated to the president’s agenda, including the prosecution of his perceived enemies. Trump bounced Bondi last week partly because she wasn’t effective enough in those pursuits. The agency’s shift away from prosecutorial independence has driven resignations and retirements in numbers not seen in modern times. While many veteran attorneys were troubled with the agency’s political turn, a smaller group has embraced it—and been rewarded with more power and responsibility. Justice Department attorney Robert Keenan embodies this trend, reports Joe Palazzolo.

4

These workers are opting to retire instead of taking on artificial intelligence.

The share of Americans over 55 years old and in the workforce has slipped to 37.2%, the lowest level in more than 20 years, after rising for decades. The financial cushion of rising home equity and stock-market returns is driving some of the decline, economists and retirement advisers say. But for some older professionals, money is only part of the equation. They say they don’t want to spend the last years of their career going through the tumult of AI adoption, which has brought new tools, new expectations and a lot of uncertainty, report Lauren Weber and Ray A. Smith.

Go inside what’s driving D.C.

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: What are donor-advised funds, and how are some using them to help lower their tax bills?

Wealthy Americans are buzzing about the funds, which are allowing those giving to charity to get ahead of tax-law changes, explains reporter Miriam Gottfried.

A: A donor-advised fund can be used for planned charitable gifts. Wealthy people have been flocking to them partly to stockpile tax deductions. Many were aiming to get ahead of new rules in last summer’s tax law that limit tax breaks on charitable giving for high earners and those who itemize deductions.

Funding a new DAF with highly appreciated shares of stock allows the donor to avoid capital-gains taxes while also taking a tax deduction. The deduction occurs when they transfer assets to a DAF. The money can be invested within the DAF tax-free and doled out to charity years into the future.

Starting this year, charitable donations below 0.5% of adjusted gross income won’t be deductible.

Even those who missed the boat on opening a DAF last year might find it useful for bunching deductions into one tax year. That would make it easier to clear the new 0.5% floor in 2026 and onward, advisers say. A DAF can make sense for people who aren’t ultrawealthy if they plan to give to charity and itemize deductions.

6

These cities and states are taking aim at data centers.

Maine looks poised to become the first state to freeze building of new data centers with legislation that could pass this spring, but community backlash against these properties is spreading across the country. Lawmakers in more than 10 states have proposed temporary bans on data-center construction this year. Dozens of county and city governments have already passed such measures.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

Trump’s deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is at 8 p.m. ET. Economic data: The Census Bureau will release its report on durable-goods orders for February. Earnings: Levi Strauss 

THE NUMBER

8

 97%

The discount one buyer in Denver scored on a two-building office complex. Developer Asher Luzzatto paid a mere $5.3 million for the Denver Energy Center, which sold for $176 million in 2013. America’s battered office market is holding a fire sale. After years of holding out for a turnaround, landlords and lenders are finally capitulating and accepting enormous losses.

AND FINALLY...

9

Accountants desperately wish AI would take over this dirty job.

Accounting firms and their clients are increasingly using AI and drones to do work long handled by humans. But so far, there’s been no technological solution to what is often the dirtiest part of an audit: counting inventory. That means the messy, bizarre field trips remain a rite of passage for young professionals in an otherwise deskbound field. It also means April actually isn’t the worst time of the year for some accountants.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Taken literally, Trump is proposing to hit many targets that would harm Iranian civilians. Striking indiscriminately at critical infrastructure would be wrong as well as unwise, punishing the Iranian people we need on our side.
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 早安。我剛結束一趟橫跨亞洲兩週的行程,拜訪了本報在韓國、日本與中國的分社。在與記者們的對話中,最令我印象深刻的,是中東不斷升級的衝突如何在太平洋彼岸激起漣漪——這也是我與本報日本分社社長傑森·道格拉斯(Jason Douglas)討論的話題。你可以在此觀看我們完整的對談內容。

另外一則消息:下週一,我將與哈佛大學校長艾倫·加伯博士,在紐約92街Y中心一同對談高等教育的未來。對他有問題嗎?歡迎回覆這封郵件與我們分享。

今日頭條

1

談判代表對伊朗是否會在今晚川普總統設定的期限前,同意重新開放荷莫茲海峽,持悲觀態度。與此同時,伊朗拒絕了一項停火提議。點此觀看我們的即時報導。比爾·艾克曼旗下的Pershing Square Capital表示已出價收購環球音樂集團。伊朗戰爭讓美國在歐洲、亞洲及中東的盟友,面臨一個棘手的兩難局面。中國一直在幫助伊朗緩解制裁衝擊,並資助其戰爭機器。原因如下。經歷了一個多月戰爭考驗的伊朗人,正為川普若真的兌現升級攻擊民用基礎設施的威脅、情勢進一步惡化做好準備。肯伊·威斯特(Kanye West)正尋求救贖。前方的路還很長。

市場即時動態

2

最新 漲跌 漲跌幅 道瓊期貨 46991.00 89.00 0.19% 標普500期貨 6660.00 9.00 0.14% 那斯達克100期貨 24383.00 24.50 0.10%

資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年4月7日上午6:00(美東時間)

美國天然氣出口商Venture Global,有望受益於日益緊縮的全球天然氣市場。能源類股正迎來一波可能持續下去的漲勢,金珠·李(Jinjoo Lee)寫道。

獨家搶先看

3

這位檢察官原本前途黯淡。如今他成了川普司法部的紅人。

在近期遭撤換的司法部長潘·邦迪(Pam Bondi)任內,司法部已轉型為一個致力於推動總統議程(包括起訴他所認定的政敵)的機構。川普上週撤換邦迪,部分原因是她在這些行動上不夠得力。該機構從檢察獨立性的轉向,已引發近代前所未見規模的離職與退休潮。儘管許多資深律師對該機構的政治轉向感到不安,一小部分人卻擁抱了這股趨勢——並因此獲得更多權力與職責。司法部律師羅伯特·基南(Robert Keenan)正是這股趨勢的體現,記者喬·帕拉佐洛(Joe Palazzolo)報導。

4

這些勞工選擇退休,而非面對人工智慧的挑戰。

55歲以上仍在職的美國人比例,已下滑至37.2%,這是二十多年來的最低水準——此前這項比例已上升了數十年。經濟學家與退休規劃顧問表示,不斷上升的房屋淨值與股市回報所帶來的財務緩衝,是推動這項下滑的部分原因。但對某些年長專業人士而言,金錢只是考量因素之一。他們表示,他們不想在職業生涯的最後幾年,經歷AI採用帶來的動盪——這帶來了新工具、新期待,以及大量的不確定性,記者勞倫·韋伯(Lauren Weber)與雷·A·史密斯(Ray A. Smith)報導。

5

問:什麼是「捐贈者建議基金」(donor-advised funds),有些人如何利用它們來降低稅負?

富裕的美國人正熱議這類基金,它能讓慈善捐贈者搶先因應稅法變動,記者米瑞安·戈特弗里德(Miriam Gottfried)解釋。

答:捐贈者建議基金可用於規劃中的慈善捐贈。富人紛紛湧向這類基金,部分原因是想藉此累積稅務扣除額。許多人的目標,是搶在去年夏天稅法新規定生效之前行動——該規定限制了高收入者及採用逐項扣除者的慈善捐款稅務優惠。

以大幅增值的股票資助一個新的捐贈者建議基金,能讓捐贈者避免資本利得稅,同時仍可獲得稅務扣除額。扣除額是在資產轉入該基金時發生的。這筆資金可以在基金內免稅投資,並在未來數年內分批捐給慈善機構。

從今年開始,低於調整後總收入0.5%的慈善捐款將不再可扣除。

即便是去年錯過設立捐贈者建議基金的人,也可能發現它有助於將扣除額集中在一個報稅年度內。顧問表示,這能讓人更容易在2026年及以後跨過新的0.5%門檻。對於並非極度富裕、但計劃捐贈慈善並採用逐項扣除的人來說,捐贈者建議基金也可能是合理的選擇。

6

這些城市與州正把矛頭指向數據中心。

緬因州看起來有望成為第一個透過今年春天可能通過的立法,凍結新數據中心建設的州,但針對這類設施的社區反彈情緒,正蔓延至全美各地。超過10個州的議員已提出今年暫停數據中心建設的法案。數十個郡與市政府已經通過了此類措施。

今日看點

7

川普要求伊朗重新開放荷莫茲海峽的期限,是美東時間晚上8點。經濟數據:美國普查局將公布2月耐久財訂單報告。財報:Levi Strauss。

數字看新聞

8

97%

一位丹佛買家所獲得的折扣,他購入一座兩棟建築的辦公綜合體。開發商亞瑟·盧扎托(Asher Luzzatto)僅花費530萬美元,買下丹佛能源中心(Denver Energy Center)——這座建築2013年的售價曾高達1.76億美元。美國飽受重創的辦公樓市場正在拋售求現。歷經多年苦等市況好轉後,房東與放款機構終於開始讓步,接受巨額虧損。

最後,輕鬆一下

9

會計師迫切希望AI能接管這項苦差事。

會計師事務所及其客戶正越來越多使用AI與無人機,來執行過去長期由人力完成的工作。但到目前為止,尚未有任何技術解決方案,能取代審計工作中最骯髒的一部分:盤點存貨。這意味著這些混亂、古怪的實地考察,仍是這個原本以坐辦公桌為主的行業中,新進人員的必經之路。這也意味著,對某些會計師來說,4月其實還不是一年中最難熬的時候。

新聞室之外

10

評論:若照字面解讀,川普正提議打擊多個會傷及伊朗平民的目標。不分青紅皂白地打擊關鍵基礎設施,既不明智,也是錯誤之舉,只會傷害我們需要爭取到我們這邊的伊朗人民。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: How the U.S. Pulled Off a Risky Rescue in Iran
emails.contentEn:
✏️ For nearly two days, injured and alone, a U.S. aviator hid in a remote mountain crevice as Iranian forces and militias closed in on him with helicopters and drones. The U.S. responded with a high-stakes rescue mission into enemy territory. The operation was the kind military commanders both plan for and dread: a downed American airman in enemy territory, hostile forces converging and early recovery attempts faltering under fire.The sprawling effort to rescue the officer involved some 100 special operations forces, dozens of warplanes and helicopters, and a last-minute CIA deception campaign to buy more time.

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

The next target for the U.S. and Israel is Iran’s economy. Follow live coverage of the conflict. The oil shock set off by the war in Iran is already rippling through Asia—and foreshadows tough times for Europe. OpenAI and Anthropic are racing toward potentially record-breaking IPOs by the end of the year. An inside look at their financials prior to funding rounds completed earlier this year shows their Achilles’ heel. A fight over feta is straining America’s ties with Europe.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 46779.00 47.00 0.10 S&P 500 Futures 6644.50 22.25 0.34 Nasdaq 100 Futures 24373.25 155.25 0.64

Source: Factset, Market data as of 4/6/2026, 5:58:41 AM ET

Paramount is in talks to secure signed equity commitments of close to $24 billion from three sovereign-wealth funds led by Saudi Arabia to help back its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery. Don’t toss junk bonds out with private-credit debt, writes Telis Demos. Fears over corporate debt are rising, but high-yield bonds should prove resilient.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

We spent a day listening to voices from the nation’s economic front line—the gas pump.

At a busy intersection near highway 190, the Food N’ Geaux gas station sits at an economic crossroads: where Americans’ patience and resilience is tested every time they fill up. On Thursday, the price for a gallon of regular gas with a credit card was $3.84 at Food N’ Geaux. Nationally, the average price of gas hit $4.11. At the pumps, the mood was tense as customers watched the fuel counter tick up, sometimes pulling out the nozzle before the satisfying “ca-chunk” that indicates a full tank, report Rachel Wolfe and Dave Cole. Here’s what they told us.

4

Saudi Arabia’s grand vision is slamming into financial reality—and the Iran war.

Vast development sites around Riyadh trumpet images of a shiny new future for the country—part of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s grandiose Vision 2030 agenda to become an international hub of trade, technology and culture. Yet those plans are slamming into reality. Over the past year, the world’s largest oil exporter began pulling back on many of its promised projects and investments, met with budget shortfalls and unrealistic designs. And now the war with Iran has plunged the vision deeper into jeopardy—it has already cost Saudi Arabia more than $10 billion in lost revenues and expenses, report Stephen Kalin, Eliot Brown and Summer Said.

Get set for the trading day ahead.

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: How are elite American forces trained to survive behind enemy lines?

Air Force crews learn to eat bugs, treat their wounds and evade capture before ever flying a mission, explains reporter James T. Areddy.

A: Elite U.S. military aviators and special forces undergo intense training for the prospect they are trapped behind enemy lines—like the F-15 crew member rescued in Iran.

The training is called SERE, which stands for “survival, evasion, resistance and escape.” According to an Air Force recruitment video: “The survivor’s mission is to return, with honor.”

The SERE instruction is taught in many ways across the U.S. military but is a particular focus for the Air Force. The first order of business is to survive, which includes prioritizing needs to minimize stress and calorie burn.

SERE training introduces pilots into hostile environments, from deserts to the Arctic, according to an Air Force video. It shows trainees plunged into water and landing with parachutes. They get drinking water from a river, start fires and build shelters, as well as prepare meals of cactus and beetles.

Each mission plan includes contingencies for a rescue that are agreed in advance of a flight by the aviator and home base, so the pilot is both evading the enemy and executing an exit strategy.

If a downed aviator is spotted by the enemy, the SERE training calls for resistance. But what that exactly means isn’t public information.

6

Here’s why the U.S. spends so much on healthcare.

Note: Median claims paid by private insurers as of 2022 in U.S. dollars. Peer nation is the median of the 8 other nations in the dataset. Sources: International Federation of Health Plans; Health Care Cost Institute

Americans spend more on healthcare than anyone else in the world. Just insuring a family costs nearly $27,000 a year, enough to buy a car. The main cause: Prices are far higher in the U.S. than in other nations for the same medical products and services, from surgeries to drugs. American patients have also been using more care recently, including costly hospital treatment and expensive new drugs for weight loss, pushing up spending. Here are some of the factors that make U.S. healthcare so expensive.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

President Trump is set to hold a press conference with the military at 1 p.m. ET. The championship round of the men’s March Madness tournament pits the University of Connecticut against the University of Michigan. 📰 Today’s paper

THE NUMBER

8

 $650 million

How much the Kansas City metro area has poured into building world-class training facilities and stadiums over the past 15 years in an effort to become America’s soccer capital. Starting in June, Kansas City will host six matches for the World Cup. The Missouri city is preparing for its moment on the global stage during the tournament, when it is expecting visitors to outnumber its residents.

AND FINALLY...

9

Kids are discovering the joys—and pains—of the landline.

Families are combating screen time with a blast from the past: home phones. The transition hasn’t always been smooth, bringing confusion over dial tones and the mechanics of voice conversations versus texting. Yet kids are also rediscovering time-honored traditions: recording an outgoing voicemail message, prank calling and fighting with a sibling over who gets to use it.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

✏️ 近兩天內,一名美軍飛行員一邊受傷、一邊孤身一人,躲藏在一處偏遠的山崖裂縫中,伊朗軍隊與民兵則出動直升機與無人機步步逼近。美國隨即展開一場高風險的救援行動,深入敵方領土。這場行動正是軍事指揮官既會為之規劃、也最為忌憚的情況:一名美軍飛行員被困敵境,敵對勢力步步進逼,而早期的救援嘗試又在炮火下受挫。這場動員近百名特種作戰部隊、數十架戰機與直升機,並最後靠中央情報局一場欺敵行動爭取時間的龐大營救行動,終於成功救出這名軍官。

今日頭條

1

美國與以色列的下一個目標,是伊朗的經濟。持續關注我們對這場衝突的即時報導。伊朗戰爭引發的石油衝擊,已在亞洲激起漣漪——並預示著歐洲即將面臨艱難時期。OpenAI與Anthropic正朝著可能創紀錄的首次公開發行(IPO)邁進,有望在今年底前完成。對它們在今年稍早完成的募資輪之前財務狀況的深入了解,揭露了它們的軟肋。一場關於菲達起司(feta)的爭端,正讓美國與歐洲的關係緊繃。

市場即時動態

2

最新 漲跌 漲跌幅 道瓊期貨 46779.00 47.00 0.10% 標普500期貨 6644.50 22.25 0.34% 那斯達克100期貨 24373.25 155.25 0.64%

資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年4月6日上午5:58(美東時間)

派拉蒙正洽談從以沙烏地阿拉伯為首的三個主權財富基金那裡,取得近240億美元的股權承諾,以支持其收購華納兄弟探索頻道(Warner Bros. Discovery)。別把垃圾債券和私募信貸債務混為一談,泰利斯·德莫斯(Telis Demos)寫道。對企業債務的擔憂正在升溫,但高收益債券應能證明自己具有韌性。

獨家搶先看

3

我們花了一整天,傾聽來自這個國家經濟前線——加油站——的聲音。

在190號公路附近一個繁忙路口,Food N' Geaux加油站正處於一個經濟十字路口:美國人的耐心與韌性,每次加油都要接受一次考驗。週四,Food N' Geaux使用信用卡支付、一加侖普通汽油的價格是3.84美元。全國平均油價則達到4.11美元。在加油站,隨著顧客盯著油量表不斷攀升,情緒相當緊繃,有些人甚至在聽到那聲代表油箱加滿的滿意「喀嚓」聲之前,就先拔出油槍,記者瑞秋·沃爾夫(Rachel Wolfe)與戴夫·科爾(Dave Cole)報導。以下是他們告訴我們的內容。

4

沙烏地阿拉伯的宏大願景,正撞上財務現實——以及伊朗戰爭。

利雅德周邊龐大的開發用地上,矗立著宣傳這個國家嶄新未來的宣傳圖像——這是王儲穆罕默德·本·薩爾曼(Mohammed bin Salman)宏大的「2030願景」議程的一部分,旨在讓沙國成為貿易、科技與文化的國際樞紐。然而這些計畫正撞上現實。過去一年,這個全球最大石油出口國,已開始收回許多曾承諾的項目與投資,面臨預算短缺以及不切實際的設計問題。如今,與伊朗的戰爭讓這個願景陷入更深的危機——這場戰爭已讓沙烏地阿拉伯損失超過100億美元的收入與支出,記者史蒂芬·卡林(Stephen Kalin)、埃利奧特·布朗(Eliot Brown)與薩默·賽義德(Summer Said)報導。

5

問:美國菁英部隊如何受訓,以在敵後求生?

空軍機組人員在執行任務前,要學會吃蟲子、治療傷口,以及躲避俘虜,記者詹姆斯·T·阿雷迪(James T. Areddy)解釋。

答:美國菁英軍事飛行員與特種部隊,都要接受高強度訓練,以應對受困敵後的情況——就像這位在伊朗獲救的F-15機組人員一樣。

這種訓練稱為SERE,即「生存、逃避、抵抗與逃脫」(survival, evasion, resistance and escape)。根據一支空軍招募影片:「倖存者的任務,是光榮歸來。」

SERE訓練在美軍中以多種形式教授,但空軍尤其重視。首要任務是生存,其中包括優先處理各項需求,以將壓力和熱量消耗降到最低。

根據一支空軍影片,SERE訓練會將飛行員置身於從沙漠到北極的各種敵對環境中。影片顯示受訓者被投入水中,並以降落傘著陸。他們要從河裡取得飲用水、生火、搭建庇護所,還要準備仙人掌與甲蟲做成的餐點。

每項任務計畫,都包含飛行員與基地事先商定好的救援應變方案,因此飛行員既要躲避敵人,也要執行撤離計畫。

如果一名被擊落的飛行員被敵方發現,SERE訓練要求進行「抵抗」。但這具體代表什麼,並未對外公開。

6

這裡告訴你,美國為什麼在醫療保健上花這麼多錢。

註:私人保險公司支付理賠金額中位數,截至2022年,以美元計。「同儕國家」是數據集中其他8個國家的中位數。資料來源:國際健康計畫聯盟(International Federation of Health Plans);醫療保健成本研究所(Health Care Cost Institute)。

美國人在醫療保健上的花費,超過世界上任何其他國家。光是為一個家庭投保,每年就要花費近2.7萬美元,足以買一輛車。主要原因是:從手術到藥物,美國同類醫療產品與服務的價格,遠高於其他國家。美國病患近來也使用了更多醫療服務,包括昂貴的住院治療,以及用於減重的昂貴新藥,這些都推升了支出。以下是讓美國醫療保健如此昂貴的一些因素。

今日看點

7

川普總統預計於美東時間下午1點與軍方一同召開記者會。男子NCAA籃球錦標賽「瘋狂三月」冠軍賽,將由康乃狄克大學對戰密西根大學。

數字看新聞

8

6.5億美元

過去15年間,堪薩斯城都會區為打造世界級訓練設施與體育場館所投入的資金,目的是成為美國的「足球之都」。從6月開始,堪薩斯城將主辦六場世界盃比賽。這座密蘇里州城市正為登上世界舞台的時刻做準備,屆時預計訪客人數將超過當地居民人數。

最後,輕鬆一下

9

孩子們正發現家用電話的樂趣——以及痛苦。

家庭正用一項來自過去的產物——家用電話——來對抗螢幕使用時間過長的問題。這項轉變並非總是一帆風順,撥號音的困惑以及語音通話與傳簡訊之間操作方式的差異,都讓孩子們摸不著頭緒。然而孩子們也在重新發現一些歷久彌新的傳統:錄製語音信箱的問候語、惡作劇電話,以及為了誰能使用電話而與手足爭吵。

新聞室之外

emails.contentEn:
Last year, the Journal’s Valerie Bauerlein unspooled the story of Scott Spivey’s death, a shooting that might have gone unnoticed, if not for one man’s decision to record all of his phone calls, a police coverup and a grieving sister’s quest to find the truth. After the WSJ series was published, a judge ruled that the shooters can’t claim “stand your ground” protection, setting up a review of the original investigation. Now, in the latest twist in the story, testimony from the crime-scene investigator raises new questions about what was going on behind the scenes.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. U.S. forces rescued the remaining crew member of a downed combat jet in Iran, capping one of their most complex search-and-rescue efforts in decades. Follow our live coverage. Trump’s repeated declarations that the war is nearly over are colliding with the gritty battlefield reality. John Robinson Block and Allan Block, the twin heirs to the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette and Toledo Blade, are estranged after years of trying to guide their empire through changes in the media industry. More aspiring young lawyers are asking for—and getting—extra time to finish the bar exam, according to a WSJ analysis.

FROM THE MARKETS

2. Value stocks, one of the market’s last havens, are now at risk.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. This CSI detective smelled trouble in her own police department. Crime-scene investigator Shellneil Tamasi arrived on the scene about an hour after the shootout that killed Scott Spivey. She saw trouble right away, reports Valerie Bauerlein. The two suspected killers sat together fiddling with their phones. In any other homicide investigation, they would have been separated, with their phones taken away. But this investigation was unlike any Tamasi had seen in 19 years in law enforcement. After a WSJ series last year revealed police overlooked evidence that raised questions about the officers’ self-defense claim, a state grand jury is currently reviewing evidence of alleged misconduct. Tamasi’s sworn account raises more questions about the deputy police chief’s behind-the-scenes influence.

4. Aboard ships stranded near the Strait of Hormuz, it’s life and death. There are roughly 2,000 ships stuck in the Persian Gulf with more than 20,000 seafarers on them, according to the International Maritime Organization. Most have been stuck on board more than a month. Now, fresh vegetables and freshwater are running out on many ships, and sailors are using social media and marine radios to share survival tips and tactics, reports Rebecca Feng. Some Chinese crew members have filmed themselves collecting condensate from air-conditioning units to shower and wash laundry. Others have taken to fishing over the side of their tankers, catching tuna, squid and largehead hairtail to cook.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: Will the oil shock push central banks to raise interest rates? As war on Iran leads to higher inflation, some investors are betting that central banks will tighten policy. Columnist James Mackintosh wrote about why he thinks they’re wrong. A: Central banks live in fear of their last mistake. As the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran leads to higher inflation, investors are betting policymakers will do what they should have done in 2021: raise rates or at the least drop planned cuts. But there’s a fundamental difference between the new oil shock and the postpandemic boom. Inflation today is driven by restricted supply as Iran cuts off oil and other shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The 2021-22 inflation was driven by soaring demand as stimulus-rich consumers emerged from enforced hibernation during lockdowns. Central banks know how to deal with too much demand. They should have raised rates much earlier than their eventual 2022 rises to hold back borrowing and spending. Today, they can’t do anything about the hit to supply, because, as the saying goes, you can’t print oil. Yet traders are pricing in almost three quarter-point rate rises by the European Central Bank this year. In the U.S. they expect rates to be flat, rather than the three cuts by the Fed previously priced in. And the Bank of England is priced for four more rises than just before the war. To me this makes no sense, for three reasons: history, the hit to the economy from expensive oil and the bigger threat posed to Europe than the U.S.

6. More Americans are breaking into the upper middle class. Research by the right-leaning American Enterprise Institute shows that the ranks of the affluent have grown markedly over the last 50 years or so, while the lower rungs of the middle class have shrunk. The rise in affluence is powering a U.S. economy built on consumer spending, and transforming the types of products and services companies offer. These tend to be the people buying $1,700 bassinets for their babies, artisanal food for their dogs, pricey gym memberships, luxury cruises and spots in business-class airplane cabins.

HAPPENING THIS WEEK

7. Monday: The championship round of the men’s March Madness tournament pits the University of Connecticut against the University of Michigan. The crew of Artemis II is expected to take photos while the Orion craft flies past the Moon. Wednesday: The Federal Reserve releases its latest minutes, which could offer clues as to whether the central bank is likely to raise interest rates to tackle rising inflation. Friday: Consumer-price index data for March will give investors information about how high energy costs are lifting prices more broadly.

THE NUMBER

8. 44 years — The age of the median American home, a record number, according to the Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies. More recent new construction hasn’t replaced America’s graying housing stock, and the cost of maintaining and modernizing these homes is going up fast.

AND FINALLY...

9. A Texas Congressional race has become all about…quinceañeras. Bobby Pulido is an award-winning Tejano singer vying to represent Texas’ 15th district. After his opponent suggested he was better suited to entertain at parties than serve in Congress, the Democrat began doing exactly that, crisscrossing the state to perform at the traditional Hispanic celebrations of a girl’s 15th birthday. “In South Texas, a quinceañera isn’t just a pachanga. It’s a rite of passage that brings family and neighbors together. And honestly that’s exactly what this campaign is about,” Pulido said in a video.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. MarketWatch's Don't Short Yourself: Join us for a live talk and Q&A on April 8 on AI trends shaping markets and what they mean for your next investment move.

WSJ | Buy Side: Premium build quality and audio make the Sonos Play speaker worth considering, even if you’re not already in the Sonos ecosystem.
emails.contentZh:
去年，本報記者瓦萊麗·鮑爾萊恩揭露了斯科特·斯皮維之死的故事——一起本可能無人問津的槍擊案，若非一名男子決定將自己所有的電話通話全程錄音、加上一起警方掩蓋真相的行徑，以及一位悲痛姐姐鍥而不捨追尋真相的努力，真相恐將永遠石沉大海。這篇系列報導刊出後，一名法官裁定，槍手不得援引「持槍自衛」（stand your ground）條款作為保護傘，為重新審視原始調查鋪平了道路。如今，這起案件迎來最新的轉折：犯罪現場調查員的證詞，讓外界對幕後究竟發生了什麼，產生了更多疑問。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 美軍已救出一架在伊朗上空被擊落的戰機中，最後一名尚未尋獲的機組人員，這也是數十年來難度最高的搜救行動之一。請關注本報即時報導。川普一再宣稱戰爭即將結束，卻與嚴峻的戰場現實相互衝突。約翰·羅賓森·布拉克與艾倫·布拉克，這對雙胞胎兄弟——分別是《匹茲堡郵報》與《托萊多刀鋒報》的繼承人——在多年試圖帶領家族媒體帝國度過產業變革之後，如今卻已形同陌路。據本報一項分析顯示，越來越多有志成為律師的年輕人，正要求——並且成功獲得——更長時間來完成律師資格考試。

市場動態

2. 價值型股票——市場上僅存的少數避風港之一——如今也面臨風險。

搶先讀

3. 這位犯罪現場調查員，在自己所屬的警局裡嗅到了不對勁的氣息。犯罪現場調查員雪妮爾·塔馬西，在斯科特·斯皮維遭槍殺的槍戰事發約一小時後抵達現場。瓦萊麗·鮑爾萊恩報導指出，她當下便立刻察覺情況不對：兩名嫌疑槍手當時竟坐在一起，各自擺弄著手機。換作任何其他命案調查，他們早該被分開偵訊，手機也早該被沒收。但這起案件的調查方式，與塔馬西19年執法生涯中所見過的任何案件都截然不同。去年本報一系列報導揭露，警方曾忽略了對這兩名警員自衛主張構成質疑的證據，如今州大陪審團正在審查涉嫌不當行為的相關證據。塔馬西的宣誓證詞，讓外界對這位副警察局長幕後的影響力，產生了更多疑問。

4. 對困在荷莫茲海峽附近的船隻上的人來說，這是攸關生死的處境。據國際海事組織統計，目前約有2,000艘船隻困在波斯灣，船上共有逾2萬名船員。這些船隻大多已受困超過一個月。瑞貝卡·馮報導指出，如今許多船上的新鮮蔬菜與淡水都已見底，船員們正透過社群媒體與船用無線電交流求生訣竅與應對策略。部分中國籍船員甚至自拍影片，展示自己如何收集空調冷凝水用來洗澡、洗衣。也有船員開始在油輪邊緣垂釣，捕撈鮪魚、烏賊與白帶魚來烹煮食用。

專家解讀

5. 問：這波石油衝擊，會迫使各國央行升息嗎？隨著伊朗戰爭推升通膨，部分投資人正押注各國央行將收緊貨幣政策。專欄作家詹姆斯·麥金塔許撰文說明他為何認為這種看法是錯的。答：各國央行始終活在對上一次犯錯的恐懼陰影之中。隨著美以對伊朗的戰爭推升通膨，投資人正押注政策制定者將採取他們早該在2021年就採取的行動：升息，或至少放棄原定的降息計畫。但這波新的石油衝擊，與疫情後的經濟景氣熱潮之間，存在根本性的差異。如今的通膨，是由於伊朗切斷經荷莫茲海峽運送的石油及其他航運，導致供給受限所致；而2021至2022年的通膨，則是由於在封鎖措施解除後，手握大量刺激資金的消費者需求暴增所致。各國央行深諳如何應對需求過剩的問題——它們理應遠早於2022年才真正動手升息，及早遏制借貸與支出。但如今，面對供給端受到的衝擊，它們幾乎無計可施，因為俗話說得好：你印不出石油。然而，交易員如今預期歐洲央行今年將升息近三次、每次一碼（0.25個百分點）；在美國，市場預期利率將維持不變，而非此前預期的三次降息；英格蘭銀行的利率定價，也較開戰前多計入了四次升息。在我看來，這種預期毫無道理，理由有三：歷史經驗、高油價對經濟造成的衝擊，以及歐洲相較美國面臨更大的威脅。

6. 越來越多美國人正躋身中上階層。傾向右翼立場的美國企業研究所（American Enterprise Institute）的研究顯示，過去約五十年間，富裕階層的人數已顯著增長，而中產階級較低層級的人數則不斷萎縮。這股財富攀升的趨勢，正推動著這個建立在消費支出之上的美國經濟，並重塑企業所提供的產品與服務類型。這群人往往就是那些願意花1,700美元購買嬰兒搖籃、給狗狗吃手工訂製食品、辦理昂貴健身房會員、搭乘豪華郵輪，並購買商務艙機票的消費者。

本週看點

7. 週一：男子「三月瘋狂」錦標賽總決賽，將由康乃狄克大學對戰密西根大學。「阿提米絲二號」機組人員預計將在獵戶座太空船飛越月球時拍攝照片。週三：聯準會將公布最新會議紀要，這可能為央行是否可能升息以應對通膨升溫提供線索。週五：3月消費者物價指數數據，將讓投資人了解居高不下的能源成本，正如何推升整體物價水準。

數字看新聞

8. 44年——據哈佛大學住房聯合研究中心統計，美國房屋屋齡中位數，創下歷史新高紀錄。近年來的新建住宅，並未能取代美國日益老化的既有住宅存量，而維護與現代化改造這些房屋的成本，也正快速攀升。

最後花絮

9. 一場德州國會選戰，如今卻圍繞著……「成年禮」（quinceañera）打轉。巴比·普利多是一位屢獲殊榮的德哈諾（Tejano）風格歌手，正競選代表德州第15選區。在對手暗示他更適合在派對上表演娛樂、而非在國會服務之後，這位民主黨候選人索性真的這麼做：他跑遍全州各地，在拉丁裔傳統的少女十五歲成年禮慶典上獻唱表演。普利多在一段影片中表示：「在德州南部，『quinceañera』不只是一場派對，而是一種將家人與鄰里凝聚在一起的成年儀式。老實說，這正是這場競選活動的核心宗旨所在。」

新聞室之外

10. MarketWatch「別做空自己」（Don't Short Yourself）節目：歡迎於4月8日參加我們的線上直播座談與問答，探討正在形塑市場的AI趨勢，以及這對你下一步投資決策的意義。

《華爾街日報》｜Buy Side：Sonos Play喇叭以優異的做工品質與音質表現，即便你尚未使用Sonos生態系產品，也值得列入考慮。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Iran’s Asymmetric Strikes
emails.contentEn:
Iran’s asymmetric warfare is raising the cost of the conflict for the U.S. and Israel. After 13,000 U.S. combat flights and five weeks of devastating American and Israeli airstrikes, Tehran downed two U.S. warplanes yesterday. The shootdowns successfully demonstrated Iran’s military strategy, which involves inflicting tactical defeats on the U.S. and its allies not to win militarily, but to survive. Now, the question is: Will these blows weaken President Trump’s resolve to continue fighting a war he already appears eager to end?

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. A search-and-rescue operation was under way for the remaining crew member of an F-15E downed over Iran. The pilot of a second plane that was also hit ejected outside of Iran’s airspace and was rescued. Follow our live coverage here. An Iranian drone attack last month on the U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia did more damage than previously disclosed. Trump has called on allies to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but naval escorts through the waterway would be nearly impossible, officials and experts say. Todd Blanche, the new acting attorney general, must lead a Justice Department in turmoil while satisfying the president’s demands. Trump’s budget outline has a vision for reshaping how the government collects money and where it spends it—but ultimately does little to rein in yawning deficits.

FROM THE MARKETS

2. Bond yields rose after a strong March jobs report showed the U.S. added a better-than-expected 178,000 jobs. The labor market is holding up, but the story of reacceleration has given way to a question about how much damage the Iran war will do, writes Nick Timiraos.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. Iran is using asymmetric warfare to inflict pain from a weakened position. The downing of two U.S. warplanes is the deadliest evidence yet that, despite enormous military losses, Tehran can still significantly raise the cost of continuing the conflict for the U.S. and Israel. Instead of seeking to fight them toe to toe, Iran has adopted an asymmetric strategy, targeting Arab Gulf states, knocking out radars and other facilities critical to air defenses and shutting down most tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The question is how much such blows weaken Trump’s resolve to continue the war—or even to expand it, report David S. Cloud and Shelby Holliday.

4. Chrysler, once an American icon, now sells just one minivan. Can it survive? The brand that invented the minivan in the 1980s is fighting for its life, reports Ryan Felton. Chrysler is one of 14 big car brands owned by the European-American conglomerate Stellantis, a big portfolio compared with General Motors’s four or Ford’s two. And Chrysler is the only major brand to sell just one model: the Pacifica. Amid competition from upstart Chinese carmakers that are making lower-cost vehicles, a turnaround will be expensive and difficult. Stellantis will either need to invest a lot more or consider the unthinkable.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: Our columnist uploaded her bloodwork to AI. Should you? When you connect medical records and health data to a chatbot, you get results. Personal Tech columnist Nicole Nguyen wrote about her experience evaluating these bots—and what you should know before you use them. A: One-third of U.S. adults have turned to AI for health advice in the past year, and of those, around 41% uploaded personal medical information to a chatbot, according to a recent survey from the health nonprofit KFF. Data sharing is getting even easier. In recent months, the most popular AI apps—OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, Perplexity and Microsoft’s Copilot—unveiled ways to connect data from your wearables and medical records. A headache can be benign or life-threatening depending on the context. In the white-hot AI race, a model that can navigate that medical complexity successfully could gain an edge. I gave Claude and Perplexity access to my health data to search for hidden patterns in my personal metrics, and better understand what the risks are. After lots of prompting, I found that the bots are expert explainers, though occasionally prone to overstatement. But gaining some AI-enabled medical clarity means losing some privacy. Here’s how I prompted the bots, which ones did the best job and what you should know about the risks.

6. These AI whiz kids dropped out of college—and got investors to pay their bills. When Andrew Castellano decided to take a leave of absence from Harvard to work full-time on his AI startup, his mother cried. His VC backers saw an opportunity. Castellano then moved out of the dorms—and into an apartment complex owned by his investors, Link Ventures. Amid rapid AI development, it’s no longer enough for VC firms to invest in companies. Now, they’re buying apartments and Ikea furniture, and providing housekeeping for their teenage and 20-something founders. The logic: Fewer responsibilities means more waking hours for working.

HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

7. Saturday: The Final Four round of the men’s March Madness tournament concludes, determining who will play for the championship. Sunday: Easter; here’s why chocolate is so expensive this year, despite much-lower cocoa prices. The championship round of the women’s March Madness tournament pits South Carolina against UCLA.

THE NUMBER

8. $20 billion — How much Hamza Lemssouguer now manages at his own hedge fund, after turning down an offer to manage several billion dollars for Ken Griffin in 2020. The 35-year-old launched Arini Capital with $1.3 billion in 2022 and has been the fastest-growing new hedge-fund manager since then, according to Hedge Fund Research. Moroccan-born Lemssouguer sticks out in London’s clubby finance scene: He neither drinks alcohol nor drives a car—and his hobby of choice is raising rare parrots.

AND FINALLY...

9. This electric Rolls-Royce is $535,550—and might even be worth it. The most powerful car in the company’s history, the Black Badge Spectre clocks a 0-60 mph acceleration of 4.1 seconds, three-tenths quicker than the standard Spectre. Defying the odds, this majestic two-door, four-seat coupe is hushed, refined and utterly gorgeous, writes Dan Neil.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: Diplomacy failed to stop North Korea from getting the bomb. Donald Trump didn’t make the same mistake with Iran.

emails.contentZh:
伊朗的不對稱作戰正持續推高美國與以色列在這場衝突中付出的代價。歷經13,000架次美軍作戰飛行任務，以及五週美以聯軍毀滅性空襲之後，德黑蘭昨日擊落了兩架美軍戰機。這次擊墜行動成功展示出伊朗的軍事戰略：對美國及其盟友施以戰術性挫敗，目的不在於贏得軍事勝利，而在於求生存。如今的問題是：這些打擊，是否會削弱川普總統繼續打這場——他似乎早已急欲結束——戰爭的決心？

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 一項搜救行動正針對一架在伊朗上空被擊落的F-15E戰機中，尚未尋獲的最後一名機組人員展開。同時遭擊中的另一架戰機的飛行員，已在伊朗領空外彈射逃生並獲救。請關注本報即時報導。上月伊朗無人機對美國駐沙烏地阿拉伯大使館發動的攻擊，造成的損害遠比先前披露的更為嚴重。川普已呼籲盟友重新開放荷莫茲海峽，但官員與專家表示，要為船隻提供海軍護航幾乎是不可能的任務。新任代理司法部長陶德·布蘭奇，必須在滿足總統要求的同時，領導一個陷入動盪的司法部。川普提出的預算綱要，勾勒出一套重塑政府徵稅方式與支出去向的願景——但終究對緩解龐大財政赤字幫助有限。

市場動態

2. 在強勁的3月就業報告顯示美國新增就業人數達17.8萬人、優於預期後，公債殖利率隨之上揚。尼克·蒂米拉奧斯撰文指出，儘管就業市場依然穩健，但市場關注焦點已從「經濟重新加速」的敘事，轉向「伊朗戰爭究竟將造成多大損害」的疑問。

搶先讀

3. 伊朗正利用不對稱作戰，從自身劣勢地位對敵方造成痛擊。兩架美軍戰機遭擊落，是迄今為止最慘痛的證據，說明儘管遭受巨大軍事損失，德黑蘭仍有能力大幅推高美國與以色列繼續這場衝突所需付出的代價。伊朗並未尋求與對手正面硬碰硬，而是採取一套不對稱戰略：將矛頭對準阿拉伯海灣國家，摧毀對防空系統至關重要的雷達等設施，並幾乎切斷了荷莫茲海峽的油輪通行。大衛·克勞德與雪碧·哈樂黛報導指出，問題在於這類打擊將在多大程度上削弱川普繼續——甚至擴大——這場戰爭的決心。

4. 曾是美國經典品牌的克萊斯勒，如今只剩一款迷你廂型車在售，它還能存活下去嗎？萊恩·費爾頓報導指出，這個1980年代發明迷你廂型車的品牌，如今正為自身的存續奮力一搏。克萊斯勒是歐美合資企業Stellantis旗下14個大型汽車品牌之一，相較於通用汽車旗下的四個品牌、福特的兩個品牌，Stellantis的品牌陣容相當龐大。而克萊斯勒是唯一一個僅販售單一車型——Pacifica——的主要品牌。面對造價更低廉的中國新興車廠帶來的競爭，扭轉頹勢的成本高昂且困難重重。Stellantis要麼得大幅追加投資，要麼就得考慮那個難以想像的選項。

專家解讀

5. 問：本報專欄作家將自己的血液檢驗報告上傳給AI分析，你也該這麼做嗎？將病歷與健康數據連結至聊天機器人，確實能得出一些結果。個人科技專欄作家阮妮可撰文分享了她評測這些機器人的經驗，以及使用前你應該知道的事項。答：根據健康非營利組織KFF近期一項調查，過去一年裡，三分之一的美國成年人曾向AI尋求健康建議，其中約41%曾將個人病歷資料上傳給聊天機器人。數據分享如今變得更加容易——近幾個月，包括OpenAI的ChatGPT、Anthropic的Claude、Perplexity與微軟的Copilot在內，這些最受歡迎的AI應用程式，都相繼推出了連結穿戴裝置數據與病歷資料的功能。頭痛這種症狀，根據不同情境，可能只是小毛病，也可能攸關性命。在這場如火如荼的AI競賽中，一款能成功駕馭這種醫療複雜性的模型，或許能就此取得領先優勢。我讓Claude與Perplexity取得我的健康數據，搜尋我個人各項指標中隱藏的模式，並更深入理解其中的風險所在。經過多次提問嘗試後，我發現這些機器人在解說方面確實表現出色，但偶爾也會有誇大其詞的傾向。不過，換取AI帶來的部分醫療洞察，也意味著要犧牲部分隱私。以下是我向這些機器人提問的方式、哪一款表現最佳，以及你在使用前應該了解的風險。

6. 這些AI神童輟學了——卻讓投資人替他們買單。當安德魯·卡斯特拉諾決定從哈佛休學、全職投入自己的AI新創事業時，他的母親哭了，而他的創投金主們卻看到了商機。卡斯特拉諾隨後搬出宿舍——搬進了他的投資方Link Ventures名下的一處公寓大樓。在AI快速發展的浪潮下，創投公司如今光是投資企業已經不夠了：如今他們還會替這些十幾、二十來歲的創辦人購置公寓、添購Ikea家具，甚至提供家務服務。背後的邏輯是：責任越少，清醒工作的時間就越多。

本週末看點

7. 週六：男子「三月瘋狂」錦標賽四強賽落幕，將決出爭冠隊伍。週日：復活節；儘管可可價格已大幅下滑，本文解析今年巧克力為何依舊如此昂貴。女子「三月瘋狂」錦標賽總決賽將由南卡羅來納大學對戰加州大學洛杉磯分校（UCLA）。

數字看新聞

8. 200億美元——哈姆扎·萊姆蘇蓋爾如今在自己創立的對沖基金所管理的資金規模，此前他曾在2020年婉拒了肯·格里芬提供的一份管理數十億美元資金的邀約。這位35歲的基金經理2022年以13億美元創立Arini Capital，據對沖基金研究機構Hedge Fund Research統計，此後一直是成長速度最快的新興對沖基金經理人。出生於摩洛哥的萊姆蘇蓋爾，在倫敦那個講究人脈圈子的金融圈中顯得格格不入：他滴酒不沾，也不開車——他鍾情的嗜好，則是飼養珍稀鸚鵡。

最後花絮

9. 這款電動勞斯萊斯售價535,550美元——但或許真的物有所值。這款「黑武士」Spectre，是該公司史上馬力最強大的一款車型，0到60英里時速加速僅需4.1秒，比標準版Spectre快了0.3秒。丹·尼爾撰文指出，令人意外的是，這款氣勢恢弘的雙門四座轎跑車，開起來竟安靜、精緻，且極其優雅動人。

新聞室之外

10. 評論：外交手段未能阻止北韓擁核。而唐納·川普在伊朗問題上，並未重蹈同樣的覆轍。

《華爾街日報》｜Buy Side：我們檢視了免體檢壽險的保額上限、費用與客訴情況。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Inside Pam Bondi’s Ouster
emails.contentEn:
After months on the ropes, Pam Bondi thought she was finally safe. She was wrong. “I think it’s time,” President Trump told the attorney general yesterday, she recounted to an associate. The president had regularly expressed dissatisfaction with the speed at which Bondi handled his agenda, and she had often seemed to go out of her way to appease him. It was never enough.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. Iran is responding to the threat of a ground invasion by stepping up its defenses and recruiting children, while threatening to attack more targets around the Gulf. Follow live coverage. Whether the war ends in success or defeat for Iran depends on whether it emerges from the conflict holding the Strait of Hormuz, writes Yaroslav Trofimov. Harvard’s faculty is set to vote next week on a proposal to cap the number of A’s per course, which has prompted an outcry from undergraduates. Sleepy Hartford, Conn., is the hottest housing market in America. OpenAI’s surprise purchase of TBPN, a popular online tech-news show, underscores its efforts to help shape the narrative about AI.

FROM THE MARKETS

2. The wealthy investors who powered private credit are now rushing for the exits. The U.S. economy entered the Iran war on solid footing, and now it is absorbing a global oil shock far better than most of the world—but it isn’t fully insulated from the conflict.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. This is the inside story of Pam Bondi’s ouster. For the attorney general, yesterday was as awkward and chaotic as the rest of her 14-month tenure, report Josh Dawsey, Alex Leary, C. Ryan Barber and Sadie Gurman. Bondi and Trump, who decided earlier this week he was replacing her, briefly sat near each other during the Supreme Court’s birthright citizenship hearing, but the president soon switched chairs. Later, Bondi would ask Trump if she could keep her job until the summer. He declined. Some people close to Trump and Bondi say it wasn’t a single issue that led to her dismissal, but a steady drip of frustrations. Trump hasn’t decided on a replacement, White House officials say. These five moments defined Bondi’s tumultuous tenure.

4. This college student—and his cat meme—hunted the world’s biggest cyberweapon. Benjamin Brundage, a senior at the Rochester Institute of Technology, conducted his own investigation into a network of hacked devices that was launching the biggest cyberattacks ever seen. Investigators didn’t know who had built this powerful cyberweapon, or how. Brundage started messaging online with an anonymous user who seemed to have insider knowledge, and got key information after sending a cat meme to lighten the mood. Brundage joined a team that learned that a new internet vulnerability threatened tens of millions of consumers and as much as a quarter of the world’s corporations, reports Robert McMillan. His findings impressed veteran researchers—including federal law enforcement, which took action against the network two weeks ago. Here’s how to figure out whether your devices are being used by illegal botnets.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: Some heirs are saying thanks but no thanks to inheritances. Why? Reporter Laura Saunders wrote about a useful tax-planning tool that some older savers may want to consider. A: It’s called a disclaimer. In essence, it is a strategic rejection of an inherited asset by an heir. The result is that part or all of the inheritance passes to someone else, often a child or grandchild. The move can save taxes and accomplish other goals for families. It can be used with IRAs and also other inherited assets. I’m betting many older savers are overlooking disclaimers as an IRA tax-planning tool. I was one of them. However, I recently disclaimed part of a traditional IRA I inherited, and it worked out well. My adult children received a legacy from a relative they loved and the overall taxes will be lower. As a result, I’m struck by how useful disclaimers can be for retirees and pre-retirees who have traditional IRAs far larger than they expected. Thanks to diligent saving, 401(k) rollovers, and market growth, these accounts are often a retiree’s largest asset. While this is a great problem to have, it poses dilemmas for savers trying to minimize income taxes.

6. Homeowners are ditching all-white interiors for something less vanilla. For years, white walls and light-oak floors have ruled the home-decor world, especially when it’s time to sell. But maximalist interiors are gaining traction across the country as homeowners experiment with bold prints and patterns, enveloping colors and showstopper embellishments. Yet opinions are divided on how these types of designs fare when it comes to attracting a buyer.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. Stock markets are closed for Good Friday. Bonds will close early. The Trump administration is expected to submit its annual budget request, for the fiscal year beginning Oct. 1. Jobs data for March will provide a snapshot of the health of the labor market amid spiking energy prices due to war in the Middle East. Here’s what we’re watching.

THE NUMBER

8. $1.8 trillion — The value of sovereign wealth funds in the U.A.E., making the small country the leading sovereign wealth power in the Gulf. See WSJ’s guide to the four wealthiest countries in the region, their funds and the key people to know.

AND FINALLY...

9. Drivers are celebrating the demise of the stop-start. Designed to lower emissions by temporarily shutting off the engine while the brake is engaged, the feature also makes driving feel unnatural and jerky, critics argue. After federal incentives during the Obama administration kicked U.S. adoption into high gear, stop-start haters this year finally found their champion: Trump. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced the agency was eliminating the federal credits that contributed to stop-start’s spread.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: President Trump’s budget shows a welcome new realism about the threats America faces, as he follows through on his vow to increase defense spending to $1.5 trillion.

WSJ | Buy Side: See our guide to Apple's laptop lineup to decide which one is right for you.
emails.contentZh:
在苦撐數月之後，帕姆·邦迪原以為自己終於安全過關了。她錯了。她向一位同僚轉述，川普總統昨日對這位司法部長說：「我想是時候了。」總統一直以來都對邦迪處理其施政議程的速度表示不滿，而她也似乎總是竭盡所能地討好他。但無論如何都不夠。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 面對地面入侵的威脅，伊朗正加強防禦並徵召兒童入伍，同時揚言將攻擊波斯灣周邊更多目標。請關注即時報導。亞羅斯拉夫·特羅菲莫夫撰文指出，這場戰爭最終對伊朗而言究竟是勝是敗，取決於戰後伊朗是否仍掌控著荷莫茲海峽。哈佛大學教職員將於下週就一項限制每門課程「A」等成績比例的提案進行投票，此舉已引發本科生的強烈抗議。看似不起眼的康乃狄克州哈特福德市，如今成了全美最火熱的房市。OpenAI出人意料地收購了頗受歡迎的線上科技新聞節目TBPN，凸顯出該公司試圖主導外界對AI敘事的努力。

市場動態

2. 曾推動私募信貸蓬勃發展的富裕投資人，如今正爭相尋求退場。美國經濟是在根基穩固的狀態下步入這場伊朗戰爭的，如今面對全球石油衝擊，其承受能力也遠優於世界上大多數國家——但這場衝突對美國的影響，仍未能完全免疫。

搶先讀

3. 這是帕姆·邦迪遭撤換的內幕故事。喬什·道西、亞歷克斯·利里、C·萊恩·巴伯與莎蒂·古爾曼報導指出，對這位司法部長而言，昨天就和她長達14個月任期中的其餘日子一樣，充滿尷尬與混亂。在最高法院審理出生公民權案件的聽證會上，本週稍早已決定撤換邦迪的川普，一度與她相鄰而坐，但總統很快便換了座位。後來，邦迪曾詢問川普，自己是否能留任至夏天，遭到川普拒絕。部分親近川普與邦迪的人士表示，導致她遭撤換的並非單一事件，而是長期累積的不滿情緒逐漸發酵所致。白宮官員表示，川普尚未決定接任人選。以下這五個時刻，定義了邦迪動盪不安的任期。

4. 這名大學生——連同他的一則貓咪迷因——追查出了全球最大的一起網路武器攻擊事件。羅切斯特理工學院大四學生班傑明·布倫戴奇，展開了一場針對某個駭客設備網路的個人調查，該網路正發動有史以來規模最大的網路攻擊。調查人員原本並不知道，是誰打造了這款強大的網路武器，又是如何辦到的。布倫戴奇開始與一名似乎握有內部消息的匿名網友通訊聯繫，並在傳送一則貓咪迷因緩和氣氛後，取得了關鍵資訊。羅伯特·麥克米倫報導指出，布倫戴奇隨後加入了一個團隊，發現一項新的網路安全漏洞正威脅著數千萬消費者，以及全球多達四分之一的企業。他的調查發現讓資深研究人員印象深刻，其中包括聯邦執法機構——該機構已於兩週前對這個網路採取了行動。以下教你如何判斷自己的設備是否正被非法殭屍網路利用。

專家解讀

5. 問：有些繼承人竟主動拒絕遺產，這是為什麼？記者蘿拉·桑德斯撰文介紹了一項部分年長儲蓄者或許值得考慮的實用節稅工具。答：這項工具稱為「聲明放棄」（disclaimer）。本質上，這是繼承人策略性地拒絕接受一項遺產，結果是部分或全部遺產轉而傳承給另一人，通常是子女或孫輩。此舉可為家庭節省稅款，並達成其他財務目標，適用於個人退休帳戶（IRA）及其他各類繼承資產。我猜想，許多年長的儲蓄者其實都忽略了「聲明放棄」這項可用於IRA節稅規劃的工具——我自己就曾是其中之一。不過，我最近針對自己繼承的一筆傳統IRA中的部分資產聲明放棄，結果相當理想：我的成年子女從一位他們深愛的親人那裡獲得了這筆遺產，而整體稅負也因此降低。這讓我深刻體會到，對於那些傳統IRA帳戶規模遠超預期的退休人士及準退休人士而言，「聲明放棄」能有多大的用處。得益於長年勤勉儲蓄、401(k)轉存，以及市場成長，這類帳戶往往是退休人士最大宗的資產。儘管這是個令人欣喜的「幸福煩惱」，但對於希望盡量減少所得稅負擔的儲蓄者來說，這也帶來了不小的抉擇難題。

6. 屋主們正紛紛拋棄全白色系內裝，轉而追求不那麼「香草」的風格。多年來，白牆與淺色橡木地板一直主宰著居家裝潢界，尤其是在準備賣房的時候。但如今隨著越來越多屋主開始嘗試大膽的印花與圖案、濃郁飽和的色調，以及引人注目的裝飾細節，「極繁主義」風格的室內設計正在全美各地日益盛行。不過，對於這類設計究竟有助於還是不利於吸引買家，外界看法仍存在分歧。

今日要聞預告

7. 股市因耶穌受難日休市，債券市場則將提前收盤。川普政府預計將提交下一財政年度（自10月1日起算）的年度預算申請。3月就業數據將呈現就業市場的健康狀況，恰逢中東戰爭導致能源價格飆升之際。以下是我們關注的焦點。

數字看新聞

8. 1.8兆美元——阿聯主權財富基金的總值，使這個蕞爾小國成為海灣地區首屈一指的主權財富大國。參見本報整理的該地區四個最富裕國家指南，包括其主權基金及需要認識的關鍵人物。

最後花絮

9. 駕駛人正在慶祝「怠速熄火」（stop-start）技術的終結。這項設計旨在踩下煞車時暫時關閉引擎、藉此降低排放的技術，批評者卻認為它也讓開車體驗變得不自然、頓挫感十足。在歐巴馬政府時期的聯邦補貼政策大力推動下，這項技術一度在美國加速普及，如今，討厭「怠速熄火」技術的人們終於找到了自己的代言人：川普。美國環保署署長李·澤爾丁宣布，該機構將取消曾助長「怠速熄火」技術普及的聯邦稅收抵免。

新聞室之外

10. 評論：川普總統的預算案，展現出對美國所面臨威脅的一種令人樂見的全新務實態度，他正兌現自己將國防支出提高至1.5兆美元的承諾。

《華爾街日報》｜Buy Side：參見我們整理的蘋果筆電系列指南，助你決定哪一款最適合自己。

emails.contentEn:
Last night, President Trump sought to reassure skeptical Americans that the war in Iran is in the national interest, arguing the operation was necessary to decimate a threatening regime and insisting that economic pain would be short-lived. In a 20-minute address, his most direct sales pitch to the nation since the war began, Trump said the U.S. had succeeded on the battlefield and declared that U.S. military objectives would be completed “very shortly.” The president said he still aims for a diplomatic agreement to end the war. But in the meantime, he vowed to hit Iran “extremely hard” in the coming weeks. Follow live coverage of the conflict.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. Trump’s bid to redefine American citizenship might still be a legal long shot. These are the key arguments on birthright citizenship from the Supreme Court. The president endorsed a plan to quickly fund most of the DHS and then use a special procedure to pay for immigration enforcement with only GOP votes. Investors are moving early into Venezuela, seeing an opportunity to get in on the ground floor of the country’s potential recovery. China is building another massive base in the South China Sea. Maine is about to become the first state to ban new data centers.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 46331.00 -475.00 (1.01%); S&P 500 Futures 6540.25 -77.50 (1.17%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 23832.75 -362.00 (1.50%). Source: Factset, market data as of 4/2/2026, 5:53:54 AM ET. The stock market climbed for a second straight day ahead of Trump’s address, but some of the enthusiasm fizzled during his speech. A disruption in helium supplies spells opportunity for some, writes Jinjoo Lee.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. Nursing is the surefire new path to American prosperity. Factory work used to be Americans’ most reliable ticket to the middle class. Office jobs offered another dependable route. But as automation, globalized manufacturing and now artificial intelligence threaten or narrow some of these paths, healthcare jobs have become the surest bet. At a time of uncertainty in the labor market, nursing offers not only stability but, for some, a pathway to real prosperity. Abundant job opportunities and potential six-figure incomes are drawing young people to the field as other industries falter, reports Jeanne Whalen.

4. Meet the women who love the manosphere. In the new-media universe—where bro-friendly hosts like Theo Von and Joe Rogan reign supreme—female fans represent an undertapped market. Podcasts increasingly run on advertising revenue, and women are the ultimate audience to reach because they influence the bulk of household spending. Many of them are looking for exactly what these shows deliver: a politically adaptable, occasionally vulgar lens on the complicated times we’re living through, reports Will Groff.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: Is moving abroad the way to find your dream job? People frustrated by political and job-market disruptions think the grass might be greener elsewhere. Columnist Callum Borchers explores the benefits and drawbacks of an international career move: A: The short answer is probably not. Moving abroad is one of those things people like to dream and talk about. Following through is another story. Still, it’s striking that so many Americans are even thinking about this. STEM professionals, in particular, say jobs in government, academia and even the private sector feel less secure because of federal shutdowns and funding cuts. Foreign countries are actively wooing these workers. I recently attended an event where a contingent from Finland pitched a Nordic escape to science and tech types. Most people I met weren’t ready to take the (very cold) plunge. Common hangups include settling for a lower salary overseas, learning a new language and losing your professional network. Some told me they will get over those barriers if their professional prospects worsen at home. And one man who works in sales said he will relocate to Finland in May. He’ll be part of a net out-migration from the U.S. this year, according to a projection by the Brookings Institution.

6. These islands give Iran a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz. Iran’s fortifications on small islands near the Strait of Hormuz boost its power to control the key waterway, and reopening shipping there might require U.S. or allied forces to capture some of those same dots of land. The importance of the islands is increasingly coming into view as Iran causes an economic crisis by blocking most oil tankers from transiting the strait.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. Economic data: Initial jobless claims and the U.S. Energy Information Administration’s weekly report on natural gas storage are due. Earnings: Acuity.

THE NUMBER

8. >250,000 — How many miles from Earth Artemis II—which successfully launched last night—is set to take four astronauts. Their mission is to circle around the moon, setting a record for the deepest that humans have ever flown in space. The voyage is part of NASA’s renewed push to return American astronauts to the moon’s surface.

AND FINALLY...

9. The IRS chief and a sports collector are fighting over Muhammad Ali’s shorts. Frank Bisignano has two demanding jobs, running the Social Security Administration and serving as the CEO of the Internal Revenue Service during tax season. But these days the Trump administration heavyweight has something else to worry about: He’s locked in a fight with Eric Inselberg, a sports memorabilia buff and entrepreneur, over a pair of Muhammad Ali’s boxing shorts. Inselberg estimates the shorts are now worth $800,000. Bisignano called the sports collector’s valuation of the shorts bogus.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: If the NFL would prefer to dun fans for more money while broadcasters are hollowed out, then Congress might consider whether the league’s 1961 antitrust exemption has ceased to make sense.

WSJ | Buy Side: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

Correction: Quest Diagnostics will report earnings on April 21. Monday’s edition of The 10-Point incorrectly said the company would report earnings on March 31.
emails.contentZh:
昨晚，川普總統試圖說服心存懷疑的美國民眾，相信這場伊朗戰爭符合國家利益，主張這項軍事行動是徹底摧毀一個構成威脅政權的必要手段，並堅稱這場經濟陣痛只是暫時的。在這場長達20分鐘、也是他自開戰以來對全國最直接的一次「推銷」演說中，川普表示美國已在戰場上取得成功，並宣告美軍的作戰目標「很快」就將全部達成。他表示，自己仍以達成外交協議、結束戰爭為目標，但與此同時，他誓言未來幾週將對伊朗發動「極其猛烈」的打擊。請關注本報對這場衝突的即時報導。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 川普試圖重新定義美國公民權的舉措，恐怕在法律上仍是一場勝算渺茫的豪賭。以下是最高法院審理出生公民權議題的幾項核心論點。總統已同意一項計畫，先迅速為國土安全部大部分部門提供撥款，隨後再運用一項特殊程序，僅憑共和黨票數為移民執法撥款。投資人正提前佈局委內瑞拉，看好這個國家潛在復甦帶來的先發優勢機會。中國正在南海興建又一座大型軍事基地。緬因州即將成為全美首個禁止新建資料中心的州。

市場即時動態

2. 道瓊期貨46331.00，跌475.00點（1.01%）；標普500期貨6540.25，跌77.50點（1.17%）；納斯達克100期貨23832.75，跌362.00點（1.50%）。資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年4月2日美東時間上午5:53:54。在川普發表演說前，美股已連續第二天上漲，但演說過程中，部分樂觀情緒逐漸消退。Jinjoo Lee撰文指出，氦氣供應中斷對部分業者而言正是商機所在。

搶先讀

3. 護理工作正成為通往美國繁榮生活的全新穩妥途徑。工廠工作過去一直是美國人躋身中產階級最可靠的門票，辦公室工作則是另一條穩定的途徑。但隨著自動化、全球化製造，以及如今人工智慧的興起，威脅甚至縮窄了這些傳統路徑，醫療保健相關工作已成為最穩妥的選擇。珍妮·惠倫報導指出，在就業市場充滿不確定性之際，護理工作不僅提供了穩定性，對某些人來說，更是一條通往真正富足生活的道路——充裕的就業機會與可能達六位數的收入，正吸引年輕人投身這個領域，即便其他行業正步履維艱。

4. 認識這些鍾情於「男性圈」（manosphere）文化的女性們。在這個由西奧·馮、喬·羅根等迎合男性聽眾的主持人稱霸的新媒體世界裡，女性粉絲其實代表著一塊尚未被充分開發的市場。Podcast節目日益仰賴廣告營收維生，而女性正是最理想的目標受眾，因為她們主導著家庭消費支出的大部分決策。威爾·格羅夫報導指出，許多女性聽眾正尋求的，恰恰正是這些節目所提供的東西：以一種政治立場靈活多變、偶爾不失粗俗的視角，觀看我們身處的這個複雜時代。

專家解讀

5. 問：移居海外，是找到夢想工作的途徑嗎？對政治與就業市場動盪感到沮喪的人們，開始覺得或許外國的月亮比較圓。專欄作家卡勒姆·博切爾斯探討了跨國轉職的利弊：答：簡短的答案大概是「不」。移居海外是人們喜歡幻想、掛在嘴邊談論的事情之一，真正付諸實行則完全是另一回事。不過，如此多美國人竟開始認真考慮這件事，本身就相當引人注目。尤其是STEM（科學、科技、工程、數學）領域的專業人士表示，由於聯邦政府停擺與資金削減，政府機構、學術界乃至私部門的工作都讓人感覺不再穩固。外國政府正積極招攬這些人才。我最近參加了一場活動，一支芬蘭代表團向科技與科學界人士推銷「北歐避風港」的概念。我遇見的大多數人，都還沒準備好縱身一躍（跳進那個異常寒冷的國度）。常見的顧慮包括：得接受海外較低的薪資、得學習一門新語言，以及失去現有的職業人脈網絡。有些人告訴我，如果國內的職涯前景進一步惡化，他們會設法克服這些障礙。一位從事銷售工作的男性表示，他將於5月搬遷至芬蘭——根據布魯金斯學會的預測，他將成為今年美國淨遷出人口的其中一員。

6. 正是這些島嶼，讓伊朗牢牢扼住了荷莫茲海峽的咽喉。伊朗在荷莫茲海峽附近數座小島上建立的防禦工事，增強了其掌控這條關鍵水道的能力；若要重新開放該處的航運，美國或盟軍恐須先奪下部分同樣的島嶼。隨著伊朗透過封鎖大多數油輪通行海峽而引發一場經濟危機，這些島嶼的重要性也日益凸顯。

今日要聞預告

7. 經濟數據：每週初次申請失業救濟人數，以及美國能源資訊署每週天然氣庫存報告即將公布。財報：Acuity Brands。

數字看新聞

8. 超過25萬英里——昨晚成功發射的「阿提米絲二號」任務，預計將帶著四名太空人飛越的距地球距離。他們的任務是繞月飛行，這將創下人類迄今為止飛行至太空最深處的紀錄。此行是NASA重啟推動美國太空人重返月球表面計畫的一環。

最後花絮

9. 國稅局局長與一位體育收藏家，正為穆罕默德·阿里的一條拳擊短褲爭執不下。法蘭克·比西尼亞諾身兼兩份繁重的工作：掌管社會安全局，同時在報稅季擔任國稅局局長。但這位川普政府的重量級人物，如今還多了一件煩心事：他正與體育紀念品收藏愛好者兼企業家艾瑞克·殷賽爾伯格，為一條穆罕默德·阿里的拳擊短褲爭執不休。殷賽爾伯格估計，這條短褲如今價值80萬美元。比西尼亞諾則稱這位收藏家對短褲的估值根本是胡扯。

新聞室之外

10. 評論：如果NFL寧願在轉播商日益被掏空之際，繼續向球迷索取更多錢，那麼國會或許該考慮，這個聯盟自1961年起享有的反壟斷豁免權，是否已經不再合理。

《華爾街日報》｜Buy Side：參見這些頂尖高利活存帳戶，讓你的存款利率跑贏平均水準。

更正：桂格診斷（Quest Diagnostics）將於4月21日公布財報。週一版《The 10-Point》先前誤植該公司財報公布日期為3月31日。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The U.A.E. Prepares for a Fight
emails.contentEn:
The United Arab Emirates is preparing to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz by force. Though Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states are turning against Iran’s regime, the U.A.E.—which has been hit by more Iranian missiles and drones than even Israel—would be the first Persian Gulf country to become a combatant. The U.A.E. is also pushing the U.S. to occupy islands in the strategic waterway. Iran, meanwhile, continues to take aim at its Gulf neighbors, including the industries behind their pivot away from oil.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. President Trump said the U.S. would leave Iran in two to three weeks, and plans to address the nation regarding the war later today. Follow our live coverage here. Iran is targeting industries tied to Persian Gulf states’ efforts to diversify beyond oil, including metals factories, bank offices and tourist sites. Trump signed an executive order to create lists of people it considers eligible to vote in federal elections, as well as placing new restrictions on mail-in voting, moves that will likely face legal challenges. Airlines are raising fares, adding baggage fees and dialing back routes as they try to cover the skyrocketing costs of jet fuel.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 46814.00 +232.00 (0.50%); S&P 500 Futures 6602.75 +32.00 (0.49%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 24070.00 +155.00 (0.65%). Source: Factset, market data as of 4/1/2026, 5:59:28 AM ET. With the economy on the edge, here’s a look at best-case and worst-case scenarios. Gas has hit $4 a gallon. Is that really as bad as it sounds? Stephen Nesbitt’s Cliffwater helped bring private credit to the masses, but now the firm is racing to calm investors after steep withdrawals.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. The U.A.E. wants to join the fight to reopen Hormuz. The U.A.E. is actively lobbying for a U.N. Security Council resolution that would authorize action to reopen the Strait of Hormuz by force, and has also said that the U.S. should occupy islands in the strait, including one that the U.A.E. claims. The Gulf nation’s newly combative approach marks a fundamental shift in its strategic outlook, report Summer Said, David S. Cloud and Michael Amon. Iran, meanwhile, has been stepping up its bombardments of the Emirates, raining down more missiles and drones on the U.A.E. than on any other country.

4. America now has an EV Rust Belt, and high gas prices won’t rescue it. Magna International built a large factory in Michigan after securing a big contract to make parts for General Motors’ new electric pickup. Five years later, that million-square-foot plant is mostly empty and losing money—a casualty of America’s messy breakup with EVs. It’s one of dozens of now desolate or sparsely used EV-parts plants across the country. Now the war in Iran has driven gas prices up so sharply that some are daring to wonder whether U.S. buyers might give EVs another look. But amid ongoing uncertainty, Magna and its big Detroit customers are forging ahead with plans to roll back EV investments, reports Sharon Terlep.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: It was a rough quarter for markets. What stocks and sectors succeeded amid the turmoil? The quarter began with one jolt to the oil market—the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro—only to end with one far larger: the war with Iran. Reporter Jared Mitovich wrote about which investments outperformed the broader market. A: In a period marked by Middle East conflict and surging oil prices, it may come as no surprise that energy stocks were among the biggest winners in a forgettable first quarter. But America’s oil-and-gas giants such as Exxon Mobil and ConocoPhillips weren’t the only early 2026 successes. Here are a few others: Agriculture shares and commodities: The closure of Hormuz has benefited American fertilizer producers, which investors are betting will gain market share while competitors in the Middle East struggle to get their output to market. Defense companies: An increasing U.S. appetite for foreign intervention from Venezuela to Iran—and Trump’s request for a $1.5 trillion defense budget—tipped financial markets in weapon makers’ favor in the first quarter. The U.S. dollar: The greenback extended its winning streak, helped by the U.S.’s position as a net oil exporter. It could rise further due to the energy price shock, Morgan Stanley strategists have said. Tariff-exposed companies: These businesses, such as construction firms and appliance makers, climbed after the Supreme Court struck down many of the duties.

6. These are the highs and lows of a $939 upgrade to business class on United Airlines. WSJ columnist Dawn Gilbertson took advantage of a tantalizing offer to upgrade from economy to a plush Polaris business-class cabin. She enjoyed the champagne, ice-cream-sundae cart and Saks Fifth Avenue bedding. But the largely inoperable Wi-Fi was a huge downer—underscoring the harsh reality that inconsistency still rules in the airline arms race for big-spending travelers.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on Trump’s executive order seeking to end birthright citizenship. NASA’s Artemis II mission is set to embark on the deepest human spaceflight since the final Apollo moon mission in 1972, a big test for the agency and several contractors. Earnings: Cal-Maine Foods, Conagra Brands, Lamb Weston Holdings.

THE NUMBER

8. 22 — The number of corporate deals valued at $10 billion or more that have been announced globally so far in 2026—a record quarterly number, according to LSEG data. This week alone, Unilever unveiled a more than $65 billion deal, including debt, to combine its food business with spice maker McCormick, and Sysco agreed to buy Jetro Restaurant Depot for over $29 billion, including debt.

AND FINALLY...

9. How did these five friends become the kings of ‘Seinfeld’ trivia? Mike Rapanaro and four of his friends in the New York City area make up the Venetian Blinds, a team that’s dominating the “Seinfeld” trivia circuit. They take inspiration from the characters in their daily lives—and refuse to watch any other TV shows. One of them falls asleep to episodes hoping some details stick in his head. Another listens to the show’s audio while showering.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: The place to fight illegal immigration is at the border. It doesn’t require trying to change the settled meaning of the 14th Amendment by executive order.

WSJ | Buy Side: Life insurance can help high-net-worth families with estate planning, tax mitigation and building a legacy for future generations.
emails.contentZh:
阿拉伯聯合大公國正準備協助以武力重新開放荷莫茲海峽。儘管沙烏地阿拉伯及其他海灣國家已逐漸倒向反對伊朗政權的一方，但阿聯——遭受的伊朗飛彈與無人機攻擊甚至比以色列還多——將成為波斯灣地區首個直接參戰的國家。阿聯同時也在敦促美國出兵佔領這條戰略水道中的島嶼。與此同時，伊朗持續將矛頭對準其海灣鄰國，包括支撐這些國家擺脫石油依賴、實現經濟多元化的相關產業。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 川普總統表示，美國將在兩到三週內撤出伊朗，並計劃於今日稍晚就這場戰爭向全國發表講話。請關注本報即時報導。伊朗正將攻擊目標對準與波斯灣國家擺脫石油依賴、實現產業多元化相關的產業，包括金屬工廠、銀行辦公室與觀光景點。川普簽署行政命令，要求建立聯邦選舉合格選民名單，並對郵寄投票實施新的限制，這些舉措預料將面臨法律訴訟挑戰。隨著航空燃油成本飆升，各航空公司正紛紛調漲票價、增收行李費，並削減航線，以彌補成本。

市場即時動態

2. 道瓊期貨46814.00，漲232.00點（0.50%）；標普500期貨6602.75，漲32.00點（0.49%）；納斯達克100期貨24070.00，漲155.00點（0.65%）。資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年4月1日美東時間上午5:59:28。在經濟瀕臨懸崖邊緣之際，以下檢視最佳與最壞情境的可能走向。汽油價格已觸及每加侖4美元，這真有聽起來那麼糟嗎？史蒂芬·內斯比特旗下的Cliffwater公司，曾協助將私募信貸推廣給大眾投資人，如今卻在面臨大規模贖回後，正竭力安撫投資人情緒。

搶先讀

3. 阿聯希望加入重新開放荷莫茲海峽的軍事行動。阿聯正積極遊說聯合國安理會通過一項決議，授權以武力重新開放荷莫茲海峽，並表示美國應出兵佔領海峽中的島嶼，包括一座阿聯本身宣稱擁有主權的島嶼。薩默·賽義德、大衛·克勞德與麥可·阿蒙報導指出，這個海灣國家如今展現的強硬姿態，標誌著其戰略思維出現根本性轉變。與此同時，伊朗持續加強對阿聯的轟炸攻勢，落在阿聯境內的飛彈與無人機數量，已超過落在任何其他國家的數量。

4. 美國如今出現了一條「電動車鐵鏽帶」，而居高不下的油價也救不了它。麥格納國際（Magna International）在拿下為通用汽車新款電動皮卡生產零件的大單後，曾在密西根州興建一座大型工廠。五年後的今天，這座佔地逾百萬平方英尺的工廠幾乎已是空蕩一片，虧損連連——成為美國與電動車「混亂分手」的犧牲品之一。這只是全美數十座如今已荒廢或使用率低落的電動車零件工廠之一。如今伊朗戰爭導致油價急遽飆升，已有人大膽揣測，美國消費者是否會重新考慮電動車。但莎朗·特勒普報導指出，在持續存在的不確定性中，麥格納及其在底特律的大客戶們，仍在推進削減電動車投資的計畫。

專家解讀

5. 問：這一季對市場來說相當顛簸，在這場動盪中，哪些股票和產業表現亮眼？這一季開局便迎來一次油市震盪——委內瑞拉領導人馬杜洛遭逮捕——結尾則以規模遠更龐大的伊朗戰爭收場。記者傑瑞德·米托維奇撰文分析了哪些投資標的表現優於大盤。答：在這段以中東衝突與油價飆升為特徵的時期，能源類股成為這個乏善可陳的第一季裡表現最亮眼的贏家之一，這或許並不令人意外。但2026年初的贏家，並不僅限於埃克森美孚、康菲石油等美國油氣巨頭，以下還有幾個值得一提：農業類股與大宗商品：荷莫茲海峽封鎖讓美國肥料生產商受益，投資人押注，當中東地區競爭對手難以將產品運往市場之際，這些美國企業將趁機搶佔市場份額。國防類公司：美國從委內瑞拉到伊朗，對外國軍事介入的胃口與日俱增——加上川普提出的1.5兆美元國防預算請求——讓第一季金融市場明顯偏向軍火製造商。美元：受惠於美國作為石油淨出口國的地位，美元延續了升值走勢；摩根士丹利策略師表示，受能源價格衝擊影響，美元未來可能進一步走高。受關稅影響的企業：建築公司與家電製造商等此類企業，在最高法院裁定推翻多項關稅後股價走高。

6. 這是聯合航空一次939美元升等商務艙的甘苦體驗。本報專欄作家道恩·吉爾伯森把握住一項誘人優惠，將座位從經濟艙升等至豪華的Polaris商務艙。她享受了香檳、冰淇淋聖代推車服務，以及薩克斯第五大道品牌的寢具。但幾乎完全無法使用的機上Wi-Fi，卻讓體驗大打折扣——凸顯出在航空業爭奪高消費旅客的軍備競賽中，服務品質參差不齊仍是殘酷的現實。

今日要聞預告

7. 最高法院將就川普尋求終結出生公民權的行政命令舉行口頭辯論。NASA的「阿提米絲二號」任務即將啟程，這將是自1972年阿波羅登月計畫最後一次任務以來，人類最深入的一次太空飛行，也是該機構及多家承包商的一大考驗。財報：卡爾梅恩食品、康尼格拉食品、蘭姆威士頓控股。

數字看新聞

8. 22——據倫敦證交所集團（LSEG）數據，2026年迄今全球已宣布的價值100億美元以上企業併購交易數量，創下單季新高紀錄。僅本週，聯合利華便宣布一項連同債務逾650億美元的交易，計劃將其食品業務與香料製造商味好美合併；西斯科（Sysco）也同意以連同債務逾290億美元的價格收購Jetro Restaurant Depot。

最後花絮

9. 這五位好友是如何成為「歡樂單身派對」（Seinfeld）冷知識問答之王的？麥克·拉帕納羅與他四位居住在紐約市地區的朋友組成了「威尼斯百葉窗」（Venetian Blinds）隊，這支隊伍如今在「歡樂單身派對」冷知識問答巡迴賽中所向披靡。他們從劇中角色汲取日常生活靈感——並且拒看任何其他電視節目。其中一人甚至邊聽劇集邊入睡，希望某些細節能潛移默化地留在腦海中；另一人則習慣在洗澡時聽這部劇的音軌。

新聞室之外

10. 評論：打擊非法移民的戰場應該在邊境，而不需要試圖以行政命令改變已然確立的憲法第14修正案的含義。

《華爾街日報》｜Buy Side：人壽保險有助於高淨值家庭進行遺產規劃、減輕稅負，並為後代建立財富傳承。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Trump Talks of Ending Iran War Without Reopening Hormuz
emails.contentEn:
The longer the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, the more it will roil the global economy and boost gas prices, which have hit $4 for the first time since 2022. Now, President Trump is telling aides he’s willing to end the U.S. military campaign against Iran even if the strait remains largely closed, administration officials said. That will likely mean extending Tehran’s firm grip on the waterway and leaving a complex operation to reopen it for a later date, report Alexander Ward and Meridith McGraw. Follow our live coverage for the latest developments on the war.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. Trump’s decision to allow a Russian tanker’s one-time shipment of oil to Cuba effectively breaks a two-month blockade. Unilever is nearing a deal to create a $60 billion food giant with spice maker McCormick. The American Heart Association’s new nutrition guidance contradicts government recommendations. Washington State enacted a tax on income over $1 million, the latest Democratic state to levy a tax aimed squarely at the wealthy. Companies of every size are wrestling with uncertainty about when, how—and even if—they will get tariff refunds.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 45871.00 +406.00 (0.89%); S&P 500 Futures 6442.75 +54.50 (0.85%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 23323.50 +183.75 (0.79%). Source: Factset, market data as of 3/31/2026, 5:58:40 AM ET. Investors had high expectations for 2026. Now they’re just hoping to sidestep a recession. The Iran conflict is triggering a surge in demand for war insurance in the region. Stocks of U.S. liquefied-natural-gas companies have been on a tear, but higher-for-longer prices muddy the long-term outlook for LNG, writes Carol Ryan.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. An unlikely ensemble is leading Trump’s hunt for 2020 election fraud. Nearly six years after Donald Trump lost that election, once-fringe theories have gained new traction inside the White House, drawing in top officials at the Justice Department, the FBI and intelligence agencies, according to U.S. officials and others involved in the effort, report Vera Bergengruen, Josh Dawsey and Sadie Gurman. The White House declined to comment on the 2020 effort, but called for Congress to pass a Trump-backed voting package.

4. Exxon scientists had doubts about algae biofuels. The oil giant touted them anyway. We reviewed an internal presentation made in early 2020 by Exxon Mobil’s scientists and examined other documents related to the company’s efforts on algae. Some of the documents—none of which have been previously reported—show executives knew its $500 million algae research project wasn’t meeting its goals outside the lab, even as they continued to promote it to investors as a potential boon, reports Collin Eaton. “Our communications reflected the science as it was understood at the time, and when it became clear the technology would not scale commercially, we ended the program. Any suggestion otherwise is a lie,” an Exxon spokesman said.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: A simple test can assess your risk of heart disease. Should you get one? Measuring cholesterol levels has long been the main way doctors assess the risk. Increasingly, people are also opting for a simple, relatively affordable test: a coronary artery calcium scan. Health reporter Sumathi Reddy lays out what you need to know. A: These scans have been around for decades, but they got a boost from influential clinical guidelines issued earlier this month by leading cardiology groups. The tests, which take less than 10 minutes, show if there are calcium deposits in the heart, which is a proxy for plaque. If paying out-of-pocket, the scans typically cost about $75 to $200, says Dr. Michael Blaha, a professor of cardiology at the Ciccarone Center for the Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease at Johns Hopkins Medicine, although they are increasingly covered by insurance. Not everyone needs a calcium scan. If you’re middle-aged and not already on a cholesterol-lowering medication but have risk factors for heart disease, you fall into the bucket of people who should get one. Is there a downside to getting a scan? One legitimate concern among cardiologists, says Blaha, is doctors who may inappropriately use a calcium score to justify doing a procedure, such as putting a stent in.

6. Japan is fortifying a string of islands close to China. Beijing’s ambitions to absorb Taiwan—and its regular displays of power encircling the self-governing island with warships, aircraft, missiles and more—have become a core security challenge for Japan. See how and where the country is doubling down on a shift to its strategic southwest.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Gen. Dan Caine will hold a news conference at 8 a.m. ET on the Iran conflict. Economic data: The Conference Board’s consumer confidence survey for March will offer signs of how rising energy prices are impacting consumer sentiment. Plus, the Labor Department will release its job openings and labor turnover survey, or Jolts, for February, and S&P Global will release its Case-Shiller home price index for January. Earnings: Nike, Quest Diagnostics, McCormick, Dave & Buster’s, Beyond Meat.

THE NUMBER

8. 190 million — Helium, in cubic meters, that the world produced last year—enough to fill roughly 76,000 Olympic-size swimming pools. The Iran war is cutting deeply into supplies of the gas, which is essential for cooling AI chip-making tools and keeping MRI scanners humming.

AND FINALLY...

9. A massive KitKat heist turned into promotional gold. It was the brazen chocolate heist heard around the social-media world: Over the weekend, Nestlé confirmed that thieves had swiped 413,793 units of KitKats somewhere along their way from a factory in central Italy to Poland. The chocolate bars and the truck carrying them remain missing, but no one was hurt in the theft, it said. What the Swiss company lost in chocolate, though, it gained back in a public-relations coup—as did multiple other companies quick to hop on the meme bandwagon.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: One beneficiary of SpaceX’s success is Charlie Ergen, who has used regulatory arbitrage to save his failed broadband bet. This is a tale of failed industrial policy that might end well despite government planners.

WSJ | Buy Side: We found all the best home and kitchen deals from Amazon’s Big Spring Sale.

荷莫茲海峽封鎖的時間越長，對全球經濟的衝擊就越大，汽油價格也將進一步推升——目前已觸及自2022年以來首見的每加侖4美元關口。政府官員透露，如今川普總統正告訴幕僚，即便海峽大部分仍處於封鎖狀態，他也願意結束美國對伊朗的軍事行動。亞歷山大·沃德與梅瑞迪思·麥格勞報導指出，這很可能意味著德黑蘭對這條航道的牢固掌控將延續下去，而重新開放海峽這項複雜的行動，只能留待日後處理。請關注本報即時報導，掌握這場戰爭的最新進展。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 川普允許一艘俄羅斯油輪向古巴進行一次性石油運送，此舉實質上打破了持續兩個月的封鎖。聯合利華正接近與香料製造商味好美（McCormick）達成協議，共同打造一家市值600億美元的食品巨頭。美國心臟協會發布的新版營養指南，與政府的建議相互矛盾。華盛頓州已立法對超過100萬美元的收入課稅，成為最新一個推出精準針對富人稅收政策的民主黨州。無論規模大小，各家企業都在為關稅退稅何時、如何發放——甚至是否真能拿到——的不確定性而苦惱。

市場即時動態

2. 道瓊期貨45871.00，漲406.00點（0.89%）；標普500期貨6442.75，漲54.50點（0.85%）；納斯達克100期貨23323.50，漲183.75點（0.79%）。資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年3月31日美東時間上午5:58:40。投資人原本對2026年寄予厚望，如今卻只求能躲過一場衰退。伊朗衝突正引發該地區戰爭保險需求激增。卡蘿·萊恩撰文指出，美國液化天然氣公司股價一路狂飆，但居高不下的價格也讓液化天然氣的長期前景蒙上陰影。

搶先讀

3. 一群出人意料的人馬，正主導川普對2020年大選舞弊的追查行動。距離川普輸掉那場選舉將近六年後，據美國官員及參與此事的其他人士透露，一度被視為邊緣的陰謀論，如今已在白宮內部重新獲得關注，甚至吸引了司法部、聯邦調查局與情報機構高層官員的參與，薇拉·貝根格倫、喬什·道西與莎蒂·古爾曼報導。白宮拒絕就2020年相關調查行動置評，但呼籲國會通過一項川普支持的投票法案。

4. 埃克森的科學家曾對藻類生質燃料心存疑慮，但這家石油巨頭仍持續大肆宣傳。本報審視了埃克森美孚科學家2020年初製作的一份內部簡報，並查閱了與該公司藻類研發計畫相關的其他文件。柯林·伊頓報導指出，部分此前從未曝光的文件顯示，公司高層其實早已知道，這項耗資5億美元的藻類研究計畫，在實驗室之外根本未能達成目標，但他們仍持續向投資人將其宣傳為潛在的一大利多。埃克森發言人表示：「我們的對外說法，反映的是當時所理解的科學認知；一旦確定該技術無法實現商業化規模量產，我們便終止了該計畫。任何相反的說法都是謊言。」

專家解讀

5. 問：一項簡單的檢測就能評估你罹患心臟病的風險，你該去做嗎？長期以來，測量膽固醇水平一直是醫生評估風險的主要方式。如今，越來越多人也開始選擇一種簡單、相對平價的檢測：冠狀動脈鈣化掃描。健康記者蘇瑪西·雷迪詳述你需要了解的資訊。答：這類掃描檢測其實已存在數十年，但本月稍早由主要心臟病學團體發布的具影響力臨床指南，讓其熱度大增。這項檢測耗時不到10分鐘，能顯示心臟是否有鈣質沉積——這是斑塊堆積的替代指標。約翰霍普金斯醫學院奇卡羅內心血管疾病預防中心的心臟病學教授麥可·布拉哈醫師表示，若自費支付，這項檢測費用通常約在75至200美元之間，不過如今已日益納入保險給付範圍。並非人人都需要做鈣化掃描：若你已屆中年、尚未服用降膽固醇藥物，但具有心臟病風險因素，就屬於應該接受該項檢測的族群。做這項檢測有沒有壞處呢？布拉哈表示，心臟科醫師界一項合理的擔憂是，有些醫師可能會不當地利用鈣化分數，作為進行支架植入等手術的理由。

6. 日本正加強一連串鄰近中國的島嶼防禦工事。北京意圖併吞台灣的野心——加上其定期以軍艦、戰機、飛彈等各種手段展示武力、圍繞這座自治島嶼——已成為日本的核心安全挑戰。深入了解日本正如何、又在何處加大力度，將戰略重心轉向其西南方向。

今日要聞預告

7. 國防部長皮特·海格塞斯與參謀首長聯席會議主席丹·凱恩上將，將於美東時間上午8點就伊朗衝突舉行記者會。經濟數據：本月「經濟諮商局」消費者信心調查，將顯示能源價格上漲對消費者信心的影響；此外，勞工部將公布2月職缺與勞動力流動調查（JOLTS），標普全球也將公布1月凱斯－席勒房價指數。財報：耐吉、桂格診斷、味好美、Dave & Buster's、Beyond Meat。

數字看新聞

8. 1.9億——全球去年氦氣產量（立方公尺），足以填滿約76,000座奧運規格游泳池。伊朗戰爭正嚴重削減這種氣體的供應，而氦氣正是冷卻AI晶片製造設備、維持核磁共振（MRI）掃描儀運轉不可或缺的資源。

最後花絮

9. 一起大規模「奇巧」（KitKat）巧克力失竊案，意外變成了一次促銷佳話。這是一起震驚社群媒體世界的大膽巧克力竊案：雀巢週末證實，在一批巧克力從義大利中部一間工廠運往波蘭的途中，遭竊賊偷走了413,793條「奇巧」巧克力。該公司表示，這些巧克力棒與運送它們的卡車至今仍下落不明，但這起竊案未造成任何人受傷。不過，這家瑞士公司雖然損失了巧克力，卻在公關層面贏得了一場意外的大勝——多家其他公司也迅速搭上這波迷因熱潮，紛紛跟風造勢。

新聞室之外

10. 評論：SpaceX成功的受益者之一，是查理·厄根，他運用監管套利手法挽救了自己在寬頻業務上一度失利的豪賭。這是一則失敗產業政策的故事，儘管有政府規劃者的介入，結局卻可能出人意料地圓滿。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Sudden Fall of OpenAI’s Next Big Thing
emails.contentEn:
OpenAI’s decision to scrap Sora, its nascent video-generator, reveals the brutal math of the artificial-intelligence era: how to allocate finite computing power. Despite a $1 billion commitment from Disney’s Bob Iger, Sam Altman pulled the plug to conserve AI chips—the industry’s most precious commodity—for a new AI model, code-named Spud. Sora now looks like an expensive strategic miscalculation, one led by key employees at the center of the AI talent war raging across Silicon Valley. The Journal’s Berber Jin and Jessica Toonkel go inside the sudden fall of OpenAI’s most hyped product since ChatGPT.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. President Trump is weighing a military operation to extract nearly 1,000 pounds of uranium from Iran. The U.S. is shooting down cheap Iranian drones with missiles that can cost upward of a million dollars. Follow live coverage of the conflict. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky toured Gulf countries under attack from Iran in search of new, rich allies. In India, criminals have taken digital ploys to a new level—and are looking elsewhere for victims. To lure top AI talent, startups are turning to cold hard cash.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 45569.00 +145.00 (0.32%); S&P 500 Futures 6436.00 +23.75 (0.37%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 23399.00 +70.50 (0.30%). Source: Factset, market data as of 3/30/2026, 5:56:40 AM ET. Utility stocks haven’t shined since the Iran war broke out, but they can still offer safety in this market, writes Jinjoo Lee.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. Private credit’s exposure to the ailing software industry is bigger than advertised. Many private-credit fund managers are playing down their exposure to software as fears spread about threats from AI. A detailed analysis by the WSJ revealed four large funds marketed to individual investors by Apollo Global Management, Ares Management, Blackstone and Blue Owl Capital have more exposure to the software industry than their filings suggest. Investors’ concerns about the industry’s software exposure helped prompt record withdrawals from private-credit funds in the first quarter. Fund managers contend that AI will affect each software company differently and that some will adapt or even benefit, report Jack Pitcher and Matt Wirz.

4. Iran’s wealth is parked on London’s Billionaires’ Row. Several sprawling mansion plots along a residential stretch of North London dubbed Billionaires’ Row make up a chunk of the extensive London property holdings funded by Iranian money that Western officials have linked to the country’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Now frozen by British sanctions, the properties have fallen into disrepair, the overgrown lots a blight on an upscale street lined with manicured gardens and iron gates. But they are nonetheless an illustration of how Iran has been able to move money internationally for years despite Western sanctions, reports Jenny Strasburg.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: What is Artemis II, NASA’s next big mission? The mission to fly astronauts around the moon would be the deepest humans have traveled in space in decades, reports Micah Maidenberg. A: NASA is set to launch the Artemis II mission on April 1. The 10-day trip from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center will carry NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch, alongside Canada’s Jeremy Hansen. The biggest goal for Artemis II: Safely fly the crew on vehicles that have never carried astronauts before. The towering Space Launch System rocket has the job of lofting a vehicle called Orion into space and on its way to the moon. Orion is designed to carry the crew around the moon and back. The astronauts will evaluate how the spacecraft flies, practice emergency procedures and capture images of the far side of the moon for scientific and exploration purposes. They may become the first humans to see parts of the far side of the lunar surface. Assuming it goes well, NASA will march on to Artemis III, scheduled for next year. During that operation, NASA plans to launch Orion with crew members on board and have the ship practice docking with lunar-lander vehicles that Elon Musk’s SpaceX and Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin have been developing.

6. The cost of your coffee has soared—and isn’t going down soon. After commodity coffee prices dipped in recent months, concerns about the Iran war and stepped-up trading in coffee futures markets are driving them up again. A mix of often-hidden factors, from tariffs and crop failures to higher rents and labor costs, is pushing up the cost of doing business for artisanal purveyors. To drill down into why retail coffee prices have risen—and keep going up—WSJ took a deep dive into one roaster’s expenses.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell joins a moderated discussion at a Harvard University economics class at 10:30 a.m. ET, where he could field questions on central-bank independence and interest rates. The Elite Eight round of the women’s March Madness tournament ends, determining the Final Four.

THE NUMBER

8. $7,000 — The estimated amount Diony Elias, 45, and his girlfriend spent to see Bad Bunny in Puerto Rico last summer. The price of concert tickets has been increasing for years, a reflection of both rising touring costs and ravenous demand for the top stars. Now music lovers face another potential financial hurdle: As some stars who used to trek from town to town choose to play multiple times in a smaller number of locations instead, many fans also have to drum up additional money for travel and lodging.

AND FINALLY...

9. Working in America has become so joyless. Here’s why. A malaise is sweeping office life at American companies, which appear to be in a race to find inefficiencies and cut costs. The curtailing of perks, from offsites to travel, is happening against the backdrop of an AI push that employees say seems aimed at squeezing more work out of fewer people. The upshot, many employees say, is that work has been stripped of fun. Middle managers say they’re on the front lines.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: The Democratic Party’s plan to “restore democracy” assumes that the Trump years represent democratic backsliding. The case for this claim is weak.

WSJ | Buy Side: See our guide to wealth management firms that can help you reach your financial goals.
emails.contentZh:
OpenAI決定放棄其新生的影片生成工具Sora，揭露出AI時代一項殘酷的算術題：如何分配有限的運算資源。儘管迪士尼執行長鮑勃·艾格已承諾投入10億美元，山姆·奧特曼仍選擇喊停這項計畫，以便將AI晶片——這個產業最珍貴的資源——留給一款代號「Spud」的新AI模型。如今看來，Sora已成為一次代價高昂的戰略誤判，而主導這項計畫的關鍵員工，正身處這場席捲矽谷的AI人才爭奪戰核心。本報記者貝爾伯·金與潔西卡·頓克爾深入報導，這款自ChatGPT以來OpenAI最受矚目產品，何以突然殞落。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 川普總統正考慮發動一次軍事行動，從伊朗取出近1,000磅的鈾。美國正動用單價可能超過100萬美元的飛彈，擊落造價低廉的伊朗無人機。請關注本報對這場衝突的即時報導。烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基走訪多個遭伊朗攻擊的波斯灣國家，尋求新的富裕盟友。在印度，犯罪分子已將數位詐騙手法升級到新的層次——並開始把目標轉向其他地區的受害者。為吸引頂尖AI人才，各家新創公司紛紛祭出真金白銀。

市場即時動態

2. 道瓊期貨45569.00，漲145.00點（0.32%）；標普500期貨6436.00，漲23.75點（0.37%）；納斯達克100期貨23399.00，漲70.50點（0.30%）。資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年3月30日美東時間上午5:56:40。Jinjoo Lee撰文指出，自伊朗戰爭爆發以來，公用事業類股表現一直不算亮眼，但在當前市場環境下，它們仍可提供一定的避險保障。

搶先讀

3. 私募信貸對陷入困境的軟體產業的曝險程度，遠高於外界所知。隨著外界對AI威脅的憂慮蔓延，許多私募信貸基金經理人都淡化了自身對軟體產業的曝險程度。本報一項詳盡分析發現，阿波羅全球管理、艾瑞斯管理、黑石與藍貓資本（Blue Owl Capital）向散戶投資人推銷的四檔大型基金，其對軟體產業的實際曝險，遠高於其申報文件所顯示的程度。投資人對該產業軟體曝險的憂慮，是促成第一季私募信貸基金出現創紀錄贖回潮的原因之一。傑克·皮徹與麥特·沃爾茲報導指出，基金經理人則辯稱，AI對每家軟體公司的影響各不相同，部分公司甚至可能因此受益或成功轉型。

4. 伊朗的財富，就停泊在倫敦的「億萬富翁大道」上。北倫敦一處住宅區、人稱「億萬富翁大道」的街道上，坐落著數塊佔地廣闊的豪宅地產，這些構成了倫敦龐大房地產版圖的一部分，資金來源正是西方官員認定與伊朗伊斯蘭革命衛隊有關聯的伊朗資金。如今這些房產已因英國制裁而遭凍結，年久失修，雜草叢生的地塊在這條修剪整齊的花園與鐵藝大門林立的高檔街道上顯得格外突兀。珍妮·斯特拉斯堡報導指出，儘管如此，這些房產依然說明了，多年來伊朗是如何在西方制裁下，仍設法將資金轉移至海外。

專家解讀

5. 問：「阿提米絲二號」（Artemis II）是什麼？它是NASA下一項重大任務嗎？麥卡·梅登伯格報導指出，這項將太空人送往繞月飛行的任務，將是人類數十年來最深入太空的一次探索。答：NASA預定於4月1日發射「阿提米絲二號」任務。這趟從佛羅里達州甘迺迪太空中心出發、為期10天的旅程，將搭載NASA太空人瑞德·懷斯曼、維克多·格洛弗與克莉絲蒂娜·科克，以及加拿大太空人傑瑞米·漢森。「阿提米絲二號」的最大目標，是要安全地讓機組人員搭乘從未載過太空人的載具飛行。高聳的「太空發射系統」（SLS）火箭，負責將一艘名為「獵戶座」（Orion）的太空船送入太空、飛向月球，而獵戶座則設計用來搭載太空人繞月飛行後再返回地球。太空人將評估太空船的飛行表現，演練緊急應變程序，並拍攝月球背面影像以供科學與探索用途——他們有可能成為首批目睹部分月球背面地貌的人類。若一切順利，NASA將接續推進預定明年執行的「阿提米絲三號」任務。屆時，NASA計劃讓載有機組人員的獵戶座太空船升空，並讓太空船與伊隆·馬斯克的SpaceX及傑夫·貝佐斯的藍色起源公司分別研發中的登月載具進行對接演練。

6. 你的咖啡價格已大幅上漲——而且短期內不會回落。近幾個月大宗商品咖啡價格曾一度回落，但如今隨著市場對伊朗戰爭的憂慮加劇，加上咖啡期貨市場交易更加活躍，價格再度攀升。從關稅、農作物歉收，到租金與人力成本上漲，一連串往往不為人所察覺的因素，正推高手工咖啡業者的經營成本。為深入探討零售咖啡價格為何持續上漲，本報深入剖析了一家烘豆商的成本結構。

今日要聞預告

7. 聯準會主席鮑爾將於美東時間上午10:30參加哈佛大學經濟學課堂的一場主持對談，屆時可能會被問及央行獨立性與利率相關問題。女子「三月瘋狂」錦標賽的「精英八強」賽事將決出四強名單。

數字看新聞

8. 7,000美元——45歲的迪奧尼·埃利亞斯與其女友去年夏天在波多黎各觀看「壞痞兔」（Bad Bunny）演唱會的預估花費。多年來演唱會票價持續攀升，反映出巡演成本上升與頂級明星一票難求的雙重因素。如今樂迷還面臨另一項潛在的財務難關：由於部分過去會巡迴各地演出的明星，如今選擇改在較少的城市多次加演，許多粉絲因此還得額外籌措交通與住宿費用。

最後花絮

9. 在美國上班已變得如此了無生趣，原因如下。一股低迷情緒正席捲美國企業的辦公室文化，各公司似乎都在競相尋找效率不彰之處、削減成本。從團隊出遊到差旅，各項員工福利正被大幅刪減，背後正值一波AI推動熱潮——員工們表示，這波熱潮的目的似乎是要用更少的人力榨取更多的工作產出。許多員工表示，最終結果就是工作已被抽乾了樂趣，而中階主管們則表示，他們正首當其衝站在第一線。

新聞室之外

10. 評論：民主黨「恢復民主」的計畫，其前提假設是川普執政時期代表著民主的倒退。但這項說法的論據其實相當薄弱。
