emails.subject: The 10-Point: A First Lady’s Alleged Crime Dynasty
emails.contentEn:
She was Venezuela’s first lady—and an alleged crime lord in her own right. Cilia Flores, who has declared her innocence, stands accused of conspiring with officials to smuggle hundreds of tons of cocaine into the U.S. During her husband Nicolás Maduro’s 13-year grip on power, she cultivated a family criminal enterprise known in Venezuela as “El Jardín de Flores,” or the Garden of Flowers—a play on her surname. While Maduro oversaw the country’s economic collapse, Flores’s network flourished, with her family’s patronage system woven through Venezuela’s criminal economy.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. America’s 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit arrived in the Middle East, giving President Trump more options, while Iran suffered one of the war's worst days for civilian deaths. Follow our live coverage of the war. Pakistan, once isolated by Washington for harboring Osama bin Laden, is assuming a surprisingly prominent position in the effort to push the U.S. and Iran toward talks. Investigators searched the office of a FEMA contractor as they investigate a network of aides former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem and adviser Corey Lewandowski seeded throughout the department during their turbulent tenure. Trump’s relationship with the Supreme Court risks getting even worse as the justices prepare to consider the president’s push to end birthright citizenship.

FROM THE MARKETS

2. The worst rout in Treasurys since April’s tariff chaos is a stark demonstration of how war’s disruptions to oil flows are leaving investors with few places to shelter. Stocks haven’t fallen as much as you might expect given the Iran war, and there are several good reasons for that, writes James Mackintosh. Officially, Federal Reserve policymakers are still projecting interest-rate cuts later this year, but the most probable path may be no move at all.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. The Venezuelan first lady’s other job: tending a family crime dynasty. When DEA agents flew Nicolás Maduro to New York to face narcoterrorism charges, beside him was his wife, Cilia Flores. Pursued for years by the Drug Enforcement Administration, Flores was an alleged crime lord in her own right. A federal indictment unsealed the day U.S. commandos pulled Flores and Maduro from Caracas accused her of conspiring with Venezuelan officials to smuggle cocaine into the U.S., accepting bribes to allow drug-trafficking flights and ordering murders over unpaid debts. According to court records and former associates, she rewarded a web of relatives with drug routes, state contracts and impunity, report Angus Berwick and Juan Forero. In a January appearance in federal court, Flores pleaded not guilty and said she was “completely innocent.”

4. Is another financial crisis lurking in private credit? For some, news that certain private-credit funds have capped withdrawals recalls the summer of 2007, when a European bank limited withdrawals from funds stuffed with securities linked to subprime mortgages. The global financial crisis had begun. Like subprime, private credit in just a few decades went from niche to major asset class. And like subprime, private credit is opaque, mostly unregulated and connected to other parts of the financial system. So do private credit’s troubles herald a systemic shock similar to what we saw two decades ago? Probably not, writes Greg Ip—with the caveat that crises are inherently unpredictable.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: Apple says it’s fixing the iPhone’s autocorrect feature. Do the new updates work? Users have complained about autocorrect for years. Personal tech columnist Nicole Nguyen wrote about what iOS 26.4 does to improve your typing—and offers tips to help you reclaim your keyboard. A: I was worried my fine motor skills were failing. Over the past few years, my texts have become rife with mangled words and strange punctuation. When did I become such a terrible iPhone typist? Apparently, I wasn’t the only one. I’ve heard from countless readers, especially within the past year, complaining about typos. Lots and lots of typos. Then, in Apple’s latest software iOS 26.4, an update made me think the errors weren’t totally our fault: “Improved keyboard accuracy when typing quickly.” Finally! After years of glaring typing issues, Apple is acknowledging there was a problem. But does iOS 26.4 really offer a fix? I put the new update to the test, and I have good and bad news: The improvement is real, but it only fixes some of our autocorrect woes. The iPhone running 26.4 produced fewer errors, but only marginally. The new update still produced some single-word mess-ups, while the older software had more gibberish phrases. Both devices got most words right.

6. Hear the voices of five people whose lives were caught up in the Middle East conflict. The war in the Middle East has spread to more than a dozen countries, upending lives and sending the global economy into a tailspin. These are the voices of civilians whose lives are directly entwined in the conflict, including a pregnant 39-year-old woman in Tehran who lies awake at night amid the sound of explosions from Israeli bombardment and a 64-year-old woman in Beit Shemesh, Israel, who survived an Iranian missile strike that destroyed her house.

HAPPENING THIS WEEK

7. Monday: Pakistan hosts talks aimed at finding ways to end the war. The Elite Eight round of the women’s March Madness tournament ends, determining the Final Four. Tuesday: The Conference Board’s consumer confidence survey for March will offer signs of how rising energy prices are impacting consumer sentiment. In men's soccer, playoffs will determine the last six teams to qualify for this year's World Cup. Wednesday: The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on Trump's executive order seeking to end birthright citizenship. Friday: Jobs data for March will provide a snapshot of the health of the labor market just as energy prices rise sharply due to war in the Middle East. Stock markets will be closed for Good Friday.

THE NUMBER

8. 21% — How much average tax refunds have increased from 2025 in California so far this tax season, according to an analysis by Navy Federal Credit Union of member deposits, compared with an average of 11% nationally among the credit union’s members. After last year’s tax law raised the cap for the deduction of state and local taxes to $40,000 from $10,000, refunds have been growing faster than the national average for people in some higher-tax states, such as California, New York, Virginia and Maryland.

AND FINALLY...

9. People are snapping up Japanese houses that locals won’t touch. A growing number of foreigners are buying up the country’s akiya, translated as empty or vacant homes. There are over nine million of these properties, which remain unpopular among locals. Some towns have even tried giving them away. But to foreigners undaunted by a fixer-upper, buying an akiya is a chance to own something permanent in Japan. Against the weak yen, many of them can be relatively affordable.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. WSJ | Buy Side: Progressive, Travelers and Geico are among the top car insurance companies in our extensive analysis.

她曾是委內瑞拉的第一夫人——同時也被指控是一名犯罪集團首腦。西莉亞·佛羅雷斯已聲明自己清白，但仍被控與官員合謀，將數百噸古柯鹼走私進美國。在她的丈夫尼可拉斯·馬杜洛執政的13年裡，她一手打造了一個在委內瑞拉被稱為「佛羅雷斯花園」（El Jardín de Flores，取自她姓氏「Flores」的雙關語）的家族犯罪王國。當馬杜洛主政期間國家經濟陷入崩潰之際，佛羅雷斯的關係網卻蓬勃發展，她的家族靠著一套恩庇體系，將勢力滲透進委內瑞拉的地下犯罪經濟之中。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 美軍第31陸戰遠征隊已抵達中東，為川普總統提供了更多選項，而伊朗當天也遭遇了這場戰爭中平民死傷最慘重的一日之一。請關注本報即時報導。曾因窩藏奧薩瑪·賓·拉登而遭華盛頓孤立的巴基斯坦，如今在推動美伊展開對話的努力中，意外扮演起舉足輕重的角色。調查人員搜查了一名聯邦緊急事務管理署（FEMA）承包商的辦公室，展開對前國土安全部部長克莉絲蒂·諾姆與顧問科里·萊萬多夫斯基在其動盪任期內，於該部門內部安插的一整套幕僚人脈網絡的調查。隨著最高法院大法官們準備審理川普推動終結「出生公民權」的訴求，川普與最高法院之間的關係恐將進一步惡化。

市場動態

2. 美國公債遭遇自四月關稅動盪以來最慘烈的一波拋售，鮮明地反映出戰爭對石油運輸造成的衝擊，正讓投資人幾乎無處可以避險。詹姆斯·麥金塔許撰文指出，儘管爆發伊朗戰爭，但美股跌幅並未如外界預期般劇烈，箇中有幾個充分的理由。聯準會官員目前官方立場仍預測今年稍晚將會降息，但最可能的走向，恐怕會是按兵不動。

搶先讀

3. 這位委內瑞拉第一夫人的另一份「工作」：打理一個家族犯罪王朝。當美國緝毒局（DEA）人員將尼可拉斯·馬杜洛押上飛機、送往紐約應訊毒品恐怖主義相關罪名時，坐在他身旁的正是他的妻子西莉亞·佛羅雷斯。多年來一直遭緝毒局追查的佛羅雷斯，本身也被控是一名犯罪集團首腦。就在美軍突擊隊將佛羅雷斯與馬杜洛從卡拉卡斯帶走的當天，一份公開的聯邦起訴書指控她與委內瑞拉官員合謀，將古柯鹼走私進美國，收受賄賂放行毒品運輸航班，並曾因欠債糾紛下令殺人。安格斯·柏維克與胡安·佛雷羅報導指出，根據法庭紀錄及前同夥的說法，她讓一整張親族關係網分別坐享毒品運輸路線、政府合約與司法豁免權作為回報。今年一月出庭聯邦法院時，佛羅雷斯否認全部罪名，並表示自己「完全清白」。

4. 私募信貸領域是否正潛藏著下一場金融危機？對某些人來說，部分私募信貸基金限制贖回的消息，讓人聯想起2007年夏天——當時一家歐洲銀行限制投資人從一批持有次級房貸相關證券的基金中提款，全球金融危機自此揭開序幕。與次級房貸類似，私募信貸也是在短短數十年間，從一個小眾領域搖身變成主要資產類別。而且與次級房貸一樣，私募信貸同樣不透明、大多不受監管，且與金融體系其他環節緊密相連。那麼，私募信貸目前的困境，是否預示著一場類似二十年前那場系統性衝擊即將重演？葛雷格·伊普撰文指出，可能性不大——但他也提醒，危機本質上難以預測。

專家解讀

5. 問：蘋果表示正在修復iPhone的自動校正功能，新的更新真的有效嗎？多年來，用戶始終對自動校正功能怨聲載道。個人科技專欄作家阮妮可撰文，介紹iOS 26.4版本對打字體驗的改進，並提供幾項訣竅，助你奪回鍵盤的主控權。答：我原本擔心自己的手部精細動作能力正在退化。過去幾年，我的簡訊訊息裡充斥著錯字連篇與奇怪的標點符號。我究竟是從何時開始，變成了一個如此糟糕的iPhone打字者？看來我並非唯一一人。無數讀者——尤其在過去這一年裡——都曾向我抱怨打字錯誤的問題，而且錯誤還不少。後來，在蘋果最新的iOS 26.4系統更新說明中，有一條讓我開始懷疑，這些錯誤或許並非全然是我們自己的問題：「加快打字速度時，鍵盤準確度已獲改善。」總算等到了！在多年來明顯的打字問題之後，蘋果終於承認這確實是個問題。但iOS 26.4真的解決問題了嗎？我親自測試了這項新更新，好消息和壞消息都有：改善確實存在，但只解決了部分自動校正的困擾。搭載26.4版本的iPhone確實出錯較少，但幅度並不大。新版本仍會出現一些單字打錯的情況，而舊版系統則更容易出現整段語無倫次的文字。不過，兩款系統打對大多數文字都沒有問題。

6. 聆聽五位親身捲入中東衝突者的心聲。這場中東戰爭已蔓延至十多個國家，顛覆了無數人的生活，也讓全球經濟陷入動盪。以下是幾位生活直接被這場衝突牽動的平民的心聲，包括一名39歲、身懷六甲的德黑蘭女子，她夜裡常在以色列轟炸的爆炸聲中無法入眠；以及一名64歲的以色列貝特謝梅什女子，她在一次伊朗飛彈攻擊摧毀自家房屋後倖存下來。

本週看點

7. 週一：巴基斯坦主辦旨在尋求結束戰爭途徑的會談。女子「三月瘋狂」錦標賽的「精英八強」賽事將決出四強名單。週二：本月「經濟諮商局」消費者信心調查，將顯示能源價格上漲對消費者信心的影響。男子足球方面，附加賽將決出今年世界盃最後六個晉級名額。週三：最高法院將就川普尋求終結出生公民權的行政命令舉行口頭辯論。週五：3月就業數據將呈現就業市場的健康狀況，恰逢中東戰事導致能源價格急遽攀升之際。當日股市因耶穌受難日休市。

數字看新聞

8. 21%——根據海軍聯邦信用合作社（Navy Federal Credit Union）對會員存款的分析，本報稅季迄今，加州的平均退稅金額較2025年成長的幅度，相較之下，該信用合作社會員的全國平均成長幅度僅為11%。自去年稅法將州及地方稅扣除額上限從1萬美元提高至4萬美元後，加州、紐約、維吉尼亞與馬里蘭等高稅率州居民的退稅成長速度，已快於全國平均水準。

最後花絮

9. 人們正搶購連日本當地人都不願意碰的房子。越來越多外國人正大舉收購日本的「空き家」（akiya），意即空屋或閒置住宅。這類房產在全國超過900萬戶，在當地人眼中始終乏人問津，甚至有些城鎮曾嘗試免費贈送。但對不畏懼親自動手翻修的外國人而言，購買一間空屋，正是一個能在日本永久擁有一份資產的機會。在日圓疲軟的背景下，許多這類房產的價格也顯得相對親民。

新聞室之外

10. 《華爾街日報》｜Buy Side：Progressive、Travelers與Geico，是我們深入分析後評選出的頂尖汽車保險公司之一。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Wall Street’s Iran Alarm
emails.contentEn:
How long will the Iran war last? Yesterday we got mixed signals. As the Pentagon weighed sending thousands more troops to the Middle East and Israel began to ration its best high-end missile interceptors, President Trump continued posting on social-media about potential off-ramps. Wall Street, meanwhile, was trading like the worst pain from the war is yet to come.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. Yemen’s Houthis launched a missile at Israel, their first attack in the fast-expanding war. Twelve U.S. troops were wounded in an Iranian strike on a base in Saudi Arabia. Follow our live coverage here. Israel is rationing its best missile interceptors as the war drags on—and Iran’s ballistic missiles are getting through. With Trump considering sending another 10,000 ground troops to the Middle East, this is what the influx of forces could do. Trump signed an executive order to pay TSA workers, bypassing a gridlocked Congress after the latest proposal to fund the broader DHS failed. ICE plans to spend $38.3 billion on a new detention model that includes acquiring warehouses and converting them into detention centers. Mark Lanier, the veteran plaintiff’s lawyer from Texas who beat Meta and Google in a recent social-media addiction case, moonlights as a preacher—and it shows.

FROM THE MARKETS

2. All three major stock indexes fell for a fourth-straight week, notching their worst percentage declines since April’s tariff turmoil. The market dive points to Wall Street’s growing alarm over the Iran war, which comes despite reassurances from Trump. In charts: See how Trump’s tariffs are choking trade between the U.S. and China.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. A decadelong feud is reshaping the future of AI. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has built the company’s public brand around the idea that its approach to AI is fundamentally safer than that of its rivals, particularly OpenAI, which he left in late 2020 over concerns about safety. But the reasons for Amodei’s departure also include personal wounds that have never healed, including those from his long-running rivalry with OpenAI chief Sam Altman. Now, as both companies hurtle toward an IPO, the philosophical and personal differences between their leaders have metastasized—and they are defining how the world encounters the technology, reports Keach Hagey.

4. What this year’s CPAC tells us about the Republican divide on Iran. Trump’s decision to go to war loomed over the annual Conservative Political Action Conference. The confab has often served as a sort of MAGA pep rally, with near universal support for Trump and his agenda. But this year the conference laid bare the rift among Trump’s MAGA base over the Middle East conflict, reports Sabrina Rodriguez. “What happened to America First? Why aren’t we paying attention to what’s going on here?” said 22-year-old attendee Maxwell Eckhardt. Still, many prominent speakers showered Trump with praise. And even when they expressed skepticism on Iran, many called for unity against Democrats in the midterms.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: When will airport security lines go back to normal? Trump’s executive order means Transportation Security Administration workers can be paid again. But it will be days—or longer—before U.S. air travel fully recovers, writes reporter Joseph Pisani. A: Some TSA agents could start getting paid as early as Monday, according to the Department of Homeland Security. However, tens of thousands of agents just missed their second paycheck in a row. Security lines improving depends on whether TSA agents who have been calling out start showing up to work again before their back pay arrives. What’s more, airports are also absorbing a crush of travelers during this spring break season. Travel demand was projected to be 4% higher than last year, with an average of 2.8 million passengers a day expected to fly between March 1 and April 30, according to a forecast from Airlines for America, the trade association for big airlines. Travelers should check social-media accounts of airports for wait times, but expect longer lines during the morning, when people are trying to get on early flights. Several airports say their busiest times are before 7 a.m. Lines can start getting longer again between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m., when business travelers head to the airport after work.

6. Will this “miracle” battery finally change your mind about EVs? Donut Lab, a Finnish startup, claims to have created the first production-ready solid-state battery for the EV industry. It’s fair to say the entire car-making world is deeply skeptical: How did an obscure startup beat Toyota, Stellantis and the entire nation of China to the holy grail of energy storage? But whether Donut’s hype is to be believed or not, solid-state technology is coming—and it’s a potential disrupter for the entire EV business, writes Dan Neil.

HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

7. Saturday: Demonstrators are expected to protest against Trump at “No Kings” rallies across the U.S. Sunday: The Elite Eight round of the men’s March Madness tournament concludes, determining the Final Four. In the women’s tournament, the Elite Eight round begins.

THE NUMBER

8. No. 20 — The spot on Billboard’s Hot R&B Songs chart that the AI-generated song “How Was I Supposed to Know?” by AI avatar Xania Monet reached last year. The song was made using Suno, an AI music-generator platform. The popularity of the platform has catapulted Suno’s 39-year-old CEO, Mikey Shulman, into the music industry’s elite—and made him enemy number one in some circles.

AND FINALLY...

9. Here’s a last-minute traveler’s guide to this summer’s biggest events. Did you jump on presale tickets to the World Cup quarterfinals months ago? Are you catching the August eclipse from an expedition cruise in the Arctic? We’re happy for you. Fortunately, there’s still fun to be had for procrastinators. Here’s what you’ve already missed, what’s still on the table—and some curveball alternatives.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: Even after the pandemic, high-tax states continue to lose tens of billions of dollars in taxable income to low-tax states.

WSJ | Buy Side: Don’t miss these Amazon deals to keep your phone, tablet or laptop going all day and beyond.

伊朗戰爭究竟還會持續多久？昨日傳出的訊號好壞參半：五角大廈正考慮向中東增派數千名部隊，以色列則開始限量配給其最頂級的高階飛彈攔截系統，而川普總統仍持續在社群媒體上發文，暗示可能的退場方案。與此同時，華爾街的交易走勢，卻彷彿在預告這場戰爭最痛苦的部分尚未到來。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 葉門胡塞武裝向以色列發射一枚飛彈，這是他們在這場迅速擴大的戰爭中的首次攻擊行動。伊朗對沙烏地阿拉伯一處基地的打擊，造成12名美軍受傷。請關注本報即時報導。隨著戰事持續拖延，以色列正限量配給其最頂級的飛彈攔截系統——而伊朗的彈道飛彈正逐漸突破防線。隨著川普考慮再向中東增派1萬名地面部隊，本文解析這波增兵可能帶來的影響。在最新一項為國土安全部整體提供撥款的方案宣告失敗後，川普簽署行政命令，繞過陷入僵局的國會，直接向TSA員工發放薪資。ICE計劃投入383億美元打造一套新的拘留模式，其中包括收購倉庫並改建為拘留中心。曾在近期一宗社群媒體成癮訴訟中擊敗Meta與Google的德州資深原告律師馬克·拉尼爾，私底下還兼職擔任牧師——而這一點在他身上表露無遺。

市場動態

2. 美股三大指數連續第四週下跌，創下自四月關稅動盪以來最差的單週跌幅百分比。這波市場重挫，反映出華爾街對伊朗戰爭的憂慮情緒正日益升高，儘管川普一再出言安撫。圖表看新聞：了解川普的關稅政策如何持續扼殺中美貿易。

搶先讀

3. 一場延續十年的恩怨，正在重塑AI產業的未來。Anthropic執行長達里奧·阿莫代伊，一直圍繞著「本公司的AI開發方式遠比對手——尤其是OpenAI——更安全」這項理念，打造公司的對外形象。他正是在2020年底因安全顧慮而離開OpenAI的。但阿莫代伊當初離職的原因，其實還摻雜著從未癒合的個人恩怨，包括他與OpenAI執行長山姆·奧特曼之間長期的競爭關係。如今，隨著兩家公司都朝著首次公開發行（IPO）疾速邁進，兩位領導人之間在理念與私人層面的分歧已進一步擴大——而這些分歧，正在形塑全世界接觸這項技術的方式，凱奇·哈吉報導。

4. 今年的保守派政治行動大會（CPAC），透露出共和黨在伊朗議題上的分歧。川普開戰的決定，為這場一年一度的保守派政治行動大會蒙上陰影。這場大會過去往往扮演著某種「MAGA打氣大會」的角色，與會者幾乎一致支持川普及其施政議程。但薩布麗娜·羅德里格斯報導指出，今年的大會卻暴露出川普的MAGA基本盤在中東衝突議題上的裂痕。22歲與會者馬克斯韋爾·埃克哈特表示：「『美國優先』的精神到哪去了？我們為什麼不關注這裡正在發生的事？」不過，仍有許多重量級講者對川普讚譽有加，即便他們對伊朗議題表達疑慮，多數人也呼籲在期中選舉中團結一致對抗民主黨。

專家解讀

5. 問：機場安檢隊伍何時能恢復正常？記者約瑟夫·皮薩尼撰文指出，川普的行政命令意味著運輸安全管理局（TSA）員工可以重新獲得薪資，但美國航空旅行要完全恢復正常，恐怕還需要數天，甚至更久。答：據國土安全部表示，部分TSA人員最快週一就能開始領到薪資。然而，數萬名工作人員此前已連續兩次錯過發薪日。安檢隊伍能否改善，取決於此前請假不上班的TSA人員，是否會在補發薪資到位之前就重新回崗上班。此外，機場眼下也正承受春假旅遊旺季帶來的龐大人潮：據代表各大航空公司的貿易協會「美國航空公司協會」預測，今年的旅遊需求預計較去年高出4%，3月1日至4月30日期間，平均每日將有280萬名乘客搭機出行。旅客應留意各機場社群媒體帳號公布的等候時間，但要有心理準備，上午時段——當旅客急著趕搭早班機時——排隊人潮會更長。多家機場表示，最繁忙的時段是清晨7點之前；下午4點至晚上8點之間，隨著商務旅客下班後趕赴機場，排隊人潮也可能再度變長。

6. 這款「神奇」電池，能徹底扭轉你對電動車的看法嗎？芬蘭新創公司Donut Lab聲稱，已為電動車產業打造出首款可量產的固態電池。整個汽車製造業對此深表懷疑，這也不難理解：一家名不見經傳的新創公司，究竟是如何在這場儲能技術「聖杯」的競賽中，擊敗豐田、Stellantis乃至整個中國的？但無論Donut的宣稱是否可信，固態電池技術終將到來——丹·尼爾撰文指出，它有可能顛覆整個電動車產業。

本週末看點

7. 週六：預料將有示威者在美國各地舉行「沒有國王」（No Kings）集會，抗議川普。週日：男子「三月瘋狂」錦標賽的「精英八強」賽事將決出四強名單；女子錦標賽的「精英八強」賽事同時展開。

數字看新聞

8. 第20名——AI虛擬歌手Xania Monet演唱的AI生成歌曲《How Was I Supposed to Know?》去年在《告示牌》熱門節奏藍調單曲榜上創下的最高名次。這首歌是使用AI音樂生成平台Suno製作而成。這個平台的爆紅，已將現年39歲的Suno執行長麥基·舒曼推上音樂產業精英之列——同時也讓他在部分圈子裡成了頭號公敵。

最後花絮

9. 這是一份給拖延症患者的今夏重大活動最後衝刺指南。你是否幾個月前就搶購了世界盃八強賽事的預售票？是否正搭乘北極探險郵輪，準備欣賞8月的日食奇觀？若是如此，恭喜你。不過，對於愛拖延的人來說，仍有不少樂子可尋——以下整理了你已經錯過的機會、還來得及把握的選項，以及幾個出人意料的替代方案。

新聞室之外

10. 評論：即便在疫情之後，高稅率州仍持續流失數百億美元的應稅所得，轉向低稅率州。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Musk Plans a Record-Breaking SpaceX IPO
emails.contentEn:
Elon Musk is cooking up a memorable stock-market debut for SpaceX, and not just because it’s expected to be the biggest one ever. The billionaire is writing his own playbook—from investor visits to how shares are allocated—for the blockbuster initial public offering, which is being timed for mid-June before his 55th birthday. SpaceX is expected to file confidentially with regulators for its IPO in the coming days, report the Journal’s Corrie Driebusch and Alexander Saeedy. Musk and his team are betting on massive orders for the IPO, which is expected to raise between $40 billion and $80 billion.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. The Pentagon is considering sending up to 10,000 additional ground troops to the Middle East even as President Trump weighs peace talks with Iran. Follow our live coverage here. The U.S. and Israel have pounded—but not eliminated—Iran’s missile threat. Senators passed funding for most of Homeland Security, moving to end the TSA staffing shortage. They excluded funding for immigration enforcement. A federal judge halted the Trump administration’s designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk. Steve Cahillane, the CEO of Kraft Heinz who has twice broken up companies, now takes on the surprise challenge of keeping one together.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 46150.00 -80.00 (0.17%); S&P 500 Futures 6518.00 -7.00 (0.11%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 23750.75 -43.50 (0.18%). Source: Factset, market data as of 3/27/2026, 6:00:18 AM ET. In charts: See how the Iran war compares with past market shocks. The private-credit industry is facing a dual dilemma as surging withdrawals collide with a fundraising slowdown. Investors were right to be wary of Blue Owl’s $1.4 billion deal, writes Jonathan Weil. Here’s why.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. An AI upheaval is coming for the media. This journalist is already all in. Nick Lichtenberg produced more stories in six months than any of his colleagues at Fortune delivered in a year. One Wednesday in February, he cranked out seven. His work involves what some view as the third rail of journalism: artificial intelligence playing a leading role not just in researching, but in writing stories. AI-assisted stories accounted for nearly 20% of Fortune’s web traffic in the second half of 2025. Most were written by Lichtenberg. The 42-year-old, who has penned more than 600 stories since rejoining Fortune in July, may be a bellwether for where much of the media business is headed, reports Isabella Simonetti.

4. Meet the European leader who says no to Trump. For the past year, most of Europe has walked on eggshells with Trump. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has been trialing an alternative tactic: the “Just Say No” theory of Trump diplomacy. He is betting the Western alliance will be healthier if America’s allies candidly air their disagreements with the president, rather than tiptoe around him. Spain, rarely the center of gravity in European affairs, has become the standard-bearer for Europeans frustrated at the continent’s fear of standing up to a U.S. president. Trump’s threats on Greenland and the unpopularity of the Iran war with voters have brought more Europeans around to his position, report Drew Hinshaw, Marcus Walker and Gordon Fairclough. (Video: In an interview, Sánchez said that alignment with the U.S. over Iran is a "mistake," arguing for a more autonomous Europe.)

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: What’s next for the weight-loss drug market? The market for weight-loss drugs is exploding and patients may have several new options in coming years, reports Peter Loftus. A: The obesity-drug market has long been dominated by two shots, Wegovy and Zepbound, and their diabetes versions, Ozempic and Mounjaro. That is about to change. Pills have just started to enter the market, and drugmakers are racing to develop next-generation medications in hopes of helping people lose even more weight with fewer side effects. Some of the drugs in development are designed to be taken less often than those already out there. A once-daily pill from Eli Lilly could get approved as soon as April, while a weekly shot from Novo Nordisk could get approved by the end of 2026. Then there are more weekly and monthly weight-loss shots in development from companies like Pfizer and Amgen. These experimental drugs might help people lose weight so quickly that they will be marketed for more severe forms of obesity. Other, less powerful drugs might end up being “maintenance” medications for people after they have already lost a substantial amount of weight. Any number of these drugs might be used in combinations.

6. Après-ski, minus the crowds? These homeowners built their own bars. For alpine-sports lovers, warming up with a few drinks after a day on the slopes is a time-honored tradition. But instead of heading to a crowded bar for cocktails, more and more wealthy homeowners are hosting friends at private bar areas with high-end, mountain-inspired finishes, real-estate agents say. These cozy areas become additional focal points within the house, like a fireplace or a wine room. They have features like specialty ice makers, open wine-storage columns and dramatic finishes.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. Trump is scheduled to speak at the FII Priority Summit at 5:30 p.m. ET. G-7 foreign ministers are meeting in France. The U.N. Security Council is scheduled to hold a closed-door meeting Friday on the Middle East. Economic data: The University of Michigan will release its final consumer-sentiment figures for March at 10 a.m. ET. Earnings: Carnival.

THE NUMBER

8. 6.38% — The average rate for a 30-year fixed mortgage this week, up from 6.22% last week, according to Freddie Mac. It is the fourth consecutive week rates have climbed, taking them to the highest level since September. The timing couldn’t be worse for the housing market, which has been stuck in a low gear for three years due to high home prices and elevated rates. March typically marks the start of the busiest stretch of the year for home sales.

AND FINALLY...

9. Is doomscrolling giving you wrinkles? You may have “tech neck.” Technology has been the alleged culprit behind everything from spiraling anxiety to vanishing attention spans to social isolation. Now, it has something else on its charge sheet: Wrinkles. Behold “tech neck,” a name for those lines that develop across your neck with age and apparently worsen with incessant smartphone use. Anxiety about the affliction is spreading, and the race for a cure is on. The beauty industry is offering up a bevy of solutions, including futuristic-looking LED red-light collars.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: From its dire position, the Iranian regime has been offered a cease-fire that reportedly includes the removal of all sanctions. By scorning this offer, as Iranian officials now suggest, the regime makes the case for Trump to give the war more time and see the mission through.

emails.contentZh:
伊隆·馬斯克正在為SpaceX精心策劃一場令人難忘的股市首秀，不僅僅是因為這預料將是史上規模最大的一次首次公開發行（IPO）。這位億萬富翁正親自操刀撰寫自己的一套玩法——從邀請投資人參訪，到股份分配方式無一例外——這場備受矚目的IPO預計選定在6月中旬、他55歲生日前完成。本報記者科莉·德里布施與亞歷山大·賽伊迪報導，SpaceX預計將於近日向監管機構秘密提交IPO申請。馬斯克與其團隊正押注這場預計募資400億至800億美元的IPO將迎來巨額認購。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 即便川普總統正權衡與伊朗展開和談，五角大廈仍在考慮向中東再增派最多1萬名地面部隊。請關注本報即時報導。美國與以色列已重創——但尚未徹底消除——伊朗的飛彈威脅。參議員通過了國土安全部大部分部門的撥款法案，著手解決TSA的人力短缺問題，但將移民執法部門的撥款排除在外。一名聯邦法官已暫緩川普政府將Anthropic列為「供應鏈風險」的認定。兩度拆分公司的卡夫亨氏執行長史蒂夫·卡希拉尼，如今卻意外面臨截然相反的挑戰：讓公司維持完整。

市場即時動態

2. 道瓊期貨46150.00，跌80.00點（0.17%）；標普500期貨6518.00，跌7.00點（0.11%）；納斯達克100期貨23750.75，跌43.50點（0.18%）。資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年3月27日美東時間上午6:00:18。圖表看新聞：了解伊朗戰爭與過去市場震盪事件的比較。私募信貸產業正面臨雙重困境：贖回潮激增，同時募資速度放緩。喬納森·韋爾撰文指出，投資人此前對藍貓資本（Blue Owl）14億美元交易案抱持的疑慮確有道理，並解釋箇中原因。

搶先讀

3. 一場AI變革即將席捲媒體業，這名記者早已全力擁抱這股潮流。尼克·利希滕伯格六個月內產出的報導數量，超過《財富》雜誌其他同事一整年的產量。二月的某個週三，他一口氣完成了七篇報導。他的工作涉及部分人眼中新聞業的「高壓電線」議題：人工智慧不僅參與資料研究，更在撰稿環節扮演主導角色。2025年下半年，AI輔助撰寫的報導占《財富》網站流量近兩成，其中大多數出自利希滕伯格之手。這位42歲的記者自去年7月重返《財富》以來，已撰寫超過600篇報導，或許正預示著媒體行業未來的走向，伊莎貝拉·西蒙內蒂報導。

4. 認識這位敢對川普說不的歐洲領導人。過去一年裡，歐洲大多數國家對川普都是戰戰兢兢、如履薄冰。西班牙首相佩德羅·桑切斯則一直在嘗試另一套戰術：一套可稱為「直接說不」的對川普外交理論。他押注的是，若美國的盟友能坦率地表達與這位總統的分歧，而非小心翼翼地迴避衝突，西方聯盟反而會更加健康。素來鮮少成為歐洲事務重心的西班牙，如今已成為那些不滿歐洲大陸畏於挺身對抗美國總統的歐洲人的旗手。德魯·欣肖、馬庫斯·沃克與戈登·費爾克拉夫報導指出，川普對格陵蘭的威脅言論，以及伊朗戰爭在選民間的不受歡迎，已讓更多歐洲人轉而認同桑切斯的立場。（影片：在一次專訪中，桑切斯表示，在伊朗問題上與美國保持一致是一項「錯誤」，並主張歐洲應更加自主。）

專家解讀

5. 問：減重藥物市場接下來會如何發展？彼得·洛夫圖斯報導指出，減重藥物市場正呈爆炸性成長，未來幾年患者可能會有多款新選擇。答：肥胖症用藥市場長期以來一直由兩款注射劑——Wegovy與Zepbound，以及它們的糖尿病版本Ozempic與Mounjaro——所主導。但這種局面即將改變。口服藥丸剛開始進入市場，各藥廠正競相開發下一代藥物，希望能幫助患者在副作用更少的情況下減去更多體重。部分正在開發的藥物，設計為服用頻率低於現有藥物。禮來一款每日一次的口服藥最快可望於4月獲批，諾和諾德一款每週一次的注射劑則可能在2026年底前獲批。此外，輝瑞、安進等公司也在開發更多每週或每月施打一次的減重注射劑。這些實驗性藥物或許能讓患者以極快速度減重，因此未來可能主要針對更嚴重的肥胖症患者。而其他藥效較溫和的藥物，則可能最終成為患者已大幅減重後用於「維持體重」的藥物。這些藥物中的多款，未來也可能會被搭配組合使用。

6. 滑雪後小酌，卻不想人擠人？這些屋主乾脆自己蓋起了酒吧。對熱愛高山運動的人來說，滑完一天雪後小酌幾杯暖暖身子，是一項歷史悠久的傳統。但房仲業者表示，如今越來越多富裕屋主不再前往人潮擁擠的酒吧調酒小酌，而是選擇在自家打造的私人酒吧區招待朋友，這些空間往往採用高端、充滿山居風情的裝潢。這些溫馨角落已成為住宅內的另一個焦點空間，地位堪比壁爐或酒窖，並配備特製製冰機、開放式酒藏展示柱，以及極具視覺張力的裝潢細節。

今日要聞預告

7. 川普預計於美東時間下午5:30在「未來投資倡議」（FII）優先峰會上發表演說。七大工業國（G7）外長將於法國舉行會議。聯合國安理會預計於週五就中東議題舉行閉門會議。經濟數據：密西根大學將於美東時間上午10點公布3月最終版消費者信心指數。財報：嘉年華郵輪。

數字看新聞

8. 6.38%——據房地美統計，本週30年期固定利率房貸平均利率，較上週的6.22%進一步攀升，這已是利率連續第四週上揚，來到9月以來的最高水準。對於因高房價與高利率已陷入低迷長達三年的房市而言，這個時機點可謂再糟不過——3月通常正是全年房屋銷售最旺季節的起點。

最後花絮

9. 一直滑手機看壞消息，讓你長出皺紋了嗎？你可能得了「科技頸」。從焦慮情緒飆升、注意力持續下滑，到社交孤立，科技一直被視為各種問題的元兇。如今，它的「罪狀清單」上又多了一項：皺紋。這正是所謂的「科技頸」——隨著年齡增長會自然出現的頸部紋路，據稱因持續使用智慧型手機而加劇惡化。對此症狀的焦慮情緒正持續蔓延，尋找解方的競賽也已展開。美容產業正推出琳瑯滿目的解決方案，其中包括外型充滿未來感的LED紅光頸圈。

新聞室之外

10. 評論：處境艱難的伊朗政權，據報已獲得一項包含解除全部制裁在內的停火提議。若如伊朗官員如今所暗示的那樣拒絕這項提議，恰恰會讓川普有理由給予這場戰爭更多時間，將整個行動貫徹到底。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Narrow Path to a U.S.‑Iran Deal
emails.contentEn:
President Trump has told associates in recent days that he wants to avoid a protracted war in Iran, aiming to wrap up the conflict within weeks. However, with peace negotiations in a nascent stage, easy exits are scarce. Trump’s attention has already begun shifting toward the coming midterm elections and domestic priorities like airport security and voter-eligibility rules. While some allies hope he can pivot to ousting the communist regime in Cuba, close advisers are urging a focus on the most pressing issue facing voters: Americans’ concerns about the cost of living, which have been exacerbated by the war.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. The prospects of a diplomatic deal ending the war between the U.S. and Iran look dim right now, but Middle East veterans say there is a pathway for an agreement. Follow our live coverage. Trump says the energy shock will be short-lived, but some oil-and-gas executives are painting a much bleaker picture. The war adds risks to megaprojects by Western companies like Disney and Wynn Resorts looking to tap the Middle East for much more than oil. Back-to-back jury verdicts holding Meta liable for harms to young people could open the way to a flood of litigation that could force it—and other social-media giants—to make significant changes to its products. In Napa Valley, a Michelin-starred restaurant has entered the fight over affordable housing.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 46363.00 -348.00 (0.75%); S&P 500 Futures 6585.25 -55.50 (0.84%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 24127.25 -240.50 (0.99%). Source: Factset, market data as of 3/26/2026, 5:45:58 AM ET. The explosion of so-called agentic artificial intelligence has driven a wave of demand for central processing units, once an afterthought in the world of AI. Arm Holdings picked a perfect time to jump into the AI market with its own chips, though its high stock valuation assumes a lot of success, writes Dan Gallagher.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. Iran is applying the lessons of Russia’s drone warfare against America. Video clips released by Iranian-backed Iraqi militias looked eerily familiar to anyone who has followed the Ukraine war. Drones cruised above an American base in Baghdad, then dived to strike a Black Hawk helicopter on the ground and an air-defense radar system. Trump is considering ground and naval operations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and compel Tehran to a cease-fire. If these troops come ashore in Iran, they would face a drone-dominated environment that has little in common with past U.S. campaigns in Iraq and Afghanistan, reports Yaroslav Trofimov.

4. Trump’s ambivalence on Taiwan opens a historic opportunity for China. For five decades, U.S. presidents have stuck to a choreographed set of norms around Taiwan, the most dangerous flashpoint in U.S.-China relations. The Taiwan issue promises to come up again in the two leaders’ next face-to-face summit, report Lingling Wei and Alex Leary. Xi sees Trump as unwilling to come to Taiwan’s defense, people close to Beijing’s decision-making said—especially if America’s involvement in the Middle East, which has led the U.S. to redirect major military assets away from Asia, continues to distract Washington.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: Are bots replacing workers? It’s trendy to cite AI when cutting jobs, but the reality is more complicated, writes columnist Callum Borchers. A: Leaders at Amazon, Block, Atlassian and other companies have linked recent layoffs to AI. But economists and machine-learning specialists say existing technology isn’t ready to take humans’ jobs at scale. They argue the most likely reasons for head-count reductions remain the same as ever: slower sales, shifting priorities and previous overhiring. “AI washing is pervasive right now,” says J.P. Gownder, vice president and principal analyst at Forrester Research. Businesses are reclaiming the upper hand in the employer-employee relationship after a period of worker empowerment. Using an AI boogeyman to shake people up is consistent with that effort. None of this is to say that a major reckoning won’t come at some point, or that AI hasn’t already absorbed some positions. Forrester projects 6.1% of Americans’ jobs could be lost to AI by 2030. It’s clear that AI isn’t just a helpful partner that eliminates busywork. But it also isn’t a broad replacement for human workers—not yet, anyway—and companies’ claims of AI labor breakthroughs deserve scrutiny.

6. We looked at the well-timed trades made moments before Trump’s policy surprises. The president has moved markets with sudden shifts in policy, from tariff U-turns to military strikes. On several occasions, unusual trades hit the tape ahead of his announcements. There is no evidence of leaks or insiders making trades before Trump’s posts on Truth Social. Still, some market veterans believe news is trickling out from his orbit. Here is a rundown of episodes where well-timed trades happened ahead of Trump-triggered swings.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. Opening Day for Major League Baseball. Economic data: The Labor Department reports weekly jobless claims. Earnings: Commercial Metals, Pony AI.

THE NUMBER

8. 83 — The number of U.S. metro areas that shrank in the year ended June 2025, up from 52 the prior year, according to new government data. The driver is a sharp slowdown in immigration, coupled in many places with losses from people leaving for other parts of the country. The Los Angeles, San Diego and Miami areas—three of the 20 largest metros out of 387 in the U.S.—all saw population declines.

AND FINALLY...

9. JFK Jr.’s magazine was a bust. Now everyone wants a copy. Back-issues of George, the politics and culture magazine John F. Kennedy Jr. founded in 1995, are suddenly in demand and fetching high sums. The catalyst? “Love Story,” the limited TV series chronicling Kennedy’s romance with Carolyn Bessette, which airs its finale tonight. The show has renewed infatuations with all things Kennedy and Kennedy adjacent—from backward driving caps to niche sunglasses—turning George into a status symbol 25 years after it folded.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: The verdict against Meta and YouTube is a victory for the plaintiffs bar—not for children or society.

WSJ | Buy Side: From top-rated kitchen appliances to smart tech gear, these are the discounts worth shopping from Amazon’s Big Spring Sale.

川普總統近日向身邊人士表示，他希望避免伊朗戰事拖延過久，力求在數週內結束這場衝突。然而，由於和平談判仍處於萌芽階段，簡單易行的退場方案並不多見。川普的關注焦點已開始轉向即將到來的期中選舉，以及機場安檢、選民資格規定等內政優先事項。儘管部分盟友希望他能將重心轉向推翻古巴的共產政權，但親近幕僚正敦促他專注於選民眼下最迫切的議題：因這場戰爭而加劇的美國生活成本問題。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 眼下透過外交途徑結束美伊戰爭的前景黯淡，但中東問題資深人士表示，達成協議仍有一條可行路徑。請關注本報即時報導。川普表示這波能源衝擊只是短暫現象，但部分油氣業高層描繪的景象要悲觀得多。這場戰爭也為迪士尼、永利度假村等意圖從中東擷取遠不止石油之利益的西方企業的大型計畫增添了風險。連續兩起陪審團裁定Meta須為傷害年輕用戶負責的判決，可能為隨之而來的大量訴訟開啟大門，迫使Meta及其他社群媒體巨頭對其產品做出重大調整。在納帕谷，一家米其林星級餐廳也捲入了平價住宅爭議之中。

市場即時動態

2. 道瓊期貨46363.00，跌348.00點（0.75%）；標普500期貨6585.25，跌55.50點（0.84%）；納斯達克100期貨24127.25，跌240.50點（0.99%）。資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年3月26日美東時間上午5:45:58。所謂「代理型」人工智慧（agentic AI）的爆炸性成長，已帶動一波對中央處理器（CPU）需求熱潮——這種晶片過去在AI世界裡一向不受重視。丹·加拉格爾撰文指出，安謀控股（Arm Holdings）挑了一個絕佳時機，帶著自家晶片跨入AI市場，儘管其偏高的股票估值，隱含著市場對其成功的高度期待。

搶先讀

3. 伊朗正將俄羅斯無人機戰術的經驗，應用於對抗美國。伊朗支持的伊拉克民兵發布的影片片段，讓任何關注烏克蘭戰爭的人都感到似曾相識：無人機在巴格達一處美軍基地上空盤旋，隨後俯衝攻擊了地面上的一架黑鷹直升機及一套防空雷達系統。川普正考慮採取地面與海上行動，重新開放荷莫茲海峽，並迫使德黑蘭接受停火。亞羅斯拉夫·特羅菲莫夫報導指出，若這些部隊登陸伊朗，他們將面對一個由無人機主導的作戰環境，與美軍過去在伊拉克、阿富汗的作戰經驗幾乎毫無相似之處。

4. 川普在台灣議題上的搖擺態度，為中國創造了一個歷史性機會。五十年來，歷任美國總統在台灣問題上——這個中美關係中最危險的引爆點——始終遵循一套精心編排的默契規範。魏玲玲與亞歷克斯·利里報導指出，台灣議題勢必會在兩國領導人下一次面對面峰會中再次浮上檯面。據接近北京決策圈的人士透露，習近平認為川普不願出手保衛台灣——尤其若美國持續深陷中東事務、被迫將主要軍事資源從亞洲調離，導致華盛頓分身乏術的話。

專家解讀

5. 問：機器人正在取代人類的工作嗎？專欄作家卡勒姆·博切爾斯撰文指出，如今企業裁員時搬出AI當理由已成一種風潮，但實情要複雜得多。答：亞馬遜、Block、Atlassian等公司的高層都曾將近期裁員與AI掛鉤。但經濟學家與機器學習專家表示，現有技術尚不足以大規模取代人類的工作。他們認為，裁員最可能的原因其實一如既往：銷售放緩、優先事項轉移，以及此前的過度招聘。富雷斯特研究（Forrester Research）副總裁暨首席分析師J.P.高恩德表示：「眼下『AI濫用話術』（AI washing）現象十分普遍。」在歷經一段勞工權力抬頭的時期後，企業正重新奪回勞資關係中的主導權，而搬出AI這個「假想敵」來震懾員工，正符合這一意圖。這並不代表某種重大的「AI清算」永遠不會到來，也不代表AI尚未取代任何職位——富雷斯特預測，到2030年，美國恐有6.1%的工作將被AI取代。顯然，AI已不僅僅是一個能替人分擔瑣碎工作的得力助手，但它也還不能——至少目前還不能——全面取代人類勞動力，而企業聲稱AI已帶來勞動力突破的說法，值得投以審慎眼光。

6. 我們檢視了川普政策爆出意外消息前夕、時機精準得可疑的一系列交易。這位總統的政策急轉——從關稅政策的大逆轉到軍事打擊行動——屢屢牽動市場。多次事件中，在他宣布消息之前，市場上都出現了異常交易。目前並無證據顯示存在洩密，或有內部人士搶在川普發布Truth Social貼文前進行交易。不過，部分市場老手仍認為，消息正從他身邊的圈子悄悄外洩。以下整理了幾起在川普引發的市場震盪之前、時機精準得令人玩味的交易案例。

今日要聞預告

7. 美國職棒大聯盟開幕日。經濟數據：勞工部公布每週初次申請失業救濟人數。財報：商業金屬公司、小馬智行。

數字看新聞

8. 83——根據最新政府數據，截至2025年6月的一年間，人口萎縮的美國都會區數量，較前一年的52個大幅增加。主要驅動因素是移民人數銳減，加上許多地區還面臨居民遷往美國其他地區所造成的人口流失。洛杉磯、聖地牙哥與邁阿密都會區——在全美387個都會區中排名前20大——人口皆出現下滑。

最後花絮

9. 小甘迺迪創辦的雜誌當年慘澹收場，如今人人都想要一本。小約翰·甘迺迪1995年創辦的政治文化雜誌《George》，其過期刊物如今需求暴增，售價也水漲船高。這一切的催化劑是什麼？正是今晚將播出大結局的迷你影集《Love Story》，該劇講述甘迺迪與卡洛琳·貝瑟特的戀情。這部影集重新點燃了外界對甘迺迪家族及其周邊一切事物的迷戀——從反戴鴨舌帽到小眾墨鏡皆然——讓《George》在停刊25年後，重新成為一種身分地位的象徵。

新聞室之外

10. 評論：針對Meta與YouTube的這項判決，是原告律師界的勝利——而非兒童或整個社會的勝利。

Unless peace talks between the U.S. and Iran pan out fast, high prices for Middle Eastern crude could soon cascade to the U.S. and elsewhere. A resolution means oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz again. Even then, for prices to fall, traders want to see Gulf producers reverse output cuts from the start of the war. Oil prices appear to move on every headline, but it can take weeks or months for them to ripple from wellheads to gas stations. And with utility bills climbing, WSJ’s Rachel Wolfe asked Americans how they’re recalibrating their budgets.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. Mediators from Turkey, Egypt and Pakistan are pushing for a meeting between U.S. and Iranian officials. Follow our live coverage here. Iran’s combative Parliament speaker, Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf, is emerging as an unlikely figure in Washington’s search for a deal to halt the war. The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating several problems that could have played into the deadly LaGuardia Airport crash. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen’s party suffered its worst election in a century, despite plaudits for her defense of Greenland against President Trump. A New Mexico jury found Meta Platforms liable for failing to protect young people from online dangers, including sexually explicit content and trafficking.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 46736.00 +321.00 (0.69%); S&P 500 Futures 6652.25 +46.25 (0.70%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 24423.75 +210.00 (0.87%). Source: Factset, market data as of 3/25/2026, 6:00:02 AM ET. Wall Street is betting on a veteran of both the Marines and bare-knuckle New Jersey politics to fight New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s push to raise taxes on the wealthy and corporations. New bank regulations could favor loans to private credit, writes Telis Demos.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. He had a full ride at Duke—until America cut him off. Student visas for Africa’s best and brightest have been canceled by the Trump administration, leaving empty seats and broken dreams. As a boy, Majok Bior escaped a country engulfed in war. As a gifted student, he won a full scholarship to Duke University and looked toward a dazzling future. Bior studied computer science at the North Carolina campus during his freshman year. After finishing the fall semester of his sophomore year, Bior returned to Uganda for winter break. Then Trump began to ban students from Africa, starting with South Sudan, where Bior was born. He hasn’t returned to campus since, reports Caroline Kimeu.

4. As China encroaches, even New Zealand is getting serious about its military. New Zealand is known for majestic landscapes, epic filmmaking and once-in-a-lifetime vacations. Now, the country is embarking on a more off-brand project: bolstering its tiny military, as China sends forces deeper into the Pacific. New Zealand plans to spend some $7 billion on its military in the next few years; it is also on a recruitment drive. The urgency of a well-equipped force was on display last year, when a Chinese naval task force conducted live-fire drills between Australia and New Zealand. The exercises reminded New Zealanders that the country can’t rely on its remote location to keep it out of trouble, Judith Collins, New Zealand’s defense minister, told the WSJ’s Mike Cherney.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: How has the ICE operation in Minnesota continued to impact the Twin Cities' economies? National affairs reporter Joe Barrett spoke with business owners in Minneapolis and St. Paul about the economic ripple effects from the ICE surge there: A: Six weeks after the Operation Metro Surge immigration crackdown wrapped up in the Twin Cities, local businesses that rely on immigrants—both as workers and customers—are still struggling to recover. Minneapolis and St. Paul have estimated that the operation cost the local economy hundreds of millions of dollars in lost revenue and wages, while spending on police overtime soared. “Though the actions of ICE are now off the headlines, the economic impacts will ripple out for months, and probably beyond,” Matt Varilek, commissioner of Minnesota’s Department of Employment and Economic Development, told me. Many businesses that shuttered during the height of the operation have come back, but their customers largely haven't. Others are just glad to be back to a sense of normalcy. Luis Reyes Rojas, owner of Pinedas Tacos Plus, no longer has to keep his front door locked against potential ICE raids. He said it’s “better times for everybody.”

6. They’re rich but not famous—and they’re suddenly everywhere. The number of Americans worth tens of millions and hundreds of millions of dollars has boomed in the past few decades, thanks to a rising stock market, lucrative private investments and swelling valuations for small and midsize businesses. This growing class is now a huge force in the economy, driving the demand for everything from lavish hotel rooms to private jet travel. In charts, WSJ’s Rachel Louise Ensign shows how much this class has grown and how it is transforming the U.S. economy.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. Economic data: The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release import and export price indexes for February. Earnings: Jefferies Financial, Cintas, Beyond Meat, Chewy.

THE NUMBER

8. >$10,000 — The retail price of some vintage Eames Lounge Chairs. Since its launch in 1956, the chair has become a status symbol in Hollywood films and design aficionados’ homes alike. Authentic versions carry a legacy of craftsmanship shaped by designers Ray and Charles Eames. In this video, WSJ went inside the Michigan factories where the chair is made.

AND FINALLY...

9. Our travel columnist let artificial intelligence plan her seaside break and wound up swimming in the North Sea. With Google’s Gemini chatbot as her travel agent, WSJ’s Dawn Gilbertson traveled to the little-known, but quaint English town of Saltburn-by-the-Sea for a recent trip. The goal: a trip planned entirely by AI, with no outside research or human recommendations. While the “Jim-and-I” adventure successfully uncovered a far-flung gem, she found the chatbot stumbled on real-time logistics like weather forecasts and shifting restaurant hours.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: As the U.S. weighs taking the time and risk to reopen the Strait of Hormuz by force, the Iranian regime must weigh whether it can risk losing that trump card—and bearing attacks for however long the Hormuz action extends the war.

除非美伊和談迅速取得進展，否則中東原油的高價恐將很快蔓延至美國及世界各地。要解決問題，意味著石油必須重新流經荷莫茲海峽。即便如此，要讓價格下跌，交易員還希望看到海灣產油國撤銷開戰以來的減產措施。油價看似隨著每則頭條新聞起伏，但從油井到加油站，實際的價格傳導往往需要數週甚至數月時間。而隨著水電瓦斯帳單不斷攀升，本報記者瑞秋·沃爾夫走訪美國民眾，了解他們如何重新調整自己的預算。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 來自土耳其、埃及與巴基斯坦的調停人士正積極推動美伊官員展開會談。請關注本報即時報導。伊朗態度強硬的國會議長穆罕默德—巴蓋爾·加利巴夫，意外成為華盛頓尋求停戰協議過程中一個舉足輕重的人物。美國國家運輸安全委員會正在調查數項可能促成拉瓜迪亞機場致命空難的問題因素。丹麥總理梅特·佛瑞德里克森所屬政黨遭逢一世紀以來最慘敗的選舉結果，儘管她此前因捍衛格陵蘭、抵禦川普總統而備受讚譽。新墨西哥州一個陪審團裁定，Meta平台未能保護年輕用戶免受包括色情內容與人口販運等網路危害，須負法律責任。

市場即時動態

2. 道瓊期貨46736.00，漲321.00點（0.69%）；標普500期貨6652.25，漲46.25點（0.70%）；納斯達克100期貨24423.75，漲210.00點（0.87%）。資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年3月25日美東時間上午6:00:02。華爾街正押注一位兼具海軍陸戰隊背景與新澤西州硬派政治歷練的老將，來對抗紐約市長佐赫蘭·馬姆達尼力推的富人與企業加稅政策。Telis Demos撰文指出，新的銀行監管規定可能有利於流向私募信貸的貸款。

搶先讀

3. 他原本在杜克大學拿到全額獎學金——直到美國將他拒之門外。川普政府已取消非洲頂尖優秀學生的學生簽證，留下空蕩蕩的座位與破碎的夢想。馬約克·比奧爾童年時逃離了一個深陷戰火的國家；作為一名資優生，他贏得杜克大學全額獎學金，前途一片光明。大一那年，比奧爾在北卡羅來納州校園主修電腦科學。完成大二秋季學期後，他返回烏干達過寒假。隨後，川普政府開始禁止來自非洲國家的學生入境，首當其衝的正是他的出生地南蘇丹。自此他便再也沒能返回校園，卡洛琳·基梅烏報導。

4. 隨著中國步步進逼，就連紐西蘭也開始認真看待自身軍力建設。紐西蘭素以壯麗景色、史詩級電影製作與一生一次的度假勝地聞名。如今，這個國家正著手推動一項與其形象大相逕庭的計畫：在中國將軍力持續深入太平洋之際，強化自身規模微小的軍隊。紐西蘭計劃未來幾年在軍事上投入約70億美元，同時也在積極展開招募行動。去年，一支中國海軍特遣艦隊在澳洲與紐西蘭之間海域進行實彈演習，凸顯出擁有裝備精良軍力的迫切性。紐西蘭國防部長朱蒂絲·柯林斯告訴本報記者麥克·切尼，這場演習提醒了紐西蘭人，這個國家無法僅靠地理位置偏遠，就能置身麻煩之外。

專家解讀

5. 問：明尼蘇達州的ICE行動，如何持續衝擊雙城（明尼亞波利斯與聖保羅）的經濟？國家事務記者喬·巴瑞特走訪明尼亞波利斯與聖保羅的企業主，了解當地ICE行動高峰所帶來的經濟連鎖效應：答：「大都會突襲行動」（Operation Metro Surge）這場移民執法整肅行動在雙城結束六週後，依賴移民作為員工與顧客的當地企業，至今仍在艱難復甦。明尼亞波利斯與聖保羅估計，這場行動導致當地經濟損失數億美元的營收與薪資，同時警力加班支出激增。明尼蘇達州就業與經濟發展廳廳長麥特·瓦里勒克告訴我：「儘管ICE的行動如今已不再是頭條新聞，但其經濟衝擊將持續蔓延數月，甚至更久。」許多在行動高峰期歇業的商家已重新開張，但顧客大多還沒回流。也有一些商家單純慶幸，一切終於恢復了些許正常。Pinedas Tacos Plus的老闆路易斯·雷耶斯·羅哈斯，如今已無需再為防範ICE突襲而鎖上店面前門。他表示，如今「對每個人來說都是更好的時光」。

6. 他們很有錢，卻不出名——如今卻突然無處不在。過去幾十年間，受惠於股市上漲、獲利豐厚的私人投資，以及中小型企業估值不斷攀升，身家達到數千萬乃至數億美元的美國人數量激增。這個日益壯大的階層，如今已成為經濟中一股龐大的力量，帶動了從豪華飯店客房到私人飛機旅行等各種需求。本報記者瑞秋·路易絲·恩森透過圖表，展示這個階層究竟成長了多少，以及它正如何重塑美國經濟。

今日要聞預告

7. 美國職棒大聯盟開幕日。經濟數據：勞工部將公布2月進出口物價指數。財報：傑富瑞金融、金泰斯、Beyond Meat、Chewy。

數字看新聞

8. 逾1萬美元——部分復古Eames Lounge Chair躺椅的零售價格。自1956年問世以來，這款躺椅已成為好萊塢電影與設計愛好者家中共通的地位象徵。正品版本承襲了設計師雷與查爾斯·伊姆斯夫婦所打造的工藝傳承。本報在這段影片中，實地走訪這款躺椅位於密西根的製造工廠。

最後花絮

9. 本報旅遊專欄作家讓人工智慧為她規劃了一趟海濱假期，結果她最後在北海裡游起了泳。本報記者道恩·吉爾伯森讓Google的Gemini聊天機器人擔任她的旅遊規劃師，前往鮮為人知卻別具韻味的英國小鎮索爾特本濱海鎮，展開一趟近期旅程。此行目標：一趟完全由AI規劃、不參考任何外部資料或人為建議的旅程。儘管這趟「與吉姆同行」的冒險成功挖掘出一處偏遠的隱藏寶地，她也發現，這款聊天機器人在天氣預報、餐廳營業時間變動等即時後勤資訊方面時常出錯。

新聞室之外

10. 評論：當美國正權衡是否要花費時間、承擔風險以武力重新開放荷莫茲海峽之際，伊朗政權也必須權衡，自己是否承受得起失去這張王牌的風險——以及無論荷莫茲行動讓戰爭延長多久，都得承受隨之而來的攻擊。

《華爾街日報》｜Buy Side：優質的廉價汽車保險供應商，收費低廉卻不縮水保障範圍。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: ICE Agents Deploy to Airports Amid Travel Chaos
emails.contentEn:
The week began with chaos for U.S. travelers. ICE agents arrived at major airports in New York, Atlanta, Phoenix and other cities to help ease the security bottlenecks that have sprung up amid the partial government shutdown. Compounding the strain is Sunday’s runway collision at New York’s LaGuardia Airport, which killed two pilots and led to hundreds of flight cancellations. Our latest investigation reconstructs an audio and visual timeline of the crash, while our breaking news team has the latest on what travelers should expect for the remainder of the week.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. Senators said they were closing in on a deal to fund all of the DHS except for the agency that carries out immigrant arrests and deportations. U.S. allies in the Persian Gulf are inching toward joining the fight against Iran. Residents on Israel’s northern border are staying put despite renewed Hezbollah fire. America’s chief financial officers say that artificial intelligence will push some people out of their jobs: primarily workers in routine, clerical and administrative roles.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 46441.00 -81.00 (0.17%); S&P 500 Futures 6624.75 -10.00 (0.15%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 24391.75 -16.50 (0.07%). Source: Factset, market data as of 3/24/2026, 6:04:14 AM ET. Big banks are playing both sides of the private credit meltdown. If Super Micro Computer survives its latest scandal, it can thank the law of supply and demand—and Nvidia, writes Dan Gallagher.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. Back-channel diplomacy drove President Trump’s U-turn on Iran. Foreign ministers from Egypt, Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan gathered before dawn on Thursday in Riyadh for talks aimed at finding a diplomatic off-ramp to the war in Iran. Egyptian intelligence officials managed to open a channel with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and put forward a proposal to halt hostilities for five days. Those discussions laid the groundwork for an abrupt reversal: On Monday, as word of the discussions in the Saudi capital made its way to the White House, Trump backtracked on his threat to strike Iran’s power plants, embracing diplomacy with Tehran instead, report Summer Said, Alexander Ward, Benoit Faucon and Laurence Norman.

4. Here’s how Nvidia keeps its iron grip on the AI boom. Thanks to the astronomical demand for its chips, Nvidia generates more profit than almost any other public company on the planet. The chip giant has used its fast-growing war chest to become the industry’s most powerful financier, investing tens of billions of dollars in promising startups and supporting key customers who would otherwise struggle to afford its chips. Nvidia says that the deals grow the broader AI ecosystem. But they also have another effect: keeping customers hooked on Nvidia’s products and steering them away from rival chip providers, report Berber Jin, Robbie Whelan and Kate Clark.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: What’s going on at U.S. airports? It’s spring break season—and travelers have been facing long airport lines amid TSA staffing shortages and Sunday’s accident at LaGuardia. Senior breaking news editor Lynn Cook details what travelers need to know: A: Hundreds of flights from LaGuardia were canceled or delayed yesterday after a late-night Air Canada flight crashed into a fire truck on the runway, killing two pilots and injuring dozens of passengers. The airport reopened at 2 p.m. ET, but travelers were advised to continue checking with their airlines because residual delays and cancellations were expected. Knock-on effects cascaded to other airports around the U.S., with the most delays and cancellations hitting Chicago’s O’Hare International Airport, Dallas Fort Worth International Airport and Boston’s Logan International Airport. The crash compounded an already harried flying experience due to the partial government shutdown that started in February. TSA agents have been working without pay for more than a month, prompting many to call in sick and some to quit. Security screening lines have become so long that some airports temporarily suspended the estimated wait times normally published on their web sites. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, the busiest in the U.S., said travelers should allow at least four hours to get through domestic and international security screening. ICE agents were deployed to some major U.S. airports yesterday including in Houston, Phoenix and Atlanta to support TSA operations and ease long security lines. At this point, it’s unclear when, and how, travel headaches will ease up. Senators were nearing a deal to fund all of the DHS except for the agency that carries out immigrant arrests and deportations.

6. ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini entered the WSJ bracket pool. One might actually win. This year’s March Madness is playing out at a time when AI tools are smarter than ever. With the models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google already being judged against each other in everything from coding to creative writing, we decided it was time for a new test of their intelligence: the bracket benchmark. So we secretly entered three ringers into the WSJ office pool—Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT. And after the first weekend of the NCAA tournament, all three AI models can still win it.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. Economic data: Provisional U.S. purchasing managers’ surveys for manufacturing and services will give an indication of how businesses have held up during the war. Earnings: GameStop, Core & Main, Smithfield Foods.

THE NUMBER

8. 11% — How much Chinese wine imports fell last year, defying hopes for a gradual recovery. They are now at half the peak levels of 2018, when China bought foreign wine valued at nearly $3 billion. A tough economy and leader Xi Jinping’s crackdown on what Beijing deems unbecoming behavior by government officials have caused the bottom to fall out of what was once among the most lucrative wine markets in the world.

AND FINALLY...

9. Meet the man who can find your wedding ring anywhere, even in the ocean. Resort managers on the island of Mauritius keep a series of phone numbers handy in case of emergency. The police, ambulance, fire department, cyclone-warning system and, of course, Zoël Manguillier, the guy to call when the groom drops his wedding ring in the Indian Ocean. The 61-year-old estimates he’s found 1,000 rings during more than 30 years of jewelry hunting. Sometimes he’s just out there for fun, but often he’s wielding his submersible Excalibur II metal detector to salvage someone’s destination wedding.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: The Trump Administration may soon ask Congress for $200 billion for the U.S. military. It’s instructive to watch Democrats vote the bill down before it even exists.

WSJ | Buy Side: Business-debt consolidation can improve your cash flow and repackage your obligations to potentially save you money.
emails.contentZh:
這一週，對美國旅客來說是以混亂開場。移民及海關執法局（ICE）人員已抵達紐約、亞特蘭大、鳳凰城等主要城市的大型機場，協助紓解因部分政府停擺而出現的安檢壅塞。雪上加霜的是，週日紐約拉瓜迪亞機場發生跑道相撞事故，造成兩名飛行員身亡，並導致數百架航班取消。本報最新調查重建了這起空難的音訊與影像時間軸，即時新聞團隊也帶來本週剩餘時間旅客該有何預期的最新消息。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 參議員表示，他們正接近達成一項協議，將為國土安全部除負責移民逮捕與驅逐出境業務的機構外的所有部門提供撥款。波斯灣地區的美國盟友正逐步靠攏，考慮加入對伊朗的軍事行動。儘管真主黨再度發動攻擊，以色列北部邊境居民仍選擇留守家園。美國各企業財務長表示，人工智慧將導致部分人失業，首當其衝的是從事例行性、文書與行政職務的員工。

市場即時動態

2. 道瓊期貨46441.00，跌81.00點（0.17%）；標普500期貨6624.75，跌10.00點（0.15%）；納斯達克100期貨24391.75，跌16.50點（0.07%）。資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年3月24日美東時間上午6:04:14。各大銀行在這場私募信貸崩盤中同時押注了兩方。丹·加拉格爾撰文指出，若美超微電腦（Super Micro Computer）能挺過最近這場醜聞，供需法則和輝達都是它該感謝的對象。

搶先讀

3. 幕後外交管道，促成川普總統在伊朗問題上的急轉彎。週四凌晨，埃及、土耳其、沙烏地阿拉伯與巴基斯坦的外交部長齊聚利雅德，展開旨在為伊朗戰爭尋找外交出路的會談。埃及情報官員成功與伊朗伊斯蘭革命衛隊建立起溝通管道，並提出一項為期五天的停火提案。這些磋商為隨後的急轉直下奠定了基礎：週一，隨著沙烏地首都這場會談的消息傳到白宮，川普收回了此前打擊伊朗發電廠的威脅，轉而擁抱與德黑蘭的外交途徑，薩默·賽義德、亞歷山大·沃德、伯努瓦·福孔與勞倫斯·諾曼報導。

4. 輝達如何牢牢掌控這波AI榮景。憑藉對其晶片的驚人需求，輝達創造的利潤幾乎超越地球上任何一家上市公司。這家晶片巨頭已運用其快速累積的雄厚資金，成為業界最具影響力的金主，向前景看好的新創公司投入數百億美元，並支持那些若非如此、恐怕難以負擔其晶片價格的重要客戶。輝達表示，這些交易有助壯大整個AI生態系統。但這麼做也帶來另一種效果：讓客戶持續依賴輝達的產品，並使其遠離競爭對手的晶片供應商，貝爾伯·金、羅比·惠倫與凱特·克拉克報導。

專家解讀

5. 問：美國各機場究竟發生了什麼事？眼下正值春假旺季，加上運輸安全管理局（TSA）人手短缺，以及週日拉瓜迪亞機場的意外事故，旅客們一直面臨漫長的機場排隊人潮。資深即時新聞編輯琳恩·庫克詳述旅客需要了解的資訊：答：昨日一架加拿大航空班機深夜在跑道上撞上一輛消防車，造成兩名飛行員身亡、數十名乘客受傷，導致拉瓜迪亞機場數百架航班取消或延誤。該機場已於美東時間下午2點重新開放，但建議旅客持續向所屬航空公司確認航班狀況，因為預計仍會出現後續的延誤與取消。這起事故的連鎖效應波及美國各地其他機場，其中芝加哥歐海爾國際機場、達拉斯沃斯堡國際機場與波士頓洛根國際機場受到的延誤與取消影響最為嚴重。這起事故，讓自2月開始的部分政府停擺原本就已相當混亂的搭機體驗雪上加霜。TSA人員已無薪工作逾一個月，導致許多人請病假，部分人甚至選擇辭職。安檢隊伍變得極為冗長，部分機場甚至暫停公布網站上通常會顯示的預估等候時間。全美最繁忙的哈茨菲爾德—傑克遜亞特蘭大國際機場表示，旅客應預留至少四小時，才能完成國內及國際航班的安檢流程。昨日，ICE人員已被派往包括休士頓、鳳凰城與亞特蘭大在內的美國多個主要機場，協助TSA的運作並紓解冗長的安檢隊伍。目前尚不清楚這場旅行亂象何時、又將如何獲得緩解。參議員們正接近達成一項協議，為國土安全部除負責移民逮捕與驅逐出境業務的機構外的所有部門提供撥款。

6. ChatGPT、Claude與Gemini都加入了《華爾街日報》的賽事對戰組合競猜。其中一個說不定真能勝出。今年的「三月瘋狂」（March Madness）籃球賽正值AI工具比以往任何時候都更聰明的時期。由於OpenAI、Anthropic與Google旗下的模型，早已在程式設計乃至創意寫作等各個領域相互較勁，我們認為是時候用一種新方式來測試它們的智能了：對戰組合競猜基準測試。於是，我們悄悄讓三位「暗樁」——Claude、Gemini與ChatGPT——加入了《華爾街日報》辦公室內部競猜賽。而在NCAA錦標賽首個週末結束後，這三個AI模型全都仍有機會奪冠。

今日要聞預告

7. 經濟數據：美國製造業與服務業採購經理人指數初值，將顯示企業在戰爭期間的營運狀況。財報：GameStop、Core & Main、史密斯菲爾德食品。

數字看新聞

8. 11%——去年中國葡萄酒進口量的下滑幅度，與外界原本期待的逐步復甦背道而馳。目前進口量僅為2018年高峰期的一半，當年中國進口外國葡萄酒的金額接近30億美元。疲軟的經濟，加上國家領導人習近平打擊北京認定的政府官員不當行為的整肅行動，導致這個曾是全球最有賺頭的葡萄酒市場之一徹底崩跌。

最後花絮

9. 認識這位無論你的婚戒掉在哪裡——即便是掉進海裡——都能幫你找回來的男人。模里西斯島上的度假村經理們，都會隨身準備好一串緊急聯絡電話：警察、救護車、消防隊、氣旋預警系統，當然還有佐埃爾·芒吉利耶——當新郎把婚戒掉進印度洋時，就該打給他。這位61歲的老手估計，他在超過30年的尋寶生涯中已找回1,000枚戒指。有時他只是出於興趣下海尋寶，但更多時候，他是揮舞著他那台可潛水的Excalibur II金屬探測器，去搶救別人一場異地婚禮的美好回憶。

新聞室之外

10. 評論：川普政府可能很快將向國會要求撥款2,000億美元用於美軍。值得玩味的是，民主黨人在這項法案甚至尚未成形之前，就已經打算投票否決它。

《華爾街日報》｜Buy Side：企業債務整合能改善你的現金流，並重新規劃你的債務組合，有望為你省下開支。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Taiwan’s Urgent Quest to Win Over Trump
emails.contentEn:
For the roughly 200,000 prisoners held by Iran’s regime, the war has created a new, terrifying reality. Our latest investigation shows that airstrikes have damaged complexes used to hold political detainees, putting their lives in even graver danger. Bomb blasts have ripped through windows at Tehran’s notorious Evin prison, where inmates are surviving on stale bread and polluted water. Among those trapped inside are American and European hostages, a Nobel Prize winner, political dissidents and would-be reformists. Many are the leaders of a nebulous protest movement that President Trump has urged to rise up and topple the regime.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. New York City’s LaGuardia Airport was closed after a passenger plane collided with an emergency vehicle on the runway, killing two pilots. Iranian missile strikes are costing big oil companies billions in lost revenue. Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s top diplomat, has become the most prominent voice of a government refusing to be cowed by the U.S. and Israeli military campaign. ICE officers will begin trying to ease bottlenecks at airports today, as the Trump administration scrambles for a plan to end hourslong security lines. Trump’s mass-deportation campaign is taking an economic toll on mixed-status households, pushing some families into financial ruin. Meta chief Mark Zuckerberg is building an AI agent to help him do his job.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 45545.00 -348.00 (0.76%); S&P 500 Futures 6503.50 -55.50 (0.85%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 23867.50 -234.00 (0.97%). Source: Factset, market data as of 3/23/2026, 5:53:32 AM ET. A bipartisan pair of U.S. senators are introducing legislation to prevent CFTC-regulated entities, including Kalshi and Polymarket, from offering wagers on sports. A bill that would limit the activities of big housing investors has turned Wall Street landlords into a value play, writes Carol Ryan.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. Taiwan is on an urgent quest to win over Trump. Taiwan has spent a whirlwind 15 months wooing the most unpredictable American leader in living memory as he tosses aside decades of precedent. For the democratically governed island, the stakes couldn’t be any higher. China wants to absorb Taiwan, whose defense hinges on American support. Officials in Taipei hope Trump sees Taiwan not as a security liability but as a semiconductor ace in the U.S. quest for AI dominance. But no one in the Taiwanese capital can predict what will happen when Trump travels to Beijing, possibly in the coming weeks, seeking an elusive trade truce with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, report Niharika Mandhana, Josh Chin and Joyu Wang.

4. The Fed’s most awkward leadership transition is coming. Kevin Warsh promised to overhaul the Federal Reserve and cut rates. He is being greeted by rising inflation and an oil shock, among other challenges. The war in Iran threatens to push inflation higher still in the coming months, and investors now view rate increases to be more likely than cuts this year. The confirmation process, meanwhile, has stalled, making it hard to say whether Warsh will take over when Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s term ends in two months. That means Warsh could ultimately arrive at a Fed under pressure from a president demanding lower rates and colleagues skeptical of cuts—all while Powell has signaled he may not leave, reports Nick Timiraos.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: Why are service costs up in the U.S., and how are rising prices feeding into inflation? Robust spending is driving up prices of services from haircuts to healthcare, a dynamic that is now taking center stage in the Federal Reserve’s fight against inflation, explains Konrad Putzier. A: The rising price of services is a big part of why the inflation rate has stayed above the Fed’s 2% target. Economists say prices of services keep rising because consumers still have plenty of cash. Real wages are up and unemployment is low. Rising stock prices over the past few years have made wealthy Americans wealthier. Because high-income households generally spend a relatively big share of their earnings on services such as airplane tickets and restaurant meals, services inflation has stayed elevated, according to Eugenio Aleman, chief economist at Raymond James. Prices of pet services and delivery services rose by 7.3% and 7.1%, respectively. The cost of haircuts, dry cleaning and internet services also rose faster than overall inflation. Above-target price increases and a weak labor market put the Fed in a tight spot. The recent drop in hiring normally calls for lower interest rates, but that is risky while inflation is still high. By raising energy costs, the Iran war could push up the price of services such as transportation, Atsi Sheth, chief credit officer at Moody’s Ratings, told me. At the same time, the risk of runaway inflation similar to 2021 and 2022 is low, she said. Many lower- and middle-income households are feeling the strain after years of rising expenses. That puts a limit on how much businesses can raise prices.

6. The economy cabin on airplanes keeps on shrinking. The economy cabin is losing the turf war on airplanes. Airlines are retrofitting their passenger jets or buying new ones that have a larger share of premium seats. Their goal is to squeeze more revenue out of each seat flown, catering to travelers willing to pay up for lie-flat and extra legroom seats.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. The Supreme Court hears a high-stakes case on vote-by-mail ballots to decide whether votes count if they’re postmarked by Election Day but don’t arrive until later. Economic data: A delayed Census Bureau report on construction spending for January is due, along with quarterly data on retail, manufacturing, mining and wholesale trade.

THE NUMBER

8. $80.5 million — The estimated amount “Project Hail Mary,” a science-fiction adventure starring Ryan Gosling, opened to in the U.S. and Canada this weekend, making it Amazon’s first major box-office hit. It’s also the biggest opening for any Hollywood film not part of an existing franchise since “Oppenheimer” in the summer of 2023.

AND FINALLY...

9. Ads are popping up on the fridge and it isn’t going over well. Americans have long accepted digital ads as a trade-off for connectivity, but the kitchen remained largely off-limits—until now. A software update for Samsung’s Family Hub refrigerator introduced banner ads to its 32-inch door screen. While some Americans have been taken aback by marketing messages on the appliance, Samsung says the ads can be toggled off in the device’s settings.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: Democrats across the country are making tax increases central to their 2026 campaign agenda.

WSJ | Buy Side: See our guide to the top financial adviser companies for retirees.
emails.contentZh:
對於身陷伊朗政權囚禁的約20萬名囚犯而言，這場戰爭創造出一種嶄新且令人恐懼的處境。本報最新調查顯示，空襲已損毀關押政治犯的監獄建築群，讓他們的生命處境更加險惡。德黑蘭惡名昭彰的埃文監獄多處窗戶已被炸彈爆炸震碎，獄中囚犯僅能靠發霉的麵包與受污染的水維生。被困其中的包括美國與歐洲人質、一位諾貝爾獎得主、政治異議人士，以及有志於推動改革的人士。其中許多人正是川普總統呼籲奮起推翻政權的那場模糊不清的抗議運動的領導者。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1. 紐約市拉瓜迪亞機場因一架客機在跑道上與一輛緊急車輛相撞、造成兩名飛行員身亡而關閉。伊朗的飛彈攻擊已讓各大石油公司損失數十億美元營收。伊朗最高外交官阿巴斯·阿拉克齊已成為該國政府拒絕在美以軍事行動面前屈服的最具代表性的聲音。隨著川普政府急於制定方案，結束長達數小時的安檢排隊人潮，移民及海關執法局（ICE）人員今日起將開始協助紓解機場壅塞狀況。川普的大規模驅逐出境行動正對「身分混合」家庭（成員中有合法與非法移民身分者）造成經濟衝擊，導致部分家庭陷入財務困境。Meta執行長馬克·祖克柏正在打造一個AI代理人，協助他處理公務。

市場即時動態

2. 道瓊期貨45545.00，跌348.00點（0.76%）；標普500期貨6503.50，跌55.50點（0.85%）；納斯達克100期貨23867.50，跌234.00點（0.97%）。資料來源：Factset，市場數據截至2026年3月23日美東時間上午5:53:32。兩黨兩位美國參議員正提出立法，禁止Kalshi、Polymarket等受商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）監管的機構提供體育賽事下注服務。卡蘿·萊恩撰文指出，一項擬限制大型住宅投資者活動的法案，反而讓華爾街房東們的資產成了價值型投資標的。

搶先讀

3. 台灣正急切地爭取贏得川普的青睞。過去15個月裡，台灣馬不停蹄地籠絡這位當代記憶中最難以捉摸的美國領導人，眼看他不斷推翻數十年來的外交慣例。對這座民主治理的島嶼而言，賭注不能更高了：中國一心想要併吞台灣，而台灣的防務則高度仰賴美國的支持。台北官員希望川普能將台灣視為美國在AI主導權爭奪戰中的「半導體王牌」，而非安全負擔。但台灣首都無人能預料，當川普可能於未來數週內前往北京、尋求與中國領導人習近平達成一項難以捉摸的貿易休兵協議時，局勢將如何演變，尼哈麗卡·曼達納、周浩與王若愚報導。

4. 聯準會史上最尷尬的一次領導權交接即將到來。凱文·沃許曾承諾將徹底改革聯準會並降息，如今卻迎面撞上通膨升溫、油價衝擊等多重挑戰。伊朗戰爭恐在未來數月內進一步推升通膨，如今投資人普遍認為今年升息的可能性高於降息。與此同時，他的任命確認程序陷入停滯，難以判斷聯準會主席鮑爾兩個月後任期屆滿時，沃許是否真能接任。這意味著，沃許最終上任時，恐將同時面對一位要求降息的總統，以及對降息心存疑慮的同僚——而鮑爾本人則已暗示他可能不會離任，尼克·蒂米拉奧斯報導。

專家解讀

5. 問：美國服務業成本為何上漲？物價上漲又如何推升整體通膨？康拉德·普齊爾解釋道，強勁的消費支出正推高從理髮到醫療保健等各項服務的價格，這股動態如今已成為聯準會抗通膨戰役的核心議題。答：服務價格上漲，是通膨率持續高於聯準會2%目標的一大主因。經濟學家表示，服務價格之所以持續上漲，是因為消費者手頭仍相當寬裕：實質薪資上升，失業率偏低；過去幾年股價上漲，也讓富裕的美國人變得更加富有。雷蒙詹姆斯首席經濟學家尤金尼奧·阿萊曼指出，由於高收入家庭通常將收入中相對較大的比例花在機票、餐廳用餐等服務項目上，服務業通膨因而持續居高不下。寵物服務與外送服務的價格分別上漲了7.3%與7.1%。理髮、乾洗與網路服務的費用漲幅也超過整體通膨率。物價漲幅超標，加上就業市場疲軟，讓聯準會陷入兩難：招聘放緩通常意味著應該降息，但在通膨仍居高不下之際，這麼做風險不小。穆迪評等首席信貸官阿齊·謝斯告訴我，伊朗戰爭推升能源成本，可能連帶推高運輸等服務的價格。她也表示，與此同時，重演2021、2022年那種通膨失控的風險並不高——許多中低收入家庭在歷經多年物價上漲後已備感壓力，這也限制了企業能夠調漲價格的空間。

6. 飛機經濟艙空間持續縮水。經濟艙在飛機上的「地盤爭奪戰」正節節敗退。各航空公司正對現有客機進行改裝，或直接採購高端座位比例更高的新機，目的是從每個座位上榨取更多營收，迎合那些願意為平躺座椅與額外腿部空間多付錢的旅客。

今日要聞預告

7. 最高法院將審理一宗攸關重大的郵寄選票案件，裁定選舉日前已加蓋郵戳、但之後才寄達的選票是否有效。經濟數據：普查局延遲公布的1月營建支出報告，以及零售、製造、採礦與批發貿易的季度數據，皆將於今日出爐。

數字看新聞

8. 8,050萬美元——由萊恩·葛斯林主演的科幻冒險片《拯救計畫》本週末在美國與加拿大的預估首映票房，使其成為亞馬遜首部重量級票房大片。這也是自2023年夏季《奧本海默》以來，非既有系列作品的好萊塢電影中最佳的開畫票房。

最後花絮

9. 冰箱上開始出現廣告，民眾反應不佳。美國人長期以來已接受以數位廣告換取連網功能，但廚房向來是個例外——直到現在。三星Family Hub冰箱的一次軟體更新，在其32吋門板螢幕上導入了橫幅廣告。儘管部分美國人對家電上出現行銷訊息感到錯愕，三星表示用戶可在裝置設定中關閉這些廣告。

新聞室之外

10. 評論：全美各地的民主黨人正將加稅列為2026年競選議程的核心。
