emails.subject: The 10-Point: U.S., Israel Attack Iran
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Months of threats, massing military forces and sputtering negotiations have come to a head as the U.S. and Israel earlier this morning began strikes on Iran that could last for days. President Trump urged Iranians to “take over your government” as explosions were reported across the country. Already, Tehran’s response has started with missiles targeting Israel and U.S. military facilities in the Gulf. At risk is a wider regional conflict in one of the most economically sensitive parts of the world. Follow our live coverage as the situation develops.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Trump is expected to address the nation later today on the strikes, which he said aim to ensure Americans “ will never be threatened by a nuclear-armed Iran.” The federal government will stop working with Anthropic , Trump said, escalating a clash with the AI company over how its technology can be used by the Pentagon. Nvidia plans a new processor specially tailored to help OpenAI and others build faster, more efficient tools, a move that is poised to the reset the AI race. Paramount’s David Ellison refused to take no for an answer in his bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, a process that took six months, nine offers and $81 billion. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is asking Trump for $21 billion to help revive the city’s biggest housing project in 50 years, and it might not be enough.

FROM THE MARKETS

2

Netflix actually won in many ways, even though it lost Warner , writes Dan Gallagher. U.S. businesses are shaving billions off their tariff bills using a “first sale” rule, which has led to a backlash in Congress.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

A classified report found that Kristi Noem created security vulnerabilities at airports.

The secretary of Homeland Security for months failed to appropriately respond to the findings of an internal watchdog that one of her biggest airport security changes—letting passengers pass through screening checkpoints with shoes on—is creating “significant” security risks, according to a letter from the inspector general reviewed by WSJ and officials familiar with the matter. When Noem’s office was briefed on the report, officials gave it a higher classification level and blocked it from public release, report Tarini Parti, Josh Dawsey and Michelle Hackman. A department spokeswoman disputed the claims and said Noem responded appropriately.

4

Can cities survive without their wealthiest residents?

The rich have long threatened to leave when battling local governments over taxes, but rarely done so. But as California and New York City threaten new levies, their threats now have teeth . As digital technology lets the wealthy separate where they live from where their businesses operate, they’re moving away from great cities such as New York and London and toward lifestyle tax havens such as Miami and Dubai, writes professor and author Richard Florida. This upends the underlying economic logic of cities, which are no longer self-contained economic units but networks—physical places linked by virtual ties and dynamic talent flows.

Get set for the trading day ahead.

Let the WSJ's own Spencer Jakab prepare you with expert insight into the companies and industries set to move markets. Sign up for our Markets A.M. newslette r.

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: Should spouses be talking about online passwords on date night?

Anxiety can grow when one half of a couple doesn’t have access to the family’s digital life and finances. Columnist Julie Jargon wrote about why partners should regularly chat about their digital life .

A: The division of labor in a marriage often results in one person handling the banking, subscriptions, passwords and more. That can leave the other person in the dark about how to locate and access the family’s accounts.

Douglas Boneparth, a certified financial planner, had managed his family’s finances until his wife, Heather, decided she wanted more visibility. The Boneparths—who have since co-written a book, “Money Together”—offered some tips on how both partners can get up to speed:

Do it now. Don’t wait until an emergency to figure out how to access accounts. Make sure you’re both authorized. Even when you have joint accounts, a bank might consider one person the primary account holder. Do a trial run. Whatever your partner would normally do in a given month, try to do instead (and vice versa). Write a note. Douglas composes a “death note” for Heather, detailing who to call and what to do if something were to happen to him—and Heather makes one for him, too. Make it a regular date. Douglas recommends couples meet quarterly to go over any account changes and to update passwords and documents.

SEE THE STORY

6

These charts show why so many lawmakers are retiring this year.

If the present trajectory holds, 2026 could surpass previous highs and mark the largest midterm exodus of House members in nearly a century of data. Retirement decisions stem from a mix of political and personal factors. Some lawmakers are ending long careers, while others are pursuing different offices or navigating newly redrawn district lines. For some Republicans, run-ins with Trump made life difficult.

HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

7

Saturday: Greg Abel’s first annual letter to shareholders as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway. 📰 Today's paper 

THE NUMBER

8

 13%

How much coal-fired power generation increased in 2025 from the previous year as higher natural gas costs made coal more competitive, according to the Energy Information Administration. Extreme weather and gas price spikes have created more recent openings for coal, though it isn’t clear just how long the good times will last.

AND FINALLY...

9

He’s Reese’s biggest brand advocate—and Hershey’s biggest headache.

Brad Reese, the 70-year-old grandson of company founder H.B. Reese, is the self-appointed defender of his family brand. The role takes many forms: When he’s not celebrating the candy, he’s often bashing its owner—and lately he’s been doing a lot of the latter .

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Few AI questions are more consequential than whether U.S. troops will hold the battlefield tech edge over their enemies. The big winner of the brawl between Anthropic and the Pentagon could be China.
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 數月來的威脅、軍力集結與斷斷續續的談判,終於在今日清晨迎來高潮——美國與以色列開始對伊朗發動可能持續數日的攻擊行動。川普總統敦促伊朗人民「奪回你們的政府」,同時該國各地傳出爆炸聲。德黑蘭的回應已展開,飛彈鎖定以色列及美軍在波灣的軍事設施。這場世界上經濟最敏感地區之一,如今面臨更廣泛區域衝突的風險。追蹤我們對局勢發展的即時報導。

Emma Tucker
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條
1
川普預計今日稍晚將就此次攻擊向全國發表談話,他表示此舉旨在確保美國人「絕不會受到擁核伊朗的威脅」。川普表示,聯邦政府將停止與Anthropic合作,使雙方在五角大廈能否使用該公司技術一事上的對立進一步升級。輝達計畫推出一款專為協助OpenAI等公司打造更快速、更高效AI工具而設計的新處理器,此舉可能重新洗牌AI競賽格局。派拉蒙的大衛·艾里森(David Ellison)在收購華納兄弟探索(Warner Bros. Discovery)一案中拒絕接受任何拒絕,這場歷時六個月、歷經九次出價、總價810億美元的收購案終於拍板。紐約市長佐赫蘭·馬姆達尼正向川普爭取210億美元,協助重啟該市50年來規模最大的住房計畫,但這筆錢可能仍不夠。

市場動態
2
Dan Gallagher撰文指出,即便輸掉華納,Netflix其實在許多方面仍是贏家。美國企業正利用一項「首次銷售」規則削減數十億美元的關稅支出,此舉已在國會引發反彈。

獨家搶先報導
3
一份機密報告發現,克莉絲蒂·諾姆在機場製造了安全漏洞。

根據《華爾街日報》審閱的一封監察長信函及知情官員透露,這位國土安全部長數月來未能妥善回應一項內部監督報告的調查結果——該報告指出,她推動的一項重大機場安檢變革(允許旅客穿鞋通過安檢關卡)正製造「重大」安全風險。當諾姆辦公室獲悉這份報告時,官員將其提升為更高機密等級,並阻止公開發布,Tarini Parti、Josh Dawsey與Michelle Hackman報導。一名部門發言人對相關指控表示異議,並稱諾姆的回應是適當的。

4
沒有最富有的居民,城市還能存續嗎?

富人長期以來一直以搬離作為與地方政府就稅收議題角力的籌碼,但真正付諸行動的情況並不多見。然而,隨著加州與紐約市威脅加徵新稅,他們的威脅如今變得更具實質效力。教授兼作家理查·佛羅里達(Richard Florida)撰文指出,數位科技讓富人得以將居住地與企業營運地分離,他們正從紐約、倫敦等大城市遷往邁阿密、杜拜等「生活方式稅務天堂」。這顛覆了城市的根本經濟邏輯——城市已不再是自給自足的經濟單元,而是由虛擬連結、動態人才流動所串連起的實體節點網絡。

為交易日做好準備。
讓《華爾街日報》Spencer Jakab為您提供有關即將影響市場的公司與產業的專家見解。訂閱我們的Markets A.M.電子報。

專家解讀
5
問:約會之夜,伴侶該不該聊聊網路密碼?

當夫妻中的一方無法取得家庭數位生活與財務資訊的存取權時,焦慮便可能滋生。專欄作家Julie Jargon撰文分析,為何伴侶應定期討論彼此的數位生活。

答:婚姻中的分工,常導致其中一人負責銀行事務、訂閱服務、密碼等事務,這可能讓另一方對如何查找及存取家庭帳戶一無所知。

認證財務規劃師道格拉斯·邦帕特(Douglas Boneparth)原本一直獨自打理家庭財務,直到妻子海瑟(Heather)表示希望有更多掌握度。這對夫妻此後合著了一本書《一起理財》(Money Together),並提供了以下建議,協助雙方跟上進度:

現在就開始行動。別等到緊急狀況發生才想辦法取得帳戶存取權。確認雙方都已獲得授權。即便是聯名帳戶,銀行也可能將其中一人視為主要帳戶持有人。做一次演練。嘗試代替伴侶執行他們平常每月會做的事(反之亦然)。寫一份備忘錄。道格拉斯為海瑟撰寫了一份「身後事備忘錄」,詳列萬一自己發生意外,該聯絡誰、該做什麼——海瑟也為他準備了一份。定期安排時間。道格拉斯建議夫妻每季碰面一次,檢視帳戶異動,並更新密碼與文件。

詳閱報導
6
這些圖表揭示了為何今年這麼多議員選擇退休。

若照目前趨勢發展,2026年可能超越過往紀錄,創下近一世紀數據中眾議院議員規模最大的期中選舉退休潮。退休決定源於政治與個人因素的交織。有些議員正結束漫長的職業生涯,有些人則轉而角逐其他職位,或因選區重劃而另作打算。對部分共和黨人而言,與川普的摩擦讓從政之路變得艱難。

本週末焦點
7
週六:格雷格·阿貝爾(Greg Abel)首次以波克夏海瑟威執行長身分發表年度股東信。📰 今日報紙。

數字看新聞
8
　13%

根據美國能源資訊署數據,2025年燃煤發電量較前一年成長的大致比例,原因是天然氣成本上漲使煤炭更具競爭力。極端天氣與天然氣價格飆升,為煤炭創造了近期的新機會,儘管尚不清楚這波榮景能持續多久。

最後一則
9
他是Reese's花生醬巧克力最大的品牌擁護者——也是好時公司(Hershey)最大的頭痛人物。

70歲的布拉德·里斯(Brad Reese)是公司創辦人H.B.里斯的孫子,自封為家族品牌的捍衛者。這個角色有多種展現形式:當他不是在頌揚這款糖果時,往往就是在抨擊其擁有者——而且近來他做得更多的是後者。

編輯室之外
10
評論:少有比「美軍能否在戰場科技上持續領先敵人」更攸關重大的AI議題。Anthropic與五角大廈這場衝突的最大贏家,可能是中國。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Paramount Beats Netflix for Warner Bros.
emails.contentEn:
✏️ We lead this Friday with big news from Hollywood: Paramount emerged victorious in the bidding war for Warner Bros. Discovery after Netflix said it wouldn’t match Paramount’s latest offer for the iconic entertainment company. Pending regulatory approval, Paramount will own not only Warner Bros. and HBO, but also many popular cable networks including CNN, TNT, TBS and Food Network. The deal would represent a major change for the entertainment industry, which is trying to adapt to seismic shifts in audience habits and technology.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

The Federal Reserve is waging a closed-door legal challenge to two Justice Department subpoenas issued as part of a criminal investigation into Chair Jerome Powell. Newly released documents show how JPMorgan’s bankers maintained ties with Jeffrey Epstein for years even after the bank fired him as a client. Amazon’s new artificial intelligence czar, Peter DeSantis, is betting that the company’s signature low-cost strategy can help it win the AI race. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is in India, until now a bitter rival, to mend fences and build new alliances with the world’s middle powers.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

President Trump’s push to make homes more affordable needs the banks to play ball , writes Telis Demos. Panic over software-business disruption from AI appears to have subsided after Anthropic showcased its partnership with Salesforce and other companies. Block, the payments company founded by Jack Dorsey, said that it plans to lay off 40% of its workforce , or more than 4,000 employees. Neither theory, history, nor the latest data suggests a recession driven by AI job dislocation is likely, writes Greg Ip.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Here’s how a Wall Streeter came to own New York’s biggest club.

Wall Street has thrown billions at the live-events industry. One of those efforts went south fast. For fund manager Andrew Axelrod, buying New York’s biggest club looked like a home run—until it devolved into a saga of sudden deaths, overcrowding and the vanishing of a founder before an $80 million sale. Now, Axelrod’s fund owns the bankrupt venue, with executives from its other companies—including a funeral-home conglomerate—pitching in to keep the lights on, reports Alexander Saeedy.

4

Trump diplomats bashing Europe get a sharp reply: Butt out.

The president’s representatives in Europe are increasingly willing to chastise governments in public. The response from authorities there has been sharp: Mind your own business . In recent weeks, U.S. envoys have waded into some of Europe’s most sensitive political debates, demanding action to counter far-left violence, migration and antisemitism. As the guarantors of European security, U.S. officials have long prodded European politicians on various issues—but usually behind closed doors. The criticism has added an irritant to a trans-Atlantic relationship that is on its shakiest ground since World War II, report Matthew Dalton, Noemie Bisserbe and Robbie Gramer.

Take a break from the news.

Sign up for the WSJ. Magazine newsletter for a weekly roundup of fashion, entertainment, design, food, travel, art, architecture and more.

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: Mortgage rates fell below 6% for the first time since 2022. Should you refinance?

The 30-year rate dipped below an important psychological threshold and is expected to boost home sales going into the crucial spring season. Reporter Veronica Dagher breaks down the math homeowners should consider before refinancing:

A: With mortgage rates finally dipping below 6%, homeowners who are locked in at 7% or 8% may be eager to pull the refinance trigger. But before you refi, do the math.

Closing costs have surged, now typically ranging from 2% to 6% of your loan balance. On a $400,000 mortgage, that’s an $8,000 to $24,000 hit. To make the move worthwhile, aim for a rate at least half a percentage point lower than your current one and plan to stay put for at least four years to reach the break-even point.

While Trump has pressured the Fed to lower costs, mortgage rates track the volatile 10-year Treasury yield. Trying to time the bottom is a gamble. In 2026, a "good deal" isn't a magic number—it’s one that improves your immediate cash flow while fitting your long-term housing plans.

SEE THE STORY

6

New Zealand is rolling out the welcome mat for wealthy American home buyers.

PHOTO: JACKIE MEIRING FOR WSJ

Around 2018, New Zealand became a famed destination for tech billionaires said to be building “doom-prep” bunkers. Long seen as a safe haven due to its geographic isolation, it is now a magnet for a larger group of Americans, many of them venture capitalists, entrepreneurs and investment advisers drawn to the country’s vibrant startup community. Adding fuel to the fire is a recent shift in New Zealand’s visa policies, which makes it easier for wealthy foreigners to buy homes there.

問:房貸利率自2022年以來首次跌破6%。該重新申辦房貸嗎?

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Americans Are Leaving the U.S. in Record Numbers
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Last year, the U.S. experienced something unseen since the Great Depression: negative net migration. The Trump administration has hailed the exodus as the fulfillment of its promise to ramp up deportations and restrict visas. But beneath the optics lies a less-noticed reversal: Americans are leaving in record numbers for lands they find more affordable. On another note entirely, we have written about an issue that transcends national borders: Our annoyance at corporate jargon. We asked for the buzzwords you hate most , and it got pretty granular. You can deep dive into our full report as we unpack the most-hated terms here.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Wall Street traders are pouncing on the tariff refund chaos, paying more for claims since the Supreme Court’s decision last week. In other tariff news: At least 1,800 companies have filed lawsuits seeking refunds from the government following the court’s ruling. The U.S. has sent top-of-the-line jet fighters to Israel, marking the first time it has deployed combat aircraft to the country for a potential wartime mission in Iran. The Washington Post lost more than $100 million last year, according to people familiar with the matter. More Americans under 55 are dying of severe heart attacks, a new study has found.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 49478.00 -56.00 0.11 S&P 500 Futures 6956.50 -3.25 0.05 Nasdaq 100 Futures 25368.50 -13.50 0.05

Source: Factset, Market data as of 2/26/2026, 5:44:29 AM ET

📈 Follow our live financial coverage all day.

Nvidia’s huge numbers don’t settle the latest artificial-intelligence fears, writes Dan Gallagher. 📊 In charts: The $1.6 trillion meltdown that swept through software stocks.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Americans are leaving the U.S. in record numbers.

Since the Eisenhower administration, the U.S. hasn’t collected comprehensive statistics on the number of citizens leaving. But data on residence permits, foreign home purchases, student enrollments and other metrics from more than 50 countries show that Americans are voting with their feet to an unprecedented degree. A millions-strong diaspora is studying, telecommuting and retiring overseas. The new American dream, for some of its citizens, is to no longer live there, report Drew Hinshaw and Joe Parkinson.

4

Jeffrey Epstein used his fortune to infiltrate America’s most prestigious universities.

Epstein never earned a college degree—let alone one from a fancy Ivy League university. Yet some of Epstein’s deepest ties were with America’s most distinguished academics, cultivated over years through financial support, shared interests and hospitality at his glittering properties. Those relationships are now imploding careers at elite universities as millions of Epstein-related documents released by the Justice Department show how the late sex offender stretched his tentacles deep into academia, report Joshua Chaffin, Neil Mehta and Douglas Belkin.

Your news, your way.

Get more of the Journal’s trusted insights by setting us as your preferred source on Google .

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: Is the remote-work dream dead?

Roles that allow you to work from home are four times harder to get than other jobs, by one estimate. Columnist Callum Borchers writes about the future of the remote-job market. 

A: We appear to be reaching remote-work equilibrium, after years of conflicting trends and predictions. The share of open jobs listed as remote on the career site Indeed has held steady between 8% and 8.6% for the past six months.

That’s roughly triple what the rate was in 2019 but markedly less than it was in 2022. Not only is the remote slice of the market narrowing, the overall pie is also shrinking amid layoffs and slower hiring.

If you’re wondering what the remote job market will look like in the long run, there’s a good chance what you see today is what you’ll get for the foreseeable future.

Millions of people got a taste of the WFH life and loved it. Forty percent of applications submitted through LinkedIn are for remote roles, even though those jobs represent only 8% to 9% of listings.

Business sectors with the biggest shares of remote opportunities include technology, information and media, Kory Kantenga, LinkedIn’s head of economics for the Americas, said.

So, where is there hope? Startups and midsize companies are often more willing to let employees work remotely. It’s one of the few ways they can lure talent that would otherwise go to blue-chip brands.

SEE THE STORY

6

Here’s a look at the math behind Trump’s eye-catching economic ideas.

In a record-length State of the Union address, President Trump threw out a string of eye-catching economic ideas. Among them: new retirement accounts for Americans without access to 401(k)s; replacing income taxes with tariff revenue; and balancing the federal budget by eliminating fraud. His proposals and promises come as American voters are increasingly frustrated with the economy. We crunched the numbers behind some of Trump’s economic notions.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

Hillary Clinton is set to testify as part of a House investigation into Epstein, with Bill Clinton to follow a day later. U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are meeting with an Iranian delegation in Geneva to discuss Tehran’s nuclear program. Earnings: Warner Bros Discovery, CoreWeave, Dell Technologies 📰 Today's paper 

THE NUMBER

8

 $7 million

The rough amount real-estate developers Nina and Michael Marco spent restoring a circa-1955 house in Delray Beach, Fla., designed by Paul Rudolph, the noted midcentury architect. The Marcos spent six years reconstructing the residence . To them, the project was a faithful reconstruction of an architectural icon. But a nonprofit dedicated to promoting Rudolph’s legacy says otherwise, raising questions about what, in fact, constitutes historic preservation.

AND FINALLY...

9

‘Leverage.’ ‘Reach out.’ ‘Circle back.’ This is the corporate jargon we hate the most.

An email arrived recently from our IT staff, alerting us to a “zero-day vulnerability” on our devices that would require an immediate update. What exactly did that mean? And was it as bad as it sounds? So it goes with corporate jargon. The idea is to sound professional or strategic, but more often it just sounds unclear. Or silly. We pinged our readers for the terms that really annoy them. The list is long .

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Trump speaks of regime change in Iran, but without an argument for why this is in U.S. interests. This failure is creating uncertainty even inside his administration.

✏️ 去年,美國出現了自大蕭條以來從未見過的現象:淨遷出人口為負值。川普政府將這波人口外流,譽為其加大遣返力度、限縮簽證承諾的實現。但在這個表象之下,還隱藏著一個較少被關注的逆轉現象:美國人正以創紀錄的人數,遷往他們認為生活成本更負擔得起的地方。另外,我們也報導了一個跨越國界的普遍議題:我們對企業行話的厭惡。我們請讀者分享他們最痛恨的流行詞彙,結果相當細緻入微。你可以在這裡深入閱讀我們彙整的完整報告,一探眾人最痛恨的用語。

美國人正以創紀錄人數離開美國。

自艾森豪政府時代以來,美國從未針對離境公民人數收集完整統計數據。但來自逾50個國家的居留許可、海外購屋、學生入學等指標數據顯示,美國人正以前所未有的規模「用腳投票」。數以百萬計的僑民正在海外求學、遠距工作與退休生活。對部分美國公民而言,新的美國夢,就是不再住在美國,Drew Hinshaw與Joe Parkinson報導。

問:遠距工作的夢想已經破滅了嗎?

據一項估計,能讓你在家工作的職缺,獲取難度是其他職缺的四倍。專欄作家Callum Borchers撰文分析遠距工作市場的未來走向。

答:歷經多年相互矛盾的趨勢與預測後,我們似乎正邁向一種「遠距工作均衡」狀態。求職網站Indeed上列為遠距工作的職缺比例,過去六個月一直穩定維持在8%至8.6%之間。

這大致是2019年比例的三倍,但明顯低於2022年的水準。不僅遠距工作在市場中的佔比正在縮小,隨著裁員與招聘放緩,整體職缺總量也在萎縮。

如果你想知道遠距工作市場長遠來看會是什麼樣貌,那麼很可能今天所見,就是在可預見的未來你能得到的樣貌。

數百萬人曾嘗過在家工作的滋味,並樂在其中。透過LinkedIn提交的求職申請中,有40%是針對遠距職缺,儘管這類職缺僅佔所有職缺的8%到9%。

LinkedIn美洲區首席經濟學家Kory Kantenga表示,遠距機會佔比最高的產業板塊包括科技、資訊與媒體業。

那麼,希望何在?新創公司與中型企業往往更願意讓員工遠距工作。這是它們吸引原本會流向藍籌企業的人才的少數方式之一。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Trump's 'Bigger, Better, Richer' America
emails.contentEn:
✏️ President Trump used his State of the Union address last night to declare a “turnaround for the ages,” pitching a “bigger, better, richer and stronger” America. Faced with low approval ratings ahead of the midterms, the president touted a robust stock market, falling mortgage rates and larger tax refunds. It’s a calculated wager: Trump is betting he can persuade the public that the economy is in better shape than many voters think it is. Our reporters in Washington, D.C., review the president’s statements—and the widespread economic anxiety—shaping this fall’s election.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

In an address heavy on patriotism, Trump defended his economic policies but polls show him struggling to connect with the public on the economy. These are the main takeaways from his speech. Bill Gates apologized to staff of the Gates Foundation over his ties to Jeffrey Epstein, admitting he made mistakes that had cast a cloud over the philanthropic group while insisting he didn’t participate in Epstein’s crimes. From small startups to giants including Meta and Google, tech companies are factoring artificial-intelligence use into performance reviews and trying to track productivity gains. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is attempting to chart a new path for a nation long dependent on the U.S. for security and China for growth as he embarks on high-stakes visits to Beijing and Washington.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

An obsession with AI is pushing skeptical traders to search for ways to profit from what they feel will be an inevitable shakeout. The Blue Owl fallout has set off a retail-investor panic , even as wealth advisers urge their clients to remain calm. Private equity was headed for a correction even without the AI gloom, writes Telis Demos.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Trump hailed an economic turnaround that many voters don’t see.

Faced with low approval ratings and growing GOP worries about the midterm elections, the president told his audience that he had unleashed a new era of prosperity that was already producing results. Trump’s State of the Union address, his most prominent speech ahead of this fall’s elections, opted against sending a message to voters that he understands the anxiety that polling shows is widely felt. For months, his advisers have urged him to focus on the economy, but his attention has often shifted to other subjects, including foreign affairs. As he spoke, Trump was weighing military strikes in Iran, report Alex Leary and Aaron Zitner.

4

Violent militias stand between the U.S. and Venezuela’s vast mineral riches.

Hidden in the jungle are diamonds, huge deposits of gold and—of most interest to the Trump administration—coltan, a compound that contains elements needed for cellphones, electric vehicles and more. Since the raid that removed Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, U.S. officials have repeatedly expressed their desire to access these minerals— part of a larger plan to break China’s stranglehold on the supply of critical minerals used in modern technology. But getting to the jungle’s riches won’t be easy. Armed criminal groups control large swaths of territory in southern Venezuela, including the gold and coltan mines, reports Ian Lovett.

Go inside what’s driving D.C.

Washington Coverage Chief Damian Paletta brings you an expert guide to the politics, power and people in the nation’s capital. EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: How did a viral memo on AI risks spook markets?

Citrini Research’s blog post appears to have sparked a stock selloff. Reporter Jack Pitcher breaks down the memo that captivated Wall Street and rattled investors:

A: James van Geelen’s Citrini Research has gained a cult following on Substack since it began publishing macro and thematic stock research in 2023, thanks in part to an early focus on AI and weight-loss drugs.

A fictional blog post from Citrini Research hit stock prices on Monday—underscoring just how jumpy investors have become about the prospects for AI.

The report—structured as a research memo from the future—posits “a scenario that’s been relatively underexplored,” wrote the authors. The memo taps into a new strain of fears about AI, painting a dark portrait of a future in which technological advancements hollow out the white-collar workforce and upend dozens of business models.

It isn’t a prediction, the authors cautioned. That didn’t stop worries from hitting real-world companies, with shares of DoorDash, Visa, Mastercard, ServiceNow and Blackstone, all mentioned by name in the post, falling sharply on Monday. Stocks recovered in the following sessions but the episode still left many surprised by how sensitive markets have become to AI uncertainty.

SEE THE STORY

6

See where Mexico’s cartels are in control, in maps.

MAP: EMMA BROWN/WSJ

Cartels operate in nearly all of Mexico’s 32 states. Domestic authorities are facing increased pressure from Trump to rein them in. His administration has designated Cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación, Cártel de Sinaloa, Cártel del Golfo and other crime syndicates as foreign-terrorist organizations. Mexican security forces are now racing to stop a cartel war from breaking out after they tracked down and killed Nemesio “El Mencho” Oseguera, the feared Jalisco cartel leader. Here’s where the organizations operate .

HAPPENING TODAY

THE NUMBER

 $342,195.63

The amount that Alan Cole, a 37-year-old Washington tax economist, put into a prediction-market wager—effectively, his life savings . While some people bet that Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency would transform and shrink the federal government, Cole took the opposite position.

AND FINALLY...

9

Don’t feed the trolls: How to survive the Wild West of Facebook travel groups

The surest way to get great travel tips, overwhelmed and riled up all at once while planning a vacation? Dive into a Facebook travel group. There’s one, and typically many more, for every inch of the travel spectrum, from travel-hacking moms to national park superfans. This corner of the travel internet is still the place for practical advice from ordinary travelers who have been there, done that, writes WSJ travel columnist Dawn Gilbertson. You just have to know how to navigate the groups skillfully.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

emails.contentZh:
✏️ 川普總統昨晚利用國情咨文演說,宣告一場「劃時代的大逆轉」,主打「更大、更好、更富裕、更強大」的美國。面對期中選舉前夕低迷的支持率,總統誇耀股市表現強勁、房貸利率下滑,以及更豐厚的退稅金額。這是一場精心算計的賭注:川普押注他能說服大眾,相信經濟狀況比許多選民所認為的還要好。我們駐華府的記者,檢視了總統的發言內容——以及形塑今年秋季選戰的普遍經濟焦慮情緒。

Emma Tucker
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條
1
在一場充滿愛國主義色彩的演說中,川普為其經濟政策辯護,但民調顯示,他在經濟議題上難以獲得民眾共鳴。以下是他演說的重點摘要。比爾·蓋茲就其與傑佛瑞·愛潑斯坦的關係,向蓋茲基金會員工道歉,承認自己犯下錯誤,為這個慈善機構蒙上陰影,但堅稱自己並未參與愛潑斯坦的罪行。從小型新創公司到Meta、Google等巨擘,科技公司正將AI使用情況納入績效考核,並試圖追蹤生產力提升成效。德國總理弗里德里希·梅爾茨(Friedrich Merz)正試圖為這個長期在安全上依賴美國、在成長上依賴中國的國家,開闢一條新路——他即將展開北京與華府兩地的高風險訪問行程。

市場即時動態
2
　最新 漲跌 漲跌幅 道瓊期貨 49288.00 52.00 0.11 標普500期貨 6911.75 8.00 0.12 納斯達克100期貨 25069.75 41.00 0.16

對AI的執念,正促使抱持懷疑態度的交易員,設法從他們認為勢不可免的市場洗牌中尋求獲利。Blue Owl的餘波已引發散戶投資人恐慌,儘管財富顧問們敦促客戶保持冷靜。Telis Demos撰文指出,即便沒有AI帶來的陰霾,私募股權本就已步入修正階段。

獨家搶先報導
3
川普誇耀經濟大逆轉,但許多選民卻不這麼認為。

面對低迷的支持率與共和黨內部對期中選舉日益升高的憂慮,總統向聽眾表示,他已開啟一個已見成效的繁榮新時代。川普的國情咨文演說,是他在今秋選舉前最重要的一次演說,卻選擇不向選民傳達他理解民調顯示普遍存在的焦慮情緒。數月來,幕僚一直敦促他聚焦經濟議題,但他的注意力經常轉向其他議題,包括外交事務。就在他發表演說之際,川普正權衡是否對伊朗發動軍事打擊,Alex Leary與Aaron Zitner報導。

4
暴力民兵組織橫亙在美國與委內瑞拉豐富礦產資源之間。

叢林深處藏有鑽石、大量黃金礦藏,以及川普政府最感興趣的鈳鉭鐵礦(coltan)——一種手機、電動車等產品所需元素的化合物。自那場推翻委內瑞拉總統尼可拉斯·馬杜羅的突襲行動以來,美國官員一再表達取得這些礦產資源的意願——這是打破中國對現代科技所需關鍵礦產供應壟斷這項更大計畫的一環。但要進入這片叢林中的寶藏並不容易。武裝犯罪集團控制著委內瑞拉南部包括黃金與鈳鉭鐵礦礦區在內的大片領土,Ian Lovett報導。

深入了解華府脈動。
華府新聞主編Damian Paletta為您帶來首都政治、權力與人物的專家導覽。

專家解讀
5
問:一份關於AI風險的病毒式備忘錄,如何驚動了市場?

Citrini Research的一篇部落格文章,似乎引發了一波股票拋售潮。記者Jack Pitcher解析這份令華爾街著迷、也令投資人不安的備忘錄:

答:詹姆斯·范·基林(James van Geelen)創辦的Citrini Research,自2023年開始發布宏觀與主題性股票研究以來,已在Substack上累積一批死忠追隨者,部分得益於其對AI與減重藥物的早期關注。

Citrini Research一篇虛構的部落格文章,週一衝擊了股價——凸顯出投資人對AI前景的神經,已變得多麼緊繃。

這份報告以一份「來自未來」的研究備忘錄形式撰寫,提出作者所稱「相對較少被探討」的一種情境。這份備忘錄觸動了一股新興的AI恐慌情緒,描繪出一幅陰暗的未來圖景:科技進步將掏空白領勞動力,並顛覆數十種商業模式。

作者提醒,這並非一項預測。但這並未阻止市場的憂慮情緒衝擊現實中的企業,週一,備忘錄中點名提及的DoorDash、Visa、萬事達卡(Mastercard)、ServiceNow與黑石(Blackstone)股價皆大幅下挫。儘管股價在隨後幾個交易日回穩,但這起事件仍讓許多人驚訝於,市場對AI不確定性已變得多麼敏感。

詳閱報導
6
透過地圖,看看墨西哥毒梟集團的勢力範圍。

地圖:EMMA BROWN/WSJ

毒梟集團的勢力遍布墨西哥32個州中的幾乎每一個州。國內當局正面臨川普日益加大的壓力,要求其加以遏制。川普政府已將哈利斯科新一代卡特爾(Cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación)、錫那羅亞卡特爾(Cártel de Sinaloa)、灣岸卡特爾(Cártel del Golfo)等犯罪集團列為外國恐怖組織。墨西哥安全部隊如今正加緊行動,在追蹤並擊斃令人聞風喪膽的哈利斯科卡特爾首腦內梅西奧·「小門薩」·奧塞格拉(Nemesio "El Mencho" Oseguera)後,試圖阻止卡特爾之間爆發火拚。以下是這些組織的勢力範圍地圖。

今日焦點事件
7
財報:輝達、Salesforce、派拉蒙Skydance。📰 今日報紙。

數字看新聞

37歲的華府稅務經濟學家艾倫·科爾(Alan Cole),投入一項預測市場賭注的金額——實際上等同於他畢生積蓄。當一些人押注伊隆·馬斯克的政府效率部(DOGE)將改造並縮減聯邦政府規模時,科爾則採取了相反的立場。

最後一則
9
別餵養酸民:如何在Facebook旅遊社團的蠻荒西部中生存下來

規劃假期時,想獲得絕佳旅遊建議、同時感到不知所措又心浮氣躁,最保險的方法是什麼?一頭栽進Facebook旅遊社團。從旅遊省錢達人媽媽到國家公園狂熱愛好者,幾乎旅遊光譜的每個角落,都有一個、通常是好幾個相應的社團。《華爾街日報》旅遊專欄作家Dawn Gilbertson撰文指出,這個網路旅遊角落,依然是普通旅人分享實用經驗的地方——這些人都曾親身經歷、實際嘗試過。你只需要知道如何巧妙地在這些社團中周旋。

編輯室之外
10
評論:FDA生物製劑主管維奈·普拉薩德(Vinay Prasad)本月已否決了兩款正申請加速核准、用於治療罕見疾病的前景看好藥物。局長馬蒂·馬卡里(Marty Makary)注意到這件事了嗎?

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Trump Aims to Sell Americans on the Economy
emails.contentEn:
Your guide to the WSJ's exclusive reporting and analysis.

Good morning from snow-covered New York. Tonight, President Trump will use his State of the Union address to sell the public on the economy and unveil new measures meant to lower costs, as Republicans try to address voters' concerns ahead of the midterm elections later this year. He's already given himself a grade—“A-plus-plus-plus-plus-plus.” The report card for the economy is a bit more mixed, however, after his first year back in office. Our reporters graded the economy on key metrics, from jobs and unemployment to the stock market and GDP.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

During his State of the Union address, Trump is expected to argue that the U.S. is “strong, prosperous and respected” as it enters its 250th year. In the president's first year, the economy endured some turbulence and managed some unexpected wins. The Trump administration is considering new national security tariffs on a half-dozen industries, while FedEx sued the U.S. government seeking a tariff refund. Rep. Tony Gonzales faced calls from fellow Republicans to resign over an alleged affair with an aide after new text messages surfaced. The Pentagon is raising concerns to Trump about an extended military campaign against Iran, while some Iranians worry American strikes will make things worse.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

DJIA Futures 48909.00 (+0.12%); S&P 500 Futures 6863.75 (+0.18%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 24830.00 (+0.27%) as of 2/24/2026, 5:59:31 AM ET.

A viral report by Citrini Research was one factor in the Dow's 800-point drop on Monday, underlining the sensitivity of stocks right now. Jane Street was accused of insider trading that helped collapse the crypto empire Terraform Labs. Resale is one of the fastest-growing corners of the luxury market, but brands haven't figured out how to compete, writes Carol Ryan.

READ IT HERE FIRST

Inside Apple's push to build an all-American chip.
Under pressure from the Trump administration, Apple vowed last year to invest $600 billion in the U.S. over four years. The commitment includes the more than 100 million chips the iPhone maker plans to buy this year from a mammoth chip-manufacturing facility that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, or TSMC, is building in Arizona. Apple is also committing billions to suppliers that make glass for devices in Kentucky, recycle rare-earth magnets in California and build silicon components in Texas. Rolfe Winkler toured the desert southwest with Apple executives to see facilities that its purchasing heft and investments are helping to build. Apple will move some production of its Mac Mini desktop computer to the U.S. from Asia.

Binance fired employees who flagged that $1 billion had moved to sanctioned Iranian entities.
Weeks after Trump pardoned convicted Binance founder Changpeng Zhao in October, executives at the crypto exchange dismantled a staff investigation into cryptocurrency that had recently moved through Binance to a network funding Iran-backed terror groups, according to company documents and people familiar with Binance's operations. The company subsequently fired the investigators who had uncovered the transfers—and the network remained active, report Patricia Kowsmann, Angus Berwick and Ben Foldy. A Binance spokeswoman said the investigators weren't “suspended or terminated for raising compliance concerns” but instead left “based on individual circumstances.” The investigation continued, she said, and resulted in the entities identified being removed from Binance's platform.

EXPERT TAKE

Q: How will the Supreme Court's tariff decision affect the coming U.S.-China summit?
With Trump on the back foot after a stinging judicial rebuke of his power to impose tariffs, Xi Jinping is spying a chance to reset relations with the U.S. on Beijing's terms ahead of Trump's trip to China, scheduled for March 31 to April 2. Chief China correspondent Lingling Wei writes about how the battleground of the U.S.-China trade fight has suddenly shifted.

A: The Supreme Court has effectively dismantled the cornerstone of Trump's trade strategy, ruling that the White House can't use emergency powers as a blank check to levy broad, across-the-board tariffs. By stripping away these duties, the court has deprived the president of his preferred weapon of economic pressure just weeks before he lands in Beijing for a summit with the Chinese leader.
The impact on the ground is immediate. The effective U.S. tariff rate on Chinese goods will tumble from 32% to 23%, according to Capital Economics. This drop reflects the administration's new—albeit temporary—15% global tariff rate, a fallback the administration reached for immediately after the ruling.
As a result, China emerges as the biggest winner of this shift so far, according to Capital Economics. As the import duty on Chinese goods shrinks, the incentive for companies to move production to other parts of Asia diminishes.
Yet, Trump still holds formidable tools to squeeze Beijing, from blocking the sale of advanced chips, jet engines and other high-tech gear to threatening new tariffs over Beijing's failure to meet past trade promises, namely the commitments struck under a trade agreement during Trump's first presidency.

Mexico is racing to prevent a cartel war.
A predawn ambush in a sleepy mountain town brought down drug kingpin Nemesio “El Mencho” Oseguera. Now that the head of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel is dead, Mexico is bracing for a civil war among his top lieutenants. Oseguera exerted control over smuggling routes that spanned from Mexico's border with Guatemala to the Gulf Coast state of Tamaulipas neighboring Texas and the Baja California peninsula.

HAPPENING TODAY

Trump's first State of the Union address of his second term. Earnings: Home Depot, HP.

THE NUMBER

<9,000 — The number of apartment units Austin is expected to deliver this year, roughly half that in 2025 and 72% lower than the 2024 peak, according to CoStar. Rents in the Texas capital look poised to rise for the first time in years, as the backlog of newly built apartments starts to run dry and people keep moving to the city.

AND FINALLY...

Americans are going all in on the Chinese lifestyle.
Drink hot water, never cold beverages. Don't walk around the house barefoot. Do longevity exercises. Across the U.S. and Western world, non-Chinese people are embracing Chinese lifestyles. In Gen Z parlance, they're “Chinamaxxing”—becoming the most Chinese they can be. China's state media is thrilled, amplifying Chinamaxxing as a sign of the country's growing global influence. Many Chinese Americans, on the other hand, are confused.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

Opinion: President Trump is reacting to his tariff defeat at the Supreme Court not by calming the trade waters but by roiling them further. He will end up hitting the economy and Republicans in Congress.
