為您導覽《華爾街日報》的獨家報導與分析。

人工智慧競賽正在改變美國的郊區樣貌。谷歌與亞馬遜等科技巨頭正搶購土地興建資料中心,排擠了全美各地急需的住宅用地。與此同時,在華府,Anthropic發現自己成為五角大廈瞄準的目標。我們帶您深入了解這場高風險爭端。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

在各大AI實驗室激烈爭奪後,OpenAI延攬了爆紅的OpenClaw個人AI助理平台創辦人。南希·古思里失蹤案調查已進入第三週,讓皮馬郡警長克里斯·納諾斯承受嚴厲的輿論檢視。北加州一場雪崩導致九名滑雪者失蹤,同一團隊中的六人已於昨夜獲救。一項雄心勃勃的泛歐計畫原本被宣傳為美國高科技匿蹤戰機的解方——結果反而暴露出該地區在國防議題上的深層分歧。敘利亞政府正著手關閉一座龐大的伊斯蘭國拘留營,此前該設施接管僅數週,便因動盪而威脅到政府對其的掌控。

市場即時看

道瓊工業指數期貨 49848.00(+0.48%);標普500期貨 6898.00(+0.55%);那斯達克100期貨 24924.50(+0.63%),截至美東時間2026年2月18日上午6:03:18。

億萬富豪偏低的稅負,正逐漸成為經濟的一項問題,卡蘿·萊恩寫道。

獨家搶先看

資料中心圈地潮,成為急需住宅供給的又一障礙。
AI的快速成長及其所需大型資料中心建設的激增,正逐漸成為美國住宅短缺的另一個潛在原因。地主與開發商發現,將土地出售給資料中心開發商,獲利可能遠高於土地的其他任何用途。地方分區法規也讓興建資料中心比興建住宅更容易、更快速。以已成為全球資料中心之都的北維吉尼亞州為例,該地區同時也正遭受住宅短缺之苦。類似的動態也在其他資料中心熱點地區上演,威爾·帕克報導。

這位共和黨州長讓川普總統如坐針氈。
奧克拉荷馬州州長凱文·斯提特身為跨黨派全國州長協會的主席,一直走在鋼索之上。他曾溫和地反對川普的部分行動,引發外界擔憂總統強勢動用聯邦權力正侵犯各州權利。但他同時也試圖避免與這位牢牢掌控共和黨的總統為敵。本週各州州長將造訪白宮,參加由斯提特協助籌辦的週五上午會議,以及與總統的晚宴,屆時這種緊張關係將表露無遺,肯恩·湯瑪斯報導。

專家觀點

問:五角大廈與Anthropic之間究竟發生了什麼事?
記者奇奇·哈吉、阿姆里斯·拉姆庫馬爾、黛博拉·阿科斯塔與維拉·貝根格倫解釋,一場關於這家新創公司工具如何被用於國防工作的衝突,為何可能對美國國防體系造成衝擊:

答:五角大廈希望能將Anthropic及其他AI工具用於所有合法用途。而Anthropic方面則不希望自家技術被用於包括國內監控與自主致命行動在內的作業。
研究與工程事務次長埃米爾·麥可表示,競爭對手OpenAI、谷歌與xAI已原則上同意讓自家模型部署於任何合法使用情境中,這是五角大廈的一項關鍵優先事項。但Anthropic並未同意。
Anthropic與國防部已就這家新創公司的技術——曾用於今年1月捕獲前委內瑞拉總統尼可拉斯·馬杜洛的行動中——該如何被使用一事,爭執了數週。
在國防部長皮特·海格塞斯的領導下,五角大廈已將「覺醒」科技公司視為一種負擔,並將任何限制條件都視為妨礙軍事效能的阻力。該機構正在檢討與Anthropic的合作關係。一名國防部高層官員表示,五角大廈內部越來越多人將Anthropic視為一項供應鏈風險,並可能要求承包商與供應商證明自己並未使用該公司的Claude模型。
這樣的舉措將是對一家美國公司異乎尋常的譴責。科技專家表示,將Anthropic貼上供應鏈風險的標籤,將阻礙軍方的AI能力,也會為其與其他公司的合作樹立不良先例。Anthropic一名發言人表示,該公司正與五角大廈進行「本著善意的、富有成效的對話」。

您今年的實際稅率可能會更低。我們告訴您為什麼。
去年夏天簽署生效的重大稅法,可能會讓您的實際稅率降低得比您想像的更多。即便您的最高稅級與最高稅率可能不會下降,但這往往沒有您想像中那麼重要。美國採行累進稅制。其結果是,實際(或平均)稅率會低於您的最高稅率。

今日焦點

Meta執行長馬克·祖克柏將於洛杉磯一場關於社群媒體成癮的指標性審判中出庭作證。聯準會將公布1月27至28日會議紀要,市場將密切關注其中透露的未來利率走向線索。財報:亞德諾半導體、Booking Holdings、Carvana、DoorDash、穆迪。

數字看世界

9.5%——若市長佐赫蘭·馬姆達尼無法說服紐約州長凱西·霍楚爾同意調高企業與富人稅——這是他為2027財年提出的預算籌措資金的首選方案——他提議對紐約市居民調漲的房產稅幅度。

最後一則……

摩根大通為員工開了一間酒吧。只可惜他們進不去。
曼哈頓中城最搶手的訂位,或許就是摩根大通新摩天大樓13樓的英式酒吧「摩根酒吧」。這棟大樓內約有1萬名員工上班,而摩根酒吧內僅有55個座位。想小酌一杯放鬆的職場螞蟻雄兵們,往往連玻璃門都進不去——玻璃門後有時能看見主吧檯座無虛席,而被銀行家訂位卻爽約的空桌則靜靜擺在一旁。

新聞編輯室之外

評論:2009年伊朗暴力鎮壓抗議活動後,歐巴馬總統曾試圖以美國的沉默換取核談判。如今德黑蘭似乎正指望川普重蹈覆轍。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Private Side Bets of UnitedHealth’s CEO
emails.contentEn:
Your guide to the WSJ's exclusive reporting and analysis.

UnitedHealth Group's Stephen Hemsley has for years made private side bets on healthcare startups that do business with—or compete against—the $450 billion conglomerate he leads. Nearly every company in healthcare touches the business of UnitedHealth, which owns the nation's largest insurer. A Journal investigation found that Hemsley's unannounced stakes involved tens of millions of dollars and stretched back at least seven years. While UnitedHealth says Hemsley abides by all disclosure and conflict-of-interest policies, ethics specialists warn of potential conflicts for the CEO.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

Jesse Jackson, the civil-rights activist and political leader, has died at 84. He was the first Black man to wage a nationwide presidential campaign. Goldman Sachs plans to drop race, gender identity, sexual orientation and other diversity factors from the criteria for its board. In Iran, payment plans for groceries are signaling a deepening economic crisis. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is trying to stop the trans-Atlantic rift between Europe and the U.S. under President Trump from becoming a divorce.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

DJIA Futures 49488.00 (-0.16%); S&P 500 Futures 6826.50 (-0.35%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 24606.75 (-0.79%) as of 2/17/2026, 6:06:26 AM ET.

Activist Elliott Investment Management has built a more than 10% stake in the struggling cruise-ship operator Norwegian Cruise Line. Lenders to commercial real-estate owners are reaching the breaking point, calling in tens of billions of dollars of troubled loans. Companies are converting aircraft engines into land-based natural gas turbines for power generation in the artificial-intelligence boom, writes Jinjoo Lee.

READ IT HERE FIRST

UnitedHealth chief made private side bets on healthcare startups.
A dominant force at UnitedHealth for the past two decades, Stephen Hemsley returned as chief executive last May to help stabilize the finances of the behemoth he helped build. In 2019, while he was UnitedHealth board chairman, Hemsley founded an investment firm, Cloverfields Capital Group LP. Cloverfields, which Hemsley still owns, has said in filings that it invests in publicly held companies. But Cloverfields has a less-visible side. Cloverfields Capital and entities affiliated with it have bought stakes in privately held healthcare startups. UnitedHealth never told its shareholders about the investments, report Mark Maremont and Anna Wilde Mathews.

Britain's monarchy can't escape the shadow of the Epstein scandal.
A cache of recently published Justice Department emails and texts has shed new light on the relationship between Jeffrey Epstein and Prince Andrew, the younger brother of King Charles III. The disclosures threaten to tarnish the image of the British monarchy. Charles has been heckled over Epstein at recent public events, an almost unheard of act in the U.K. Buckingham Palace said in a statement that the king has “profound concern” about allegations against his brother and said the palace would cooperate with any police investigation. Andrew hasn't publicly commented on the recently released emails, but has previously denied wrongdoing, report Max Colchester and Margot Patrick.

EXPERT TAKE

Q: Why does RFK Jr. want to overhaul America's baby formula guidelines?
The Trump administration is expected to begin unveiling a sweeping review of U.S. formula ingredients, led by Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., this spring. Reporter Sabrina Siddiqui explains why the operation has slowed—and what's next.

A: When Operation Stork Speed was announced last year, a flurry of activity followed. Industry groups met with regulators and a Food and Drug Administration panel convened in June. Kennedy questioned infant-formula executives about seed oils, heavy metals and how U.S. formula stacks up against Europe's.
Kennedy has said that the current federal list of nutrient requirements for infant formula is outdated and “not based on good science.”
There is little disagreement among policymakers, manufacturers and doctors that a re-examination of the requirements is long overdue. But industry representatives and pediatric experts who have consulted with the administration on the initiative say communication has slowed and visibility into the process has been limited.
Since launching its review, the administration has grappled with the practicalities of overhauling one of the most tightly regulated sectors of the U.S. food industry.
An HHS spokesman said the operation remained “a top priority” for the administration and that more updates would be shared “as they become available.”
Formula manufacturers say they use seed oils because they provide key fats that babies need to grow, including linoleic acid. Many doctors say it would be difficult to swap out seed oils, which are also used in European formulas and long regarded as safe.

As Russian sabotage ramps up, Poland prepares for a war on energy.
Poland is on high alert after a series of hybrid attacks targeting its critical civilian infrastructure. The key NATO hub is now scrambling to protect one of its weakest points: its energy grid.

HAPPENING TODAY

Lunar New Year. South Carolina's “stand your ground” law faces a courtroom test as a hearing begins in the Scott Spivey wrongful-death case. Earnings: Kenvue, Caesars Entertainment, Palo Alto Networks, Devon Energy.

THE NUMBER

$200 billion — The amount Micron Technology is spending to expand U.S. manufacturing. The largest American memory-chip maker is racing to avert the biggest supply crunch the industry has seen in more than 40 years. Behind the frenetic manufacturing arms race is the AI boom. As large language models have become increasingly complex and firms such as OpenAI, Oracle, xAI and Anthropic have announced lofty plans to build trillions of dollars worth of data centers, demand has far outpaced capacity in the memory-chip market.

AND FINALLY...

No views, no hikes, just zzzs: Welcome to the sleepcation.
A growing cohort of Gen Z and millennial travelers are choosing REM-fueled trips they've dubbed the “sleepcation.” For them, the ultimate vacation luxury isn't a nice view—it's a mattress. For the hospitality industry, the sleepcationer is a dream demographic. A guest in bed isn't wearing down the lobby or requiring a concierge. Instead, they're bringing in extra money with the charcoal bedtime lattes they're ordering from room service and the upgrades for hotel-offered sleep doctors.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

Opinion: Judge Richard Leon gives Defense Secretary Hegseth an education in the First Amendment.
emails.contentZh:
為您導覽《華爾街日報》的獨家報導與分析。

UnitedHealth Group的史蒂芬·漢姆斯利多年來一直私下投資與他所領導這家4500億美元企業集團有業務往來、或彼此競爭的醫療保健新創公司。幾乎每一家醫療保健公司都與擁有美國最大保險公司的UnitedHealth有業務往來。本報一項調查發現,漢姆斯利未公開的持股涉及數千萬美元,且至少可追溯七年之久。儘管UnitedHealth表示漢姆斯利遵守所有揭露與利益衝突政策,但道德倫理專家警告這位執行長可能存在潛在利益衝突。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

民權運動人士暨政治領袖傑西·傑克森逝世,享壽84歲。他是首位發起全國性總統競選的黑人。高盛計畫將種族、性別認同、性傾向及其他多元化因素從董事會遴選標準中移除。在伊朗,雜貨分期付款方案正顯示經濟危機日益加深。義大利總理喬治亞·梅洛尼正試圖阻止川普總統治下歐洲與美國之間的跨大西洋裂痕演變成一場「離婚」。

市場即時看

道瓊工業指數期貨 49488.00(-0.16%);標普500期貨 6826.50(-0.35%);那斯達克100期貨 24606.75(-0.79%),截至美東時間2026年2月17日上午6:06:26。

維權投資機構艾略特投資管理公司已在陷入困境的郵輪營運商挪威郵輪建立超過10%的持股。商業地產業主的放款機構已逼近臨界點,正在催收數百億美元的問題貸款。企業正將飛機引擎改造成陸上天然氣渦輪機,用於AI熱潮下的發電需求,金珠·李寫道。

獨家搶先看

UnitedHealth執行長私下投資醫療保健新創公司。
身為過去二十年來UnitedHealth的主導人物,史蒂芬·漢姆斯利去年5月重返執行長職位,協助穩定這家由他親手打造的巨頭企業的財務狀況。2019年,漢姆斯利在擔任UnitedHealth董事會主席期間,創立了一家投資公司Cloverfields Capital Group LP。漢姆斯利至今仍擁有的Cloverfields,曾在申報文件中表示其投資對象為上市公司。但Cloverfields還有較不為人知的一面。Cloverfields Capital及其關係企業已買入多家私人持有醫療保健新創公司的股份。UnitedHealth從未向股東透露這些投資,馬克·馬雷蒙與安娜·懷爾德·馬修斯報導。

英國王室無法逃脫愛潑斯坦醜聞的陰影。
一批近期公布的司法部電子郵件與簡訊,為傑佛瑞·愛潑斯坦與查爾斯三世國王胞弟安德魯王子之間的關係,揭露了新的細節。這些揭露內容有可能玷污英國王室的形象。查爾斯近期在公開場合遭到民眾就愛潑斯坦一事起鬨叫罵,這在英國幾乎是聞所未聞之事。白金漢宮在一份聲明中表示,國王對針對其弟弟的指控「深感憂慮」,並表示王室將配合任何警方調查。安德魯尚未就近期公布的電子郵件公開發表評論,但此前曾否認有不當行為,麥克斯·科爾切斯特與瑪歌·派翠克報導。

專家觀點

問:小羅伯特·甘迺迪為何想要全面改革美國嬰兒配方奶粉指南?
預計川普政府將於今年春天,在衛生與公共服務部長小羅伯特·甘迺迪的主導下,展開對美國配方奶粉成分的全面審查。記者莎布莉娜·希迪基解釋這項行動為何放緩——以及接下來會如何發展。

答:去年「鸛鳥速度行動」宣布後,隨即引發一連串忙碌的動作。產業團體與監管機構會面,食品藥物管理局的一個小組也於6月召開會議。甘迺迪就種子油、重金屬,以及美國配方奶粉與歐洲相比表現如何等問題,質詢了嬰兒配方奶粉業高層。
甘迺迪曾表示,目前聯邦針對嬰兒配方奶粉的營養素需求清單已經過時,「並非基於嚴謹的科學」。
政策制定者、製造商與醫師之間幾乎沒有異議:重新審視這些規範早已刻不容緩。但曾就此計畫與政府協商的業界代表與兒科專家表示,溝通已經放緩,整個過程的透明度也相當有限。
自啟動這項審查以來,政府一直在應對全面改革美國食品業監管最嚴格領域之一所面臨的種種實務難題。
衛生與公共服務部一名發言人表示,這項行動對政府而言仍是「首要優先事項」,並將「在有進展時」分享更多消息。
配方奶粉製造商表示,他們使用種子油是因為它們提供嬰兒生長所需的關鍵脂肪,包括亞麻油酸。許多醫師表示,要替換掉種子油相當困難,因為歐洲配方奶粉也使用種子油,且長期以來被認為是安全的。

隨著俄羅斯的破壞行動升級,波蘭正為一場能源戰做準備。
在一連串針對關鍵民用基礎設施的混合戰攻擊後,波蘭已進入高度戒備狀態。這個重要的北約樞紐,如今正急於保護其最脆弱的環節之一:其能源電網。

今日焦點

農曆新年。南卡羅來納州的「持地自衛」法在史考特·斯皮維冤死案聽證會開始之際,面臨法庭考驗。財報:Kenvue、凱撒娛樂、Palo Alto Networks、德文能源。

數字看世界

2000億美元——美光科技用於擴大美國本土製造的支出金額。這家美國最大的記憶體晶片製造商,正競相避免業界40多年來最嚴重的供應緊縮。這場瘋狂製造軍備競賽背後的推手,正是AI熱潮。隨著大型語言模型日益複雜,加上OpenAI、甲骨文、xAI與Anthropic等公司宣布了斥資數兆美元興建資料中心的宏大計畫,需求已遠遠超過記憶體晶片市場的產能。

最後一則……

沒有美景,沒有健行,只有滿滿睡意:歡迎來到「睡眠假期」。
越來越多Z世代與千禧世代旅客,選擇以充足睡眠為主軸的旅行,他們稱之為「睡眠假期(sleepcation)」。對他們而言,終極的度假奢侈品不是美景,而是一張床墊。對飯店業而言,睡眠度假客堪稱夢幻客群。一位整天待在床上的房客不會磨損大廳設施,也不需要禮賓服務。相反地,他們還會透過客房服務點購助眠的炭燒睡前拿鐵,以及升級飯店提供的睡眠醫師諮詢服務,帶來額外收入。

新聞編輯室之外

評論:理查·里昂法官給國防部長海格塞斯上了一堂關於第一修正案的課。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Sleuths Hunting for Signs of Xi's Next Purge
emails.contentEn:
Your guide to the WSJ's exclusive reporting and analysis.

Many were stunned when Xi Jinping purged his top general. Not “Pekingologists.” These obsessive China watchers hunt for clues in seating arrangements and funeral wreaths to determine which Beijing officials are in trouble. Like Kremlinology, this process is an inexact science. But that doesn't stop people from poring over documents and state-media coverage. Also, the 10-Point won't publish tomorrow on Presidents Day. We'll be back Tuesday.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

The latest tranche of Jeffrey Epstein emails flesh out the extent to which he was involved in the operations of Manhattan's Core Club and his dealings with its owner. Russian dissident Alexei Navalny was almost certainly killed by a poison derived from a rare frog toxin, several European governments said. In Ukraine, emergency-repair teams and other workers are fighting around the clock to restore power and heating under constant Russian attacks. The contest between Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos is only going to get more heated now that the two are directly competing for the moon, writes Tim Higgins. Halfway through Milan Cortina, it's clear that the biggest comeback at the Olympics is the Olympics itself, Joshua Robinson and Ben Cohen write.

FROM THE MARKETS

Though inflation is easing, jobs are holding up and growth is solid, declarations of victory feel premature, writes Nick Timiraos.

READ IT HERE FIRST

Farmers are aging, and their kids don't want to be in the family business.
Don Guinnip, 74, estimates he can maintain his current workload for a few more years. After that, the Illinois farmer and his siblings—who co-own the family farm that dates back to 1837—don't know what will become of their land. Guinnip's son Andy, who was raised to be the farm's sixth-generation operator, instead chose to work in pharmaceuticals. Though the number of U.S. farmers has long been shrinking, rising costs and weak prices are pushing more families out at a faster rate, Patrick Thomas reports. The disappearance of small farms has carried steep consequences for rural America, upending the transfer of wealth between generations.

China watchers are trying to spot the next target of Xi's purges.
The Chinese leader's motives for ejecting Gen. Zhang Youxia may never be definitively known. But that hasn't stopped foreign academics, officials and business executives from trying to find out, report Chun Han Wong and Roque Ruiz. Some are turning to arcane tea leaf-reading techniques dating back to the era of Mao Zedong. “Pekingology,” as this Chinese analog of Kremlinology is known, often involves scrutinizing official speeches, documents and state-media coverage in a bid to divine insights from language, behavior and deviations from the norm.

EXPERT TAKE

Q: Ivy League schools are rethinking their investment strategies. How?
America's wealthiest universities have been grappling with subpar returns on their private-capital investments. That's leading the Ivies to have second thoughts about where they put their money, reporter Heather Gillers writes.

A: Private equity is on academic probation.
Princeton University is lowering expectations for its endowment's returns because its private-capital investments have disappointed. Yale trimmed its portfolio of leveraged buyouts for the first time in a decade. Harvard says cashing out of some private-market investments early is now part of a long-term strategy.
Private equity has long counted America's wealthiest universities among its largest and most-loyal clients. But the market for private-company investments has gotten crowded, and returns now struggle to match broader stock-market benchmarks.
University endowments grew to lean on once-juicy private equity returns to cover more of their overall budget. That strategy faltered when the long lockup investments returned an annualized 7.4% in the three years ended June 30, according to Cambridge Associates—much of it paper gains. Over that period, the S&P 500 rose 19.7% a year.
Some endowment chiefs are running out of patience. They are turning to the secondary market where institutional investors can sell private-equity stakes to other investors before maturity, usually for less than what the manager says they are worth.

These charts show just how crazy this winter in the U.S. has been.
In the eastern U.S., residents have been suffering through one of the most frigid seasons in recent memory. Yet for much of the West, temperatures have been unusually mild and snowpack levels are at record lows.

HAPPENING THIS WEEK

Monday: Presidents Day. U.S. markets are closed. Tuesday: Lunar New Year. Wednesday: The Fed will release the minutes from its Jan. 27-28 meeting, which will be closely watched for hints about the future direction of rate cuts. Thursday: December trade figures are due. Friday: The personal consumption expenditures price index for December—the Fed's preferred inflation gauge—is released, along with an advance estimate of fourth-quarter GDP. The Supreme Court is expected to issue opinions after its winter recess.

THE NUMBER

40% — The share of 26-year-olds who have transferred funds to investment accounts since turning 22 as of May 2025, up sharply from 8% in 2015, according to data from the JPMorgan Chase Institute. The numbers don't include people investing in 401(k)s. Locked out of home ownership, a younger generation of investors is instead trying to build wealth by putting money into the stock market.

AND FINALLY...

This tiny Lake Tahoe enclave has some of America's priciest waterfront homes.
Crystal Bay, a roughly 200-home community on Nevada's North Side, had a median listing price of $14.9 million in December, according to a custom analysis by Realtor.com, which is operated by WSJ parent News Corp. The enclave's faded commercial strip sits adjacent to multimillion-dollar residential real estate favored for steep-slope privacy and elite lakefront living.
emails.contentZh:
為您導覽《華爾街日報》的獨家報導與分析。

當習近平整肅他的頭號將領時,許多人大感震驚。但「北京學家」們並不意外。這群執著的中國觀察家透過座位安排與花圈等細節尋找線索,判斷哪些北京官員正陷入麻煩。就像克里姆林宮學一樣,這個過程並非精確科學。但這並未阻止人們埋首鑽研文件與官媒報導。此外,《The 10-Point》明日總統節將暫停發送,週二再與您見面。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

最新一批傑佛瑞·愛潑斯坦電子郵件詳細揭露了他涉入曼哈頓Core Club營運的程度,以及他與該俱樂部老闆的往來。多國歐洲政府表示,俄羅斯異議人士阿列克謝·納瓦尼幾乎可以確定是遭一種源自罕見蛙毒的毒物殺害。在烏克蘭,緊急維修team及其他工作人員正24小時不間斷地奮戰,在俄羅斯持續攻擊下搶修電力與暖氣系統。提姆·希金斯寫道,如今伊隆·馬斯克與傑夫·貝佐斯已直接在月球議題上正面交鋒,兩人之間的競爭只會愈演愈烈。喬舒亞·羅賓森與班·柯恩寫道,米蘭-科蒂納冬奧進行到一半,顯然本屆奧運最大的「逆轉勝」故事,就是奧運本身。

市場動態

尼克·蒂米拉奧斯寫道,儘管通膨正在緩解、就業維持穩健、經濟成長也表現扎實,但現在就宣告勝利似乎為時過早。

獨家搶先看

農民逐漸老去,他們的孩子卻不想接手家業。
74歲的唐·金尼普估計自己還能再維持目前的工作量幾年。之後,這位伊利諾州農民與他的兄弟姊妹——他們共同擁有這座可追溯至1837年的家族農場——都不知道這片土地未來會如何。金尼普的兒子安迪原本被培養為這座農場第六代經營者,卻選擇了進入製藥業工作。派翠克·湯瑪斯報導,儘管美國農民人數長期以來持續萎縮,但不斷上漲的成本與低迷的價格,正讓更多家庭以更快的速度退出這個行業。小型農場的消失,對美國鄉村地區造成了嚴重後果,顛覆了世代之間的財富傳承。

中國觀察家們正試圖找出習近平下一波整肅的目標。
這位中國領導人罷黜張又俠將軍的動機,或許永遠不會有定論。但這並未阻止外國學者、官員與企業高層試圖一探究竟,鐘翰·黃與洛克·魯伊斯報導。有些人甚至求助於可追溯至毛澤東時代那種晦澀的「看茶葉占卜」式技巧。這種與克里姆林宮學相對應的中國式分析,被稱為「北京學」,通常涉及仔細審視官方演說、文件與官媒報導,試圖從語言、行為及偏離常態之處中揣測出蛛絲馬跡。

專家觀點

問:常春藤名校正在重新思考其投資策略。具體是怎麼做的?
美國最富有的大學,一直在應對私募資本投資報酬不佳的難題。這正促使常春藤名校們重新考慮資金該投向何處,記者希瑟·吉勒斯寫道。

答:私募股權正處於「學術察看期」。
普林斯頓大學正調降其校務基金報酬的預期,因為其私募資本投資表現令人失望。耶魯大學十年來首次縮減其槓桿收購投資組合。哈佛大學表示,提前出脫部分私募市場投資,如今已成為其長期策略的一部分。
長期以來,私募股權一直將美國最富有的大學視為其最大、也最忠實的客戶群之一。但私人企業投資市場已變得日益擁擠,報酬如今難以追上更廣泛的股市基準。
大學校務基金逐漸依賴曾經豐厚的私募股權報酬,來支應整體預算中更大的比例。根據劍橋顧問公司的數據,截至6月30日止的三年間,這些長期鎖定的投資年化報酬率僅7.4%——其中大部分還只是帳面獲利,這項策略因此受挫。同期間,標普500指數的年漲幅為19.7%。
部分校務基金負責人已逐漸失去耐心。他們正轉向次級市場,機構投資人可以在到期前將私募股權持股出售給其他投資人,通常售價低於基金經理人所宣稱的價值。

這些圖表顯示今年冬天的美國有多瘋狂。
在美國東部,居民正經歷近年來記憶中最嚴寒的季節之一。然而在西部大部分地區,氣溫卻異常溫和,積雪量更創下歷史新低。

本週焦點

星期一:總統節,美股休市。星期二:農曆新年。星期三:聯準會將公布1月27至28日會議紀要,市場將密切關注其中透露的未來降息走向線索。星期四:12月貿易數據即將公布。星期五:12月個人消費支出物價指數(聯準會偏好的通膨指標)公布,同時公布第四季GDP初估值。預計最高法院將在冬季休庭後公布裁決意見。

數字看世界

40%——根據摩根大通研究院的數據,截至2025年5月,自22歲以來已將資金轉入投資帳戶的26歲人士比例,較2015年的8%大幅攀升。這項數據不包括投資401(k)退休帳戶的人。由於無力負擔購屋,年輕一代投資人轉而試圖透過投入股市來累積財富。

最後一則……

這座太浩湖畔的迷你聚落,坐擁全美數一數二昂貴的濱水豪宅。
根據《華爾街日報》母公司新聞集團旗下Realtor.com的一項客製化分析,水晶灣是內華達州北岸一個約200戶住宅的社區,12月的房屋掛牌中位數價格為1490萬美元。這個聚落略顯褪色的商業街緊鄰價值數百萬美元的住宅地產,以陡坡帶來的隱密性與頂級湖景生活備受青睞。

emails.subject: The 10-Point Special Edition: 250 Years of American Entertainment
emails.contentEn:
Your guide to the WSJ's exclusive reporting and analysis.

Ahead of the 250th anniversary of the United States, WSJ is exploring the triumphs, trials and innovations that have shaped America and the world in a special multimedia series, “USA250: The Story of the World's Greatest Economy.” In this edition of The 10-Point, we're taking a look at the evolution of entertainment in America.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

250 Years of American Entertainment

The American monoculture that dominated most of the 20th century is gone.
Pop culture was once the glue that held the U.S. together: Both Chicago factory workers and California farmers loved “Star Wars.” But today we're all watching and listening to different things, fed to us by algorithms designed to divide us into uniquely satisfied consumers, writes Ben Fritz.

Inventions such as the phonograph and the electric guitar have transformed entertainment.
Technology and entertainment in the U.S. have always been in dialogue with one another. These 10 technological marvels had cultural implications that their inventors could barely have imagined.

What's your American culture IQ?
From the origins of “Yankee Doodle” to the first rock 'n' roll single to hit No. 1, there's a lot to know about culture in America. Test yourself with this WSJ quiz to see how well you know the past 250 years of books, music, movies and other culture.

You've probably never heard about these six defining moments in TV history.
American TV viewers have shared triumphs and tragedies, from Neil Armstrong's moonwalk to the 9/11 attacks. But lesser-known moments—like the remote control's debut and the first laugh track—also reshaped the cultural landscape.

Theme parks have turned nostalgia into historical landmarks.
America's amusement parks have acted as time capsules of cultural history since they were introduced in the 19th century. Many of their attractions are rooted in past eras—and some parks have morphed into landmarks in their own right.

These songs defined America.
Nearly every era since the country's founding has had its hit songs, whether measured by copies of sheet-music sold or by position on the Billboard charts. Here's a look at 20 of those songs—and what they reveal about their times.

How did pro football become America's national obsession?
Our collective obsession with the NFL is shaped by both the violence of the sport's spectacle and the gumption of the league's business promoters, writes Andy Serwer.

These people changed the course of American entertainment.
P.T. Barnum and Walt Disney are among the entertainment pioneers who have helped form a distinctly American culture, which reflects the ideals, experiences and struggles of the country's inhabitants.

Here are the most influential American films of the past 110 years.
Though motion pictures have been around for less than half of America's history, few inventions have been as effective at telling the country's story. From “The Birth of a Nation” to “Barbie,” these movies defined cinema—and the U.S.

Young writers shared the early American authors they most admire.
These five writers spoke with WSJ about their personal GOATs of early American literature, and why their long-ago works still resonate with them.
emails.contentZh:
為您導覽《華爾街日報》的獨家報導與分析。

在美國建國250週年即將到來之際,《華爾街日報》正透過一系列特別多媒體專題「USA250:全球最強經濟體的故事」,探索形塑美國與世界的種種成就、挑戰與創新。在本期《The 10-Point》中,我們將帶您一探美國娛樂產業的演變歷程。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

美國娛樂250年

主宰二十世紀大部分時光的美國「單一文化」已不復存在。
流行文化曾是凝聚美國的黏著劑:芝加哥的工廠工人與加州的農民都同樣熱愛《星際大戰》。但如今我們各自觀看、聆聽著不同的內容,由演算法餵養、刻意將我們分割成各自獨立滿足的消費者,班·弗里茨寫道。

留聲機與電吉他等發明,已徹底改變了娛樂產業。
美國的科技與娛樂一直以來相互對話、彼此影響。以下這十項科技奇蹟,對文化造成的影響,是它們的發明者幾乎無法想像的。

您的美國文化智商有多高?
從《洋基歌》的起源,到史上第一首登上排行榜冠軍的搖滾單曲,關於美國文化,有太多值得了解的知識。透過這份《華爾街日報》測驗來考考自己,看看您對過去250年來的書籍、音樂、電影及其他文化了解多少。

您很可能從未聽過電視史上這六個決定性時刻。
從尼爾·阿姆斯壯的月球漫步到911恐怖攻擊,美國電視觀眾共同見證了無數的榮耀與悲劇。但一些較鮮為人知的時刻——如遙控器的問世與首次使用罐頭笑聲——同樣重塑了文化版圖。

主題樂園已將懷舊情懷轉化為歷史地標。
自19世紀問世以來,美國的遊樂園一直扮演著文化歷史時光膠囊的角色。許多園內設施都根植於過去的年代——有些樂園本身甚至已蛻變成獨具意義的地標。

這些歌曲定義了美國。
自建國以來,幾乎每個時代都有屬於自己的暢銷歌曲,無論是以樂譜銷量還是告示牌排行榜名次來衡量。以下是其中20首歌曲的回顧——以及它們所反映的時代樣貌。

職業美式足球如何成為美國的全民狂熱?
我們對國家美式足球聯盟(NFL)的集體癡迷,既源自這項運動場面的暴力奇觀,也源自聯盟商業推廣者的膽識與魄力,安迪·瑟沃寫道。

這些人物改變了美國娛樂產業的走向。
P.T.巴納姆與華特·迪士尼,都是協助塑造獨具美國特色文化的娛樂先驅之一,這種文化反映了這個國家居民的理想、經歷與奮鬥。

以下是過去110年來最具影響力的美國電影。
儘管電影問世的時間還不到美國歷史的一半,但很少有發明能像電影一樣有效地訴說這個國家的故事。從《一個國家的誕生》到《芭比》,這些電影定義了電影藝術——也定義了美國。

年輕作家分享了他們最欽佩的早期美國作家。
這五位作家向《華爾街日報》分享了他們心目中早期美國文學的個人「最佳典範(GOAT)」,以及這些久遠的作品為何至今仍能引起他們的共鳴。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Republicans Show (Some) Resistance to Trump
emails.contentEn:
Your guide to the WSJ's exclusive reporting and analysis.

President Trump faced little GOP resistance this past year. But rank-and-file Republicans are starting to show (some) independence. Now, as the midterms approach, the White House is contending with pushback on multiple fronts, from trade to immigration. The party as a whole could take a hit. At the Munich Security Conference, meanwhile, Secretary of State Marco Rubio worked to repair another frayed relationship as he aimed to recast the president's disputes with European allies as a form of tough love.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

As the midterms approach, Trump and the White House are finding they need to expend more and more effort to keep the GOP rank-and-file in line. Rubio's remarks received a standing ovation in Munich, but some senior European officials said they didn't allay all their concerns about the alliance. Casey Wasserman told staff he's putting his talent agency up for sale. The move follows the release of emails he exchanged years ago with Ghislaine Maxwell. Figure skater Ilia Malinin was expected to strike awe at the Winter Games. Instead, writes Jason Gay, he fell apart during his climactic performance. The Pentagon used Anthropic's AI tool Claude in its operation to capture former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.

FROM THE MARKETS

Even a cooler-than-expected inflation reading couldn't keep stocks from posting their worst week since November. The report showed annual inflation slowed to 2.4% in January, but consumers still saw higher costs for certain items such as computers and appliances. In China, a group of state-linked investors are unloading holdings to keep the AI-stock boom in check. Ozempic has brought a “Napster moment” to Big Pharma, writes David Wainer.

READ IT HERE FIRST

America fell out of love with the sedan—but Detroit wants to bring it back.
As drivers seek more affordable options, U.S. automakers are having second thoughts about abandoning the mass-market sedan. The conundrum is that carmakers get better profit margins on more expensive trucks and SUVs. A U-turn on sedans would be a reversal of uncharacteristic speed, even for Detroit's notoriously fickle industry, report Sharon Terlep and Christopher Otts. But these are unusual times. After prepping for an electric-vehicle revolution, GM, Ford and Stellantis have dialed back their EV plans.

A pilot's parents are working to clear his name after the deadliest crash in decades.
A year ago, Sam Lilley was the first officer in the cockpit of an American Airlines regional jet when it was hit midair by a Black Hawk helicopter, killing all 67 onboard both aircraft. Since the accident, Tim and Sheri Lilley have fought hard to show that their son had done everything right, reports Christopher Kuo. Systemic failures in the FAA and Army led to the crash, the parents believe, a conviction that drove them to push for safety reforms. The Justice Department and other victims' families, meanwhile, have also made their claims about who or what had contributed to the collision, creating unlikely friendships and advocates.

EXPERT TAKE

Q: Top FDA scientist Richard Pazdur quit after he was promoted by Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Why?
The oncologist and former drugs chief at the Food and Drug Administration left his role less than a month after his appointment. Reporter Liz Essley Whyte spoke to him and wrote about why he decided to depart.

A: Pazdur said that under FDA Commissioner Marty Makary, fast-track drug approvals had been politicized in a way he had never experienced in his 26 years at the agency. Past FDA commissioners carefully avoided interfering in individual drug approvals, instead letting the scientific reviewers have sway. “This wall between the commissioner's office and the review staff has been breached,” Pazdur said.
That incident and other frustrations led to Pazdur's abrupt departure in December. As the FDA's drugs chief, Pazdur was responsible for thousands of employees overseeing most of the new medicines the FDA weighs for approval, as well as over-the-counter and generic drugs.
Pazdur is now sounding alarm bells about Makary's leadership. “We have an unclear future of what the FDA will be,” he said.
The FDA's powerful drug division has had five leaders in the past year, contributing to an unprecedented level of turmoil at the agency responsible for ensuring the drugs Americans take are safe and effective. In addition to the drug division turnover, the FDA's vaccines chief was ousted by Kennedy, and his replacement, Dr. Vinay Prasad, was fired and rehired after initially sparking concern at the White House.
The FDA didn't respond to a request for comment.

New York City's looming deficit threatens to curb Mayor Zohran Mamdani's ambitions.
Tax revenue has grown steadily in recent years but failed to keep up with ballooning costs in areas including the city's rental-voucher program and public assistance. New York could face a $2 billion deficit in the current fiscal year and a $10 billion hole in the coming one—a significant challenge for a mayor who has vowed not to cut social programs and has an ambitious affordability agenda that would involve expanding them.

HAPPENING TODAY

Saturday: The U.S. men's hockey team will play Denmark at the Winter Olympics. Sunday: The Munich Security Conference concludes.

THE NUMBER

3,486,000 — The approximate number of downloads of the top dating apps in Saudi Arabia in 2025, up from roughly 862,000 in 2019. Liberalization has opened the door to more casual relationships in the country of 35 million, but society is still catching up.

AND FINALLY...

How far does $1,000 take you on a trip to Paris?
On a recent visit, our writer set out to prove that even on a strict budget, you can eat well, sleep soundly and immerse yourself in the art and culture that draws millions every year. Here's how he checked all the boxes without spending a fortune.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

Opinion: In California, the teachers union is taking political extortion to a whole new level with a coordinated campaign threatening strikes across the state.
emails.contentZh:
為您導覽《華爾街日報》的獨家報導與分析。

過去一年,川普總統幾乎沒有遭遇多少共和黨內的抵抗。但如今基層共和黨人開始展現出(些許)獨立性。隨著期中選舉逼近,白宮正面臨從貿易到移民等多個戰線的反彈,整個政黨都可能因此受挫。與此同時,在慕尼黑安全會議上,國務卿馬可·魯比歐正努力修補另一段緊張的關係,試圖將總統與歐洲盟友之間的爭執,重新包裝成一種「愛之深、責之切」的表現。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

隨著期中選舉逼近,川普與白宮發現他們需要投入越來越多心力,才能讓共和黨基層保持一致步調。魯比歐在慕尼黑的發言獲得起立鼓掌,但部分歐洲資深官員表示,這並未完全消除他們對這個聯盟的憂慮。凱西·瓦瑟曼告訴員工,他打算出售自己的經紀公司。此舉是在他多年前與吉斯蓮·麥斯威爾往來的電子郵件曝光後做出的。花式滑冰選手伊利亞·馬林寧原本被寄予厚望,將在冬奧驚豔全場。但傑森·蓋伊寫道,他卻在關鍵演出中崩潰失常。五角大廈在捕獲前委內瑞拉總統尼可拉斯·馬杜洛的行動中,使用了Anthropic的AI工具Claude。

市場動態

儘管通膨數據優於預期,仍未能阻止股市寫下自去年11月以來最差的一週表現。該報告顯示,1月年度通膨率放緩至2.4%,但消費者在電腦與家電等特定商品上仍感受到成本上升。在中國,一批與政府有關聯的投資人正拋售持股,以壓制AI概念股的過熱漲勢。大衛·韋恩納寫道,Ozempic為大型製藥業帶來了一個「Napster時刻」。

獨家搶先看

美國人已對房車失去熱情——但底特律想把它找回來。
隨著駕駛人尋求更實惠的選擇,美國車廠正重新考慮放棄大眾市場房車的決定。難題在於,車廠在售價更高的貨卡與休旅車上能獲得更好的利潤率。莎朗·特勒普與克里斯多福·奧茨報導,即便對以善變著稱的底特律車廠而言,在房車議題上來個大轉彎,轉變速度也顯得異常之快。但這是個不尋常的時代。在為電動車革命做足準備後,通用汽車、福特與Stellantis已相繼縮減電動車計畫。

一名飛行員的父母,正努力為他洗刷數十年來最致命空難的污名。
一年前,山姆·萊利是美國航空一架支線客機的副機師,該機在半空中與一架黑鷹直升機相撞,兩機上共67人全數罹難。事故發生後,提姆與雪莉·萊利夫婦一直努力想證明他們的兒子當時做的每一步都是正確的,克里斯多福·郭報導。這對父母相信,是聯邦航空總署(FAA)與陸軍的系統性失靈導致了這起空難,這份信念促使他們積極推動安全改革。與此同時,司法部與其他罹難者家屬也對誰或什麼原因造成這起相撞事故各自提出主張,意外促成了一些不尋常的友誼與倡議者。

專家觀點

問:FDA頂尖科學家理查·帕茲杜爾在遭小羅伯特·甘迺迪拔擢後卻選擇辭職。為什麼?
這位腫瘤學家、前食品藥物管理局藥品部門負責人,在獲得任命後不到一個月便離職。記者麗茲·艾斯利·懷特採訪了他,撰文說明他決定離開的原因。

答:帕茲杜爾表示,在FDA局長馬蒂·馬卡里的領導下,快速核准藥物的流程已被政治化到他在該機構任職26年來從未見過的程度。過去的FDA局長一向謹慎避免干預個別藥物的核准,而是讓科學審查人員擁有決定權。帕茲杜爾說:「局長辦公室與審查人員之間的這道防火牆已被打破。」
這起事件加上其他令人沮喪的因素,導致帕茲杜爾在12月突然離職。身為FDA藥品部門負責人,帕茲杜爾曾負責監督數千名員工,他們負責審核FDA所評估的大多數新藥,以及成藥與學名藥。
帕茲杜爾如今正對馬卡里的領導方式發出警訊。他說:「FDA未來會變成什麼樣子,我們並不清楚。」
FDA這個握有重權的藥品部門在過去一年間已換了五任領導人,使得這個負責確保美國人所服用藥物安全有效的機構,陷入前所未有的動盪。除了藥品部門的人事更迭外,FDA的疫苗部門負責人也遭甘迺迪撤換,其繼任者維奈·普拉薩德醫師則在最初引發白宮疑慮後,遭到解僱又復職。
FDA並未回應置評請求。

紐約市迫在眉睫的財政赤字,可能限縮市長佐赫蘭·馬姆達尼的施政野心。
近年來稅收持續穩定成長,但仍跟不上該市房租券計畫與公共援助等領域不斷膨脹的成本。紐約市本財政年度可能面臨20億美元赤字,下個財政年度更可能出現100億美元的資金缺口——這對一位誓言不刪減社會福利計畫、且懷有雄心壯志、意欲擴大這些計畫的可負擔性議程的市長而言,是一項重大挑戰。

今日焦點

星期六:美國男子冰球隊將在冬奧對戰丹麥。星期日:慕尼黑安全會議閉幕。

數字看世界

348.6萬——2025年沙烏地阿拉伯頂尖交友App的大約下載次數,較2019年的約86.2萬次大幅成長。這個擁有3500萬人口的國家,自由化已為更多輕鬆隨性的關係開啟了大門,但整體社會觀念仍在迎頭趕上。

最後一則……

1000美元的預算,在巴黎旅行能撐多遠?
在最近一次造訪中,我們的作者試圖證明,即便預算嚴格控管,您依然能吃得好、睡得香甜,並沉浸在每年吸引數百萬遊客的藝術與文化之中。以下是他如何在不花大錢的情況下,做到面面俱到。

新聞編輯室之外

評論:在加州,教師工會正透過一場協調一致、威脅在全州發動罷工的行動,將政治勒索手段推向了全新高度。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Constant Chaos Inside Kristi Noem’s DHS
emails.contentEn:
Your guide to the WSJ's exclusive reporting and analysis.

Throughout her tenure as secretary of Homeland Security, Kristi Noem has attempted to burnish her personal stardom at every turn. With TV-ready hair and makeup, she has donned flak jackets on ICE raids and recorded messages urging immigrants to self-deport. Noem and adviser Corey Lewandowski frequently berate DHS staff. In one incident, Lewandowski fired a Coast Guard pilot after Noem's blanket was left on a plane. Simmering criticism over Noem's leadership exploded in Minneapolis, jeopardizing her grip over DHS. Now, Congress has until midnight to reach a funding deal or the agency could shut down.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

Goldman Sachs general counsel Kathryn Ruemmler will step down after files showed she remained a close ally of Jeffrey Epstein's through his 2019 arrest. The U.S. is sending its largest and most advanced aircraft carrier to the Middle East, as it steps up plans for a potential attack on Iran. The classified whistleblower complaint against Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard is related to an intercepted conversation about Jared Kushner. Iran's clampdown is now targeting the reformist politicians who took a stand against the bloody crackdown on protesters. In Venezuela, small cracks are showing in the government's repression machine.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

DJIA Futures 49398.00 (-0.25%); S&P 500 Futures 6843.00 (-0.12%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 24755.00 (-0.05%) as of 2/13/2026, 6:00:02 AM ET.

U.S. stocks have rallied, but the dollar's slide and slowing foreign purchases of Treasurys are warning signs that foreign investors are nervous about the U.S. A memory-chip shortage is squeezing the world's biggest electronics companies—and it's set to get worse. The artificial-intelligence gold rush is breaking a Silicon Valley taboo: cashing out before the IPO.

READ IT HERE FIRST

A pilot was fired over Noem's missing blanket—one example of the chaos inside DHS.
Noem has carried out confrontational operations over the objections of longtime immigration officials who warned such flashy displays would discredit the department's ultimate mission, according to two dozen current and former administration officials. Instead, she's made the case that her approach would lead to more arrests as well as induce more people to leave on their own. Though some in Trump's inner circle have tried to persuade the president to fire Noem and her top adviser, according to administration officials, he has so far resisted, saying publicly he has no plans to dismiss her, report Michelle Hackman, Josh Dawsey and Tarini Parti.

The Guthrie kidnapping is making a difficult family conversation about aging in place even harder.
The Nancy Guthrie case, while a nightmare for one high-profile family, is striking a personal chord with millions. We all have aging relatives or friends and worry about something happening to them. Many live alone, hundreds of miles away. They may have lots of friends or golf five times a week, but are still 80 or 90 and likely to have chronic health conditions. What if they fall, get in an accident, get scammed? The Guthrie case adds another, more horrific scenario, writes Clare Ansberry. The search for Guthrie continues but with fizzled leads and, so far, few answers.

EXPERT TAKE

Q: How would a Department of Homeland Security shutdown affect ICE and TSA?
Funding is set to lapse this weekend unless Democrats and Republicans reach a deal. Reporter Anvee Bhutani explains what that would mean for DHS and the agencies it oversees:

A: DHS is the only department on a shutdown clock right now.
Congress deliberately split it off from the rest of the government's appropriations, and it is currently being funded on a short-term continuing resolution that expires today. The move reflected unresolved disagreements over immigration enforcement and oversight.
If there is a funding lapse, agencies like ICE would have access to pre-existing funds from Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill Act. This means most staff could continue to be paid even if the current stopgap funding bill expires, lessening pressure on lawmakers to resolve the impasse.
TSA airport employees would continue working, but without pay. Travelers could face flight delays if there is a longer shutdown and staffing shortages develop because of missed paychecks. All government employees typically receive backpay once a shutdown ends.
Most DHS headquarters staff, policy offices and oversight units aren't considered essential and would be furloughed.
To back a DHS funding package, Democrats are pushing for requirements that would mandate body cameras and visible identification for ICE and CBP agents, among other initiatives.
Republican leaders are using the coming deadline to push their own priorities, including preserving agent anonymity during operations.

A German general prepares his country for war—and the clock is ticking.
Germany's top military officer, Gen. Carsten Breuer, is racing to prepare the country's armed forces for war. Germany's military-intelligence agency estimates that within the next three years, Russia will have amassed enough weaponry and trained enough troops to be able to start a wider war across Europe. Breuer, 61, says a smaller attack could come at any time. To that end, he has been waging a multi-front campaign to speed Germany's rearmament and conflict preparedness.

HAPPENING TODAY

21-year-old U.S. figure skater Ilia Malinin is the overwhelming favorite to win gold in the men's final at the Winter Olympics. Economic data: The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release the postponed consumer-price index for January. Earnings: Moderna, Wendy's.

THE NUMBER

>$50 billion — The combined write-downs following years of investments into electric-vehicle technology from the Detroit Big Three: GM, Ford and Jeep maker Stellantis. The automakers' retreats come as Republican lawmakers abolished a lucrative federal tax credit for EVs last fall while doing away with federal fuel-efficiency mandates. But even with federal support, EV demand was below expectations.

AND FINALLY...

They're the only Olympians having a less romantic week than that Norwegian biathlete.
For most couples, the ultimate relationship stress tests involve household temperatures, airport arrival times and trips to Ikea. For engaged hockey stars Anna Kjellbin and Ronja Savolainen, there is another source of domestic strife: smashing each other into the boards as they battle for Olympic gold. Kjellbin is Swedish. Savolainen is Finnish. And before the Games are over, they could find themselves on a romantic Italian date, facing off in the elimination round of the Olympic women's hockey tournament.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

Opinion: The EPA yesterday at long last repealed Barack Obama's so-called endangerment finding that declared greenhouse gas emissions a threat to public health and safety. Cue the apocalyptic warnings unhinged from reality.
emails.contentZh:
為您導覽《華爾街日報》的獨家報導與分析。

在擔任國土安全部長期間,克莉絲蒂·諾姆一直試圖在每個時刻打磨自己的個人光環。她頂著上鏡的髮妝造型,穿上防彈背心參與ICE(移民及海關執法局)突襲行動,並錄製呼籲移民自行遣返的訊息。諾姆與顧問柯瑞·勒萬多斯基經常斥責DHS(國土安全部)員工。曾有一次事件,勒萬多斯基因諾姆的毛毯被遺留在飛機上,便將一名海岸防衛隊飛行員解僱。外界對諾姆領導方式積壓已久的批評,在明尼亞波利斯爆發,危及她對DHS的掌控。如今,國會必須在午夜前達成資金協議,否則該部門可能面臨停擺。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

高盛法務長凱瑟琳·魯姆勒將卸任,原因是文件顯示她在傑佛瑞·愛潑斯坦2019年遭逮捕前,一直與他保持親密盟友關係。美國正將其最大、最先進的航空母艦派往中東,以加強對伊朗發動潛在攻擊的計畫。針對國家情報總監圖爾西·加巴德的機密舉報投訴,與一段涉及賈瑞德·庫許納的截獲對話有關。伊朗的鎮壓行動如今正瞄準那些曾挺身反對血腥鎮壓抗議者的改革派政治人物。在委內瑞拉,政府鎮壓機器已出現一些小裂痕。

市場即時看

道瓊工業指數期貨 49398.00(-0.25%);標普500期貨 6843.00(-0.12%);那斯達克100期貨 24755.00(-0.05%),截至美東時間2026年2月13日上午6:00:02。

美股已出現反彈,但美元的跌勢與外國購買美國公債步伐的放緩,是外國投資人對美國感到緊張不安的警訊。記憶體晶片短缺正擠壓全球最大電子公司的獲利空間——而且情況預計還會惡化。人工智慧淘金熱正打破矽谷的一項禁忌:在IPO之前就先套現離場。

獨家搶先看

一名飛行員因諾姆遺失的毛毯而遭解僱——這是DHS內部混亂的一個縮影。
根據二十多位現任與前任政府官員的說法,諾姆一再推行對抗性行動,不顧資深移民官員的反對意見,這些官員警告,如此高調招搖的展示只會損害該部門的最終使命。相反地,她主張自己的做法將帶來更多逮捕行動,同時促使更多人自願離境。據政府官員透露,儘管川普核心圈中有人試圖說服總統解僱諾姆及其首席顧問,但他至今仍拒絕這麼做,並公開表示自己並無解僱她的打算,蜜雪兒·哈克曼、喬許·道西與塔里尼·帕爾蒂報導。

古思里綁架案讓一場關於在地養老的艱難家庭對話變得更加棘手。
南希·古思里案,雖然對一個備受矚目的家庭而言是場噩夢,卻在數百萬人心中引發了個人共鳴。我們都有年邁的親人或朋友,也都擔心他們遭遇意外。許多人獨居,遠在數百英里之外。他們或許有很多朋友,或每週打五次高爾夫球,但終究已經80、90歲,很可能患有慢性疾病。萬一他們跌倒、發生意外、被詐騙怎麼辦?古思里案更增添了另一種、更加可怕的情境,克萊爾·安斯貝里寫道。搜尋古思里的行動仍在持續,但線索逐漸中斷,迄今答案寥寥無幾。

專家觀點

問:國土安全部若停擺,將如何影響ICE與TSA(運輸安全管理局)?
除非民主黨與共和黨達成協議,否則資金將於本週末中斷。記者安薇·布塔尼解釋這對DHS及其監管的機構意味著什麼:

答:DHS目前是唯一面臨停擺倒數計時的部門。
國會刻意將其與政府其他撥款分開處理,目前是依靠一項將於今日到期的短期持續撥款決議案提供資金。此舉反映出各界在移民執法與監管議題上尚未解決的分歧。
若出現資金缺口,ICE等機構仍可動用川普《大而美法案》中既有的資金。這意味著即便目前的權宜撥款法案到期,大多數員工仍能繼續領薪,從而減輕了國會議員解決僵局的壓力。
TSA機場員工將繼續工作,但無薪。若停擺時間拉長、且因員工未領到薪水而出現人手短缺,旅客可能面臨航班延誤。所有政府員工在停擺結束後通常都能領到補發薪資。
大多數DHS總部員工、政策辦公室與監管單位並不被視為必要人員,將被強制休無薪假。
為支持DHS撥款方案,民主黨正推動要求ICE與CBP(海關及邊境保護局)幹員配戴隨身攝影機及可見識別證等強制規定。
共和黨領袖則利用即將到來的截止期限,推動自身的優先事項,包括在行動期間保留幹員的匿名性。

一位德國將軍正為國家備戰——時間正在流逝。
德國最高軍事將領卡斯滕·布洛伊爾將軍,正加緊為國家武裝部隊備戰。德國軍事情報機構估計,未來三年內,俄羅斯將累積足夠的武器裝備並訓練出足夠的部隊,足以在全歐洲發動一場更大規模的戰爭。現年61歲的布洛伊爾表示,規模較小的攻擊隨時可能發生。為此,他一直在多條戰線上發起行動,加速德國的重整軍備與應戰準備。

今日焦點

21歲的美國花式滑冰選手伊利亞·馬林寧,是冬奧男子單人滑決賽奪金的絕對大熱門。經濟數據:勞工統計局將公布延後發布的1月消費者物價指數。財報:莫德納、溫蒂漢堡。

數字看世界

超過500億美元——底特律三大車廠通用汽車、福特,以及Jeep母公司Stellantis,多年投資電動車技術後累計的減損金額。這些車廠的撤退之舉,正值共和黨議員去年秋天廢除了一項對電動車頗為優厚的聯邦稅收抵免,同時取消聯邦燃油效率規定之際。但即便有聯邦支持,電動車需求仍低於預期。

最後一則……

他們是本屆奧運中,唯一一對本週浪漫指數比那位挪威兩項選手還低的運動員。
對大多數情侶而言,終極的感情壓力測試,不外乎家中溫度設定、機場接機時間,以及跑一趟宜家家居。但對已訂婚的冰球明星安娜·謝爾賓與蘿妮亞·薩沃萊寧來說,還有另一種家庭紛爭的來源:在爭奪奧運金牌時,把彼此撞向界牆。謝爾賓是瑞典人,薩沃萊寧是芬蘭人。而在本屆奧運結束前,兩人可能會在奧運女子冰球錦標賽的淘汰賽中正面對決,賽後再共赴一場浪漫的義式約會。

新聞編輯室之外

評論:美國環保署昨日終於廢除了歐巴馬所謂的「危害認定」,該認定曾宣告溫室氣體排放對公共衛生與安全構成威脅。準備迎接一波脫離現實的末日式警告吧。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: A Trump Ally's Gamble to Unlock Venezuela's Oil
emails.contentEn:
The American workforce is increasingly donning scrubs. Yesterday's jobs report reflects rising demand for people in healthcare and social services, but a bleaker environment for factory workers and cubicle dwellers. Over the past year, demand for healthcare workers has quietly propped up the labor market as other sectors reined in hiring, or even shed jobs. Healthcare is outperforming, though economists warn of a heavy reliance on a single industry. Ashby Jones, the Journal's deputy economics editor, breaks down the report.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. Nearly all of the 130,000 new jobs added to the U.S. economy in January were healthcare jobs or positions related to healthcare. The Chinese owners of the famed Waldorf Astoria in New York City are preparing to put the hotel up for sale, only months after it reopened. Elon Musk announced a reorganization of xAI, his artificial-intelligence startup, just days after merging it with SpaceX, his rockets-and-satellites business. A fresh wave of pressure has left Russia's most important industry—oil—in a precarious state.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 50338.00 +133.00 (0.26%); S&P 500 Futures 6978.75 +18.25 (0.26%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 25344.25 +55.75 (0.22%). Source: Factset, Market data as of 2/12/2026, 5:53:58 AM ET.

A new AI borrowing frenzy and lingering fears about potential defaults haven't deterred investors hungry for bonds from U.S. companies, states and cities. A major concern for investors during the AI boom is that they can't find depreciation expenses listed on big tech companies' income statements, writes Jonathan Weil.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. Savior or 'supervillain'? A Trump ally gambles to unlock Venezuela's oil.
Few Americans have worked harder and longer than Florida energy mogul Harry Sargeant III to pry open the Venezuela market. And with stakes in companies that could potentially produce hundreds of thousands of barrels of crude a day, arguably no one had more at stake financially in the surprise U.S. military raid in Venezuela than him. The former Top Gun pilot—and sometime golfing partner of Donald Trump's—is now in a position to be the latest of the president's allies to reap a windfall based on his second-term policies and actions. Sargeant is also deeply unpopular within the Venezuelan political opposition, report Scott Patterson, Kejal Vyas and Alex Leary.

4. The mega-rich are turning their mansions into impenetrable fortresses.
In an era of high-profile violence—including the suspected abduction of Savannah Guthrie's mother from her Arizona home over a week ago—the wealthy are investing heavily in their personal security, particularly when it comes to their homes. Security measures such as biometric access controls and laser-powered perimeter defenses are now mainstream items in luxury residences. Executive-protection teams and armed guards patrol gated enclaves and suburban estates. The shift reflects a hardening view among the affluent: Traditional policing and communal safety are no longer enough, report Katherine Clarke and E.B. Solomont.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: What can a cold snap tell us about the U.S. power grid?
A winter storm brought freezing temperatures across the U.S. two weeks ago and still holds much of the Northeast in its grip. Americans cranked up the heat, posing the biggest test of the electric grid this season. Reporter Jennifer Hiller shares key takeaways:
A: When the Arctic blast sent wholesale power prices soaring, cryptocurrency miners powered down their operations. Data centers for cloud computing and AI kept using electricity at a high and steady rate, according to research and consulting firm Wood Mackenzie.
Ahead of the storm, the Energy Department ordered grid operators to be prepared to take extraordinary steps to tap in to backup power generation at data centers or manufacturers.
Grid operators and utilities countrywide managed tighter supplies and issued varying levels of alerts—but avoided rolling blackouts.
The weak point emerged at the usual spot—the smaller distribution lines and poles that carry electricity through cities and neighborhoods. Across the South, where ice accumulated instead of snow, hundreds of thousands of customers lost power.
The U.S. leaned on fossil fuels to get through the storm. That was especially true in New England, where natural-gas generation and electricity imports make up a large share of power supplies.
Coal and natural-gas use also surged as soaring demand and frozen gas fields led to a record drawdown in supplies.

6. Here's how NATO hunts for Russian submarines in the Arctic.
The Journal's Daniel Michaels joined a Spanish warship for NATO military exercises as the alliance tries to show Trump it can take on Russia's growing presence in the region.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. Millions of Bangladeshis voted in national parliamentary elections today, the first since student-led protests in 2024 ousted the country's authoritarian leader. Earnings: Coinbase, Applied Materials, Airbnb, Hyatt, DraftKings.

THE NUMBER

8. 25,000 — The approximate number of jobs lost in the financial-activities sector from a year earlier, according to the latest jobs report from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The past year was lackluster for most white-collar workers. Economic uncertainty has dissuaded many of the sector's employers from hiring. And a growing share say that they are experimenting with the use of AI to replace some functions.

AND FINALLY...

9. The Olympics have invaded Milan. Italians would rather watch the apocalypse.
In the shadow of the Duomo, the Milan Cortina Winter Games are inescapable. Tourists throng the Olympic megastore. But only a short walk away, at the world's most storied opera house, all that fanfare fades into Wagnerian gloom. During the Games, La Scala is producing only one opera, an epic tale about a world consumed by cleansing fire. Before a recent matinee of Richard Wagner's "Götterdämmerung," most operagoers were looking forward to escaping the madness of the Olympics for 5½ hours.
Speaking of winter sports: Being an alpine ace can help you stand out at work, especially with company ski outings on the rise, writes Callum Borchers.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: The job market isn't as stagnant as many feared, as private employers returned to hiring in January.

emails.contentZh:
美國勞動力正日益「換上醫護服」。昨天公布的就業報告顯示,醫療保健和社會服務業的需求持續上升,但工廠工人和坐辦公室的白領環境卻更加黯淡。過去一年,醫療保健產業的用人需求悄悄撐起了整體勞動市場,而其他產業則縮減招聘,甚至裁員。醫療保健表現優於大盤,但經濟學家警告,經濟過度依賴單一產業存在風險。《華爾街日報》副經濟編輯阿什比·瓊斯(Ashby Jones)為讀者解讀這份報告。

艾瑪·塔克(Emma Tucker)
《華爾街日報》總編輯

【今日頭條】

1. 一月份美國新增的13萬個工作機會中,幾乎全部屬於醫療保健或相關職位。紐約著名的華爾道夫酒店(Waldorf Astoria)的中資業主正準備出售這家酒店,距離酒店重新開業僅數月。伊隆·馬斯克(Elon Musk)宣布重組其人工智慧新創公司xAI,就在該公司與他旗下的火箭和衛星業務SpaceX合併數天之後。俄羅斯最重要的產業——石油業,正面臨新一波壓力,處境岌岌可危。

【市場直擊】

2. 道瓊期貨50338.00,上漲133.00點(0.26%);標普500期貨6978.75,上漲18.25點(0.26%);那斯達克100期貨25344.25,上漲55.75點(0.22%)。資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年2月12日美東時間上午5:53:58。

儘管人工智慧掀起新一波舉債熱潮,加上對潛在違約的疑慮揮之不去,投資人對美國企業、州政府與地方政府發行債券的胃口依然強勁。喬納森·魏爾(Jonathan Weil)撰文指出,在這波AI熱潮中,投資人的一大隱憂是,他們在大型科技公司的損益表中找不到折舊費用的蹤影。

【獨家搶先報導】

3. 救星還是「超級反派」?川普盟友豪賭解封委內瑞拉石油。
論在委內瑞拉市場拼搏的時間之長、投入之深,少有美國人能與佛羅里達能源大亨哈利·薩金特三世(Harry Sargeant III)相比。他持有多家公司的股份,這些公司有潛力日產數十萬桶原油,可以說在美國此次出人意料的委內瑞拉軍事突襲行動中,沒有人比他承擔的財務風險更大。這位前「捍衛戰士」飛行員——也是川普偶爾的高爾夫球友——如今有望成為又一位因總統第二任期政策與行動而大發橫財的川普盟友。薩金特在委內瑞拉政壇反對派中也極不受歡迎。報導:斯科特·帕特森(Scott Patterson)、凱賈爾·維亞斯(Kejal Vyas)與亞歷克斯·萊瑞(Alex Leary)。

4. 超級富豪正將自家豪宅打造成銅牆鐵壁。
在這個高調暴力事件頻傳的年代——包括一週多前莎凡娜·古思里(Savannah Guthrie)的母親疑似在亞利桑那州家中遭綁架——富人正大舉投資個人安全,尤其著重於自宅防護。生物辨識門禁系統與雷射防禦周界等設施如今已成為豪宅的標準配備。行政保安團隊與武裝警衛巡邏在門禁社區與郊區豪宅之間。這種轉變反映出富裕階層日益強硬的觀點:傳統警力與社區安全已不足以保障安全。報導:凱瑟琳·克拉克(Katherine Clarke)與E.B.所羅門(E.B. Solomont)。

【專家解讀】

5. 問:一波寒流能告訴我們美國電網的什麼狀況?
兩週前一場冬季風暴為全美帶來凍寒氣溫,東北部至今仍未解凍。美國人紛紛開暖氣取暖,對電網構成本季最大考驗。記者珍妮弗·希勒(Jennifer Hiller)整理出以下重點:
答:北極寒流導致躉售電價飆升時,加密貨幣礦工紛紛關閉營運。根據研究顧問公司伍德麥肯茲(Wood Mackenzie)的數據,雲端運算與AI用的資料中心則持續以高且穩定的速率用電。
風暴來襲前,美國能源部已要求電網營運商做好準備,必要時可採取非常手段,調用資料中心或製造商的備用發電設施。
全美電網營運商與公用事業公司在供應吃緊之下勉力維持運作,發布不同等級的警戒,但都成功避免了輪流停電。
薄弱環節仍出現在老地方——輸送電力進入城市與社區的較小型配電線路與電線桿。在降下的是冰而非雪的南部地區,數十萬用戶因此斷電。
美國靠化石燃料撐過這場風暴,新英格蘭地區尤其如此,該地天然氣發電與進口電力占供電比重甚高。
隨著需求飆升、天然氣田因寒凍而產量受限,煤炭與天然氣的用量也創下供應提取新高。

6. 北約如何在北極追蹤俄羅斯潛艦。
《華爾街日報》記者丹尼爾·邁克爾斯(Daniel Michaels)登上一艘西班牙軍艦參與北約軍事演習,北約試圖藉此向川普展現,自己有能力應對俄羅斯在該地區日益擴大的軍事存在。

【今日焦點】

7. 數百萬孟加拉人今日參與全國國會選舉投票,這是2024年學生主導的抗議活動推翻該國威權領導人以來的首次選舉。財報:Coinbase、應用材料(Applied Materials)、Airbnb、凱悅(Hyatt)、DraftKings。

【數字看時事】

8. 25,000——根據美國勞工統計局最新就業報告,金融活動產業相較去年同期流失的工作機會約略數字。過去一年對多數白領工作者來說表現平淡,經濟不確定性使該產業許多雇主不願招聘,越來越多雇主表示正在嘗試以AI取代部分職能。

【最後一則】

9. 奧運攻佔了米蘭,義大利人卻寧願在旁邊看世界末日。
在米蘭大教堂的陰影下,米蘭-科爾蒂納冬奧無所不在,遊客擠滿了奧運紀念品旗艦店。但只要走幾步路,來到這座舉世聞名的歌劇院,滿場的節慶氣氛便瞬間轉為華格納式的陰鬱。奧運期間,史卡拉歌劇院只演出一齣歌劇——一部講述世界被淨化之火吞噬的史詩故事。在理查·華格納《諸神的黃昏》一場近期的日場演出開演前,大多數觀眾都期待能藉此逃離奧運的喧囂,享受五個半小時的清靜。
說到冬季運動:身懷滑雪絕技也能讓你在職場上脫穎而出,尤其隨著公司滑雪團建活動日益盛行,卡勒姆·博切斯(Callum Borchers)撰文報導。

【新聞編輯室之外】

10. 評論:一月份民間雇主恢復招聘,顯示就業市場並不如許多人擔心的那樣停滯不前。
《華爾街日報》Buy Side:精選幾款頂級高息儲蓄帳戶,幫你打敗平均利率。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The $5 Billion Fortune in the Epstein Files
emails.contentEn:
What do personal finances look like for someone worth billions? The Epstein files provide a rare look. The complex finances of former Apollo Global Management CEO Leon Black, who turned to Epstein for tax and estate-planning advice, are laid out in the Justice Department's recent releases, down to the exact balances in each of his 69 bank accounts. The documents offer an exceptionally granular look at the strategies used by many of the ultrarich to build wealth and minimize their tax bills.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. Activist investor Ancora Holdings has built a roughly $200 million stake in Warner Bros. Discovery and is planning to oppose Warner's deal with Netflix. Nine people were killed in a mass shooting in Canada and at least 25 people were injured. OpenAI fired one of its top executives, on the grounds of sexual discrimination, after she voiced opposition to the rollout of AI erotica in its ChatGPT product. The U.S. is sending 200 troops to Nigeria to train the country's military to fight Islamist militants.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 50309.00 +36.00 (0.07%); S&P 500 Futures 6958.75 -2.75 (0.04%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 25173.00 -45.25 (0.18%). Source: Factset, Market data as of 2/11/2026, 5:58:34 AM ET.

Fake invoices duped a BlackRock unit into making a $400 million loan. Europe's growing reliance on American gas looks foolish given how unpredictable the White House has become, writes Carol Ryan.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. The Epstein files reveal the complex finances behind a $5 billion fortune.
The documents are dated, so Black's finances are different today. But they offer a window into the financial habits of the ultrawealthy. Some of the richest Americans borrow, even though they are worth billions on paper. And they spend millions of dollars on things like rare books and Chinese bronzes. Black's art collection, book collection and personal items were worth $2.8 billion, report Rachel Louise Ensign and Miriam Gottfried. Black stepped down as Apollo CEO in 2021 after a review found he paid Epstein $158 million for his services, though the probe found no evidence he was involved in Epstein's criminal activities. A spokesman for Black declined to comment.

4. Hands-free driving systems confuse drivers, but carmakers are pushing for more.
Ford is a leader in the push to automate driving. More than two million Ford cars and trucks in 2025 were equipped with its BlueCruise driving system or some of its elements. But some drivers have found the technology confusing, reports Ryan Felton. Ford has long known about the dangers. Confidential company documents show Ford learned while developing BlueCruise that some drivers didn't understand how to use certain features. Ford told the Journal it took steps to improve BlueCruise before rolling it out. After two deadly crashes in 2024, federal regulators are looking into whether the technology is still posing problems for drivers.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: How are big tech companies planning to skirt Trump's $100,000 H-1B fee?
In September, the Trump administration announced its new fee for the coveted H-1B visa. Some giant firms are discussing ways to avoid paying, while smaller ones have fewer options, explains reporter Amrith Ramkumar.
A: Amazon, Google, Microsoft and others generally plan to find workers in categories that don't have to pay the fee, including existing H-1B visa holders, students and people on other types of visas, according to people familiar with the companies' plans.
Some of the companies have been reducing their reliance on the H-1B program. But many smaller companies can't easily navigate the policy changes or invest in cheaper alternatives.
The H-1B visa is the main pathway to the U.S. for highly skilled foreign workers.
Every March, the government conducts a lottery that decides who will receive the new 85,000 visas available for the coming year. The administration recently changed the lottery to give workers who will be paid higher salaries better odds, another factor expected to favor the top tech companies.
One common program used by big tech companies is the Optional Practical Training program, which gives foreign graduates at U.S. universities temporary employment after graduation, typically for a year. Those with STEM degrees can get another two years of employment before transferring to the H-1B program. Those employees won't have to pay the H-1B fee.

6. Getting a job is harder than toppling a government for Bangladesh's Gen Z.
In 2024, young Bangladeshis frustrated with their job prospects took to the streets. The demonstrations grew into a revolution that toppled Bangladesh's authoritarian leader and helped inspire a string of similar protests in Nepal, Indonesia and Madagascar. But now, as Bangladesh prepares to vote in the first national elections since that revolution, some young protesters are losing hope that new leaders can solve their generation's problems.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. The January jobs report is due, after a temporary government shutdown delayed its release. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is set to meet with President Trump in Washington, D.C., where they are expected to discuss Iran. Earnings: Cisco, McDonald's, Kraft Heinz, Shopify, Hilton, T-Mobile.

THE NUMBER

8. 54 — The age of Rich Ruohonen, an alternate for the U.S. men's curling team at the 2026 Milano Cortina Games. Ruohonen, a personal-injury attorney, could become the oldest American athlete in Winter Olympics history. All he needs is for someone to slip and fall. The irony, Ruohonen's teammate Aidan Oldenburg said, is not lost on Team USA.

AND FINALLY...

9. Our travel columnist tried Royal Caribbean's new beach club—but passed on the overpriced cabana.
Royal Caribbean's latest effort to capture a bigger share of passengers' dollars is Royal Beach Club in the Bahamas, the cruise line's first stand-alone beach club. Another beach club is due to open in Greece this year. Unlike Royal Caribbean's private island in the Bahamas, cruisers have to pay extra to visit. One cabana goes for $10,000 for the day. Executives gush about early results. Columnist Dawn Gilbertson paid $175 to visit the club and see if it's worth the hype.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: MedPAC has been co-opted by progressives who dislike private markets and the Medicare Advantage program for seniors. Why does Washington need one more government health policy shop lobbying for more control over American healthcare?

emails.contentZh:
一個身家數十億美元的人,個人財務究竟是什麼樣子?愛潑斯坦文件提供了難得一見的窺探機會。阿波羅全球管理公司(Apollo Global Management)前執行長里昂·布萊克(Leon Black)曾向愛潑斯坦諮詢稅務與遺產規劃建議,他複雜的財務狀況在司法部近期公布的文件中一覽無遺,細節精確到他69個銀行帳戶的餘額。這些文件極為詳盡地揭露了許多超級富豪用以累積財富、將稅負降到最低的種種策略。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

【今日頭條】

1. 維權投資人安科拉控股(Ancora Holdings)已建立華納兄弟探索公司(Warner Bros. Discovery)約2億美元的持股部位,並計畫反對華納與Netflix的併購案。加拿大一起大規模槍擊案造成9人死亡,至少25人受傷。OpenAI一名高階主管因反對在ChatGPT產品中推出AI情色內容而遭到解僱,理由是性別歧視。美國將派遣200名軍人前往奈及利亞,協助訓練當地軍隊打擊伊斯蘭主義叛亂分子。

【市場直擊】

2. 道瓊期貨50309.00,上漲36.00點(0.07%);標普500期貨6958.75,下跌2.75點(0.04%);那斯達克100期貨25173.00,下跌45.25點(0.18%)。資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年2月11日美東時間上午5:58:34。

假發票詐騙了貝萊德(BlackRock)旗下一個部門,使其放出一筆4億美元的貸款。卡蘿·萊恩(Carol Ryan)撰文指出,鑑於白宮如今變幻莫測,歐洲日益依賴美國天然氣的做法看來相當不智。

【獨家搶先報導】

3. 愛潑斯坦文件揭露一筆50億美元財富背後錯綜複雜的財務狀況。
這些文件年代已久,布萊克如今的財務狀況早已不同,但它們讓外界得以一窺超級富豪的理財習慣。部分身家最雄厚的美國人儘管帳面上坐擁數十億財富,卻仍選擇借貸,並豪擲數百萬美元購買珍本書籍與中國青銅器等物品。瑞秋·露易絲·恩辛(Rachel Louise Ensign)與米里亞姆·戈特弗里德(Miriam Gottfried)報導,布萊克的藝術收藏、藏書與個人物品總值達28億美元。布萊克於2021年在一項調查發現他為愛潑斯坦的「服務」支付了1.58億美元後辭去阿波羅執行長一職,不過調查並未發現他涉入愛潑斯坦犯罪活動的證據。布萊克的發言人拒絕置評。

4. 免持駕駛系統讓駕駛人一頭霧水,但車廠仍持續加碼推廣。
福特是推動自動駕駛的領頭羊。2025年,福特超過200萬輛汽車與卡車配備了BlueCruise免持駕駛系統或其部分功能。但萊恩·費爾頓(Ryan Felton)報導指出,部分駕駛人發現這項技術令人困惑。福特其實早已知悉相關風險——內部機密文件顯示,福特在研發BlueCruise期間便已發現,部分駕駛人不理解某些功能該如何使用。福特向本報表示,在推出產品前已採取措施加以改進。2024年發生兩起致命車禍後,聯邦監理機關正在調查這項技術是否仍對駕駛人構成問題。

【專家解讀】

5. 問:大型科技公司打算如何規避川普祭出的10萬美元H-1B簽證費用?
去年9月,川普政府宣布針對搶手的H-1B簽證徵收新費用。記者阿姆里斯·拉姆庫馬(Amrith Ramkumar)解釋,部分科技巨頭正在討論如何避免繳費,而規模較小的公司則選擇有限。
答:據熟悉相關計畫的人士透露,亞馬遜、Google、微軟等公司普遍打算改用不需繳費的類別來招募人才,包括現有H-1B簽證持有人、學生以及持有其他類型簽證的人員。
部分公司已逐漸降低對H-1B計畫的依賴,但許多規模較小的公司難以因應政策變動,也無力投資成本更低的替代方案。
H-1B簽證是高技術外籍勞工進入美國的主要管道。
政府每年3月都會舉行抽籤,決定誰能獲得來年度新開放的8.5萬個名額。政府近期修改抽籤規則,讓薪資較高的申請者中籤機率更大,這項改變預料將對頂尖科技公司更為有利。
大型科技公司常用的另一個管道是選擇性實習訓練(OPT)計畫,讓美國大學的外籍畢業生在畢業後可獲得通常為期一年的臨時工作許可。擁有STEM學位者可再延長兩年工作許可,之後才轉為H-1B簽證。這些員工不需繳納H-1B費用。

6. 對孟加拉Z世代而言,找工作比推翻政府還難。
2024年,對就業前景感到挫折的孟加拉年輕人走上街頭。示威活動演變成一場革命,推翻了孟加拉的威權領導人,並帶動尼泊爾、印尼與馬達加斯加相繼爆發類似的抗議行動。如今,隨著孟加拉即將舉行這場革命以來的首次全國大選,部分年輕抗議者開始對新一代領導人能否解決他們這一代的問題感到心灰意冷。

【今日焦點】

7. 因政府一度停擺而延後公布的一月份就業報告即將出爐。以色列總理納坦雅胡(Benjamin Netanyahu)將於華盛頓與川普總統會面,雙方預期將討論伊朗議題。財報:思科(Cisco)、麥當勞、卡夫亨氏(Kraft Heinz)、Shopify、希爾頓(Hilton)、T-Mobile。

【數字看時事】

8. 54——里奇·魯霍寧(Rich Ruohonen)的年齡,他是美國男子冰壺隊角逐2026米蘭-科爾蒂納冬奧的替補選手。魯霍寧本業是人身傷害律師,他有望成為美國冬奧史上年紀最大的運動員,唯一需要的條件就是有人滑倒摔跤。他的隊友艾丹·奧登伯格(Aidan Oldenburg)說,美國隊上下都心知肚明這其中的諷刺意味。

【最後一則】

9. 本報旅遊專欄作家試玩了皇家加勒比全新海灘俱樂部——卻拒絕了天價的私人涼亭。
皇家加勒比郵輪最新的攬客手法是設於巴哈馬的「皇家海灘俱樂部」(Royal Beach Club),這是該郵輪公司首座獨立海灘俱樂部,另一座預計今年將在希臘開幕。與皇家加勒比在巴哈馬的私人島嶼不同,旅客造訪這座海灘俱樂部須額外付費,一座私人涼亭一天要價高達1萬美元。高層主管對初步成果讚不絕口。專欄作家道恩·吉爾伯森(Dawn Gilbertson)則花了175美元入場,一探究竟是否真的物有所值。

【新聞編輯室之外】

10. 評論:MedPAC(醫療照護支付諮詢委員會)已遭反對私人市場與老年人「聯邦醫療保險優勢計畫」(Medicare Advantage)的進步派人士把持。華盛頓為何還需要多一個政府醫療政策機構,遊說擴大對美國醫療體系的控制?
《華爾街日報》Buy Side:我們評比了顧問資歷、收費與服務項目等條件,精選出幾家頂尖財務顧問公司。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: The Social-Media Star Under FBI Investigation
emails.contentEn:
Tai Lopez was living proof the American dream was attainable for young men willing to bet on themselves. The college dropout made a name for himself on social media by offering get-rich-quick advice. He urged his followers to invest in his new company with a promise to turn them into e-commerce winners. Now, the SEC has filed a civil lawsuit accusing Lopez and his partners of running a Ponzi scheme—and the FBI is investigating, too.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. The Trump administration is planning its most far-reaching rollback of U.S. climate policy to date. Blackstone Chief Executive Steve Schwarzman, one of the wealthiest people in the world, is ramping up his philanthropic efforts. Israel's government is deepening a push by far-right ministers to expand its authority and settlements in the West Bank. The White House is at loggerheads with Congress over one of President Trump's signature housing proposals, a ban on Wall Street investors buying single-family homes.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 50257.00 +38.00 (0.08%); S&P 500 Futures 6988.50 +5.25 (0.08%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 25357.25 +3.25 (0.01%). Source: Factset, Market data as of 2/10/2026, 5:57:01 AM ET.

Investors are moving more money into international markets, wagering that America's wide lead on the rest of the world will shrink. The big money in today's economy is going disproportionately toward capital instead of labor, writes Greg Ip. Red Lobster CEO Damola Adamolekun is reviewing the chain's real-estate footprint and leases in an attempt to cut costs.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. He vowed to revive RadioShack and Pier 1. Investors say they were swindled.
Tai Lopez raised more than $230 million from hundreds of mostly small investors for his company Retail Ecommerce Ventures, which snapped up struggling retailers. Some of Lopez's investors said in interviews that they believed in his message and were reassured by the monthly payments they were collecting—until the checks stopped arriving. The SEC has since filed a civil lawsuit against Lopez and his partners. The FBI has been contacting investors as part of a criminal investigation, report Suzanne Kapner and Alexander Gladstone. No charges have been filed. Lopez and his lawyer didn't respond to requests for comment.

4. OpenAI decided to kill the AI model that people loved too much.
In January, OpenAI announced that it will retire ChatGPT's 4o model on Feb. 13, saying its traffic had dwindled. The announcement signaled the end of the road for an AI model that proved sticky for users but helped to drive OpenAI's fast consumer growth and attracted a set of loyal fans for whom it felt like a friend and confidant. It has also been criticized for being overly sycophantic toward users and linked by doctors with cases of chatbot users developing psychotic delusions, reports Sam Schechner.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: Why can't doctors agree on how to diagnose Alzheimer's?
How should Alzheimer's disease be defined? Divergent diagnostic criteria are raising concerns that some patients are being misdiagnosed and unnecessarily treated, writes columnist Sumathi Reddy.
A: Divergent diagnoses for Alzheimer's are the result of different criteria for diagnosing the disease. Some doctors worry the differing approaches can result in patients going misdiagnosed.
The Alzheimer's Association 2024 criteria for diagnosis requires evidence of the brain protein amyloid. At the International Working Group, a global consortium of neurologists and researchers, its criteria requires the presence of amyloid; tau, another biomarker of Alzheimer's disease; and cognitive symptoms.
Dr. Gayatri Devi is a neurologist who says over the past year she has seen an increasing number of patients who were told they had Alzheimer's disease when they didn't.
While the Alzheimer's Association criteria define the disease by amyloid pathology in the brain, it says testing and treatment should occur only if a patient has cognitive symptoms.
But doctors like Devi say this isn't always done in practice. Symptoms can be variable and subjective.
The Alzheimer's Association says amyloid is a good proxy for tau. But the current tests for amyloid aren't sensitive enough to detect a few amyloid plaques in the brain.

6. Here's how the Dow got to 50000, in charts.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average topped 50000 for the first time on Friday. In a tech-dominated market, some surprising stocks powered the climb. It took just over eight years for the blue-chip index to climb from 25000 to 50000, after a more-than-century-long journey to that 2018 milestone. Here is a look at the stocks leading the latest leg higher—and the ones slowing things down.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. Economic data: Retail sales for December and the employment cost index for the fourth quarter of 2025. Earnings: Coca-Cola, Marriott, Robinhood, Ford, Spotify, S&P Global, Gilead Sciences.

THE NUMBER

8. $400 million — The record amount Hermès spent on the largest-ever retail real-estate acquisition in Beverly Hills, ending months of speculation over who now owns two adjoining properties on the city's famed Rodeo Drive. It isn't clear what the French luxury-goods company plans to do with its purchase.

AND FINALLY...

9. A Stanford experiment to pair 5,000 singles has taken over campus.
Created by a graduate student, Date Drop has students answer questions about their values, lifestyles and political views. These responses are fed into an algorithm to pair compatible students. Matches "drop" every Tuesday night. More than 5,000 Stanford students have used Date Drop, and it has spread to 10 other colleges. The growth, fans say, reflects a reality about many college kids: They're intimidated by real-life courtship and overwhelmed by the endless scroll of dating apps.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: Permitting difficulties are America's biggest economic Achilles' heel. Let's hope they don't get in the way of U.S. space innovation.
WSJ | Buy Side: No-credit-check business loans usually require income or revenue documentation and might focus on revenue-based financing.

泰·洛佩茲(Tai Lopez)曾是活生生的證明:只要肯放手一搏,美國夢對年輕男性來說觸手可及。這位大學輟學生靠著在社群媒體上兜售快速致富秘訣闖出名號,他鼓勵追隨者投資他的新公司,承諾能讓他們成為電商贏家。如今,美國證券交易委員會(SEC)已對洛佩茲及其合夥人提起民事訴訟,指控他們經營龐氏騙局,聯邦調查局(FBI)也已介入調查。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

【今日頭條】

1. 川普政府正計畫實施迄今最全面的美國氣候政策鬆綁。全球首富之一、黑石集團(Blackstone)執行長蘇世民(Steve Schwarzman)正加碼慈善事業投入。以色列政府正加深由極右翼部長推動的行動,擴大其在約旦河西岸的權力與屯墾區。白宮與國會就川普總統標誌性的住房提案之一——禁止華爾街投資人購買單一家庭住宅——陷入僵局。

【市場直擊】

2. 道瓊期貨50257.00,上漲38.00點(0.08%);標普500期貨6988.50,上漲5.25點(0.08%);那斯達克100期貨25357.25,上漲3.25點(0.01%)。資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年2月10日美東時間上午5:57:01。

投資人正將更多資金轉往國際市場,押注美國相對於世界其他地區的巨大領先優勢將會縮小。葛雷格·艾普(Greg Ip)撰文指出,當今經濟中的巨額財富正不成比例地流向資本,而非勞動力。紅龍蝦(Red Lobster)執行長達莫拉·阿達莫勒昆(Damola Adamolekun)正檢討這家連鎖餐廳的房地產布局與租約,試圖藉此削減成本。

【獨家搶先報導】

3. 他曾誓言復興RadioShack與Pier 1,投資人卻說自己遭到詐騙。
泰·洛佩茲透過他的公司Retail Ecommerce Ventures,從數百名多為小額投資人手中募得超過2.3億美元,用於收購陷入困境的零售商。部分投資人在受訪時表示,他們相信洛佩茲的說詞,而且每月都能收到款項,讓他們安心——直到支票不再寄達為止。SEC隨後對洛佩茲及其合夥人提起民事訴訟,FBI也已開始接觸投資人,展開刑事調查。報導:蘇珊·卡普納(Suzanne Kapner)與亞歷山大·格拉德斯通(Alexander Gladstone)。目前尚未有人遭到起訴。洛佩茲及其律師未回應置評請求。

4. OpenAI決定「賜死」一款太受用戶喜愛的AI模型。
今年1月,OpenAI宣布將於2月13日淘汰ChatGPT的4o模型,理由是其流量已經下滑。這項宣布意味著一款黏著度極高的AI模型即將走到終點——儘管它曾協助推動OpenAI消費端用戶的快速成長,並吸引一批將其視為朋友與知己的忠實粉絲。該模型也曾因過度迎合使用者而受到批評,醫師更指出部分使用者因此出現精神錯亂的案例。報導:山姆·謝克納(Sam Schechner)。

【專家解讀】

5. 問:為何醫師們對阿茲海默症的診斷標準莫衷一是?
阿茲海默症究竟該如何界定?專欄作家蘇瑪蒂·雷迪(Sumathi Reddy)撰文指出,各方診斷標準分歧,引發外界擔憂部分病患遭到誤診並接受不必要的治療。
答:阿茲海默症診斷結果分歧,源於各方採用不同的診斷標準。部分醫師擔心,做法不一可能導致病患遭到誤診。
阿茲海默症協會2024年的診斷標準要求須有腦內類澱粉蛋白(amyloid)的證據。而由全球神經科醫師與研究人員組成的「國際工作小組」(International Working Group),其標準則要求同時具備類澱粉蛋白、另一項生物標記濤蛋白(tau),以及認知症狀。
神經科醫師加雅特里·德維(Gayatri Devi)表示,過去一年她遇到越來越多被告知罹患阿茲海默症、但實際上並未患病的病患。
阿茲海默症協會的標準雖以腦內類澱粉蛋白病變來定義該疾病,但也指出唯有病患出現認知症狀時才應進行檢測與治療。
但德維等醫師表示,實務上並非總是如此,症狀的表現可能因人而異,且帶有主觀性。
阿茲海默症協會表示,類澱粉蛋白可作為濤蛋白的良好替代指標,但目前的類澱粉蛋白檢測敏感度不足,難以偵測腦中少量的類澱粉斑塊。

6. 圖表解析:道瓊指數如何攻上5萬點。
道瓊工業平均指數於週五首度突破5萬點大關。在這個由科技股主導的市場中,若干出人意料的股票成為推升指數的主力。這個藍籌股指數從2.5萬點攀升至5萬點僅耗時逾八年,而在此之前,指數從無到有花了超過一個世紀才在2018年首度觸及2.5萬點的里程碑。以下一覽領漲與拖累指數表現的個股。

【今日焦點】

7. 經濟數據:12月零售銷售與2025年第四季就業成本指數。財報:可口可樂、萬豪(Marriott)、Robinhood、福特(Ford)、Spotify、標普全球(S&P Global)、吉利德科學(Gilead Sciences)。

【數字看時事】

8. 4億美元——愛馬仕(Hermès)在比佛利山莊創下史上最大零售不動產收購紀錄的金額,終結了外界數月來對於該市著名羅迪歐大道(Rodeo Drive)兩處相鄰物業新業主身分的猜測。目前尚不清楚這家法國奢侈品公司打算如何運用這筆收購。

【最後一則】

9. 史丹佛大學一項為5000名單身學生配對的實驗席捲校園。
由一名研究生創立的「Date Drop」讓學生回答有關價值觀、生活方式與政治立場的問題,再由演算法據此配對相容的學生,配對結果於每週二晚間「投放」公布。超過5000名史丹佛學生使用過這項服務,並已擴展至其他10所大學。支持者表示,這股熱潮反映出許多大學生的真實處境:他們既畏懼真實世界的追求,又被交友軟體無止盡的滑動選擇淹沒。

【新聞編輯室之外】

10. 評論:核發許可的困難,是美國經濟最大的罩門,但願這不會阻礙美國的太空創新。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Job Hunters Are Paying to Get Recruited
emails.contentEn:
Landing a white-collar job has become so difficult that candidates—not companies—are paying recruiters to find them work. With more unemployed people than open roles for the first time since the pandemic, job seekers are paying up to 20% of their first month's salary just to bypass applicant-tracking bots. It is another sign of the mounting challenges for white-collar workers in a market where the average search now nears six months.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. Japanese leader Sanae Takaichi's election win gives her an unprecedented shot at shaking the country out of its economic funk and taking on a bigger security role deterring Chinese ambitions. Trade groups in South Texas are raising alarms about aggressive immigration enforcement wreaking economic havoc in the region. A Hong Kong court sentenced former tycoon Jimmy Lai to 20 years in prison, a ruling that adds further friction in U.S. relations with China. American figure skater Ilia Malinin delivered an electric performance to clinch gold for Team USA—and potentially launch a historic run for the U.S. There was plenty of on-field action during the Seattle Seahawks' Super Bowl LX rout of the New England Patriots. But pop culture dominated the night.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 50118.00 -87.00 (0.17%); S&P 500 Futures 6928.00 -24.75 (0.36%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 25006.25 -157.00 (0.62%). Source: Factset, Market data as of 2/9/2026, 5:58:20 AM ET.

The snowballing retreat in software stocks ended in a remarkable rebound, leaving investors bracing for more turbulence ahead. The artificial-intelligence trade has become more fraught, but at least one constant remains: Investors are choosing the companies on the receiving end of big tech's spending spree, writes Dan Gallagher.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. Job hunters are so desperate that they're paying to get recruited.
In a competitive job market, candidates are hiring recruiters to help match them with positions. So-called reverse-recruiter models vary—many require part of job seekers' first month's pay, others charge a set rate to submit applications on a candidate's behalf. A tough hiring landscape means recruiters chasing business might have more luck pitching themselves to job seekers instead of employers, reports Lindsay Ellis.

4. This Chinese factory opened in the U.S. and clobbered its rivals.
President Trump spent much of last year courting foreign investment in U.S. factories, promising to replace jobs lost to the global economy. The rise of a Chinese automotive glass plant in the Ohio heartland shows the risks when America's biggest rival sets up shop. The state's governor welcomed Fuyao and the project was hailed as a step to reviving a battered Rust Belt region. Now, many feel duped. Competition from the plant is threatening about 250 jobs at a rival factory operating since the 1950s, reports Gavin Bade.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: Why might inflation be about to come in hot?
Prices have a habit of spiking in January. This year, tariffs might be a reason, but a likelier culprit is more esoteric, explains reporter Matt Grossman.
A: January's inflation numbers land on Friday and the consensus calls for a moderate 0.3% monthly rise in consumer prices that cools the annual inflation rate to 2.5%.
Still, many on Wall Street are bracing for an unpleasant surprise. In recent years, inflation in January has tended to come in relatively hot. Last year, the consumer-price index rose more in January than in any other month. The same thing happened in 2023.
If that happens again, it will be seen as proof that companies are passing Trump's tariffs on to consumers. Some Federal Reserve officials have cited this possibility as a reason to be cautious about further interest-rate cuts.
But an upside surprise could also be a quirk of how the numbers are calculated, which will make interpreting January's figures especially difficult.
The start of the year is a natural time to boost prices: for gyms to raise membership fees, streaming services to hike subscription rates, or retailers to roll back holiday discounts.
The Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics, which compiles the CPI, seasonally adjusts the results to erase patterns that recur each year. In other words, if prices always rise more in January, that shouldn't show up in the seasonally adjusted CPI.

6. Ukraine is seeking a war plan that goes beyond killing as many Russian soldiers as possible.
As the conflict nears the four-year mark, Russia's increasingly effective use of drones is helping its forces maintain a grinding, slow-motion advance. It is weakening Kyiv's hand at the negotiating table, where it is under pressure to cede strategically vital territory. Many Ukrainian soldiers and officers say that a shift is needed and that Ukraine needs to match Russia's strategy of systematically targeting the rear.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. The House Oversight Committee is expected to depose Jeffrey Epstein's associate Ghislaine Maxwell as part of its investigation into the late convicted sex offender. Earnings: Apollo Global Management, Becton Dickinson.

THE NUMBER

8. 75 — The mandatory retirement age for presidents, cabinet officials, members of Congress and federal judges—proposed by Rahm Emanuel, the 66-year-old Democrat and Washington veteran. Working well past retirement age is an area of rare bipartisan agreement in Washington. Trump will turn 80 this year and Joe Biden left office at age 82. Yet an aging political class is prompting fresh calls for forcing older officeholders to step aside in favor of younger faces.

AND FINALLY...

9. Bad Bunny used joy to put out a political firestorm at the Super Bowl halftime.
In a show performed almost entirely in Spanish, the Puerto Rican star paid tribute to his heritage and the many countries whose people have come to shape the modern-day U.S. Just a week after he denounced Immigration and Customs Enforcement while accepting a Grammy award, he offered up a buoyant celebration of Latino culture. The show still sparked controversy, however, with conservatives criticizing Bad Bunny's past political statements and Trump calling it "absolutely terrible."

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM
