超市面臨新的糧食券難題。

圖表:ANDREW MOLLICA

十八個州正推動限制民眾以「營養補充援助計畫」(SNAP,俗稱糧食券)資金購買的品項。但各州的限制範圍差異極大,雜貨業高層表示,判斷哪些商品符合、哪些不符合糧食券資格,已成為一項複雜的工作。諸如爆米花是否已預先爆開、椒鹽脆餅是否裹有優格等細微差異,如今都可能決定一項商品能否用食物援助資金購買。

今日焦點

聯準會利率決議:預計聯準會將在2026年首次利率會議上維持利率不變。主席鮑爾下午2:30召開的記者會,將是他透露司法部正對他展開調查後首次亮相。點此觀看我們的記者會直播。華府:國務卿馬可·魯比歐(Marco Rubio)預定於上午10點,就美國對委內瑞拉政策向參議院外交委員會作證。財報:AT&T、IBM、Meta、微軟、西南航空、星巴克、特斯拉、惠而浦。📰 今日報紙。

數字看世界

8

15億美元

由25歲的班·斯佩克特(Ben Spector)創立的人工智慧實驗室Flapping Airplanes的估值。其投資人包括GV與紅杉資本。Flapping Airplanes是一波被部分人稱為「新實驗室」(neolabs)新創熱潮的一員,這類公司優先重視長期研究與開發新AI模型,而非追求眼前獲利。隨著投資人尋找下一個OpenAI(該公司最初也是以研究實驗室起家),市場對「新實驗室」的興趣正急速升溫。

最後,還有這則

9

這個男孩團體夠格拿到簽證嗎?

在美國移民法中,「非凡能力」一詞通常指的是奧運選手或知名藝術家。一個初出茅廬的男孩團體,正希望「爆紅」也能算數。四名二十來歲的年輕人於11月在TikTok上推出了Boy Throb組合。他們在一部影片中宣稱:「我們將是全世界下一個最紅的男孩團體。」問題是:團員達爾山·馬格杜姆(Darshan Magdum)住在印度。要讓團體湊齊,他需要一張簽證。而要拿到簽證,Boy Throb必須說服政府,證明他們的表演確實「非凡」。

✏️ President Trump is changing course in Minnesota after the fatal shooting of Alex Pretti. By Monday, Border Patrol Commander Gregory Bovino was leaving the state and Tom Homan, Trump’s border czar, was en route to Minneapolis to take charge. The president’s pivot came after Republican lawmakers and other allies raised concerns that he was squandering public support for his signature campaign issue and senior administration officials increasingly saw the chaotic scenes in Minneapolis as a political liability. Our reporters go inside the 48 hours that convinced the president to de-escalate.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

As Minneapolis videos splashed across the news, Trump was watching.

Working from the Oval Office as a winter storm barreled toward Washington, D.C., the president was paying attention as footage of a federal immigration agent shooting Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old intensive-care nurse and U.S. citizen, played on repeat. Roughly 48 hours after the shooting, he moved to pull back one of his administration’s most high-profile and divisive immigration-enforcement campaigns. In the process, Trump appeared to take sides—for now—in a simmering debate that has been playing out quietly in the administration, report Annie Linskey, Alex Leary and Michelle Hackman.

4

Trump is making a high-stakes bid to dole out $100 billion more in tax refunds.

The annual tax-filing season that opened yesterday will produce a cash surge estimated at $100 billion beyond last year’s $329 billion total, and it is engineered to buoy Republicans’ sagging voter approval. At stake is whether Republicans can retain narrow House and Senate majorities that give them the authority to control the federal agenda. The tax-policy strategy is simple: Put money in voters’ wallets and get rewarded at the polls. In reality, it is a double-bank shot with little guarantee of success, reports Richard Rubin.

Q: How does the federal investigation of Alex Pretti’s death differ from past cases?

The Department of Homeland Security is leading an investigation into the killing of Pretti by a Border Patrol agent, amid objections from Minnesota officials who say they are being shut out. Justice Department reporter Sadie Gurman explains the state of play. 

A: U.S. officials said Homeland Security Investigations, an agency within DHS, is leading the probe, with the Federal Bureau of Investigation serving in an assisting role. Usually, the FBI takes the lead.

HSI agents have the authority to arrest people if they have probable cause. But any potential prosecution would have to be handled by the Justice Department.

Most shootings by officers involve local police, rather than federal agents. Federal authorities work alongside local investigators to determine whether an officer engaged in obstruction of justice or violated someone’s civil rights.

The Justice Department typically reviews any shooting involving a federal agent. What’s more, the FBI and DOJ normally investigate almost every high-profile officer-involved killing because prosecutors consider them incidents of national significance that warrant such inquiries.

Minnesota officials want to conduct detailed investigations in the killings of Pretti and Renee Good, who was shot in her car by an agent with Immigration and Customs Enforcement. But they say federal authorities are interfering with their sovereign right to investigate possible violations of state law.

The Trump administration says the state has no legal right to information in what were federal incidents. Both sides have said they don’t trust each other to conduct a fair investigation.

A gold boom is spurring miners to dig for the mother lode.

PHOTO: GULSHAN KHAN FOR WSJ

For years, hundreds of illegal miners known locally as zama zamas prospected for gold on a patch of land on the outskirts of Johannesburg with hammers and chisels in hand-dug tunnels. Now, the site has been transformed into South Africa’s first new underground gold mine in more than 15 years, part of a global rush to boost production of a metal trading at record prices.

3

當明尼阿波利斯的畫面在新聞上瘋傳時,川普正在關注。

當一場冬季暴風雪正朝華府逼近之際,總統正在橢圓辦公室工作,他密切關注著一名聯邦移民探員槍殺37歲重症加護病房護理師、美國公民艾力克斯·普雷提的畫面被反覆播放。槍擊事件發生約48小時後,他決定收手,撤回其政府最受矚目、也最具爭議性的移民執法行動之一。在此過程中,川普似乎——至少目前——在政府內部一場暗地醞釀已久的爭論中選邊站了,安妮·林斯基(Annie Linskey)、亞歷克斯·利里(Alex Leary)與蜜雪兒·哈克曼報導。

4

川普正孤注一擲,計劃額外發放1000億美元的退稅款。

昨日開跑的年度報稅季,預計將產生一波估計比去年3290億美元總額多出1000億美元的現金潮,而這項安排正是為了提振共和黨低迷的選民支持度而設計。攸關的是共和黨能否保住讓其掌控聯邦議程的參眾兩院微弱多數。稅務政策的策略很簡單:把錢放進選民口袋,再從投票結果中獲得回報。但實際上,這是一記成功機率難以保證的「雙重賭注」,理查·魯賓(Richard Rubin)報導。

依你的方式獲取新聞。
將本報設為你在Google上的首選新聞來源,獲取更多本報值得信賴的深度報導。

專家解讀

5

問:對艾力克斯·普雷提死因的聯邦調查,與過去案例有何不同?

國土安全部正主導對一名邊境巡邏探員槍殺普雷提一案的調查,明尼蘇達州官員則抱怨自己被排除在外。司法部新聞記者莎蒂·古爾曼(Sadie Gurman)解釋目前的情況。

答:美國官員表示,國土安全部轄下的「國土安全調查局」(HSI)正主導此案調查,聯邦調查局則擔任協助角色。通常情況下,是由聯邦調查局主導此類案件。

國土安全調查局探員若有相當理由,有權逮捕嫌犯。但任何潛在起訴都必須由司法部處理。

大多數執法人員涉及的槍擊案都涉及地方警察,而非聯邦探員。聯邦當局通常會與地方調查人員合作,判斷該名執法人員是否妨礙司法或侵犯了他人的公民權利。

司法部通常會對任何涉及聯邦探員的槍擊案進行審查。此外,聯邦調查局與司法部通常會調查幾乎所有備受矚目、涉及執法人員的致命案件,因為檢察官認為這類事件具有全國性重要意義,值得展開此類調查。

明尼蘇達州官員希望能對普雷提及蕾妮·古德(Renee Good,遭移民與海關執法局探員在車內開槍擊斃)的槍殺案展開詳盡調查。但他們表示,聯邦當局正干預他們調查可能違反州法行為的固有權利。

川普政府則表示,對於這些屬於聯邦事件的案件,該州並無取得相關資訊的法律權利。雙方都表示不信任對方能公正地展開調查。

閱讀全文

6

黃金熱潮正促使礦工挖掘「母礦脈」。

照片:GULSHAN KHAN FOR WSJ

多年來,數百名當地人稱為「zama zamas」的非法礦工,在約翰尼斯堡郊外一塊土地上,手持鐵鎚與鑿子,在手工挖掘的隧道中淘金。如今,這處場址已被改造成南非十五年多來首座新開發的地下金礦,這是全球礦業為提高這種目前交易價格創新高的金屬產量而掀起熱潮的一部分。

今日焦點

7

美國人口普查局即將公布首批2025年數據,其中將包含全國與各州人口估計數字。川普預計將在愛荷華州就經濟與能源議題發表演說。財報:美國航空、波音、通用汽車、諾斯洛普·格魯曼、RTX公司、德州儀器、聯合健康集團、UPS。📰 今日報紙。

數字看世界

8

超過10,000

部分人權團體估計,伊朗政權鎮壓反政府抗議活動所導致的死亡人數。此次鎮壓死亡人數的初步估計約為數千人,這使其成為該政權數十年來對異議人士最致命的一次鎮壓行動。伊朗當局已承認逾3100人死亡,並將責任歸咎於他們宣稱滲透抗議活動的暴徒與恐怖分子。

最後,還有這則

9

為人父母唯一的心願,就是坐在車裡滑手機。

「車內滑手機」(Carscrolling)已成為疲憊不堪的父母鍾愛的小奢侈享受,他們珍惜這段介於繁忙工作日與回家後種種瑣事之間的緩衝時光。爸媽們選擇偷偷滑手機,以免被指責言行不一——畢竟他們總是叫孩子放下螢幕。

新聞編輯室之外

10

社論:川普政府關於遣返罪犯的言論,與其目前實際執行的、範圍廣泛得多的大規模遣返政策並不相符。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: An American City at War With the U.S. Government
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Good morning. Last night, President Trump told the Journal’s Josh Dawsey that the administration was reviewing the latest fatal shooting in Minneapolis and signaled a willingness to eventually withdraw immigration enforcement officials from the Twin Cities. The conflict reflects the nation’s split views of immigration policy—an issue that helped carry Trump to the White House a year ago. Many residents see it as a fight against an occupying army bent on subduing their progressive city. Follow our live coverage here .

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY’S HEADLINES

1

Trump told the Journal that immigration-enforcement officers will “at some point” leave Minneapolis. Some Republicans have criticized Alex Pretti—who was killed by a federal Border Patrol agent—for carrying a gun during protest activity. But Second Amendment groups have long fought for the right to do so. Senate Democrats, angered by the shooting in Minneapolis, threatened a partial government shutdown, saying they wouldn’t vote for a funding package without major changes to its homeland security provisions. Rearmament, an aging population, technological change and fear of voters are fueling a risky trend toward deficit spending across the globe. Michelle Bowman, the Fed’s vice chair for supervision, has slashed staff and pursued what many inside and outside the central bank view as a housecleaning of the supervision and regulation division’s senior leadership.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 49238.00 -25.00 0.05 S&P 500 Futures 6935.50 -10.25 0.15 Nasdaq 100 Futures 25655.00 -83.25 0.32

Source: Factset, Market data as of 1/26/2026, 5:54:22 AM ET

📈 Follow our live financial coverage all day.

Gold futures prices reached an all-time high of $5,000 a troy ounce . Resale values suggest that even rare goods such as Hermès Birkin bags and Rolex watches aren’t pulling in crowds like they used to, writes Carol Ryan.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

This American city found itself at war with the U.S. government.

For months, Minneapolis’s mayor watched with dread as the number of federal agents in his city swelled to carry out Trump’s promise of the largest deportation of illegal immigrants in American history. Then Renee Good was fatally shot on Jan. 7 by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent during one of the many protests against the action. On Saturday, it happened again when Pretti was shot and killed by a Border Patrol agent. Those fatalities marked a new and alarming phase in a confrontation between the residents of an American city, carrying phones and whistles, and armed officers of the U.S. government, report Joshua Chaffin and Michelle Hackman.

4

Health insurance is now more expensive than the mortgage for these Americans.

Millions are starting to see their monthly health-insurance bills rise. Many of those facing the most dramatic dollar increases are middle-income earners who buy health insurance through the marketplaces set up by the government’s Affordable Care Act. Expanded subsidies for those insured under the act expired on Dec. 31. Now, they are having to figure out how to pay, or go without, reports Rachel Louise Ensign.

Go inside what’s driving D.C.

Washington Coverage Chief Damian Paletta brings you an expert guide to the politics, power and people in the nation’s capital. Sign up for our politics newsletter. 

 MESSAGE FROM: MARKETWATCH Introducing Don’t Short Yourself 

When the market’s spinning and the headlines keep piling on, MarketWatch cuts through the noise and delivers insights to help grow your money. Introducing Don’t Short Yourself, a weekly newsletter from MarketWatch that distills the news of the day into real-life money moves—from saving smarter to investing with confidence—so you can turn uncertainty into clarity.

Sign Up Now 

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: What new rules could get you a bigger refund this tax season?

Taxpayers can file 2025 returns starting today. Reporters Ashlea Ebeling and Richard Rubin explain the most important changes you need to be aware of.

A: Americans can expect smaller tax bills and bigger refunds this year—after they navigate a pile of new rules from last year’s tax law.

The standard deduction for 2025 is $15,750 for single filers and $31,500 for married couples filing jointly. Last year’s tax law raised those by $750 and $1,500, respectively, on top of the Internal Revenue Service’s normal year-to-year inflation adjustments.

Taking the standard deduction is still the best option financially for nearly 90% of taxpayers. Still, this year’s changes might mean you would be better off itemizing your deductions.

Another change to be aware of: The maximum state-and-local-tax deduction for property taxes plus income or sales taxes is $40,000 for 2025, up from $10,000. As a result, many taxpayers will be better off itemizing instead of taking the standard deduction this year.

Be aware, however, that the maximum SALT deduction begins phasing down to $10,000 once a taxpayer’s modified adjusted gross income crosses $500,000, whether single or married filing jointly.

Other tax laws offer credits and deductions for parents, seniors and those with overtime pay, among other categories.

Just because you get a new federal tax break doesn’t mean it also applies to your state income-tax return. California, for example, doesn’t have its own versions of the tax law’s new deductions for people 65 and up, tipped and overtime workers or auto-loan interest.

SEE THE STORY

6

In one Kyiv apartment building, they are freezing—but not giving up.

PHOTO: EMANUELE SATOLLI FOR WSJ

Four years of Russian airstrikes have devastated Ukraine’s electricity grid and disrupted heating. A million Kyiv residents were without power as of Tuesday evening. But there hasn’t been the societal collapse that Russia has long sought by attacking civilian infrastructure. Instead, Ukrainians are showing the resilience and make-do attitude that have frustrated Moscow’s efforts to pummel them into submission.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

Winter storm watch: Expect widespread airline disruptions and a slowdown in East Coast transit. Major cities like Philadelphia and Washington, D.C., have declared snow emergencies. Earnings: Nucor, Steel Dynamics 📰 Today’s paper 

THE NUMBER

8

 ~200 million

The estimated number of people in the path of a massive winter storm lashing parts of the U.S. with snow, causing frozen roads and thousands of flight cancellations and power outages. Forecasters said the storm would stretch 2,000 miles from New Mexico to Maine; one meteorologist at the National Weather Service told the Journal it is “rare” for a storm to have that wide of an expanse.

AND FINALLY...

9

There’s a secret society of people who know the formula for WD-40.

The handwritten formula for WD-40 is kept in a lockbox at an undisclosed Bank of America location in San Diego. The notebook is the only version that has the full makeup of the original formula, which accounted for nearly 80% of WD-40’s revenue as of August 2025. Seeing it requires a special key, nondisclosure agreements, passage through a bank vault and, typically, an executive title. Steve Brass, the chief executive at WD-40, was only admitted 18 months ago.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Alex Pretti made a mistake by interfering with ICE agents, but he wasn’t a “domestic terrorist” who deserved to be shot.
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 早安。昨晚,川普總統告訴本報記者喬許·道西,政府正在檢討明尼阿波利斯最新的一起致命槍擊案,並暗示願意最終從雙城地區撤出移民執法人員。這場衝突反映了全國對移民政策的分歧看法——這正是一年前將川普送進白宮的關鍵議題之一。許多當地居民將此視為對抗一支意圖壓制他們這座進步城市的「佔領軍」。點此追蹤我們的即時報導。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1

川普告訴本報,移民執法人員「終究」會離開明尼阿波利斯。部分共和黨人批評遭聯邦邊境巡邏探員擊斃的艾力克斯·普雷提在抗議活動中攜帶槍枝,但擁槍團體長期以來一直為這項權利抗爭。因明尼阿波利斯槍擊案而憤怒的參議院民主黨人揚言,若撥款法案未對國土安全相關條款做出重大修改,他們將不惜投票支持部分政府停擺。重整軍備、人口老化、科技變遷與對選民的畏懼,正助長全球日益冒進的赤字支出趨勢。聯準會負責監理業務的副主席蜜雪兒·鮑曼(Michelle Bowman)大幅裁減人力,並展開一場許多央行內外人士視為對監理與法規部門高層領導進行「大清洗」的行動。

市場即時動態

2

道瓊期貨 49238.00 -25.00 0.05%;標普500期貨 6935.50 -10.25 0.15%;那斯達克100期貨 25655.00 -83.25 0.32%
資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年1月26日美東時間上午5:54:22

📈 全天追蹤我們的即時財經報導。

黃金期貨價格觸及每金衡盎司5000美元的歷史新高。轉售價值顯示,即便是愛馬仕柏金包與勞力士手錶等稀有商品,如今也不再像過去那樣吸引搶購人潮,卡蘿·萊恩撰文分析。

搶先看

3

這座美國城市發現自己正與美國聯邦政府開戰。

數月來,明尼阿波利斯市長懷著憂懼之心,眼看聯邦探員人數在市內不斷增加,執行川普所承諾的美國史上最大規模非法移民驅逐行動。隨後,蕾妮·古德於1月7日在多起反對此行動的抗議活動之一中,遭移民與海關執法局探員開槍打死。週六,類似事件再度上演,普雷提遭邊境巡邏探員開槍打死。這些死亡事件標誌著這場對峙進入一個令人擔憂的新階段——手持手機與哨子的美國城市居民,對上全副武裝的美國政府執法人員,約書亞·查芬與蜜雪兒·哈克曼報導。

4

對這些美國人來說,健康保險費用如今比房貸還貴。

數百萬人開始看到自己每月的健康保險帳單上漲。許多面臨最大幅度金額漲幅的人,是透過政府《平價醫療法案》(ACA)建立的市場購買保險的中等收入者。針對ACA投保人的擴大補貼已於12月31日到期。如今他們必須想辦法籌錢繳費,否則就得放棄保險,瑞秋·露易絲·恩賽恩(Rachel Louise Ensign)報導。

深入了解華府局勢。
華府新聞主編達米安·帕列塔為您帶來首都政治、權力與人物的專家導覽。訂閱我們的政治通訊。

專家解讀

5

問:今年報稅季有哪些新規定可能讓你拿到更多退稅?

納稅人今天起可申報2025年度稅表。記者艾希莉亞·艾伯林(Ashlea Ebeling)與理查·魯賓解釋你需要了解的最重要變動。

答:在應付去年稅法帶來的一大堆新規定後,美國人今年可望迎來較低的應繳稅額與較高的退稅金額。

2025年單身申報者的標準扣除額為15,750美元,已婚聯合申報者為31,500美元。去年的稅法在美國國稅局例行的年度通膨調整之外,又分別上調了750美元與1500美元。

對近九成的納稅人而言,採用標準扣除額在財務上仍是最佳選擇。不過,今年的變動可能意味著你採用列舉扣除額反而更划算。

另一項需留意的變動是:2025年州及地方稅(包括財產稅加上所得稅或銷售稅)的最高扣除額為4萬美元,較先前的1萬美元大幅提高。因此,今年許多納稅人採用列舉扣除額會比標準扣除額更划算。

不過要注意,一旦納稅人(無論單身或已婚聯合申報)的調整後總收入超過50萬美元,州及地方稅最高扣除額將開始逐步降回1萬美元。

其他稅法還為父母、長者以及有加班費收入者等群體提供了扣抵與扣除額。

即便你獲得了新的聯邦稅務優惠,也不代表這項優惠同樣適用於你的州所得稅申報。例如加州就沒有針對65歲以上人士、領取小費或加班費的勞工,或汽車貸款利息設立自己版本的相應新扣除額。

閱讀全文

6

在基輔的一棟公寓大樓裡,居民正在挨凍——但沒有放棄。

照片:EMANUELE SATOLLI FOR WSJ

四年來的俄羅斯空襲已重創烏克蘭的電網,並擾亂了供暖系統。截至週二晚間,基輔有百萬居民斷電。但俄羅斯長期以來試圖藉由攻擊民用基礎設施引發的社會崩潰並未發生。相反地,烏克蘭人展現出的韌性與克難精神,一直讓莫斯科試圖以砲火迫使他們屈服的努力屢屢受挫。

今日焦點

7

冬季暴風雪警戒:預計航空業將出現大範圍中斷,東岸交通也將放緩。費城與華府等主要城市已宣布進入降雪緊急狀態。財報:紐柯鋼鐵、鋼鐵動力。📰 今日報紙。

數字看世界

8

約2億

一場肆虐美國部分地區的大型冬季暴風雪,預估影響範圍內的人口數,帶來道路結冰以及數千架次航班取消與大規模停電。氣象預報員表示,這場暴風雪的範圍將從新墨西哥州一路延伸至緬因州,綿延2000英里;美國國家氣象局一名氣象學家告訴本報,暴風雪能有如此大的覆蓋範圍「相當罕見」。

最後,還有這則

9

有一個知曉WD-40配方的秘密團體。

WD-40的手寫配方保存在聖地牙哥一處未公開的美國銀行地點的保險箱中。這本筆記本是唯一保有原始配方完整內容的版本,截至2025年8月,這項配方貢獻了WD-40近八成的營收。要一睹配方,需要一把特殊鑰匙、簽署保密協議、通過銀行金庫,而且通常還得具備高階主管職銜。WD-40執行長史蒂夫·布拉斯(Steve Brass)在18個月前才獲准查看。

新聞編輯室之外

10

社論:艾力克斯·普雷提干預ICE探員執法是個錯誤,但他並非一名該遭槍殺的「國內恐怖分子」。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Another Minneapolis Killing, More Conflicting Narratives
emails.contentEn:
✏️ After another fatal shooting in Minneapolis, the Journal's Mariah Timms explains what it was like being on the ground . As with the earlier killing of Renee Good by an ICE officer, starkly different narratives about the man who was fatally shot quickly spread online. We analyze videos that appear to contradict federal claims . The killing marks an escalation in the standoff between state and federal authorities in Minnesota. Amid this mounting tension, local police in other parts of the U.S. who once backed ICE are starting to lose faith in its tactics .

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

A U.S. Border Patrol officer shot and killed a 37-year-old man in Minneapolis yesterday morning, after he was confronted while filming the activities of ICE officers. Local law-enforcement officials were blocked from conducting an investigation. Alex Pretti, an intensive-care nurse , was described as a “domestic terrorist” by the Trump administration, a portrayal that his parents called "sickening lies." Under the First Amendment, anyone—regardless of their citizenship status—has the right to engage in peaceful protest. Here are the rules for immigration officers . 🎥 A WSJ reporter described clouds of gas and a stream of unmarked cars following Pretti’s killing. Senate Democrats signaled that they’d be willing to shut down much of the government rather than vote for a package that includes funds for immigration enforcement after the latest fatal shooting in Minneapolis. In Gaza, Israel is quietly backing new Palestinian militias with air support and intelligence to help them target Hamas.

FROM THE MARKETS

2

The events of this month have the potential to profoundly change the political and economic landscape for years to come, writes Greg Ip. Once a favorite of Wall Street, software stocks have been sliding lately on concerns about how the sector could be upended by AI . With tax refunds expected to be higher on average this year, millions of Americans would benefit from changing their withholding for 2026.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Police who once backed ICE’s mission are losing faith in its tactics.

As federal immigration agents conduct high-profile operations across the U.S., from “Metro Surge” in Minnesota to “Catch of the Day” in Maine, some local and state law-enforcement leaders are voicing concerns that these efforts have strayed from the administration’s stated focus on public-safety threats, Jack Morphet and Kris Maher report. Many police leaders say they still support combating illegal immigration and believe the troubling actions stem from a minority of officers, but they say these problems undermine their efforts to put a human face on law enforcement. Federal authorities have defended their tactics.

4

The hardest part about being a billionaire in California? Proving you left.

A proposed billionaire tax has some of the state’s richest residents eyeing the exits. First they’ll have to contend with dogged tax collectors : State officials pore through phone logs, look for country club memberships and double-check dentist visits to figure out what really serves as home. For high earners hoping to dodge the state’s tax net, some advisers recommend leaving breadcrumbs, like a “we’ve moved” note on your Christmas card, Laura J. Nelson and Juliet Chung report.

Go inside the U.S.-China relationship.

Sign up for the WSJ China newsletter to get exclusive insights on the contest between the U.S. and China, brought to you every week by the WSJ’s top China correspondent.

 EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: Can Trump and Big Pharma get the world to pay more for drugs?

Manufacturers are pushing for higher drug prices overseas. Heard on the Street columnist David Wainer wrote about the political and economic resistance they face.

A: Americans pay about three times what other wealthy nations do for branded prescription drugs. For years, policymakers have tried to fix this by cutting U.S. drug prices directly. President Trump has pushed a different idea: make foreign countries pay more so Americans can pay less.

For Big Pharma, there’s potential upside. But it is easier said than done.

Last year, after threatening the industry with crushing tariffs, Trump secured several commitments. The most important one: Drugmakers agreed to charge the U.S. no more than what other wealthy countries pay for newly launched medicines.

On paper, it makes sense. If American prices are tethered to what the U.K. or Switzerland pays, drugmakers would need to raise prices abroad and lower them in the U.S. to balance things out. But the reality is messier.

What’s clear is that pharmaceutical executives are eager to seize the moment. They have new leverage, including the backing of U.S. trade representatives and the Commerce Department. The U.K. already agreed to increase what it pays for medicines as part of a wider trade deal. Germany and Switzerland are signaling greater openness on the issue as well.

SEE THE STORY

6

These videos contradict the U.S. account of the Minneapolis shooting.

Federal agents claimed Alex Pretti forced their hand, alleging he “violently resisted” disarmament until officers fired “defensive shots.” Bystander footage appears to tell a different story . A frame-by-frame review by WSJ shows an officer pulling a handgun away from Pretti. Less than a second later, an agent fires several rounds. Pretti died at the scene.

HAPPENING THIS WEEK

7

Tuesday: The Census Bureau is set to release its first set of 2025 figures, which will include national and state population estimates. Trump delivers a speech on the economy and energy in Iowa. Wednesday: The Federal Reserve is projected to hold rates steady at its first interest-rate meeting of 2026. Chair Jerome Powell will hold his first press conference since he released a video disclosing a DOJ probe into his testimony on the central bank’s building renovations. Friday: Charli XCX stars as a fictionalized version of herself in “The Moment.” Check out everything else on this week’s arts & culture calendar .

THE NUMBER

8

 $1 trillion

The approximate cost of replacing current U.S. military equipment and personnel in Europe, according to the International Institute for Strategic Studies. The continent’s once-sclerotic defense industry is churning out drones, tanks, ammunition and other weaponry at its fastest pace in decades as it looks to rearm in the face of Russian aggression and divides with Washington. But there is still some way to go.

AND FINALLY...

9

China is training its AI-controlled weapons with insights from hawks and coyotes.

As Beijing works to harness AI to deploy swarms of drones, “robot wolves” and other autonomous systems, researchers are turning to nature for inspiration . After observing how hawks target their prey, engineers at one of China’s top military-linked universities trained defensive drones to single out and destroy the most vulnerable enemy aircraft.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 在明尼阿波利斯再度發生致命槍擊案後,本報記者瑪麗亞·蒂姆斯(Mariah Timms)描述了她在現場的所見所聞。與先前ICE官員擊斃蕾妮·古德一案類似,關於這名遭擊斃男子的說法,截然不同的敘事迅速在網路上流傳開來。我們分析了似乎與聯邦說法相矛盾的影片。這起槍擊案標誌著明尼蘇達州州與聯邦當局之間對峙的進一步升級。在這股日益升高的緊張氛圍中,美國其他地區曾支持ICE的地方警方,也開始對其執法手段失去信心。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1

昨天上午,一名美國邊境巡邏隊探員在明尼阿波利斯開槍打死一名37歲男子,此前他因拍攝ICE探員的執法活動而遭到攔阻。地方執法官員被禁止介入調查。這名重症加護病房護理師艾力克斯·普雷提,遭川普政府形容為「國內恐怖分子」,他的父母稱這種說法是「令人作嘔的謊言」。根據憲法第一修正案,任何人——無論公民身分為何——都有權從事和平抗議。以下是移民執法人員應遵守的規範。🎥 一名本報記者描述,普雷提遭擊斃後,現場瀰漫著陣陣煙霧氣體,還有一連串無標誌車輛駛離。在明尼阿波利斯最新一起致命槍擊案後,參議院民主黨人表態,他們寧可讓政府大部分部門停擺,也不願投票支持一項包含移民執法撥款的法案。在加薩,以色列正悄悄以空中支援與情報,暗中扶植新的巴勒斯坦民兵組織,協助他們打擊哈馬斯。

市場動態

2

本月發生的這些事件,有可能在未來多年徹底改變政治與經濟版圖,葛雷格·伊普撰文分析。曾是華爾街寵兒的軟體類股,近來因外界擔憂AI可能顛覆整個產業而持續下滑。由於今年平均退稅金額預計提高,數百萬美國人若調整2026年度的預扣稅額,將可從中受益。

搶先看

3

曾支持ICE使命的警方,如今對其執法手段失去信心。

隨著聯邦移民探員在全美各地展開高調行動,從明尼蘇達州的「都會激增行動」到緬因州的「當日捕獲行動」,部分地方與州級執法首長表達了擔憂,認為這些行動已偏離政府所宣稱、聚焦公共安全威脅的目標,傑克·莫菲(Jack Morphet)與克里斯·馬赫(Kris Maher)報導。許多警方領導人表示,他們依然支持打擊非法移民,並認為這些令人憂心的行為源自少數探員,但他們表示,這些問題正在破壞他們努力為執法工作塑造親民形象的成果。聯邦當局則為其執法手段辯護。

4

在加州當億萬富豪最難的部分是什麼?證明你已經搬走了。

一項擬議中的億萬富豪稅,讓該州部分最富有的居民開始盤算出走。但他們首先得應付緊咬不放的稅務稽查員:州官員會仔細翻查電話紀錄、查看鄉村俱樂部會籍,並反覆核對牙醫看診紀錄,以判定當事人真正的居住地究竟在哪裡。對於希望躲避該州稅網的高收入者,部分顧問建議留下一些「痕跡」,例如在聖誕卡上寫一句「我們搬家了」,蘿拉·尼爾森(Laura J. Nelson)與朱麗葉·鍾(Juliet Chung)報導。

深入了解美中關係。
訂閱《華爾街日報》中國通訊,每週由本報首席中國特派記者為您帶來獨家見解。

專家解讀

5

問:川普與大型製藥公司能否讓全世界為藥品支付更高價格?

藥廠正推動提高海外藥價。「街頭傳聞」專欄作家大衛·韋納撰文分析他們所面臨的政治與經濟阻力。

答:美國人為品牌處方藥支付的價格,約為其他富裕國家的三倍。多年來,政策制定者一直試圖直接壓低美國藥價來解決這個問題。川普總統則提出了不同的想法:讓外國支付更多,好讓美國人少付一點。

對大型製藥公司而言,這其中存在潛在利多。但說起來容易做起來難。

去年,在以嚴厲關稅威脅該產業後,川普取得了幾項承諾。其中最重要的一項是:藥廠同意,對新上市藥物向美國收取的價格,不會高於其他富裕國家所支付的價格。

理論上這說得通。如果美國藥價與英國或瑞士的支付水準掛鉤,藥廠就必須提高海外售價、降低美國售價,以求平衡。但現實情況要複雜得多。

顯而易見的是,製藥業高層都急於把握這個時機。他們手握新的談判籌碼,包括美國貿易代表署與商務部的支持。英國已同意作為更廣泛貿易協議的一部分,提高其藥品支付價格。德國與瑞士也釋出在此議題上更加開放的訊號。

閱讀全文

6

這些影片與美方對明尼阿波利斯槍擊案的說法相矛盾。

聯邦探員聲稱是艾力克斯·普雷提逼得他們不得不採取行動,指控他「暴力抗拒」繳械,直到探員開出「防衛性槍擊」。但旁觀者拍攝的影片似乎講述了另一個故事。《華爾街日報》逐格檢視畫面顯示,一名探員將手槍從普雷提身邊拉開。不到一秒後,另一名探員連開數槍。普雷提當場死亡。

本週焦點

7

週二:美國人口普查局即將公布首批2025年數據,其中將包含全國與各州人口估計數字。川普將在愛荷華州就經濟與能源議題發表演說。週三:預計聯準會將在2026年首次利率會議上維持利率不變。主席鮑爾將召開自其發布影片、揭露司法部就其有關央行大樓翻修工程證詞展開調查以來的首場記者會。週五:查莉·XCX在《The Moment》中飾演虛構版本的自己。這裡是本週其餘的藝文行事曆。

數字看世界

8

1兆美元

根據國際戰略研究所估計,更換美國目前部署在歐洲的軍事裝備與人員的大致成本。這片大陸曾經僵化遲滯的國防工業,如今正以數十年來最快的速度生產無人機、坦克、彈藥及其他武器裝備,以因應俄羅斯的侵略行動並應對與華府之間的分歧,力圖重新武裝。但距離目標仍有一段路要走。

最後,還有這則

9

中國正利用老鷹與郊狼的行為模式,訓練其AI控制的武器。

隨著北京致力運用AI部署無人機蜂群、「機器狼」及其他自主系統,研究人員正轉向大自然尋求靈感。在觀察老鷹如何鎖定獵物後,中國一所頂尖軍方相關大學的工程師,訓練防禦性無人機辨識並摧毀最脆弱的敵方飛行器。

新聞編輯室之外

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Hedge Funds Are Back on Top
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Hedge funds are back on top of Wall Street’s pecking order. In 2025, performance across these funds was the best it’s been in over a decade, and investors are poised to keep pumping money into the asset class this year. For Intel, it’s been a tougher ride. After months of positive vibes, investors saw the chip maker’s stock come crashing back to earth this week. We look at how the company missed out on what should’ve been an easy win .

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

As some progressives push to disband ICE, Democrats face a familiar debate about how to resist Trump policies without being perceived as the anti-law-and-order party. At Davos, President Trump’s disruptive presence forced attendees to make decisions about big issues (a prospective U.S. takeover of Greenland) and small ones (conflicting parties). China’s Xi Jinping has put his No. 1 general under investigation, extending a crackdown on military corruption and disloyalty that is hollowing out the top ranks . The Syrian president’s offensive against a Kurdish-led militia has proved his military boldness and willingness to risk his relationship with the U.S. Generative AI is making voice interactions with devices more productive and less annoying, and tech will never be the same , writes Christopher Mims.

FROM THE MARKETS

2

The Dow industrials ticked 0.5% lower this week , while the S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the Nasdaq 0.1%, showing few signs that markets had narrowly avoided a potential trade shock. A 17% dive in Intel’s stock—which had been buoyed by votes of confidence from the White House, Nvidia and SoftBank—came after an earnings call revealed the chip maker had struggled to meet booming AI-linked demand. Adam Jonas, a top researcher at Morgan Stanley, is betting his reputation on robots and flying cars .

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

With the fate of Greenland in flux, it’s back to the age of empire.

Though Trump has backed down—for now—from threats to use economic or military coercion to take over the Danish territory, the shock of the U.S.’s expansionist ambition still hangs in the air, report Drew Hinshaw and Marcus Walker. In European capitals, there’s little confidence trans-Atlantic relations will return to normal. In remarks this week, Trump cast territorial expansion as a normal historical process. What he failed to mention: Most land gains in the age of empires were achieved through bloodshed, not purchase. And when money changed hands, it was sometimes under duress as the victor in a war imposed a sale on the loser.

4

This NFL season’s fiercest rivalry is sports betting vs. prediction markets.

Americans are expected to set a record by wagering more than $1.5 billion on the Super Bowl. For the first time, nearly everyone in the U.S. will be able to get in on the action thanks to prediction-market companies Polymarket and Kalshi, which are challenging sports-betting giants FanDuel and DraftKings. Though sports betting remains illegal in 11 states, federally regulated prediction markets allow a way in, report Katherine Sayre and Jared Diamond. These markets let users bet on outcomes in many fields, including politics and popular culture, but sports remain the majority of their business.

Enjoy the best of the Journal’s feature writing.

Get a weekly look at our most colorful, thought-provoking and original features on the business of life. Sign up for the WSJ Weekend Reads newsletter .

 EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: Europe is worried the U.S. could block access to its tech. How big of a problem would that be?

Rising tensions with the U.S. are spurring new plans in Europe to break with American technology in favor of homegrown alternatives. Reporters Sam Schechner, Berber Jin and Kim Mackrael wrote about the region’s push for “technological sovereignty.”

A: Trump’s approach to Greenland has pushed European officials and diplomats to toughen their views on the need for Europe to curb its dependence on the U.S., from tech to defense to trade. The European Parliament on Thursday passed a “technological sovereignty” resolution that supports using public procurement criteria to favor European products where possible and proposes new legislation to promote European cloud providers.

A potential “decoupling” of Europe and U.S. tech was a hot topic among business leaders and policymakers at the World Economic Forum in Davos this week. Many said it would be a complex undertaking given the breadth of American tech used.

The scale of Europe’s dependence on U.S. tech has never been so large, particularly for cloud-computing services from companies including Amazon, Google and Microsoft. In 2024, European customers spent nearly $25 billion on infrastructure services from the top five U.S. cloud companies, or 83% of the total market in Europe, according to research firm IDC.

Many European entrepreneurs blame Europe’s plight on a risk-averse culture, a fragmented market and onerous regulations. That’s in large part why the EU is now trying to relax some of its digital rules, though progress has so far been slow.

SEE THE STORY

6

Investors are flocking back to hedge funds after an ‘alpha winter.’

A recent stretch of strong returns is making hedge funds the most favored asset class for institutions that allocate money to outside investment firms, according to a Goldman Sachs survey of 317 fund investors viewed by WSJ. About 45% of them plan to increase their exposure to hedge funds in 2026, net of those looking to decrease it, an all-time high in survey records going back to 2017 and an 18-percentage-point increase from last year.

HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

7

Sunday: The NFL Conference Championships, which will determine the two teams that play in the Super Bowl. 📰 Today's paper 

THE NUMBER

8

 >4 billion

The number of barrels of Venezuelan oil to which Chinese government-owned oil companies hold claims, nearly five times as much as Chevron, the only U.S. major that today produces in the South American nation. Beijing’s production deals, oil rigs and debt-backed supply arrangements have long bought it enormous sway in Venezuela—and all of it is now subject to the Trump administration’s preferences.

AND FINALLY...

9

Why choose between a ski vacation and an urban escape?

A day on the mountain might not be the type of escape you usually tack onto a vacation at the last minute. But it’s surprisingly easy to pull off from a few cities , including Denver, Tokyo and Munich. In these three locations on three continents, here’s how you can get out on the snow after breakfast and still be back in time for après-ski cocktails at the hotel bar.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: Donald Trump’s proposed $1.5 trillion military budget is the right decision. The best way to go down as a peacemaker is by building a military no one wants to fight.
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 對沖基金重返華爾街食物鏈頂端。2025年,這類基金的整體表現創下十多年來最佳紀錄,投資人今年也準備繼續向這一資產類別注入資金。相較之下,英特爾的處境則艱難得多。經過數月的正面氛圍後,投資人本週目睹這家晶片製造商的股價重摔回地面。我們探討這家公司如何錯失一場本應輕鬆到手的勝利。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1

隨著部分進步派人士推動解散ICE,民主黨人面臨一場老問題:如何在不被視為「反法治」政黨的情況下抵制川普的政策。在達沃斯,川普總統帶來的衝擊性存在感,迫使與會者必須就重大議題(美國可能接管格陵蘭)與小議題(各方之間的衝突)做出決斷。中國國家主席習近平已將其頭號將領交付調查,延續了一場正掏空軍方高層的反軍中貪腐與不忠誠整肅行動。敘利亞總統對庫德族主導的民兵組織發動的攻勢,證明了他的軍事膽識,以及不惜冒險與美國關係惡化的意願。生成式AI正讓與裝置的語音互動變得更有效率、更不惱人,科技產業將從此不同,克里斯多福·米姆斯撰文分析。

市場動態

2

本週道瓊工業指數小跌0.5%,標普500指數下跌0.4%,那斯達克指數下跌0.1%,幾乎看不出市場曾一度險些遭遇貿易衝擊的跡象。英特爾股價暴跌17%——此前該股曾因白宮、輝達與軟銀的信心投票而受到提振——原因是財報電話會議揭露,這家晶片製造商難以滿足暴增的AI相關需求。摩根士丹利頂尖研究員亞當·喬納斯(Adam Jonas)正拿自己的聲譽,押注機器人與飛天車的未來。

搶先看

3

隨著格陵蘭前途未定,世界似乎又回到了帝國時代。

儘管川普目前已暫時收回以經濟或軍事脅迫手段接管這塊丹麥領土的威脅,但美國擴張主義野心帶來的震撼仍未消散,德魯·欣肖(Drew Hinshaw)與馬庫斯·沃克(Marcus Walker)報導。在歐洲各國首都,幾乎沒有人相信跨大西洋關係將恢復正常。本週的談話中,川普將領土擴張描述為一種正常的歷史過程。但他隻字未提的是:帝國時代大多數領土的取得,靠的是流血衝突,而非金錢購買。而當金錢確實易手時,有時也是在戰勝國強迫戰敗國出售的脅迫之下進行的。

4

本賽季NFL最激烈的對決,是體育博彩對決預測市場。

美國人預計將創下紀錄,在超級盃上下注超過15億美元。由於預測市場公司Polymarket與Kalshi正挑戰體育博彩巨頭FanDuel與DraftKings,美國幾乎人人都能首度參與其中。儘管體育博彩在11個州仍屬非法,但受聯邦監管的預測市場提供了一條參與途徑,凱瑟琳·塞爾(Katherine Sayre)與傑瑞德·戴蒙(Jared Diamond)報導。這些市場讓用戶可以對包括政治與流行文化在內的許多領域下注,但體育賽事仍佔其業務的大宗。

盡享本報最精彩的特稿寫作。
每週瀏覽我們關於人生百態最生動、發人深省又原創的特稿內容。訂閱《華爾街日報》週末讀物通訊。

專家解讀

5

問:歐洲擔心美國可能封鎖其技術取得管道,這問題有多嚴重?

與美國日益升高的緊張關係,正促使歐洲擬定新計畫,擺脫美國科技、轉而扶植本土替代方案。記者山姆·謝克納(Sam Schechner)、伯柏·金(Berber Jin)與金姆·麥克雷爾(Kim Mackrael)撰文分析該地區對「科技主權」的追求。

答:川普對格陵蘭的做法,促使歐洲官員與外交人員在歐洲需在多大程度上降低對美依賴——從科技、國防到貿易——的問題上,採取更強硬的立場。歐洲議會週四通過了一項「科技主權」決議,支持在可能的情況下利用公共採購標準優先選用歐洲產品,並提議制定新法規以扶植歐洲雲端服務供應商。

歐洲與美國科技可能出現的「脫鉤」,是本週達沃斯世界經濟論壇上企業領袖與政策制定者熱議的話題。許多人表示,鑑於美國科技使用範圍之廣,這將是一項複雜的工程。

歐洲對美國科技的依賴程度,從未像現在這麼高,尤其是在來自亞馬遜、Google與微軟等公司的雲端運算服務方面。根據市場研究機構IDC的數據,2024年,歐洲客戶在五大美國雲端服務公司的基礎設施服務上花費近250億美元,佔歐洲市場總額的83%。

許多歐洲企業家將歐洲的困境歸咎於規避風險的文化、分裂的市場以及繁重的法規。這也是歐盟如今試圖鬆綁部分數位法規的重要原因之一,儘管進展至今仍相當緩慢。

閱讀全文

6

在經歷「阿爾法寒冬」後,投資人正重新湧向對沖基金。

根據高盛對317名基金投資人所做、《華爾街日報》取得的調查,近期一波強勁報酬,正讓對沖基金成為那些將資金配置給外部投資機構的機構投資人最青睞的資產類別。約45%的受訪者計劃在2026年增加對沖基金的配置(扣除計劃減少配置的受訪者比例後的淨值),這是自2017年開始進行此項調查以來的歷史新高,較去年上升了18個百分點。

本週末焦點

7

週日:NFL聯盟冠軍賽,將決定角逐超級盃的兩支隊伍。📰 今日報紙。

數字看世界

8

超過40億桶

中國國有石油公司對委內瑞拉石油擁有的權利桶數,幾乎是雪佛龍(目前唯一在這個南美國家生產石油的美國大型石油公司)的五倍。北京的生產協議、鑽油平台以及以債務擔保的供應安排,長期以來為其在委內瑞拉帶來巨大影響力——而如今,這一切都取決於川普政府的意向。

最後,還有這則

9

何必在滑雪假期與城市小旅行之間二選一?

在山上度過一天,或許不是你通常會臨時安排進假期行程的那種休閒方式。但令人意外的是,從包括丹佛、東京與慕尼黑在內的幾座城市出發,其實相當容易實現。在這三大洲的三座城市,以下告訴你如何在早餐後出門滑雪,又能及時趕回飯店酒吧享用滑雪後的雞尾酒。

新聞編輯室之外

10

社論:川普提出的1.5兆美元國防預算案是正確的決定。要在歷史上留下「和平締造者」的美名,最好的方法就是打造一支沒有人敢招惹的軍隊。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Congress Can’t Claw Back War Powers From Trump
emails.contentEn:
✏️ In a dizzying three weeks on the world stage, President Trump deposed Venezuela’s leader, threatened its neighbors with military action, raised the specter of new strikes on Iran and ignited—then tamped down—a diplomatic crisis with Europe over his efforts to acquire Greenland. At each fresh turn, Congress has found itself scrambling to keep up, sparking new debates among lawmakers about how to claw back constitutional powers from the presidency over matters of foreign policy in the Trump era.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

A resolution to rein in Trump’s powers to wage war in Venezuela was narrowly defeated in the House, after Republican leaders hustled a lawmaker back from Texas to cast the deciding vote. It failed in a tie vote of 215-215. Elon Musk is opening his wallet and reigniting his political apparatus for the 2026 midterm elections. China has seized upon the disarray left by Trump within the trans-Atlantic alliance, trying to entice U.S. allies with the promise of reliable trade partnerships. Vice President JD Vance placed himself at the center of a clash between the federal government and state and local officials over immigration enforcement, calling for greater cooperation with ICE. Venezuela’s interim government unveiled a bill to loosen the state’s iron grip on its beleaguered oil industry, a move aimed at attracting U.S. energy companies.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

TikTok officially established a joint venture that would allow it to keep operating in the U.S., the company said, resolving a yearslong fight to address Washington’s national-security concerns. Trump’s push for a credit-card interest-rate cap could be a problem for issuers of plastic. But if the experience of other industries is any guide, investors might want to consider buying bank stocks , writes Telis Demos.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

The West stepped back from the brink. But Europe’s distrust of America lingers.

The crisis over Greenland, though now defused, already has many European leaders worrying about long-term damage. Trump’s approach has also prompted leaders in Europe and Canada to focus more on reducing their countries’ economic, technological and military dependence on the U.S., the kind of derisking previously reserved for China and Russia. Some European officials have started seriously worrying about the exposure of their economies to U.S. software, payment systems and communications platforms that could be switched off or disrupted in case of an escalating conflict, reports Yaroslav Trofimov.

4

Congress can’t claw back war powers from Trump.

Many U.S. lawmakers—Democrats and a small but growing number of Republicans—are searching for ways to rein in the president. At stake, they say, is the U.S.-led global order that’s been in place since the end of World War II. So far, these lawmakers concede they are failing. The latest Republican-controlled Congress has accelerated a decadeslong shift giving the White House greater authority to take on America’s adversaries and even some allies, write Robbie Gramer and Lindsay Wise.

 EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: How can a ‘raise’ from Social Security result in less take-home pay for retirees?

Nearly six million seniors owe extra Medicare premiums called Irmaa, and these charges are set to rise , writes Laura Saunders.

A: The short answer is that rising Medicare premiums ate into their monthly benefit.

Now here’s more: For 2026, Social Security’s inflation adjustment is 2.8%. Despite this “raise,” some seniors will see their monthly benefits shrink.

That’s because Medicare premiums are based on the overall cost of the Medicare program, and its costs and premiums have been rising. These premiums are subtracted from the monthly Social Security payments, so they can reduce a senior’s “take-home” pay.

Nearly six million higher-earning seniors face yet another Medicare charge that affects their Social Security payment. This charge is based on income and is called Irmaa, for “Income related monthly adjustment amount.”

Congress enacted Irmaa to have higher earners pick up a greater portion of their own Medicare costs. Annual Irmaa charges in 2026 for Part B Medicare (for doctors and outpatient care) range from about $974 to about $5,844 per recipient, depending on income.

According to the 2025 Medicare Trustees Report, overall Part B Irmaa charges are expected to increase 30% from 2026 to 2030–so Irmaa’s bite will likely grow as well.

SEE THE STORY

6

We have no idea how to code. So we got Claude to code this article for us.

GIF: EMIL LENDOF/WSJ

Using Anthropic’s Claude Code, two WSJ columnists with no formal programming background vibe coded this article —chat bubbles, Easter eggs and all. Vibe-coding apps aren’t new, but Claude Code has proved to be a leap ahead in capabilities and smarts. The results are wondrous and unsettling: People without a lick of coding experience are building things that once required trained software developers.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

U.S., Russian and Ukrainian negotiators are holding trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi. Economic data: University of Michigan consumer sentiment for January Earnings: Comerica, SLB Helen Macdonald’s critically acclaimed memoir, “H Is for Hawk,” lands on the big screen, starring Claire Foy. Check out everything else on this week’s arts calendar . 📰 Today's paper 

THE NUMBER

The forecasts have stoked fears of a repeat of the deadly winter storm that froze Texas in 2021 and left millions of people without electricity for days. Energy producers and utilities are preparing for the worst. Subzero temperatures are in store for Minneapolis, Chicago and Detroit starting today. New York and Washington, D.C., are expected to be buried in snow by the end of the weekend.

AND FINALLY...

9

Dana White’s empire of testosterone now stretches to the White House.

When asked what connects his two spheres of influence—mixed martial arts and Trump’s MAGA base—Ultimate Fighting Championship mogul Dana White has a simple answer: “Testosterone.” White has built an empire off it. Over more than two decades, he’s taken the UFC from obscurity to an operation estimated to be worth more than $20 billion by parent TKO Group Holdings. White occupies a unique position in the zeitgeist: A sports kingpin, he’s also part of a circle of Trump whisperers and influencers.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

He is constrained by democratic institutions in the U.S., the necessity of maintaining alliances abroad, and public opinion as measured by polls and investors.
emails.contentZh:
✏️ 在令人目不暇給的三週內,川普總統推翻了委內瑞拉領導人,威脅要對其鄰國採取軍事行動,重新掀起對伊朗發動新一輪打擊的可能性,並在爭取取得格陵蘭的過程中引爆——隨後又平息——一場與歐洲的外交危機。每一次局勢轉折,國會都發現自己疲於奔命地追趕局勢,這也在議員之間引發新一輪辯論:在川普時代,國會該如何從總統手中奪回涉及外交政策的憲法權力。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1

一項旨在約束川普在委內瑞拉發動戰爭權力的決議案,在共和黨領袖緊急將一名議員從德州召回投下關鍵一票後,以215票對215票的平手結果在眾議院險遭否決。馬斯克正為2026年期中選舉重新打開錢包、啟動他的政治機器。中國正抓住川普在跨大西洋聯盟中留下的混亂局面,試圖以承諾建立可靠貿易夥伴關係來拉攏美國盟友。副總統范斯(JD Vance)將自己置於聯邦政府與州及地方官員在移民執法問題上衝突的核心,呼籲加強與ICE的合作。委內瑞拉臨時政府公布一項法案,擬鬆綁國家對其陷入困境的石油產業的嚴格控制,此舉旨在吸引美國能源公司。

市場即時動態

2

道瓊期貨 49429.00 -129.00 0.26%;標普500期貨 6927.50 -17.50 0.25%;那斯達克100期貨 25560.00 -98.25 0.38%
資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年1月23日美東時間上午5:46:03

📈 全天追蹤我們的即時財經報導。

TikTok表示,該公司已正式成立一家合資企業,使其得以繼續在美國營運,這解決了華府對國家安全疑慮長達數年的爭端。川普推動的信用卡利率上限政策,可能對發卡機構帶來麻煩。但若參考其他產業的經驗,投資人或許該考慮買進銀行股,泰利斯·德莫斯撰文分析。

搶先看

3

西方陣營從懸崖邊緣退了回來。但歐洲對美國的不信任依然揮之不去。

雖然格陵蘭危機目前已經解除,但許多歐洲領袖已開始擔心此事造成的長期損害。川普的做法也促使歐洲與加拿大領袖更加專注於降低本國在經濟、科技與軍事上對美國的依賴——這種「去風險化」做法過去通常只用於應對中國與俄羅斯。部分歐洲官員已開始認真憂心,自身經濟過度依賴美國的軟體、支付系統與通訊平台,一旦衝突升級,這些系統可能遭切斷或中斷,亞羅斯拉夫·特羅菲莫夫報導。

4

國會無法從川普手中奪回戰爭權力。

許多美國國會議員——民主黨人以及數量雖小但正在增加的共和黨人——正尋求約束總統權力的方法。他們表示,攸關的是自二戰結束以來一直存在的美國主導全球秩序。到目前為止,這些議員也承認自己並未成功。目前由共和黨掌控的國會,加速了數十年來讓白宮在應對美國對手乃至部分盟友時擁有更大權力的趨勢轉變,羅比·格雷默(Robbie Gramer)與琳賽·懷斯(Lindsay Wise)報導。

暫時遠離新聞喘口氣。
訂閱《華爾街日報》雜誌通訊,每週彙整時尚、娛樂、設計、美食、旅遊、藝術、建築等內容。

專家解讀

5

問:社會安全金的「加薪」,為何反而讓退休人士實際到手金額變少?

近六百萬名長者需額外支付一項名為Irmaa的聯邦醫療保險保費,而這筆費用即將上漲,蘿拉·桑德斯(Laura Saunders)撰文分析。

答:簡短的答案是,不斷上漲的聯邦醫療保險保費侵蝕了他們每月的給付金額。

進一步說明:2026年,社會安全金的通膨調整幅度為2.8%。儘管有這項「加薪」,部分長者每月的實際給付金額仍將縮水。

這是因為聯邦醫療保險保費是根據該計畫整體成本計算的,而其成本與保費一直在上漲。這些保費會從每月的社會安全金給付中扣除,因此可能減少長者實際到手的金額。

近六百萬名收入較高的長者,還面臨另一項影響其社會安全金給付的聯邦醫療保險費用。這項費用依收入計算,稱為Irmaa,即「收入相關月度調整金額」。

國會制定Irmaa制度,目的是讓高收入者承擔更大比例的自身醫療保險成本。2026年B部分聯邦醫療保險(涵蓋醫師與門診照護)的年度Irmaa費用,依收入不同,每人約在974美元至5844美元之間。

根據2025年聯邦醫療保險受託人報告,整體B部分Irmaa費用預計將從2026年到2030年間增加30%——因此Irmaa帶來的負擔預計也將隨之加重。

閱讀全文

6

我們完全不會寫程式。所以我們讓Claude替我們寫了這篇文章的程式碼。

動圖:EMIL LENDOF/WSJ

兩位毫無正式程式設計背景的本報專欄作家,利用Anthropic的Claude Code「氛圍編程」(vibe coding)完成了這篇文章——聊天氣泡、彩蛋一應俱全。氛圍編程應用程式並非新鮮事,但Claude Code已證明其能力與智慧有了長足躍進。結果既令人驚嘆又令人不安:完全沒有寫程式經驗的人,如今正打造出過去需要專業軟體開發人員才能完成的東西。

今日焦點

7

美、俄、烏三方談判代表正在阿布達比舉行三邊會談。經濟數據:密西根大學1月消費者信心指數。財報:美國聯信銀行、斯倫貝謝。海倫·麥克唐納(Helen Macdonald)備受讚譽的回憶錄《H is for Hawk》搬上大銀幕,由克萊兒·芙伊(Claire Foy)主演。這裡是本週其餘的藝文行事曆。📰 今日報紙。

數字看世界

8

63%

本週天然氣價格因預測顯示即將迎來數年來最冷、降雪量最大的天氣而飆漲的幅度。這些預測已引發外界擔憂,恐重演2021年凍住德州、導致數百萬人斷電數日的致命冬季風暴。能源生產商與公用事業公司正為最壞情況做準備。從今天起,明尼阿波利斯、芝加哥與底特律將迎來零下低溫。紐約與華府預計在週末結束前將被大雪掩埋。

最後,還有這則

9

戴娜·懷特(Dana White)的「睪固酮帝國」如今已延伸至白宮。

當被問及他所涉足的兩個影響力領域——綜合格鬥與川普的MAGA支持基礎——之間有何關聯時,終極格鬥錦標賽(UFC)大亨戴娜·懷特的答案很簡單:「睪固酮。」懷特靠這個詞打造了一個帝國。二十多年來,他將UFC從默默無聞,發展成如今由母公司TKO集團控股(TKO Group Holdings)估值超過200億美元的事業。懷特在當代文化氛圍中佔據著獨特地位:他既是體壇霸主,也是川普身邊「密語圈」與網紅圈子的一員。

新聞編輯室之外

10

社論:川普並非為所欲為就能全身而退。他仍受制於美國的民主體制、維繫海外盟邦關係的必要性,以及以民調與投資人反應衡量的公眾輿論。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: After Venezuela, U.S. Turns Pressure on Cuba
emails.contentEn:
✏️ When President Trump arrived in Davos yesterday afternoon, European leaders were panicking that his push to acquire Greenland would trigger a trans-Atlantic conflagration. By sunset, Trump had backed down . But Greenland isn’t the only island on the president’s “Donroe Doctrine” map: We have exclusive new reporting on the Trump administration’s search for Havana insiders to help cut a deal to end Communist rule in Cuba by the end of the year.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY’S HEADLINES

1

Trump’s head-spinning U-turn on Greenland followed days of back-channel conversations between the president, his advisers and European leaders. Supreme Court justices across the ideological spectrum expressed deep unease about Trump’s attempt to fire a member of the Federal Reserve. The Trump administration is asserting new powers to forcibly enter the homes of people it is hoping to arrest without a criminal warrant signed by a judge. In an ominous sign for Iran’s regime, the bloodiest crisis in the country’s recent political history started in a conservative bastion : Tehran’s market area. Beijing’s spy machine is enticing Taiwan’s military personnel to share intelligence and pledge allegiance to China.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 49459.00 194.00 0.39 S&P 500 Futures 6951.50 41.50 0.60 Nasdaq 100 Futures 25692.25 221.25 0.87

Source: Factset, Market data as of 1/22/2026, 5:59:19 AM ET

📈 Follow our live financial coverage all day.

For the first time since the start of the private-credit boom, large numbers of individual investors are trying to get their money out . Insurance companies that cover homes and cars are reaping the rewards of price increases , but the contrast between near-record profits and sharp rate hikes has put the industry in the regulatory firing line. America’s removal of Nicolás Maduro has captured the imaginations of oil-field services companies. But Venezuela isn’t the main reason to get excited about these companies, writes Jinjoo Lee.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

In Greenland, anxiety over U.S. ambitions puts normal life on pause.

Trump, speaking at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, yesterday, said he wouldn’t deploy the military to take control of the territory. But his assurances did little to calm the nerves of its residents. Through it all, many have felt like pawns in a global game that has upended their politics. Before Trump renewed his bid to take over, the debate wasn’t if—but when—Greenland would become independent from Denmark. Now that process is on hold as the island tries to ride out the political storm, reports Drew Hinshaw.

4

The U.S. is actively seeking a regime change in Cuba by the end of the year.

Emboldened by the ouster of Venezuela’s president, the Trump administration is searching for Cuban government insiders who can help cut a deal to push out the Communist regime by the end of the year, people familiar with the matter said. The administration has assessed Cuba’s economy as being close to collapse and that the government has never been this fragile. Officials don’t have a concrete plan to end the Communist government, but they see Maduro’s capture and subsequent concessions from his allies left behind as a blueprint and a warning for Cuba, report José de Córdoba, Vera Bergengruen and Deborah Acosta.

Take control of your news.

Make the Journal your preferred source on Google to see more of our award-winning journalism.

 EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: What’s the best airline to fly?

WSJ ranked nine major U.S. airlines on seven operations metrics including flight cancellations and on-time arrivals. The winner has spent billions improving operations—while navigating a corporate shake-up and revamping its strategy, write Dawn Gilbertson and Allison Pohle.

A: Southwest Airlines took first place in the Journal’s 18th annual airline scorecard for the first time since 2020. The nation’s largest domestic carrier by passengers won by a wide margin, ending Delta’s four-year winning streak.

Budget carrier Allegiant came in second, followed by Delta in third. In our ratings basement: American and Frontier, which tied for last place. It was a return trip for Frontier.

Southwest didn’t best rivals in every category but had high showings across the board. It had the fewest customer complaints and delays, and was second best in on-time arrivals and the rate of canceled flights. Its worst finish was fourth, for baggage handling.

Despite industry challenges and sweeping internal changes, its operation hummed. The airline, which long eschewed layoffs, cut its corporate workforce by 15%. It started red-eye flights to get more use out of its planes and began charging for checked bags and saw the volume of carry-on bags surge.

Overall, airlines performed about the same as they did the prior year. The industry averages for cancellations, bags lost and bumping were essentially flat compared with 2024.

SEE THE STORY

6

Americans are traveling the world only to end up at Costco.

Tommy Breaux and Danny Terrebonne at a now-closed Costco in Australia. PHOTO: TOMMY BREAUX

As the retailer planted its flag in 13 foreign markets, its devoted American members have followed. Search online for Costco in Sweden or Taiwan, and you’ll find videos narrated in breathless wonder. Travelers hunt for regional souvenirs, soothe their homesickness and investigate a burning question: Is the hot dog different ?

HAPPENING TODAY

Vice President JD Vance is scheduled to visit Minnesota for a roundtable with local leaders and community members amid escalating tensions over federal immigration operations in the state. Oscar nominations are announced at 8:30 a.m. ET. Elon Musk is set to appear at the World Economic Forum at 10:30 a.m. ET. Starting annual salary for a sports trader at Susquehanna International Group, roughly on par with a parole officer in nearby Philadelphia. Prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket have exploded in popularity recently and finance firms are in the early stages of figuring out how they can make money from them. The relatively low salaries being offered to would-be bettors reflect that.

AND FINALLY...

9

Here’s how Canada pulled off the sexiest show of the year.

Executives at Bell Media were hunting for their own version of Netflix’s “Bridgerton” when they received a script about rival pro-hockey players in a secret romance. Other companies might have balked, but the script came from one of their most trusted showrunners, so Bell seized it. Their bet on “Heated Rivalry” paid off . The series has become the Canadian media company’s most successful original series of the streaming era—despite being solo-financed and launched with minimal promotion.

✏️ 昨天下午,當川普總統抵達達沃斯時,歐洲領袖正為他爭取取得格陵蘭的行動可能引發跨大西洋衝突而感到恐慌。到日落時分,川普已經退讓。但格陵蘭並非總統「唐羅主義」(Donroe Doctrine)版圖上唯一的一座島嶼:我們獲得獨家報導,川普政府正在尋找哈瓦那內部人士,協助促成一項在今年底前結束古巴共產政權統治的協議。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1

川普在格陵蘭問題上令人瞠目結舌的大轉彎,是在總統、其幕僚與歐洲領袖歷經數日幕後溝通後才發生的。橫跨意識形態光譜的最高法院大法官們,都對川普試圖解僱一名聯準會理事的做法表達深切不安。川普政府正主張新的權力,在未經法官簽署刑事逮捕令的情況下,強行進入其欲逮捕對象的住宅。對伊朗政權而言,一個不祥的徵兆是:該國近期政治史上最血腥的危機,竟起源於一個保守派堡壘——德黑蘭的市集區。北京的間諜機構正誘使台灣軍事人員洩露情報,並宣誓效忠中國。

市場即時動態

2

道瓊期貨 49459.00 +194.00 0.39%;標普500期貨 6951.50 +41.50 0.60%;那斯達克100期貨 25692.25 +221.25 0.87%

📈 全天追蹤我們的即時財經報導。

自私募信貸熱潮興起以來,首次有大批散戶投資人試圖將資金撤出。承保住宅與汽車險的保險公司正坐享漲價帶來的收益,但這種近乎歷史新高的獲利與大幅調漲保費之間的反差,已讓該產業成為監管機構關注的焦點。美國推翻尼古拉斯·馬杜洛一事,已激起油田服務公司的想像空間。但委內瑞拉並非看好這些公司的主要理由,李金珠(Jinjoo Lee)撰文分析。

搶先看

3

在格陵蘭,對美國野心的憂慮讓日常生活按下了暫停鍵。

川普昨天在瑞士達沃斯世界經濟論壇發表演說時表示,他不會部署軍隊來奪取這塊領土的控制權。但他的保證並未能安撫當地居民的不安情緒。整個過程中,許多人感覺自己像是一場顛覆其政治格局的全球博弈中的棋子。在川普重啟接管企圖之前,爭論的焦點並非格陵蘭是否會脫離丹麥獨立,而是何時獨立。如今,隨著這座島嶼試圖挺過這場政治風暴,這一進程已被擱置,德魯·欣肖報導。

4

美國正積極尋求在今年底前促成古巴政權更迭。

受到委內瑞拉總統遭推翻一事的鼓舞,知情人士透露,川普政府正在尋找古巴政府內部人士,協助促成一項在今年底前迫使共產政權下台的協議。政府評估認為,古巴經濟已接近崩潰邊緣,該國政府從未如此脆弱過。官員們目前尚無終結共產政府的具體計畫,但他們將馬杜洛遭逮捕、以及其盟友隨後做出的讓步視為古巴的一份藍圖與警訊,何塞·德科爾多瓦(José de Córdoba)、薇拉·貝根格倫(Vera Bergengruen)與黛博拉·阿科斯塔(Deborah Acosta)報導。

將本報設為你在Google上的首選新聞來源,獲取更多我們屢獲殊榮的新聞報導。

專家解讀

5

問:哪家航空公司飛行體驗最好?

本報針對包括航班取消率與準點抵達率在內的七項營運指標,對美國九家主要航空公司進行評比。這次奪冠的公司,已投入數十億美元改善營運——同時還在經歷公司內部改組並調整策略,道恩·吉爾伯森(Dawn Gilbertson)與艾莉森·波爾(Allison Pohle)報導。

答:西南航空在本報第18屆年度航空公司評比中,自2020年以來首度奪冠。這家美國國內載客量最大的航空公司以懸殊優勢勝出,終結了達美航空連續四年的冠軍紀錄。

廉價航空公司Allegiant位居第二,達美航空排名第三。排名墊底的是美國航空與前沿航空,兩者並列最後一名,前沿航空則是重返榜末。

西南航空並非在每個項目都擊敗對手,但整體表現十分亮眼。該公司客訴與延誤次數最少,準點抵達率與航班取消率則排名第二。表現最差的一項是行李處理,排名第四。

儘管面臨產業挑戰與大規模內部變革,該公司營運依然順暢運轉。這家長期避免裁員的航空公司,將企業員工人數削減了15%。該公司開始開闢紅眼航班,以提高飛機使用率,並開始對託運行李收費,結果隨身攜帶行李的數量隨之激增。

整體而言,今年航空業表現與去年大致相當。取消航班、行李遺失與超賣的產業平均值,與2024年相比基本持平。

閱讀全文

6

美國人跑遍全世界,結果只是為了逛好市多。

湯米·布羅(Tommy Breaux)與丹尼·特雷本(Danny Terrebonne)在澳洲一家如今已歇業的好市多門市前合影。照片:TOMMY BREAUX

隨著這家零售商在13個海外市場插旗,它忠實的美國會員也緊隨其後。在網路上搜尋「瑞典好市多」或「台灣好市多」,你會找到用充滿驚嘆語氣旁白的影片。旅人四處尋找當地限定紀念品,藉此緩解思鄉之情,同時探究一個令人好奇的問題:那裡的熱狗跟美國的一樣嗎?

今日焦點

7

在該州聯邦移民行動引發的緊張局勢持續升高之際,副總統范斯預計將前往明尼蘇達州,與地方領袖及社區居民舉行圓桌會議。奧斯卡入圍名單將於美東時間上午8:30公布。馬斯克預計於美東時間上午10:30出席世界經濟論壇。財報:亞培實驗室、第一資本金融公司、通用電氣航空、英特爾、寶潔。📰 今日報紙。

數字看世界

8

9萬美元

Susquehanna International Group一名體育交易員的起薪年薪,大致與鄰近費城的一名假釋官薪資相當。Kalshi與Polymarket等預測市場近來人氣暴增,金融公司也才剛開始摸索如何從中獲利。這些提供給潛在投注員的相對偏低薪資,正反映出這一點。

最後,還有這則

9

加拿大是如何打造出年度最性感劇集的。

Bell Media高層原本正在尋找自家版本的Netflix《柏捷頓家族》,結果收到了一部關於敵對職業冰球選手秘密戀情的劇本。換作其他公司或許會猶豫,但這部劇本出自他們最信任的一位劇集主創之手,於是Bell Media毫不猶豫地接下了。他們押注《Heated Rivalry》的決定獲得了回報。這部劇集已成為這家加拿大媒體公司在串流時代最成功的原創劇集——儘管是由公司獨資製作、且僅以極少量宣傳推出上映。

新聞編輯室之外

社論:中國與俄羅斯最樂見的,莫過於格陵蘭成為引爆北約、造成跨大西洋永久裂痕的導火線。

✏️ President Trump will be at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, today, where tensions over Greenland continue to dominate discussions. Still, the president said world leaders and CEOs are “very happily” waiting for his arrival. He’s expected to speak at the gathering and hold a meeting about Greenland while he’s here. In other WEF news: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei sat down with me and answered your questions on AI.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY’S HEADLINES

1

A fierce backlash is mounting among U.S. allies over Trump’s threats to impose punitive tariffs and use military force to acquire Greenland. The president is on his way to Davos where he is scheduled to give a special address later today. Follow our live coverage of the forum here . Russian President Vladimir Putin has sought to undermine NATO for nearly two decades—now, as Trump’s push to control Greenland strains the alliance, Moscow is cheering from the sidelines . After pulling back from strikes on Iran last week, Trump continues to seek “decisive” military options as the U.S. deploys an aircraft carrier and jet fighters to the Middle East. Trump accelerated his effort to prevent institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2

 LAST CHG %CHG DJIA Futures 48735.00 69.00 0.14 S&P 500 Futures 6846.25 16.75 0.25 Nasdaq 100 Futures 25176.25 47.00 0.19

Source: Factset, Market data as of 1/21/2026, 5:43:51 AM ET

📈 Follow our live financial coverage all day.

Amazon is launching a megastore outside Chicago with a footprint so large it could fit nearly two average-size Target stores under its roof. Elon Musk is racing to take SpaceX public this year. Here’s why . The new Netflix is still a ways off, but the old one is doing fine. Given what Netflix is trying to accomplish, though, fine doesn’t quite cut it , says Dan Gallagher.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Trump’s Greenland strategy draws from a familiar playbook.

European leaders have for months responded to the president’s desire to acquire Greenland with a simple refrain: It isn’t for sale. Now, those same leaders are rushing to set up meetings with him about the future of the territory after he threatened to bludgeon Europe’s economy with stiff tariffs.The shift is the result of an established strategy for Trump: make audacious demands, threaten economic or military consequences if those demands aren’t met—then wait for his opponents to bend, report Meridith McGraw and Natalie Andrews.

Escalating tensions over Greenland are supercharging a shift away from a U.S.-centered global economy, as Trump’s combative policies compel countries to seek new trade alliances and invest elsewhere.

4

Chinese electric vehicles are blowing past Tesla and tariffs en route to global reign.

Not long ago, few would buy the idea that a Chinese EV maker such as BYD could sweep European buyers off their feet. Yet the company is leading a pack of Chinese automakers whose global export onslaught has surpassed even bullish expectations. BYD, which replaced Tesla as the world’s biggest EV seller, delivered more than a million vehicles outside China in 2025, more than double the previous year’s total, report Stephen Wilmot and Santiago Pérez.

Check out the future—today.

Sign up for The Future of Everything newsletter for a look at how innovation and technology are transforming the way we live, work and play.

 EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: Why does Trump want Greenland?

Reporter Georgi Kantchev explains why the president has doubled down on his campaign to acquire the island:

A: In Greenland, Trump has set his sights on a vast, ice-covered and sparsely populated island with a strategic location on the edge of the Arctic.

It has ample deposits in rare earths, oil and gas and its commanding position astride crucial trade and military arteries has made it a focal point for rival major powers.

Russia and China have been beefing up their activities in the region in recent years and Trump has said that Greenland is important to his plans to implement a “Golden Dome” missile-defense plan.

His aspiration also aligns with his desire to establish U.S. hegemony over the Western Hemisphere, an idea dubbed the “Donroe Doctrine.” Control over Greenland and the broader Arctic is valuable for projecting power, monitoring activities of rivals and securing shipping routes.

But extracting these minerals isn’t easy. Mining companies operating there contend with high costs, sparse infrastructure and hostile weather.

SEE THE STORY

6

This booming mountain town has Montana’s most expensive real estate.

PHOTO: ALYSSA FREESE FOR WSJ

In southwestern Montana, near Yellowstone National Park, is Big Sky, a mountain community that emerged around 1973 with the opening of remote ski area. Over time, Big Sky has transformed from a scattering of residences and businesses into a true town and a destination for wealthy ski-home buyers. The median listing price is $3.05 million as of December 2025. Despite this growth, the community keeps an authentic Montana feel: Dressing up still means putting on cowboy boots, jeans and, maybe, a cowboy hat.

HAPPENING TODAY

7

The Supreme Court is set to hear oral arguments in Fed Governor Lisa Cook’s case against Trump, who is trying to fire her for alleged mortgage fraud. Earnings: Johnson & Johnson, Charles Schwab 📰 Today’s paper 

THE NUMBER

8

 $100

The amount New Hampshire state legislators are paid per year since voters etched it into the state constitution in 1889. Granite State lawmakers are the lowest paid in the U.S.; their counterparts in most states have salaries of around $47,900. Many past bids to boost pay for NH lawmakers by amending the constitution failed. Now, there is a bipartisan push to delete the pay language from the foundational document.

AND FINALLY...

9

Meet the Americans who are going a whole month without buying anything.

This January, some aren’t just giving up alcohol but forgoing buying anything at all. Fueled by social media, some consumers are starting the new year with a pledge to eliminate purchases of anything nonessential for the whole month. Thrifty challenges have gained in popularity. Google searches for “ No Buy January ” hit a five-year high in December, driven largely by Gen Z and millennials.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10

Opinion: The Supreme Court will consider today whether Trump has the power to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook. The stakes are high for presidential power and the central bank’s independence.

✏️ 川普總統今天將出席在瑞士達沃斯舉行的世界經濟論壇,格陵蘭議題引發的緊張情勢持續主導著論壇的討論。儘管如此,總統表示各國領袖與企業執行長都「非常樂於」等待他的到來。他預計將在會議上發表演說,並在此期間就格陵蘭問題舉行會談。另一則世界經濟論壇消息:Anthropic執行長達里奧·阿莫迪(Dario Amodei)接受了我的訪問,並回答了讀者關於AI的提問。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1

美國盟友對川普以懲罰性關稅與軍事力量威脅奪取格陵蘭一事,正掀起強烈反彈。總統正在前往達沃斯的途中,預計今天稍後將在論壇上發表特別演說。點此追蹤我們對論壇的即時報導。俄羅斯總統普丁近二十年來一直致力於削弱北約——如今,隨著川普爭取控制格陵蘭的行動使聯盟關係緊繃,莫斯科正在一旁樂觀其成。在上週撤回對伊朗的打擊行動後,隨著美國向中東部署航母與戰機,川普仍持續尋求「果斷」的軍事選項。川普加速推動防止機構投資人購買獨棟住宅的行動。

市場即時動態

2

道瓊期貨 48735.00 +69.00 0.14%;標普500期貨 6846.25 +16.75 0.25%;那斯達克100期貨 25176.25 +47.00 0.19%
資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年1月21日美東時間上午5:43:51

📈 全天追蹤我們的即時財經報導。

亞馬遜正在芝加哥郊外開設一家大型商店,其規模之大,幾乎可容納近兩座一般大小的Target門市。馬斯克正加緊腳步,計劃今年讓SpaceX上市。以下是原因。全新的Netflix尚未問世,但舊有的Netflix表現依然不錯。不過,以Netflix想要達成的目標來看,「不錯」還遠遠不夠,丹·加拉格說。

搶先看

3

川普的格陵蘭策略沿用了他慣用的一套打法。

數月來,歐洲領袖對總統想要取得格陵蘭的意圖,一直以一句簡單的話回應:格陵蘭不賣。如今,在川普威脅要以嚴厲關稅重創歐洲經濟後,這些同樣的領袖們正急於安排與他會面,討論這塊領土的未來。這一轉變正是川普慣用策略奏效的結果:提出大膽要求,威脅若對方不從就將施加經濟或軍事後果——然後靜待對手屈服,梅麗迪絲·麥格勞與娜塔莉·安德魯斯(Natalie Andrews)報導。

隨著格陵蘭議題引發的緊張局勢不斷升高,這正加速推動世界擺脫以美國為中心的全球經濟格局,因為川普的強硬政策正迫使各國尋求新的貿易聯盟,並將投資轉往他處。

4

中國電動車正超越特斯拉與關稅壁壘,邁向全球稱霸之路。

不久前,幾乎沒有人相信像比亞迪這樣的中國電動車製造商能夠迷倒歐洲消費者。然而如今,該公司正領軍一批中國車廠,其全球出口攻勢已超越了最樂觀的預期。已取代特斯拉成為全球最大電動車銷售商的比亞迪,2025年在中國以外地區交付超過100萬輛汽車,較前一年成長逾一倍,史蒂芬·威爾莫(Stephen Wilmot)與聖地牙哥·佩雷斯報導。

搶先看見未來——就在今天。
訂閱《The Future of Everything》通訊,了解創新與科技如何改變我們的生活、工作與娛樂方式。

專家解讀

5

問:川普為何想要格陵蘭?

記者喬治·坎切夫(Georgi Kantchev)解釋總統為何加倍下注,持續推動取得這座島嶼的行動:

答:在格陵蘭,川普看上的是一座廣袤、冰雪覆蓋、人口稀少,卻在北極邊緣佔有戰略要位的島嶼。

這裡蘊藏豐富的稀土、石油與天然氣礦藏,而其扼守重要貿易與軍事航道要衝的位置,也使其成為多個對手大國角力的焦點。

近年來,俄羅斯與中國一直在加強在該地區的活動,川普也表示,格陵蘭對他推動「金穹頂」(Golden Dome)飛彈防禦計畫的構想至關重要。

他的野心也與其確立美國在西半球霸權地位的意圖相契合,這一構想被稱為「唐羅主義」。控制格陵蘭與更廣泛的北極地區,對於展示國力、監控對手動向以及確保航運路線安全都極具價值。

但開採這些礦藏並不容易。在當地營運的礦業公司,必須應付高昂成本、基礎設施匱乏以及惡劣氣候等挑戰。

閱讀全文

6

這座蓬勃發展的山城,擁有蒙大拿州最昂貴的房地產。

照片:ALYSSA FREESE FOR WSJ

在蒙大拿州西南部、鄰近黃石國家公園的地方,有一座名為大天空(Big Sky)的山城社區,自1973年一處偏遠滑雪場開幕以來逐漸發展起來。隨著時間推移,大天空已從零星的住宅與商店,發展成一座真正的城鎮,並成為富豪買家購置滑雪別墅的熱門目的地。截至2025年12月,當地房屋掛牌中位價為305萬美元。儘管發展迅速,這個社區依然保留著純正的蒙大拿風情:盛裝打扮在這裡依然意味著穿上牛仔靴、牛仔褲,或許再戴頂牛仔帽。

今日焦點

7

最高法院將就聯準會理事麗莎·庫克(Lisa Cook)控告川普一案聽取口頭辯論,川普正試圖以涉嫌房貸詐欺為由將她解僱。財報:嬌生、嘉信理財。📰 今日報紙。

數字看世界

8

100美元

自1889年選民將此規定寫入州憲法以來,新罕布夏州議員每年領取的薪資金額。「花崗岩州」的議員是全美薪資最低的州議員;其他多數州的同僚薪資約為4.79萬美元。過去多次試圖修憲提高新罕布夏州議員薪資的努力都以失敗告終。如今,一項跨黨派的推動行動正試圖將這項薪資條款從這份根本大法中刪除。

最後,還有這則

9

認識這些整整一個月不買任何東西的美國人。

今年一月,有些人不只戒酒,還乾脆完全不買任何東西。在社群媒體的推波助瀾下,部分消費者以「新年新願望:整個月不買任何非必需品」作為新年的開始。這類節儉挑戰的人氣持續攀升。Google對「一月不買」(No Buy January)的搜尋量在12月創下五年新高,主要由Z世代與千禧世代帶動。

新聞編輯室之外

10

社論:最高法院今天將審理川普是否有權解僱聯準會理事麗莎·庫克一案。這攸關總統權力與央行獨立性的重大利害關係。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Trump Doubles Down on Greenland
emails.contentEn:
✏️ Good morning from Davos. I’ll be here all week for the World Economic Forum. Later today, I’m interviewing Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on the company’s $10 billion raise and his stark timeline for AI-driven employment disruption. I’ll also be putting your submitted questions to him—thank you for the input. You can watch our conversation at 11 a.m. ET here . In the meantime, we’ve got live coverage on the rising tensions between the U.S. and its European allies , the latest reporting on the protests in Iran , and more.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

President Trump fired off a series of social-media posts stressing his desire to acquire Greenland, and said he had agreed to hold a meeting in Davos about his plans for the island. Trump’s pursuit of Greenland has become a focus of his second presidential term. Here’s why he set his sights on the territory . The Supreme Court will hear arguments Wednesday over whether Trump can fire Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook —a case that will test the central bank’s independence and the court’s stance on regulatory power. In a firsthand account provided to the WSJ, an Iranian businessman describes a multiday crackdown in Tehran that human-rights activists say killed thousands. Indiana capped a perfect 16-0 season by defeating Miami 27-21 on Monday night to win its first national championship.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

Chevron lobbied hard for proximity to oil wealth in Venezuela, but the company has little appetite for making major investments there in the near term. Conflicting interests are making it hard for policymakers to give young Americans a leg up in a brutal housing market , writes Carol Ryan.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Goldman Sachs grapples with its top lawyer’s Epstein problem.

When Kathryn Ruemmler, a top Washington lawyer with an elite pedigree, joined Goldman Sachs in 2020, she disclosed to top executives a connection that didn’t appear on her LinkedIn page: Jeffrey Epstein. But it’s what Goldman didn’t know about her association with the notorious sex offender—details that have become public in the stream of documents released from Epstein’s estate—that now looms over Ruemmler and the bank. The extent of their relationship has drawn scrutiny inside Goldman, where the lawyer is general counsel and a top adviser to CEO David Solomon, reports AnnaMaria Andriotis.

4

Europe contends with a big new threat: the U.S.

The collapse of trust in the U.S. over the past year among the European public and its leaders is forcing the continent to re-examine its reliance —from security to trade—on America under an unpredictable Trump administration that has expressed an antipathy toward Europe and is now insisting on taking an ally’s territory. Even if a compromise is found on Greenland, a sense is spreading in Europe that the historically unique friendship known as the West will never be the same again, report Marcus Walker and David Luhnow.

Sign up for WSJ’s Sports newsletter.

Every week, get a curated tour of our unique take on the sports world.

 EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: What would a break with Europe mean for the American economy?

Europe is the U.S.’s biggest trading partner, largest investor and closest financial ally. If a trade war breaks out, the U.S. economy could feel the pain , write Konrad Putzier, Chao Deng and Sam Goldfarb.

A: Trump’s bid to annex Greenland and unleash tariffs on several European countries has plunged the trans-Atlantic alliance into crisis.

European leaders are considering the bloc’s options to retaliate, including imposing tariffs on more than $100 billion of American goods, and making it harder for American multinationals to bid on European contracts.

Economists say tit-for-tat tariffs probably won’t cause a recession in the U.S. but could slow growth, hit an already sluggish domestic manufacturing sector and push up prices for consumers and businesses when the U.S. is already struggling to get inflation back to comfortable levels.

In the long run, worsening ties could lead Europe to lessen its dependence on the U.S. and deepen trade ties elsewhere, weakening a relationship that has been a driver of prosperity on both sides of the Atlantic.

A trade war isn’t the only economic risk. Some analysts warn that Trump’s threats against Europe could also cause European investors to pare back investments in U.S. stocks and bonds, leading to a weaker dollar, declines in American stocks and higher U.S. borrowing costs.

SEE THE STORY

6

6,000 Truth Social posts later, here are the promises Trump kept—and broke.

PHOTO ILLUSTRATION: WSJ

Trump’s Truth Social account has published more than 6,000 posts since the president took office a year ago, according to a WSJ review of its online activity . More than half the time, the account simply linked to news articles, shared images or videos, or reshared previous posts by others or the president himself. But of the rest—the more than 2,700 primarily text-based postings that chronicled the president’s thinking—hundreds amounted to clear promises to enact change. Here’s a scorecard of whether the president followed through on some of the most notable directives he made using his social-media megaphone.

HAPPENING TODAY

AND FINALLY...

9

Hotels are getting rid of proper bathroom doors and guests are revolting.

First they came for the closets. Then they took the bath tubs. Now, hotels are stripping away the only thing separating us from the animals: the bathroom door. Guests are waving goodbye to the luxury of a fully closable opaque barrier between the restroom and bedroom, checking in to find sliding barn doors, curtains, strategically placed walls and other replacements that aren’t as proficient in the art of noise and smell containment. In some cases, they’re not even good at hiding the view .

✏️ 早安,我目前人在達沃斯,整週都會在此參加世界經濟論壇。今天稍晚,我將訪問Anthropic執行長達里奧·阿莫迪,談論該公司100億美元的融資案,以及他對AI衝擊就業市場提出的嚴峻時間表。我也會將讀者提交的問題轉達給他——感謝大家的提問。你可以在美東時間上午11點於此收看我們的對談。與此同時,我們也持續提供關於美國與歐洲盟友緊張關係升高的即時報導、伊朗抗議活動的最新報導等內容。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1

川普總統連發多則社群貼文,強調他想要取得格陵蘭的意願,並表示他已同意在達沃斯就其對該島的計畫舉行會談。川普對格陵蘭的追求已成為他第二任期的焦點之一。以下是他看上這塊領土的原因。最高法院將於週三就川普是否有權解僱聯準會理事麗莎·庫克一案聽取辯論——此案將考驗央行的獨立性,以及最高法院對監管權力的立場。在向本報提供的第一手描述中,一名伊朗商人講述了德黑蘭一場持續數日的鎮壓行動,人權運動人士表示已造成數千人死亡。印第安納大學以完美的16勝0敗戰績,在週一晚間以27比21擊敗邁阿密大學,奪得隊史首座全國冠軍。

市場即時動態

2

雪佛龍曾大力遊說爭取接近委內瑞拉石油財富的機會,但該公司短期內對在當地進行重大投資興趣不高。相互衝突的利益,讓政策制定者難以在嚴峻的房市中助年輕美國人一臂之力,卡蘿·萊恩撰文分析。

搶先看

3

高盛正應付其首席法律顧問的艾普斯坦難題。

當出身顯赫、來自華府的頂尖律師凱瑟琳·魯姆勒(Kathryn Ruemmler)於2020年加入高盛時,她向高層主管揭露了一項未出現在她LinkedIn頁面上的關係:與傑佛瑞·艾普斯坦的往來。但如今真正籠罩魯姆勒與高盛的,是高盛當初並不知情的、她與這名惡名昭彰性犯罪者之間關係的細節——這些細節已隨著艾普斯坦遺產陸續公開的文件而曝光。這段關係的深淺程度已在高盛內部引發審視,魯姆勒目前是該行總法律顧問,也是執行長大衛·所羅門(David Solomon)的頂尖顧問,安娜瑪麗亞·安德里奧提斯(AnnaMaria Andriotis)報導。

4

歐洲正面對一項嶄新的重大威脅:美國。

過去一年來,歐洲民眾與其領袖對美國信任的崩解,正迫使這塊大陸重新審視其在安全乃至貿易上對美國的依賴——這是在一個對歐洲表現出敵意、如今更堅持奪取盟友領土的、難以預測的川普政府治下發生的。即便格陵蘭問題最終找到妥協方案,一種氛圍正在歐洲蔓延:那段被稱為「西方」的、歷史上獨一無二的友誼,恐怕再也回不去了,馬庫斯·沃克與大衛·魯諾報導。

訂閱《華爾街日報》體育通訊。
每週為你精選我們對體育世界的獨特觀點。

專家解讀

5

問:與歐洲決裂對美國經濟意味著什麼?

歐洲是美國最大的貿易夥伴、最大的投資者,也是最緊密的金融盟友。若爆發貿易戰,美國經濟恐將承受痛苦,康拉德·普齊爾(Konrad Putzier)、鄧超(Chao Deng)與山姆·戈德法布(Sam Goldfarb)報導。

答:川普企圖吞併格陵蘭並對多個歐洲國家發動關稅攻勢,已讓跨大西洋聯盟陷入危機。

歐洲領袖正考慮歐盟的反制選項,包括對逾1000億美元的美國商品加徵關稅,以及讓美國跨國企業更難競標歐洲的合約。

經濟學家表示,以牙還牙的關稅可能不至於讓美國陷入衰退,但可能拖累成長、衝擊本已疲軟的國內製造業,並在美國本已難以將通膨壓回舒適水準之際,推高消費者與企業的物價負擔。

長期而言,惡化的關係可能促使歐洲降低對美依賴,並深化與其他地區的貿易關係,削弱這段一直是跨大西洋兩岸繁榮驅動力的關係。

貿易戰並非唯一的經濟風險。部分分析師警告,川普對歐洲的威脅也可能導致歐洲投資人削減對美股與美債的投資,進而導致美元走弱、美股下跌,以及美國舉債成本上升。

閱讀全文

6

發布超過6000則Truth Social貼文後,來看看川普履行了哪些承諾——又打破了哪些。

照片合成:WSJ

根據本報對川普Truth Social帳號活動的檢視,自總統一年前上任以來,該帳號已發布超過6000則貼文。半數以上的貼文只是單純轉貼新聞連結、分享圖片或影片,或是轉發他人或總統本人先前的貼文。但在其餘、超過2700則以文字為主、記錄總統想法的貼文中,有數百則等同於明確承諾要推動改變。以下是一份成績單,檢視總統利用其社群媒體擴音器發表的一些最引人矚目的指示,是否真正兌現。

今日焦點

7

本報總編輯艾瑪·塔克將在達沃斯世界經濟論壇期間、於《華爾街日報》「Journal House」與Anthropic執行長達里奧·阿莫迪對談。美東時間上午11點於此收看直播。財報:Netflix、聯合航空、美國合眾銀行。📰 今日報紙。

數字看世界

8

1,699美元

沃爾瑪一台Delonghi義式咖啡機的售價——而沃爾瑪傳統上是平價好物的大本營。這款產品只是這家零售商為吸引更多高收入消費者、改善利潤率,並更有力地與亞馬遜競爭,而在貨架上添加的高檔、更時尚居家用品之一例。

最後,還有這則

9

飯店正在拆除真正的浴室門,顧客憤而抗議。

先是衣櫃遭殃,接著是浴缸被拿掉。如今,飯店正在拆除唯一將我們與野獸區隔開來的東西:浴室門。顧客們正揮別浴室與臥室之間那道能完全緊閉的不透光屏障的奢侈享受,入住後才發現迎接他們的是穀倉式滑門、簾幕、刻意設置的隔牆,以及其他在隔絕聲音與氣味方面遠不如傳統門扇的替代品。在某些情況下,這些設計甚至連遮擋視線都做不到。

新聞編輯室之外

10

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Shifting Views on Trumponomics
emails.contentEn:
✏️ What to make of Trumponomics? In April, “Liberation Day” tariffs spooked analysts. Today it’s more of a mixed bag. Though economists are boosting their previously gloomy forecasts , uncertainty persists. President Trump’s challenge to Fed independence, for example, is threatening the dollar’s dominance —just as Beijing pushes the yuan. Speaking of economics, I'm heading to Davos this week for the World Economic Forum, where I'll interview the CEOs of Anthropic and Goldman Sachs at WSJ ’s Journal House . Have a question for them? Share it by replying to this email. Also, the 10-Point won’t publish tomorrow on Martin Luther King Jr. Day. We’ll be back Tuesday.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Trump said he'd impose 10% tariffs on imports from several European countries in a bid to pressure Denmark to sell Greenland to the U.S. Only U.S.-bound tankers of crude have left Venezuela since the arrest of Nicolás Maduro, a report shows, shutting off shipments to China and Cuba . Trump said it was time for new leadership in Iran after its supreme leader called him a criminal responsible for protester deaths. TSMC’s plans for a massive expansion in Arizona reflect the new realities of the U.S.-Taiwan relationship . In San Francisco, a proposed apartment tower atop an iconic Safeway highlights tensions between California’s state and local zoning laws.

FROM THE MARKETS

2

Shrugging off their prior concerns about Trumponomics, a group of economists who are regularly surveyed by WSJ boosted their 2026 growth outlook back above 2%. Trump’s investigation into Fed Chair Jerome Powell risks damaging investor confidence in the U.S. financial system and the dollar, just as China is expanding the use of its own currency around the world.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3

This Wall Street legend ran a penthouse sex dungeon, prosecutors say.

Howard Rubin rose, fell and rose again as a star trader in the 1980s, embodying the excessive wealth and risk of a gunslinger era in finance. Now he’s been charged with luring women into what he called his sex “dungeon,” where he abused and tortured them high above the Manhattan skyline. Since being arrested for sex trafficking and other crimes in September, the 70-year-old now lives in a Brooklyn jail cell. His attorneys, allies and even his estranged wife say he’s a retiree living a quiet life. He has pleaded not guilty. Rubin’s lawyers have argued that the women were aware of what the encounters involved and were willing participants.

4

Germany’s military recruitment drive has a Gen Z problem.

European nations have stepped up military spending to prepare for a potential conflict with Russia, and the country on the front line of the rearmament effort is struggling to meet its recruitment goals, reports Bertrand Benoit. The problem isn’t pacifism, but young people posing a new variation on the age-old question: “What is in it for me?” After Germany introduced a new military service, for now on a voluntary basis, tens of thousands of school-age demonstrators took to the streets. Their objections are more about economics than politics— a big difference from the idealism of the German peace movement in the 1970s and 1980s.

Be smarter about your finances.

Sign up for The Intelligent Investor , a weekly newsletter from WSJ’s Jason Zweig on investment strategy and ways to think about money.

 CONTENT FROM: NORTHERN TRUST New Tax Rules, Global Shifts, AI Advice: Are You Ready? 

What wealth planning strategies will be most effective in the year ahead in light of recent policy? How can business owners and investors take advantage of unprecedented opportunities for tax savings? How are wealthy families navigating an increasingly international world? And how is AI rapidly evolving client advice? Find out in our annual Wealth Planning Outlook.

Download the Report 

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: Silicon Valley worries the American Dream is dying. Why?

Some in the tech world fear this is the last chance to amass generational wealth before AI makes money essentially worthless. Columnist Tim Higgins explains where this perspective comes from.

A: One of Silicon Valley’s wild-eyed ideas—long debated on subreddits and in hacker houses—is becoming a real-life nightmare.

The argument is that tech companies (and their leaders) will become a class unto their own with infinite wealth. No one else will have the means to generate money for themselves because AI will have taken their jobs and opportunities.

In other words, the bridge is about to be raised for those chasing the American dream. And everyone is worried about being left on the wrong side.

It’s the kind of FOMO that on first blush seems to require a huge suspension of disbelief. But the idea’s mere existence helps explain some of the increasing class worries in California, where a growing movement to tax billionaires is roiling the Democratic Party, affordable housing is a real concern and the idea of the middle class seems out of reach.

Yes, it smacks of sci-fi thinking. But in San Francisco it feels real. And it’s made more believable by the exploits of Elon Musk, the rise of OpenAI’s Sam Altman and warnings by Anthropic’s Dario Amodei about Great Depression-like worker displacement.

SEE THE STORY

6

This is what $25,000 a night buys on a luxury cruise line.

PHOTO: FOUR SEASONS YACHTS (RENDERING)

As the fast-growing luxury cruise segment targets well-heeled travelers, companies are racing to create more extravagant accommodations . Regent Seven Seas Cruises is launching a new ship in December that offers a two-story suite featuring a private massage room, an ocean-facing bar and a butler to unpack suitcases or deliver caviar. On the day the $25,000-a-night suite opened for reservations, it was booked for six of the first 13 voyages, according to a spokeswoman.

HAPPENING THIS WEEK

✏️ 該如何看待「川普經濟學」?4月,「解放日」關稅政策曾令分析師大為緊張。如今情況則更為複雜參半。儘管經濟學家正上調先前偏悲觀的預測,不確定性依然存在。舉例來說,川普總統對聯準會獨立性的挑戰,正威脅美元的主導地位——恰逢北京大力推動人民幣國際化之際。談到經濟議題,我這週將前往達沃斯參加世界經濟論壇,屆時我將在《華爾街日報》「Journal House」訪問Anthropic與高盛的執行長。對他們有問題想問嗎?請回覆這封郵件分享你的問題。另外,明天適逢馬丁·路德·金恩紀念日,《10-Point》將暫停發行一天,週二將照常與大家見面。

艾瑪·塔克

今日頭條

川普表示,他將對多個歐洲國家的進口商品課徵10%關稅,以此向丹麥施壓,要求其將格陵蘭賣給美國。一份報告顯示,自尼古拉斯·馬杜洛遭逮捕以來,離開委內瑞拉的原油油輪僅剩駛往美國的航線,對中國與古巴的運輸已全數中斷。伊朗最高領袖稱川普為應為抗議者死亡負責的「罪犯」後,川普表示伊朗該迎來新的領導層了。台積電在亞利桑那州大規模擴建的計畫,反映出美台關係的新現實。在舊金山,一項擬在一座地標性Safeway超市樓頂興建公寓大樓的計畫,凸顯了加州州級與地方分區法規之間的緊張關係。

檢方稱這位華爾街傳奇人物曾在頂樓公寓經營一座「性愛地牢」。

霍華德·魯賓(Howard Rubin)在1980年代作為明星交易員經歷了大起大落,又東山再起,體現了那個金融業「槍手」年代的過度財富與風險。如今他被控誘騙女性進入他所謂的「地牢」,在俯瞰曼哈頓天際線的高處對她們施以虐待與凌辱。自9月因人口販運及其他罪名遭逮捕以來,這位70歲的老人如今住在布魯克林的一間牢房裡。他的律師、盟友甚至已分居的妻子都表示,他其實是一名過著平靜生活的退休人士。他已表示不認罪。魯賓的律師辯稱,那些女性都清楚這些性愛過程涉及什麼,且是自願參與。

讓你的理財更聰明。

問:矽谷擔心美國夢正在消逝。為什麼?

科技圈部分人士擔憂,在AI讓金錢基本上變得毫無價值之前,這是累積世代財富的最後機會。專欄作家提姆·希金斯解釋這種觀點的由來。

答:矽谷一項瘋狂的構想——長期以來在Reddit論壇與駭客聚會屋中被熱議——正逐漸變成現實中的噩夢。

這種論點認為,科技公司(及其領導者)將成為擁有無窮財富的獨立階層。其他人將無力再為自己創造財富,因為AI已奪走了他們的工作與機會。

換句話說,對於那些追逐美國夢的人來說,吊橋即將被拉起。每個人都在擔心自己會被困在錯誤的一側。

這種「錯失恐懼」乍看之下似乎需要極大的懷疑暫緩才能相信。但這個構想的存在本身,恰恰有助於解釋加州日益加劇的階級焦慮——在那裡,一場向億萬富豪徵稅的運動正在民主黨內掀起波瀾,可負擔住房是一項真實的隱憂,而「中產階級」這個概念似乎已遙不可及。

沒錯,這聽起來像科幻小說式的思維。但在舊金山,這種感覺卻十分真實。而馬斯克的種種舉動、OpenAI創辦人山姆·奧特曼的崛起,以及Anthropic的達里奧·阿莫迪關於「大蕭條式」勞動力替代的警告,更讓這種說法顯得可信。
