emails.contentEn:
✏️ Donald Trump is pushing boundaries at home and abroad this month, threatening to upend governments in Latin America, take military action in Iran and seize control of Greenland. Some officials have privately nicknamed him “President of the World.” But what do Americans think about their emboldened president ? A new WSJ poll shows that most U.S. voters think he’s going too far —though members of the MAGA base remain steadfast in their support.

Emma Tucker

Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1

Senior U.S. military officials were prepared to strike Iran on Wednesday, but President Trump decided against the move after regional allies warned him that a bombing campaign might lead to a wider conflict. Trump is pushing boundaries at home and abroad as he looks to demonstrate power, cement his legacy and beat the clock ahead of midterm elections. Voters are increasingly unhappy with how Trump is handling the economy, according to a new WSJ poll, though support among loyal fans remains resilient. Joe Rogan expressed concerns about the killing of Renee Nicole Good in Minneapolis by an ICE agent, a criticism that some saw as a watershed moment . Delcy Rodríguez, a pariah during Trump’s first term, is now the U.S.’s primary partner in Venezuela, putting Trump in league with a canny politician. Minneapolis has become a tinderbox as the Trump administration’s huge immigration operation has collided with enormous pushback from residents.

FROM THE MARKETS

2

Treasury yields climbed Friday after Trump said he might want to keep Kevin Hassett —a top contender for Fed chairman—in his current job. READ IT HERE FIRST

3

Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei is running out of road.

The recent protests have posed one of the most serious threats yet to the Islamic Republic’s nearly five-decade rule. Iran can now only fix the economic problems underpinning the public anger if it gets relief from international sanctions, which would require Khamenei to compromise on Iran’s nuclear program and other deeply held beliefs, reports Sune Engel Rasmussen. Iran’s economic crisis has deepened at the worst possible time for Khamenei. Since the Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel, Iran’s allies Hezbollah and Hamas have been weakened, and Israeli and U.S. bombings last year exposed Tehran’s vulnerability.

4

The global memory-chip shortage will cost us all.

Just three companies make more than 90% of these chips, which are fast-appreciating assets: SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron. Prices for memory shot up 50% in the last quarter of 2025 and are projected to increase another 40% to 50% by the end of the first quarter of 2026, according to Counterpoint Research. As AI firms crowd out other buyers, unexpected consequences will likely reverberate across industries, writes Christopher Mims. Effects could include delayed data centers, higher prices for consumer electronics, and possible chip shortages for automakers that could trigger a repeat of the pandemic car crisis.

EXPERT TAKE

5

Q: Supersize CEO pay packages have taken off. Are they paying off for shareholders?

In recent years, companies have dangled nine-figure “moonshot” pay packages to motivate executives. WSJ’s Theo Francis wrote about what the data say about the effectiveness of this compensation strategy .

A: Promising CEOs the moon hasn’t been a great way to get out-of-this-world results.

Dozens of companies—including KKR, Rivian Automotive, Roblox and Robinhood Markets—hammered out $100-million-plus “moonshot” pay packages with their chiefs in the years after Tesla awarded billions of dollars in stock options to Elon Musk in 2018. The potential for huge payoffs was meant to spur outsize returns.

So far, few of the CEOs have managed to deliver, a new analysis has found.

Shareholder returns trailed the S&P 500 at three-quarters of the 20 companies crafting such pay packages for their chief executive officers in 2020 and 2021, at the peak of the trend. Half of the CEOs forfeited much or all of their stock awards. Four, including the private-equity firm KKR’s co-CEOs, have met all their targets for awards recently valued at a combined $2.6 billion. Where the meter is still running, CEOs have earned only about a quarter of the total, on average.

Grocery prices are among Americans’ biggest gripes, with food-at-home prices up 2.4% from a year earlier in December, an acceleration from 2024’s increase of 1.8%.

✏️ 這個月,川普正在國內外不斷試探底線,威脅要顛覆拉丁美洲的政府、對伊朗採取軍事行動,並奪取格陵蘭的控制權。一些官員私下給他取了「世界總統」的綽號。但美國人對這位日益大膽的總統有何看法?本報最新民調顯示,大多數美國選民認為他做得太過火了——儘管MAGA基本盤的支持依然堅定不移。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1

美軍高層官員原本已準備好在週三對伊朗發動打擊,但在區域盟友警告轟炸行動可能引發更廣泛衝突後,川普總統決定放棄此舉。川普正在國內外不斷試探底線,力圖展現實力、鞏固自己的政治遺產,並趕在期中選舉前爭取時間。根據本報最新民調,選民對川普處理經濟問題的方式日益不滿,儘管其忠實支持者的支持度依然堅韌。喬·羅根(Joe Rogan)對明尼阿波利斯一名ICE探員擊斃蕾妮·妮可·古德(Renee Nicole Good)一事表達了擔憂,這一批評被部分人視為一個分水嶺時刻。在川普第一任期曾被視為拒絕往來戶的德爾西·羅德里格斯(Delcy Rodríguez),如今已成為美國在委內瑞拉最主要的合作夥伴,讓川普與這位精明的政治人物結為盟友。隨著川普政府大規模移民行動與居民排山倒海的反彈相互碰撞,明尼阿波利斯已成為一觸即發的火藥桶。

市場動態

2

三大主要指數本週均以下跌作收,但一項衡量小型股表現的指標,在市場對經濟前景樂觀的帶動下創下歷史新高。週五,在川普表示他可能想讓聯準會主席熱門人選之一凱文·哈塞特留任現職後,公債殖利率上揚。川普威脅將對反對其奪取格陵蘭控制權行動的國家課徵關稅。

搶先看

3

伊朗最高領袖哈米尼(Ali Khamenei)已經走投無路。

近期的抗議活動,對這個伊斯蘭共和國近五十年的統治構成了迄今最嚴峻的威脅之一。如今伊朗唯一能解決引發民眾憤怒的經濟問題的辦法,是獲得國際制裁的鬆綁,而這將要求哈米尼在伊朗核計畫及其他根深蒂固的信念上做出妥協,蘇尼·恩格爾·拉斯穆森報導。伊朗的經濟危機正在最不利的時機加劇惡化。自2023年10月7日對以色列發動攻擊以來,伊朗的盟友真主黨與哈馬斯實力已遭削弱,以色列與美國去年的轟炸行動也暴露了德黑蘭的脆弱性。

4

全球記憶體晶片短缺將讓所有人付出代價。

僅有三家公司生產超過九成的這類晶片——這些晶片正快速增值——分別是SK海力士、三星與美光。根據Counterpoint Research的數據,記憶體價格在2025年第四季飆漲了50%,預計到2026年第一季末還將再上漲40%至50%。隨著AI企業排擠其他買家,這將對各行各業產生意想不到的連鎖反應,克里斯多福·米姆斯撰文分析。可能的影響包括數據中心建設延誤、消費電子產品漲價,以及汽車製造商可能面臨晶片短缺,進而可能重演疫情期間的汽車產業危機。

在職場上搶佔先機。
訂閱我們每週的「職涯與領導力」通訊,掌握職涯發展、商業、管理與領導力的最新資訊。

專家解讀

5

問:天價執行長薪酬方案近年來大行其道,這對股東而言真的划算嗎?

近年來,企業紛紛拋出九位數的「登月計畫」薪酬方案,以激勵高階主管。本報記者西奧·法蘭西斯(Theo Francis)撰文分析數據對這種薪酬策略成效的看法。

答:承諾執行長「摘星攬月」般的薪酬,並未真正換來同等驚人的成果。

自2018年特斯拉授予馬斯克價值數十億美元的股票選擇權後,包括KKR、Rivian汽車、Roblox與Robinhood Markets在內的數十家公司,都與其執行長敲定了超過一億美元的「登月計畫」薪酬方案。這種巨額回報的可能性,原本是為了激勵超乎尋常的業績表現。

但一項最新分析發現,迄今為止,鮮少有執行長真正兌現了承諾。

在2020與2021年——這股風潮的高峰期——為執行長設計此類薪酬方案的20家公司中,有四分之三的股東報酬表現落後於標普500指數。半數執行長已放棄其大部分或全部股票獎勵。包括私募股權公司KKR的兩位聯合執行長在內,共有四位執行長已達成全部獎勵目標,這些獎勵近期估值合計達26億美元。至於那些目標仍在計時中的方案,執行長平均只拿到了總額約四分之一的獎勵。

✏️ When authorities in Iran shut down the internet on Jan. 8, they didn’t just block the world out; they created a vacuum for an unprecedented wave of state violence . Our latest reporting reconstructs the 24 hours that followed, a period one human-rights group leader describes as a “massacre.” While President Trump said that the killing of protesters had stopped, Iranians said the bloodshed has left a tense pall over many cities.

Top U.S. oil producers have expressed hesitancy about rushing back to Venezuela, but the companies that provide them with equipment and expertise are raring to go . What happened in Iran when the internet went dark?

Tehran carried out its fierce crackdown under the cover of an internet shutdown and extensive disruption to phone services, so it is hard to judge its true scale. Human-rights groups are trying to assemble a full account of the death toll, compiling evidence that includes images of body bags and testimonies from relatives, medical workers and others. But eyewitness accounts of localized violence and estimates by rights groups and intelligence services point to bloodshed that far exceeds the toll in previous bouts of protests, whatever the final tally of the dead may be, report Benoit Faucon and Margherita Stancati.

4

The Powell investigation threatens to upend the final stretch of the Fed chair contest.

The criminal probe into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell is creating new obstacles on Capitol Hill and raising hard questions about whether any nominee Trump chooses to replace him can be seen as independent—tension that was always present but is now much harder to ignore. Trump has made clear he prizes loyalty in his pick, but the Justice Department investigation—which Powell said was part of a campaign to get the Fed to lower interest rates—threatens to make that quality a liability. The backlash on Capitol Hill could force Trump’s pick to walk a tightrope in any confirmation process this spring, report Nick Timiraos, Siobhan Hughes and Josh Dawsey.

Q: Gen X and Millennials will inherit trillions in real estate over the next decade. What will be the ripple effects of the great wealth transfer?

Baby boomers and older Americans have spent decades amassing one of the largest concentrations of private wealth in history. Now, it is starting to be passed down. Katherine Clarke writes about the changes it’s bringing to the high-end property market:

A: Over the next decade, roughly 1.2 million individuals with net worths of $5 million or more are projected to pass down more than $38 trillion globally, according to a new report from brokerage Coldwell Banker Global Luxury reviewed exclusively by WSJ.

Real estate is poised to play a significant role in the great wealth transfer. Gen Xers and Millennials are set to inherit $4.6 trillion in global real estate over the next 10 years, according to the report. Nearly $2.4 trillion of that property is located in the U.S.

Real-estate brokers, attorneys and family offices say they are already seeing profound changes in who buys luxury homes and how purchases are structured. High-net-worth families are bringing children into conversations about inheritance earlier and making high-stakes real-estate decisions sooner.

At the high end of the market, agents say more parents aren’t waiting for kids to inherit their wealth; they are buying them luxury properties sooner. It’s reshaping the definition of luxury real estate, as more sellers cater to the tastes and preferences of a younger generation of buyers.

Some heirs are discovering that legacy properties are more than they want to take on. Large estates requiring significant maintenance and full-time staff are increasingly coming to market, brokers say.

Many among the younger generations prefer more contemporary living arrangements or more liquid assets. Higher home prices and higher mortgage rates have also made it impractical for some heirs to buy out their siblings.

許多年輕世代更偏好更現代化的居住安排,或是流動性更高的資產。房價與房貸利率雙雙走高,也讓部分繼承人買下兄弟姊妹持份的做法變得不切實際。

Q: Could a jump to the trades be the way out of a white-collar career slump?

Layoffs and stagnant wages have a lot of white-collar workers feeling stuck. Meanwhile, blue-collar industries face a labor shortage. Columnist Callum Borchers explains why it could be time for struggling workers to think about switching to something more hands-on.

A: Pivoting to an industry outside traditional white-collar havens is an option many professionals don’t consider. That’s even though the jobs are generally less vulnerable to artificial intelligence, the earning potential is often comparable, and the work-life balance is frequently better.

Of course, it takes years to master a trade and make good money at it. Starting in your 30s or 40s leaves a short window before your back and knees give out.

But in a blue-collar job market being reshaped by technology and private equity, there are faster routes to six-figure paychecks than learning a skilled trade—ones that are easier on the joints, too.

For example: Crash Champions, a car-repair chain in 38 states, is hungry for service advisers. The role involves assessing damage, estimating the cost to fix it and overseeing the process. You don’t need to sweat under the hood; you just need to know a lot about cars.

The starting salary is roughly $60,000, but service advisers can double their salaries in 18 months, says Chief Executive Matt Ebert.

After shelling out for college and amassing years of experience, it is natural to fixate on jobs in your one field to justify those investments. Career changes are never easy, but this is no time to let status and labels get in the way of the right long-term move.

✏️ 傑米·戴蒙,美國最有權勢的執行長之一,數月來一直在小心翼翼地走鋼索,設法維持與川普總統的良好關係。在公開場合,這位摩根大通執行長支持川普大部分的議程,把較尖銳的批評留給與總統的私下對話。但這種默契在圍繞聯準會主席鮑爾的爭鬥中,或許已經觸及極限。我們帶你深入了解白宮與這位華爾街最老練外交家之間日益擴大的裂痕。

《華爾街日報》總編輯

美國在加勒比海的軍力集結——這是針對委內瑞拉如今已遭推翻領導人的施壓行動的一部分——限制了川普在與伊朗爆發衝突時的選項。川普表示,伊朗已停止殺害反政權抗議者,也不會處決那些被控試圖推翻政府的人。在尼古拉斯·馬杜洛遭撤除後,根基深厚的委內瑞拉領導層對美國的語氣已趨於軟化,同時在國內仍維持反帝國主義的言論基調。將薩克斯第五大道(Saks Fifth Avenue)與尼曼馬庫斯(Neiman Marcus)合併,原本應打造出一個奢侈品巨頭。但短短一年多後,未償還債務就導致其申請破產。

傑米·戴蒙原本似乎已摸透川普——直到這一週。

在造訪白宮後,丹麥與格陵蘭高層官員表示,他們並未能說服川普放棄吞併這塊領土的野心。

問:轉行從事技術工種,能否成為擺脫白領職涯困境的出路?

裁員與薪資停滯讓許多白領工作者感覺被困住了。與此同時,藍領產業卻面臨勞動力短缺。專欄作家卡勒姆·博切斯解釋,為何陷入困境的勞工或許該考慮轉向更需要動手實作的工作。

答:轉行到傳統白領職業以外的產業,是許多專業人士從未考慮過的選項。儘管這類工作通常較不易受人工智慧衝擊,收入潛力往往也相當可觀,工作與生活的平衡更常常更好。

當然,要精通一項技術工種並靠此賺得高薪,需要花上多年時間。若從三、四十歲才開始,留給你的時間窗口相當有限,畢竟腰背與膝蓋撐不了太久。

但在一個正被科技與私募股權重塑的藍領就業市場中,其實有比學習一項技術工種更快速通往六位數薪資的途徑——而且對關節也更友善。

舉例來說:在38個州擁有據點的汽車維修連鎖店Crash Champions,正急需服務顧問。這項工作內容包括評估車損、估算維修費用並監督整個維修流程。你不需要親自鑽到引擎蓋下揮汗如雨,只需要對汽車知識瞭若指掌。

起薪約為6萬美元,但執行長麥特·艾伯特(Matt Ebert)表示,服務顧問的薪資可在18個月內翻倍。

在花錢念完大學、累積多年經驗之後,人往往很自然地會執著於留在自己的專業領域內找工作,好證明這些投入是值得的。轉換職涯從來都不容易,但現在不是讓身分地位與職稱標籤,阻礙你做出正確長期職涯選擇的時候。

關於委內瑞拉,他們該知道的一切都是從《傑克·萊恩》學來的。

Q: What would a 10% credit-card rate cap mean for your wallet?

Trump’s call for a temporary 10% cap on credit-card interest rates promises to save Americans billions in interest but also could lead to tightened access to credit. Reporter Veronica Dagher explains what a cap might mean for your money :

A: The president didn’t offer any details on how the one-year cap would be enacted but said he wanted it to begin on Jan. 20.

Credit-card issuers are already pushing back, saying it will only hurt the people it is intended to help.

Credit-card interest rates average around 23% and haven’t been below 10% in data going back to 1994. People with lower credit scores can pay rates of up to 36%.

A 10% cap could save American households roughly $100 billion a year in interest payments, according to Vanderbilt University. That could translate to meaningful savings for Americans.

Trump didn’t say whether his cap would apply to new or existing balances. Other rate-cap proposals have focused more on new balances.

The card industry warns that many people, especially those with lower incomes and lower credit scores, would lose access to credit cards. One industry estimate said close to 90% of cardholders could lose access to credit, either through account closures or reduced credit lines.

Credit-card lending would become a lot less profitable, and issuers would likely make their rewards programs a lot less generous. Cards issuers could also introduce new annual fees or increase existing ones.

It isn’t clear how Trump would enforce a cap. Most legal experts say that the president can’t unilaterally cap interest rates by executive order and that such a cap would require an act of Congress.

✏️ 伊朗即將分崩離析的最大徵兆,並非來自該國反對派受挫的怒火,也不是年輕人破滅的希望,而是來自一場銀行倒閉事件。Ayandeh銀行的倒閉,暴露了一個因裙帶關係而被掏空的金融體系,以及一種正急速貶值的貨幣。隨著川普總統釋出「援助即將到來」的訊號給正在抗議的伊朗民眾,我們解析這場起義背後的經濟危機,以及美國可能採取的干預方式會是什麼樣子。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

今日頭條

1

今天,川普政府將宣布美國正推進其加薩計畫的下一步,並任命一個巴勒斯坦人委員會暫時管理這塊飛地。薩克斯環球(Saks Global)申請破產,距離薩克斯第五大道與尼曼馬庫斯合併、原本應打造出一個奢侈品巨頭的交易,還不到一年時間。一份司法部備忘錄聲稱,由瑪麗亞·科琳娜·馬查多領導的委內瑞拉反對派對美國推翻尼古拉斯·馬杜洛行動的支持,有助於川普推翻他的法律論證。川普上週在白宮一場活動中批評一群美國檢察官,稱他們軟弱,並抱怨他們在起訴他鎖定的目標時動作不夠迅速。聯邦住房金融局局長比爾·普爾特(Bill Pulte)告訴本報,建商在降低住房成本方面做得不夠,並暗示對未配合政府推動政策的公司將施以懲罰。

川普正採取前所未見的手段讓經濟保持過熱運轉,而他極有可能會成功,葛雷格·伊普撰文分析。在一週內接連祭出一系列快速行動、殺華爾街一個措手不及後,川普似乎正在對華爾街發出警告。去年秋天汽車零件供應商First Brands的倒閉,讓金融工程手法再度受到嚴格審視,強納森·魏爾撰文分析。

一家名不見經傳的銀行倒閉,讓伊朗陷入了螺旋式下墜。

去年年底,由政權親信經營、背負近50億美元壞帳損失的Ayandeh銀行倒閉了。這場危機正好發生在最糟糕的時機。伊朗政府的公信力,早已因6月與以色列及美國之間為期12天的戰爭而受創,那場戰爭顯示出伊朗政府無力保護民眾免受攻擊。這家銀行的倒閉,既成為經濟崩解的象徵,也加速了這場經濟崩解,並引爆了如今對這個伊斯蘭共和國構成半世紀建國以來最重大威脅的抗議活動,賈瑞德·馬爾辛(Jared Malsin)報導。

4

美國已粉碎了中國在拉丁美洲的野心。

尼古拉斯·馬杜洛遭撤除,正迫使北京對其野心進行一場高風險的重新盤算。多年來,中國不斷打入拉丁美洲,以興建道路、港口與鐵路的貸款誘使各國放棄對台灣的支持,大舉採購大宗商品,並開採銅等關鍵金屬。委內瑞拉這位強人領袖曾是中國最重要的盟友——一位坐擁石油資源的反美領導人。如今,北京短期內已不再尋求在該地區取得新的進展,魏玲靈報導。

深入了解美中關係。
訂閱《華爾街日報》中國通訊,每週由本報首席中國特派記者為您帶來獨家見解。

專家解讀

5

問:信用卡利率若被限制在10%上限,對你的荷包意味著什麼?

川普呼籲暫時將信用卡利率上限設在10%,承諾能為美國人省下數十億美元的利息支出,但也可能導致信貸取得管道收緊。記者維若妮卡·達格爾(Veronica Dagher)解釋利率上限可能對你的財務帶來什麼影響:

答:總統並未說明這項為期一年的上限將如何實施,但表示他希望於1月20日開始生效。

信用卡發卡機構已表態反對,稱此舉只會傷害它原本想幫助的對象。

信用卡利率平均約為23%,自1994年有數據紀錄以來從未低於10%。信用評分較低者支付的利率甚至可能高達36%。

根據范德堡大學的研究,10%的利率上限每年可為美國家庭省下約1000億美元的利息支出。這對美國人而言可能意味著相當可觀的實質節省。

川普並未說明這項上限是否適用於新產生的欠款,還是也涵蓋既有欠款。過去其他利率上限提案大多只針對新產生的欠款。

信用卡業界警告,許多人——尤其是低收入與低信用評分族群——可能會因此失去信用卡使用資格。業界一項估計指出,近九成持卡人可能因帳戶遭關閉或信用額度遭縮減,而失去信用卡的使用權。

信用卡放款業務的獲利將大幅縮水,發卡機構很可能會大幅縮減其回饋方案的優惠程度。發卡機構也可能推出新的年費,或提高現有年費。

目前尚不清楚川普將如何落實這項上限。多數法律專家表示,總統無法僅憑行政命令單方面設定利率上限,此類上限須經國會立法才能實現。

閱讀全文

6

在「讓美國再度健康」(MAHA)與Ozempic的時代,雜貨貨架正在改變。

插畫:EMMA BROWN

「讓美國再度健康」。Ozempic。「瘋狂補纖」(Fibermaxxing)。強大的力量正推動美國食品業對超市貨架進行數十年來規模最大的一次全面改造。隨著外界對美國人飲食狀況的擔憂不斷升高,各城市、州政府乃至聯邦政府都在嚴格審視加工食品的成分。對許多消費者而言,蛋白質與全脂牛奶正在回歸,而種籽油則被打入冷宮。

今日焦點

7

最高法院可能就多起重大案件做出裁決,包括川普全球關稅政策的合法性。經濟數據:11月生產者物價指數;11月零售銷售、12月成屋銷售。財報:美國銀行、富國銀行、花旗集團。📰 今日報紙。

數字看世界

8

超過700美元

來自Ernest Wright、深受裁縫師喜愛的一把高階手工訂製剪刀的售價。這家擁有124年歷史的公司與其競爭對手Whiteley——兩者僅相距8英里,均位於英格蘭雪菲爾——是這座曾擁有數十家剪刀製造商的城市中,僅存的兩家傳承悠久的剪刀廠。這兩家工坊目前都面臨困境,使其備受推崇的剪刀產業命懸一線。

最後,還有這則

9

馬修·麥康納正為自己申請商標,以對抗AI濫用。

這位奧斯卡影帝已獲美國專利商標局核准八項商標申請,內容涵蓋他凝視、微笑與說話的畫面。他的律師表示,這些商標旨在阻止AI應用程式或使用者未經許可模擬麥康納的聲音或肖像——這是表演者日益普遍的擔憂。這些商標包括一段麥康納站在門廊上的片段,以及他說出「好的,好的,好的」(Alright, alright, alright)的音訊。

新聞編輯室之外

10

社論:川普一再告訴美國人,他們從未過得這麼好,但勞工部最新數據顯示,實質工資的成長速度,根本追不上仍在上漲的物價。

emails.subject: The 10-Point: Trump Allies Fear Blowback from Powell Probe
emails.contentEn:
The fallout from the Justice Department's probe into Jerome Powell is already rippling through Washington, D.C., and Wall Street. Some Trump administration officials and allies have expressed concern that the investigation could imperil the president's nominees in the Senate and rattle financial markets. One Trump adviser described the immediate blowback as a "huge cluster." We take you inside the clash and explain what it could mean for the future of the Fed and the economy.

Emma Tucker
Editor in Chief, The Wall Street Journal

TODAY'S HEADLINES

1. The federal immigration crackdown in Minnesota has descended on the stores and parking lots of Target, putting the hometown retailer in a tough political spot. Minnesota has filed a lawsuit against U.S. immigration officials, seeking to end what the state called an unlawful surge of federal agents. Trump has privately ramped up criticism of Pam Bondi, describing her as weak and ineffective. Iranians are turning to Elon Musk's Starlink to bypass internet blackouts and share videos of protests, even as the regime intensifies efforts to jam it. Panama's supreme court is winding up deliberations that will decide whether a Hong Kong company can run two ports at either end of the Panama Canal. New York is preparing to loosen its environmental law to make it faster and cheaper to build housing in the state.

LIVE FROM THE MARKETS

2. DJIA Futures 49733.00 -76.00 (0.15%); S&P 500 Futures 7004.50 -12.00 (0.17%); Nasdaq 100 Futures 25880.50 -76.25 (0.29%). Source: Factset, Market data as of 1/13/2026, 6:00:48 AM ET.

Trump is pitching proposals to lower costs and boost spending power that could bring big changes to housing markets, the oil industry and finance. After more than two years of negotiations, one of the biggest credit-card deals of all time will see Goldman replaced by JPMorgan on the Apple credit card. Hospital stocks have outperformed insurers in recent years. That may not last, writes David Wainer.

READ IT HERE FIRST

3. Trump allies and officials fear blowback from the Powell probe.
Several Senate Republicans have expressed concern with the Justice Department's criminal investigation into Powell, including Senate Majority Leader John Thune, who said he hoped the dispute was resolved quickly. Others worried that the fight would rattle markets and boost borrowing costs. Some aides in the White House were concerned about the market reaction to the probe, according to administration officials, one of whom said the White House wasn't made aware of the investigation in advance. One administration official who lobbied for a probe was Bill Pulte, head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, report Brian Schwartz, Meridith McGraw, Josh Dawsey and Nick Timiraos.

4. America's biggest power-grid operator has an AI problem.
America's artificial intelligence boom is pushing the nation's largest power-grid operator to the brink of a supply crisis. Sixty-seven million people get their power from a market operated by nonprofit PJM. So, too, do the many AI data centers springing up in Northern Virginia's "Data Center Alley," which have a bottomless appetite for electricity. Rates are going up for consumers and the grid's capacity is in danger of maxing out during periods of high demand, report Katherine Blunt and Jennifer Hiller.

EXPERT TAKE

5. Q: What is the investigation into Powell about and why does it matter?
The Justice Department's probe represents an escalation of an unprecedented White House campaign to shape what happens at the central bank. Reporter Matt Grossman explains what you need to know about the conflict and what it could mean for the Fed's future.
A: The investigation is centered on testimony Powell gave to Congress last summer, when he defended the Fed's efforts to renovate its headquarters in Washington. Trump and his allies have seized on the project's duration and expense to argue Powell has managed the central bank poorly.
Powell said Sunday that Trump's fixation on the construction project is only a pretext for gaining leverage in a deeper conflict: Trump's demands, going back years, that Powell more aggressively slash interest rates.
Fed independence is a highly sensitive issue for financial markets, where investors rely on the Fed to make policy based on economic reality, not the president's political preferences.
Investors worry that presidents would often favor cutting rates too aggressively, prioritizing a booming economy over keeping inflation low.
On Monday, markets didn't move dramatically. Yet gold prices rallied and the dollar depreciated against foreign currencies, moves that could signal jitters about the U.S. policy landscape.
Powell's term as Fed chair ends in May, but his term as an ordinary Fed governor extends until 2028. Powell hasn't said whether he will stay on.

6. In Midland, Texas, the last thing anyone wants is cheap Venezuelan oil.
For most Americans, cheap oil is good news. In Midland, Texas, it is a problem. Oil prices have mostly slumped since last spring, and the U.S. intervention in oil-rich Venezuela is stoking Trump's desire to push prices down further. This raises a new risk for Midland, where a host of businesses linked to the oil field are feeling squeezed.

HAPPENING TODAY

7. Trump is set to meet aides to discuss responses to protests in Iran that could include military action. Economic data: Consumer-price index for December; U.S. budget deficit. Earnings: JPMorgan, Delta Air Lines, Bank of New York Mellon.

THE NUMBER

8. $1.7 trillion — The total U.S. student loan debt, a record high, prompting the Trump administration to tighten the spigot on federal loans. New rules effective July 2026 will cap total graduate school borrowing at $100,000, or $200,000 for professional degrees. Parents borrowing on behalf of their children will also see caps.

AND FINALLY...

9. A custody battle over dogs is rocking an African nation.
It's no secret who let the presidential guard dogs out, but the question roiling Malawi is more existential: Are the animals pets or policemen? The former president and his successor are fighting over the answer—and who gets to keep the dogs.

BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

10. Opinion: DOJ's subpoena to Powell is self-defeating folly. Picking a fight with the Fed—and the bond market—over an issue that voters will find confusing and irrelevant is lawfare for dummies.
WSJ | Buy Side: We found the best pet insurance companies to safeguard your wallet from high pet medical bills.
emails.contentZh:
司法部對聯準會主席鮑爾(Jerome Powell)展開調查所引發的後座力,已在華盛頓與華爾街掀起陣陣漣漪。部分川普政府官員與盟友已表達憂慮,擔心這項調查可能危及總統在參議院的人事提名,並震撼金融市場。一位川普顧問將這波立即反彈形容為「一大團亂麻」。本文帶你深入這場衝突,解析其對聯準會與整體經濟未來可能造成的影響。

艾瑪·塔克
《華爾街日報》總編輯

【今日頭條】

1. 明尼蘇達州的聯邦移民執法行動已延燒至Target的門市與停車場,使這家發跡於當地的零售商陷入棘手的政治處境。明尼蘇達州已對美國移民官員提起訴訟,尋求終止該州稱之為「非法激增」的聯邦幹員行動。川普私下已加大對司法部長帕姆·邦迪(Pam Bondi)的批評力道,形容她軟弱無能。伊朗人正轉向伊隆·馬斯克旗下的Starlink,以規避網路封鎖並分享抗議影片,儘管當局正加大力道進行干擾。巴拿馬最高法院即將完成審議,裁定一家香港公司是否能繼續經營巴拿馬運河兩端的兩座港口。紐約州正準備鬆綁環境法規,以加快並降低該州興建住宅的成本。

【市場直擊】

2. 道瓊期貨49733.00,下跌76.00點(0.15%);標普500期貨7004.50,下跌12.00點(0.17%);那斯達克100期貨25880.50,下跌76.25點(0.29%)。資料來源:Factset,市場數據截至2026年1月13日美東時間上午6:00:48。

川普正提出一系列旨在降低生活成本、提升民眾消費力的方案,這些方案可能為房市、石油產業與金融業帶來重大變革。經過兩年多的談判,史上最大宗信用卡合作案之一即將迎來變化——高盛將被摩根大通取代,成為蘋果信用卡的合作銀行。近年來,醫院類股的表現一直優於保險類股,但大衛·韋納撰文指出,這種局面恐怕難以持續。

【獨家搶先報導】

3. 川普盟友與官員憂心鮑爾調查案將引發反噬。
包括參議院多數黨領袖約翰·圖恩(John Thune)在內,多名共和黨參議員已對司法部針對鮑爾展開的刑事調查表達憂慮,圖恩表示希望這場爭端能盡快落幕。其他人則擔心這場衝突將震撼市場、推升借貸成本。布萊恩·施瓦茨(Brian Schwartz)、梅雷迪思·麥格勞(Meridith McGraw)、喬希·道西(Josh Dawsey)與尼克·蒂米拉奧斯報導,據政府官員透露,白宮部分幕僚對這項調查可能引發的市場反應感到憂心,其中一人更表示,白宮事先並未獲知這項調查。積極遊說推動調查的政府官員之一,是聯邦住房金融局局長比爾·普特(Bill Pulte)。

4. 美國最大電網營運商正面臨AI難題。
美國的人工智慧熱潮正將全國最大的電網營運商推向供電危機的邊緣。凱瑟琳·布朗特(Katherine Blunt)與珍妮弗·希勒報導,6700萬人的用電來自由非營利組織PJM營運的電力市場,而如今在維吉尼亞州北部「資料中心走廊」如雨後春筍般興建的眾多AI資料中心,對電力的胃口同樣永無止境。消費者電費正持續上漲,電網在用電高峰期也面臨產能吃緊的風險。

【專家解讀】

5. 問:針對鮑爾的調查究竟在查什麼?為何如此重要?
司法部這項調查,代表白宮這場前所未見、企圖左右央行運作的行動再度升級。記者麥特·葛羅斯曼解析這場衝突的來龍去脈,以及它對聯準會未來可能帶來的影響。
答:這項調查聚焦於鮑爾去年夏天在國會作證時,為聯準會翻修華盛頓總部的計畫進行辯護的證詞。川普及其盟友抓住這項工程的工期與花費大做文章,藉此指控鮑爾治理央行不力。
鮑爾週日表示,川普對這項整修工程的執著,不過是為了在一場更深層的衝突中取得談判籌碼——川普多年來一直要求鮑爾更積極地降息。
對金融市場而言,聯準會的獨立性是極其敏感的議題,投資人仰賴聯準會根據經濟現實、而非總統的政治偏好來制定政策。
投資人擔心,總統往往傾向於過度激進地降息,將經濟榮景置於抑制通膨之上。
週一當天市場雖未出現劇烈波動,但金價上漲、美元兌外幣走貶,這些動向可能顯示市場對美國政策走向已感到不安。
鮑爾的聯準會主席任期將於5月屆滿,但他作為普通理事的任期則延續至2028年。鮑爾尚未表態屆時是否會續留。

6. 在德州米德蘭(Midland),沒有人希望看到便宜的委內瑞拉石油。
對大多數美國人來說,油價便宜是件好事,但在德州米德蘭,這卻是個問題。自去年春天以來,油價多半處於低迷狀態,而美國介入石油蘊藏豐富的委內瑞拉,更助長了川普希望進一步壓低油價的意圖。這對米德蘭構成新的風險——當地眾多與油田相關的企業正感受到日益沉重的壓力。

【今日焦點】

7. 川普將與幕僚會面,討論可能包括軍事行動在內、對伊朗抗議活動的因應對策。經濟數據:12月消費者物價指數;美國預算赤字。財報:摩根大通、達美航空、紐約梅隆銀行。

【數字看時事】

8. 1.7兆美元——美國學生貸款總額,創下歷史新高,促使川普政府收緊聯邦貸款的發放。2026年7月生效的新規定,將把研究生就學貸款總額上限訂為10萬美元,專業學位則為20萬美元;代子女借貸的家長也將面臨貸款上限。

【最後一則】

9. 一場為狗爭奪監護權的官司,正撼動一個非洲國家。
是誰放出了總統衛隊的守衛犬早已不是秘密,但真正困擾馬拉威的問題更為根本:這些動物究竟是寵物,還是「執法人員」?前總統與現任總統正為此爭執不休——同時爭的還有誰能保有這些狗的監護權。

【新聞編輯室之外】

10. 評論:司法部向鮑爾發出的傳票,是一場弄巧成拙的愚蠢之舉。為了一個選民只會感到困惑、也毫不相干的議題,對聯準會與債券市場挑起爭端,根本是「入門級」的法律戰操作。
